skills.principle: From a GitLab project page, select the project-navigation link labeled “Issues,” not the global dashboard Issues link. Verify the resulting page is the project’s Issues section by checking the project name, Issues heading or breadcrumb, and issue list; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a project’s Issues section and the accessibility tree shows both global and project-specific “Issues” links. Prefer the link under “Project navigation.”

skills.title: Read Project Storage From Overview
skills.principle: On a GitLab project overview, inspect the project summary/navigation links for a label containing "Project Storage." Extract the displayed size directly and report it; opening the storage-usage page is unnecessary when the overview already provides the value.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a GitLab project's storage size and the project overview accessibility tree is available. Confirm the displayed "Project Storage" label belongs to the target project before answering.

skills.title: Use Visible Project Storage Summary
skills.principle: On a GitLab project page, inspect the project metrics before opening deeper settings. If a metric is labeled “Project Storage” and includes a size, treat that visible value as the answer, report it immediately, and terminate. Only open “Usage Quotas” when the summary is absent or the task explicitly requires a detailed breakdown.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a GitLab project’s storage size and the project overview visibly shows a “Project Storage” metric, especially when the Usage Quotas page exposes little or no additional accessible content.

skills.title: Recognize Existing GitLab Files View
skills.principle: Inspect the current GitLab repository page before navigating. If the repository contents table and Files breadcrumb are already visible for the target project, treat the Files-page goal as complete, report the visible contents, and stop without unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a GitLab repository’s Files page and the current accessibility tree already shows the target project, repository file listing, and Files breadcrumb.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Files Page
skills.principle: In GitLab, open the target project, select Repository, and verify the page title or visible file table indicates Files. Once the repository file listing is displayed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a GitLab project’s Files page and the observation already shows the Files view, repository breadcrumb, and files/directories table.

skills.title: Open a GitLab Project README
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target project in the GitLab project list and open it.
2. Select Repository or Files, then choose the README.md file from the repository listing.
3. Confirm the README page displays its rendered contents, including headings or project description.
4. Once the file is visibly open and readable, report completion and stop instead of repeatedly scrolling or using no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read or inspect a project README in GitLab and the project is accessible from the dashboard or project list.

skills.title: Recognize Inline README Content
skills.principle: Inspect the current GitLab accessibility tree before navigating. If the README is already rendered inline with its headings and text, read that content directly, summarize the relevant project information, and stop. Only navigate when the requested file content is absent; then use the observed link's accessibility identifier rather than guessing from visible text or URLs.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read a GitLab README and the repository page already exposes a rendered README article beneath the file list.

skills.title: Stop After Detail Confirmation
skills.principle: Once a search result’s detail page confirms the target name, requested category, and location, use those fields as sufficient evidence. Report the finding immediately and terminate; do not click coordinates, zoom, or perform visual checks that add no task-relevant evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map searches when the result detail page visibly provides the target’s name, category tag, and address or locality, especially after a matching search result has already been opened.

skills.title: Read Visible Map Scale Directly
skills.principle: Inspect the current map view for the visible scale bar or scale text. Read and report both displayed units directly; do not zoom, click, or hover unless the scale is absent or obscured. Once the requested scale is visible and verified, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for map scale at the current zoom and the map page visibly exposes scale text or a scale bar, such as kilometer and mile values.

skills.title: Read Scale Text Directly
skills.principle: Inspect the complete map accessibility tree for static text near the map controls or attribution before taking actions. If distance labels such as kilometers or miles are present, report them as the current scale; do not infer scale by zooming or searching unrelated controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a map’s current scale and the accessibility tree includes distance labels, especially near the map’s lower edge, controls, or attribution.

skills.title: Generate and Verify Map Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Fill the “From” and “To” textboxes separately with the requested locations; avoid batching fills if the interface rejects combined actions.
3. Click “Go” after both fields resolve to locations.
4. Confirm completion by checking for a “Directions” heading and a populated turn-by-turn instruction table, then report the instructions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap direction requests when the directions panel exposes “From,” “To,” and “Go” controls. Verify the resulting Directions panel before responding.

skills.title: Terminate After Directions Appear
skills.principle: Enter the origin and destination, click “Go,” then verify that a “Directions” heading and turn-by-turn table are visible. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map routing tasks after both location fields are accepted and the page visibly shows generated route details, such as distance, travel time, or numbered directions.

skills.title: Request Walking Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions form and fill the From and To fields with the requested locations.
2. Choose the walking option, such as “Foot (OSRM),” rather than the default driving mode.
3. Click “Go” and verify the page shows a Directions panel with route steps, distance, or travel time before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting walking directions between two named places, once the directions form exposes From, To, a travel-mode selector, and a Go button.

skills.title: Stop After Route Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the directions page shows the requested origin and destination plus a generated route summary or turn-by-turn directions, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated waits or other unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after submitting map directions when the page visibly confirms both endpoints and displays the resulting route, distance, time, or turn-by-turn instructions.

skills.title: Adapt Export Method to Area Size
skills.principle: Open the map’s Export page and inspect the area-size message. If direct XML export is unavailable because the selection is too large, either zoom in or manually select a smaller area, or use the listed bulk-download source appropriate to the coverage needed, such as regional extracts or complete database data.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting OpenStreetMap data and the Export page reports that the current bounding box is too large for direct XML export.

skills.title: Use the Directions Form Directly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's directions form; if it is already visible, use its From and To fields instead of reopening navigation.
2. Enter the origin in From and destination in To, allowing each location to resolve to a recognized place.
3. Keep the requested travel mode selected, then click Go.
4. Confirm the Directions panel shows route details such as distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: For map-routing tasks when a directions form is visible or accessible, especially after a navigation link is hidden, duplicated, or no longer clickable.

skills.title: Verify Export Navigation
skills.principle: Select the navigation control whose accessible name is exactly “Export,” not a neighboring menu button such as “Edit.” After activating it, inspect the updated URL and accessibility tree for the export page and its download controls. If the page remains on directions, retry using the observed Export link rather than assuming navigation occurred.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a map or other page state, especially when adjacent navigation controls have empty labels or expandable menus. Verify the destination before reporting completion.

skills.title: Update Route Destination
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested place in the directions page’s “To” textbox, replacing any existing destination.
2. Click “Go” to submit the route request.
3. Confirm the destination resolves to a specific place or address and the route calculation begins, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a route destination in OpenStreetMap directions. The directions form must expose a “To” textbox and “Go” button; verify the resolved destination after submission before terminating.

skills.title: Use Dedicated Directions Fields
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” page.
2. Enter the origin in the dedicated “From” field and destination in “To”; do not assume earlier search text carries over.
3. Keep or select the requested travel mode, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm a route, distance, or turn-by-turn results appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map site opens a separate directions page showing “From,” “To,” travel-mode controls, and a “Go” button, especially after using a general map search field.

skills.title: Use the Directions Workflow
skills.principle: For route changes, open “Find directions between two points” rather than using the map’s general Search box. Fill the destination field in the directions form, submit the form, and verify that the route panel or map updates to show the requested destination. If an action returns “empty action,” correct the tool-call format before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the map page shows a general Search box plus a directions entry, and the task asks to change a route endpoint rather than merely locate a place.

skills.title: Zoom Until Street Detail Improves
skills.principle: Use the map’s labeled “Zoom In” control repeatedly, checking the URL’s zoom level or scale bar after each click. Stop once the map visibly provides street-level detail sufficient for the request, then report completion rather than continuing unnecessary zooming.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests closer street detail and the accessibility tree exposes a “Zoom In” control. Confirm that each click increases the zoom level or reduces the scale-bar distance before stopping.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Zoom
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom In” control, then inspect the updated map state after each click. Confirm progress through a higher zoom level, reduced scale indicator, or visible street details. Once the requested detail is clearly available, report completion and stop instead of repeatedly clicking.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map zoom tasks when a “Zoom In” control is accessible and the page exposes observable zoom changes such as URL level, scale bar, refreshed tiles, or street detail.

skills.title: Verify Diary Availability Directly
skills.principle: Open the map site's “User Diaries” section and inspect its rendered state. If it explicitly shows “No diary entries,” treat that as confirmation that no matching diaries are currently available, report the result, and terminate without checking unrelated sections such as GPS Traces.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore diaries for a geographic area and the User Diaries page is accessible. Use this when the page provides an explicit empty-state message and no search or location filter is present.

skills.title: Submit And Verify Search Actions
skills.principle: After filling a search field, emit a valid browser action that submits it (such as clicking “Go” or pressing Enter), then inspect the resulting page before concluding. If an action error reports an empty or malformed action, retry with the correctly structured action and verify that the field value and page state changed.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever a task requires searching or filtering from a page with a textbox and submit control, especially after the browser reports that a proposed action was empty or did not execute.

skills.title: Calculate and Verify Walking Distance
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in “To.”
2. Select the walking option, such as “Foot (OSRM),” rather than the default driving mode.
3. Click “Go” and wait for the directions panel.
4. Confirm the panel displays a “Distance” value, then report that value and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on an OpenStreetMap directions page when a task asks for walking distance between two named locations and the From, To, travel-mode, and Go controls are available.

skills.title: Select Walking Mode Before Routing
skills.principle: On the directions page, verify both endpoints, change the travel-mode combobox from its default to “Foot (OSRM),” then click “Go.” Wait for the route result panel or distance text to appear and report that walking distance; do not infer it from map tiles or repeatedly focus unrelated images.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when calculating a walking route in OpenStreetMap directions, especially when the travel-mode control visibly defaults to “Car (OSRM)” and the endpoints are already populated.

skills.title: Verify Destination After Navigation
skills.principle: Use the navigation entry matching the requested destination, then verify the resulting page before reporting completion. Confirm using multiple observable cues when available, such as the URL path, page title or heading, and focused or selected navigation state. If the destination is already displayed, report that directly rather than performing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests opening a specific page in a web application and the current accessibility tree may already show that destination or provides a clearly labeled navigation link.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Navigate using the visible link matching the requested destination, then verify the resulting URL or page heading reflects that destination. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the destination page is visibly loaded and its URL, title, or heading confirms the requested location.

skills.title: Generate and Verify Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” interface.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To”; select the requested travel mode, such as “Car (OSRM)”.
3. Click “Go” and wait for the route results.
4. Confirm a “Directions” panel shows distance, travel time, and turn-by-turn steps, then report the result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting route directions when the page exposes origin and destination fields, a travel-mode selector, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Fill Separate Direction Endpoints
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” rather than combining both places in the map search box.
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To” as separate fields.
3. Keep or select “Car (OSRM),” then click the directions form’s “Go” button.
4. Confirm a route, distance, or travel-time result appears before reporting failure.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions page when routing between two locations. The prerequisite is that the separate “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls are visible.

skills.title: Recover From Duplicate Username Errors
skills.principle: When submission reports that the display name is already taken, replace it with a genuinely unique name, then re-scan the form because validation may clear password fields. Refill every required field that is empty, submit again, and verify a success or confirmation state before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use during account registration when the form remains displayed after submission and shows a display-name uniqueness error, especially if other fields appear cleared or changed.

skills.title: Recover From Duplicate Signup Values
skills.principle: When signup reports that an email or display name is already taken, replace every affected value with genuinely unique values, then update the email confirmation to exactly match the new email and re-enter matching passwords if validation cleared them. Submit again and verify a success or confirmation state before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on registration forms after submission shows uniqueness errors such as “has already been taken,” especially when changing one field can leave confirmation fields stale or required fields reset.

skills.title: Use Labeled Navigation Links
skills.principle: When a requested informational page has a matching navigation link, activate that link rather than using search or guessing URLs. Verify navigation succeeded by checking the resulting URL or page heading, then report completion and stop once the requested content is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for website tasks asking to view a clearly named informational page, when the accessibility tree exposes a matching link and the destination shows a confirming heading or relevant content.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: After navigating to the requested information page, verify its distinctive heading or content. Once the target state is visible, report completion and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions or waiting for more observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational browsing tasks when navigation succeeds and the resulting page visibly contains the requested heading or content, such as a copyright or license page.

skills.title: Verify Empty Diary State
skills.principle: Open the site's User Diaries navigation entry and inspect the resulting page. If it shows the explicit status "No diary entries" and provides no diary links or entry controls, report that no entries are available on this instance and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to read community diaries and the page is accessible through a clearly labeled User Diaries navigation link. Treat an explicit empty-state heading as the completion signal.

skills.title: Act on Explicit Empty States
skills.principle: When the requested page clearly shows an empty-state message such as “No diary entries,” treat that as the verified result. Report that no matching content is available and stop, rather than exploring unrelated sections or repeatedly reopening the same page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task asks you to read or inspect content and the target listing visibly reports no entries, results, or records, with no relevant filters or pagination available.

skills.title: Generate Walking Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” control.
2. Enter the origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields, allowing place resolution to complete.
3. Set the travel-mode selector to “Foot (OSRM)” rather than its default driving mode, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm completion by checking for a “Directions” panel with distance, time, turn-by-turn steps, and the displayed route.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap direction tasks requesting walking routes between two places, once the directions form exposes origin, destination, travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Read the Visible Map Scale
skills.principle: Inspect the current map view for the scale-bar labels, typically displayed near the map edge or attribution area. Report the displayed metric and imperial distances exactly as shown; do not infer scale from zoom level or map coordinates.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for the distance scale of the currently displayed map and the map view is already loaded. Confirm the scale labels are visible before reporting.

skills.title: Report the Visible Map Scale
skills.principle: When the map accessibility tree contains scale text, extract its displayed distance and units, then report that value as the answer. Do not repeat no-op actions; the task is complete once the scale is identified and communicated.
skills.when_to_apply: For map tasks asking for the current view’s distance scale, when visible text such as a kilometer or mile value appears in the map’s accessibility tree.

skills.title: Search a Location on the Map
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the map interface if starting elsewhere.
2. Enter the requested place in the textbox labeled “Search,” then activate “Go.”
3. Confirm completion when a search-results panel appears and the map centers on the requested location; then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring a place-name search, once the map page exposes a Search textbox and Go control. A results panel and centered map confirm the search succeeded.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Map Search
skills.principle: Enter the target place in the map Search field and activate Go. Confirm completion when a Search Results panel shows a relevant place result and the map URL/view has moved to that location. Report completion immediately; do not add unnecessary waits or zoom actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-location searches when Go produces relevant geocoding results and the map view or URL changes to the target area.

skills.title: Verify Available Map Layers
skills.principle: Open the map’s labeled “Layers” control and inspect the “Map Layers” list. If the requested imagery type is not explicitly listed, treat it as unavailable in that instance, distinguish overlays from base layers, and report the limitation rather than guessing from unlabeled controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map’s visual layer, especially satellite or aerial imagery, after reaching the map view and opening its labeled layer panel.

skills.title: Verify Layer Labels Before Selecting
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and inspect the displayed layer names. Select only a layer explicitly indicating satellite imagery, then verify the map tiles or active-layer state changed accordingly. Do not equate thematic styles such as “Humanitarian” with satellite imagery; if no satellite option is listed, preserve the current layer and report that the requested imagery is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map basemap through a visible layers menu, especially when the menu lists multiple styles but does not visibly include a satellite option.

skills.title: Activate Map Location Control
skills.principle: From a non-map page, navigate to the site's main map. Locate the clearly labeled location control, such as “Show My Location,” and activate it. If the browser requests geolocation permission, allow it; completion is indicated when the map centers on the current position or displays a location marker.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to show the user's current position in a web map and the page provides a geolocation control. Ensure the main map is open and be prepared for a browser location-permission prompt.

skills.title: Handle Location Requests Deliberately
skills.principle: On the map page, activate “Show My Location” once and inspect for a location marker, recentering, or permission prompt. If nothing changes, resolve the browser’s geolocation permission or report that location access is unavailable; do not repeatedly click the unchanged control.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires displaying the user’s current position and the map exposes a “Show My Location” control. Verify a visible marker or recentered map before declaring completion.

skills.title: Zoom the Map Incrementally
skills.principle: If the current page is not the map, open the main map view. Locate the control labeled “Zoom In,” activate it as needed, and verify the map URL or scale reflects a higher zoom level. Once the requested closer view is achieved, report completion and stop rather than continuing unnecessary zoom actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requesting a closer map view, especially when starting on another site page and the accessibility tree exposes a “Zoom In” control plus a map URL whose zoom value updates.

skills.title: Verify Zoom Then Stop
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom In” control once, then verify that the map scale or zoom level increased in the updated page state. Once a closer view is visibly achieved, report completion and stop; do not continue clicking merely because the control remains focused.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests a closer view without specifying an exact zoom level, and the accessible tree exposes a “Zoom In” control plus observable scale or URL changes.

skills.title: Switch OpenStreetMap Map Style
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the main map view and open the “Layers” control.
2. Select the requested map style from the Map Layers panel.
3. Confirm completion when the URL, rendered tile sources, or attribution reflects the selected style, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requiring a base map style change, when the map view and “Layers” control are available. Verify the selected style through visible attribution or updated map state.

skills.title: Verify Map Style and Stop
skills.principle: Open the map’s Layers control, select the requested style, then verify the map state changed. For Humanitarian, confirmation includes the URL gaining the humanitarian layer indicator and tiles or attribution reflecting that style. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When switching an OpenStreetMap map style or layer and the interface updates automatically. Use the resulting URL, tile sources, attribution, or selected-layer state as completion evidence.

skills.title: Enable Public GPS Traces Overlay
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the main map view and open the “Layers” control.
2. In “Map Layers,” locate the “Public GPS Traces” checkbox and click it only if unchecked.
3. Confirm it is checked and GPS trace line tiles or recorded routes appear, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to display recorded GPS routes in OpenStreetMap and the map view is available. Use the Layers menu; completion is indicated by the checkbox becoming checked and trace overlays loading.

skills.title: Use Map Layers for GPS Overlay
skills.principle: Return to the map view and open the map’s “Layers” control. Select or enable “Public GPS Traces,” then verify the control reflects the enabled state or GPS tracks appear on the map. The “GPS Traces” navigation page is for browsing or uploading traces, not enabling map overlays.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to display a map overlay and the current map observation includes a “Layers” control. Use that control rather than navigating to a similarly named content or upload page.

skills.title: Compare Map Layers at Urban Zoom
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, identify every available style, and switch through each option. Zoom into a representative urban area before judging detail, comparing buildings, street networks, infrastructure, and points of interest. Select the style that best matches the requested detail criterion, then report the comparison and recommendation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to compare map styles or layers for urban detail. Ensure the Layers menu is available and evaluate styles at a sufficiently close zoom level for meaningful visual comparison.

skills.title: Verify Layer Menu State
skills.principle: After activating the map’s “Layers” control, inspect the updated accessibility tree before retrying. If “Map Layers” and named style options are present, select each relevant style and compare the same urban area at the same zoom; do not repeatedly click the trigger or scroll. Report the style with the greatest visible urban detail once comparison is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: When comparing map styles and the accessibility tree shows a “Map Layers” panel with selectable style names such as Standard, CyclOSM, or other alternatives.

skills.title: Toggle Map Styles Through Layers
skills.principle:
1. Open the main map interface and select the “Layers” control.
2. In “Map Layers,” select the requested alternate style, such as “Humanitarian,” and confirm the map tiles change.
3. Select “Standard” to switch back; verify the standard tiles return, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map-style comparison is requested and the map interface provides a “Layers” control with named style options. Verify each selection by observing the map tiles or URL state change.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Both Map Styles
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, select the target alternate style, and verify the map tiles or URL reflect the change. Select the original style once to compare it, verify the return, then report completion and stop instead of repeating toggles.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-style comparison tasks when a “Layers” panel exposes named styles such as “Standard” and “Humanitarian,” and the map or URL visibly updates after selection.

skills.title: Copy a Map’s Short Share Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Share” control.
2. Choose “Short Link” so the share field contains a compact URL.
3. Focus the resulting textbox, select all text, and copy it with the platform keyboard shortcut.
4. Confirm the textbox contains the short URL, then report that it is copied and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to share the current map view and the map interface exposes a “Share” control with a “Short Link” option and editable URL textbox.

skills.title: Copy a Map View Short Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Share” control.
2. In the “Link or HTML” section, select “Short Link” to populate the share field.
3. Focus the populated textbox and copy it with ControlOrMeta+C.
4. Confirm the short-link field remains populated, then report that it is copied.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap-style tasks requesting a shareable short link for the currently displayed map view. Ensure the intended view is already loaded before opening “Share”.

skills.title: Populate Both Direction Endpoints
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form rather than relying on the map search field.
2. Enter the requested origin in the “From” textbox and destination in the “To” textbox.
3. Select “Foot (OSRM)” for walking, then activate “Go”.
4. Confirm that route details or a rendered route appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when requesting route directions in OpenStreetMap and the directions page shows separate empty “From” and “To” fields, even if a place was previously entered in the map search box.

skills.title: Export Map Through Share Dialog
skills.principle: On the map Export page, open Share to reveal image export controls. Use the Format combobox to select PDF with select_option rather than clicking the hidden PDF option directly, confirm the combobox value is PDF, then click Download.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a map as PDF and the Export page shows no direct PDF control, especially after opening Share and finding an Image section with a Format combobox and Download button.

skills.title: Export Map Through Share Image Controls
skills.principle: Open the map’s Share panel, locate the Image section, change the Format selector to PDF, then click Download. Confirm that the format is visibly PDF before downloading and verify a download or completion state afterward.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap Export page is open and the task requests a PDF map. This works even when the XML export area is reported as too large, because PDF is provided through the Share panel’s image export controls.

skills.title: Download Map in the Requested Format
skills.principle: Open the map’s Share dialog, locate the Image section, select the requested format from the Format combobox, and verify the combobox value changed. Then click Download and confirm the resulting download or completion state before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When downloading a map image and the export page offers a Share dialog with an Image section, format selector, and Download button.

skills.title: Use Share for Image Format
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, open the Share dialog rather than Layers. In the Image section, change the Format combobox from PNG to the requested format, verify the selected value updates, then click Download.
skills.when_to_apply: When downloading a map image and the Export page lacks visible format controls. Prerequisite: the map and Export page are loaded, with the Share control available.

skills.title: Calculate Walking Distance with Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the starting place in “From” and destination in “To”, confirming both resolve to intended locations.
3. Select the walking mode, such as “Foot (OSRM)”, then activate “Go”.
4. Read the resulting Directions panel and report the displayed distance and walking time once present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for walking distance or travel time between two places, when the map provides From/To fields, a travel-mode selector, and a route-results panel.

skills.title: Calculate Walking Distance in OpenStreetMap
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” and enter the requested locations in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Select “Foot (OSRM)” in the transportation mode selector.
3. Click “Go” and verify the Directions result displays a distance and walking time.
4. Report those values to the user.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks asking for walking distance or duration between two named places, when the directions page provides “From,” “To,” a transportation selector, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Use Reverse Directions Control
skills.principle: On the map’s directions page, locate the control labeled “Reverse Directions” and activate it to swap the route’s From and To endpoints. Confirm the resulting page state shows the endpoints exchanged, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a planned route already exists in a directions form and the task requests reversing its travel direction; the directions page must expose a reverse-direction control.

skills.title: Verify Route Before Reversing
skills.principle: On the directions page, inspect the “From” and “To” fields before acting. If either is empty, load or enter the planned route first. Then click “Reverse Directions,” verify the nonempty values have swapped, and only proceed when the reversed route is visibly reflected in the fields or map.
skills.when_to_apply: When reversing a planned route in a map directions interface, especially if the page may open with empty “From” and “To” fields.

skills.title: Generate a Cycling Route Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” interface and fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations.
2. Set the transportation combobox to “Bicycle” using select-option behavior; do not click the hidden option element directly.
3. Click “Go” and verify the combobox shows Bicycle and a Directions panel displays distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap directions tasks requiring a specific travel mode, once the directions form and its From, To, mode, and Go controls are available.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Locations Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Enter origin and destination with disambiguating region or country when names are ambiguous.
2. Inspect the resolved field values before clicking “Go”; confirm both correspond to the intended places.
3. If either resolves incorrectly, clear and refill that field with more specific text, then rerun the route.
4. Confirm the Directions result and map location match the requested geography.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map directions pages whenever place names can match multiple cities, streets, or regions. Verify resolved locations before generating or reporting the route.

skills.title: Use the Directions From Field
skills.principle:
1. Navigate from the map interface to the directions feature using the link labeled “Find directions between two points.”
2. In the directions form, fill the textbox labeled “From” with the requested starting location.
3. Confirm completion when the “From” field visibly contains the requested location; do not submit “Go” unless a route is requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to enter a starting location for directions in OpenStreetMap and the directions form is not yet open. Confirm the From field displays the requested place before reporting completion.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Destination
skills.principle: In the directions form, enter the target city with state and country to disambiguate it, then submit with “Go.” Inspect the resulting “To” value; if it resolves to a river, street, or similarly named place, clear the field, refine the query, and resubmit until the canonical result identifies the intended city.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions form autocompletes place names and the target has ambiguous matches. Confirm the resolved location after submission before treating the destination as set.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Destination
skills.principle: In the directions form, enter the destination in the “To” field and select or submit it. Inspect the resolved place name after submission; if it identifies a similarly named river, street, or location in another region, clear the field, refine the query with city, state, and country, then submit again. Treat the destination as set only when the resolved result matches the intended place.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions form geocodes free-text destinations and the target name may have ambiguous matches. A “To” field and a submission control must be available.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Route Endpoints
skills.principle: Enter both route endpoints, keep driving mode selected, and submit the directions form. Inspect the resolved endpoint text, route map, road names, distance, and time. If they indicate different cities or implausible geography, refine both location queries and rerun; report only after the displayed route matches the requested places.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map directions involving ambiguous place names or locations with duplicates. Apply after submitting a route, especially when resolved fields, road names, map position, distance, or travel time contradict the intended endpoints.

skills.title: Disambiguate Map Route Locations
skills.principle: For directions between places with ambiguous names, enter each endpoint with its city and region/country before calculating. After clicking “Go,” verify the resolved endpoint addresses and route geography match the requested locations; if not, clear both fields, refine the queries, recalculate, and only report the route once the result is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map directions form accepts free-text place names and the resolved addresses may refer to streets, neighborhoods, or cities in different regions.

skills.title: Request Missing Login Credentials
skills.principle: Open the site's “Log In” page and inspect the form. If username/email and password are not supplied, do not guess or submit placeholders; ask the user for both credentials before attempting authentication.
skills.when_to_apply: When a login task reaches a form requiring credentials that are absent from the task instructions or current browser state.

skills.title: Read Coordinates From Map URL
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, open the main map, enter the requested place in the Search box, and activate Go. After results load, read the URL fragment formatted as `#map=zoom/latitude/longitude`; report the latitude and longitude, ignoring the zoom value. Use the result page’s selected place and URL rather than estimating from the visual map.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a place’s coordinates on OpenStreetMap and the map search interface is available. Confirm that search results loaded and the URL contains a map fragment with latitude and longitude.

skills.title: Use the Copyright Navigation Link
skills.principle:
1. From an OpenStreetMap page, locate the navigation entry labeled “Copyright” and activate it.
2. Confirm completion by checking the URL or page heading for copyright information and verifying license details are visible.
3. Report the relevant information, then stop once the requested page is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view OpenStreetMap copyright or licensing information and the page navigation contains a visible “Copyright” link.

skills.title: Verify Map History Across Zoom Levels
skills.principle: Open the map’s History view, inspect the current area, and zoom in a few levels when needed to verify the result. If the page consistently displays “No changesets in this area,” report that no edits are visible and stop rather than continuing unnecessary exploration.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view edit history for a map area and the History page is available, especially when the initial view shows no changesets.

skills.title: Verify External Export Navigation
skills.principle: When an export link targets an external download service, treat a click timeout as potentially successful navigation. Wait briefly, inspect the current page or download state, and confirm the export before trying another source. If the area is too large, select a smaller area or use one listed bulk-download source, then verify its resulting page or file.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s Export page when the selected bounding box is reported too large or an external source link times out after the click action.

skills.title: Handle Oversized Map Exports
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s Export page and inspect the selected-area message.
2. If the area is too large, zoom in or use “Manually select a different area” to choose a smaller bounding box.
3. Retry the standard export and confirm that a download or resulting data page appears.
4. For intentionally large regions, choose a listed bulk-download source such as Geofabrik instead of repeatedly retrying a direct export link.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when exporting OpenStreetMap data and the Export page reports that the selected area is too large for XML export, or a download link times out without changing the visible page.

skills.title: Verify Empty-State Completion
skills.principle: Navigate to the relevant content page and inspect its primary heading or status message. If it explicitly reports an empty state such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the check as complete and report that no matching user-contributed items are available. Do not open upload or informational links unless the user requested those actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check whether a page contains user-contributed content, after reaching the page and observing its authoritative empty-state message.

skills.title: Verify Help Documentation Destination
skills.principle: Navigate to the site's Help page, choose the resource matching the request (such as a beginner guide), then wait for and verify the destination page or link content before reporting completion. Do not assume a click succeeded without observing the resulting documentation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find documentation through a site's help or support navigation, especially when the selected resource opens an external page or requires a page-load transition.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Help Resources
skills.principle: Use the site’s clearly labeled “Help” navigation entry, then verify the resulting page contains documentation or support resources. Once that page satisfies a broad request to find help documentation, report completion and stop instead of opening an additional external resource without a requirement to do so.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find general help documentation and the current site exposes a Help link. Apply after navigation succeeds and the resulting page visibly lists relevant guides, forums, or documentation.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Stopping
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to identify the navigation link matching the requested page and activate it. After navigation, verify completion using the page title, URL, focused or selected navigation state, and distinctive page content. If these confirm the target page, report completion and stop rather than clicking the same link again.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to visit a named page and the current page may already be that destination; verify observable page state before taking additional navigation actions.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation Links
skills.principle: When the requested page is directly represented by a visible, semantically labeled navigation link, activate that link rather than inferring or constructing a URL. Confirm completion by checking that the resulting page URL and accessible heading/content match the requested destination, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a website’s accessibility tree exposes a navigation entry matching the requested destination and the task only requires visiting that page.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the requested destination by its visible semantic label in the page navigation, activate that link, then verify the resulting page through its URL or heading. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the current page exposes a clearly labeled link matching the requested destination and the post-navigation page provides an observable heading or URL confirmation.

skills.title: Disambiguate Map Locations Before Routing
skills.principle: Use the directions form’s From and To fields, adding state or country qualifiers for ambiguous place names. Submit with Go, then verify the resolved place labels and route summary match the requested locations; if not, clear and correct the ambiguous field before reporting results.
skills.when_to_apply: When planning a route between places with potentially duplicated names, especially when the first result resolves to an unexpected region or produces an implausible distance or travel time.

skills.title: Navigate Using Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose visible label matches the requested destination, activate it, and verify the resulting page heading or URL matches the goal. Once the destination and relevant content are visible, report completion and stop rather than taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree exposes a labeled link for the requested page and completion can be confirmed by the resulting URL, heading, or page content.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the target navigation link, verify the destination using the page heading, URL, or distinctive content. Once the expected page is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree already shows the requested destination page and its distinctive heading or content after a successful link click.

skills.title: Select Transportation Mode Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” route planner.
2. Identify the transportation-mode combobox and open it.
3. Use the dropdown-selection operation to choose the requested mode; do not click an invisible option element directly.
4. Confirm the combobox value changed to the requested mode, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a route’s travel mode in OpenStreetMap directions and the accessibility tree exposes a combobox with selectable mode options, especially after direct option clicking fails.

skills.title: Reverse Directions Directly
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap directions page, locate the labeled “Reverse Directions” button and click it. This swaps the route’s “From” and “To” endpoints; then report completion once the control has been activated.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a route-planning task asks to reverse an existing route and the directions interface exposes “From,” “To,” and “Reverse Directions” controls.

skills.title: Share a Generated Map Route
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions tool and enter the origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Select the travel mode if needed, then click “Go” and confirm directions and route details appear.
3. Click “Share,” choose “Short Link,” and verify the generated URL appears focused in the textbox.
4. Report that the link is ready to copy and share; stop once the shareable link is available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap route-sharing tasks when the map interface and directions tool are accessible, and the user needs a reusable link for a route between two locations.

skills.title: Verify Empty Trace Listings
skills.principle: Open the GPS Traces section and inspect the listing page. If it displays an explicit empty-state message such as "Nothing here yet," treat that as confirmation that no traces are available; do not pursue redundant listing controls. Report the empty result and mention any offered upload or informational options.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse public GPS traces and the site’s GPS Traces navigation is available. Use after reaching the listing page, especially when an explicit empty-state message is visible.

skills.title: Verify Trace Availability Before Exploring
skills.principle: Open the GPS Traces section and inspect its result state. If it displays “Nothing here yet,” treat the browsing task as complete with no available traces, report that clearly, and stop. Do not switch to upload, login, help, or wiki pages unless the task explicitly requires creating or learning about traces.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse public GPS traces and the traces page visibly shows an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet.”

skills.title: Verify History Page State
skills.principle: Use the navigation link labeled “History” when available. After navigation, verify the page title or focused navigation state and inspect the changeset panel. If it displays “No changesets in this area,” report that the History page is open and the visible map area has no changes; stop once the goal is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a map application's History page, especially when the current page may already be that destination and the result should be confirmed from visible page content.

skills.title: Calculate Driving Time with Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature from the main map interface.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To,” preserving the requested travel mode, such as “Car (OSRM).”
3. Select “Go” and wait for the route results.
4. Read the summary showing “Distance” and “Time,” then report the requested travel time and optionally the distance.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for travel time or distance between two places, when the site provides a directions form with origin, destination, travel-mode controls, and a route summary.

skills.title: Calculate Driving Distance in OpenStreetMap
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To”; keep the travel mode set to “Car” for driving distance.
3. Click “Go” and wait for the Directions panel.
4. Read the value after “Distance:” and report it with its displayed unit.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks asking for driving distance between two locations, when the directions form exposes “From,” “To,” a car travel-mode selector, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Navigate Using Semantic Help Links
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation link whose label matches the requested documentation, then activate it. Confirm completion by checking the destination page’s heading and relevant help resources. Once the target documentation is visibly loaded, report success and stop without extra navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access site documentation and the current accessibility tree exposes a labeled Help or documentation link. If already on the matching page, verify its heading and content, then finish.

skills.title: Report Completion After Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the requested destination is reached, verify the page heading or URL matches the task, then provide the completion response and terminate. Do not repeatedly issue noop actions after success has been visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the target page is already displayed and its heading, URL, or relevant content confirms completion.

skills.title: Verify Reversal Then Stop
skills.principle:
1. Enter the origin and destination, resolve each to the intended geographic place, and click “Go” to establish the route.
2. Click “Reverse Directions” once.
3. Confirm the From and To fields visibly swapped and the resulting route state reflects the reversal; then terminate without clicking the reversal control again.
skills.when_to_apply: When reversing a route in a map directions form, especially after autocomplete or routing updates. Use only after both endpoints are populated and stop immediately once the swapped endpoint order is visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Verify Endpoints Before Reversing
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and fill the origin and destination fields with the requested locations.
2. Wait for each location to resolve, selecting the correct autocomplete result when necessary; verify the fields show distinct places.
3. Click “Go” to establish the intended route, then click “Reverse Directions” once.
4. Confirm the fields are swapped and the resulting route reflects the reversed endpoints before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when reversing a route in OpenStreetMap or similar mapping interfaces. Prerequisite: both endpoint fields must contain correctly resolved, distinct locations; do not reverse an empty, unresolved, or already incorrect route.

skills.title: Generate Turn-by-Turn Route Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To”; ensure each resolves to a recognized place.
3. Keep the requested travel mode, then select “Go” to calculate the route.
4. Confirm a “Directions” panel or table appears with route distance, duration, and individual turn steps; report completion once displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting driving or other turn-by-turn directions between two places, when the map interface provides “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Inspect the Map Layers Panel
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the map view and activate the control labeled “Layers.”
2. Read the “Map Layers” panel to list all base-layer labels.
3. Separately record overlay checkboxes and their availability notes, such as zoom prerequisites.
4. Report the observed base layers and overlays, then stop once the panel provides the complete list.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which layers or overlays a map supports and the map view is accessible. Open the Layers control first; distinguish selectable base layers from optional overlays and note disabled prerequisites.

skills.title: Stop After Reading Map Layers
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Layers” control, read the visible “Map Layers” list and overlay states, then report those options immediately. Once the requested availability is observable, do not click headings, close controls, or unrelated Help links; terminate the task.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which map layers are available and the Layers panel visibly lists base layers or overlays, including any disabled or unchecked options.

skills.title: Search Maps and Verify Address
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested place name in the map’s Search field and activate Go.
2. Select the matching result from the Search Results list to open its map record.
3. Read address fields from the record’s Tags table, such as house number, street, city, state, and postal code.
4. Report the assembled address once the record clearly matches the requested place.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap when locating a named landmark or place and the search interface is available. Prefer the matching result’s details page over relying only on map position or zoom level.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Map Result
skills.principle: Once search results identify the requested place and the map centers on it, treat the task as complete. Report the visible location or address immediately and terminate; do not use unrelated controls such as “Show My Location,” repeated zooming, or guessed URLs.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-location searches when the search results show the target and the map or detail panel visibly confirms its location. No further navigation is required unless the requested information remains missing.

skills.title: Verify Geographic Search Matches
skills.principle: When a map search returns unrelated streets, buildings, or similarly named places, refine the query with the target’s full geographic context (city, region, country). Submit the refined search, inspect result labels and addresses, and select only the result whose place type and location match the requested destination. Confirm the map has recentered to that result before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after submitting a map search when results contain ambiguous names, unrelated locations, or a map position inconsistent with the requested destination.

skills.title: Validate Map Search Results
skills.principle: After submitting a place search, inspect result names and addresses before selecting anything. If results refer to similarly named streets, buildings, or people rather than the requested place, refine the query or load the currently displayed “More results” control. Select a result only when its geographic identity matches the target, then verify the map view changed accordingly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map searches with ambiguous names or unexpected results. Re-observe the accessibility tree after each search update, especially before clicking dynamic result controls.

skills.title: Use the Dedicated Directions Workflow
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s dedicated directions feature rather than relying on general search.
2. Fill the labeled “From” and “To” fields with the origin and destination.
3. Confirm the requested travel mode, then activate “Go.”
4. Verify completion by checking that a route map, distance/time summary, and turn-by-turn directions appear.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting directions between two places, when the map interface exposes a “Find directions between two points” control and labeled origin, destination, travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Complete Directions After Navigation
skills.principle: After opening a mapping service, inspect the new page for its directions control, enter the requested origin and destination, select driving mode when available, and verify that a route summary or displayed route confirms completion before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for route-planning tasks when the initial page is not a map or directions view, especially after navigating to another mapping service; a page transition alone does not complete the task.

skills.title: Generate Cycling Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” control.
2. Fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, checking their resolved place values.
3. Select “Bicycle” in the travel-mode combobox instead of the default driving mode.
4. Click “Go” and confirm a Directions panel shows route distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-routing tasks requiring bicycle directions between two named places, once the directions form is available and both endpoint fields can be populated.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Route Endpoints
skills.principle: For ambiguous place names, use city and region or country in both origin and destination fields. Select the matching geocoding suggestion when offered, then submit the route. Verify the resulting endpoint labels, map markers, and route summary identify the requested locations; if stale or unrelated results remain, correct the selections and resubmit before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting directions between common or ambiguous place names, especially after a route result appears geographically implausible or its endpoint labels do not match the requested cities.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Gates Clearly
skills.principle: When a map-editing action redirects to a login page, recognize authentication as a prerequisite. If credentials are unavailable, explain that the user must log in or use the visible “Sign Up”/“Register now” option, then describe that the editor becomes available afterward. Do not claim the location was added.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap editing tasks when selecting “Edit” leads to a login form and no usable username or password is provided.

skills.title: Verify Credentials Before Editing
skills.principle: Before attempting a protected map edit, authenticate with known, authorized credentials. If the login form reports rejected details, stop guessing passwords; use the documented recovery or registration path, or request valid credentials. Proceed to the editor only after a successful redirect or authenticated UI confirms access.
skills.when_to_apply: When selecting OpenStreetMap’s Edit entry leads to a Login page and no verified credentials are available, especially after an explicit authentication failure.

skills.title: Authenticate Before Map Editing
skills.principle: When selecting “Edit” redirects to the login page, treat authentication as a prerequisite for changing map data. Use an already authenticated session or an approved credential-entry mechanism, then return to the editor and verify that editing controls are available before modifying the point of interest.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a map-editing action leads to a login form instead of the editor, especially when the task requires changing a point of interest and authentication status is uncertain.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Before Trace Upload
skills.principle: Navigate to “GPS Traces” and select “Upload a trace.” If the site redirects to Login, recognize authentication as a prerequisite, preserve the return path to the upload form, and request the user to authenticate or provide an authorized login step before continuing. After successful authentication, resume the upload flow rather than reporting completion prematurely.
skills.when_to_apply: When uploading a GPS trace on OpenStreetMap and the upload control redirects to a Login form, especially when no authenticated session or credentials are available.

skills.title: Complete Registration Before Trace Upload
skills.principle: When uploading a GPS trace requires authentication, follow the redirected registration flow completely: fill all required account fields, accept both required agreements on the Terms page, verify that “Continue” becomes enabled, and proceed until login returns you to the trace-upload form.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when selecting “Upload a trace” redirects to Login or Sign Up and the account-registration Terms page shows required agreement checkboxes with a disabled Continue button.

skills.title: Verify Diary Availability Before Reading
skills.principle: Open the site's User Diaries section and inspect the resulting page. If it explicitly displays “No diary entries,” treat that as the verified result, report that no entries are available, and stop rather than inventing content or taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read recent diary entries and the diary page is accessible but visibly reports that no entries exist.

skills.title: Handle Authentication-Gated Navigation
skills.principle: Select the target navigation entry and verify the resulting URL and page state. If access redirects to a login page with the target preserved as a referer, authenticate using available credentials, then confirm the destination loads. If credentials are unavailable, report the authentication prerequisite accurately instead of claiming the target page was reached.
skills.when_to_apply: When a requested page is linked publicly but the resulting observation shows a login form and a referer identifying the protected destination.

skills.title: Authenticate Before Protected Navigation
skills.principle: When a protected destination redirects to a login page, stop retrying the destination link. Use the displayed login form with valid credentials, submit Login, and verify that the browser returns to the requested destination. If credentials are unavailable, report the authentication prerequisite instead of repeating navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when selecting a protected action such as OpenStreetMap’s Edit link produces a login page with username/email, password, and Login controls, especially when a return-path parameter preserves the requested destination.

skills.title: Handle Empty GPS Trace Lists
skills.principle: Open the navigation entry labeled “GPS Traces” and verify the destination heading and contents. If the page shows an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet,” report that no traces are available and mention displayed alternatives like uploading a trace or reading help. Once this state is confirmed, terminate without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view public GPS traces and the GPS Traces navigation link is available. Use when the destination page visibly confirms an empty list rather than showing trace entries.

skills.title: Use OpenStreetMap’s Help Page
skills.principle: Select the navigation link labeled “Help” from any OpenStreetMap page. Verify the destination shows “Getting Help” and lists resources such as the Beginners’ Guide, Help Forum, Community forum, IRC, or Wiki, then summarize these options to the user.
skills.when_to_apply: When the user asks for help using OpenStreetMap and the current page exposes a navigation link labeled “Help”; completion is indicated by the “Getting Help” page and its resource links.

skills.title: Use the Site Logo for Home
skills.principle: When starting on another page of OpenStreetMap, activate the branded OpenStreetMap logo link to return to the homepage. Confirm completion by checking that the map interface, map tiles, and exploration controls such as Search, Zoom In, and Zoom Out are visible, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task requires reaching the OpenStreetMap homepage and the current page exposes the site logo link. If the map interface is already visible, confirm the goal directly without navigating further.

skills.title: Search and Select a Map Location
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the map page and locate the Search textbox.
2. Enter the requested location and activate the “Go” button.
3. Review “Search Results,” choose the result matching the intended place or feature, and open it.
4. Confirm the map or details page is centered on the target and shows its identifying information before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring a named location. The map page and its Search textbox must be available; when multiple results appear, select the semantically matching result rather than stopping at the initial result list.

skills.title: Use OpenStreetMap Directions Form
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the map and open “Find directions between two points.”
2. Fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, allowing them to resolve to recognized place names.
3. Keep or select the requested travel mode, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm the Directions panel shows distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for directions between two locations in OpenStreetMap and the map page provides the directions link, From/To fields, travel-mode selector, and Go button.

skills.title: Use Unique Registration Credentials
skills.principle:
1. Fill the sign-up form with a genuinely unused email address and display name, using the same email in both email fields.
2. Submit the form and inspect validation messages.
3. If either value is taken, replace it with another unique value, update its confirmation field, refill any password fields cleared by validation, and resubmit.
4. Confirm registration succeeded from the resulting page state before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a new OpenStreetMap account and the sign-up form reports that an email or display name is already taken, especially if validation clears password fields.

skills.title: Share the Current Map View
skills.principle: If not already viewing the map, navigate to the main map page. Activate the "Share" control, then select the link in the sharing dialog’s textbox so it is ready to copy. Confirm completion when the dialog is open and the shareable link textbox is focused.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requesting the current map view’s shareable link. The prerequisite is access to the map interface; if another page is open, return to the main map first.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose label matches the requested page, activate it, and verify completion by checking the resulting page heading and URL. Once the expected page content is visible, report the relevant information and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a website already displays a navigation menu and the requested informational page is represented by a clearly labeled link, such as Copyright, Help, or About.

skills.title: Verify Route Data Before Reversing
skills.principle: Before using “Reverse Directions,” confirm the “From” and “To” fields contain the intended endpoints. If either is empty, enter and select valid locations first, then click “Reverse Directions” and verify the fields swap. Click “Go” when the task requires recalculating the route, and stop only after the reversed endpoints or route result is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions form when reversing an existing route. The prerequisite is a populated, recognized origin and destination; an empty field or unchanged route state requires correction before reversal.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Redirects
skills.principle: When a protected navigation link redirects to a login page, treat the redirect as confirmation of an authentication prerequisite. Use the displayed login form if valid credentials are available; otherwise report that access is blocked and request credentials instead of repeatedly clicking the same link.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a requested page is linked in navigation but selecting it produces a login page whose URL or content preserves the requested destination as a referer.

skills.title: Use Navigation Labels Directly
skills.principle: Identify the requested section from the page’s accessible navigation labels, activate its link, then verify the destination heading or URL matches the requested section. Report the observed content, including an explicit empty-state message when the section contains no entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to inspect a named section and the current page exposes that section as a clearly labeled navigation link.

skills.title: Recover From Empty Browser Actions
skills.principle: When a browser action returns an empty-action error, do not repeat the same malformed payload. Re-issue a valid action using the observed link’s accessible label or destination URL, then verify navigation by checking the page heading or URL changed to the requested section.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the target link is visible in the accessibility tree but click attempts repeatedly produce empty-action errors and the page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Success
skills.principle: Once the target page is reached, verify the page title, URL, or distinctive content matches the task. Then report completion and terminate immediately; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree already shows the requested destination and its identifying heading, URL, or content.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Help Page
skills.principle: Navigate to the site’s Help link, verify the destination heading and available resources, then summarize the observed content and terminate. Do not open an individual external resource unless the task explicitly requires deeper exploration.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore or review a website’s Help section and the Help page is visibly loaded with its heading and resource links.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Help Content
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested Help section and inspect its visible headings, links, and descriptions. Once the page clearly contains the requested resources and the full relevant content is observed, report completion and terminate instead of opening optional external resources or continuing to scroll unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks you to explore or review a site section, and the target page is loaded with its relevant content visible, especially when no specific subsection or external resource was requested.

skills.title: Systematically Explore Map Layers
skills.principle:
1. Open the main map and activate the Layers control.
2. Select each listed base style in turn, confirming the map refreshes after each selection.
3. Toggle any enabled overlay and verify its checkbox becomes checked and overlay tiles appear.
4. Record disabled overlays and their stated prerequisite, such as zooming in, rather than attempting them prematurely.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or compare map styles and overlays, provided the map page exposes a Layers control and accessibility observations show selectable styles, checkboxes, or prerequisite messages.

skills.title: Use the Map View Layer Control
skills.principle: Navigate from non-map pages to the site's main map view using the logo or home navigation. Locate the map's layer/style control, open it, and select the requested layers or rendering styles. Confirm completion by checking that the selected options are visibly enabled and the map rendering changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks to view or switch map layers/styles but the current page is a list, help, or other content page without map controls.

skills.title: Calculate Car Route Travel Time
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature and identify the “From,” “To,” travel-mode selector, and “Go” controls.
2. Enter the requested origin and destination, ensuring the travel mode is set to “Car (OSRM)” or the equivalent car option.
3. Select “Go,” then read the resulting Directions summary; report the displayed “Time” value once a route and duration appear.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for driving time between two named places, when the map provides a directions form with origin, destination, travel-mode, and route submission controls.

skills.title: Read Map Scale Directly
skills.principle: When the map is visible, inspect the accessibility tree for scale-bar text, typically showing metric and imperial distances. Report the displayed scale values directly, and optionally use the map URL’s zoom parameter as supporting context. Do not infer scale from map content or navigate elsewhere once the indicators are present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-scale requests when a rendered map and its accessibility-tree scale text are available. If starting on a non-map page, navigate to the main map view first, then inspect the resulting page state.

skills.title: Report Visible Map Scale
skills.principle: Read the scale-bar labels already exposed in the map accessibility tree, including both distance units when present. State the observed scale as the task result, then terminate; do not repeatedly issue no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check a map’s current scale and the accessibility tree visibly contains scale-bar text such as kilometer or mile labels.

skills.title: Use About for Contributor Information
skills.principle: Open the map site's “About” page when asked who contributes to the project. Read the “Community Driven” or equivalent section, identify contributor categories and their role, then summarize only information visibly supported by the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for factual questions about a map project's contributors when the current page offers an “About” navigation link and the answer is likely documented in project overview content.

skills.title: Answer From Relevant Page Content
skills.principle: When the current page already states the requested information, extract and report it directly. For contributor questions, use the page’s descriptive text identifying contributor groups; do not treat section headings or surrounding prose as controls unless the accessibility tree marks them as links or buttons. Navigate only if the needed information is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on informational pages where visible text directly answers the task, especially when headings or paragraphs resemble clickable elements but are not exposed as links or buttons.

skills.title: Enter Route Endpoints Separately
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, use “Find directions between two points” first, then enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To” separately.
