Keep “Car (OSRM)” selected, click “Go,” and only report a time after the directions result visibly appears. Do not reuse or search through the map’s general Search field once on the directions page.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting driving time between two places and the directions page provides distinct “From,” “To,” transport-mode, and “Go” controls. Verify both endpoint fields are populated before submitting.

skills.title: Verify Empty Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested content section using its semantic navigation label. Inspect the resulting page for an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries.” If present, treat the request as complete and report that no matching content is currently available; do not search unrelated sections or perform unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view updates or records in a site section and the page provides navigation plus a clear empty-state message after selection.

skills.title: Stop When Diaries Are Empty
skills.principle: Open the User Diaries page and inspect its content. If it explicitly shows “No diary entries,” treat that as the terminal result, report that no contributor updates are available, and stop instead of exploring unrelated Communities, History, Help, or RSS pages.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view contributor diary updates and the User Diaries page is accessible but displays an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries.”

skills.title: Recover From Ineffective Navigation Clicks
skills.principle:
1. After clicking a navigation entry, verify the current URL and page heading in the next accessibility tree.
2. If the page remains unchanged, navigate directly to the destination URL exposed by the entry.
3. On the destination page, use the visible community link list to identify a relevant group and share its displayed URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When exploring communities or similar directory pages, especially if clicking a labeled navigation link leaves the accessibility tree and URL unchanged; the destination URL must be visible in the current page structure.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Communities
skills.principle: For a broad request to explore communities, open the site’s “Communities” navigation entry and verify the resulting page contains community categories or group listings. Once that page is displayed, treat exploration as complete and report it; do not open an individual external community unless the user requests a specific group.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task asks to explore or find communities generally, and the Communities page is visible with relevant sections, lists, or links.

skills.title: Use Map View For Style Changes
skills.principle: For a map-display style task, avoid the authenticated Edit workflow. Navigate to the site’s main map view, open its map-style or layer control, select the requested style, and verify the map visibly updates. If Edit redirects to login, return to the map view rather than requesting credentials.
skills.when_to_apply: When a non-map page offers an Edit link but the task only changes visual map rendering, especially when selecting Edit immediately redirects to a login page.

skills.title: Enable Map Overlays Through Layers
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, locate the requested overlay in the overlays section, and select its checkbox when unchecked. Confirm completion by verifying the checkbox is checked and, when available, that overlay-specific map tiles or visuals have loaded; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring a named overlay, when the map is already open and a “Layers” control is available. Verify the overlay’s current checked state before clicking to avoid disabling an already-enabled layer.

skills.title: Reevaluate After Navigation
skills.principle: After each navigation action, re-read the current accessibility tree instead of relying on earlier page assumptions. When the map page appears, dismiss any blocking welcome dialog, open the “Layers” control, enable “Public GPS Traces,” and verify the layer is selected or visible on the map.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task begins on a non-map page and navigation may change the available controls. The current observation must show the map and its layer control before attempting overlay actions.

skills.title: Compare Map Styles Systematically
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and inspect each available style individually. After selecting a style, verify the rendered map for the requested feature rather than inferring from the style name. If no listed style visibly provides the feature, report that limitation and suggest a specialized mapping service.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task asks which visual layer or style best displays a specific feature and the map offers a “Layers” or equivalent style selector.

skills.title: Navigate to the Relevant Map View
skills.principle: First verify that the current page supports the requested capability. For map-style comparisons, leave unrelated sections such as GPS traces, Help, or About and use the site logo or map entry to reach the actual map view. Then locate the map’s layer/style control, switch styles, and compare the displayed transportation features.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task opens on an unrelated informational or data-management page and the accessibility tree lacks map controls, layers, or style options.

skills.title: Find Public Map Layer Controls First
skills.principle: When a map-layer task starts on a non-map page, search available public map views or navigation entries for layer controls before entering an authenticated editor. If one route redirects to login, treat that route as restricted and continue checking other accessible map pages; report a credential prerequisite only after confirming no public route exposes the requested controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the current page lacks a map or layer controls and an editor link redirects to login, especially when the task only requires viewing or comparing map layers.

skills.title: Use the Direct Copyright Navigation Link
skills.principle: When a site’s navigation visibly contains a link matching the requested information, activate that semantic link rather than searching elsewhere. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading, URL meaning, and relevant content. Once the requested information page is clearly displayed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational tasks when the accessibility tree shows a directly labeled navigation link for the requested topic and the destination can be verified from the resulting page.

skills.title: Verify Copyright Page Then Stop
skills.principle: Open the navigation entry labeled “Copyright,” then verify the resulting page shows the “Copyright and License” heading and relevant license text. Once the target content is visibly loaded, report completion and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view copyright or license information and the page offers a clearly labeled Copyright navigation link. Confirm the destination heading or content before ending the task.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Help Page
skills.principle: When asked to get help with OpenStreetMap, select the main “Help” navigation entry and verify the resulting page shows the “Getting Help” heading and assistance resources. Once that destination is displayed, treat the task as complete and stop instead of opening a specific forum or external resource.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to broad help-navigation requests when the site’s main Help page lists multiple support options and no specific resource, forum, or question topic is requested.

skills.title: Use Only User-Provided Login Credentials
skills.principle: On a login page, click “Log In,” then fill the username and password fields only with credentials supplied by the user or securely available in context. Never invent example credentials. Submit the “Login” form and verify success through a redirect or authenticated navigation. If an error says the details are invalid, request corrected credentials or use password recovery instead of repeatedly refocusing the field.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests account login but the username or password is missing, or after the page reports invalid credentials. The login form and its “Login” button must be visible.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Redirects
skills.principle:
1. Activate the target navigation link and inspect the resulting page.
2. If it redirects to a login form, authenticate using credentials already provided or available in the task context.
3. Submit the form and verify that the browser returns to the requested page; if credentials are unavailable, report the authentication prerequisite accurately.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a requested map-editing or other protected page redirects to a login screen instead of displaying the target content.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Redirects
skills.principle: When selecting a protected map-editing feature redirects to a login page, treat authentication as a prerequisite. Use available account credentials, submit the login form, and verify that the browser returns to the requested Edit page before reporting success. If credentials are unavailable, clearly report the access blocker rather than claiming navigation completed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an Edit or other protected navigation link redirects to a login form with username/email and password fields, especially when the redirect preserves the original destination.

skills.title: Recover from Malformed Link Actions
skills.principle: When a visible link is the intended target, submit a complete, valid click action using its current accessibility reference and button syntax. If the tool reports an empty or malformed action, stop repeating the same payload; use the link’s observed destination URL instead, then verify that the page title or content changed as expected.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap help or resource pages when a target link is visible but click attempts return parsing or empty-action errors. Ensure the destination URL is present in the current accessibility tree before navigating directly.

skills.title: Locate the Map Directions Interface
skills.principle: When a GPS-trace page does not expose routing, navigate to the site's map or directions interface, then enter both requested points in the origin and destination fields. Submit the route request and verify that directions or a route result is displayed before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when asked for directions but the current map site page is a secondary section such as GPS traces and no origin/destination controls are visible.

skills.title: Verify Empty List States
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested collection using its labeled navigation link. Inspect the resulting page for an explicit empty-state heading or message; if present, report that no items are available instead of attempting further item actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view or browse a collection and the page provides a clearly labeled navigation entry. Confirm completion when the destination shows an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries.”

skills.title: Search and Share Map URL
skills.principle: Enter the requested place in the map's Search field and activate Go. Confirm the page title, map view, or URL reflects the requested location, then share the current URL directly. The URL's map fragment preserves the resulting center and zoom.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to share a map link for a named place and the map application provides a Search field and Go control. Share only after the resulting page visibly centers on or identifies the requested place.

skills.title: Navigate to User Diaries
skills.principle: From the map homepage, select the navigation link labeled “User Diaries.” On the diary page, verify the heading and inspect the content: report the entries if listed, or report that none are available when “No diary entries” is shown.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view OpenStreetMap users’ diary entries and the map homepage displays the “User Diaries” navigation link.

skills.title: Use the Map Share Control
skills.principle:
1. Locate the map control explicitly labeled “Share,” rather than an adjacent unlabeled link.
2. Activate it and inspect the resulting share panel or updated URL.
3. Copy the generated map link, or copy the address-bar URL if the map state is encoded there, then provide that link to the requester.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to share a map view and the page exposes a labeled “Share” control. Verify that a share panel or map URL appears before reporting completion.

skills.title: Recognize Existing Directions Results
skills.principle: When the map page already shows the requested endpoints and a populated “Directions” table with numbered steps, treat the task as complete. Report that the directions are displayed and terminate; do not repeatedly issue noop actions or submit the route again.
skills.when_to_apply: For map direction requests when the current page visibly contains matching From/To values and a Directions section with route summary and step-by-step instructions.

skills.title: Target Actual Direction Inputs
skills.principle: On the directions page, identify controls by their accessible role and label, not nearby marker images. Fill both the actual “From” and “To” textboxes with the requested coordinates, verify both values remain populated, then choose the requested travel mode and click “Go.” Confirm that route details or step-by-step instructions appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting directions in OpenStreetMap or similar map UIs where marker images and textboxes appear together, especially after an element action reports that the target is not editable.

skills.title: Open Map History and Verify Results
skills.principle: From the map page, select the navigation link labeled “History.” If an editor menu opens instead, select the separate “History” link rather than an editor option. Confirm the destination by checking for the “Changesets” heading and its result text, then report whether changesets are present or absent.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view history for the currently displayed map area and the map interface exposes a navigation link labeled “History.”

skills.title: Generate Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” control.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To”; keep the travel mode set to “Car” when driving is requested.
3. Click “Go” and verify a “Directions” heading with route summary and turn-by-turn instructions appears.
4. Stop once the directions list is displayed and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting driving directions between two places, after the directions form is available and both locations can be entered as searchable place names.

skills.title: Fill Both Direction Endpoints
skills.principle:
1. Open the dedicated directions interface before entering route locations.
2. Fill the From field with the origin and the To field with the destination; do not rely on the map’s general Search box.
3. Keep the requested travel mode, then click the directions form’s Go button.
4. Confirm that a route summary or turn-by-turn instruction list appears before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when requesting a route on OpenStreetMap and the directions page exposes separate From, To, travel-mode, and Go controls. Both endpoint fields must contain valid locations before submission.

skills.title: Inspect Directions Mode Options
skills.principle: On a map directions page, locate the transportation-mode combobox and inspect its currently visible options. Expand it when necessary to reveal the complete list, then report each available mode exactly as labeled. No route recalculation is needed when the task only asks which modes are available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked what transportation modes a mapping site supports for directions and a directions page with a mode selector is already open or accessible.

skills.title: Report Findings After Confirmation
skills.principle: When the directions page exposes transportation modes in its combobox, read all listed options and report them directly. Selecting every option is unnecessary; once the complete list is visible, provide the answer and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for information-seeking map tasks where the requested values are already visible in a directions-mode dropdown and no route calculation is required.

skills.title: Submit a Complete Final Message
skills.principle: After identifying the routing engine, send one syntactically complete user message with properly escaped quotes and a closed action call. Do not repeat malformed or truncated actions; verify the payload is non-empty before submitting. Report the engine using the selected routing-mode label and, when available, corroborate it with URL parameters or attribution.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions page visibly shows the routing mode or engine in a combobox, URL, or attribution, especially after a prior message action failed with an empty or malformed payload.

skills.title: Format Completion Messages Correctly
skills.principle: When the page already exposes the requested fact, send one valid completion message directly. Use a complete, properly escaped string with balanced quotes; do not embed unfinished JSON or truncate the action payload. After the message is accepted, stop rather than repeatedly retrying the same malformed action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map page visibly identifies the requested routing engine through attribution, the selected routing mode, or URL parameters, and the task only requires reporting that information.

skills.title: Change Route Transportation Mode
skills.principle: On a directions page, inspect the transportation-mode combobox and choose the requested option using the dropdown’s selection control. If clicking an individual option fails because it is not visible, use `select_option` on the combobox with the option label. Confirm completion when the combobox value and route engine update, and the directions summary refreshes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map directions route already has origin and destination fields populated and the task requests switching between modes such as Car, Bicycle, or Foot.

skills.title: Stop After Opening History
skills.principle: Click the map application's “History” navigation entry, then verify the destination shows the “Changesets” heading. Once the History page is displayed—even if it reports “No changesets in this area”—the viewing task is complete; report completion and stop instead of zooming, searching, or opening unrelated results.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view map-change history and the History navigation entry is available. Treat the loaded Changesets page, including an explicit empty-state message, as sufficient completion unless the task requests specific changesets.

skills.title: Verify Target Mode Before Continuing
skills.principle: After selecting the requested transportation mode, re-read the original task and inspect the combobox value and route state. If they show the requested mode, treat the task as complete, report success, and stop. Do not infer a reversed goal from later observations or perform additional mode changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map direction pages when a transportation-mode selection immediately updates the combobox, URL, or directions. The prerequisite is a clear requested mode to compare against the observed state.

skills.title: Generate Car Route Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's “Find directions between two points” page.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To,” allowing each place to resolve to a recognized location.
3. Verify the travel mode is “Car (OSRM)” and click “Go.”
4. Confirm completion when a “Directions” panel displays route details such as distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap directions tasks requiring a driving route between two named places, when the directions form provides “From,” “To,” a travel-mode selector, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Verify Navigation After Click Timeout
skills.principle: When a download or external-link click reports a navigation timeout, first inspect the current page or open tabs to determine whether navigation already completed. If the destination loaded, verify its download or export state and stop; otherwise retry the intended link or choose an appropriate fallback. Do not assume the click failed solely because the wait timed out.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on export or download pages when clicking a link produces a timeout during scheduled-navigation waiting, especially when the log indicates the click action completed.

skills.title: Handle External Download Timeouts
skills.principle: When an export-page alternative link reports a timeout after the click action completed, treat navigation or download as potentially in progress. Verify the resulting URL, new page, or download state before acting again; do not repeatedly click the same link or switch alternatives without evidence it failed. If verification confirms no download, use a smaller bounding box or an appropriate bulk-download source.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map export pages when direct export is rejected as too large and an external source link produces a timeout after the click was performed.

skills.title: Switch OpenStreetMap Layer Style
skills.principle:
1. Open the map's “Layers” control.
2. In the “Map Layers” panel, select the list item labeled with the requested style, such as “Humanitarian.”
3. Confirm completion by checking that the URL or map attribution reflects the selected style, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap map pages when the task requests changing the base-map display style and a visible “Layers” control is available.

skills.title: Stop After Layer Confirmation
skills.principle: Open the Layers menu and select the target map style. Confirm completion from observable state, such as the map tiles changing, attribution updating, or the URL gaining the style parameter. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly reopening the menu or clicking the already-selected style.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing an OpenStreetMap map display style through Layers, especially after the target style is reflected in the URL, tile sources, or attribution.

skills.title: Switch Map Styles Through URL Layers
skills.principle: When the map-style control is unavailable, preserve the route URL and append the map’s layer parameter to the hash to load the alternate style (for example, Standard plus CyclOSM). Wait for tiles to load, then verify the same route remains displayed before reporting that both styles are available for comparison.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions pages when the current route is already displayed but the Layers control or style selector is inaccessible, missing the requested style, or repeatedly times out.

skills.title: Verify Empty Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Open the requested content using its semantic navigation link, then inspect the destination for both item listings and explicit empty-state text. If the page states that no items exist, report that the requested content was accessed but nothing is available, and mention any offered alternatives only when relevant.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when browsing a site section such as public GPS traces and the destination page may contain no records. Confirm the page heading and empty-state message before concluding the browse task.

skills.title: Dismiss Overlays Before Switching Map Styles
skills.principle:
1. If a welcome dialog or sidebar overlays the map, activate its visible “Close” control first.
2. Open “Layers” only after the map controls are unobstructed.
3. In the “Map Layers” panel, click the “CyclOSM” option or its list item; do not use select_option on the “Layers” link.
4. Confirm the map tiles change while the current route and viewport remain unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When comparing a route across Standard and CyclOSM in OpenStreetMap and the accessibility tree shows a welcome modal, pointer interception, or a “Map Layers” panel.

skills.title: Find Alternative OSM Download Sources
skills.principle: Navigate from the OpenStreetMap map to the Export page. If the page indicates the selected area is too large for XML export, inspect the listed alternatives: Overpass API for a bounding box, Planet OSM for the complete database, Geofabrik Downloads for regional extracts, and Other Sources for additional options. Report the visible source names and their purposes once the list is present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for alternative OpenStreetMap data downloads, especially when the Export page warns that the selected area is too large for direct XML export.

skills.title: Use Export Page Sources Directly
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, open the Export page and read the alternative-source description list directly. Report each listed source and its stated scope. Do not open individual external links unless the task explicitly requires deeper details; if navigation times out, rely on the already visible labels and descriptions and finish.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which alternative OpenStreetMap download sources are available and the Export page visibly lists source names with descriptions.

skills.title: Read Export Bounding-Box Coordinates
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, open the Export page when the current view is not an export interface. Read the four displayed bounding-box fields in order: northern latitude, western longitude, eastern longitude, and southern latitude. Report the area as the two diagonal corners: (north latitude, west longitude) and (south latitude, east longitude).
skills.when_to_apply: Use for tasks asking for the currently selected export area’s coordinates, after the Export page is visible and its coordinate textboxes contain values.

skills.title: Use the Correct Export Control
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, activate the navigation link labeled “Export,” not the adjacent “Edit” dropdown button. After navigation, inspect the export page for the selected area’s bounding-coordinate fields and report those values only after verifying the page changed successfully.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for coordinates of the current export area and the map header contains both an “Edit” control and an “Export” link. Use accessible labels or roles rather than nearby element IDs.

skills.title: Handle Empty Trace Listings Directly
skills.principle: Navigate to the site's GPS Traces section and inspect its result state. If it shows an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the browse request as completed with no available traces; report that result and stop instead of exploring unrelated sections or help pages.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse user-uploaded GPS traces and the GPS Traces page is reachable but displays an explicit empty-state message, especially when no specific trace or upload action was requested.

skills.title: Keep Export Areas Within Limits
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, use the bounding-coordinate fields to define a different area when map dragging is obstructed. Change at least one boundary, keep the box valid and modest in size, then select Export. Verify the resulting page does not report that the request exceeds the node limit; if it does, return and reduce the bounding box before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When manually selecting a different OpenStreetMap export area, especially when the existing selection overlay intercepts map clicks or the export response reports too many nodes.

skills.title: Choose a Small Export Bounding Box
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, use the four bounding-box coordinate fields to define a genuinely different, compact area. Change values rather than re-entering existing ones, verify north exceeds south and east exceeds west, then click “Export.” If the result reports too many nodes, return and reduce the box before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When manually selecting a different OpenStreetMap export area, especially after the page displays a default bounding box or an export fails because the requested area exceeds the node limit.

skills.title: Reduce Export Area Before Retrying
skills.principle:
1. After selecting the requested map style, open Export and inspect the proposed bounding box.
2. If the area is broad or export reports the 50,000-node limit, return to the map and choose “Manually select a different area.”
3. Select a smaller bounding box, export again, and verify that the data download succeeds rather than showing an API error.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting OpenStreetMap data through the Export page, especially for a large visible region or after seeing “too many nodes”; the map style must already be set as requested.

skills.title: Verify Export Readiness Before Proceeding
skills.principle: When the export page reports that the area is too large, reduce the bounding box through zooming or manual area selection. After each change, inspect the page for the enabled “Export” button; click it once it appears, rather than repeatedly reopening the Export page or zooming without verification. Confirm the resulting download or completion state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap export tasks when the export panel shows an oversized-area warning and offers zoom controls, manual area selection, or alternative download sources.

skills.title: Verify GPS Traces Page State
skills.principle: Select the navigation link labeled “GPS Traces,” then verify the destination by its page heading and URL. Report the observable contents, including an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet” and available upload or help options; stop once access is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access GPS traces in OpenStreetMap and the current page exposes a semantic “GPS Traces” navigation link. Use the page’s heading and visible state to confirm completion.

skills.title: Stop When Empty State Confirms Result
skills.principle: When a target page explicitly shows an empty state such as “Nothing here yet,” treat that as the observed result. Report that no items are available and stop. Do not repeatedly follow upload, refresh, or navigation links unless the task explicitly requires creating data and the necessary authentication or inputs are available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when accessing a listing page such as public GPS traces and the accessibility tree shows an explicit empty-state message with no records. Verify the page title or section matches the requested resource first.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the navigation entry whose accessible name matches the requested destination, activate it, then verify the resulting URL and page heading/content before reporting completion. If the page is already at that destination, skip navigation and confirm its recognizable resources directly.
skills.when_to_apply: When a website task requests opening a named section and the accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link or the destination is already visibly loaded.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: If the requested destination is already visible, verify it using the page heading, title, or URL. Otherwise, activate the clearly labeled navigation control and recheck the resulting page. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree shows either a direct destination link or evidence that the requested page is already open.

skills.title: Select Route Mode Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Identify the directions page’s transportation-mode combobox and the requested option.
2. For a native select, use `select_option` on the combobox rather than clicking an individual option, which may be invisible.
3. Click “Go” to apply the selection and recalculate directions.
4. Confirm the combobox shows the requested mode and the route summary has updated before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing travel mode on an OpenStreetMap directions page, especially when accessibility-tree options appear but direct option clicks time out.

skills.title: Verify Mode Then Stop
skills.principle: On the directions page, select the requested transportation mode and verify the combobox value shows that mode as selected. If the task only asks to change the mode, report completion immediately. Click “Go” only when route recalculation is required, then confirm a route result before stopping; do not repeat waits or issue malformed selections.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a route’s transportation mode in a map directions form, especially after the accessibility tree already shows the requested option selected.

skills.title: Use the Show My Location Control
skills.principle: On a map page, locate the control labeled “Show My Location” and activate it. After the control is triggered and the map remains displayed, report that the current location is being shown and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task asks to display the user’s current position and the map accessibility tree exposes a “Show My Location” button or equivalent location-control label.

skills.title: Verify Location Display Before Reporting
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then verify a location marker, recentered map, or other visible state change. If the map remains unchanged, address any blocking popup or location-permission requirement and retry. Report completion only after the location is visibly displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to show the current location on an interactive map and the location control is available. Use especially when clicking it produces no accessibility-tree change or other confirmation.

skills.title: Switch Map Layer Through Layers Menu
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, select the list item labeled with the requested map style, then verify the map refreshes with that style’s tiles or a corresponding layer indicator in the URL. Once confirmed, report completion without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap map pages when a task requests changing the visual map style and the accessibility tree exposes a “Layers” control and named style options.

skills.title: Select and Verify Map Layer
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and choose the requested layer from the “Map Layers” list, not the directions routing-mode combobox. Verify success by checking that map tiles or attribution reflect the selected layer, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a visible map style or layer, especially on OpenStreetMap pages containing both a Layers control and a separate routing-mode combobox.

skills.title: Verify Diary Page Empty State
skills.principle: Open the map site's “User Diaries” navigation entry, then inspect the resulting page for diary content. If the page displays “No diary entries,” report that no community updates are available and stop; do not continue navigating or speculate about login requirements.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read community diary updates on OpenStreetMap and the diary page is accessible. Apply after navigation succeeds and the page’s heading or content confirms whether entries exist.

skills.title: Verify Empty States Before Continuing
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested content page and inspect its main status message. If it explicitly reports an empty state such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the task as complete insofar as possible, report that no items are available, and mention the prerequisite action shown by the page (such as uploading an item) instead of repeatedly switching pages.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or retrieve content from a site, especially after navigating between related pages, and the destination page visibly reports that no records or uploads exist.

skills.title: Revalidate Targets After Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Use the exact action syntax required by the browser tool; malformed payloads produce empty-action errors.
2. After every navigation, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree and select controls by their current role and label, not stale bids.
3. Confirm the destination URL or heading matches the request before acting again; once the target page is displayed, stop instead of clicking a reused identifier.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating through accessibility-tree pages where element IDs change after page loads, especially after recovering from an action-format error or reaching a page that already satisfies the task.

skills.title: Stop After Community Listing
skills.principle: Open the “Communities” navigation entry and inspect its categorized listings, such as “Local Chapters” and “Other Groups.” Once the page visibly presents communities from multiple regions, treat exploration as complete and report success instead of opening an individual external community link.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for broad OpenStreetMap community-exploration tasks when the Communities page is accessible and visibly lists groups across countries or regions.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Communities Directory
skills.principle: When the OpenStreetMap Communities page displays worldwide groups, treat the task as completed: inspect its headings and listed community links, then report that the directory was found. Do not open an arbitrary external community unless the user requests details about a specific group.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a broad exploration request leads to the Communities page and its accessible tree shows categorized local chapters or other groups with multiple regional links.

skills.title: Handle Empty Diary Results
skills.principle: After opening User Diaries, inspect the page for diary entries. If the explicit empty-state message “No diary entries” appears, report that no community updates are available and terminate; do not repeatedly wait or poll without a task requirement to monitor live changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When a browsing task asks you to read a list of community updates and the destination page visibly displays an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Calculate Coordinate Route
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the origin coordinates in “From” and destination coordinates in “To”; retain or select the requested travel mode.
3. Click “Go” and verify the Directions panel displays both “Distance” and “Time”.
4. Report those values exactly as shown, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting distance and estimated travel time between two coordinates when the directions page provides “From”, “To”, travel-mode selection, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Report Visible Route Results
skills.principle: When the Directions panel visibly contains the requested route metrics, extract the distance and estimated time, provide them in the final response, and terminate immediately. Do not repeat no-op actions after the result is already confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to map-routing tasks when the requested origin and destination are set and the page visibly shows a completed Directions result containing distance and time.

skills.title: Read Existing Route Directions
skills.principle: When a map page already shows the requested origin and destination, use the displayed Directions panel instead of recalculating. Extract the ordered maneuver text and distances, include total distance and travel time when visible, and report the final destination step. Confirm the displayed endpoints match the request before responding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction tasks when the page visibly contains a Directions panel with matching origin and destination fields and an ordered route table.

skills.title: Report Directions After Route Generation
skills.principle: Enter the origin and destination, click “Go,” then inspect the resulting “Directions” section. Once the page shows the route summary and ordered maneuver table, extract those steps and immediately provide them to the user instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map direction tasks after both route fields are populated and the route result visibly contains a “Directions” heading with ordered steps or a destination-reached entry.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested destination, then verify the page heading or URL confirms arrival. Once confirmed—even if the page reports no available entries—report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task reaches a page whose heading or URL clearly matches the requested destination, including pages with empty-content messages such as “No diary entries.”

skills.title: Apply And Verify Route Reversal
skills.principle:
1. On the directions page, use the labeled “Reverse Directions” control to swap the origin and destination.
2. Click “Go” to recalculate and apply the reversed route.
3. Verify the From and To fields are exchanged and the directions panel reflects the updated route before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map directions task requests reversing an existing route and the page provides “Reverse Directions” plus a separate “Go” or recalculate control.

skills.title: Verify Reversed Route Before Continuing
skills.principle:
1. Click the map’s “Reverse Directions” control once.
2. Verify that the From and To fields have swapped and the route URL or directions panel reflects the reversed order.
3. If the control fails, fill both endpoint fields with swapped values, click “Go,” and verify the updated route.
4. Once the reversed route is confirmed, stop instead of repeatedly clicking.
skills.when_to_apply: When reversing an existing OpenStreetMap directions route, especially after the page updates but before the endpoint fields or directions panel confirm the requested reversal.

skills.title: Verify Transportation Mode After Selection
skills.principle: Select the requested transportation option in the directions combobox, then inspect the updated page before taking further action. Confirm the combobox value and resulting route engine or directions reflect the chosen mode; if already updated, report completion without clicking additional controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map directions pages when changing travel mode. The origin and destination must already be correct, and completion is indicated by the selected mode plus a refreshed route or directions matching that mode.

skills.title: Stop After Route Confirmation
skills.principle:
1. Enter the origin and destination in the directions form, select the requested transportation mode, and click “Go.”
2. Verify completion from the resulting page: the mode remains selected, the route URL reflects the requested endpoints, and a “Directions” panel appears.
3. Once these indicators are present, report completion and terminate; do not issue unnecessary waits or additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap directions tasks after submitting a route. Stop when the selected mode and requested route are reflected in the resulting URL and a Directions panel with route details is visible.

skills.title: Use Already-Displayed Route Directions
skills.principle: When the map page already shows the requested origin, destination, travel mode, and a populated table under the “Directions” heading, treat the task as complete. Report that the turn-by-turn directions are available there, then terminate without re-submitting the route or performing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For map direction tasks when the current accessibility tree visibly confirms matching route fields, travel mode, and turn-by-turn instructions.

skills.title: Use Direction Form Inputs Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the dedicated directions page rather than using the general map search for route requests.
2. Fill the actual "From" and "To" textboxes with the endpoints; do not target nearby marker images.
3. Keep the travel mode set to "Car (OSRM)" and click the directions "Go" button.
4. Confirm that route details or turn-by-turn instructions appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests routing between two places and the directions page exposes labeled "From" and "To" inputs, a travel-mode selector, and a "Go" button.

skills.title: Retrieve Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's “Find directions between two points” tool.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To”; keep or select the requested travel mode, such as “Car (OSRM)”.
3. Click “Go” and verify the page displays a “Directions” heading with turn-by-turn route steps.
4. Report the listed streets and turns in order, including the destination step.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking how to travel between two named places, when the directions tool exposes origin and destination fields and a selectable travel mode.

skills.title: Use Dedicated Directions Fields
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature and fill its dedicated “From” and “To” fields with the origin and destination; do not reuse the map search box.
2. Select the requested travel mode, then click the directions-page “Go” button.
3. Verify that route instructions or street names appear in the directions panel before reporting results; do not interact with decorative map tiles.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map search redirects to a separate directions page showing “From,” “To,” travel-mode controls, and “Go,” especially when route details are not yet present in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use the Actual Transportation Combobox
skills.principle: Identify the transportation-mode combobox by its observed role and current value, not a nearby button’s identifier. Select the requested mode, then verify the combobox value and refreshed route state reflect that mode before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a route’s travel mode in OpenStreetMap directions or similar map pages, especially when accessibility-tree IDs for the combobox and submit button are adjacent or easy to confuse.

skills.title: Complete Directions Inputs Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
2. Select the requested transportation mode, such as “Foot (OSRM)”.
3. Click “Go” only after both endpoint fields contain the intended places, then verify that route results or map directions appear.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap direction tasks whenever the directions form shows empty or unverified “From” and “To” fields; a mode selection alone does not create a route.

skills.title: Reverse and Recalculate a Route
skills.principle:
1. On the directions page, use the “Reverse Directions” control to swap the existing origin and destination.
2. Verify the “From” and “To” fields now match the requested direction.
3. Click “Go” to recalculate the route, then confirm the directions panel reflects the swapped endpoints before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map already displays directions but the requested travel direction is the opposite, and the page provides “Reverse Directions” plus a route submission control.

skills.title: Verify Reversed Route Before Acting Again
skills.principle: Click “Reverse Directions” once, then inspect the updated “From” and “To” fields and route summary. Confirm that the origin and destination are swapped and the directions list reflects the requested route. Once confirmed, stop; button focus alone is not evidence of failure, and clicking again reverses the route back.
skills.when_to_apply: When reversing an existing map route and the page visibly updates after the first click. Use the displayed endpoint fields or route URL as confirmation before taking further actions.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Targets Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to match the requested link by its visible label and role, not by a guessed or stale element ID. After clicking, verify the page title, URL path, or content confirms the destination; once confirmed, stop rather than repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When several nearby navigation controls have similar structure or element identifiers, especially on map pages where overlays can intercept clicks. Reinspect the current tree after any click error before retrying.

skills.title: Show Current Location on Route
skills.principle: When a route is already displayed, activate the map’s “Show My Location” control rather than rebuilding the route. Confirm the map displays a current-location marker alongside the route, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking to compare the user’s position with an existing route, provided the route is already visible and the map exposes a “Show My Location” control.

skills.title: Verify Location Against Route
skills.principle: After generating the route, explicitly verify that the current-location marker is visible on the same map view as the route. If it is absent, use “Show My Location” and wait for a location result; adjust zoom only as needed. Stop and report only after both the route and location marker are observable, rather than assuming repeated clicks succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring comparison between the user’s current location and a displayed route, especially when geolocation feedback or the location marker is not immediately visible.

skills.title: Enable Map Data Through Layers
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control to reveal base maps and troubleshooting overlays.
2. Locate the “Map Data” checkbox and activate it when unchecked.
3. Confirm completion by verifying “Map Data” shows checked=true or the URL/state reflects the data layer, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires detailed geographic data or a Map Data overlay, and the page exposes a “Layers” control with overlay checkboxes.

skills.title: Inspect Layers Before Declaring Unavailable
skills.principle: When a requested map overlay is not visible, activate the map’s “Layers” control and inspect the expanded layer options before concluding it is unsupported. Select the matching overlay if present, then verify that the map display changes or the layer is marked active. Only report unavailability after checking this control.
skills.when_to_apply: On a map or directions page showing a “Layers” control while the requested overlay is absent from the initial accessibility tree.

skills.title: Retrieve a Route’s Short Link
skills.principle:
1. Confirm the requested route is displayed, then open the map’s “Share” control.
2. In the sharing dialog, select “Short Link.”
3. Verify the generated URL appears in the link textbox, then report that exact URL to the user and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on an OpenStreetMap directions page when the requested origin and destination route is already displayed and the task asks for a shareable short link.

skills.title: Verify Share Control Before Clicking
skills.principle: On a directions map, activate the control explicitly labeled “Share,” not nearby unlabeled map controls. Verify that a share dialog or short-link field appears. If the page changes to an unrelated map workflow such as “New Note,” return to the directions page, restore the route, and retry the labeled Share control.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing a computed route and the map has multiple adjacent controls, especially unlabeled links. The route must already be displayed, and completion requires observing a generated share dialog or short URL.

skills.title: Use Print PDF for Map Directions
skills.principle: When a PDF of displayed directions is requested, keep the directions view active and use its print or browser “Save as PDF” workflow. Do not select OpenStreetMap’s “Export” link: it exports raw map data for a bounding box, not a PDF, and may fail on large areas. Verify the resulting PDF contains the route and directions.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on map direction pages when the route is already displayed and the task requests a PDF or printable map, especially when the page’s “Export” control is clearly data-oriented.

skills.title: Use Share for PDF Map Downloads
skills.principle: On the loaded directions page, open the map’s “Share” control rather than the top-level “Export” page. In the Share panel, set “Format:” to “PDF,” then activate “Download.” Confirm the PDF option remains selected and the download action completes while the intended route is still displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map route is already calculated and the task requests a PDF image of that route. The Share panel must expose an image Format selector containing PDF and a Download button.

skills.title: Handle Editor Authentication Redirects
skills.principle: Select the map site's “Edit” navigation entry. If it redirects to a login page, verify the page shows username/email, password, and Login controls; recognize authentication as a prerequisite, then request the required credentials rather than repeatedly selecting “Edit.”
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a map editor from a public map page and the editor requires authentication, especially when the resulting page is clearly a login form and no credentials are available.

skills.title: Verify Editor Access After Navigation
skills.principle: Use the visible “Edit” navigation entry or its destination URL, but validate the resulting accessibility tree before declaring success. If navigation reaches a login page, treat authentication as a prerequisite and sign in or report that access is blocked; do not infer editor access from the URL alone. After errors, issue a correctly formed action and re-check the page state.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a map editor from a public map page, especially after click or navigation errors, redirects, or authentication prompts. Completion requires visible editor controls or map-editing UI, not merely an editor-like URL.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose accessible name matches the requested page or topic, activate it, then verify the destination through the URL and page heading. Once the target content is visible, extract the relevant sections and report the findings instead of performing unnecessary additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requires visiting a specific informational page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching labeled navigation link. Confirm the destination page and relevant headings before responding.

skills.title: Use About Pages for Mission Details
skills.principle: When a homepage offers a “Learn More” link, open it and inspect the About page. Extract the mission from relevant headings and supporting paragraphs, such as local knowledge, community, and open data. Report a concise synthesis once the required information is visible, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational tasks asking about an organization’s mission or values when the homepage provides a Learn More link or an About navigation entry.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: When the requested page is reached, verify its heading and relevant content in the accessibility tree, then report completion and terminate. Do not continue scrolling or open secondary links unless the task explicitly requests deeper exploration or specific information.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks such as “Explore Communities” when the destination page loads successfully and visibly contains the requested topic.

skills.title: Use the Logo to Return Home
skills.principle: On an OpenStreetMap subpage, activate the top “OpenStreetMap logo OpenStreetMap” link. Confirm navigation by checking that the URL is the site root and the accessibility tree shows homepage controls such as Search, “Where is this?”, and the map view, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks to return to the OpenStreetMap homepage and the current page is a subpage such as directions, editing, history, or export, with the branded logo link visible.

skills.title: Report Findings After Reading
skills.principle: After opening the relevant informational page, extract the main mission points from its visible headings and paragraphs, then provide a concise user-facing summary. Once the summary is ready, submit it as the task output and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for knowledge-seeking tasks where the requested information is visible on an About, Help, or informational page and no further navigation is required.

skills.title: Verify Diary Availability
skills.principle: Open the map site's “User Diaries” navigation entry, then inspect the page heading and content. If it displays “No diary entries,” report that no readable entries are currently available and mention the visible “Log In” option only as a possible access prerequisite, not a confirmed cause.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read other mappers’ diaries and the site provides a “User Diaries” navigation entry. Use the page’s explicit empty-state message to determine whether diary content is available.

skills.title: Stop When Diaries Are Empty
skills.principle: Open the User Diaries section and inspect the page result. If it explicitly shows “No diary entries,” report that no diaries are available and stop; do not repeatedly revisit the page, wait for changes, or substitute unrelated Communities, Help, or History pages unless the user requests an alternative source.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read user diaries and the User Diaries page visibly contains “No diary entries,” with no diary list or entry controls available.

skills.title: Verify Empty Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate through the relevant navigation entry to the target listing page. Confirm the page title or URL matches the requested destination, then inspect the listing content. If an explicit empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet” appears, report that the destination was reached but no items are available, rather than attempting unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task asks you to view or browse all items in a site section and the destination page may legitimately contain no records.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target List
skills.principle: After selecting the task-specific navigation entry, verify the resulting page heading and content. If it shows the requested list—even an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet”—the viewing task is complete. Report completion and stop; do not click upload, help, or unrelated links.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task asks to view or browse a collection and the destination page visibly confirms the collection context, including an explicit empty-state message. Requires no further action unless the requested page failed to load.

skills.title: Use About and Copyright Pages
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's About page to identify contributors, community roles, and collection methods.
2. Follow its Copyright or license link to find authoritative data-source details and attribution requirements.
3. Summarize only claims supported by headings and page text, including individual contributors, institutional sources, licenses, and any relevant restrictions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked about a mapping project's contributors, data origins, or licensing and the site exposes About, Copyright, License, or Contributors navigation links.

skills.title: Stop After Finding the Answer
skills.principle: When the requested information is visible in a relevant page section, extract the needed facts immediately, verify that the section addresses every part of the request, then report completion. Do not keep scrolling or follow supplementary links once sufficient evidence is present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational browsing tasks when a page visibly contains the requested topic, such as a contributors section listing people and data sources, and no required subquestion remains unanswered.

skills.title: Use Verified Credentials for Login
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s login form and fill the username and password only with credentials explicitly provided or securely available to the user.
2. Submit once, then inspect the resulting page for a logged-in state or an explicit authentication error.
3. If authentication fails, do not guess or repeatedly submit placeholder passwords; use the password-recovery flow or ask the user to verify credentials.
skills.when_to_apply: When a login form is available but credentials are missing, unverified, or rejected. The user must provide valid authentication details before submission can succeed.

skills.title: Use OpenStreetMap Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” from the map.
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To”; retain the car routing mode for driving distance.
3. Click “Go” and verify the results panel shows “Distance” before reporting that value, optionally converting units accurately.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for driving distance between two places in OpenStreetMap and the map page exposes the directions link, origin/destination fields, a car mode, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Use Semantic Direction Inputs
skills.principle: On the directions page, target the controls by accessible role and label, not nearby marker images. Enter the origin in the textbox named “From” and destination in “To”; if autocomplete appears, select the intended place. Confirm both resolved values, keep the driving mode selected, click “Go,” then read the resulting route distance before reporting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When calculating a driving route in OpenStreetMap and the accessibility tree contains marker images alongside separately labeled “From” and “To” textboxes. Verify resolved locations and a visible route result before finishing.

skills.title: Generate Map Directions
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” page, fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, choose the requested travel mode if needed, and click “Go.” Confirm completion when a “Directions” panel displays the route, distance, and estimated time, then report those results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for directions between two locations, when the map interface exposes “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Directions
skills.principle: Once the route results are visible, verify the page shows the "Directions" heading, route summary, and turn-by-turn instruction list. Then report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or continuing unnecessary review.
skills.when_to_apply: For map-routing tasks after submitting origin and destination, when the resulting page visibly contains a route summary and ordered driving instructions.

skills.title: Extract Highways From Route Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's directions tool and enter the requested origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Keep the driving mode selected when the task asks about highways, then activate “Go.”
3. After the route loads, inspect the directions table and collect roadway names and route numbers, including names appearing in exits or merge instructions.
4. Report the deduplicated highway list only after confirming the route details are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking which highways or roads connect two locations, provided the site exposes a directions tool with origin, destination, and route instructions.

skills.title: Extract Highways From Route Directions
skills.principle: Once the directions page shows a generated route and a directions table, inspect the visible table text directly. Collect road names containing highway identifiers or major parkway/turnpike names, deduplicate repeated segments, and report them. Stop when the table includes the destination or no additional route entries; do not keep scrolling if the accessibility tree already exposes the full table.
skills.when_to_apply: After submitting origin and destination in OpenStreetMap Directions, when a Directions heading, route summary, and table of turn-by-turn entries appear in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Native Dropdowns
skills.principle: On a directions page, identify the transportation combobox and inspect its current value and available options. For a native HTML select, use the select-option operation with the desired mode rather than clicking an individual option, which may be invisible. Confirm the combobox value changed to the requested mode, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a route’s transportation mode in a map directions form and the accessibility tree exposes a combobox with selectable options, especially after direct clicking an option fails because it is not visible.

skills.title: Fill Route Before Requesting Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To.”
2. Select the desired transportation option, such as “Bicycle (OSRM),” from the mode control.
3. Click “Go” only after both locations are populated, then verify route details appear and the selected mode remains displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions page when changing travel mode for a route. The origin and destination fields must be filled before submitting; completion requires visible route results, not merely a changed dropdown.

skills.title: Reverse and Recalculate Map Directions
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s directions page, use the “Reverse Directions” control to swap the endpoints. If the fields are empty or unresolved, fill the origin and destination, then click “Go.” Confirm the “From” and “To” values reflect the requested order and that a “Directions” result with route details appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task requests reversing an existing route or displaying directions in the opposite order, especially when the directions page may initially lack resolved endpoint values.

skills.title: Set and Verify Reversed Route
skills.principle: On the map directions page, enter the desired origin in “From” and destination in “To”. If using “Reverse Directions” causes ambiguous or duplicated fields, overwrite both endpoints explicitly. Click “Go”, then verify the fields and directions panel show the intended origin-to-destination route before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task requires reversing or correcting route direction and the directions form is available. Verify both endpoint values and a generated directions result, not merely the button click.

skills.title: Compare Route Modes Systematically
skills.principle:
1. Open the map directions tool and enter the requested origin and destination, confirming each field resolves to a location.
2. Select the first travel mode and click “Go”; record the displayed distance and time.
3. Change the mode, click “Go” again, and record the second route’s distance and time.
4. Compare the recorded values, calculate any time difference, and report the result once both route summaries are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks comparing travel modes between two places, when the directions form provides origin and destination fields, a mode selector, a “Go” control, and route summaries showing distance and time.

skills.title: Use the Directions Form Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and fill the “From” and “To” textboxes with the requested locations.
2. Select the travel mode through the visible mode combobox, targeting its value or label; do not click an individual hidden option element.
3. Click “Go” and verify that a route and estimated time appear before recording that mode.
4. Repeat for the other requested mode, then compare the displayed estimates.
skills.when_to_apply: When comparing travel modes on OpenStreetMap’s directions page, especially when the mode options appear as hidden child options and the form’s From/To fields are still blank.

skills.title: Rank Route Segments by Distance
skills.principle: Open the directions tool, enter the requested origin and destination, and activate “Go.” After the directions table appears, scan every segment’s distance cell, sort the segments in descending order, and report the requested longest segments with their road names and distances. Confirm completion by checking that the table shows the full route and a destination-reaching step.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking which route portions have the longest distances between turns, after the directions page provides valid origin and destination fields and the generated route displays a complete directions table.

skills.title: Compare Route Segment Distances
skills.principle: Once directions appear, inspect every route-step distance, convert units consistently, and compare numeric values. Identify the largest segment by its associated road or turn instruction, then report that segment and distance. Do not keep focusing or re-reading the table after the maximum is established.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an OpenStreetMap Directions result shows a route-step table with distance values and the task asks for the longest segment between turns.

skills.title: Navigate to Export and Verify
skills.principle: Use the navigation entry labeled “Export” rather than manipulating the map. After clicking it, verify the page URL or heading shows “Export.” If direct export is unavailable because the selected area is too large, report that state and present the page’s available alternatives; stop once the requested page is reached.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks to open the Export page and the site exposes an “Export” navigation link. Confirm the Export heading or URL before reporting completion.

skills.title: Handle Download-Link Navigation Errors
skills.principle: When an export link reports a click timeout or `ERR_ABORTED` after activation, treat it as a possible download initiation rather than immediate failure. Check the browser’s download state or resulting file; if confirmed, stop. If no download occurred, reduce the selected map area or choose an appropriate bulk-download source, then verify completion before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s Export page when the selected area is too large for direct XML export and activating an alternative download link produces a timeout or aborted navigation.

skills.title: Verify Trace Availability Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate to the map site's “GPS Traces” page and inspect the content state. If it shows “Nothing here yet,” report that no user traces are available; mention the visible upload option only as a possible next step. Treat this empty-state message as completion rather than attempting unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view public GPS traces and the navigation exposes a “GPS Traces” entry. After opening it, use the visible heading or empty-state message to determine whether any traces can be viewed.

skills.title: Stop When No Traces Exist
skills.principle: On the Public GPS Traces page, inspect the result state. If it says “Nothing here yet,” recognize that no user traces are available to view, report that limitation, and terminate. Do not pursue upload, help, diaries, communities, or history links unless the task explicitly asks for those alternatives.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view uploaded GPS traces and the traces page visibly reports no available uploads, especially when uploading requires authentication or would create new data.

skills.title: Verify Geolocation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then wait and inspect the updated map state. Confirm a visible location marker, recentered view, or other observable geolocation result before claiming success. If the state is unchanged, address the browser permission requirement or report that location could not be confirmed rather than asserting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires finding the user’s current location and the geolocation control is available. Apply especially when clicking produces no observable map change or permission feedback.

skills.title: Trust Explicit Empty-State Messages
skills.principle: When the target content page displays an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries,” treat it as the observed result. Report that no matching content is available and terminate; do not repeatedly reload, revisit the page, or substitute unrelated sections such as traces, communities, or history.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to the requested content section succeeds but its accessibility tree shows a definitive empty-state heading or message and no controls for filtering or pagination.

skills.title: Enable Editing Before Clicking Edit
skills.principle: When the map’s Edit control is disabled and its tooltip indicates insufficient zoom, use “Zoom In” incrementally. After each zoom, inspect the control state; click Edit only once it is enabled and no longer blocked by the disabled edit container.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap map pages when the Edit link is visible but marked disabled, especially when clicking it times out because the edit control intercepts pointer events.

skills.title: Verify Edit Availability Before Clicking
skills.principle: When the map’s Edit control is disabled and its tooltip says to zoom in, use the visible Zoom In control and wait for the map state to refresh. Recheck the Edit control after each zoom; click it only after it is no longer marked disabled and the blocking overlay is gone.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a map editor from a map view and the Edit link is visibly disabled or click attempts are intercepted by a disabled edit container.

skills.title: Verify Location After Geolocation
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then inspect the updated map state before reporting success. Confirm that the map centers on the user or displays a location marker; if no change appears, wait and handle any permission or geolocation error instead of assuming completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking to find the current position when a “Show My Location” control is available. The operation is complete only after the map visibly updates or reports a geolocation result.

skills.title: Verify Available Map Layers
skills.principle: Open the map's Layers control and inspect the displayed layer names. If the requested imagery type is listed, select it and verify the map updates; otherwise, report that the current map instance does not provide that layer, citing the available alternatives.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change map imagery or basemap style, especially on an OpenStreetMap-style page with a visible Layers control.

skills.title: Verify Trace Availability Before Browsing
skills.principle: Open the map site's “GPS Traces” navigation entry and inspect the Public GPS Traces page. If it shows “Nothing here yet,” report that no public traces are currently available and stop; mention the upload option only as an alternative, not as an action required to view others' traces.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view other users’ GPS traces on an OpenStreetMap-style site, after reaching the GPS Traces page and before attempting further browsing or uploading.

skills.title: Verify Empty Content Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate to the task-specific section using its semantic navigation label. Inspect the resulting page for an explicit empty-state message, such as “No diary entries,” before claiming content is unavailable. Report the observed empty state directly and stop once the requested browsing result is established.
skills.when_to_apply: When a browsing task leads to a list or collection page and the page visibly provides an explicit empty-state message indicating that no matching content exists.

skills.title: Report Findings After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When the target page and requested heading are visible, read the relevant content, summarize the requested information in the task response, and terminate. Do not repeat no-op actions merely because the page remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for information-review tasks when navigation has succeeded and the accessibility tree shows the requested page heading and content, such as a Copyright and License page.

skills.title: Share the Current Map View
skills.principle:
1. Activate the map’s “Share” control to open sharing options.
2. Choose the “Link” option and focus its populated URL field; use “Short Link” when a compact URL is preferable.
3. Confirm the displayed link encodes the current map view, then provide it for copying or sharing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map is already positioned at the requested view and the task asks for a shareable link. The Share control and link field must be visible or accessible.

skills.title: Locate Password Recovery Through Login
skills.principle:
1. From the site homepage, open the visible “Log In” navigation link.
2. On the login page, select the “Lost your password?” link.
3. Confirm the destination shows a forgotten-password heading, an email field, and a “Reset password” button; report the page once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a password-recovery page and the homepage exposes login navigation, but no direct recovery link is visible. Stop after confirming the recovery form rather than submitting it.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once the target page is reached, verify its URL and identifying heading or content. Then immediately report completion and terminate; do not repeat noop actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task’s accessibility tree already shows the requested page, such as a matching URL and page heading, and no further interaction is required.

skills.title: Locate and Verify an RSS Feed
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant content page from site navigation.
2. Identify the RSS control by its feed icon or link role, then activate it.
3. Confirm the destination displays RSS/XML content and report the feed URL for subscription.
