skills.when_to_apply: Use when a website task asks for an RSS subscription and the site exposes a relevant section with an RSS link or feed icon.

skills.title: Recognize Raw RSS Feed Completion
skills.principle: When the GPS Traces page exposes an RSS icon or link, open it. If the resulting page shows valid RSS/XML content, treat that endpoint as the subscription feed, record the exact observed URL, report completion, and stop. Do not navigate back searching for a separate subscription button or invent a different feed URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when subscribing to a site's RSS feed and clicking the feed link opens raw XML rather than a reader prompt. Verify the XML contains an RSS channel before completing.

skills.title: Verify Authentication Before Diary Creation
skills.principle: Open the User Diaries section and inspect the available controls. If creating an entry requires authentication and the page shows login fields or a Log In link, stop before attempting submission and request valid account credentials or user authorization to register. Do not invent or guess credentials.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing an OpenStreetMap diary entry and the current page shows Log In/Sign Up controls or otherwise indicates the user is unauthenticated.

skills.title: Authenticate Before Creating Diary Entries
skills.principle: On the User Diaries page, first verify whether a diary-creation control is available. If it is absent and the header shows Log In or Sign Up, authenticate through that account flow before proceeding. Do not use the map’s Edit link, which leads to map editing and does not create diary entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating an OpenStreetMap diary entry while the diary page shows no creation control and the user is visibly unauthenticated, such as when Log In and Sign Up links are present.

skills.title: Use the Local Chapters List
skills.principle: Open the Communities page and inspect the visible Local Chapters section. Treat its explanatory text and linked chapter list as the primary result; summarize the listed chapters and their destinations. Open an individual chapter website only when the task explicitly requires deeper exploration, then verify the new page before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore OpenStreetMap Local Chapters and the Communities page displays a formal Local Chapters list with linked organizations.

skills.title: Complete Exploration From The Listing
skills.principle: When a page directly presents the requested collection, inspect the full accessible list and summarize the relevant entries before opening an individual link. Treat the collection page as sufficient evidence of completion unless the task explicitly requests details about particular items; then open only the necessary items and verify each result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for open-ended exploration tasks when the current page contains a heading and list matching the requested topic, especially when many linked entries are already visible.

skills.title: Verify Edit Availability After Zooming
skills.principle: When OpenStreetMap’s Edit control is disabled, use the visible “Zoom In” control, then re-inspect the accessibility tree after each zoom. Stop zooming once Edit is enabled and click it; verify navigation by checking that the page URL or heading reflects the Edit page rather than repeating zoom actions indefinitely.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating from an OpenStreetMap map to editing and the Edit control is disabled with a “Zoom in to edit the map” indication.】【。

skills.title: Navigate to the Export Page
skills.principle: Click the clearly labeled “Export” navigation link, then verify the destination by checking the page title or heading for “Export.” If the page reports that the selected area is too large, communicate that direct XML export is unavailable and identify the listed alternatives or smaller-area option.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to access OpenStreetMap’s map-data export workflow from the main map page, especially when the selected area may exceed direct XML download limits.

skills.title: Verify GPS Traces Empty State
skills.principle: Open the site's labeled “GPS Traces” navigation entry, then inspect the page heading and content. If the page shows “Nothing here yet,” report that no traces are available to view and stop rather than attempting uploads or unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check public GPS traces on OpenStreetMap and the navigation exposes a “GPS Traces” entry. Confirm the page's explicit empty-state message before reporting results.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Trace Status
skills.principle: Navigate to the GPS Traces page and inspect its visible state. If it explicitly reports that no traces are available, treat the check as complete, report that result, and terminate. Do not follow upload, login, refresh, or help links unless the task explicitly requests troubleshooting or creating a trace.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check or view GPS traces and the GPS Traces page visibly shows an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet.”

skills.title: Verify Empty Content Before Proceeding
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested content page through its labeled navigation link, then inspect the rendered page for entries or an explicit empty-state message. If the page states that no content is available, report that observed result and stop rather than inventing entries or taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to read or access list-based content, after reaching the relevant page and confirming its visible heading or empty-state text.

skills.title: Handle Explicit Empty States
skills.principle: When the target page displays an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries,” treat it as the current result. Report that no contributions are available, rather than repeatedly waiting, refreshing, or navigating to unrelated sections.
skills.when_to_apply: After opening a requested content page, when its accessibility tree clearly shows an empty-state heading or message and no content items are present.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested page, verify its heading and relevant content are present, then report completion and terminate. Do not perform exploratory clicks or send an empty action after the goal is already satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for browse tasks asking you to explore or inspect a specific page when the target page is loaded and its relevant sections or links are visible.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested section, then verify the page heading and relevant content are visible. Once the target page clearly provides the requested community information, treat exploration as complete and stop instead of opening an arbitrary external link.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to explore a site section and the corresponding page is already displayed with its heading and content. Only continue if the task explicitly requires selecting or visiting a specific community.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation Links
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree for a navigation link matching the requested page, activate it, then verify the resulting URL or page heading/content. If the requested page is already open and its relevant content is visible, report completion immediately instead of navigating or taking extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to open a named informational page and the current accessibility tree exposes either a matching navigation link or evidence that the target page is already displayed.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested destination, then verify the resulting URL or page heading. Once the target page is visibly loaded and satisfies the request, report completion and terminate instead of opening additional links or exploring related resources.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the requested destination is confirmed by its URL, heading, or distinctive page content, especially when no information beyond reaching that page is requested.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Informational Pages
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation link matching the requested informational page, activate it, then verify the destination URL and page headings or body text contain the requested subject. Summarize the relevant observed information and stop once the goal is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit an informational page and understand its content, especially when the page is reachable through a labeled navigation link and success requires both navigation and factual summarization.

skills.title: Terminate After Page Verification
skills.principle: After selecting the requested navigation link, verify the destination URL and page content match the task. Once the target page is confirmed, provide the requested completion response and terminate immediately; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the destination page is visibly loaded and its URL or heading/content confirms the requested location.

skills.title: Verify Location Display After Clicking
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then verify completion through an observable change such as a location marker, changed map center, or success status. If the map remains unchanged, check for a browser geolocation permission prompt or error before retrying; do not report success without confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests the user’s current location and the “Show My Location” control is available, especially when clicking it produces no immediate accessibility-tree change.

skills.title: Switch OpenStreetMap Map Layers
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control to reveal available base layers.
2. Select the requested layer by its visible label, such as “CyclOSM.”
3. Confirm application by observing refreshed tiles or attribution matching the selected layer, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap view is already open and the task requests changing its displayed map style or base layer. The Layers control and requested layer must be visible or discoverable in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify and Preserve the New Map Layer
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, select a different available base layer, and verify the map tiles or URL reflect that choice. Once the requested layer change is visibly active, stop without switching back or repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map-layer task lacks a specified target layer and the layer menu lists selectable base maps. Use the changed tile source, map appearance, or URL state as confirmation.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Directions
skills.principle: After submitting the route, verify that a Directions panel shows the requested endpoints plus distance, travel time, or turn-by-turn steps. Once confirmed, report the result and terminate immediately rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map routing tasks after selecting the directions tool, entering both endpoints, submitting the route, and observing a populated directions result.

skills.title: Generate and Verify Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions tool and enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
2. Keep the travel mode set to driving unless another mode is requested, then click “Go.”
3. Confirm completion when a “Directions” panel shows distance, travel time, and route steps; report those results and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting a route between two locations when the directions interface provides “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Report Completed Directions and Stop
skills.principle: After clicking “Go,” verify that a “Directions” panel appears with route summary and numbered turn-by-turn instructions. Once confirmed, report completion and any requested summary to the user, then terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-routing tasks after both origin and destination are resolved and the directions page visibly shows a route summary plus turn-by-turn instructions.

skills.title: Extract Highways From Route Directions
skills.principle: After submitting origin and destination, verify the Directions panel appears. Read the accessible directions table and collect road entries containing interstate, state, U.S., parkway, or turnpike identifiers. Consolidate unique major highways, then report them and stop once the route result is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking which major roads or highways appear on a route, after the directions form accepts both locations and displays a route summary or directions table.

skills.title: Verify Map History State
skills.principle: Open the map's History navigation entry and inspect the resulting Changesets panel. Treat the task as complete when the page displays either recent changesets or an explicit message such as "No changesets in this area," then accurately report that observed state.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view recent map changes and the map interface provides a History entry. Confirm the history page and its Changesets content before reporting results.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Map History
skills.principle: Open the map’s “History” view and inspect the “Changesets” panel. If it displays “No changesets in this area,” treat that as the observable result for the current map extent; report that no recent changesets were found and stop instead of repeatedly zooming or reopening History.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view recent map changes and the History page is open, especially when the Changesets panel explicitly reports no changesets in the displayed area.

skills.title: Handle Large Map Exports
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Export” page and inspect the area-size message. If direct XML export is unavailable because the bounding box is too large, either zoom in or select a smaller area, or use the page’s provided bulk-download source such as the Overpass API link. Treat download-trigger timeouts as possible browser-wait behavior; avoid repeatedly clicking and provide the exact link or Save Link As guidance.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting the current OpenStreetMap view and the Export page reports that the selected area is too large for direct XML export, especially when clicking a bulk-download link triggers a navigation or download timeout.

skills.title: Reduce Export Area Before Downloading
skills.principle: When the Export page reports that the current area is too large, use “Manually select a different area” and define a smaller bounding box rather than repeatedly zooming without checking results. Confirm the warning disappears and an export/download control appears, then activate it. Treat Overpass, Planet, and Geofabrik links as alternative bulk-data sources, not proof that the current export completed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on OpenStreetMap’s Export page when the current map bounding box triggers the “area is too large” warning and the task requires an actual downloadable export.

skills.title: Choose a Community Link
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Communities page, distinguish actionable community links from informational text. Select a relevant Local Chapter or other group link to reach that community’s mapper-facing site; use the Communities wiki only when specifically seeking general group-creation guidance.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore OpenStreetMap communities or connect with mappers and the Communities page displays both group links and a general wiki link.

skills.title: Inspect Communities Before Leaving
skills.principle: Open the map site's “Communities” page and verify that community information is visible. Review the “Local Chapters” and “Other Groups” sections and their links as evidence that mapper communities are available. Once the requested community information is displayed, stop or report completion rather than navigating to an external wiki unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore OpenStreetMap communities and the “Communities” navigation link is available. Use this after reaching the page and confirming its headings, descriptions, or community links are visible.

skills.title: Keep Registration Emails Unique and Matching
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap sign-up form, use a genuinely available email address, enter the exact same address in both “Email” and “Email Confirmation,” then complete the remaining fields and submit. If submission reports “has already been taken,” replace the email in both fields before resubmitting, and verify the resulting page confirms registration rather than assuming success.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating an OpenStreetMap account and the sign-up form displays an email-availability error or the confirmation field still contains an older address.

skills.title: Recover Signup Validation Errors
skills.principle: After submitting an OpenStreetMap signup form, inspect every validation message. If the email is already taken, replace it with a genuinely available address, update Email Confirmation to match exactly, refill any password fields cleared during rerender, then click Sign Up again and verify a success or confirmation state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on the OpenStreetMap Sign Up page after submission returns validation errors such as “has already been taken,” mismatched confirmation, or emptied password fields.

skills.title: Use the Map Layers Panel
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control to reveal base styles and overlays.
2. Select the requested map style or toggle an enabled overlay.
3. Verify completion from the updated map tiles, attribution, or checkbox state.
4. If an overlay is disabled with a zoom requirement, zoom in before attempting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing map appearance or displayed data on OpenStreetMap, especially when the Layers panel exposes selectable styles, checkboxes, and zoom-dependent disabled overlays.

skills.title: Use Export for Map Bounding Boxes
skills.principle:
1. From the current OpenStreetMap view, open the "Export" navigation entry rather than relying on the share URL, which provides only center and zoom.
2. Read the four coordinate fields in the Export panel as North, West, East, and South.
3. Report them in that labeled order; confirm against the displayed Overpass bbox link when available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the current map view’s bounding box on OpenStreetMap, with the map loaded and the Export navigation entry available.

skills.title: Use Export to Read Map Bounds
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Export” link rather than guessing from the URL or advising manual actions. The export page represents the current view with bounding-box fields; read the west, south, east, and north coordinates and report them only after verifying they match the displayed map extent.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap view is open and the task asks for its exact bounding box, especially when the accessibility tree exposes an “Export” navigation link but no bounds readout.

skills.title: Use Export to Find OSM Sources
skills.principle: Open the OpenStreetMap “Export” page and inspect its data-source list. If the selected area is too large for direct XML export, use the listed alternatives: Overpass API for bounding boxes, Planet OSM for the complete database, Geofabrik for regional extracts, and Other Sources for additional options. Report each source with its intended scope.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore or recommend OpenStreetMap download sources and the site’s navigation exposes an “Export” link or page.

skills.title: Use Export Listings Before External Links
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, first read the available bulk-download sources and their descriptions directly. If the requested exploration is satisfied by the listing, report those sources and stop. If opening an external source is necessary and a click times out after completion, verify the resulting page or URL before retrying or choosing another link.
skills.when_to_apply: When exploring OpenStreetMap download options and the Export page displays source names, descriptions, and links, especially when an external-link click reports a navigation timeout.

skills.title: Zoom Map Until Export Unlocks
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom In” control repeatedly, checking the map URL or visible zoom state after each click. Stop when the zoom reaches the threshold that enables export (observed here at level 13), then report completion without performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requiring a higher zoom level before data export becomes available, when the map exposes a labeled “Zoom In” control and the current zoom is visible in the map URL or page state.

skills.title: Verify Zoom Before Exporting
skills.principle: Use a closed loop: click “Zoom In” once, inspect the updated map state or URL zoom level, and repeat only while export remains unavailable. When the required zoom is reached, stop zooming and select “Export”; verify the export page or enabled export controls appear.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires zooming before export and each zoom action updates an observable zoom level, URL, or export-control state.

skills.title: Edit Export Bounds Directly
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap Export page, use the “Manually select a different area” control, then edit a bounding-box coordinate textbox directly when map interaction is obstructed. Replace the current value with a valid coordinate closer to the opposite boundary to create a different, smaller rectangle, and verify the textbox displays the new value.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when manually changing an OpenStreetMap export area, especially when map tiles or Leaflet overlays intercept clicks. Ensure the Export page exposes North, West, East, and South coordinate fields.

skills.title: Verify Export Navigation Before Selecting
skills.principle: Use the navigation entry labeled “Export,” not a neighboring unlabeled or “Edit” control. After activating it, verify that the URL or accessibility tree shows the export page and its area-selection controls; only then adjust the map selection and confirm the new area is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap task requests manually selecting a different export area and the navigation contains multiple nearby controls, especially when the export page has not yet been confirmed.

skills.title: Calculate Map Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's directions feature.
2. Fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, using the available travel mode unless the task specifies another.
3. Click “Go” to calculate the route.
4. Confirm the directions panel shows a route, distance, travel time, and turn-by-turn steps before reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting directions between two named places when the site provides a directions form with “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Use Directions Form After Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions page using the directions link.
2. Fill the dedicated “From” and “To” textboxes separately with the requested locations.
3. Choose the requested travel mode if needed, then click the directions form’s “Go” button.
4. Confirm that route details or a mapped route appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map site switches to a dedicated directions page showing “From,” “To,” travel-mode controls, and “Go”; do not reuse the previous page’s hidden directions link.

skills.title: Search and Verify Map Location
skills.principle: Use the map application's Search textbox to enter the requested place, then activate the Go control. Confirm completion when search results identify the target location and the map view updates to a relevant centered area with loaded map tiles. Report completion and stop once the requested map is visibly displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring a named place or area to be displayed, when the page provides a Search field and Go/submit control.

skills.title: Confirm Map Location and Stop
skills.principle: Use the map Search box with the target place or coordinates, click “Go,” then verify the map URL or search results reflect the target location. If results remain open, select the exact coordinate result to center the map. Once the map view is confirmed, report completion and stop instead of repeating waits or unnecessary zoom actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks you to display a specific place and the search results or URL show the requested location after submitting the query.

skills.title: Inspect Directions Mode Options
skills.principle: Open the map site's directions feature, expand its transportation-mode combobox, and read every visible option and its selected state. Report the complete set of modes once the expanded control confirms the available choices; entering origin and destination is unnecessary when the task only asks which modes exist.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which transportation methods a map site's directions tool supports and the directions page exposes a mode selector. Use the expanded accessibility tree or menu to verify all options before answering.

skills.title: Target Controls by Role and Label
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s role and label to distinguish routing textboxes from adjacent marker images. To check available transportation options, inspect the directions panel’s combobox directly; it lists Bicycle, Car, and Foot, so do not enter locations or calculate a route unless requested. Verify the selected control’s type and value before acting.
skills.when_to_apply: When OpenStreetMap’s directions panel is open and the task asks which transportation modes are available, especially when marker images and labeled From/To textboxes appear adjacent in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: After selecting the task’s destination link, verify the resulting URL and page heading match the requested destination. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks where success is indicated by a destination URL or distinctive page heading, such as reaching OpenStreetMap’s Communities page.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: In the accessibility tree, locate the navigation link whose label matches the requested destination and activate it. Confirm the resulting URL or page heading matches the target and that relevant content is visible, then report completion without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for tasks asking to open a clearly labeled informational page, especially when the current page exposes the destination in navigation and the resulting page can be verified by its heading or URL.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Page
skills.principle: After navigating to the requested page, verify the URL or a distinctive heading matches the goal. Once confirmed, provide the requested result or completion message and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions while the page remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree shows the target page’s URL, title, or distinctive heading. This is especially important when the environment expects an explicit final response after successful navigation.

skills.title: Navigate Using Visible Semantic Links
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation link matching the requested destination, activate it with a valid click action, then verify the resulting URL or page heading/content. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and stop instead of repeating the action.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests opening a named page and the current page exposes a matching accessible navigation link, especially in OpenStreetMap’s site-wide navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Target Page
skills.principle: After selecting the relevant navigation entry, verify the destination using its URL, page heading, and requested content. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the destination page visibly contains the requested heading or content and the browser state confirms the intended route.

skills.title: Check Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and accessibility tree before taking navigation actions. If the target page is already open and its content matches the request, report that it is ready and stop; otherwise activate the visible navigation link matching the target page, then verify the resulting URL and page content.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the browser may already be on the requested page. The current URL and visible page headings or content must be available for comparison.

skills.title: Stop When Trace List Is Empty
skills.principle: Open the GPS Traces section and inspect the resulting list. If it displays an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet,” report that no uploaded traces are available and terminate; do not follow upload, help, or wiki links unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse or list public GPS traces and the GPS Traces page visibly shows an empty-state message with no records.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Login Page
skills.principle: When the task is to navigate to a login page, click the visible “Log In” navigation link and verify that the destination shows a “Login” heading or login form. Once that state is visible, report completion and terminate; do not enter credentials or submit the form unless authentication is explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only requests where the observed page contains a “Log In” link and the destination displays the login form. Credentials are unnecessary unless the task explicitly asks you to sign in.

skills.title: Complete OpenStreetMap Directions Workflow
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” and identify the “From” and “To” textboxes.
2. Enter the origin and destination, preserving any location disambiguation the page resolves.
3. Click “Go” and verify a “Directions” panel appears with distance, time, and route steps.
4. Report the displayed route summary and stop once completion is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requesting directions between two named places, when the directions page provides “From,” “To,” and “Go” controls and a route panel can confirm success.

skills.title: Stop After Directions Appear
skills.principle: On the directions page, fill the From and To fields, click Go, and verify completion by checking for a Directions heading plus route distance, time, or turn list. Once those results are visible, report the route as complete and terminate; do not continue clicking, focusing, or reversing directions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap routing tasks after submitting two locations. Stop when the page shows populated route results such as distance/time and turn-by-turn instructions.

skills.title: Disambiguate Map Searches with Coordinates
skills.principle: When a landmark search returns an unrelated namesake, inspect the result’s location instead of accepting it. Refine the query if useful; if place-name searches fail, enter the target’s known latitude and longitude and click “Go.” Confirm the map URL and coordinate result show the intended area before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map searches where search results contain replicas, namesakes, incorrect regions, or “No results found,” especially when the target’s coordinates are known.

skills.title: Stop After Search Results Appear
skills.principle: After entering the target place and clicking “Go,” inspect the updated page. If a “Search Results” panel appears and the map view changes to the result location, treat the search as complete and terminate; do not add unnecessary waits, scrolling, or zooming.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap place searches when the search results panel and a changed map view are visible after submitting the query.

skills.title: Stop After Destination Confirmation
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested page, then verify the resulting heading or URL confirms arrival. Once confirmed—even if the page is empty—report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the target link is visible and the resulting page provides an observable title, heading, URL, or empty-state message confirming the destination.

skills.title: Target Direction Fields by Role
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap directions page, use the controls labeled “From” and “To” as the input targets, not adjacent marker images. Fill the origin and destination textboxes separately, retain the requested travel mode such as “Car (OSRM),” then click “Go.” Verify both fields contain the intended locations and confirm that route details or a calculated route appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when requesting map directions and the accessibility tree shows labeled From/To textboxes alongside decorative or draggable marker images. Verify field contents before submitting the route.

skills.title: Select Hidden Dropdown Options Properly
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and inspect the transportation combobox.
2. If its options appear as non-visible HTML option elements, use the select-option operation on the combobox rather than clicking an option directly.
3. Fill the origin and destination, then activate Go.
4. Confirm the selected mode and generated route summary before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map directions forms when the requested transportation mode is represented by a native select control and direct option clicks fail because options are not visible.

skills.title: Generate Walking Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature and enter the requested start and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Select “Foot (OSRM)” or the equivalent walking mode before submitting.
3. Click “Go” and verify a “Directions” result appears with distance, duration, and route steps.
4. Report the displayed walking distance and time, using the route steps when detailed directions are requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting a walking route between two named places, once the directions form exposes start, destination, travel-mode, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Set Travel Mode Before Routing
skills.principle: On a map directions page, fill the origin and destination, explicitly select the requested travel mode (such as “Foot (OSRM)”), then activate “Go.” Confirm the resulting Directions panel shows a route summary and step-by-step itinerary before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for route-planning tasks when the directions form has origin and destination fields, a travel-mode combobox, and a “Go” control. Verify the resolved locations and mode match the request.

skills.title: Configure Walking Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. On the directions form, fill both the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations; do not assume the prior search populated the origin.
2. Set the travel-mode combobox to the exact visible “Foot (OSRM)” option, using the native select control rather than clicking an invisible option.
3. Verify the fields and combobox visibly show the intended values, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm a route result or directions summary appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When OpenStreetMap directions opens with separate From, To, travel-mode, and Go controls, especially if the origin is blank or the default mode remains “Car (OSRM).”

skills.title: Select Walking Mode Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Fill the directions form’s From and To fields with the requested locations.
2. Set the transportation combobox to the walking option, such as “Foot (OSRM),” instead of leaving the default driving mode.
3. Click “Go” and verify that a Directions panel appears with route details and the walking mode remains selected.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map directions pages when the user requests walking directions. Ensure both endpoints are entered and the route-mode selector is available before submitting.

skills.title: Use the Directions Form Directly
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions page, then fill the visible “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations.
2. Select “Foot (OSRM)” in the travel-mode combobox.
3. Click the visible “Go” button and verify that route details or step-by-step instructions appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests walking directions and the directions page is open. Do not reuse the map page’s “Find directions between two points” link after navigation; use the visible route form instead.

skills.title: Verify Directions Before Claiming Success
skills.principle: Check that the From and To fields contain the requested locations before reversing. Click “Reverse Directions,” then inspect both fields and the resulting page state to confirm they are swapped. If fields are empty or unchanged, populate the required endpoints or report that reversal was not completed; do not claim success from the click alone.
skills.when_to_apply: When reversing routes in a map directions form, especially when the initial accessibility tree may show empty or unresolved From/To fields.

skills.title: Reduce Export Area After Limit Error
skills.principle:
1. After calculating the route, open Export and inspect the proposed bounding box.
2. If export reports too many nodes, return to Export and choose “Manually select a different area.”
3. Select a tighter bounding box containing the complete route, then click “Export” again and verify the download or resulting map data.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a routed map in OpenStreetMap and the initial Export action produces a node-limit error; the route must already be calculated and the Export page must offer manual area selection.

skills.title: Reduce Export Bounding Box
skills.principle:
1. After generating the route, open Export and inspect the selected bounding box.
2. If export reports too many nodes, use “Manually select a different area” or edit the bounds to tightly enclose both endpoints and the route.
3. Submit Export only after confirming the smaller area still covers the complete route, then verify the download or successful export response.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when OpenStreetMap’s Export action returns a node-limit error. The route must already be generated, and the reduced bounding box must include both requested locations and the displayed route.

skills.title: Verify Reversed Directions
skills.principle: For a directions-reversal task, first confirm the From and To fields contain the current endpoints. Activate “Reverse Directions,” then inspect the resulting fields and route state. If the fields are empty or the route is unset, restore the endpoints and submit with “Go.” Report completion only after the displayed origin and destination visibly match the reversed order.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when reversing an existing map route, especially if the accessibility tree does not expose textbox values or the reversal may navigate to a refreshed directions page.

skills.title: Zoom Out Until Minimum Level
skills.principle: Use the map’s labeled “Zoom Out” control repeatedly, checking the updated map state after each click. Stop when the zoom indicator or URL shows the minimum level and the map displays a global view; the control may remain visible even when the task is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to zoom out a map, especially to the furthest or global view, and the accessibility tree exposes a “Zoom Out” control plus observable zoom-level or scale changes.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify User Diaries
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation link labeled “User Diaries” and activate it. Confirm completion by checking the page title or heading and inspect the resulting content, such as whether diary entries exist. If posting is requested, report the visible authentication prerequisite when a “Log In” link is present.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open OpenStreetMap’s User Diaries page to read or write mapping-related posts, beginning from another OpenStreetMap page and relying on accessibility-tree navigation.

skills.title: Use the Map Location Control
skills.principle: On a map page, identify the control labeled “Show My Location” and activate it. If the browser requests geolocation permission, allow it so the map can obtain and display the current position. Once activated, report completion without taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When the user asks to display their current position and the map exposes a visible “Show My Location” control; geolocation permission may be required.

skills.title: Recognize Successful Empty States
skills.principle: After selecting the requested navigation entry, verify the page title, URL, and main heading. If they identify the target page—even when it shows an explicit empty state such as “No diary entries”—treat navigation as complete, report success, and stop instead of repeatedly clicking or switching pages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a page that may legitimately contain no records. Prerequisite: the observed page identity matches the requested destination and its empty-state message is explicit.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Retrying
skills.principle: After a navigation action, inspect the current URL and page heading. If they match the requested destination, use the visible content to answer the task and stop. Only retry or use direct navigation when the destination is not reached or the page state shows an error.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when clicks fail, produce empty-action errors, or the target link remains visible; the current page may already be the requested destination.

skills.title: Use the Visible Login Link
skills.principle: From an OpenStreetMap page, locate the navigation link labeled “Log In” and activate it. Confirm completion when the resulting page shows the “Login” heading and username/email, password, and Login controls. Report that the login page is ready without entering credentials unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to OpenStreetMap’s login page and the current page exposes a visible “Log In” navigation link; stop once the login form is displayed.

skills.title: Open and Verify Map Layers
skills.principle: Click the map control labeled “Layers,” then inspect the updated accessibility tree for a “Map Layers” heading and available layer options. Once the panel is visibly open, report completion without selecting an unnecessary layer or taking further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests opening or exploring layers and the current page exposes a Layers control. Confirm the panel opened by checking for its heading and listed base-layer or overlay options.

skills.title: Verify Existing Route Before Acting
skills.principle: When a directions page already contains the requested origin, destination, route summary, and turn-by-turn table, treat the route as complete. Extract the displayed distance, duration, and useful step highlights, report them to the user, and stop without re-submitting the form.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on map directions pages where the requested endpoints are already populated and observable route results, such as distance, time, or driving steps, are displayed.

skills.title: Use Semantic Sign-Up Navigation
skills.principle: Select the visible “Sign Up” navigation link or equivalent account-creation entry, then verify the destination by checking for a sign-up heading and registration fields. Once the form is displayed, report completion and stop without filling or submitting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only requires reaching an account-registration page and the current page exposes a labeled sign-up link or another clearly equivalent entry point.

skills.title: Verify Direction Fields Before Submission
skills.principle: On the directions page, fill the actual textboxes labeled “From” and “To,” not adjacent marker images. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To,” then verify both displayed values and their order before clicking “Go.” After submission, confirm that route instructions or a rendered route appear; if fields are missing or unchanged, correct them instead of repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when requesting map directions with coordinates or place names, especially when accessibility-tree element IDs include nearby decorative markers and the page must display both populated endpoints before routing.

skills.title: Calculate Route Distance and Time
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions interface and enter the starting location in “From” and destination in “To,” using coordinates when provided.
2. Keep the requested travel mode selected, then activate “Go.”
3. Confirm the results panel displays both “Distance” and “Time,” and report those values exactly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting distance and estimated travel time between two locations, after the directions form exposes “From,” “To,” a travel-mode selector, and “Go.”

skills.title: Generate and Verify Map Directions
skills.principle:
1. Fill the directions form’s “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, accepting resolved place names when shown.
2. Keep the requested travel mode selected, then activate “Go.”
3. Confirm completion by checking a “Directions” panel, route map, and distance/time summary before reporting the result.
4. Once confirmed, send one concise summary and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a map directions page when the origin and destination inputs, travel-mode selector, and “Go” control are available. Completion requires visible route results and a distance/time summary.

skills.title: Target Route Inputs by Role
skills.principle: On the directions page, locate the actual textboxes labeled “From” and “To,” not adjacent marker images. Enter the two coordinate pairs, verify both fields retain the requested values, keep the required travel mode, then click “Go.” Confirm the resulting route panel contains both distance and estimated travel time before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for coordinate-based routing tasks when the accessibility tree exposes marker images near separately labeled From/To textboxes, especially after a fill action targets a non-input element or a route result is not visible.

skills.title: Authenticate Before Map Editing
skills.principle: Use a known valid account or complete registration with an accessible email address and any required confirmation before entering the editor. Do not guess credentials or assume demo passwords. After submitting authentication, verify that the edit interface loads and editing controls are available before attempting map changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap task starts on a map, directions, or login page and editing requires authentication. This is especially important after a failed login, when credentials are not explicitly provided, or when registration requires email verification.

skills.title: Handle Authentication Before Editing
skills.principle: When selecting OpenStreetMap’s “Edit” redirects to a login page, treat that redirect as confirmation that authentication is required. Ask the user to log in or use “Sign Up” if they lack an account, then stop until credentials or a completed login are available. Do not repeatedly revisit the editor or registration page without new user input.
skills.when_to_apply: When an editing action reaches a page containing “Login,” credential fields, and an edit-page referer, especially when no credentials are provided.

skills.title: Open and Verify Public GPS Traces
skills.principle:
1. From the map interface, select the navigation link labeled “GPS Traces.”
2. Confirm the destination by checking for the “Public GPS Traces” heading and the “All Traces” view.
3. Report the displayed state; if “Nothing here yet” appears, explain that no public traces are currently available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or review all public GPS traces from an OpenStreetMap-style map page, especially when the GPS Traces navigation link is visible.

skills.title: Calculate and Verify Driving Routes
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin and destination in the directions page’s “From” and “To” fields.
2. Confirm the transportation mode matches the request, selecting “Car” when needed, then activate “Go.”
3. Read the generated directions summary and report the displayed distance and travel time only after confirming the route results are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map directions tasks requesting route distance or estimated travel time when the directions form provides origin, destination, travel-mode controls, and a route summary after submission.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Trace Availability
skills.principle: Open the map site's “GPS Traces” navigation entry and inspect the resulting “Public GPS Traces” page. If it displays an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the task as complete with no public traces available, report that result, and stop instead of following informational or upload links.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or browse all public GPS traces and the dedicated traces page is reachable. Apply after checking whether the page contains trace entries or an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Generate and Verify Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
2. Confirm the driving mode is selected, such as “Car (OSRM),” then activate “Go.”
3. Verify completion by checking that a directions panel appears with route distance, travel time, and a turn-by-turn step list; then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions page when a user requests driving directions between two places and the origin, destination, and driving mode controls are visible.

skills.title: Use Communities for Local Chapters
skills.principle: Open the site's Communities page and locate the heading "Local Chapters." Extract every item in the list under the statement identifying formally established Local Chapters, excluding entries under "Other Groups." Report the complete list once the page visibly shows the full section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks asking for all Local Chapters when the initial map view exposes a Communities navigation link and the Communities page contains a labeled Local Chapters list.

skills.title: Extract Visible Lists Directly
skills.principle: When a page already shows the requested list, read every item under the relevant heading, stop at the next section heading, and report the complete set. Do not open individual item links unless the task asks for details unavailable in the list; verify the list boundary before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for list-retrieval tasks when the accessibility tree visibly contains the target heading and its itemized entries, especially when a subsequent section indicates the list has ended.

skills.title: Generate and Verify Map Routes
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
2. Keep the requested travel mode selected, then activate “Go.”
3. Verify the resulting “Directions” panel shows the route summary, distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps.
4. Summarize the observed route details and stop once the result is reported.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap-style directions pages when the origin and destination fields, travel-mode selector, and “Go” control are visible. Completion is indicated by a Directions panel and route summary appearing.

skills.title: Read Route Summary Directly
skills.principle: Use the current directions page’s accessibility tree to find the summary text labeled “Distance” and “Time.” Extract both values, convert units or time format only when clarifying, and report them without reopening or recalculating the route.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions page already displays the current route and its accessibility tree contains a distance-and-time summary, such as “Distance: … Time: …”.

skills.title: Calculate Route Metrics
skills.principle: On the directions page, enter the route’s origin in “From” and destination in “To”, select the requested travel mode, then press “Go”. Wait for the route results and read both distance and estimated travel time from the route summary before reporting them.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks for distance or travel time and the directions form shows “From”, “To”, a travel-mode selector, and “Go”; endpoint locations must be known or supplied.

skills.title: Recognize Already-Displayed Directions
skills.principle: Inspect the current map page before interacting. If a visible “Directions” panel contains a turn-by-turn table and route summary, treat the request as complete and report the displayed steps or summary instead of recalculating or clicking controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for route-direction tasks when the current map page already shows a Directions panel with ordered steps and distance or travel-time information.

skills.title: Handle Authentication-Gated Edit Pages
skills.principle: Select the map’s “Edit” navigation link and verify the resulting page. If it redirects to a login page, recognize authentication as a prerequisite, avoid repeated direct-navigation attempts, and report that credentials or account registration are required to continue.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening an OpenStreetMap edit page from a map view and the accessibility tree shows a login page with username/password fields instead of the editor.

skills.title: Handle Authentication-Gated Editing
skills.principle: When selecting the map’s “Edit” navigation entry redirects to a login page, recognize authentication is required. Do not retry the same link; request valid credentials or explain that access cannot continue without them.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires opening an editing interface and the observed page shows a login form after selecting “Edit,” especially when no credentials are available.

skills.title: Generate Routes From Exact Coordinates
skills.principle:
1. On the directions page, enter the starting latitude/longitude pair in the “From” field and the destination pair in “To”.
2. Click “Go” after both fields contain the requested coordinates.
3. Confirm the fields remain populated and a calculated route appears on the map before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when exact coordinate-based directions are required and the map page provides “From”, “To”, and “Go” controls. Ensure both coordinate pairs are entered before submitting.

skills.title: Switch OpenStreetMap Layer Style
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control to reveal the “Map Layers” panel.
2. Select the requested named style from the available layer options.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the map tiles or attribution reflect the selected style, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap map page is loaded and the task requests changing its visual layer style. The map must expose a “Layers” control and selectable named styles.

skills.title: Select Layer Controls, Not Map Tiles
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and choose the desired style by clicking its labeled layer option or selectable list-item control, such as “CyclOSM” or “Humanitarian.” Do not click the preview tile image or overlay checkboxes; those may be noninteractive or serve different purposes. Verify success when the map refreshes with tiles from the selected style.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map’s visual style and the Layers panel lists named basemaps alongside preview images and separate overlay checkboxes.

skills.title: Generate Route Before Sharing
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin and destination in the directions form, resolving autocomplete values when they appear.
2. Click “Go” and verify a “Directions” panel with route details is displayed.
3. Open or reuse the “Share” dialog, choose “Short Link,” and verify its textbox contains the updated route link.
4. Leave the short-link textbox focused so the user can copy it.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing map directions and the page may initially show an empty, stale, or unrelated map state. Confirm the requested route is generated before selecting a share format.

skills.title: Copy a Map Share Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the map's “Share” control.
2. In the “Link or HTML” panel, select the standard “Link” option and verify the generated URL appears in the textbox.
3. Copy the focused URL with the platform shortcut, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map or route is displayed and the task requires sharing it, provided the page exposes a “Share” control and a generated link textbox.

skills.title: Verify Map Control Identity Before Acting
skills.principle: Use the accessibility name and role, not an element ID alone, to select map controls. For route sharing, activate the control explicitly labeled “Share,” then inspect the updated accessibility tree for a share dialog, URL field, or copy action. If the result instead shows an unrelated tooltip or page, return to the map and retry the correctly labeled control.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing a map or route and several unlabeled or similarly positioned controls appear. Confirm the selected control’s accessible label and verify the post-click state before filling fields or navigating elsewhere.

skills.title: Navigate to OpenStreetMap Communities
skills.principle: Use the visible “Communities” navigation link rather than searching the map. On the resulting page, verify the “Communities” heading, review “Local Chapters” and “Other Groups,” then report the available community categories and offer to open a specific listed community or the Communities wiki page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find or explore OpenStreetMap communities and the page exposes a “Communities” navigation link. Completion is confirmed by the Communities heading and categorized community links.

skills.title: Systematically Explore Map Layers
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, then select each requested layer by its visible label in turn. After every selection, verify the map tiles or attribution reflect the chosen style. Return to the default layer if appropriate, then report all explored options.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task asks you to explore or compare multiple available layer styles and the Layers control exposes the requested options.

skills.title: Trace Adjacent Route Instructions
skills.principle: Read the directions table sequentially and compare neighboring street instructions. If the requested intersection is not named in a single step, report the route’s actual transition between streets and identify the closest explicit turn instruction, including its step number when available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction questions asking about a specific intersection, especially when the route may pass through an intermediate street and no instruction explicitly names both requested streets.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Directions Results
skills.principle: Use the directions form with a recognized origin and the target intersection as destination. Submit with “Go,” then verify that a route and turn-instruction list appears. If no route or instructions appear, refine the destination or choose nearby recognized addresses before reporting results; do not substitute an arbitrary example origin or rely on waiting and scrolling alone.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map search returns no result and the task requires turn instructions. The directions page must expose “From,” “To,” and “Go” controls, and completion requires visible route instructions.

skills.title: Navigate Using Visible Page Links
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree for a navigation link whose label matches the requested destination, activate it, then verify the resulting page through its title, heading, URL path, or relevant content. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests viewing a named page and the current map application exposes that destination as a visible navigation link.

skills.title: Stop After Route Comparison
skills.principle: After each transport mode recalculates, record the displayed distance and time. Once all requested modes are compared, summarize the results through the supported response channel and terminate. Do not invoke an unavailable messaging action or continue exploring reverse routes unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking to compare routing modes when the directions panel visibly reports results for every requested mode and the agent is ready to respond.

skills.title: Compare Modes Then Stop
skills.principle: Select each available travel mode and submit with “Go” when required. After each mode, record the displayed distance and time from the Directions panel. Report only observed values, including any mode whose details were not captured. Once all modes are checked and the summary is sent, terminate instead of reversing routes, probing extra controls, or sending duplicate messages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-routing tasks asking to explore multiple transportation options, when origin and destination are already set and the mode selector lists alternatives such as car, bicycle, and foot.

skills.title: Recognize Completed Directions Pages
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and accessible page content before navigating. If the page is already the directions view, the requested travel mode is selected, both endpoints are populated, and a route summary or turn-by-turn directions is visible, report completion immediately instead of reloading or changing the route.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open or obtain map directions and the current page already shows the directions interface with populated endpoints and a calculated route.

skills.title: Verify Endpoints Before Requesting Directions
skills.principle: On the directions page, inspect the actual values of the “From” and “To” fields rather than inferring they are filled. Enter both requested locations, keep or select the desired travel mode, then click “Go” once. Confirm that a route or directions result appears; if the page remains unchanged, investigate missing or invalid inputs instead of repeatedly clicking the same button.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on map directions forms when endpoint fields may be blank or their values are not exposed clearly, especially after a submission produces no visible route or page change.

skills.title: Handle Editor Authentication Redirects
skills.principle: When selecting the map editor redirects to a login page, recognize authentication as a prerequisite. Use the visible username/email and password fields with authorized credentials, submit Login, and verify that the browser returns to the editor before attempting map changes. If credentials are unavailable, request them without claiming the editor was accessed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an editing link leads to a login page and the task requires modifying map data. Credentials or an already authenticated session are required before proceeding.

skills.title: Verify Smaller Export Bounds
skills.principle: After an export reports too many nodes, select a substantially smaller area using the map’s manual-selection control. Confirm the displayed bounding coordinates and map selection actually changed before clicking Export; editing a coordinate field alone may leave the submitted bounding box unchanged. If the limit persists, reduce the area again or use an alternate source.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s Export page after a node-limit error, especially when coordinate fields and the map selection may be independently managed. Verify the resulting request bounds before retrying.

skills.title: Verify Page State Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate through the clearly labeled navigation entry for the requested resource. Confirm the destination using its page heading and inspect the primary content for an explicit empty-state or result message. Report the observed status and any relevant available next actions, then stop once the requested check is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to check a site section, especially when the current page is different and the destination may show either records or an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Verify Page State Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree and current URL before navigating. If the requested page is already loaded, stop navigating and use its visible headings, lists, and links to answer. Otherwise, activate the navigation link with the exact supported action syntax, then verify the destination page content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a site section and the current page may already be that section, especially after an action error or repeated failed clicks.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation After Click Failure
skills.principle:
1. Identify the intended navigation link and its observed destination URL.
2. If clicking produces an empty-action or navigation error, use the observed URL with direct navigation instead of repeatedly retrying.
3. Verify the destination by checking its heading and content state; if it reports no entries, report that state and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation link is visible in the accessibility tree but click actions fail, especially on pages such as User Diaries where an empty-state message can complete the task.

skills.title: Verify Routing Field Targets
skills.principle: Use the accessibility role and label, not nearby marker IDs, when entering directions. Fill the actual “From” and “To” textboxes, select “Foot (OSRM),” then press “Go.” Confirm that a route summary or directions panel appears before reporting completion; if an element is an image or marker, re inspect the tree instead of attempting to fill it.
skills.when_to_apply: When OpenStreetMap’s directions page is already open and the accessibility tree shows routing markers alongside separate labeled input textboxes. Particularly useful after a locator error or when nearby element IDs are easy to confuse.

skills.title: Interpret Disabled Map Export Controls
skills.principle: On the map export page, inspect the Export control’s accessibility state before attempting it. If it is disabled, treat that as direct evidence that the selected bounding box exceeds standard export limits. Cite the page’s fallback message and offer the visible “Manually select a different area” control, zooming in, or listed alternatives such as Overpass API.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked why a map area cannot be exported and the export page shows a disabled Export button, a bounding box, and fallback download options.

skills.title: Verify Export Limits Directly
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Export” page and inspect its explicit area-size warning or export controls. Use the displayed bounding box, dimensions, or error message to identify why export may fail; do not infer export limits from zoom-button responsiveness or map tile changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked why a visible OpenStreetMap area may be too large for export, especially when zoom changes are ambiguous. Ensure the Export navigation link is available before diagnosing.

skills.title: Verify Empty Collection States
skills.principle: Navigate to the page representing the requested collection and inspect its primary content state. If it explicitly reports an empty result, such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the browse task as complete, report that no items are available, and mention any visible prerequisite action only as an optional next step.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a website collection or feed, after reaching the correct page and confirming its heading and empty-state message rather than assuming items exist.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Empty Results
skills.principle: Navigate to the task-specific GPS Traces page and inspect its main content. If it explicitly shows an empty-state message such as “Nothing here yet,” treat that as the complete result, report that no recent uploads are available, and terminate instead of exploring unrelated sections or upload flows.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing recent GPS trace uploads and the Public GPS Traces page is accessible but displays an explicit empty-state message. No login or upload capability is required to report the result.

skills.title: Use the About Page for Community Information
skills.principle: For OpenStreetMap questions about community and contributors, open the visible “About” navigation link. Read the “Community Driven” and “Local Knowledge” sections, including contributor types, mapping methods, and linked resources. Summarize the observed facts and stop once the requested information is covered.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task asks who contributes to OpenStreetMap, how contributors maintain data, or where community resources are found, and the page navigation exposes an “About” link.

skills.title: Use Visible Community Information
skills.principle: When the current page visibly answers the request, extract its key facts and report them immediately. For community queries, summarize the page’s statements about participants, formal local chapters, and informal groups, then stop rather than opening supplementary links unless required details are missing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on informational pages when headings, paragraphs, and lists already contain relevant answer content and no explicit requirement demands external sources or deeper research.

skills.title: Verify Existing Route Before Acting
skills.principle: When a map directions page is already populated, verify that the From and To locations match the request, the travel mode is correct, and a Directions result shows distance, time, and route steps. If all are present, report the result immediately and terminate without submitting the form again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map routing tasks when the current page already displays a route. Prerequisite: confirm both endpoints, requested travel mode, and completed route summary match the user’s request.

skills.title: Target Direction Inputs by Role
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap directions page, interact with the labeled “From” and “To” textboxes, not the adjacent marker images. Enter both coordinates, explicitly choose “Foot (OSRM)” from the travel-mode combobox, then click “Go.” Verify the combobox value and resulting route or directions before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting route directions with coordinates and the accessibility tree shows marker images near separately labeled From/To textboxes, especially when the default travel mode is not walking.

skills.title: Navigate Via Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to identify the navigation link whose label matches the requested destination, activate it, then verify the resulting page heading or URL. If the page reports an empty state such as “Nothing here yet,” report that state while confirming the requested page was reached; do not attempt unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests opening a named page from a website’s current view, especially when the destination appears as a clearly labeled navigation link and the resulting page may legitimately contain no records.

skills.title: Change Route Transportation Mode
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the directions page’s transportation combobox and identify the requested mode option.
2. Use the combobox selection operation rather than clicking an individual native option, which may be invisible.
3. Confirm the combobox value and route engine reflect the requested mode, then click “Go” if needed to recalculate.
4. Report completion only after the updated directions are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a route’s travel mode on a directions page, especially when the accessibility tree exposes native <option> elements that cannot be clicked directly.

skills.title: Verify Mode Then Terminate
skills.principle: Select the requested transportation option in the directions mode control. Confirm the control shows the target mode and the refreshed directions panel reflects the new route. Once both are visible, report completion and stop; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for another state change.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map directions tasks when the requested mode can be changed through a transportation-mode combobox and the page refreshes route details after selection.

skills.title: Verify Route Orientation After Reversing
skills.principle: On a directions page, compare the current “From” and “To” values with the requested origin and destination. Click “Reverse Directions” only when they are opposite, then verify both fields and the route summary show the requested orientation. If the fields already match, leave the route unchanged and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map direction tasks requiring reversed routing, when “From,” “To,” and “Reverse Directions” controls are visible and the desired origin-destination order can be checked after the action.

skills.title: Populate and Verify Route Endpoints
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and enter the requested origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Verify both fields visibly contain the intended coordinates before using “Reverse Directions.”
3. After reversal, verify the endpoints are swapped, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm a route result or directions panel appears; do not infer success from an unchanged form.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction tasks when the directions form opens with empty or unknown endpoint fields, especially when reversing an existing route before requesting directions.

skills.title: Use Overpass When Export Is Disabled
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Export” page and inspect the primary “Export” button. If it is disabled or fails, use the “Overpass API” fallback link, which downloads OpenStreetMap data for the displayed bounding box. After the link is activated, report that the download was initiated and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting the current OpenStreetMap view, especially a view containing a route, and the export page shows populated bounding-box coordinates but its primary Export button is disabled.

skills.title: Verify Export Control Identity
skills.principle: Use the accessible label and current page state to distinguish controls before acting. On OpenStreetMap, select the link labeled “Export,” not the unlabeled Edit menu button. After activation, confirm the page heading and URL indicate the Export page; if a tooltip intercepts clicks, move focus away or dismiss it before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a map view or route and multiple nearby controls have unlabeled elements or numeric accessibility IDs, especially when clicks open an unexpected menu or a tooltip blocks interaction.

skills.title: Update a Route Starting Point
skills.principle:
1. Locate the directions form’s “From” textbox and replace its existing value with the requested starting place.
2. Click “Go” to submit the change and recalculate the route.
3. Confirm completion when the field resolves to the requested location and the directions panel shows refreshed route details.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on an OpenStreetMap directions page when a route already exists and the task requests changing its starting location while preserving the destination and travel mode.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Route Update
skills.principle: Update the “From” field, click “Go” once, then verify completion by checking that the field resolves to the requested place and the route/directions refresh. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly clicking “Go” or waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions tasks after changing an origin or destination, when the refreshed route, resolved location text, or route URL visibly confirms the requested change.

skills.title: Check Map History by Area
skills.principle:
1. From the current OpenStreetMap view, activate the “History” navigation link.
2. Read the “Changesets” panel for the current map extent.
3. If it states “No changesets in this area,” report that no map edits are available; otherwise summarize the displayed history.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect edit history for the currently displayed map area and the OpenStreetMap page provides a “History” link. Verify the changesets panel before reporting the result.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Map History
skills.principle: Open the map’s “History” page and inspect the Changesets panel. If it displays “No changesets in this area,” treat that as the requested result, report that no edits were found, and terminate. Do not repeatedly zoom, switch areas, or search elsewhere unless the user explicitly requests broader investigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking edit history for the currently displayed map area and the History/Changesets panel visibly reports no changesets.

skills.title: Share Directions Using the Link Field
skills.principle:
1. With the requested route already displayed, activate the map’s “Share” control.
2. In the “Link or HTML” section, read the populated link textbox rather than selecting unrelated formats.
3. Return that URL as the shareable link and stop once it is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions pages when a route is already calculated and the task requests sharing it via a link. Ensure the Share dialog is open and the Link field contains the current route URL.

skills.title: Target Controls by Role, Not Nearby IDs
skills.principle: When an action fails, re-inspect the accessibility tree and select the element matching the required role and label. For directions, fill the actual textboxes labeled “From” and “To”; do not use nearby marker images. After a successful click or fill, verify focus or value changed before continuing, and change strategy instead of repeating the same failed action.
