skills.when_to_apply: Use on map or directions forms when element IDs are dense or adjacent decorative images share the same region, especially after a locator error or when repeated clicks leave the interface unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Satellite Availability Before Switching
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and inspect the listed base layers. Select satellite only when an explicitly labeled satellite or imagery layer is present; otherwise, recognize that the requested view is unavailable and report that limitation instead of testing unrelated thematic layers or zoom controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests satellite imagery and the Layers menu is visible. Apply after checking all listed base-layer labels and confirming whether an explicit satellite option exists.

skills.title: Inspect Layers Before Selecting
skills.principle: Open the map’s Layers control once, then inspect the current accessibility tree for the exact available layer labels and element targets. Select the requested layer only if it is listed; otherwise, avoid invented bids or repeated toggles and report that the requested layer is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map layer through a Layers panel, especially after the panel opens but the requested option is not visible in the current accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Share Image for PNG Downloads
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, use the map’s “Share” control rather than the data “Export” page. In the Share dialog, open “Image,” confirm the “Format” selector is set to “PNG,” then click “Download.” Verify that a download is triggered before reporting completion; the data Export button may be disabled and does not create a PNG image.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to download the visible OpenStreetMap view as an image, especially when the Export page offers data export and its Export button is disabled.

skills.title: Download Map as PNG
skills.principle: Open the map’s Share control, use the Image section rather than data Export, confirm the Format selector is set to PNG, then click Download. Verify that the browser reports or produces the requested PNG file before declaring completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page offers Share and Export controls and the task requests an image file, especially PNG. Use the Image subsection and confirm the selected format before downloading.

skills.title: Use Share for Map Image Formats
skills.principle: Distinguish data export from map-image download. For image format options, open the map’s “Share” control and inspect its download section for formats such as image links. Use “Export” only when the task requests map data or a selected-area dataset. If the current page shows licensing, bounding-box fields, and data-source links instead of image formats, return to the map and open “Share” rather than repeatedly scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check downloadable map image formats and the map interface exposes both “Export” and “Share”; image-format options require the map-sharing panel, while “Export” presents geographic data downloads.

skills.title: Enable a Map Overlay
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control to reveal available overlays.
2. Locate the requested overlay checkbox by its visible label and select it when unchecked.
3. Confirm completion by verifying the checkbox is checked and, when applicable, overlay imagery or tracks appears on the map; then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task requires displaying a named overlay and the map exposes a Layers control with labeled checkboxes. Verify the resulting checked state before stopping.

skills.title: Compare Map Layers Systematically
skills.principle:
1. Open the map's “Layers” control and identify every available base-layer option.
2. Select each layer in sequence, allowing the map tiles to render after every change.
3. Confirm the displayed tiles or attribution reflect the selected layer, then report the complete set compared.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to compare map styles for a displayed route or region, with the map already loaded and a visible “Layers” control containing selectable base layers.

skills.title: Verify Layers Before Acting
skills.principle: After opening the map’s “Layers” control, inspect the updated accessibility tree immediately. If a “Map Layers” panel and named options are visible, enumerate those labels and compare them directly; do not repeatedly click, wait, or hover unless details are missing. Report the comparison once the visible options are captured.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking to compare layer options, when the Layers control has been activated and the observation shows a Map Layers panel with labeled choices.

skills.title: Trust Explicit Empty-State Messages
skills.principle: When the requested content page explicitly reports an empty state such as “No diary entries,” treat that as the current result. Report that no readable entries are available and stop, rather than exploring unrelated navigation links or attempting login without provided credentials.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a target listing page loads successfully and its accessibility tree shows an explicit empty-state heading or message, with no item links or entries to open.

skills.title: Open Map Layers Settings
skills.principle: Click the map control labeled “Layers,” then verify that the “Map Layers” panel appears with base-style choices and overlay checkboxes. Once the panel is visible, report access without changing any settings unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks to access layer settings and the accessibility tree shows a map control labeled “Layers.” Completion is confirmed by a visible “Map Layers” heading and layer or overlay options.

skills.title: Confirm Layers Panel and Finish
skills.principle: Click the map control labeled “Layers,” then verify the settings panel is open by finding the “Map Layers” heading and layer options. Once this confirmation appears, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For map tasks requesting access to layer settings, after the map is loaded and a visible “Layers” control is available.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the accessibility tree for a navigation link whose label matches the requested destination.
2. Activate that semantic link rather than relying on coordinates or hard-coded element IDs.
3. Verify the resulting URL and page heading/content match the requested destination, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to navigate to a named page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link. Verify the destination before taking further actions.

skills.title: Terminate After Verifying Help Page
skills.principle: Click the navigation link labeled “Help,” then verify the destination by checking the URL or the “Getting Help” heading and listed support resources. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a site’s Help page and the accessibility tree shows the Help link or, after clicking, the expected Help-page heading and resource links.

skills.title: Stop After Homepage Confirmation
skills.principle: Navigate using the site logo or homepage control, then verify the page shows the homepage identity, such as the welcome heading and homepage navigation. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When returning to a website homepage, especially after clicking a branding link and observing homepage-specific content. Stop as soon as the destination state is visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Use Navigation Labels and Verify Destination
skills.principle: Select the navigation link whose visible label matches the requested page, then verify the resulting URL and accessibility-tree content. Once the destination page is confirmed and its relevant information is visible, summarize the findings and stop; do not issue an empty or redundant action.
skills.when_to_apply: When a web task requires visiting an informational page from an existing site, especially when the target navigation label is visible and completion is indicated by the destination URL and page headings.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Completion
skills.principle: Once the target page is visibly loaded and its content satisfies the request, treat the task as complete. Report completion immediately and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or waiting for further changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigation succeeds and the accessibility tree confirms the requested destination and relevant content are present, especially for informational page-visit tasks.

skills.title: Recover From Signup Email Conflicts
skills.principle: When signup reports that an email is already taken, choose a genuinely unique usable address, immediately update Email Confirmation to the identical value, and recheck all required fields because validation may clear them. Submit again only after the form is consistent, then verify a success or confirmation state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on account-registration forms when submission returns an email-availability error or changing the email leaves Email Confirmation mismatched. A usable unique email and access to its confirmation channel are prerequisites.

skills.title: Resolve Duplicate Registration Fields
skills.principle: When submission reports that an email or display name is already taken, replace every rejected unique field with genuinely new values. Update email confirmation to exactly match the new email, refill any cleared password fields, submit again, and verify that the page leaves the sign-up form or shows successful account creation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s Sign Up form after submission displays “has already been taken” for email or display name. Ensure all required fields remain complete before resubmitting.

skills.title: Select the Exact Map Search Result
skills.principle:
1. Review search results for the entry whose full name and place type match the requested location.
2. Select that result rather than a similarly named landmark or feature.
3. Confirm the resulting page identifies the target and the map is centered on or highlights it, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map search returns multiple similarly named results, especially when the request specifies an administrative place, city, region, or country.

skills.title: Retrieve Directions Between Two Points
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To”; optionally choose the requested travel mode.
3. Click “Go” and verify a “Directions” panel appears with route details such as distance, time, or turn-by-turn steps.
4. Report completion once the route is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap when the task requires routing between two named locations and the directions feature is accessible. Both endpoints must be entered before selecting “Go”.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: After activating a navigation link, inspect the next accessibility tree and URL before retrying. If the target page is loaded—here indicated by the directions form with “From,” “To,” and “Go”—treat the task as complete and stop. Do not click the original link again, especially when it is hidden or stale.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking a feature link when the page may navigate asynchronously or the original control may remain in the accessibility tree. Confirm the destination state before issuing another action.

skills.title: Explore Sections Through Semantic Navigation
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation link matching the requested section, then verify the destination by its URL and page heading. Read the accessible content across its headings, lists, and paragraphs, scrolling only when needed. Once the complete section is visible and understood, summarize the findings and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore or review a named website section and the accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link, page heading, and structured content.

skills.title: Validate Action Syntax Before Retrying
skills.principle: When a browser action repeatedly returns an empty-action error, stop repeating the malformed payload. Reissue a syntactically complete action using the observed element’s accessible label or a valid reference, then verify navigation by checking the URL and page heading. Once the target section is displayed, terminate successfully.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when clicking a visible navigation link produces an empty-action or parsing error, especially when the page remains unchanged and the target link is still present.

skills.title: Use the Map Zoom-In Control
skills.principle: Locate the map’s clearly labeled “Zoom In” control and activate it once. Confirm completion from observable changes such as a higher map zoom level, refreshed tiles, or a reduced scale-bar distance, then report success without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page is open and the task requests a closer view. The map controls must be visible or discoverable in the accessibility tree, including a labeled “Zoom In” control.

skills.title: Use the Correct Zoom Control
skills.principle: Locate the map control whose accessible name is exactly "Zoom In" and activate its current element identifier. Do not infer the identifier from nearby controls. Verify completion by checking that the map view zoom level increases or the displayed map scale changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests zooming in and the accessibility tree exposes multiple nearby links, buttons, or unlabeled controls. Use the current observation’s exact "Zoom In" label and identifier.

skills.title: Use the Map Location Control
skills.principle: When the map accessibility tree exposes a button labeled “Show My Location,” click that control directly. This initiates location retrieval and may trigger browser permission handling; after the click, report completion and stop rather than taking unrelated map actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking to locate the user’s current position, when the map is loaded and its accessibility tree contains the clearly labeled location control.

skills.title: Dismiss Overlays Before Map Controls
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the map for blocking dialogs or welcome overlays and close them first.
2. Click the control labeled “Show My Location” once.
3. Verify success by checking for a recentered map, location marker, or permission/error feedback; do not repeat unchanged clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map control remains unchanged after clicking, especially while a welcome dialog or modal overlay is visible. Close the overlay before interacting with underlying map controls.

skills.title: Verify the Map Share Control
skills.principle: Use the accessibility label to activate the map’s “Share” control, not a nearby unlabeled element. After clicking, inspect the updated page for a share panel, generated URL, or changed state. Only report completion when the shared-view URL is visibly available; otherwise continue investigating the share interface.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing the current view in an interactive map and multiple nearby controls have ambiguous or unlabeled accessibility-tree identifiers.

skills.title: Refresh Element References After Navigation
skills.principle: After any navigation or rerender, re-inspect the current accessibility tree before acting; element bids are not stable across page states. If the target result opens a page identifying the requested place and the map remains centered there, treat that as completion and stop rather than repeating stale clicks or searches.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map search result click changes the page, an element bid becomes invalid, or the current page already shows the target place’s relation/details and map location.

skills.title: Inspect Map Layers Panel
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and read the resulting “Map Layers” panel. Report base layers separately from overlays, preserving whether each overlay is enabled or disabled. Once all listed options are captured and the panel answers the request, report the findings without changing layer selections.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which map layers are available for a searched or displayed location, and the map page exposes a visible “Layers” control. Verify the panel is open before summarizing options.

skills.title: Use the Correct Map Control
skills.principle: On map pages, distinguish the labeled “Layers” control from adjacent unlabeled controls such as “Map Key.” Activate “Layers” by its accessible name, then inspect the newly exposed layer list or controls. Do not navigate to the control’s hash URL or substitute the map legend; verify completion by confirming layer names or selectable overlays appear in the accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which map layers are available and the map toolbar contains both “Layers” and nearby unlabeled or legend controls. Prefer the labeled Layers control and inspect the resulting UI before trying unrelated navigation.

skills.title: Generate Cycling Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations.
3. Select “Bicycle (OSRM)” from the transport dropdown, then click “Go.”
4. Confirm a “Directions” panel appears with distance, time, and route steps before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap route requests requiring bicycle directions between two named places, after the directions form exposes “From,” “To,” transport selection, and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Target the Actual Direction Fields
skills.principle: Use the accessibility role and label to identify controls: fill the textbox labeled “From” and the textbox labeled “To,” not nearby map marker images. Select the requested travel mode, enter both locations, click “Go,” and verify that route details or a rendered route appears.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap directions panel shows labeled From/To textboxes alongside draggable marker images. Confirm the target locator resolves to an editable textbox before calling fill.

skills.title: Configure Walking Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's directions tool and enter the requested origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Select the walking mode, such as “Foot (OSRM),” rather than the default driving mode.
3. Activate “Go” and verify a Directions panel appears with distance, walking time, and turn-by-turn steps before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for walking-route requests when the map directions form is available and its travel-mode selector may default to driving. Stop after the resulting route details visibly confirm the requested trip.

skills.title: Report Route Results After Calculation
skills.principle: Once the directions page shows a completed route, extract the requested mode, endpoints, distance, travel time, and any needed turn-by-turn details. Provide these results in the final response, then terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after clicking “Go” on a map directions page and observing a route summary such as “Distance” and “Time,” confirming the requested travel mode is selected.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Directions
skills.principle: On the directions page, inspect the current accessibility tree and target the textboxes by their observed element bids, not their visible labels. Fill the origin and destination, keep or select the requested travel mode, activate “Go,” and verify that the resulting panel displays a route and estimated travel time.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions form visibly contains “From,” “To,” a travel-mode selector, and “Go,” but label-based BrowserGym actions report that elements cannot be found.

skills.title: Locate Target Before Zooming
skills.principle:
1. Search for the requested map area in the Search textbox and submit with Go before changing zoom.
2. Confirm the map view relocates to the target area, then activate Zoom In until the requested street detail is visible.
3. Stop after verifying the map is centered on the target and detailed streets are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring detailed streets in a named place when the initial view may be centered on a different nearby area.

skills.title: Separate Zooming From Map Panning
skills.principle: Use the labeled “Zoom In” control only to increase detail, verifying the map URL or scale after each click. Do not click individual tile images; they are intercepted by the map container. Once the required detail is reached, pan by dragging the map container or use the search result for the target area, then verify the displayed center is actually the requested location.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires both a specific area and detailed streets, especially when the initial search center may be outside the target area and scrolling changes zoom rather than panning.

skills.title: Copy a Map View Link
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Share” control, choose the full “Link” option rather than HTML or Geo URI, then copy the populated link textbox with ControlOrMeta+C. Confirm the textbox contains the current map view URL before reporting that it is ready to paste.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page is displaying the requested location and the task asks for a shareable link. The page must expose a Share control and a generated Link field.

skills.title: Compare Map Layers Systematically
skills.principle: Open the map’s Layers control, identify every available base layer, and select each one in turn. After each selection, verify the map refreshes and compare how clearly the target features are displayed. Select or recommend the layer with the clearest visual emphasis, then report the comparison and how to switch layers.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task asks for the best view of a feature and multiple named base layers are available. Ensure the target location is already loaded and the Layers control is visible.

skills.title: Compare Layers Then Stop
skills.principle: Open the Layers control, inspect each available layer once, and compare it against the task’s stated criterion. Select the best-fitting layer, verify that the map tiles or attribution reflect the selection, then report completion and stop instead of repeatedly cycling through already inspected layers.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks you to find or choose the best view among multiple available layers, and the Layers panel lists selectable basemaps with visible map updates after each selection.

skills.title: Download Map Image Through Share
skills.principle: Open the map’s Share control rather than relying on the data Export page. In the Share panel, locate the Image section, confirm the format selector is set to PNG, then activate Download. Verify that the browser reports or otherwise reflects a completed file download before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests a PNG image and the map interface exposes Share and Export controls. The map must already be centered on the requested area; use the Image options in Share, not the XML/data export warning.

skills.title: Extract Geo URI From Map Share
skills.principle:
1. Read the map’s current center coordinates from the URL hash or visible map state.
2. Open the map’s “Share” control and choose the geo URI option.
3. Report the displayed `geo:latitude,longitude` value, confirming it matches the requested map view; stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests a geo URI for the current view and the page exposes a Share control or URL containing map center coordinates.

skills.title: Read and Report the Geo URI
skills.principle: Open the map’s Share panel and locate the “Geo URI” link. Read its displayed href/value directly and report it as the answer. Do not treat the link as a textbox, repeatedly click it, or perform extra actions once the URI is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map-sharing task requests a geo URI and the Share panel visibly contains a “Geo URI” link with coordinates and zoom information.

skills.title: Choose Image Download Over Data Export
skills.principle: For a downloadable map image, adjust the map’s zoom and center first, then use the map’s sharing or image-download control rather than the data “Export” page. The Export form downloads map data for a bounding box and can fail with node-limit errors; verify that the resulting action produces an image download or image link.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task requests a map image or screenshot and the page offers both map controls such as “Share” and a separate “Export” data form.

skills.title: Shrink Export Area Before Downloading
skills.principle:
1. On the OpenStreetMap Export page, treat zoom level and export area as separate controls.
2. Use “Manually select a different area” or edit the bounding-box fields to select only the requested locality.
3. Click “Export,” and if the page reports too many nodes, reduce the bounding box substantially and retry.
4. Confirm success by checking that the download completes rather than stopping at a node-limit error.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting map data or images for a detailed locality, especially after an export reports a 50,000-node limit. Zooming in alone may not sufficiently reduce the selected bounding box.

skills.title: Open History for the Current Map
skills.principle: After locating the target place on OpenStreetMap, use the navigation link labeled “History” rather than searching again. The link preserves the current map extent. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Changesets” and the changeset list or “No changesets in this area” message is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after the target location has been found and the map is centered on it, especially when the task asks for that area’s edit history.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree for the requested page heading, URL, and relevant content. If already present, report completion and stop. Otherwise, activate the navigation link matching the task, then verify the destination contains the expected heading and actionable links before concluding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current page may already satisfy the request and semantic navigation links are visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Recheck Navigation Targets After Page Changes
skills.principle: After navigation, re-read the current accessibility tree before acting. Locate the target link by its accessible name and current role, rather than reusing an old element ID. Confirm completion through the resulting URL or page heading; if the target page is already open, stop instead of clicking repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a page navigation changes accessibility-tree element IDs or ordering, especially when repeated clicks leave the URL unchanged or the visible heading does not match the requested destination.

skills.title: Use Navigation Labels to Reach Help
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose label matches the requested destination, activate it, then verify the resulting page by its URL, heading, or relevant content. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion without taking unnecessary additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map website task requests a documentation or resource page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link or shows that destination already loaded.

skills.title: Use Navigation Labels to Reach Informational Pages
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose accessible label matches the requested informational topic, activate it, then verify the destination through the page URL or heading. Read the relevant sections and report the requested facts only after confirming the target page is loaded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a website’s accessibility tree exposes a direct navigation link for the requested policy, licensing, help, or informational page.

skills.title: Terminate After Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target page is visible and its expected heading or content confirms successful navigation, stop issuing browser actions. Report completion immediately; if the task asks to learn information, include the relevant observed facts in the final response rather than repeating noop actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigating to a requested informational page when the accessibility tree shows the expected page title, heading, or content and no additional interaction is required.

skills.title: Disambiguate Search Results Before History
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “History” page, then search for the requested place.
2. In “Search Results,” select the result whose geographic type and name match the request, distinguishing a city from a state or other feature.
3. Confirm the map centers on that selected place, then use “History” again if needed.
4. Stop only when the page heading shows “Changesets” and the URL remains on `/history` centered on the target.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an OpenStreetMap location search returns multiple similarly named results and the task requires that location’s History page. Select the intended geographic scope before verifying the History view.

skills.title: Search OpenStreetMap Locations
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested location in the OpenStreetMap textbox labeled “Search”.
2. Activate the adjacent “Go” button to submit the query.
3. Confirm completion when a “Search Results” panel appears with matching places and the map recenters on the result area.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap location-search tasks when the map page exposes a Search textbox and Go button. Stop after results are displayed and the map has visibly recentered.

skills.title: Stop After Search Results Appear
skills.principle:
1. Fill the OpenStreetMap Search textbox with the requested location.
2. Activate the Go button.
3. Confirm the map recenters and a Search Results panel appears; this verifies the search succeeded.
4. Stop instead of opening a result or repeatedly using noop actions unless the task explicitly requests details about a result.
skills.when_to_apply: For OpenStreetMap tasks asking only to search for a location, after Go produces Search Results and the map view updates.

skills.title: Use the Map View’s Export Link
skills.principle: From an OpenStreetMap view already centered on the requested location, activate the navigation link labeled “Export.” Confirm completion when the page heading is “Export,” the URL path is the export page, and the bounding-box fields and export options are visible; then report completion without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the requested place is already displayed on OpenStreetMap and the task is to reach its Export page, rather than change the map area or download data.

skills.title: Generate OpenStreetMap Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” from the map page.
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To”; retain or select the requested travel mode.
3. Click “Go” after both locations resolve.
4. Confirm a “Directions” result with distance, travel time, turn-by-turn steps, and a mapped route before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks requesting directions between two locations, when the directions form exposes “From,” “To,” a travel-mode selector, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Report Results After Routing
skills.principle: After clicking “Go,” verify that the page shows a “Directions” heading plus distance, time, and route steps. Then provide those results in the task response and terminate; do not rely on repeated `noop()` actions as the final answer.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap direction tasks once both locations resolve and the directions panel visibly displays a calculated route.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Export Page
skills.principle: After clicking the map site's “Export” navigation entry, verify that the page heading is “Export” and the URL is the export route for the target map view. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not zoom, select areas, or press “Export” unless the task explicitly requests data downloading.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks only to navigate to a map site's Export page and the resulting page visibly shows the Export heading and export route.

skills.title: Verify History Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Open the map’s “History” navigation entry for the current viewport, then inspect the resulting “Changesets” panel. Treat the task as complete when the panel displays either changesets or the explicit message “No changesets in this area.” Report that observed result and stop; do not repeat the same message action after completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view edits or changesets for the currently displayed OpenStreetMap area and the History link is available in the map navigation.

skills.title: Verify Destination Page State
skills.principle: Navigate using the semantically labeled destination link, then inspect the resulting page title, URL, and main content. Once the requested page is reached, report its observable state—including empty-state text or available follow-up options—and stop without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation requests where success means reaching a named page and observing its contents, especially when the destination may show either records or a clear empty state.

skills.title: Confirm Destination and Report Completion
skills.principle: Navigate through the visible “GPS Traces” link, then verify the destination by checking the page heading or URL. Once the GPS Traces page is displayed—even if it says “Nothing here yet”—report that the page was reached and terminate without repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a browsing task asks only to visit a specific page and the destination is visibly confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive empty-state message.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current page and accessibility tree first. If the requested destination is already open, confirm it using the page heading, URL, or relevant form controls, then report completion without navigating or performing extra actions. Otherwise, activate the clearly labeled navigation link matching the requested destination and verify the resulting page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial page may already be the requested destination or contains an obvious link to it; verify the destination after any navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Page Arrival
skills.principle: Navigate using the semantically labeled link, then verify the destination through its URL and distinctive page heading or content. Once the requested page is visibly loaded and confirmed, report completion and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple page-navigation tasks when the target link is available in the accessibility tree and the destination can be confirmed by its URL or unique heading.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Identify the navigation link whose accessible name matches the requested page, activate it, and verify the destination by checking the resulting URL or page heading. Once the target page visibly contains the requested resource categories or content, report completion without additional navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for website tasks requiring navigation to a named section when the accessibility tree exposes a matching link and the destination can be confirmed by its heading or visible content.

skills.title: Switch Map Layers Through Layers
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, select the requested alternative layer from the labeled layer list, and verify completion by checking that the map tiles or attribution reflect the chosen style. Once the layer is visibly active, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap-style map pages when the task requests changing the visual layer and a “Layers” control is visible. Ensure the requested layer appears in the layer chooser.

skills.title: Stop After Layer Change
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” control and select a different labeled layer.
2. Verify completion when the map tiles or attribution reflect the selected layer, or the map state updates accordingly.
3. Once verified, report completion and terminate; do not repeatedly click the already-selected layer.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map layer through a visible “Layers” menu, especially after the map imagery, attribution, or URL visibly updates to the selected layer.

skills.title: Verify Location Recenter Before Reporting
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then inspect the updated map state rather than assuming success. Confirm that the viewport changes to the current location or a location indicator appears; only then report completion. If no visible change occurs, continue troubleshooting the location request instead of claiming the map was centered.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires centering on the user’s current location and the click produces no explicit success confirmation. A post-click map update or location indicator is required before declaring completion.

skills.title: Verify Map Recenter Completion
skills.principle: After activating the map’s location control, wait for the map to update and inspect the resulting state for an observable location marker, changed center, or other confirmation. Only report success when the map visibly reflects the user’s location; otherwise investigate the unchanged state rather than assuming the click succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task requires centering on the current location and the initial click produces no explicit success message or terminal observation.

skills.title: Select Walking Mode Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions form and enter the requested origin and destination.
2. Change the travel-mode combobox from its default to “Foot (OSRM)” before submitting.
3. Click “Go” and verify the Directions panel shows distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps; then report the result once and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap directions tasks requesting walking routes when the directions form provides From, To, a travel-mode selector, and a Go button.

skills.title: Select Exact Routing Mode
skills.principle: Use the directions form’s transportation combobox and select the exact available walking option, including complete punctuation such as "Foot (OSRM)". Verify the combobox visibly changes from the default driving mode before clicking "Go"; do not proceed with directions while the wrong mode remains selected.
skills.when_to_apply: When calculating walking directions in OpenStreetMap, after entering valid From and To locations and before submitting the directions form.

skills.title: Verify Zoom Level Before Stopping
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom In” control, then verify the map state changed to a closer view, such as an increased zoom level or smaller scale-bar distance. Stop and report completion once the requested closer view is achieved; do not continue clicking solely because the control remains available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to zoom in on a map and no exact target zoom level is specified. Use the visible “Zoom In” control and confirm that the map location remains centered while detail increases.

skills.title: Copy a Shareable Map View Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Share” control to reveal sharing options.
2. Select the “Link” option and identify the textbox containing the current map URL.
3. Copy the textbox contents with the platform’s copy shortcut.
4. Confirm the link is copied, then report that it can be shared.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map-view sharing task is requested and the page exposes a “Share” control with a generated Link option and URL textbox.

skills.title: Use the Correct Share Control
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree and activate the element whose accessible name is exactly “Share,” not a nearby unlabeled map control. After clicking, re-read the page for a share panel, link, or changed state. If nothing changes, stop repeating the same element and reassess the control identity before trying alternatives.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing a map view and the page exposes multiple nearby links or controls, especially when the observed “Share” label belongs to a different element than the focused or clicked control.

skills.title: Follow Direct Contribution Guidance
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Help page, choose the most task-specific resource first, especially “Beginners’ Guide,” rather than a broad documentation index. Open it, inspect the resulting content for contribution instructions, and continue navigating only if it lacks the requested information. Confirm the page contains actionable guidance before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked how to contribute to OpenStreetMap and the Help page presents multiple resources, including a beginner-oriented guide and broader forums or wiki links.

skills.title: Follow Help Resources to Completion
skills.principle: When the site’s Help page lists relevant resources, open the most task-specific link, inspect its destination, and extract the requested guidance. Do not treat merely opening the link as completion; continue until the page provides actionable contribution instructions or another clearly relevant resource.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational tasks when the current page offers Help, Beginners’ Guide, documentation, or similar links but does not itself answer the request.

skills.title: Extract Coordinates from Map URL
skills.principle: Read the current map URL’s fragment, identify its latitude and longitude values, and format them as `geo:latitude,longitude`. Return the URI directly once both coordinates are confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to generate a geo URI for the currently displayed map location and the page URL exposes coordinates in its map fragment.

skills.title: Derive Geo URI From Map Coordinates
skills.principle: Read the map’s current latitude and longitude from the URL hash or the search/location result, then format them as `geo:<latitude>,<longitude>`. Use the coordinate result itself—not a nearby place name—as the authoritative source, and report the URI once the coordinates are confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a geo URI representing the current OpenStreetMap view or location, provided the page URL, search results, or location panel exposes latitude and longitude.

skills.title: Configure Dimensions Before Downloading
skills.principle: In the Share dialog, enable “Set custom dimensions,” then inspect the newly revealed controls and set or verify the requested dimensions. Do not treat the existing “Scale” value as proof that custom dimensions are configured. Click “Download” only after the displayed image dimensions reflect the intended settings.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing a map image through OpenStreetMap’s Share dialog and custom dimensions are requested. Prerequisite: the Share dialog is open and the custom-dimensions option is available.

skills.title: Configure Dimensions Before Sharing
skills.principle: In the map’s Share dialog, enable “Set custom dimensions,” then inspect and use the newly revealed dimension controls rather than relying on the default preview size. Confirm the displayed image dimensions change to the intended custom values, then select the requested sharing output and verify its resulting link, embed code, or download state.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing an OpenStreetMap view with custom image dimensions and the Share dialog exposes a “Set custom dimensions” option plus additional sizing controls.

skills.title: Zoom Until Export Becomes Available
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s Export page and inspect the current zoom, scale reference, and export status.
2. If the page says the area is too large, activate “Zoom In” and recheck the updated bounding box and status.
3. Repeat until the warning disappears and an “Export” button appears; then report the resulting zoom and scale reference.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap export tasks when the current map area is too large for download and the Export page provides a “Zoom In” control and export-status message.

skills.title: Verify Scale Before Adjusting
skills.principle: Read the map’s visible scale indicator after every zoom action. Use “Zoom In” to reduce the displayed distance for finer download detail or “Zoom Out” to enlarge coverage. Stop adjusting once the requested scale is visibly confirmed; do not rely on waiting or assumptions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks you to find or adjust scale for downloading and the page visibly exposes a scale indicator plus Zoom In and Zoom Out controls.

skills.title: Verify Destination Then Stop
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation link matching the requested page, activate it, and verify completion through the resulting URL and page heading/content. Once the destination is confirmed, send one correctly formatted completion message and terminate without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a website to a named page, especially when the accessibility tree exposes semantic navigation links and the destination can be confirmed by its URL or distinctive heading.

skills.title: Open Map History and Verify State
skills.principle: Select the map application's clearly labeled “History” navigation entry. Confirm the destination by checking for the “Changesets” heading and read the resulting status, such as whether changesets exist in the currently visible area. Report that exact state, including an empty-history message, rather than assuming records are present.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view map-change history and the map interface exposes a History navigation entry; use the visible area and zoom level as the scope of the reported result.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target page is visibly loaded and its identifying heading or URL matches the task, treat the task as complete: report completion and terminate immediately. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for additional observations after successful navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after a navigation task when the browser observation confirms the requested destination is open, such as a matching page heading, navigation state, or URL.

skills.title: Verify Diary Availability Before Reading
skills.principle: Open the site's “User Diaries” navigation entry and inspect the resulting page. If it displays “No diary entries,” report that no entries are available and stop; otherwise, read the listed entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read user diaries on OpenStreetMap and the navigation includes a “User Diaries” link. The page must be checked for an explicit empty-state message before attempting further actions.

skills.title: Use the About Page for Overview
skills.principle: For broad “learn more” requests, select the site’s clearly labeled “About” or “Learn More” link. Read the resulting page’s headings and paragraphs, summarize its main purpose, community, policies, and relevant resources, then report completion once the page content answers the request.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the user requests general information about a website or project and the current page exposes an About/Learn More navigation link. Confirm the destination by its URL or page heading before summarizing.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Informational Content
skills.principle: Follow the page’s primary “Learn More” or equivalent link, verify that the destination contains relevant explanatory content, then summarize completion and stop. Do not continue exploring secondary headings or policy links unless the user explicitly requests deeper details.
skills.when_to_apply: When an informational request is satisfied by a clearly labeled destination page and its accessibility tree shows relevant headings and explanatory text.

skills.title: Submit Map Directions Directly
skills.principle: On the OpenStreetMap directions page, fill the “From” textbox with the starting place and the “To” textbox with the destination, then click “Go.” Wait for the page to show a “Directions” heading with distance, time, and turn-by-turn results before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requiring directions between two places when the directions form is visible or the page has already navigated to /directions; avoid retrying an invisible navigation link.

skills.title: Use Valid Locations and Verify Routes
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions tool and enter the actual requested start and destination, using specific, geocodable place names rather than generic placeholders.
2. Choose the requested travel mode if needed, then activate “Go.”
3. Confirm that a route, distance, or directions panel appears; if unchanged, inspect for validation or geocoding errors and correct the locations instead of repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting directions in OpenStreetMap and the form is available, especially when the map remains unchanged after submission or the endpoint fields contain generic, unresolved text.

skills.title: Handle Signup Email Conflicts
skills.principle: When signup reports that an email is already taken, replace it with a genuinely available email and immediately update Email Confirmation to the identical value. Recheck every required field, submit Sign Up, and verify that the page confirms account creation before proceeding to mapping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting mapping through OpenStreetMap’s Start Mapping signup flow and the form displays an email-availability error. Requires a valid email address the user can access for confirmation.

skills.title: Use Where Is This for Map Location
skills.principle:
1. On an OpenStreetMap page, activate the visible “Where is this?” control.
2. Read the resulting Search Results panel, using the coordinate entry and the Nominatim place-name result to identify the displayed location.
3. Report the coordinates and corresponding geographic area only after both results are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to identify the current map location and the OpenStreetMap view exposes a “Where is this?” control. Verify the resulting Search Results panel before answering.

skills.title: Stop After Coordinates Appear
skills.principle: After selecting “Where is this?”, inspect the search results and map state. If the search field shows coordinates and the results include the corresponding coordinate link or map marker, treat the location as identified, report it, and terminate. Do not repeatedly use “Show My Location” or zoom controls unless the requested location is still absent.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap “Where is this?” tasks when the coordinate query, matching search result, or marker appears after activation. These observations are sufficient to answer the location request.

skills.title: Change Map Style Through Layers
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control, choose a different named base-map style, and verify the map refreshes with that style’s tiles or attribution. Inspect overlay checkbox states before changing them; toggle only when required. Once the display visibly updates, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-display tasks when a visible “Layers” control exposes multiple base-map styles or overlays. Confirm the Layers menu is open and verify the selected style or refreshed map before finishing.

skills.title: Verify Layer Changes Before Continuing
skills.principle: After opening Layers, select the desired base-map style and verify success from updated map tiles, attribution, or URL state. If those observations show the new style is active, stop and report completion; do not revert it, repeatedly toggle controls, or declare infeasibility.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map display through a Layers panel, especially when accessibility labels expose list items rather than explicit checkboxes. Use the rendered tiles, attribution, or URL as the completion signal.

skills.title: Submit Map Search and Verify Results
skills.principle: Fill the map page’s Search textbox with the requested location, activate the adjacent Go button, then verify that the page shows a Search Results section and the map updates to the searched area. Once results are visible, report completion without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a map task asks you to search for a location and the page exposes a Search textbox with a Go button. Completion is indicated by displayed search results and an updated map view.

skills.title: Verify Search Completion Before Acting
skills.principle: Enter the location in the Search textbox and activate Go. Confirm completion when a Search Results panel or updated map/search URL appears. For a task requiring only a search, stop immediately; do not open a result. If further navigation is required, re-observe the current accessibility tree and use newly exposed controls rather than stale element identifiers.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap location-search tasks, especially when Go produces results or changes the map. Stop after confirming the requested location search succeeded unless the instruction explicitly asks for result details.

skills.title: Use the Visible Login Link
skills.principle: When a map page exposes a clearly labeled “Log In” link, activate it rather than constructing a URL. Confirm completion by checking for a “Login” heading and username/email, password, and login controls, then stop and report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task is to reach the site’s login page and the current accessibility tree contains a labeled “Log In” navigation link.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: After navigation, verify the destination using observable page evidence such as the expected heading and form controls. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task reaches a page whose accessibility tree clearly identifies the requested destination, such as a Login heading and login fields.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation After Click Errors
skills.principle: When a labeled navigation link repeatedly produces an empty-action error, stop retrying it. Navigate directly to the link’s observed destination URL, then verify the page title or heading and any empty-state message before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a target page is clearly identified in the accessibility tree, clicking its link fails repeatedly, and direct navigation is available.

skills.title: Stop After Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested page, then verify its heading or distinctive content in the accessibility tree. Once the target page is confirmed—even if it shows an empty-state message—report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the requested destination and its identifying content are visible. Treat messages such as "No diary entries" as valid page-state confirmation, not a reason to keep acting.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation Links
skills.principle: When the target page is exposed as a labeled navigation link, activate that link directly rather than interacting with unrelated map controls or content. Verify the destination by checking the page URL and a matching heading, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple OpenStreetMap navigation tasks when the requested destination appears as a labeled link in the accessibility tree, such as “Communities,” “Help,” or “About.”

skills.title: Validate Action Serialization
skills.principle: When a browser action returns an empty-action or parsing error, correct the action payload format before retrying. Emit exactly one valid BrowserGym action, with properly closed arguments and no nested or truncated JSON. Prefer activating the observed link by its accessible role or navigating to its displayed destination, then verify the URL or page content changed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply whenever an intended click repeatedly produces an empty-action, parsing, or ValueError response while the target link remains visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Show My Location
skills.principle: Locate the map control labeled "Show My Location" and activate it. This initiates the browser geolocation request; the map centers on the current location after location permission is granted.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requires centering on the user's current position and the map exposes a "Show My Location" control. Ensure browser location permission is granted if prompted.

skills.title: Retrieve Driving Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map site's "Find directions between two points" interface.
2. Enter the requested origin in "From" and destination in "To"; retain the car mode when driving is requested.
3. Click "Go" and verify a "Directions" result displays the route plus total distance and estimated time.
4. Report those confirmed values and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks requesting driving directions between two locations, once the directions interface exposes "From," "To," a travel-mode selector, and "Go."

skills.title: Report Directions After Verification
skills.principle: After submitting the route request, verify that the page shows a “Directions” heading plus route summary or turn-by-turn results. Then report the requested directions or summary in the task response and terminate immediately; do not continue issuing no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction tasks after entering origin and destination and clicking “Go,” when the resulting page visibly contains route details such as distance, travel time, or navigation steps.

skills.title: Configure and Verify Bicycle Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Fill the “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations, confirming each resolves to the intended place.
3. Select “Bicycle (OSRM)” instead of the default travel mode, then click “Go.”
4. Verify the Directions panel shows the bicycle mode plus distance and time before reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap route requests requiring a specific travel mode, especially when the form defaults to driving and place-name resolution may select an unintended locality.

skills.title: Fill Both Direction Fields
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions interface rather than using the single-location search box.
2. Enter the origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
3. Select the requested travel mode, such as “Bicycle (OSRM),” then click “Go.”
4. Confirm that a route summary or drawn route appears before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for route requests when the map homepage offers a single Search box plus a separate “Find directions between two points” control. The directions form must show populated “From” and “To” fields before submission.

skills.title: Disambiguate Route Destinations
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature and enter the origin and destination in the From and To fields.
2. Submit with Go, then inspect the resolved place names and route summary.
3. If a same-named locality is incorrect or the distance is implausible, refine the location with its city, county, or region and submit again.
4. Finish only when the resolved endpoints and displayed route match the requested places.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when routing between named places that may have duplicate localities. Verify the resolved endpoint names and plausibility of the distance before reporting completion.

skills.title: Stop After Route Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the directions result is displayed, verify the origin and destination fields plus the visible route or Directions panel. When confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of zooming or performing exploratory actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map routing tasks after submitting valid From and To locations and observing a rendered route, route markers, or a Directions panel with distance and travel time.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Destinations Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Enter both route endpoints and submit directions.
2. Inspect the resolved place names and route summary, especially county, distance, and travel time.
3. If a similarly named location is selected or the route is implausibly long, clear the destination, enter a more specific query including region, and resubmit.
4. Extract highways only after the resolved endpoints match the requested locations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use map directions when place names may be ambiguous. Verify the geocoder’s resolved endpoint and plausible route distance before reporting roads or highways.

skills.title: Verify Geocoded Route Endpoints
skills.principle: Before submitting directions, inspect the resolved locations shown in the From and To fields. If a city name resolves to an unintended town, county, or region, refine the query with the state or country and verify the displayed endpoint matches the requested destination. Only then select the driving mode and click Go.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting directions using ambiguous place names, especially when autocomplete expands entries into fully qualified locations. Apply before generating the route and confirm both resolved endpoints match the task.

skills.title: Verify Geolocation After Activation
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Show My Location” control, then verify a concrete state change such as a new map center, location marker, or updated URL. If unchanged, inspect the page or browser for a geolocation permission request or error and address it before retrying once. After bounded retries without evidence of movement, report the limitation instead of repeatedly waiting or clicking.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map offers “Show My Location” and the first activation leaves the map view, control state, and accessibility tree unchanged; browser geolocation access must be available for success.

skills.title: Verify Direction Endpoint Order
skills.principle: Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To” exactly as stated. Use “Reverse Directions” only after both fields contain the original route; it swaps populated endpoints. Before finishing, confirm the displayed fields and route summary begin at the requested origin and end at the requested destination.
skills.when_to_apply: When using a map directions form, especially for reversal requests. Ensure both endpoints are populated before reversing, then verify the resulting “From” and “To” values and generated route direction.

skills.title: Retrieve a Map Route
skills.principle: On the map page, open the link labeled "Find directions between two points." Fill the "From" and "To" fields with the requested locations, retain or select the required travel mode, then click "Go." Confirm the directions page reflects both locations and provides the route before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for directions between two locations when the page exposes a directions link and "From," "To," travel-mode, and "Go" controls.

skills.title: Verify History Navigation
skills.principle: Select the map application's clearly labeled “History” navigation link rather than relying on a URL. Confirm the destination by checking the page title or “Changesets” heading and read the displayed status, including an explicit “No changesets in this area” message. Once verified, report the result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view map edit history and the page exposes a labeled History link. Use the resulting Changesets view as completion evidence, whether it lists changes or explicitly reports none.

skills.title: Navigate Via the Export Link
skills.principle: Use the page navigation to select the clearly labeled “Export” link. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Export” and that export controls or download-source options are visible. If the selected area is too large for direct XML export, report the available alternatives rather than taking unrequested additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks to reach OpenStreetMap’s export interface from the main map page, and the navigation exposes an “Export” link.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Target Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s role and label to select the intended navigation link, distinguishing it from nearby buttons or menu controls. After clicking, verify the URL or page heading changed to the requested destination before reporting completion; if unchanged, retry using the correct target.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a map site with adjacent Edit, History, and Export controls, especially when accessibility IDs are easy to confuse or clicking opens a menu instead of navigating.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Optional Actions
skills.principle: Navigate using the clearly labeled destination link, then inspect the resulting page before pursuing optional actions. Confirm the page title and visible controls, distinguish public browsing from authentication-gated upload, report the available choices and prerequisites, and stop once the requested destination is reached.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a feature page that offers multiple actions, especially when some controls may require login while the destination itself is publicly accessible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: After selecting the relevant navigation entry, verify the resulting page using its heading, URL, or distinctive content. Once the requested GPS Traces page is confirmed, report completion and stop. Do not click adjacent upload, RSS, or browse controls unless the user explicitly requested that follow-up action.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task asks only to reach a page and the accessibility tree shows the target heading or page content. Re-observe after navigation before choosing any additional control.

skills.title: Confirm Target Page and Finish
skills.principle: Navigate using the semantically labeled navigation link, then verify the destination through its URL or distinctive heading and content. Once the requested page is visibly confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks where the requested destination is a page identifiable by a navigation label and a distinctive heading or content after loading.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation Links
skills.principle: Select the navigation link whose accessible name matches the requested destination, activate it, then verify the resulting page heading, URL, or form content confirms arrival. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and stop without entering credentials or performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a page and the current accessibility tree exposes a clearly labeled link for that destination, especially when arrival can be verified by distinctive page content.

skills.title: Search Map Locations and Verify Results
skills.principle:
1. Enter the target place or landmark in the map's Search textbox.
2. Activate the labeled Go control to submit the query.
3. Confirm completion when a Search Results panel identifies the target and the map view or URL centers on its location.
4. Report the displayed location details, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap-style map pages when the task asks you to locate a named place and a Search textbox with a Go control is available.

skills.title: Click the Matching Map Result
skills.principle: After submitting a map search, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree and click the result link whose label matches the requested place. Confirm the page centers or opens details for that place, then report completion and stop. Do not repeat focus actions or reuse element IDs after navigation changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap-style searches when search results are visible and the target place appears as a labeled link. Re-read the current tree before acting because navigation can invalidate previous element IDs.

skills.title: Retrieve Map Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” control.
2. Enter the requested origin in “From” and destination in “To,” allowing each location to resolve.
3. Click “Go” and wait for the route to load.
4. Confirm a “Directions” panel shows distance, travel time, and step-by-step route instructions before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for directions between two named places when the map interface provides “From,” “To,” and “Go” controls.

skills.title: Fill Both Directions Endpoints
skills.principle: On the directions page, explicitly enter the origin in the “From” field and the destination in the “To” field, then click “Go.” Do not assume a prior map search populates the origin. Confirm completion by checking that a route or directions result appears, not merely that the destination was geocoded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap route requests when the directions form is visible, especially after navigating there from a separate place search and the “From” field is still empty.

skills.title: Verify GPS Trace Availability
skills.principle: Navigate to the map site's GPS Traces page and inspect the trace list. If it shows “Nothing here yet,” report that no traces are available and mention the provided upload links; do not upload anything unless explicitly requested. If traces are listed, use the list to view them.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view GPS traces and the GPS Traces navigation entry is available. Check the page's actual contents before attempting uploads or claiming traces exist.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming the Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested GPS Traces page and verify its displayed state. If it shows the expected page, including an explicit empty state such as “Nothing here yet,” treat the viewing task as complete. Do not upload data, open Help, or navigate to unrelated authenticated pages unless the task explicitly requires it.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or open a page and navigation reaches the requested destination, especially when the page clearly reports that no records are available.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Empty Results
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested content page and inspect its main status. If it explicitly reports an empty state such as “No diary entries,” treat that as the confirmed result, report it, and terminate. Do not repeatedly revisit the same page or explore unrelated sections unless the task specifically requests an alternative source.
skills.when_to_apply: When a browsing task asks you to visit or explore a listing page and the page visibly confirms that no matching content exists.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to Discovered Page
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to identify the navigation entry or destination URL matching the user’s requested page, then navigate directly. Verify the resulting page by checking its URL and heading/content. Once the requested page is open and its relevant content is visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a user asks to visit or review a specific page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link or destination URL.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation After Click Errors
skills.principle: When a visible navigation link repeatedly produces an empty-action or execution error, stop retrying the malformed click. Navigate directly to the link’s observed destination, then verify the URL and page heading/content match the requested destination before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple page-navigation tasks when the accessibility tree exposes a target link URL and click attempts return empty actions or unchanged page state.

skills.title: Terminate After Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested page, verify its URL or distinctive heading/content, then immediately report completion and terminate. Do not repeat no-op actions after the target state is visibly confirmed, because they consume interaction turns without advancing the task.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree shows the requested page has loaded and contains its expected heading or content. Once confirmed, provide the task result instead of issuing further browser actions.

skills.title: Report Completion After Verification
skills.principle: After navigating to the requested page, verify the URL and relevant headings or text match the task. Then provide a concise completion response summarizing what was found, and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for informational navigation tasks when the target page is visibly loaded and its content confirms the requested topic or purpose.

skills.title: Parse Coordinates From Map URL
skills.principle: Inspect the current map URL hash and parse the `#map=zoom/latitude/longitude` pattern. Report latitude and longitude in that order, optionally including zoom. Use the URL’s current hash rather than estimating from the rendered map.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the current coordinates on an OpenStreetMap-style page and the address bar or accessibility observation exposes a `#map=` hash.

skills.title: Report Coordinates From Map URL
skills.principle: Read the map URL hash in the form `#map=zoom/latitude/longitude`, extract latitude and longitude, then immediately provide them in the task response. Once the coordinates are reported, terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks for current coordinates and the page URL visibly contains a `#map` fragment with zoom, latitude, and longitude.

skills.title: Report Results After Route Generation
skills.principle: After clicking “Go,” verify that the page shows a Directions panel with route details such as distance, time, or turn instructions. Once confirmed, provide the requested result in the final response and terminate; do not issue repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction tasks after both endpoints are entered, the requested travel mode is selected, and the resulting Directions panel visibly confirms a calculated route.

skills.title: Verify and Navigate to History
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree and current URL first. If the History page is already active, report completion without further actions. Otherwise activate the navigation link labeled “History,” then verify the resulting page title or URL indicates the history/changesets view before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open map edit history and the page may already be open; requires visible navigation and a post-click page-state check.

skills.title: Stop After History Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Click the map application's “History” navigation entry, then verify the page heading or URL indicates the Changesets/History view. Once that state is visible, report completion and terminate; do not search, pan, or adjust the map unless the task explicitly requests finding edits in a particular area.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only asks to open or navigate to the map History page and the History/Changesets view is visibly loaded, even if it reports no changesets.

skills.title: Parse Coordinates From Map URL
skills.principle: When a map page URL contains a fragment such as `#map=zoom/latitude/longitude`, read the coordinate pair directly from that fragment. Ignore the zoom value, preserve the latitude and longitude signs and precision, label them clearly, and report them without unnecessary map interaction.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for the current displayed coordinates when the accessibility-tree observation exposes a URL containing a `map=zoom/latitude/longitude` fragment.

skills.title: Extract Coordinates Before Reporting
skills.principle: Read the map’s coordinate source directly, such as the URL hash containing zoom, latitude, and longitude, or a verified coordinate readout. Confirm the value is actual text, then report the latitude and longitude; never send an unevaluated placeholder or confuse a control tooltip with coordinates.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the current map coordinates and the page URL exposes a map hash or the interface provides a coordinate readout. Verify the selected element’s text actually contains numeric latitude and longitude.

skills.title: Use Where Is This for Map Location
skills.principle: For a map-location task, activate the map’s “Where is this?” control rather than editing or changing layers. Inspect the resulting search results, especially the geocoder/Nominatim entry, and report the displayed administrative area shown there. Stop once the result identifies the location.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the map view has a “Where is this?” control and the task asks which area, town, county, or region is currently displayed. Prefer this even if editing is disabled or unavailable.

skills.title: Read Map State From URL
skills.principle: For a map-area question, inspect the URL hash for the current zoom and center coordinates, then identify the geographic region containing that center. Use the visible map only to confirm context; do not scroll the webpage or repeatedly change zoom unless the task explicitly asks for navigation. Report the area once the center and map context support it.
skills.when_to_apply: When an OpenStreetMap view has a URL hash such as #map=zoom/latitude/longitude and the task asks what region or area is currently displayed.

skills.title: Calculate Bicycle Directions Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open OpenStreetMap’s “Find directions between two points” page.
2. Fill the actual “From” and “To” textboxes, not nearby marker images; confirm each field contains the intended place.
3. Select “Bicycle (OSRM)” in the travel-mode combobox, then click “Go”.
4. Confirm a “Directions” panel appears with route instructions, distance, and time before reporting completion.
