skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap routing tasks requiring bicycle directions between two named places, once the directions form and its labeled From, To, mode, and Go controls are visible.

skills.title: Use the Dedicated Directions Form
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” before entering route locations; the map search box is not a From/To field.
2. Fill the separate “From” and “To” textboxes with the origin and destination.
3. Select “Bicycle (OSRM)” in the travel-mode combobox, then click the form’s “Go” button.
4. Confirm the route result appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: For OpenStreetMap route tasks when the page initially shows a general Search box. Prerequisite: navigate to the dedicated directions page and verify its From, To, travel-mode, and Go controls.

skills.title: Use Map Zoom Controls
skills.principle: Identify the map’s labeled “Zoom In” and “Zoom Out” controls from the accessibility tree, then click the control matching the requested direction. Confirm completion by checking that the map view or URL zoom level changes, and stop once the requested zoom adjustment is achieved.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page exposes accessible zoom controls and the task requests changing map scale. Use only the needed direction and verify the resulting map state before reporting completion.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Zoom Change
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom In” or “Zoom Out” control once, then verify the URL hash or map scale changed. Once the zoom level has changed, treat the task as complete and stop; do not keep experimenting, refresh, or reverse the adjustment.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change a map’s zoom level without a specified target, and the map exposes labeled zoom controls plus an observable URL/hash or scale change.

skills.title: Verify Layer Change and Stop
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Layers” control and select the option matching the requested style. Verify completion through observable state changes, such as updated map tiles, attribution, or a layer indicator in the URL. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeating the same click.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a map display style through a layer chooser, especially after the map visibly updates or the URL and tile attribution identify the requested style.

skills.title: Open and Inspect Map Layers
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Layers” control, then inspect the displayed “Map Layers” panel. Read the listed base layers and available overlay checkboxes; report that panel’s contents once visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view available map layers and the map page exposes a “Layers” control. Completion is indicated by a visible “Map Layers” heading and layer list.

skills.title: Verify Layer Panel Before Acting
skills.principle: After selecting the map’s “Layers” control, inspect the updated accessibility tree. If a “Map Layers” panel appears with named layer options, treat the task as complete, summarize those visible options, and stop. Do not click individual layers unless the user explicitly requests changing or testing one.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view available map layers and the Layers control opens a panel showing a heading and layer names such as Standard, CyclOSM, ÖPNVKarte, or Humanitarian.

skills.title: Calculate Route Through Directions
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” feature.
2. Enter the requested origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields, retaining the appropriate travel mode such as “Car (OSRM)”.
3. Click “Go” and wait for the directions panel.
4. Confirm the panel displays a distance and travel time, then report those values and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks asking for a route, especially the fastest route, when the directions interface provides origin/destination fields, a travel-mode selector, and a “Go” control.

skills.title: Generate a Map Short Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s Share control.
2. In the Share dialog, select Short Link.
3. Read the generated URL from the focused textbox; no editing or copying is required if it is already populated.
4. Return that URL and stop once the short-link value is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on an OpenStreetMap-style map when asked to create a shareable short link for the currently displayed location and the Share control is available.

skills.title: Use Map Share Controls Correctly
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, activate the visibly labeled “Share” control rather than nearby unlabeled map controls. Inspect the resulting accessibility tree for a share panel, short-link field, or copy action. If the control produces no state change, retry using the labeled control and verify the panel before reporting completion; do not substitute the full URL for the requested short link.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to generate a short link for the current OpenStreetMap view and the map toolbar includes a labeled “Share” control. Verify that a share interface or short-link result appears before responding.

skills.title: Compare Routes Across Travel Modes
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s directions feature and fill the From and To fields with the requested locations.
2. Select a transportation mode and activate “Go”; read the Directions panel’s distance and time.
3. Repeat mode selection and “Go” for each requested option, recording each result.
4. Report the collected times together and identify the fastest option.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map tasks comparing travel times across transportation modes when the directions page provides From/To fields, a mode combobox, a “Go” button, and a Directions result panel.

skills.title: Verify Both Direction Endpoints
skills.principle: On the directions page, explicitly fill both the “From” and “To” fields; a prior map search does not reliably populate “From.” Keep the driving mode selected, click “Go” once, then verify that route details or a rendered route appears. If the form remains unchanged, correct the blank or unresolved endpoint before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting driving directions after navigating from a map search, especially if the directions form shows separate blank “From” and “To” fields and clicking “Go” produces no route.

skills.title: Use Directions Form Correctly
skills.principle: Navigate to the map’s directions page, then re-read the accessibility tree and fill the separate “From” and “To” fields with the two locations. Keep driving mode selected, click the directions form’s “Go” button using a complete valid action, and verify that a route and distance appear before reporting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When calculating driving distance on OpenStreetMap and the directions page exposes distinct “From,” “To,” travel-mode, and “Go” controls. Reinspect after navigation rather than reusing stale search-field references.

skills.title: Report After Confirming Route
skills.principle: After selecting the requested travel mode and pressing “Go,” verify that a “Directions” result shows the route summary and turn-by-turn steps. Then report completion and the available route details to the user, terminating instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-direction tasks when the directions page visibly displays the requested origin, destination, travel mode, and a populated route result.

skills.title: Calculate Driving Time in OpenStreetMap
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points.”
2. Enter the origin in “From” and destination in “To”; keep the travel mode set to “Car (OSRM)” for driving.
3. Click “Go” and read the route result’s “Time” value, then report it in user-friendly units.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks asking for driving time between two places, when the directions page exposes “From,” “To,” a car mode, and a “Go” button.

skills.title: Target Labeled Direction Inputs
skills.principle: On the directions page, use the elements labeled “From” and “To” as the input controls, not adjacent marker images. Enter the origin and destination into those textboxes, keep the driving mode selected, then activate “Go” and verify that a route result containing travel time appears.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions form is open and the accessibility tree shows labeled From/To textboxes alongside decorative marker images; inspect roles and labels before choosing element identifiers.

skills.title: Unlock Map Editing Before Clicking Edit
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the Edit control’s state and tooltip rather than repeatedly clicking a disabled element.
2. If it indicates “Zoom in to edit the map,” use the map’s Zoom In control until Edit becomes active.
3. Click Edit and verify navigation; if redirected to a login form, stop and request authentication before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: When OpenStreetMap’s Edit link is visibly disabled or pointer events are intercepted, especially at a broad map zoom, and editing requires an authenticated account.

skills.title: Open Map History and Verify Results
skills.principle: Select the map's "History" navigation entry, then inspect the resulting "Changesets" panel. Report the displayed changesets when present; if the panel explicitly says "No changesets in this area," report that no recent changes are available instead of inferring details.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for requests to view recent map edits when the map page exposes a "History" link. Completion requires reaching the Changesets view and checking its result message or listed changesets.

skills.title: Use Valid Click Syntax and Verify Navigation
skills.principle: Issue browser actions in the exact supported syntax, such as `click("element_id")`, without embedding malformed JSON, extra arguments, or truncated escaping. After the action, inspect the new page state; for map history, completion is indicated by the Changesets page heading or changeset status. Once that state appears, stop issuing actions and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating OpenStreetMap through accessibility-tree links such as History, especially after an action error or when the URL and page content have not changed.

skills.title: Verify Trace Access Requirements
skills.principle: Open the navigation entry labeled “GPS Traces” and inspect the resulting page. Confirm whether traces exist, then select “Upload a trace” to test the upload path. If it redirects to login, report that viewing is available but uploading requires authentication.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or upload GPS tracks on a map site, especially when account credentials are unavailable. Verify the page state and authentication requirement before claiming an upload succeeded.

skills.title: Handle GPS Trace Login Redirects
skills.principle: After opening “Upload a trace,” inspect the resulting page. If it redirects to “Login,” authenticate or register first, then resume the preserved upload destination. Do not click upload controls from the old trace page or repeat stale element IDs; act only on controls present in the current accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When uploading a GPS track from OpenStreetMap’s GPS Traces page and navigation lands on a Login page, especially when the upload destination is preserved in the redirect.

skills.title: Verify Empty Content Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested content section using its semantic navigation label. Inspect the destination page for an explicit empty-state message such as “No diary entries.” If the message remains after confirming the page loaded, report that no matching content is currently available and stop; do not repeat the same navigation action.
skills.when_to_apply: When a user asks you to read or summarize content from a site section and the destination page visibly presents an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Stop When Content Is Unavailable
skills.principle: When the target page explicitly shows an empty state such as “No diary entries,” treat that as the completed observation: do not repeatedly wait, revisit, or browse unrelated sections. Report that the requested content is unavailable and terminate, unless the task explicitly requests an alternative source.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after navigating to User Diaries or a similar content page and confirming its accessibility tree displays an empty-state message with no available items.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Retrying
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to activate the navigation link matching the requested page. After navigation, verify the destination by its URL or heading. If the target page is already displayed, stop retrying clicks and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a site with accessibility-tree element IDs, especially after a click error or stale-element issue, and the requested destination may already be visible.

skills.title: Use Navigation Links to Reach Help
skills.principle: Identify the navigation entry whose visible label matches the requested destination, activate it, and verify the resulting page by its URL, heading, or distinctive content. Once the destination and relevant guidance are visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a website task requests a named informational page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link or menu item.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Page
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested page, then verify completion using its URL and distinctive heading or content. Once the requested page is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of exploring related links or external resources.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks where the target page is directly reachable from the current interface and the accessibility tree shows the requested URL or page heading.

skills.title: Pan via Focused Map Container
skills.principle:
1. Close any welcome or modal overlay blocking the map.
2. Focus the map container itself, not an individual tile, because the container receives pointer and keyboard events.
3. Press an arrow key to pan in the desired direction.
4. Confirm completion when the map URL center coordinates or visible tiles change.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap-style maps when tile clicks or drag actions are intercepted. The map container must be focusable, and a changed center coordinate or refreshed tile set confirms the pan.

skills.title: Focus Map Container for Keyboard Panning
skills.principle: Focus the map’s interactive container rather than individual tile images or overlay controls. Press directional arrow keys on the focused container to pan horizontally or vertically, then verify the map URL center coordinates change or newly loaded tiles appear.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to pan an OpenStreetMap-style map and tile clicks, scrolling, or drag targets are intercepted. Ensure the map container is visible and focusable, dismissing obstructive overlays if necessary.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When navigation changes to the requested page, verify the new URL or distinctive heading/content, then report completion and terminate. Do not click form controls, retry stale element IDs, or attempt sign-in unless the task explicitly requires authentication.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the requested destination is visibly confirmed, such as a Login heading and credential fields appearing after selecting a Log In link.

skills.title: Verify Directions After Submission
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions page and fill the “From” and “To” fields with the actual requested locations, not placeholder text.
2. Select the requested travel mode if needed, then click “Go.”
3. Inspect the updated page for a route, distance, directions, or an explicit error; take corrective action if no result appears rather than repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When using OpenStreetMap’s directions form and both endpoints are known. After clicking “Go,” verify that route output or an error appears before reporting completion.

skills.title: Use Copyright Pages for Data Sources
skills.principle: For OpenStreetMap questions about data origins, open the navigation entry labeled “Copyright.” Read the “Our contributors” section for contributor types, national agencies, source licenses, and attribution caveats; use its “Contributors page” link for fuller details. Confirm the answer from visible page text before reporting.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which sources, agencies, contributors, or licenses supply OpenStreetMap data, provided the site navigation exposes a “Copyright” page or equivalent attribution page.

skills.title: Reverse a Route Direction
skills.principle: On the map directions page, locate the control labeled "Reverse Directions" and activate it. This swaps the route's origin and destination; once the control has been activated and the directions view remains present, report completion without unnecessary additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a route is already available or the directions interface exposes From and To fields plus a "Reverse Directions" control. Navigate to the directions page first if the current map view lacks route controls.

skills.title: Handle Signup Validation Correctly
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Sign Up form, complete every required field, using a genuinely available email address and copying it into Email Confirmation. If submission reports that the email is taken, replace both email fields with the same new address, then resubmit using the currently displayed Sign Up button. Verify navigation or a success message before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting mapping requires account creation and the signup form displays validation errors such as an unavailable email or mismatched confirmation.

skills.title: Verify GPS Trace List State
skills.principle: Open the map site's “GPS Traces” navigation entry and inspect the resulting “Public GPS Traces” page. Treat “Nothing here yet” as confirmation that no traces exist; otherwise report the displayed traces. Once the list state is confirmed, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all GPS traces on an OpenStreetMap-style site and the GPS Traces navigation link is available. Verify the page heading and empty-state message before concluding.

skills.title: Zoom Before Opening Map Editor
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap, inspect the Edit control’s enabled state and tooltip. If it is disabled with “Zoom in to edit the map,” use Zoom In repeatedly, checking the map zoom and control state after each change. Once Edit becomes enabled, open it; if redirected to Login, report that authentication is required before editing can continue.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from an OpenStreetMap map view to editing and the Edit control is disabled or intercepted because the current zoom level is too broad.

skills.title: Resolve Edit Prerequisites Before Retrying
skills.principle: When an editing control is disabled, follow its observed prerequisite rather than repeatedly clicking it. Zoom in using the map’s “Zoom In” control until the edit control becomes enabled, then select “Edit.” If navigation redirects to a login form, recognize authentication as the remaining prerequisite and stop until credentials are available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap map pages when “Edit” is disabled with a “Zoom in to edit the map” message, or when selecting it redirects to a login page requiring user credentials.

skills.title: Open Map Edit History
skills.principle: Use the map site's labeled “History” navigation link to open the changeset view. Confirm completion by checking for the “Changesets” heading and reading the result, such as listed edits or “No changesets in this area.” Report the observed state rather than assuming edits exist.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view map edits or changes and the map page exposes a visible “History” navigation link. After navigation, verify the changeset page and its current-area result.

skills.title: Handle Download-Link Navigation Timeouts
skills.principle: When an export or download link is visibly enabled, activate it once and inspect the resulting URL, download state, or page change before retrying. A click timeout after the browser reports “click action done” may reflect a slow download or navigation, not a failed click. For oversized map areas, use the offered bulk-download source or reduce the selected area.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap export pages when the area-too-large warning appears or a download link times out after activation, especially when external URLs may trigger downloads rather than render a normal page.

skills.title: Access OpenID Login
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's "Log In" page.
2. Locate the third-party authentication section labeled "Alternatively, use a third party to login:".
3. Select "Login with OpenID" and verify the OpenID input field and its accompanying "Login" button are visible.
4. Stop once the OpenID form is exposed; do not submit without a user-provided OpenID URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to access or reveal a site's OpenID or third-party login option, starting from a page that provides a "Log In" link.

skills.title: Verify Route Before Reversing
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions panel and inspect the From and To fields for a populated route.
2. If either field is empty, enter the required endpoints and click Go to calculate the route.
3. Click Reverse Directions only after a valid route exists.
4. Confirm the endpoints or route state have swapped before reporting completion; button focus alone is not confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when reversing directions in OpenStreetMap or similar map interfaces, especially when the directions panel may open with empty From, To, or route values.

skills.title: Verify Map History Empty State
skills.principle: Open the map page’s “History” navigation entry, then inspect the resulting “Changesets” panel. If it explicitly says “No changesets in this area,” treat the request as complete, report that no edit history is available, and terminate without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view edit history for the currently displayed map area and the map interface provides a “History” link. Confirm completion by checking the resulting changeset status message.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Target Before Acting
skills.principle: Use the control’s accessible name and role to distinguish nearby navigation items. After activating a control, inspect the updated accessibility tree and URL; if an edit menu opened instead of the History page, close or bypass it, then activate the actual “History” link. Confirm navigation by observing the history route or history-specific content before declaring completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page has adjacent controls such as Edit, History, and Export, especially when activating an unlabeled button may open a menu instead of navigating.

skills.title: Fill the Directions Starting Point
skills.principle: Open the map’s “Find directions between two points” form, then enter the requested location in the “From” textbox. Do not use the general Search box or invent a destination. Verify the “From” field contains the requested place, then stop unless additional fields are explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for tasks asking to enter or set a starting point for directions when the directions form is available or reachable through its navigation link.

skills.title: Verify Travel Mode Before Routing
skills.principle: On a directions page, enter the origin and destination, choose the requested travel mode, and verify the combobox value or selected option changed before clicking “Go.” After submission, confirm the displayed route and directions reflect that mode; if the mode remains unchanged, correct it and recalculate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for map-routing tasks requiring a specific mode such as bicycle, especially when selecting an option times out or merely opening the combobox does not visibly change its selected value.

skills.title: Use Semantic Controls, Not Nearby Markers
skills.principle: Inspect the accessibility tree to identify the actual interactive element behind each label. In the directions form, enter locations into the textboxes labeled “From” and “To,” select “Bicycle (OSRM)” only in the routing combobox, then click “Go.” Do not fill or select image markers or confuse routing-mode options with place fields.
skills.when_to_apply: When calculating a route in OpenStreetMap directions and the tree exposes labeled From/To textboxes plus a separate routing-mode combobox, especially after an action targets a nearby non-input marker.

skills.title: Complete Both Route Comparisons
skills.principle:
1. Enter the origin and destination, run the first travel mode, and record the displayed Distance and Time.
2. Change the mode using the combobox’s exact option label, not by clicking an invisible option element.
3. Verify the selected mode and updated Directions result, record its Distance and Time, then report both values and the comparison.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks to compare travel modes and the directions form provides one mode at a time. Prerequisite: both locations are resolved and each route result visibly reports distance and time.

skills.title: Recover From Duplicate Signup Fields
skills.principle: When signup reports that an email or display name is already taken, replace each affected value with a genuinely unique one. Immediately update Email Confirmation to match the new email, choose a unique display name, refill any cleared password fields and confirmation, then submit again. Confirm success from the resulting page rather than assuming submission worked.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s Sign Up form after submission returns “has already been taken” validation errors. Reinspect the current accessibility tree because field identifiers may change after validation.

skills.title: Compare Map Layers at a Target Location
skills.principle:
1. Open the map’s “Layers” panel and search for the target location, then activate the search with “Go.”
2. Confirm the map is centered on the intended result, especially when names have multiple matches.
3. Select each available layer in turn, keeping the location and zoom fixed; note each layer’s displayed emphasis and attribution.
4. Summarize the differences and identify the currently selected layer.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to compare map styles or layers for a specific place and the map provides a searchable location field plus a “Layers” control.

skills.title: Center Target Before Layer Comparison
skills.principle:
1. Use the map Search field to locate the requested place, then activate “Go.”
2. Verify the map is centered on the target before opening “Layers.”
3. Select each relevant layer in turn, observing the target at the same location and zoom.
4. Report the visual differences; do not stop after merely switching layers.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to compare map layers for a named place, especially if the initial map view is elsewhere. Search and verify the target location before comparing layers.

skills.title: Recover From Signup Uniqueness Errors
skills.principle: When submission reports that an email or display name is already taken, replace each rejected value with a genuinely distinct one. Keep the email confirmation exactly synchronized with the new email, refill any password fields cleared by validation, submit again, and verify that the page shows successful account creation rather than another validation error.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on account-registration forms after submission returns uniqueness errors such as “has already been taken,” especially when validation rerenders the form and clears password fields or leaves confirmation values stale.

skills.title: Use the Map’s Zoom In Control
skills.principle: Identify the map control labeled “Zoom In” in the current accessibility tree and activate it once. Confirm completion by checking that the map’s zoom level or displayed map scale increases, then report completion without taking unnecessary additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to zoom in on an interactive map and the page exposes a labeled Zoom In control. One activation is sufficient unless the requested zoom amount specifies otherwise.

skills.title: Validate Both Route Locations
skills.principle: Use the two locations explicitly supplied by the task. If either endpoint is missing, request clarification instead of inventing a destination. On the directions page, fill the “From” and “To” fields, choose the requested travel mode, click “Go” once, and verify that a route result appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task requests directions but the origin or destination is absent, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed; prerequisites are two user-specified endpoints and an available directions form.

skills.title: Select the Correct Map Search Result
skills.principle: From map search results, choose the entry whose feature type and full name match the requested place, rather than similarly named states or points of interest. Open that result and verify the destination is its detailed feature page, indicated by a feature-specific heading and metadata such as tags, boundaries, or population.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map search returns multiple results for the same name and the task requires detailed information about a specific city, region, or mapped feature.

skills.title: Submit Map Searches and Inspect Results
skills.principle: After entering a place in OpenStreetMap’s Search box, click the “Go” button and inspect the resulting search/sidebar content for the place details. Do not treat background map tiles as clickable markers; close any welcome overlay first if it blocks controls. Confirm the page shows the requested place information before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page has a place name entered in its Search box but remains on the unchanged map, especially when overlays or tile images obscure the actual search result.

skills.title: Select the Correct Map Search Result
skills.principle: In map search results, distinguish similarly named places by the result-type label (for example, State versus City or point of interest). Open the result matching the requested administrative level, then verify the detail page heading and inspect its tags or metadata for the requested facts before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map search returns multiple entities sharing a name and the task asks for a specific geographic or administrative entity. A result list with type labels must be visible.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Relation
skills.principle: When a search result opens the target geographic entity’s relation page, verify the heading identifies the requested place and its details or tags are visible. Treat that page as completion; do not navigate to unrelated About, History, Help, or Wiki pages unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap tasks asking to view information about a place, once the search result opens a matching relation page with the place heading and descriptive tags visible.

skills.title: Refresh Element References After Navigation
skills.principle: After a navigation, form submission, or validation error, reacquire controls from the current accessibility tree before acting. Match fields by their current label and role, not by an earlier element ID; verify the target is visible and editable, then fill or submit it. This prevents accidentally targeting hidden inputs from a prior page state.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever a page reloads, redirects, displays validation errors, or changes its accessibility-tree element IDs, especially while completing login or upload forms.

skills.title: Set Travel Mode Before Routing
skills.principle:
1. Fill the From and To fields with the requested locations.
2. Inspect the transport selector and choose the requested mode, such as “Bicycle (OSRM),” rather than accepting its default.
3. Click “Go” and confirm the Directions panel reports route metrics such as distance and time before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions page when a user requests a route with a specific travel mode and the form contains From, To, transport selection, and Go controls.

skills.title: Verify Routing Fields Before Submission
skills.principle: Use the accessibility labels “From” and “To” to target the actual editable textboxes, not nearby marker images or stale element IDs. Enter both locations, then verify both fields visibly contain the intended values before selecting the travel mode and clicking “Go.” After submission, confirm that route details or a rendered route appear; do not assume success from waiting alone.
skills.when_to_apply: When requesting directions on a map page with labeled origin, destination, travel-mode controls, and a “Go” button, especially when accessibility-tree IDs may refer to adjacent images or other elements.

skills.title: Select Native Route Mode Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Fill the origin and destination fields, then inspect the transportation combobox’s current value.
2. If the requested mode is not selected, use the combobox’s native selection action (such as `select_option`) rather than clicking an invisible `<option>` element.
3. Confirm completion when the combobox shows the requested mode and the directions panel updates with the corresponding route.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions pages when changing travel modes through a native select control, especially after direct clicking an accessibility-tree option fails or times out.

skills.title: Fill Route Endpoints Before Calculating
skills.principle:
1. Open the directions form and enter the requested origin in the “From” field and destination in the “To” field.
2. Select the requested transportation mode, such as “Bicycle (OSRM)”.
3. Click “Go” only after both fields contain the intended places.
4. Confirm that route results or directions appear; if the page remains unchanged, inspect the fields and correct missing or invalid entries rather than repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions tasks when the directions form shows “From”, “To”, a transportation-mode combobox, and “Go”. The endpoints must be entered before route generation can succeed.

skills.title: Fill the Directions Destination Field
skills.principle:
1. Locate the directions form’s textbox labeled “To” in the accessibility tree.
2. Focus it only if necessary, then fill it with the requested custom location.
3. Verify the textbox displays the entered location; report completion without pressing “Go” unless route calculation was requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions task asks only to enter a destination, and the directions page exposes a labeled “To” textbox. Stop after the field visibly contains the requested location.

skills.title: Request Missing Destination Details
skills.principle: Before entering a custom destination, verify that the user supplied the location value. If the destination is absent, ask for it directly instead of performing no-op actions or attempting the directions search; enter it only after the user provides it.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a directions page when the “To” field is available but the requested destination is missing from the task instruction or conversation.

skills.title: Stop After Verified Zoom Change
skills.principle: Click the map’s “Zoom Out” control once, then inspect the updated map state. If the zoom level or scale has changed, the request is complete; stop rather than repeatedly clicking. If it no longer changes, treat the minimum zoom as reached and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to zoom out on an interactive map and the accessibility tree exposes a “Zoom Out” control. Use the changed URL, zoom level, or scale indicator to verify completion.

skills.title: Use the Labeled Share Control
skills.principle: Identify the control explicitly labeled “Share” rather than relying on nearby unlabeled map controls. Activate it once, then verify that a share panel, URL, or other sharing options appear. If nothing changes, re inspect the accessibility tree and target the labeled control instead of repeating the same coordinate or declaring infeasibility.
skills.when_to_apply: When sharing a map view and the map toolbar contains several adjacent links, including unlabeled controls. Requires accessibility-tree inspection and confirmation that the sharing UI or generated share information appeared.

skills.title: Target Semantic Input Controls
skills.principle: Use the accessibility role and label to identify the actual editable control, not nearby icons or marker images. For directions, fill the textbox named “From” and the textbox named “To”; verify each value appears, then select the travel mode and click “Go.” If an action reports a non-editable element, re-inspect the tree and choose the labeled textbox instead of retrying the same target.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map directions form shows labeled origin and destination textboxes alongside decorative route-marker images, especially after a fill action reports that the chosen element is not editable.

skills.title: Generate Mode-Specific Map Directions
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested origin and destination in the “From” and “To” fields.
2. Select the requested travel mode, such as “Bicycle (OSRM),” instead of accepting the default.
3. Click “Go” to calculate the route.
4. Confirm a Directions panel appears with distance, time, and turn-by-turn steps before reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap’s directions page when a task requests routing between two places with a specific transportation mode. Verify the selected mode and visible Directions panel before concluding.

skills.title: Configure Bicycle Directions Explicitly
skills.principle:
1. Open “Find directions between two points” and fill the dedicated “From” and “To” fields with the requested locations.
2. Set the travel-mode combobox to “Bicycle (OSRM)” instead of leaving the default car mode.
3. Click “Go” and verify that route results appear before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on OpenStreetMap directions pages when the task requests a route type, especially after navigation from the map search; confirm the directions form is populated because prior search text may not transfer.

skills.title: Derive Geo URI From Map URL
skills.principle: Read the map URL hash for the current view, typically formatted as `map=zoom/latitude/longitude`. Ignore the zoom value, preserve latitude and longitude order, and construct `geo:latitude,longitude` for sharing. Confirm the coordinates come from the current map state before reporting the URI.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to share the current map location as a geo URI and the map page URL visibly contains its current coordinates, especially if the Share control does not expose a usable URI.

skills.title: Read Geo URI Link Directly
skills.principle: After opening the map’s “Share” panel, locate the “Geo URI” entry and read its displayed link text or href. Use that URI as the task output; do not fill or edit the link, because an anchor is not an input control. Once the URI is visible and captured, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map-sharing dialog displays the requested location as a Geo URI link, especially when the accessibility tree identifies it as a link rather than a textbox.

skills.title: Use Copyright Page for License Terms
skills.principle: On an OpenStreetMap page, open the navigation entry labeled “Copyright.” Read the “Copyright and License” section, identify the stated data license and its legal-code link, then report both accurately. Confirm the page distinguishes data licensing from documentation licensing before answering.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked about OpenStreetMap data licensing and the current site exposes a “Copyright” navigation link or equivalent legal-information page.

skills.title: Report Findings After Verification
skills.principle: When the target page visibly contains the requested information, extract the key terms and immediately provide the user-facing answer. Do not repeat no-op actions or wait for another observation after verifying the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to information-retrieval tasks when the accessibility tree shows the relevant heading, text, or linked legal details and no further interaction is required.

skills.title: Use Bulk Download Alternatives
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, first confirm the area-too-large message, then inspect the listed alternatives and match them to scope: Overpass API for the selected bounding box, Planet OSM for the complete database, Geofabrik Downloads for regional extracts, and Other Sources for additional providers. For an exploration task, report these options once displayed rather than navigating away unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the Export page states that the selected area is too large for XML export and presents alternative bulk-download links.

skills.title: Verify Export Limits from Page Evidence
skills.principle: Open the map site's Export page and inspect the displayed size-status message. If it says the selected area is too large, report that direct export is limited, but do not invent an exact area threshold when none is shown. Preserve the page's recommended remedies, such as zooming in, selecting a smaller area, or using bulk-download alternatives.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked about a map export size limit and the Export page provides a bounding box plus an explicit too-large warning but no numeric maximum.

skills.title: Search and Confirm Map Locations
skills.principle: Use the map’s Search textbox to enter the requested place, then activate the Go control. Confirm completion when the page shows search results identifying the target and the map view updates to that location; then report success without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map page provides a labeled Search field and Go control, and the task is to locate a named city, place, or geographic feature.

skills.title: Detect Export Limit From Page State
skills.principle: On OpenStreetMap’s Export page, reduce the selected bounding box incrementally and inspect the updated accessibility tree after each zoom. Stop immediately when the warning that the area is too large disappears and an “Export” button appears. Read the four coordinate fields at that transition as the largest directly exportable area; do not continue zooming after this confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when determining OpenStreetMap’s direct-export area limit and the Export page initially shows the “area is too large” warning. Ensure the bounding-box coordinates and export controls are visible after each zoom.

skills.title: Handle Map Editing Prerequisites
skills.principle:
1. If the map’s Edit control is disabled and indicates zooming is required, use Zoom In until the control becomes enabled.
2. Select Edit and inspect the resulting page.
3. If redirected to Login, authenticate using available credentials; otherwise report that authentication is the blocking prerequisite instead of repeatedly clicking Edit.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from an OpenStreetMap map or directions view to editing, especially when Edit is disabled at the current zoom or selecting it redirects to a login form.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Page
skills.principle: Navigate using the clearly labeled navigation link, then verify the destination by its page heading or URL. Once the requested Export page is displayed, report completion and terminate instead of following optional download-source links unless the task explicitly requests downloading the data.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to navigate to a named page and the page is confirmed by its heading or URL, especially when it offers optional secondary actions.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Export Page
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry labeled “Export,” then verify the page shows the “Export” heading and export controls. Once the target Export page is loaded, report completion and terminate; do not follow external download-source links unless the task explicitly requires obtaining a file.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to navigate to a site’s Export page and the accessibility tree confirms the Export heading or matching page URL.

skills.title: Verify History Page Completion
skills.principle: Click the map application's “History” navigation entry, then verify the resulting page by checking for the “Changesets” heading or equivalent history content. If it states “No changesets in this area,” report that the history page is open and no edits are shown for the current map view, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view map edit history and the map application exposes a visible “History” navigation entry. Confirm the destination page and its result before reporting completion.

skills.title: Verify History Page Then Finish
skills.principle: After selecting the map’s “History” navigation entry, verify the destination using the URL or the “Changesets” heading and read the resulting status, such as “No changesets in this area.” Once confirmed, provide a completion response and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a map task asks you to open edit history and the History page has loaded, especially when its panel displays a clear heading or empty-state message.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When the requested page is loaded, verify its heading or URL matches the target and terminate. Do not select secondary actions such as upload unless explicitly requested. If a secondary action requires authentication, proceed only with user-provided valid credentials; never invent or repeatedly submit credentials.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a named page succeeds and the page visibly shows the requested heading or destination URL, especially when optional actions could trigger login or other prerequisites.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When the requested destination page is loaded and its heading and relevant content are visible, treat navigation as complete. Do not click an arbitrary listed item or external link unless the task specifies a particular group or requires further interaction; report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the observed page URL, heading, and content match the requested destination, especially when the page lists optional links or resources but no specific item is requested.

skills.title: Verify Map Search Results in Details
skills.principle: Search OpenStreetMap for the place type, name, and area, then submit the search. Open the matching result and verify its detail page: the name tag matches the requested name, the category tag matches the requested place type, and the address confirms the requested area. Report only after these fields agree.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for OpenStreetMap place-existence questions when search results may conflate a place name with an address. The map search box and Go control must be available, and a result should provide a clickable details page.

skills.title: Open Share Options and Verify
skills.principle: On a map page, activate the control whose accessible name is “Share,” not nearby unlabeled map-tool icons. After clicking, verify a Share dialog or panel appears with options such as Link, Short Link, HTML, or Geo URI. Once the Share options are visible, stop if the task only requests navigation; do not select an individual sharing method unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to map sharing options and the map toolbar contains both a labeled Share control and unlabeled adjacent controls. Confirm completion by checking for a Share heading or sharing-option list.

skills.title: Navigate Forums Through the Forum List
skills.principle:
1. If the requested forum is not already shown, open the site's Forums page.
2. Locate the forum entry by its visible name, then activate its forum link rather than nearby subscription controls.
3. Confirm completion when the destination page identifies the requested forum in its heading or URL, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill tasks asking to open a specific forum when the current page is another forum or the target is not directly visible. Ensure the target forum entry appears in the forum list.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Destination
skills.principle: After navigation, verify the page heading or URL matches the requested forum. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the target page is visibly identified by its heading, URL, or distinctive content and no additional interaction is requested.

skills.title: Inspect Visible Forum Entries First
skills.principle: On a forum directory, scan the current accessibility tree for the requested forum name and activate its matching forum link immediately. Only scroll or use pagination after confirming the target is absent from the currently observed entries; verify the destination page shows the requested forum.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a named forum from a directory page whose accessibility tree lists multiple forum articles and links, before scrolling, changing sort order, or opening pagination.

skills.title: Read Forum Counts Directly
skills.principle: Open the forum directory from the site navigation, locate the target forum’s article by its visible name, and read the adjacent text labeled “submissions.” Report that displayed count directly; do not open the forum or count individual posts when the directory already provides the aggregate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Postmill forum-count tasks when the forums directory is accessible and each forum entry visibly includes an aggregate “submissions” count.

skills.title: Read Forum Counts Directly
skills.principle: Open the Forums page and locate the target forum entry by its displayed name. Read the associated text stating the number of submissions, then report that value without opening the forum unless the count is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Postmill tasks asking for a forum's submission count when the Forums listing is accessible and each forum entry displays a submissions total.

skills.title: Read Forum Submission Counts Directly
skills.principle: On the forum listing, locate the target forum entry and read the adjacent text labeled “submissions.” Treat nearby subscriber counts as unrelated. If the target entry is visible, report that count immediately instead of opening the forum, scrolling, or inspecting pagination.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a forum’s total submissions on Postmill and the Forums page is available. Confirm the target forum entry and its adjacent “submissions” text are visible before answering.

skills.title: Verify Existing Forum Sort Before Changing
skills.principle: Open the forums listing rather than assuming the home feed controls forum ordering. Inspect the visible forum names and navigation labels; if they are already alphabetically ordered, report that the requested view is already active and stop. Otherwise, use the dedicated "Alphabetical" navigation entry and confirm the resulting list order.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view forums alphabetically on Postmill, especially from the home feed. First navigate to the forums listing and check whether the displayed names are already alphabetically ordered or an "Alphabetical" view is available.

skills.title: Complete and Verify Forum Submissions
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum’s “Submit” page and keep the URL submission type selected.
2. Fill the target URL, required title, optional descriptive body, and required forum selector.
3. Expand the forum selector, choose the forum matching the content, then click “Create submission.”
4. Confirm the resulting post page shows the expected title, link, body, and forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a new link post on Postmill/Reddit-like forums, especially when the form requires both content fields and a forum selection before creation.

skills.title: Use Custom Forum Dropdown Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open the Forum combobox by clicking its visible control, rather than using select_option on the non-select element.
2. Inspect the expanded listbox and choose an actually available forum option by clicking its option.
3. Verify the combobox value changed from “Choose one…” before clicking “Create submission.”
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a Postmill forum post and the Forum field is a custom combobox with a listbox, especially when the desired forum name is not visibly available as an option.

skills.title: Infer Theme State From Toggle Label
skills.principle: Open the authenticated user/account menu and inspect the theme toggle’s accessible label. Treat a control labeled “Dark mode” as an action to enable dark mode, meaning dark mode is currently off; a control labeled “Light mode” indicates dark mode is currently on. Report the inferred state without activating the toggle.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking a website’s current dark-mode state and the accessibility tree exposes a user-menu theme toggle whose label names the mode it will switch to.

skills.title: Search Postmill and Read Comment Count
skills.principle:
1. Enter the distinctive post phrase in Postmill’s “Search query” field and submit it with Enter or the “Search” button.
2. Match the result by its title, then read the adjacent “N comments” link for the requested count.
3. Ignore search-result comments or unrelated posts; report the count only after confirming the matching post title.
skills.when_to_apply: When a requested Reddit/Postmill post is not visible in the current listing but a distinctive title phrase is available and the search box is present.

skills.title: Verify Post Title Before Counting
skills.principle: Match the requested title against article headings in the current Reddit listing. For an exact match, read the adjacent comments link and report its number. If no exact match appears after checking the listing, report that the post was not found instead of inferring a comment count.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a Reddit post’s comment count and the current submissions page contains multiple similarly formatted articles or may not include the requested post.

skills.title: Search Reddit Posts by Distinctive Phrase
skills.principle: Use the site search to locate a post efficiently: fill the search box with a distinctive phrase from the requested title, submit it, identify the matching result, and open it. On the post page, read the submission timestamp shown beside the author, then report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks when a specific post was posted and the target title or wording is searchable. Confirm the opened page’s title matches before using its displayed timestamp.

skills.title: Use Exact Search Result Metadata
skills.principle: After searching, inspect the result title and its associated metadata before scanning unrelated results. When a result matches the requested wording, read its nearby time element and report that posting date; do not claim no match merely because other results are irrelevant.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill search page shows results and the task asks when a specific question or post was posted. Confirm the title match and locate its adjacent time metadata before concluding the search failed.

skills.title: Use the Comments Navigation Link
skills.principle: From a Reddit/Postmill submissions page, locate the navigation entry labeled “Comments” and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading indicates recent comments and that comment articles are visible with author, timestamp, content, and interaction controls. Report completion once this state appears.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all comments and the current page is a Postmill submissions or home page with a visible “Comments” navigation link.

skills.title: Create a Missing Wiki Index Page
skills.principle:
1. Open the Wiki section and, when it shows “Page not found,” select “Create this page.”
2. Keep the predefined index URL, then fill the required Title and Body fields with a useful welcome, purpose, and navigation links using Markdown.
3. Check the rendered preview, select “Save,” and verify the resulting page displays the intended title and content.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Postmill Wiki navigation entry opens a missing index page and the page offers a “Create this page” link plus required Title, Body, and Save controls.

skills.title: Resolve Wiki URL Validation Errors
skills.principle: When creating a wiki page, use the page slug format accepted by the URL field, not an invalid path such as a leading-slash URL. After saving, inspect the form for validation messages; correct the URL and resubmit. Confirm success by reaching the new page or seeing it listed, rather than assuming Save succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: When the wiki creation form remains open after Save and displays “This value is not valid” for the URL, especially when the requested page may already exist and should instead be edited.

skills.title: Select and Verify Submission Forum
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's submission page using the clearly labeled "Submit" navigation entry.
2. Expand the required "Forum" combobox to reveal available forum options.
3. Choose the requested forum by its visible label, not a fixed element ID.
4. Confirm the combobox value changed from the placeholder to the requested forum, then stop once selection is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill submission task requires choosing a forum and the submission form is accessible. Ensure the requested forum appears among the combobox options before selecting it.

skills.title: Select the Forum Option
skills.principle: Open the Forum combobox, then click the option matching the requested forum in the expanded list. Verify the combobox value changes from “Choose one…” to that forum before continuing; reopening or clicking the combobox again does not select an option.
skills.when_to_apply: On Postmill’s Create submission form when Forum is required and the combobox shows “Choose one…”. The option list must be expanded so the target forum option is observable.

skills.title: Use the Account Menu
skills.principle:
1. Open the logged-in username menu in the site header.
2. Choose the option matching account management, such as “My account,” rather than profile or block-list entries.
3. Confirm completion by checking for an account-editing page with credential fields, save controls, or account deletion options, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated Reddit/Postmill page is open and the task asks to access account settings; the username menu must be visible in the header.

skills.title: Stop After Theme Change Confirmation
skills.principle: After selecting the opposite value in the Night mode control, click “Save changes” once. When the page shows “User settings have been updated” and the control reflects the requested mode, report completion and terminate; do not toggle again or repeat the save.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing Reddit/Postmill appearance settings, after the target mode is selected and a successful update alert confirms persistence.

skills.title: Navigate to a Target Forum
skills.principle:
1. On the forum list, locate the article whose heading or link matches the requested forum name.
2. Activate that forum link, then verify the destination through the page URL and forum heading.
3. Once the requested forum page is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit/Postmill task requests opening a named forum and the current page displays a forum directory with identifiable forum links.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Once the requested destination is visibly confirmed by the page heading and URL, report completion and terminate immediately. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for additional observations after the goal is achieved.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current page’s URL and accessible-tree heading clearly match the requested destination.

skills.title: Compare Visible Forum Counts
skills.principle: Scan each forum entry on the current list page, pair its forum name with the displayed submissions count, and track the largest value. Report the corresponding forum and count once every visible entry has been checked. After confirming the answer, stop instead of navigating into a forum or performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to find the forum with the most submissions on the currently displayed Reddit forum list and submission counts are visible for the entries being compared.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After each page observation, identify the target control by its current accessible name, role, and bid before acting. If a bid fails, stop guessing and re-inspect the refreshed accessibility tree. For forum-comparison tasks, count or compare the requested submission metric directly; do not substitute comment counts or thread popularity.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Reddit/Postmill lists with dynamic accessibility-tree bids, especially after an action error or when the task asks for a forum’s submission count rather than a thread’s comments.

skills.title: Use the Link URL After Repeated Click Failures
skills.principle: When a visible forum link repeatedly produces empty-action or text-encoding errors, stop retrying the same text locator. Read the target link’s observed URL from the accessibility tree and navigate directly with `goto`; then verify the page heading or URL identifies the requested forum.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on forum-list pages when the target entry is visible with a valid destination URL, but clicking by its displayed text fails repeatedly or the locator cannot resolve the text.

skills.title: Verify Forum Names Before Giving Up
skills.principle: When asked to open a specific forum, match the requested name exactly. From the current page, use the “Forums” navigation entry or “Search query” to locate the target forum; do not substitute a similarly themed forum such as “Jokes.” Report infeasibility only after checking the forum directory or search results and finding no matching destination.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task requests a named forum and the current page shows only subscribed forums or similarly themed content, especially when the exact target name is absent from the visible sidebar.

skills.title: Verify Pagination State Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and pagination controls before navigating. If the URL indicates the requested page and its pagination entry is selected, treat the goal as complete, report confirmation, and stop. Otherwise, activate the pagination link matching the requested page, then verify the resulting URL or selected page indicator.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for forum or list-pagination tasks when the initial page may already be the requested page and the page exposes a URL or visible pagination state confirming the current position.

skills.title: Use Valid Structured Pagination Actions
skills.principle:
1. Identify the visible next-page link, such as “Más,” and use its semantic link target or click action.
2. Provide the complete action payload with correctly separated action name and arguments; do not concatenate parameters into the action name.
3. After navigation, verify the URL or listing contents changed before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When paginating forum or post listings and the accessibility tree exposes a next-page link. Ensure BrowserGym actions include valid structured arguments and confirm navigation succeeded.

skills.title: Check Notification Badge and Page
skills.principle: Use the account header’s notifications link to verify the current notification state. Treat a visible zero badge, an empty notifications page, or both as confirmation that there are no new notifications, then report the result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check notifications on Postmill/Reddit-like pages and the header exposes a notifications entry with a count or link.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Notifications
skills.principle: Open the account’s Notifications link, then verify the page heading and its displayed state. If it shows an empty-state message such as “There are no entries to display,” the check is complete; report the result and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking notifications on Postmill or similar sites, after navigating to the Notifications page and observing either notification entries or an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Repeating Navigation
skills.principle: Check the current URL and page heading after navigation. If they already identify the requested forum, treat the task as complete and stop. If a target link is inaccessible or clicks fail, use its observed destination URL directly, then verify the resulting page before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a named Reddit forum from a forum list, especially after click errors, invisible elements, or a page that may already be at the requested destination.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Forum Access
skills.principle: Navigate from the forum list to the target forum, then verify the page heading and visible submissions match the requested forum. Once the target page is loaded and its content is visible, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks you to view a specific forum and the accessibility tree shows the target forum heading, submissions, or other content after navigation.

skills.title: Create and Verify a New Forum
skills.principle:
1. Open the Forums section and select “Create forum.”
2. Complete every required field: Name, Title, Description, and Sidebar, using content aligned with the requested topic.
3. Select “Create forum” only after all required fields are populated.
4. Confirm completion on the resulting forum page by checking its heading and displayed sidebar or description.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a new Postmill/Reddit-style forum and the Forums page exposes a “Create forum” control with required Name, Title, Description, and Sidebar fields.

skills.title: Use Forum Management Navigation
skills.principle: When creating a forum, do not use the “Publicar” post form. Follow the visible “Foros” navigation entry, inspect that page for a forum-creation control, and only report infeasibility after checking the dedicated forum-management interface.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task asks to create a new forum and the current page shows a post-creation form alongside a visible “Foros” navigation link.

skills.title: Open Account Settings from Username Menu
skills.principle:
1. Locate the signed-in username control, typically a button marked with the username and `hasPopup='menu'`.
2. Activate it and inspect the expanded menu for the account-management link, such as “My account.”
3. Select that link and confirm the destination by checking for an account-editing heading or account URL before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit/Postmill pages when the task requests account settings and the signed-in username is visible in the site header. Ensure the menu expands before selecting its account link.

skills.title: Select Account Settings From User Menu
skills.principle: Click the signed-in username control to expand its menu, then choose the account-settings entry labeled “Mi cuenta” (or equivalent). Verify navigation by checking that the page heading and URL indicate the account settings page; do not assume success merely because the username is focused or no error occurred.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill page shows the signed-in username as a menu button and the task requires opening account settings. Confirm the menu is expanded before selecting its account link.

skills.title: Use Account Page for Preferences
skills.principle: When a requested preference setting is absent from the current Reddit page, treat it as an account-level operation: open the signed-in username menu, navigate to the account/preferences page, and make changes there. If navigation is unavailable, clearly explain the page limitation and direct the user to the account page.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the user requests user preferences while viewing a forum list or other page whose accessibility tree contains no preferences control, but does show an authenticated username menu.

skills.title: Save Requested Preference Changes
skills.principle:
1. Open the account menu and choose the clearly labeled “User settings” link.
2. Change only the preferences explicitly requested; do not invent example values or modify unrelated options.
3. Click “Save changes” after editing.
4. Verify the page shows the saved values or a success indication before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When updating Reddit/Postmill account preferences and the settings form is accessible. Use the account menu first, and treat unsaved form changes as incomplete.

skills.title: Verify Sort State Before Acting
skills.principle: On a forums list, inspect the sorting control and its expanded options. Select the option labeled “Fecha de creación” (or equivalent) or follow its visible link. Confirm completion when the control displays that sort label and the list refreshes; then report completion without repeatedly toggling the menu.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to sort Reddit/Postmill forums and the page exposes a sorting menu or link. Use the currently displayed sort label and resulting URL/page state to determine whether the requested ordering is already active.

skills.title: Verify Sorting State and Stop
skills.principle: After selecting the requested sorting option, verify completion using the resulting URL and the sort control’s label. If the page shows the target sort as active, report completion and terminate; do not click the already-selected option again or perform unnecessary troubleshooting.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting a Reddit forum list and the page reloads after choosing an option. Confirm the URL or control label reflects the requested sort before taking further action.

skills.title: Navigate From Forum List to Target Forum
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the forum list for the entry whose visible label matches the requested forum.
2. Activate that forum’s link, using its semantic label rather than a fixed element ID.
3. Confirm completion when the destination page identifies the target forum and displays its submission content, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a specific Reddit/Postmill forum from a forum listing and view its content; the listing must expose the target forum as a link or recognizable entry.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Forum
skills.principle: Navigate from Home to Forums, locate the target forum by its visible name, and select its forum link. Once the page heading and URL identify the requested forum and its submissions are visible, treat the task as complete and stop instead of repeatedly clicking stale elements or scrolling unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific forum’s content and the target forum page visibly loads with its name, submissions, and navigation controls.

skills.title: Verify Forum Subscription State
skills.principle: Open the target forum and inspect its subscription control. Click “Subscribe” only when that label is present; after acting, confirm the control changes to “Unsubscribe.” If it already reads “Unsubscribe,” treat the goal as complete and report the existing subscription without clicking again.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a Postmill forum, especially if the account may already be subscribed. Use the forum page’s subscription button label as the observable status indicator.

skills.title: Act on Subscription State
skills.principle: Locate the target forum’s subscription control and branch on its label: click “Subscribe” when shown, then verify it changes to “Unsubscribe.” If “Unsubscribe” is already shown, treat the goal as satisfied, report completion, and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a forum from a Reddit-style forum list, after locating the target forum and its adjacent subscription button.

skills.title: Submit a Question to a Forum
skills.principle:
1. Open the target forum, then use its “Submit” link so the destination forum is preselected.
2. On “Create submission,” enter the question in the required “Title” field; leave optional “Body” blank if unnecessary.
3. Verify the “Forum” selector shows the target forum, then click “Create submission.”
4. Confirm the resulting page displays the submitted title, target forum, author, and a recent timestamp before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When posting a title-based question on Postmill/Reddit-style forums and the target forum is available in the forum list or current forum page.

skills.title: Verify Subscription State Before Acting
skills.principle: On a forum list or forum page, locate the target forum and inspect its subscription control. Treat “Unsubscribe” as confirmation that the current account is already subscribed; do not click it or keep searching for another “Subscribe” control. Report that the requested state is already satisfied and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to subscribe to a forum and the target’s visible control reads “Unsubscribe,” especially when the forum also appears under “Subscribed forums.”

skills.title: Verify Submission Then Stop
skills.principle: After clicking the post submission control, inspect the refreshed page rather than repeating the old action. Confirm success when the page shows the new post’s title, content, target forum, and a post URL. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not reuse stale element IDs or perform extra scrolling and clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a Reddit question and the page navigates away from the creation form to a post detail page showing the newly submitted title and content.

skills.title: Sort Forum Posts by Top
skills.principle:
1. Open the target forum and expand the current sorting control, such as “Sort by: Hot.”
2. Select “Top,” then verify the page shows “Sort by: Top.”
3. If the default time range shows no posts, open its time filter and select “All time.”
4. Confirm posts appear in descending vote order before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find highest-rated posts in a Reddit-style forum, especially when selecting “Top” initially yields an empty result due to a narrow default time range.

skills.title: Confirm Sorting Then Stop
skills.principle:
1. Open the current sorting control and choose the option meaning “Top” (for example, “Más votado”).
2. Confirm the page shows the selected sorting label and the updated results or URL.
3. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not repeat no-op waits or recheck unchanged state.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting a Reddit/Postmill feed and the accessibility tree shows the sorting control and its menu. After the control label reflects the requested ranking, the task is complete.

skills.title: Use Tags Navigation and Verify Empty State
skills.principle: From the forums listing, select the navigation entry labeled “Tags” (or its localized equivalent). Confirm the destination page heading matches the tags view, then inspect its content. If it displays an explicit empty-state message such as “No entries to show,” report that no forum tags are currently available and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view forum tags and the current page is a forum listing with a visible Tags navigation link. Use the empty-state text as confirmation when no tags exist.

skills.title: Use the Forums Navigation Directly
skills.principle: When asked to view all forum tags, use the explicit “Foros” navigation link rather than post pagination, “Más,” or subscribed-forum links. Inspect the resulting forums directory for the complete tag list, and only report infeasibility after verifying that directory and its available controls.
skills.when_to_apply: On Postmill’s home or post-list pages, when the task requests all forum tags/forums and an explicit “Foros” link is visible in the main navigation.

skills.title: Check Profile Search Scope
skills.principle: For a profile request, use a matching author link or the profile URL pattern shown by existing user links. If global search returns no entries, check whether it searches users before treating the result as a profile lookup; verify the destination username before reporting the profile opened.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating a user profile on a forum where global search may index posts rather than user accounts.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to User Profiles
skills.principle: For a requested Reddit user profile, use the site’s observed `/user/<username>` URL pattern directly instead of searching unrelated forum lists. Inspect the resulting page: a profile confirms success, while a clear 404 or not-found message supports reporting that the account could not be found.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a specific user profile and existing post metadata exposes `/user/<username>` links, especially when site search does not clearly return user accounts.

skills.title: Use Visible Options for Custom Comboboxes
skills.principle: When a forum field exposes a custom combobox rather than a native <select>, click the combobox, then click the visible option matching the target forum. Confirm the combobox value changes from its placeholder before completing the form; do not retry select_option on the combobox container.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Postmill/Reddit post and the forum selector has role="combobox", a listbox of options, or an error saying the element is not a <select>.

skills.title: Broaden Time Filter When Results Are Empty
skills.principle:
1. Select the relevant sorting option, such as “Most commented.”
2. If the page shows “There’s nothing here…,” inspect the active time filter rather than assuming no records exist.
3. Open the time-range menu and choose a broader option, such as “All time.”
4. Verify that posts appear ordered by the requested metric before reporting results.
