skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a forum or list page with metric-based sorting and the default time range returns no items. Requires visible sort and time-filter controls.

skills.title: Filter Forum Posts By All-Time Top
skills.principle:
1. Open the target forum and expand the current sorting control, such as “Sort by: Hot.”
2. Select “Top,” then inspect the resulting time-range control, which may default to a recent period.
3. Open the time-range control and select “All time.”
4. Confirm the page shows “Sort by: Top” and “From: All time,” with posts ordered by descending vote score.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a forum’s highest-rated posts across its entire history, especially when the site separates ranking type from time range.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Completion
skills.principle: Once the page visibly shows the requested state—here, “Sort by: Top” and “From: All time”—treat the task as complete. Report completion immediately and terminate; do not issue repeated no-op actions or continue reviewing without a specific unmet requirement.
skills.when_to_apply: After applying a forum sort and time filter, when the accessibility tree confirms both requested settings and the resulting posts are displayed.

skills.title: Submit and Verify a Forum Post
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum’s “Submit” page and keep the appropriate post type selected, such as “URL.”
2. Fill the required URL and Title fields, then expand the “Forum” combobox and select the requested forum.
3. Click “Create submission” only after required fields show values.
4. Confirm the resulting post page displays the submitted title, link, author, and forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a new URL post on the Reddit-like Postmill interface, provided the target title, URL, and forum are known and the “Submit” navigation link is available.

skills.title: Verify Submission Then Stop
skills.principle: After clicking “Create submission,” confirm completion from the resulting page: it should show the new title, body, author, and forum. Once these appear, report success and terminate instead of issuing additional waits or navigation actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when submitting content on Postmill and the page redirects from the creation form to a post detail page displaying the newly created submission.

skills.title: Use Wiki Fallback Navigation
skills.principle: When the Wiki link opens a “Page not found” page, inspect the Wiki sidebar for alternate section views. Open “All pages” and verify its heading and empty-state message; treat that view as the available Wiki destination when the index does not exist, then report the limitation and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a Reddit/Postmill Wiki link results in “Page not found” and the page offers sidebar links such as “All pages,” “Recent changes,” or “Create new page.”

skills.title: Use Wiki Navigation After Page Errors
skills.principle: When the Wiki landing link opens a “Page not found” page, inspect its Navigation sidebar rather than retrying the landing link. Select “All pages” and verify the resulting page heading or URL confirms the requested section, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: For Postmill wiki navigation when the main “Wiki” link leads to a missing page but the error page exposes sidebar links such as “All pages.”

skills.title: Use Wiki Navigation for All Pages
skills.principle: From a forums page, do not confuse the “Alphabetical” forums view with wiki pages. Open the “Wiki” navigation link, then select the sidebar link labeled “All pages.” Confirm completion when the page heading reads “All pages” (even if it reports no entries), then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Reddit’s wiki “All pages” section and the current page contains both forums navigation, including “Alphabetical,” and a separate “Wiki” link.

skills.title: Use Post Metadata Before Opening
skills.principle: On a Reddit forum listing, locate the target post by its visible title, then read its adjacent comments link/count. Open the post only when useful for verification; confirm the detail page repeats the title and comment count, then report the values and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving a Reddit post’s title and comment total from a forum listing, especially when the target is visibly present with a comments link.

skills.title: Send One Valid Final Response
skills.principle: Once the target post and requested metadata are visible, provide the result through a correctly populated final-response action. Verify the action payload is nonempty and accepted; after successful submission, terminate instead of repeatedly retrying the same message action.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit listing visibly contains the matching post and requested fields, but the environment reports an empty-action or invalid-message error after attempted response submission.

skills.title: Open Post Comments Directly
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target post by matching its visible title in the listing.
2. Activate its comments link or comment-count control rather than an unrelated post area.
3. Verify the destination page shows the post title and a visible “Comments” heading or comment list.
4. Once confirmed, report completion and stop; do not scroll or perform unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When Reddit/Postmill displays multiple posts and the task asks to open one post’s comments. The target title and a comments link or count must be visible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Comments View
skills.principle: After selecting the target post, verify the destination by checking for the post title, a “Comments” heading, comment controls, or visible comment entries. Once these indicators appear, the comments section is reached; report completion and stop instead of scrolling or clicking additional comment links.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a Reddit post’s comments and the resulting page already shows the post title plus “Comments,” a comment textbox, or comment entries.

skills.title: Submit and Verify Forum Post
skills.principle:
1. From the target forum, activate its “Submit” link.
2. On “Create submission,” choose the appropriate post type, fill the required title and any required content fields, and confirm the forum selection.
3. Activate “Create submission.”
4. Verify the resulting page displays the new post title and target forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a new post in a Postmill-style Reddit forum, provided the target forum is accessible and the submission form exposes its required fields and “Create submission” control.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Submission
skills.principle: After clicking the submission button, verify that the resulting page shows the new post in the target forum, including its title and body. Once this confirmation appears, report completion and terminate; do not click Submit again or retry using stale element identifiers.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a forum post and navigation changes from the submission form to a page displaying the newly created post. The visible post content and target forum are sufficient completion evidence.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Verification
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree shows the target username and profile URL, treat the task as complete. Report completion once using a correctly formatted user-facing action, then terminate. Do not click Overview, Submissions, or other profile controls merely to reconfirm an already verified page.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit profile-navigation tasks, after clicking a username link and observing the target user’s profile page, including its username heading or matching URL.

skills.title: Find Post With Most Comments
skills.principle: Scan each post on the forum listing and read its comment-count link, treating “No comments” as zero. Track the largest count and its associated title. Open the candidate post and verify its title and comment count are displayed, then report the result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to identify the most-commented post on a Reddit-style forum page, provided the listing exposes comment counts for all relevant posts or pages.

skills.title: Check Every Results Page
skills.principle: On a forum listing, do not assume the maximum is visible on the first page. Record each post’s displayed comment count, follow the “More” pagination control, and continue until no further results remain. Compare all collected counts, then report the corresponding post and count. Verify the winning post’s detail page still displays the same comment total before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for the post with the most comments, likes, or another maximum on a paginated Reddit forum listing, especially when a visible “More” control indicates additional results.

skills.title: Compare All Visible Comment Counts
skills.principle: Read each post’s comment link or label, treating “No comments” as zero, and track the highest numeric count rather than relying on sort order or recency. If needed, open the leading post and verify its displayed comment total. Report the post title and confirmed count once no remaining visible candidate exceeds it.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find the most-commented post on a Reddit-style forum page and the page exposes comment counts for multiple listed posts.

skills.title: Read Comment Count From Matching Post
skills.principle: Scan the forum listing for the post whose title matches the requested text exactly. Within that post’s article, read the adjacent comments link or label and report its numeric count. Do not confuse vote totals or comment counts from neighboring posts.
skills.when_to_apply: When answering how many comments a specific Reddit or Postmill forum post has, provided the relevant listing page displays post titles and comment-count links.

skills.title: Open a Post’s Comments
skills.principle:
1. Scan the forum list for the exact target post title.
2. Within that post’s article, activate its comments-count link rather than an unrelated post control.
3. Confirm the destination by checking the post title and a visible “Comments” heading with comment entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit-style forum lists many posts and the task asks to open comments for one specific post. Ensure the exact title matches before selecting its comments link.

skills.title: Open and Summarize a Target Post
skills.principle:
1. Scan the forum’s post list for the exact target title, using its visible heading and associated link.
2. Open the matching post and verify the page heading matches the requested item.
3. Read the post and representative comments, then summarize the main perspectives and relevant context.
4. Report completion once the summary is delivered; do not continue with unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check out a specific Reddit or forum post from a listing, especially when the target has many similarly formatted entries and comments provide the requested substance.

skills.title: Open and Verify a Reddit User Profile
skills.principle: On a Reddit/Postmill listing, locate the target username link in a submission or comment and activate it. Verify the resulting page by checking the page title, URL path, or profile heading matches the requested user. Once the profile is visibly loaded, report completion with a simple, properly escaped message and stop; avoid unnecessary follow-up actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a Reddit user profile and the target username is visible as a linked author or commenter in the current page. Verify the profile page before reporting completion.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page title or URL confirms the requested user profile is open, report completion once and terminate immediately. Do not repeat completion messages, issue noop actions, or continue browsing after the goal is satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit profile-view tasks when navigation has landed on the target user's profile and the accessibility tree confirms the username, profile heading, or user URL.

skills.title: Use Wiki Sidebar Navigation
skills.principle: After opening the Wiki area, inspect the page’s Navigation sidebar for the task-specific destination. If the wiki landing path shows “Page not found” but exposes an “All pages” link, activate that link and verify the resulting heading is “All pages” before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Postmill wiki task and the main Wiki link opens a landing or error page with sidebar navigation. Use the visible destination link and confirm the page heading matches the requested section.

skills.title: Use Wiki Sidebar Navigation
skills.principle: When the Wiki link opens a “Page not found” view, inspect that page’s Navigation sidebar rather than retrying the Wiki link. Select “All pages” there, then verify the destination heading is “All pages” and report completion even if it says there are no entries.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit/Postmill tasks requesting all wiki pages, when the Wiki landing route shows an error but exposes sidebar links such as “All pages” and “Recent changes”.

skills.title: Use Sidebar Links After Broken Landing Pages
skills.principle: When a requested page shows “Page not found,” inspect the accessibility tree for a navigation link matching the task, such as “Recent changes.” Open that role-labeled link directly, then verify the destination heading and status text before reporting the result. If the page states that no entries exist, treat that as the completed answer.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a wiki or similar site’s landing URL is unavailable but the accessibility tree exposes the requested section in navigation. Verify the destination before concluding.

skills.title: Terminate After Verifying Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate using the relevant sidebar link, then verify the destination by its heading and page-state message. Once the target section is displayed—even when it says there are no entries—report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task reaches a page whose heading matches the requested section and its content clearly states the current result, such as an empty recent-changes list.

skills.title: Verify Access Before Wiki Creation
skills.principle: Use the wiki’s visible navigation to locate the creation entry rather than guessing page URLs. If creation requires authentication, use only confirmed credentials, submit once, and verify that the page changes to an authenticated state. If the site reports invalid credentials, stop pursuing creation and request valid access details.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill wiki shows no visible creation control and the user is logged out, especially after a guessed page route returns “Page not found” or authentication fails.

skills.title: Authenticate Before Wiki Creation
skills.principle: When the wiki shows “Page not found” and no creation control, use the visible “Log in” link first. After authentication, return to the Wiki area and inspect the accessibility tree for the “Create new page” control instead of guessing URL patterns.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when attempting to create a Reddit/Postmill wiki page anonymously and the page exposes “Log in” but no “Create new page” or edit control.

skills.title: Verify Empty Wiki Listings
skills.principle: When the wiki landing page is missing or inconclusive, open its "All pages" navigation entry and inspect the resulting listing. Treat an explicit message such as "There are no entries to display" as confirmation that no wiki pages are available, then report that result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked whether wiki pages exist and the initial wiki page shows "Page not found" or otherwise does not list content, provided an "All pages" link is available.

skills.title: Verify Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL, page heading, and visible content before taking navigation actions. If they already match the requested section, report completion immediately. Otherwise, activate the navigation link whose accessible label matches the requested destination, then verify the resulting heading or content.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial page may already be the requested destination. A matching URL, section heading, and relevant content are sufficient completion evidence.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Navigation Actions
skills.principle:
1. Encode the browser action as a complete, valid command; do not submit truncated or doubly quoted click expressions.
2. After an empty-action or parsing error, stop repeating the same payload and use the visible destination link or its observed href with direct navigation.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page URL and displayed content correspond to the requested section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a navigation link is visible in the accessibility tree but clicking produces an empty-action or parsing error. The destination href must be observable before using direct navigation.

skills.title: Use Contextual Create-Page Links
skills.principle: When a wiki landing URL shows “Page not found,” inspect the navigation and page actions for a semantically labeled “Create new page” or “Create this page” link. Follow it, then verify the destination heading and required URL, Title, Body fields before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a wiki-entry creation page initially lands on a missing-page view that offers a creation link or sidebar navigation entry.

skills.title: Recover From Wiki Route Errors
skills.principle: When a wiki link or guessed creation URL shows “Page not found,” do not repeat the same route. Use the page’s observed navigation, such as “All pages” or “Recent changes,” then inspect those pages for a new-entry control or relevant link. Report infeasibility only after checking available UI paths and confirming none leads to creation.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a wiki or content-creation page produces a 404 and the page exposes alternative navigation links. Requires inspecting those visible routes before concluding the requested operation is unavailable.

skills.title: Recover Authentication Before Editing
skills.principle: When wiki editing is unavailable, verify authentication first. If login reports “Invalid credentials,” use the offered password-reset flow or obtain valid credentials; do not guess passwords. After successful login, return to the target wiki page and use its observed creation/edit control rather than inventing URL paths.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill wiki page shows “Page not found” without creation controls and the navigation still shows “Log in,” especially after an authentication failure.

skills.title: Verify Authentication Before Continuing
skills.principle: After submitting the login form, inspect the resulting page for a logged-in state, such as authenticated navigation or disappearance of the login form. If “Invalid credentials” remains, treat authentication as unsuccessful and use the available password-reset or account-registration flow rather than proceeding to wiki actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing Reddit/Postmill wiki content requires authentication and the login submission returns either the login form or an explicit credential error.

skills.title: Submit Reddit Searches With Enter
skills.principle:
1. Locate the Reddit/Postmill searchbox by its accessible label and enter the requested topic.
2. If no search button is visible, press Enter while the searchbox is focused to submit the query.
3. Confirm the page shows a Search heading and results count for the query, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill content-search tasks when the searchbox is visible and the interface lacks an obvious Search button. Verify the resulting page displays query-specific results before finishing.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: After navigation, inspect the latest accessibility tree before interacting. Use only element bids or accessible roles currently present; do not reuse stale IDs from an earlier observation. If a target is absent, re-identify the rendered form controls and verify the page state before filling or submitting.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a Reddit/Postmill form or control is expected but the accessibility tree does not show the previously identified element, especially after navigation, scrolling, or rerendering.

skills.title: Use Verified Credentials Before Profile Access
skills.principle: On Reddit-style sites, inspect the page for authentication state. If login is required, use only credentials explicitly provided or the site's “Reset password?” flow; do not guess passwords. Submit login and verify success by confirming the login control disappears or an authenticated account/profile navigation appears before opening the profile.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a user profile from a page showing “Log in,” especially when no valid password is available. Use the reset-password process or request credentials before continuing.

skills.title: Verify Credentials Before Retrying Login
skills.principle: Use only credentials supplied or securely available in the session. Submit the login form once, then inspect the result: a successful redirect or logged-in navigation confirms authentication; “Invalid credentials” means access is blocked. Do not guess passwords or repeatedly retry; report that the profile cannot be viewed and request valid credentials or alternative instructions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requires viewing an authenticated user profile and the page shows a login form, especially after the first submission returns “Invalid credentials.”

skills.title: Rank Forums by Submission Count
skills.principle: Open the forum directory and use its “Sort by: Submissions” control when available. Read the submission count attached to the first forum; verify the list is descending and inspect additional pages if ordering or pagination leaves the maximum uncertain. Report the forum name and count only after confirming the highest visible value.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill tasks asking which forum has the most submissions, provided the forum directory exposes per-forum submission counts and a sorting or pagination mechanism.

skills.title: Report the Verified Top Forum
skills.principle: On the forums list, use the submission-count sort and verify the first forum’s displayed count. Once the top entry is confirmed, immediately provide the forum name and count as the final answer, then terminate rather than repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which forum leads a numeric ranking and the page visibly supports sorting by that metric or shows entries in descending order.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums View
skills.principle: From the forums section, select the navigation link labeled “Alphabetical.” Confirm completion when the resulting “All forums” page groups forum links under letter headings in alphabetical order, then stop and report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse or view Reddit/Postmill forums alphabetically and the forums page exposes an “Alphabetical” navigation entry.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums View
skills.principle: On the forums list, activate the visible “Alphabetical” navigation entry using a valid click action. Verify the page changes to the all-forums view and shows letter-grouped forum links in alphabetical order. Once this state is confirmed, stop rather than issuing repeated scrolling or no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse Reddit-style forums alphabetically and the forums page exposes an “Alphabetical” link or equivalent navigation entry.

skills.title: Navigate Forums to View Tags
skills.principle: From an unrelated or missing page, open the main “Forums” navigation entry. On the forum listing, select the “Tags” link in its local navigation. Confirm the “Tags” heading and inspect the result; “There are no entries to display” is a valid completed empty-state result. Report the observed state and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all forum tags in the Reddit/Postmill interface, especially when the current page is unrelated, unavailable, or a wiki page.

skills.title: Recover From Stale Element References
skills.principle: When navigation remains unchanged or an element-reference error occurs, reacquire the current accessibility tree before acting again. Locate the navigation entry by its visible role and label, then activate the newly observed reference or navigate through its currently exposed destination. Verify the URL and page heading changed before concluding the feature is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after a click reports a missing element reference or the page remains unchanged, especially when attempting to leave an error page for a linked forum or navigation section.

skills.title: Navigate Forums Pagination Reliably
skills.principle:
1. If the current page is unrelated or shows an error, use the site navigation to open the forums list.
2. Locate the pagination controls and select the link matching the requested page number.
3. Confirm completion by checking the resulting URL or page content identifies the requested page, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific page of a Reddit-style forums list, especially when the initial page is incorrect, unavailable, or displays a page-not-found state.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Before Acting
skills.principle: On a paginated list, inspect the current URL and pagination state before clicking. Select the link labeled with the requested page number, then verify that the URL and visible page content match. Once the target page is confirmed, stop instead of clicking “Next” or repeating navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating a Reddit-style forums list or any paginated page where the requested page may already be active and “Next” advances beyond the target.

skills.title: Recover and Verify Forum Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum directory through the visible “Forums” navigation entry.
2. If a click produces an empty-action error, retry with the simplest valid click syntax rather than repeating malformed payloads.
3. Select the list entry whose accessible name matches the requested forum.
4. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and forum-specific content, then stop and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Postmill/Reddit-style forums from a homepage, especially after a browser action reports an empty-action error and the target forum must be verified.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation After Click Errors
skills.principle: When a UI click repeatedly returns an empty-action error, stop retrying the same bid. Read the target link’s observed href and navigate directly to it, then verify the URL or page heading matches the requested forum before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating a Postmill forum and a visible navigation link produces an empty-action or malformed-action error, especially when its destination URL is available in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Navigate Forums Directly After Errors
skills.principle: When an initial page is unavailable or interaction errors repeat, use the site's visible navigation structure or known forum route to open the forum directory. Inspect forum entries by their displayed names, select the entry matching the requested topic, and verify the destination heading identifies that forum before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit-like forum tasks when the starting page shows an error, search controls fail, or navigation actions do not execute, but a forums directory link or route is available.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Continuing
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and accessibility-tree heading before acting. If they already identify the requested page, report completion immediately; otherwise use the visible navigation link matching the requested destination, then verify the resulting URL or heading.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a page and the browser may already be there or may start on an unexpected route. Requires an observable URL, page heading, or equivalent destination marker.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Verify the page heading or URL shows the requested destination. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated no-op actions or continue interacting with the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the accessibility tree shows the requested page’s heading, navigation state, or destination URL after a successful link click.

skills.title: Use Wiki Navigation to Verify Pages
skills.principle: From the wiki landing page, use the sidebar's "All pages" link rather than assuming the landing route lists content. Confirm the destination heading and inspect the main content; if it says "There are no entries to display," report that the wiki currently has no pages and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all wiki pages and the wiki landing route is empty, unavailable, or shows "Page not found," provided the sidebar exposes an "All pages" navigation link.

skills.title: Verify Wiki Empty States
skills.principle: Open the Wiki section and use its “All pages” navigation entry to inspect the complete page list. If it shows “There are no entries to display,” verify “Recent changes” once; when it is also empty, treat the wiki as having no viewable pages, report that result, and stop instead of repeatedly revisiting navigation links.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all wiki pages and the Wiki landing page is missing, empty, or ambiguous. The “All pages” and “Recent changes” links must be available for confirmation.

skills.title: Use the Wiki Recent Changes Link
skills.principle: If the wiki landing page is unavailable, inspect its navigation for the “Recent changes” entry and open that destination. Confirm completion by checking the page heading and result message; “There are no entries to display” means no recent changes, which can be reported directly.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking wiki edit history and the wiki landing route shows an error, but the accessibility tree exposes a “Recent changes” navigation link.

skills.title: Use Wiki Recent Changes Link
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's Wiki section and inspect the resulting page.
2. If the Wiki landing page shows “Page not found,” use its Navigation sidebar and select “Recent changes.”
3. Confirm completion from the Recent changes page; report that there are no recent changes when it states “There are no entries to display.”
skills.when_to_apply: When checking wiki activity on Postmill-like Reddit sites, especially after the Wiki link leads to a not-found page with a Navigation sidebar containing “Recent changes.”

skills.title: Handle Invalid Login Credentials
skills.principle: When the login form reports “Invalid credentials,” do not retry guessed passwords. Use the site’s “Reset password?” flow if authorized, or request the correct password from the user. Continue to the profile only after a successful login state is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When accessing a user profile requires authentication and the login page displays an invalid-credentials error after submission.

skills.title: Use Verified Authentication Paths
skills.principle: When profile access requires authentication, use the existing authenticated session or credentials explicitly provided. If login fails, stop guessing passwords; use the visible “Reset password?” flow or report that authentication is unavailable. Create a new account only when the task explicitly requests registration, not as a substitute for accessing the requested user profile.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Reddit/Postmill profile tasks when the page shows “Log in” or login returns “Invalid credentials,” and no verified password or authenticated session is available.

skills.title: Verify Empty Tag Results Before Exploring Alternatives
skills.principle: Open the forum directory and select the “Tags” navigation entry. If the Tags page explicitly says “There are no entries to display,” treat that as the completion state for the request, report that no tags are available, and stop rather than repeatedly revisiting Tags or trying unrelated views.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing forums by tags on Postmill and the Tags page is accessible but visibly contains no entries.

skills.title: Verify Tags Then Stop
skills.principle: Open the Forums section and select the “Tags” navigation entry. If the page shows “There are no entries to display,” treat the requested tag browse as unavailable, report that observable result, and terminate instead of exploring unrelated forums, posts, or pagination.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing Reddit/Postmill forums by tags and the Tags page is reachable but visibly empty. Confirm the empty-state message before reporting that no tags are available.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums View
skills.principle: From the Reddit forums listing, select the navigation link labeled “Alphabetical” rather than changing the submission sort menu. Confirm completion when the page displays an “All forums” view with letter headings and forum links grouped alphabetically.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view Reddit forums alphabetically and the forums listing is available. If starting elsewhere, open “Forums” first, then select “Alphabetical” and verify grouped letter headings.

skills.title: Validate Browser Action Syntax
skills.principle: Issue browser actions in the tool’s exact expected syntax, without nested JSON, truncated arguments, or mismatched quotes. After an execution error, inspect the unchanged accessibility tree, then resend one clean action targeting the visible element by role or label and verify navigation before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a BrowserGym action returns a parsing or empty-action error, especially while clicking visible navigation links. Confirm the page has not changed before retrying.

skills.title: Use Visible Labels for Styled Radios
skills.principle: When a radio input is visually hidden or its label intercepts pointer events, click the associated visible label instead of the input. Confirm the radio state changes before continuing with dependent fields.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on submission forms where the accessibility tree shows a radio option plus a separate label, especially after a direct radio click times out because another element intercepts pointer events.

skills.title: Use a Verified Image File Path
skills.principle: For an image submission, select the visible “Image” tab, then upload an actual existing image file rather than a placeholder path. Confirm the file control changes from “No file chosen” before completing the title, forum, and submission fields.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill submission form offers URL and Image modes and requires a local upload. The image must already exist at a known accessible path before invoking file upload.

skills.title: Verify Empty Wiki Sections
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's Wiki navigation entry and inspect the resulting page.
2. If it shows “Page not found,” open “All pages” to check for existing content.
3. Open “Recent changes” as a second confirmation; if both show no entries, report that no Wiki content exists and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to learn about a site through its Wiki, especially when the main Wiki page displays “Page not found” and provides links to “All pages” or “Recent changes”.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Wiki Page
skills.principle: When the requested Wiki page loads, verify its title and visible content, then treat navigation as complete. Summarize or report the information available instead of clicking internal anchors or unrelated resource links, which may lead to missing pages and stale element references.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task asks you to open a site’s Wiki or index page and the page has loaded with descriptive content. Stop once the requested destination is visibly confirmed unless the task explicitly requires deeper exploration.

skills.title: Use the Home Navigation Link
skills.principle: When the current page is not Home, locate the persistent navigation link labeled “Home” and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the URL is the site root and the page displays the home feed. If the site-root URL and home content are already visible, report that the goal is complete without navigating further.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill tasks asking to return to Home, especially when viewing another page and the accessibility tree exposes a persistent “Home” navigation link or site-root URL.

skills.title: Use Fresh Bids After Navigation
skills.principle: After any navigation, re-read the accessibility tree and use only element references from the newest observation. If a bid is missing or an action errors, do not retry stale or malformed selectors; use the observed destination URL with `goto` when appropriate, then verify the page title and URL before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Reddit/Postmill between pages, especially after a failed click or page transition, and the accessibility tree may contain stale element bids.

skills.title: Execute Reddit Search and Verify Results
skills.principle:
1. Locate the navigation search box and enter the requested topic.
2. Press Enter to submit the query rather than only filling the field.
3. Confirm the Search page shows the query and a results heading such as “results for [query]”.
4. Once results are visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit tasks asking to find posts by topic when a navigation search box is available. The task is complete after the search results page visibly lists matching results.

skills.title: Access Reddit Block List
skills.principle: Open the logged-in username menu, select the visible “Block list” navigation entry, and verify the destination heading and contents. Report the listed blocked users; if the page says “There are no entries to display,” report that the block list is empty.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks to view or manage the current user’s blocked users and the authenticated page exposes a username menu with account-management links.

skills.title: Use Accessibility IDs for UI Actions
skills.principle: After each observation, identify the target by its current accessibility-tree bid and role, then act on that bid rather than passing visible text as the selector. If an action fails, re-read the latest tree and choose the newly observed bid before trying another route.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever BrowserGym reports a missing element or the page contains repeated visible labels. This is essential for navigating account menus, settings, and block-list controls reliably.

skills.title: Inspect Account Menu for Theme Controls
skills.principle: When a theme toggle is not visible in the page content, open the authenticated user/account menu and inspect its menu items for light/dark mode controls. Select the available theme option, then verify the page appearance or selected state changes before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Reddit-like pages when the profile button is visible but no theme control appears in the main content. Check the account menu before concluding the task is infeasible.

skills.title: Fill Required Submission Title
skills.principle: On a submission form, identify the required Title field by its label and fill it with a concise, descriptive title matching the requested topic. Verify the field displays the entered text, then report completion without submitting unrelated required fields unless submission is explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks you to write or provide a submission title and the form’s Title field is visible. Apply even if other submission fields, such as Forum, remain incomplete when the task does not request publishing.

skills.title: Use the Submission Form Directly
skills.principle: When asked to write a title for a new submission, open the site's “Submit” page rather than searching for an existing post. Fill the required “Title” field with a descriptive topic-specific title, using the field's observed label or role instead of hard-coded element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the user requests a submission title and the page offers a visible “Submit” navigation entry or equivalent creation form, even if no matching post already exists.

skills.title: Use Markdown Bullets and Verify Preview
skills.principle: Enter each list item on its own line in the submission Body field using Markdown bullet syntax, such as `* item` or `- item`. Check the live Preview and confirm each item appears as a rendered bullet before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Reddit/Postmill submission whose Body field indicates Markdown is allowed and a bulleted list is requested. Verify the preview updates before finishing.

skills.title: Use Single Actions and Verify State
skills.principle: In the Postmill submission editor, enter the complete Markdown list in the Body field with one fill action (for example, separate items with newlines). Afterward, verify the Body value and Preview show the expected bullet markers. Send only one BrowserGym action per turn; never combine press and fill, and do not assume an item was added when the observation still shows only the prior text.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Reddit/Postmill submission body with Markdown formatting, especially after an action error or when the accessibility tree’s Body value and Preview do not yet confirm the intended list.

skills.title: Create a Post with an External Link
skills.principle:
1. Enter the external link in the Body field using Markdown syntax: `[link text](https://target-site.example)`.
2. Confirm the preview renders the Markdown as a clickable link.
3. Fill required Title and Forum fields, then select the appropriate forum and click Create submission.
4. Verify the published post displays the title and clickable external link before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill submission must include another website link and the Create submission form provides a Markdown-enabled Body field, required Title and Forum fields, and a rendered preview.

skills.title: Open Profile Through User Menu
skills.principle: On Postmill, open the logged-in username menu in the top navigation, then select the “Profile” link. Confirm completion when the profile page loads with the user’s heading and profile navigation (such as Overview, Submissions, or Comments), then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view the current user’s Postmill profile and the top navigation shows the logged-in username as an expandable menu button.

skills.title: Verify Forum Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current page URL, title, and visible forum heading before taking navigation actions. If they already identify the requested forum, report that it is open and stop. Otherwise, use a visible forum link, such as one under “Subscribed forums,” then verify the destination heading or URL before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a forum and the browser may already be displaying it, especially on Postmill pages with visible forum links or a forum heading.

skills.title: Verify Forum Navigation Then Stop
skills.principle: Select the forum link by its visible name or role. After navigation, verify the page heading, URL path, or forum label matches the requested forum. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a specific forum and the accessibility tree shows a matching navigation link or subscribed-forum entry. Use the resulting forum heading or URL as the completion check.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Visible Labels
skills.principle: From an arbitrary Reddit page, open the global “Forums” navigation link. On the forum listing, locate the entry whose accessible label matches the requested forum, activate that forum link, and verify completion from the destination URL or page heading before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a named Postmill/Reddit forum and the current page provides a global “Forums” link. Confirm the requested forum entry is visible in the forum list before selecting it.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Forum Access
skills.principle: Once the target forum page is visible and its heading plus posts or discussions confirm the destination, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a specific forum and the current accessibility tree shows the requested forum heading, URL context, and discussion listings.

skills.title: Stop After Checking Notifications
skills.principle: Open the Notifications link and inspect the resulting page. If it displays “There are no entries to display” or lists the current activity, treat the viewing task as complete, report the observed result, and terminate instead of navigating elsewhere or repeatedly refreshing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view Reddit notifications and the Notifications page has loaded successfully, especially when its content explicitly indicates no entries or displays the available activity.

skills.title: Create a Missing Wiki Index Page
skills.principle:
1. Open the Wiki entry and recognize a missing index when the page shows “Page not found.”
2. Select “Create this page,” keep the predefined index URL, and fill the required Title and Body fields.
3. Use Markdown to provide a structured landing page with navigation links and useful sections.
4. Confirm the preview renders correctly, select “Save,” and verify the resulting page displays the title and content.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a site’s main Wiki landing page and the Wiki route exists but displays “Page not found” with a “Create this page” control. Verify required fields and the saved rendered page.

skills.title: Operate Custom Forum Comboboxes Correctly
skills.principle: For a required forum field implemented as a custom combobox, do not use native select actions. Open the combobox, use its revealed searchbox to type the intended forum, then click the matching option and verify the displayed value changed from “Choose one…”. Submit only after the required selection is visibly applied.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill submission and the Forum control has role="combobox", expanded state, or a popup listbox rather than a native <select> element.

skills.title: Recover from Wrong Article Routes
skills.principle: After a guessed article URL returns 404, return to the site and locate the current search field by role. Submit distinctive title terms, follow a matching article link, and verify its heading; describe an unsuccessful search within its checked scope instead of treating an unrelated Wiki error as article absence.
skills.when_to_apply: When a forum article request reaches a guessed or unrelated path, especially after invalid element references prevent searching.

skills.title: Stop After Opening Target Post
skills.principle: Once the target Reddit post page visibly shows the matching title, treat the viewing task as complete. Send one properly formatted completion message if required, then terminate; do not repeat messages, use noop, scroll, or perform unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit search result has been opened and the resulting page visibly matches the requested post title, especially for view-only tasks with no required interaction.

skills.title: Open And Verify Target Article
skills.principle: When a Reddit search result matches the requested title, open its title link, then verify the article page heading and body text. If the full post is already visible, read it without reopening; scroll only when needed. Once the article content is present and read, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit tasks asking you to read a specific post, starting from search results or another page where the target title is visible.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Requested Article
skills.principle: Once the target Reddit post page is loaded and its article text is visible, treat the reading task as complete. Do not repeatedly focus or issue noop actions; provide a concise completion response and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit search result has been opened and the requested post title and full body text are visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Repeating
skills.principle: Click the target article’s voting control once, then inspect its updated label and score. Treat “Retract upvote” (or equivalent selected state) as confirmation that the vote succeeded; stop immediately. Repeatedly clicking toggles the vote off and on, risking failure.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit/Postmill article from a list or search results, especially when multiple vote controls are visible. After each click, verify the target article’s control changed to the selected-state label before taking further action.

skills.title: Verify Target Post Vote State
skills.principle: Locate the target article by its visible title, then use the vote control within that article’s result—not a control belonging to another result. If it shows “Downvote,” activate it; completion is confirmed when it changes to “Retract downvote” and the score reflects a negative vote. If already labeled “Retract downvote,” report completion without clicking again.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a specific Reddit/Postmill search result, especially when multiple articles and vote controls appear together. First identify the correct article container and inspect its current vote state.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Repeating
skills.principle: After clicking a Reddit post’s vote control, inspect the updated article state. A “Retract downvote” control and a decreased score confirm the downvote succeeded; stop immediately. Do not click again, because clicking the same control may remove or toggle the vote.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit post from a list or search results, after the initial vote click and whenever the control or score visibly changes.

skills.title: Submit Updated Reddit Search
skills.principle:
1. Locate the relevant “Search query” field, preferably the main search form when duplicate navigation fields exist.
2. Clear the existing query, fill the requested search terms, and click the “Search” button.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the URL/query and results heading reflect the new terms, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill search page contains an existing query and the task requests replacing it with new terms. Ensure the updated field is submitted and verify the resulting query and results heading.

skills.title: Submit Search With Enter
skills.principle: After clearing and filling the Reddit/Postmill search box, submit the form with Enter rather than clicking the text field repeatedly. Confirm completion by checking that the URL, page content, or displayed results change to reflect the query; if unchanged, inspect the accessibility tree for the actual search-submit control.
skills.when_to_apply: When a search field contains the requested query but clicking the field does not navigate or update results. Ensure the field is focused and verify a visible page-state change after submission.

skills.title: Replace and Submit Search Query
skills.principle:
1. Identify the relevant “Search query” field, preferably in the main search form.
2. Clear the existing query and fill in the requested replacement text.
3. Activate the “Search” button.
4. Confirm completion when the URL/query field and results heading reflect the new query, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit/Postmill search pages when a task requests changing an existing query. The search form and its “Search” control must be visible, and completion should be verified from the updated query and results state.

skills.title: Stop After Search Confirmation
skills.principle: After submitting a changed search query, verify that the searchbox shows the new value and the results heading reflects it. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a Reddit/Postmill search query and the updated URL, searchbox value, and results heading visibly confirm that the new query was applied.

skills.title: Aggregate Search Results by Forum
skills.principle: Inspect every search result, including comment matches, and identify its forum from the nearby “in” link or parent post context. Count each result once per forum, compare totals, and report all forums tied for the highest count rather than selecting one arbitrarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit search asks which forum has the most results and the page lists mixed post and comment matches with forum attribution.

skills.title: Aggregate Search Results By Forum
skills.principle: Use the search results count and each result’s forum attribution to group matching posts by forum. Count result articles per forum, not comments, votes, or total submissions. Review all result pages if pagination exists, then report the forum with the highest grouped count. Do not declare infeasibility merely because results span multiple forums.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which forum has the most results for a search query and the search page displays matching posts with forum links or labels, including potentially paginated results.

skills.title: Verify Navigation State Before Repeating
skills.principle: Confirm the clicked control’s role and resulting URL/page state after every navigation. For a block-list task, authenticate first, then use the account/profile or settings navigation exposed in the authenticated view. If the page remains unchanged or still shows “Log in,” stop repeating the same control and reassess the available links.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking account-specific Reddit settings such as a block list, especially if the current page is search/forums content, login status is unclear, or a click leaves the observed page unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Theme Toggle State
skills.principle: Open the account menu and select the theme control labeled “Dark mode.” After it closes, reopen the menu only to verify that the control now reads “Light mode,” indicating dark mode is active. Stop immediately after this state change; do not click “Light mode,” which would toggle back.
skills.when_to_apply: When switching Reddit/Postmill themes through the account dropdown, especially after the menu closes and the control label changes. Use the post-click label or visible styling as confirmation before taking further action.

skills.title: Open Reddit Account Information
skills.principle:
1. Open the logged-in username menu and select “My account.”
2. On the account page, read the username, account ID, registration details, and status from visible fields or sidebar information.
3. Report the observed values and stop once the account information is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks to view the current user’s account information and the logged-in username control is visible. Requires an authenticated session and a visible “My account” menu option.

skills.title: Handle Invalid Login Credentials
skills.principle: Use the available account credentials rather than placeholder text, then submit the login form and verify that the page leaves the login screen. If “Invalid credentials” appears, recheck the username and obtain the real password or use “Reset password?” instead of repeatedly submitting guessed or placeholder passwords.
skills.when_to_apply: When an account-information task starts unauthenticated and the login form shows a prefilled username, a password field, and an “Invalid credentials” message after submission.

skills.title: Use Wiki Index After Root 404
skills.principle: When the Wiki link or direct Wiki URL shows “Page not found,” treat it as a destination failure rather than retrying the same navigation. Use the Wiki sidebar’s “All pages” link to reach the available Wiki index, and verify the resulting heading or page content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when navigating to a site’s Wiki produces a “Page not found” page but the page exposes Wiki navigation such as “All pages” or “Recent changes.”

skills.title: Re-read Page After Navigation
skills.principle: After a navigation succeeds, inspect the new accessibility tree before acting again. If the requested forum list is visible, stop clicking the parent “Forums” link and select the target forum entry by its displayed name, such as the “movies” link. Use the current visible element rather than a stale bid.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating through Reddit/Postmill forum lists, especially after the URL or page heading changes. Confirm the forum list is loaded before selecting the requested community.

skills.title: Navigate to a Named Forum
skills.principle:
1. From an unrelated Reddit page, open the visible “Forums” navigation entry.
2. Scan the forum list for the requested forum name and select its matching forum link.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading, URL path, and visible post listing identify the requested forum; then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific forum and the current Reddit page is elsewhere. The Forums navigation entry and the target forum must be accessible in the forum list.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Browser Actions
skills.principle: After an action returns an execution error or leaves the page unchanged, inspect the required action syntax and issue one valid action rather than repeatedly replaying malformed payloads. For forum navigation, use the visible link by its accessible label; if clicking continues failing, navigate to the observed forum-list route directly, then select the target forum and verify its heading or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a visible navigation link is present but BrowserGym reports an empty or malformed action, or repeated clicks produce no page transition. Confirm completion from the destination heading or URL.

skills.title: Use Wiki Navigation for Recent Changes
skills.principle: Open the site's Wiki entry, then use the Navigation sidebar's “Recent changes” link rather than stopping if the Wiki landing page says “Page not found.” Confirm completion by reading the Recent changes page and report whether entries are listed; “There are no entries to display” means no recent changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect recent Wiki updates and the Wiki landing page may be missing or unavailable, provided its sidebar navigation is still visible.

skills.title: Open the Target Post’s Comments
skills.principle:
1. Locate the post whose title matches the requested text in the forum list.
2. Open its title link or adjacent comments link to reach the post page.
3. Confirm the page shows the matching title, a “Comments” heading, and visible comment entries; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view comments for a specific Reddit/Postmill post and the forum listing contains multiple posts. Verify the opened page matches the requested title before concluding.

skills.title: Open a Reddit Post by Exact Title
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the forum listing for a post whose visible title exactly matches the requested title.
2. Activate that post’s title link, using its semantic role and current accessibility-tree reference rather than a hard-coded identifier.
3. Confirm completion when the destination page shows the matching heading, post content, and comments, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific Reddit or Postmill post and the listing page contains visible post titles. Requires an exact title match and a destination page whose heading confirms the target.

skills.title: Open the Exact Reddit Post
skills.principle:
1. Scan the forum listing for the exact requested post title, matching the visible heading or link text rather than relying on position.
2. Activate the corresponding post link.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading and URL identify the requested post and its content is visible; then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit task asks you to navigate from a subreddit or forum listing to a specific post, and the listing exposes post titles as links.

skills.title: Locate Reddit Posts by Exact Title
skills.principle: Scan the visible post list for the requested title, activate the matching post-title link, then verify the destination page heading matches the request. If the matching heading is already displayed, report completion without navigating again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Reddit/Postmill submission lists to a specific post, especially when multiple similar posts are visible and exact-title confirmation is available.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Clicking
skills.principle: On a Reddit listing, locate the target post by its title and inspect its associated voting control. Click only if it is labeled "Upvote"; if it reads "Retract upvote," the requested vote already exists. Report the confirmed state and terminate without clicking again, since clicking would remove the vote.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to upvote a Reddit post and the target is visible in a listing with its voting control. Requires checking the control label before acting.

skills.title: Verify Upvote State After Clicking
skills.principle: Locate the target post by its title and click its associated “Upvote” control once. Reinspect the post afterward: completion is indicated when the control changes to “Retract upvote” and the displayed score increases. Do not click again, because a second click reverses the vote.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit/Postmill post from a list, especially when the page remains visible after the click. Confirm the control’s changed label before terminating.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Acting
skills.principle: Locate the target post by its exact title, then inspect the vote control within that post. Click the control only when it says “Upvote”; after the page updates, confirm it says “Retract upvote.” If it already says “Retract upvote,” leave it unchanged and report that the post is already upvoted.
skills.when_to_apply: When completing an upvote task on a Reddit-style post listing, especially when the account may have voted previously and each post has separate vote controls.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Retrying
skills.principle: Locate the target post by its exact title, then activate its article-scoped “Upvote” control. After the click, re-read the accessibility tree: completion is indicated by “Retract upvote” and the updated score. If it still says “Upvote,” reassess the current control or open the post details before retrying; never repeat a stale element ID blindly.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit/Postmill list containing multiple posts and the first vote action produces no visible state change, especially when accessibility element IDs may be stale.

skills.title: Read Matching Post Metadata
skills.principle: Locate the target post by matching its visible title, then read the adjacent submission time metadata in the same post card. Report the displayed date, time, and timezone exactly, and stop once the requested posting information is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit-style forum listing pages when the target post is visible in the current accessibility tree and its card includes a submission timestamp.

skills.title: Read Matching Post Metadata Directly
skills.principle: When the target post is visible in a listing, match its title exactly, then read the associated time element in the same post entry. Report the displayed timestamp, preserving its timezone and precision, without opening the post or taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit or forum tasks asking when a specific post was published, provided the target title and its associated timestamp are already visible in the current page observation.

skills.title: Change Reddit Forum Sorting
skills.principle:
1. Locate the forum’s sorting control, such as “Sort by: Hot,” and open it.
2. Select any alternative criterion, such as “New,” from the expanded menu.
3. Confirm completion when the control label and page state reflect the chosen criterion, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forum listing is currently sorted by an unwanted criterion and the page exposes a sorting dropdown with alternative options.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Sort Change
skills.principle: Select any sorting criterion different from the current one, then verify the sort control label or resulting URL reflects the new criterion. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of exploring additional sort options or performing unnecessary clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When a forum or listing task asks for a different sort order and the page visibly updates with the requested alternate criterion.

skills.title: Change Forum Sorting
skills.principle:
1. Locate the forum’s current sorting control, such as “Sort by: Hot,” and open its menu.
2. Select the requested sorting option, such as “New,” from the expanded menu.
3. Confirm completion when the control label and resulting URL/page state reflect the requested sort.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forum displays submissions under a sorting control and the task requests changing the current order. Verify the requested option appears in the expanded menu.

skills.title: Verify Hide State Before Acting Again
skills.principle: On a forum page, expand the “Hide this forum” control once. If the expanded panel shows an “Unhide” button, hiding has already succeeded; do not click it, because it reverses the change. Report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When hiding a Reddit/Postmill forum and the sidebar’s expanded hide control displays “Unhide,” indicating the forum is currently hidden.

skills.title: Downvote the Correct Listed Post
skills.principle: Identify the target post by matching its visible title within the article list, then use the Downvote control inside that same article. Confirm completion when the control changes to “Retract downvote” and the displayed score updates, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to vote on a specific Reddit/Postmill post shown in a feed, especially when multiple nearby posts have identical voting controls and the target must be matched by visible title.

skills.title: Open Reddit User Preferences
skills.principle:
1. Open the logged-in username menu in the top navigation.
2. Select the menu item labeled “User settings.”
3. Confirm the destination by checking for the user settings heading and preference sections such as General, Notifications, Privacy, and Appearance; stop once displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Reddit/Postmill user preferences and the page shows a logged-in username control in the top navigation.

skills.title: Verify Target Forum Before Reporting
skills.principle:
1. If the current forum is only related to the requested topic, open the site’s forum directory rather than assuming it matches.
2. Locate the forum whose displayed name matches the request and open its link.
3. Confirm completion from the page heading and visible submissions, then send one complete concise report and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a forum task opens on a similarly themed but incorrect community, and the site provides a Forums directory or other list of communities.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Forum Access
skills.principle: Once the requested forum is visibly loaded and its posts are available, treat browsing as complete. Report that the forum was opened and content is visible, then terminate instead of repeatedly scrolling or loading more pages without a specific user request.
skills.when_to_apply: When a browsing task asks you to view a forum or feed and the accessibility tree shows the requested forum heading plus visible posts. Additional scrolling is optional unless the user requests broader exploration.

skills.title: Change Forum Sort Order
skills.principle: On a forum submissions page, locate the “Sort by: [current]” menu and open it. Select the requested sorting option by its visible label, then verify the page reloads with the sort button showing that option or the URL reflecting it. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change sorting for a Reddit/Postmill forum and the submissions page exposes a visible “Sort by” menu with selectable options.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Visible Name
skills.principle: From an unrelated forum, open the site-wide “Forums” navigation link. On the forum listing, locate the entry whose visible name matches the requested destination and activate its link. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL identify the target forum, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to visit a named Reddit-like forum while currently on another forum page, provided the site exposes a “Forums” directory and visible forum entries.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Visible Topic
skills.principle:
1. From an unrelated forum, open the main “Forums” navigation entry.
2. Scan the forum list for the forum whose visible name matches the requested topic.
3. Open that forum and verify its heading and post list show relevant discussions.
4. Report completion once the requested forum content is visibly loaded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to explore a named Reddit-like forum and the starting page is unknown or shows a different forum. Requires a visible Forums navigation link or equivalent directory.

skills.title: Verify Subscription State Before Acting
skills.principle: On a forum page, inspect the subscription control before clicking. If it says “Subscribe,” activate it and verify that it changes to “Unsubscribe.” If it already says “Unsubscribe,” the user is subscribed; report the confirmed state and stop without toggling it.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to subscribe to a forum and the forum page is open with a visible subscription button. Use the button’s current label and resulting state as the completion check.

skills.title: Verify Target Before Opening
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to locate the exact requested post title and activate its associated title link. After navigation, verify the page heading matches the requested title. If it does not, return to the results and select the correct matching link; only report the post as unavailable after the results contain no exact match.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a Reddit post from search results, especially when multiple similar titles appear or accessibility element identifiers may change between observations.

skills.title: Verify Homepage Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and accessibility tree before acting. If the root URL is already loaded and homepage content such as submissions, filters, or featured forums is visible, report that the homepage is open and stop. Otherwise, activate the site’s clearly labeled Home link, then verify the resulting root URL and homepage content.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access a site homepage, especially from an arbitrary page. Use when the current observation exposes the URL and navigation landmarks, allowing completion to be confirmed without unnecessary navigation.

skills.title: Navigate Directly When Link Clicking Fails
skills.principle: When a visible navigation link repeatedly produces empty-action or element-not-found errors, use the destination URL from the accessibility tree with direct navigation. Verify completion by checking that the URL and page heading/content match the requested destination, then stop without redundant actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For simple navigation tasks where the target page URL is visible in the accessibility tree and link-based interaction fails or remains unreliable.

skills.title: Verify Targeted Downvotes Before Finishing
skills.principle: Locate the target post by its visible title within the result list, then use that post’s own voting control. Click “Downvote” once and verify it changes to “Retract downvote” (and the score reflects the vote). Once confirmed, report completion and stop; do not click again, since the control now retracts the vote.
skills.when_to_apply: When downvoting a specific Reddit/Postmill post from a list or search results, especially when multiple articles have similarly positioned voting controls. Confirm the target title and the resulting “Retract downvote” state before terminating.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Clicking
skills.principle: Identify the target post by its title, then inspect its own vote controls. If the control reads “Retract downvote,” the post is already downvoted—report completion and stop. Otherwise click the target post’s “Downvote” control once, then confirm it changes to “Retract downvote.” Do not use similarly labeled controls belonging to comments.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit/Postmill post, especially pages containing many comments with their own Upvote and Downvote controls. Confirm the target post’s current vote state before acting.

skills.title: Extract Recommendations From Reddit Comments
skills.principle: Open the most relevant search result, inspect its comment thread, and collect each recommendation’s title and creator from comment text. Ignore deleted or unrelated comments, deduplicate repeated items, then present the verified title–creator pairs in a concise numbered list.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit task asks for items, recommendations, or examples discussed in posts. Requires search results containing a plausibly relevant post and an accessible comment section.

skills.title: Prioritize Exact Semantic Matches
skills.principle: On Reddit search results, rank posts by whether the title and content directly express the requested topic, not merely shared keywords. Open the result’s title or comments link to verify details, record its title and URL, and ignore incidental mentions. Once the directly matching post is confirmed, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit searches returning many noisy keyword matches, especially when one result’s title closely mirrors the request. Verify the result through its actual title or comments link before continuing.

skills.title: Recognize Default Relevance Sorting
skills.principle: On a Reddit search results page, inspect the search header and result controls for an explicit sort option. If no sort control is exposed and query terms are highlighted within matching results, treat the current ordering as relevance-based by default. Report that state and finish without unnecessary UI actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to sort Reddit search results by relevance and the accessibility tree shows search results with highlighted query terms but no visible sort dropdown, tab, or button.

skills.title: Terminate After Valid Completion Message
skills.principle: When the requested UI control is absent, send one valid user-facing message explaining the limitation and any supported alternative, then terminate. Ensure the action payload is non-empty and correctly formatted; do not repeat the same message or continue issuing actions after the task state is settled.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a page lacks the requested sorting or filtering control and the agent has verified its absence in the current accessibility tree.

skills.title: Apply Subreddit Search Filters
skills.principle:
1. Focus the Reddit search box and replace the existing query with the original terms plus `subreddit:<target>`.
2. Submit the query using the Search button or Enter.
3. Confirm the URL/query and results heading reflect the subreddit filter; treat “No results” as a successful filter with zero matches.
skills.when_to_apply: When Reddit search results span multiple subreddits and the task requires restricting them to one named subreddit. Ensure the original query is known before replacing it.

skills.title: Verify Subreddit Destination and Stop
skills.principle: Click the target subreddit link associated with a search result. Confirm the resulting page heading and URL identify the requested forum (for example, `/f/<target>`), with a submissions list visible. Once this state is confirmed, report completion; sorting controls and the forum’s Comments page do not further filter search results and should not be explored.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to restrict Reddit search results to one subreddit and a matching subreddit link is visible in the results. Verify the forum page is loaded before terminating.

skills.title: Verify Feed State Before Scrolling
skills.principle: After selecting Submissions, confirm that the URL, post list, and upvote controls actually changed. If the page still shows the same empty featured-forum message, stop scrolling; use the visible filter and sort menus to expose submissions and order them by highest upvotes, then open the top post’s comments control and verify all comments are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill submissions navigation appears to succeed but the accessibility tree remains unchanged or shows an empty featured feed. Requires visible filter and sort controls or another way to expose posts.

skills.title: Update Search Query Directly
skills.principle: Locate the page’s searchbox by its accessible label, replace its contents with the requested query, and verify the field displays the new value. Report completion once the value is visibly updated; submit only if the interface requires an explicit search action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task asks to change a site-wide search query and the searchbox is available in the current accessibility tree. Completion requires the requested text to appear in the field.

skills.title: Verify Search Field Before Submitting
skills.principle: After editing a Reddit search box, wait for a fresh accessibility-tree observation and confirm its displayed value changed. Then click the visible “Search” button once and verify the results heading or URL reflects the new query before reporting completion. Do not repeat clear or fill actions based on stale observations.
