skills.when_to_apply: When changing a query in Reddit’s search form, especially if the accessibility tree still shows the previous value after an edit or the page has not visibly refreshed.

skills.title: Count Results by Subreddit Metadata
skills.principle: Read the total-result heading, then inspect each result card’s submission metadata. Count a result only when its “in” subreddit label matches the target subreddit; exclude comment cards and unrelated communities. Report the matching count together with the displayed total.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill search page lists mixed post and comment results, and the task asks how many results belong to a specific subreddit. Ensure the full result list is visible or otherwise inspectable.

skills.title: Count Subreddit Results Directly
skills.principle: Use the search results accessibility tree as the dataset. Inspect each result article’s subreddit link or URL, increment a counter when it matches the target subreddit, and use the displayed total to ensure all results were covered. Report the count immediately after the final result; do not repeatedly scroll when the complete result list is already present.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit search page exposes result articles and subreddit links in the accessibility tree, especially when the heading shows the total number of results and the full list is already available.

skills.title: Use Inline Date Search Filters
skills.principle: In Reddit’s search box, append a date operator to the query, such as `before:YYYY-MM-DD` or `after:YYYY-MM-DD`, then activate Search. Verify the resulting heading and each visible post’s timestamp satisfy the requested boundary before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Reddit posts for a specific cutoff or time period, especially when no separate date-filter controls are visible. Requires a searchable query and the desired date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

skills.title: Use Actual Search Filters
skills.principle: Start with the visible global search control or a page’s explicit sorting/filter controls, not unrelated forum navigation. Enter the requested query or date criteria, submit with Enter or the search action, then verify that the URL, result list, or filter state changes. A year typed into a search box is only a text query, not proof of date filtering; inspect result timestamps and pagination before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Reddit/Postmill for posts within a specified period and the initial page shows a searchbox or sort control but no obvious advanced date form.

skills.title: Reply to a Specific Reddit Comment
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant discussion and locate a suitable comment by its visible text or author.
2. Activate that comment’s “Reply” control, then verify the reply textbox is associated with the intended comment.
3. Enter a relevant, substantive response and select “Post.”
4. Confirm the new comment appears in the single-comment thread or the discussion’s updated comment count before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to reply to a Reddit comment, provided the target discussion is accessible and the page exposes per-comment “Reply” controls and a required comment textbox.

skills.title: Use Current Textbox Bid
skills.principle: After clicking a comment’s “Reply,” reread the accessibility tree and target the newly exposed textbox using its current element bid (for example, the textbox node), not its `describedby` value, guessed ID, or label text. Fill that textbox, click its nearby “Post” button, and verify the reply appears in the comment thread.
skills.when_to_apply: When replying to a Reddit comment after the reply form expands, especially when repeated fills fail because accessibility labels, IDs, and BrowserGym bids differ.

skills.title: Submit a YouTube Link to Music
skills.principle:
1. Open Reddit’s “Submit” page and keep the “URL” submission type selected.
2. Enter the YouTube video URL and a descriptive title; leave optional body text empty if unnecessary.
3. Open the required “Forum” selector, choose “Music,” then click “Create submission.”
4. Confirm success when the resulting post page displays the title, YouTube link, and “Music” forum.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when submitting a YouTube music-video link on Reddit’s Postmill interface, provided the submission form exposes URL, Title, Forum, and “Create submission” controls.

skills.title: Complete Submission Forms Reliably
skills.principle: After reaching Postmill’s “Create submission” page, use valid, complete browser actions and re-check the accessibility tree after each one. Keep “URL” selected, fill the URL field, required Title, and required Forum, then click “Create submission.” Confirm a resulting success or post page before stopping; do not repeat navigation clicks or malformed actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a URL on Postmill and the “Create submission” form is visible, especially after a navigation succeeds or an action error indicates the prior command was malformed.

skills.title: Complete and Verify Markdown Submissions
skills.principle:
1. Open the submission form and fill the required title and body fields with detailed, task-relevant content using Markdown.
2. Expand the forum selector and choose the forum matching the post topic.
3. Confirm the preview renders headings, lists, emphasis, quotes, and other requested formatting, then submit.
4. Verify the resulting post page displays the title, rendered body, and selected forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a detailed Reddit-style forum post where title, body, and forum are required, especially when Markdown formatting must be demonstrated and publication should be confirmed.

skills.title: Complete the Post Submission Flow
skills.principle:
1. Use the forum’s “Submit” control for a new post rather than replying to an unrelated existing comment.
2. Fill the post title and body with the requested song discussion, using Markdown directly in the text fields.
3. Click “Post” only after verifying both required fields contain the complete content.
4. Confirm the new post appears or a success state is shown before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to publish a new Reddit-style post and the page currently shows an existing discussion with comment and reply controls.

skills.title: Reveal Reddit Markdown Formatting Help
skills.principle: On Reddit’s post creation page, open the “Formatting help +” control. If clicking the checkbox is blocked by its adjacent text, click the “Formatting help” label instead. Confirm the control changes to “Formatting help −” and inspect the displayed table for supported syntax examples before reporting the options.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked what Markdown formatting Reddit post creation supports and the submission form is not yet showing its formatting-help table.

skills.title: Verify Formatting Help Expansion
skills.principle: On the post submission page, use the visible “Formatting help +” label or its associated control rather than clicking an obscured checkbox input. After activation, confirm the accessibility tree shows newly revealed formatting guidance. Treat “Markdown allowed” alone as permission, not as evidence of specific syntax options; report only options visibly listed.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking post-creation formatting options and the checkbox input is covered by adjacent text or the page does not visibly expand. Verify the control state and newly rendered help before answering.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the relevant navigation link, verify the destination using the page title, URL, or visible heading. Once the requested section is clearly displayed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the destination page visibly matches the request, such as a forums page showing a “List of forums” heading and a corresponding URL.

skills.title: Navigate Forums By Visible Name
skills.principle: From a Reddit-style search or other page, open the main “Forums” navigation entry. On the forum listing, locate the article or link whose accessible name matches the requested forum, activate it, then verify the destination heading and URL identify that forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a specific forum and the current page does not already show that forum. Requires a visible Forums navigation entry or equivalent forum directory.

skills.title: Recover From Failed Forum Clicks
skills.principle: If a forum-link click produces an empty-action error or leaves the URL unchanged, use the link’s observed href with direct navigation. Verify the destination by checking the page URL and heading for the requested forum, then stop immediately once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Postmill/Reddit-style forum lists and a link click fails, repeats without changing the page, or the target forum is already visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Navigation
skills.principle: From the target Reddit post, click the author’s username link. Confirm the page URL is the user profile and the profile heading or username matches the target, then report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate from a Reddit post to a user profile and the resulting page visibly shows the target username or profile URL.

skills.title: Verify Forums Page Before Acting
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation label or page heading to confirm the destination. Click the relevant “Forums” link when elsewhere; once the page shows “List of forums” and forum entries, stop navigating and report that the list is ready to browse.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open or view Reddit’s forums list, especially from another page. Confirm completion from the page heading and visible forum entries before taking additional actions.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Forums Page
skills.principle: Click the visible “Forums” navigation link, then verify the destination by checking the page heading “List of forums” and visible forum entries. Once those indicators appear, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open Reddit’s forums listing and the accessibility tree shows the Forums link or, after navigation, the “List of forums” heading with forum entries.

skills.title: Verify Forum Destination Before Reporting
skills.principle: From search results, select the result’s forum/community link rather than its post title when the task asks to visit a forum. After navigation, verify the destination using the URL and page heading (for example, `/f/<community>`), confirm forum posts are visible, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit/Postmill task asks to visit a named forum and the current page is search results containing both post links and community links.

skills.title: Use Observed Forum Links
skills.principle: When the current page exposes a forum link, activate that observed link or preserve the current site’s base URL and forum path. Do not substitute a generic external domain. Confirm the resulting page identifies the requested forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a forum from an already loaded Reddit-like site, especially when the accessibility tree contains a direct link to the target forum.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Visible Name
skills.principle: From an unrelated page, open the main “Forums” navigation entry. On the forum list, locate the forum whose visible name matches the request and open its link. Confirm completion by checking that the destination page heading and URL identify the requested forum, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a named Reddit/Postmill forum and the current page does not already show that forum. The forum must be discoverable in the visible forum list or its pagination.

skills.title: Use Valid Actions and Verify Navigation
skills.principle: When a click repeatedly returns an empty-action error, stop retrying malformed payloads. Issue a syntactically complete navigation action using the currently observed URL, then verify the resulting page title and content. On the forums list, select the link whose accessible name matches the requested forum and confirm its forum page loaded.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting from an unrelated Reddit page and navigation clicks fail with empty-action or parsing errors, especially before opening a named forum such as relationship_advice.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Forum Exploration
skills.principle: Once the target forum is reached, confirm its heading and visible submissions, then report completion. Optional exploration can include one post, comments, or sort view, but stop after the requested forum has clearly been explored instead of continuing repetitive navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore a forum and the page visibly shows the target forum heading plus its submission list or another meaningful forum view.

skills.title: Navigate via Semantic Wiki Link
skills.principle: Select the site's navigation link labeled "Wiki" rather than inferring a URL. After navigation, verify the page state: a Wiki heading or a "Page not found" page with Wiki navigation confirms reaching the Wiki section. If the main page is absent, report that status without creating content unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a site's Wiki section from another page, especially when the accessibility tree exposes a clearly labeled Wiki navigation link and the destination may not yet contain a main page.

skills.title: Handle Missing Wiki Pages Directly
skills.principle: After selecting the Wiki navigation entry, verify the resulting page heading and URL. If the page shows “Page not found,” use the contextual “Create this page” option only when creation is requested; otherwise recognize the destination is unavailable and stop or report it instead of exploring unrelated site sections.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit-like site’s Wiki link opens a “Page not found” page and the task only requests navigation, with no instruction to create or edit Wiki content.

skills.title: Use Visible Wiki Navigation Links
skills.principle: After opening the Wiki, inspect the updated page rather than repeating the original navigation action. If the page shows a “Page not found” message but includes a Navigation sidebar, activate the visible “Recent changes” link and verify that the resulting page displays change entries. Use the current observation’s link role and label, not stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking Wiki activity on Postmill and the Wiki landing route is missing or redirects to a page-not-found view that still exposes sidebar links such as “Recent changes”.

skills.title: Verify Destination State After Navigation
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested section, then inspect the resulting page rather than assuming success. Confirm the URL or relevant heading; if the section shows an expected empty or missing index, report that state and mention the available section-specific navigation options.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a named site section and the destination may be empty, uninitialized, or represented by a "Page not found" page with related navigation links.

skills.title: Recover From Wiki Page Errors
skills.principle: After selecting the Wiki navigation entry, verify the resulting page heading and content. If it shows “Page not found,” do not repeat the same link or wander through unrelated sections. Use the Wiki sidebar’s valid entry points, such as “All pages” or “Recent changes,” and confirm that the destination displays wiki navigation or page listings before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Postmill’s Wiki link leads to a visible “Page not found” page while Wiki-specific sidebar links such as “All pages” or “Recent changes” are available.

skills.title: Navigate User Toolbox to Trash
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in user menu and choose an account-related entry such as “User settings” when Trash is not directly visible.
2. In the account page’s “Toolbox” section, select the “Trash” link.
3. Confirm the destination heading is “Trash” and report whether entries are listed or the page says “There are no entries to display.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Postmill tasks asking to check a user’s Trash when the homepage has no direct Trash link. Requires an authenticated user session and access to the account menu.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once the target section is visibly open, inspect its heading and contents, then report the result and terminate. If the page states that no entries are present, include that finding in the completion response rather than repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a navigation action has opened the requested section and the accessibility tree confirms its heading and content state, including an empty-list message.

skills.title: Find Registration Date on Profile
skills.principle: Open the account’s profile page rather than relying on a secondary account-management page. Inspect the profile sidebar or account information section for the “Registered on” label and read the adjacent time value. Once the registration timestamp is visible, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked when a Reddit/Postmill account was created and the current page is not the main profile, navigate to the target account’s profile first.

skills.title: Report Visible Registration Date
skills.principle: Open the signed-in account menu and select the profile or account page. Inspect the profile summary for the localized “Registered on” (“Registrado el”) label and read its associated time value. Once the date is visible, provide it directly to the user and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks when the signed-in account was created and the profile or account page is accessible. Confirm the registration value is visibly associated with the “Registered on” label before reporting it.

skills.title: Read the Profile Sidebar ID
skills.principle: On a Postmill profile-related page, inspect the complementary sidebar for the profile’s standalone identifier text, typically near registration or account-status details. Extract that value and report it directly as the user ID, without confusing it with the username or navigation links.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a Postmill user ID and the current page shows the target user’s profile sidebar, especially near account metadata such as registration status.

skills.title: Use Account Page for User ID
skills.principle: On Postmill, open the logged-in username menu and choose “My account,” not “Profile.” Inspect the account page for the user identifier. Treat bracketed IDs on submissions (`t3_…`) or comments (`t1_…`) as content IDs, not the user ID; stop once the account identifier is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a Postmill user ID while logged in and the username menu exposes both “Profile” and “My account.”

skills.title: Complete and Verify Post Submission
skills.principle:
1. Open the Reddit/Postmill “Submit” page and keep the intended submission type selected.
2. Fill every required field, including the link, title, and forum; add optional body text when provided.
3. Submit using “Create submission.”
4. Confirm the resulting post page shows the expected title, link, body, and forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a new URL or image post on Reddit/Postmill and the submission form contains required metadata fields plus a forum selector.

skills.title: Open Account Settings from User Menu
skills.principle:
1. Identify the signed-in username control in the site navigation and expand its menu.
2. Select the account-management entry labeled “My account” or its equivalent, rather than profile or preferences.
3. Confirm completion when the destination displays account-editing controls such as username, password, email, save, or deletion options, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated Reddit/Postmill page is open and the task is to access account settings, especially when no direct settings link is visible but a username menu appears in navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Account Settings
skills.principle: Open the logged-in user menu, select the account option such as “Mi cuenta,” and verify the page shows account fields (username, password, or email). Once these controls are visible, report that account settings are open and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For account-settings access tasks on Reddit-like sites, when an authenticated user menu exposes an account link and the destination visibly contains editable account controls.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation for Settings
skills.principle: When a requested preference is not visible, open the authenticated user/account menu and inspect its accessible options for preferences or settings. Follow a displayed navigation link rather than guessing a URL; if the destination returns 404, return and continue discovering settings through visible UI before concluding the feature is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for account-level interface changes when the current page lacks the requested control, especially when an authenticated profile button exposes a popup menu and direct settings URLs are not confirmed.

skills.title: Save Notification Preference Changes
skills.principle:
1. Open the account menu and choose “User settings.”
2. In the “Notifications” section, locate the target notification checkbox and uncheck it only if currently checked.
3. Click “Save changes.”
4. Confirm the checkbox is unchecked and an update confirmation appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit notification-preference tasks when the account menu exposes “User settings” and the relevant notification checkbox is visible. Verify the current checkbox state before changing it.

skills.title: Save Mention Notification Preferences
skills.principle: Open the account menu and choose “Opciones de usuario.” In the “Notificaciones” section, inspect “Notificar las menciones”; toggle it only if checked, then select “Guardar cambios.” Verify the checkbox is unchecked after saving before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When disabling mention notifications on this Reddit/Postmill interface, especially when starting from an unrelated page or when the notification checkbox may already be disabled.

skills.title: Interpret Theme Toggle Labels Correctly
skills.principle: Use the theme button’s label as the available switch, not the current state. If it says “Dark mode,” click it once to enable dark mode. Afterward, verify the menu shows “Light mode” or the page visibly uses dark styling, then stop; clicking “Light mode” would revert the setting.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing Reddit/Postmill appearance through the account dropdown, especially after a toggle closes the menu and you need to verify whether dark mode is active.

skills.title: Submit and Verify a URL Post
skills.principle:
1. Open the Reddit-style site's “Submit” form and keep the URL post type selected.
2. Fill the URL and required title fields.
3. Expand the required “Forum” combobox, choose the requested forum, then click “Create submission.”
4. Confirm the resulting page displays the submitted title, linked URL, and forum before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to create a new link post on this Reddit-style interface, with the target URL, title, and forum available. Submission is complete only after the new post page visibly shows those details.

skills.title: Select Required Forum Before Posting
skills.principle: On the Postmill “Crear publicación” form, fill the title and content, then open the required “Foro” combobox and choose a forum before clicking “Crear publicación.” Verify success through a confirmation or changed destination; if the form remains with “Elige uno…”, the submission did not complete.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a new Postmill post and the form shows a required “Foro” field, especially if clicking “Crear publicación” leaves the submission form unchanged.

skills.title: Stop After Forum Confirmation
skills.principle: When the requested forum page is already displayed, verify the URL and accessible-tree heading identify the target forum and its post list. Treat that state as completion; do not click the heading or post-navigation links repeatedly. Report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating a forum list leads to a page whose URL, heading, and visible posts match the requested forum. No further interaction is required unless the user requested a specific post or filter.

skills.title: Navigate Account Menu to Settings
skills.principle: Open the logged-in username menu, then select the clearly labeled “User settings” link rather than a specialized settings subsection. Confirm completion when the page heading indicates user settings and the settings controls are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access a Reddit/Postmill user profile or settings page and the current page already shows the logged-in username menu or another account-related page.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Account Settings
skills.principle: Once the user menu exposes account options, select the account-settings entry. Confirm the resulting page contains credential fields and a save-changes control; this verifies settings access. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing no-op actions or continuing to search.
skills.when_to_apply: For Postmill tasks requesting profile and settings access, after authentication and when the account page visibly shows credential, password, email, or save-change controls.

skills.title: Verify Wiki Content When Landing Page Fails
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's Wiki navigation entry.
2. If it shows “Page not found,” select “All pages” from Wiki navigation.
3. Check the resulting page for an explicit empty-state message such as “There are no entries to display.”
4. Report that no documentation is available and stop, rather than creating content unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view Wiki documentation or community resources and the Wiki landing page is missing or unavailable. Use this only when Wiki navigation exposes an “All pages” link.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to select the intended link by its role and label, ensuring the click action is correctly formed. After navigation, verify the heading and URL. If the target shows “Page not found,” use the page’s valid Wiki navigation, such as “All pages” or “Recent changes,” and stop once a Wiki content or index page is displayed instead of repeatedly retrying the broken route.
skills.when_to_apply: When visiting a documentation or Wiki section, especially if the main Wiki link leads to a 404 page or an action error. Requires inspecting the updated accessibility tree for alternate navigation links and confirming the resulting page state.

skills.title: Use the Wiki All Pages Link
skills.principle: Open the site's Wiki navigation entry. If it lands on a missing-page view, use the sidebar link labeled “All pages” or its localized equivalent. Confirm completion by checking the resulting page heading and empty-state message; report that no pages are available when the list shows no entries. Stop after this confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view every Wiki page and the main Wiki link may open a missing-page route. Requires an accessible Wiki navigation entry and, on the fallback page, an “All pages” navigation link.

skills.title: Use the Wiki All Pages Link
skills.principle: When the main Wiki link opens a not-found page, use the sidebar navigation link labeled “All pages” (“Todas las páginas”) to reach the listing. Verify the resulting heading and entries; an explicit empty-state message means the list has been successfully viewed. Do not create a page unless the task requests it.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all wiki pages and the Wiki landing link shows “Page not found,” especially when sidebar navigation provides “All pages” and the listing may legitimately be empty.

skills.title: Check Existing Wiki Pages First
skills.principle: Before opening the creation form, inspect the wiki’s page list for the requested URL. If the target page already exists, open it and verify its title and body instead of submitting a duplicate. Create and save only when no matching page exists; treat validation errors or server errors as signals to re-check existence and field constraints.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a wiki page with a specified URL, especially if the wiki’s “All pages” list is available before creation.

skills.title: Check Existing Wiki Pages First
skills.principle: Before creating a wiki page, inspect the wiki’s “All pages” list for the requested path. If the target already exists, open it and verify its title and body instead of submitting a duplicate. Only use “Create new page” when the path is absent; then fill the required URL, Title, and Body fields and save.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill wiki page, especially if the requested path appears in the existing pages list. This prevents duplicate-path validation errors or server failures.

skills.title: Create and Verify a Wiki Page
skills.principle:
1. On the wiki creation form, fill the URL, title, and body fields with the requested page identity and introduction.
2. Use Markdown headings or sections when helpful, then confirm the rendered preview contains the intended content.
3. Click “Save” only after all required fields are populated.
4. Verify the resulting page displays the expected title and content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill wiki page from the “Create new page” form, provided the URL, title, body, and “Save” control are available.

skills.title: Use Valid Wiki Page Slugs
skills.principle: On the wiki creation form, inspect existing page paths and enter a unique, URL-safe slug in the URL field, typically lowercase words joined by hyphens rather than a full path or encoded title. Fill the matching title and body, click “Save,” and confirm navigation to the new page or a success state; if the title already exists, edit that page instead of creating a duplicate.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Postmill wiki page and the form requires a URL field, especially after seeing existing page paths or a save-time “This value is not valid” error.

skills.title: Validate Markdown Before Saving
skills.principle:
1. Open the wiki site's “Create new page” form and fill the required URL, title, and body fields.
2. Write Markdown using hash-prefixed headers and indented list markers for nested bullets.
3. Confirm the live Preview renders the expected headings and list hierarchy.
4. Click “Save” only after the preview is correct, then verify the resulting page displays the formatted content.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Markdown-enabled wiki page and the form provides required metadata fields plus a live Preview. Use this before saving to catch formatting or nesting errors.

skills.title: Verify Required Fields Before Saving
skills.principle:
1. Fill the wiki URL, title, and Markdown body fields.
2. Reinspect the form and confirm each required field, especially the multiline Body, visibly contains its value.
3. If a validation alert identifies an empty field, refill that field and verify it again before retrying Save.
4. Save once all required values are present, then confirm navigation to the created page or another success state.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill wiki page with required URL, Title, and Body fields, especially after multiline input or when Save produces a required-field alert.

skills.title: Use Forum Submission Sorting Directly
skills.principle: On the forums directory, verify the sort control reads “Sort by: Submissions.” Treat the first listed forum and its displayed submission count as the current maximum; report it without opening posts or comparing comment counts. If sorting differs, select the submissions sort option first.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the most active forum based specifically on total submissions and the forum directory exposes a submission-count sort control and counts.

skills.title: Fix Forum Name Validation Errors
skills.principle: When submission returns a validation message, correct the named field before retrying. For Postmill forum creation, use a Name containing only letters, numbers, and underscores; replace spaces or punctuation with underscores, then resubmit and verify navigation or success feedback rather than repeatedly clicking or waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Postmill forum and the form remains visible after clicking “Create forum,” especially when an inline error states that the name format is invalid.

skills.title: Verify Subscription Before Changing State
skills.principle: Check the page’s subscribed-forums list before attempting to subscribe. If the target forum is already listed, treat the task as complete, make no state-changing action, and report that it is already subscribed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to subscribe to a forum and the current Postmill page exposes a “Subscribed forums” list or equivalent visible subscription status.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Semantic Match
skills.principle: From any Postmill page, open the global “Forums” navigation entry. Scan the forum list and select the forum whose displayed name and content match the requested topic. Confirm the destination heading or URL identifies that forum and its posts are relevant, then report completion without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to find a topic-specific forum on Postmill and the global navigation or forum list is available. Verify the selected forum’s heading and visible submissions match the requested topic.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Forum
skills.principle: Once the requested subreddit or forum page is open and its post list is visible, treat the navigation task as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of opening a thread, repeatedly scrolling, or exploring unrelated posts unless the instruction explicitly requests reading specific content.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task asks you to navigate to or browse a named forum and the target forum heading, navigation, and visible submissions are already present.

skills.title: Navigate to a Named Forum
skills.principle:
1. From another Postmill page, select the top-level “Forums” navigation entry.
2. Scan the forum list for the target forum by its visible name, then activate its forum link.
3. Confirm navigation succeeded when the page heading and submission list identify the requested forum.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a specific Postmill/Reddit-style forum and the current page is elsewhere on the site. The Forums navigation entry must be visible or otherwise reachable.

skills.title: Recognize Home Page Completion
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and page state before acting. If the URL is the site root and the page shows the Home navigation and submission feed, the Home-page goal is already satisfied. Report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly clicking the same link or reloading the page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a site’s Home page and the current observation already shows the site root URL plus Home-page content such as the main feed.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Alphabetical View
skills.principle: On Postmill, open the Forums page and select the visible “Alphabetical” navigation entry. Confirm completion when the page title is “All forums” and forum links are grouped under alphabetic headings. Once this state is observed, report completion and terminate; do not repeatedly click the already-selected link or perform unnecessary refreshes.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view forums alphabetically and the accessibility tree shows the “Alphabetical” entry, an “All forums” heading, and alphabetically grouped forum lists.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Semantic Match
skills.principle:
1. From another section, select the main “Forums” navigation entry.
2. Scan the forum list for the entry whose title and description match the requested topic.
3. Open that forum and verify its page heading, URL meaning, and topic-relevant posts.
4. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-like site opens on an unrelated page and the task requests a specific topical forum. The forum directory and main navigation must be visible.

skills.title: Use Alphabetical Forum Sections
skills.principle: On the Reddit forums alphabetical page, locate the heading matching the requested initial and read every linked forum in the immediately following list. Report all names under that heading, preserving their displayed capitalization, and stop after the section ends before the next letter heading.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks for forums beginning with a specified letter and the alphabetical forums page is available, showing letter headings followed by grouped link lists.

skills.title: Read List Content Without Editing
skills.principle: When a page already displays the requested entries, read their accessible names or text directly from the links/list items. Do not use `fill` on containers or links; `fill` is only for editable controls. For grouped alphabetical lists, identify the target heading, enumerate the entries until the next heading, then report the collected names.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on forum or directory pages where results are visibly grouped in lists and the task asks for all entries matching a heading, prefix, category, or other displayed grouping.

skills.title: Navigate to a Named Forum
skills.principle: From the forum directory, locate the requested forum by its visible name, using alphabetical sections or page search as needed. Activate that forum’s link, then verify the destination heading matches the requested forum and that discussion posts are listed before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when Reddit/Postmill opens on an all-forums directory and the task asks you to visit a specific forum. Stop once the forum heading and its submission list are visible.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Forum
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested forum, then verify the page heading matches the target and that discussion posts are listed. Once these observations confirm the task is complete, report completion and terminate instead of opening an individual post or external article.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit or view discussions in a specific Reddit-style forum and the forum page visibly shows its heading and post list.

skills.title: Create and Verify Markdown Text Posts
skills.principle:
1. Open Submit and select the submission mode that exposes a Body field; on this interface, that is the “URL” tab, not “Image.”
2. Fill the required Title and Body with Markdown, then confirm the live Preview renders headings, emphasis, lists, links, quotes, or code.
3. Choose a required forum from the Forum combobox and click “Create submission.”
4. Verify the resulting post page displays the title and rendered Markdown before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill text post with Markdown formatting. Use this flow when the submission form has URL/Image tabs, a Body field, required forum selection, and a rendered preview.

skills.title: Use Visible Submission Tabs
skills.principle: On the submission form, choose the post type by activating its visible tab or label, not the hidden radio input. Verify the selected state changes before filling title, markdown body, and required forum fields. If a click is intercepted, target the corresponding visible label and re-check the accessibility tree rather than repeating the hidden-input click.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill text submission, especially when accessibility-tree radio inputs are hidden and visible labels or tabs intercept pointer events.

skills.title: Select Styled Submission Tabs
skills.principle: On the submission form, locate the media-type options and inspect their checked state. If the target radio input is hidden or clicking it is intercepted by its label, click the visible label for the target option instead. Confirm the target is checked and the previous option is unchecked before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a Reddit/Postmill submission type such as URL to Image, especially when the accessibility tree shows a hidden radio input and a visible option label.

skills.title: Verify Submission Type Before Continuing
skills.principle: On the submission form, select the visible “Image” label when the hidden radio control is obstructed. Confirm the accessibility tree shows “Image” checked and “URL” unchecked. If the task is only switching types, report completion and stop; do not attempt an upload or invent a file path.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when switching submission modes on Postmill’s “Create submission” page, especially when the Image radio input is hidden behind its visible label and completion is indicated by its checked state.

skills.title: Expand Submission Formatting Help
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's submission creation page and locate the body field's “Formatting help +” control.
2. If the checkbox is obstructed by adjacent text, click its associated label instead.
3. Confirm expansion when the control changes to “Formatting help −” and a formatting-reference table appears; read the available Markdown syntax from that table.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which formatting options are supported in a submission body, provided the site exposes a submission form with a collapsible “Formatting help” control.

skills.title: Activate Obstructed Checkbox via Label
skills.principle: When a checkbox click is intercepted by nearby text, activate the associated visible label or use keyboard interaction after focusing the checkbox (for example, press Space). Then verify the checkbox changes to checked and the expected help content appears before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on forms such as Postmill’s submission page when a visible option like “Formatting help +” is present but direct checkbox clicks repeatedly time out because another element intercepts pointer events.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Link and Stop
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the accessibility tree and select the actual semantic navigation link, not its containing navigation or list element.
2. Activate the link whose destination matches the requested page.
3. Verify the resulting URL and page content indicate the destination was reached; report completion and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a site-level destination such as Home, especially when accessibility trees expose both container elements and nested links. Confirm the destination after activation before taking further actions.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Navigating Back
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL and page landmarks before acting. If the target home page is already displayed, stop. Otherwise activate the visible “Home” link or navigate directly to the site root; use browser history only when the prior page is verified as the target. Confirm the resulting URL and home-page landmarks before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to return from a form or subpage to a website’s home page, especially when browser history may be empty, ambiguous, or lead to about:blank.

skills.title: Verify Image Upload Before Submission
skills.principle: For an image post, select the visible “Image” label, upload a valid available image file, and confirm the file control no longer says “No file chosen.” If upload fails or the asset is unavailable, resolve that prerequisite before submitting; do not submit a text-only post or report image-post success.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting an image post through Reddit/Postmill’s “Create submission” form, especially after a file chooser error or when the upload control still displays “No file chosen”.

skills.title: Verify Image Attachment Before Submission
skills.principle: For an image post, select the visible “Image” label, upload an existing image from a known valid path, and confirm the file chooser no longer shows “No file chosen.” Complete the title and submit only after the attachment is present; verify the resulting post visibly contains the image before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting an image post on Reddit/Postmill and the form offers URL and Image modes. A valid local image path is required; do not substitute an invented filename or treat a text-only post as an image submission.

skills.title: Select Required Forum Before Submission
skills.principle: On the Postmill “Create submission” form, fill the URL and required title, then open the “Forum” combobox and select an available forum. Click “Create submission” only after all required fields have valid values, and verify navigation or a success confirmation rather than repeatedly clicking while the form remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a URL submission on Postmill and the form shows a required “Forum” field still set to “Choose one…”.

skills.title: Create and Verify Forum Link Submission
skills.principle:
1. Open the target forum and choose its “Submit” control.
2. Keep the “URL” submission type selected, enter a tech news article URL, and provide a descriptive required title.
3. Confirm the forum selector targets the requested forum, then click “Create submission.”
4. Verify the resulting page shows the title, article link, and forum name before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a link submission in a Postmill/Reddit-style forum, provided the target forum and article URL are known and the submission form exposes URL, Title, Forum, and “Create submission” controls.

skills.title: Verify Submission Then Stop
skills.principle: After clicking “Create submission,” inspect the resulting page before taking another action. Confirm the target post page shows the submitted title, article link, body, and intended forum. Once these indicators appear, treat the task as complete and terminate; do not reuse stale form element IDs or interact with unrelated comment controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a URL post on Postmill/Reddit-like forums, especially after the form redirects to a page displaying the new submission and its forum.

skills.title: Navigate to a Reddit Profile
skills.principle:
1. Open the logged-in username menu in the top navigation.
2. Select the “Profile” link rather than account or settings options.
3. Verify the page title or URL identifies the target user and review the visible profile activity.
4. Report the findings once the profile page is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect a Reddit/Postmill user profile and the target account is available in the logged-in username menu. Verify the destination before summarizing.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Profile
skills.principle: Once the target profile page is loaded and its heading or profile URL matches the requested user, treat the task as complete. Report completion immediately instead of repeating no-op actions or unnecessarily inspecting unrelated profile content.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to check a Reddit/Postmill user profile and the browser already shows the target user’s profile overview, including its heading, profile navigation, or matching URL.

skills.title: Use Alphabetical Forum Navigation
skills.principle: From the all-forums page, locate the requested forum under its alphabetical heading and activate the matching forum link. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the resulting URL and page heading for the target forum, then report completion without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill task asks you to open a named forum and the current page lists forums alphabetically. Ensure the destination heading or URL visibly identifies the requested forum before finishing.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Navigation
skills.principle: When an accessibility tree exposes a navigation link, invoke the browser action with its current numeric bid, not the visible label or a malformed selector. For the food forum, activate the observed forum link directly when available, then verify the URL or page content changed to the forum before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when BrowserGym reports empty actions or cannot find an element by text, while the accessibility tree clearly shows the target link and its numeric bid.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Confirmation
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in username menu and select the clearly labeled “Profile” link.
2. Verify the resulting page shows the account name and profile content, such as overview, registration, or submissions.
3. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For Postmill tasks asking to view the current user profile, when the username menu contains a “Profile” option and the resulting page visibly shows profile information.

skills.title: Verify Target Forum Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current page title, URL, and heading before navigating. If they identify the requested forum, treat the task as complete and report success. Otherwise, locate the forum link by its visible label in the alphabetical forum list and select it, then verify the destination page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific Reddit/Postmill forum and the initial accessibility tree may already show that forum or provide an alphabetical forum directory.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Target Forum
skills.principle:
1. Use a correctly formatted click action on the visible “Forums” navigation link.
2. On “List of forums,” use “Alphabetical,” pagination, or the forum list to locate the requested community.
3. Open the matching forum link and verify the page heading or URL names the target forum before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Postmill from the homepage to a named forum, especially when it is not visible on the initial forum-list page.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Alphabetical Link
skills.principle: On the forums index, locate the requested forum under its alphabetical heading and activate its link. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL identify the requested forum, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-like site opens on an all-forums index and the target community appears as a labeled link in an alphabetical list.

skills.title: Stop After Navigation Confirmation
skills.principle: After clicking the target forum link, verify the page heading or URL identifies the requested forum. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately; do not click the forum again or issue repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating to a named Reddit/Postmill forum and the current accessibility tree already shows the requested forum heading or URL after navigation.

skills.title: Navigate to a Named Forum
skills.principle: From the forums directory, locate the target forum by its visible name, using alphabetical sections when present, and activate its link. Confirm navigation succeeded when the page heading and URL identify the requested forum, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a specific Reddit-style forum from a directory or all-forums page, before performing any forum-specific actions.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Once the target forum page is visible and its heading or URL matches the requested destination, treat navigation as complete, report completion, and terminate immediately. Do not issue repeated noop actions or wait for additional observations after success is evident.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigating to a named Reddit forum when the accessibility tree shows the forum heading and destination URL, confirming the requested page is loaded.

skills.title: Recover From Broken Forum URLs
skills.principle: When a forum URL returns 404, use the page’s “Go to home page” link or the same site’s root instead of switching to an external domain. From the recovered site, locate the requested forum and read its displayed submission count, confirming the forum page loaded before answering.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the initial Reddit-like page is a 404 or invalid route and the task requires a forum’s submission count. Preserve the benchmark site’s host and use its recovery navigation.

skills.title: Read Forum Submission Counts
skills.principle:
1. If the current page is invalid or shows 404, use its home-page link to return to the site.
2. Open the Forums navigation entry and locate the target forum in the forum list.
3. Read the submission total displayed within that forum’s entry, then report it and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a forum’s total submissions on Postmill/Reddit-like sites, especially when the initial URL is invalid and the Forums page lists counts directly.

skills.title: Read Submission Counts From Forum Listing
skills.principle: For Postmill forum-count tasks, use the Forums listing rather than the forum’s submission page. Open “Forums,” locate the target forum article, and read its adjacent text formatted as “N submissions.” Treat the subscribe number as subscriber count, not submissions, and report the listing’s submission value once found.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a forum’s total submissions and the forum page shows posts but no total count. The Forums navigation must be accessible so the target forum’s summary entry can be inspected.

skills.title: Navigate Forums Through the Forum List
skills.principle:
1. If the initial URL shows an error, use the page’s “Go to home page” link.
2. From the homepage, open “Forums” to view available communities.
3. Locate the forum matching the requested topic by its visible name, then open its forum link.
4. Confirm completion when the destination page heading, URL path, and visible posts match the requested forum.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a named forum on Postmill/Reddit-like sites, especially when a direct URL may be invalid and the homepage provides a “Forums” navigation link.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Forum
skills.principle: Once the target forum page is loaded and its heading plus submission list are visible, treat the browsing goal as complete and stop. Do not open a submission unless the task explicitly requires reading a specific discussion; clicking image-based post links may leave the forum and create stale element references.
skills.when_to_apply: For tasks requiring visiting or viewing a topical Reddit forum, after navigation reaches the forum page and the accessibility tree shows the expected forum heading and submissions.

skills.title: Navigate to Alphabetical Forums
skills.principle:
1. If starting from an invalid forum URL, use the error page’s “Go to home page” link.
2. Open “Forums” from the main navigation, then select the “Alphabetical” navigation entry.
3. Confirm completion when the “All forums” page displays forum links grouped under letter headings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill tasks requesting all forums alphabetically, especially when the initial page is a 404 or unrelated forum view and the main navigation is available.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums Link
skills.principle: On the forums listing, use the explicit “Alphabetical” navigation entry rather than the submission-sorting control. If diverted to another page, return through the main “Forums” link, select “Alphabetical,” and verify the resulting page shows the forum list in alphabetical order before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all Reddit forums alphabetically and the forums page exposes both an “Alphabetical” link and a separate sort control, especially after navigation leaves the forums listing.

skills.title: Create a Forum Through Postmill
skills.principle:
1. If starting on an invalid page, use the visible “Go to home page” link, then open “Forums” and select “Create forum.”
2. Complete every required field: Name, Title, Description, and Sidebar; optional Tags may remain empty.
3. Click “Create forum” and verify the resulting forum page shows the requested forum name, title, sidebar, and moderator access before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a new forum on Postmill and the initial URL may be invalid. Requires access to the Forums navigation and permission to create forums.

skills.title: Check Forum Existence Before Creation
skills.principle: Before opening the creation form, search the forum list and subscribed-forums sidebar for the requested name. If the target forum already exists, verify its page and report completion rather than attempting a duplicate. Otherwise, open “Create forum,” complete every required field, submit, and confirm the resulting forum page or listing.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a forum in Postmill, especially if the requested name appears anywhere in the current accessibility tree or navigation. Verify existing entries before submitting a new forum.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Inspect the latest accessibility tree and target elements by their current numeric bid, not by visible labels or guessed names. After any action error, re-read the refreshed tree, select the matching bid for the intended search box or navigation link, and retry once. Verify the URL or resulting content before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever BrowserGym reports that a labeled element cannot be found, especially on pages where the accessibility tree exposes numeric bids alongside labels.

skills.title: Read Forum Subscriber Counts
skills.principle: Open the site's Forums list, locate the target forum by its displayed name, and read the subscriber status on that forum's row. Treat a label such as "No subscribers" or a visible count of 0 as confirmation that nobody is subscribed. Report the result and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked how many subscribers a specific forum has and the Forums list displays each forum's subscription control or subscriber count.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Forum URLs
skills.principle: When a forum URL returns “404 Not Found,” use the current site’s visible navigation or home link to recover. From the homepage, inspect the “Subscribed forums” sidebar or forum listings for the target forum and verify whether it appears. Avoid repeated `go_back()` calls after reaching `about:blank`; navigate to the observed site homepage instead of guessing an unrelated domain.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit-like forum task starts on a 404 page and requires checking whether a target forum is subscribed. The page must expose a home/navigation link or the site’s actual homepage URL.

skills.title: Access Profile Through Account Menu
skills.principle:
1. If an initial Reddit/Postmill URL shows “404 Not Found,” use “Go to home page” before continuing.
2. On the home page, open the logged-in username account menu and select “Profile,” not “My account” or “User settings.”
3. Confirm the profile page displays the username, registration information, account status, user ID, and activity navigation before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for checking the logged-in user’s profile information, especially when starting from an invalid page and the home page exposes a username button with a menu.

skills.title: Follow the Profile Menu Link
skills.principle: After opening the signed-in username menu, select the explicit “Profile” link rather than assuming the menu button navigated. Confirm navigation by checking that the URL or page content changes to the user profile; use “My account” only when account-specific information is requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill username control expands a menu containing “Profile” and “My account,” especially when the current page remains unchanged after opening the menu.

skills.title: Reopen Menu After Mode Toggle
skills.principle:
1. Open the account menu and activate the visible mode button, such as “Light mode.”
2. Re-observe the page: the menu closes and the control label changes to the opposite mode, confirming the toggle.
3. Do not reuse the stale control reference; reopen the account menu before toggling again, and stop once the requested mode change is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When toggling Postmill’s dark/light theme through the account menu, especially after the first click closes the menu or changes the mode control’s label.

skills.title: Stop After Sort Confirmation
skills.principle: Select the sorting control’s “New” option, then verify the control now reads “Sort by: New” and the list begins with the most recent timestamps. Once this state is visible, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill listing has a sort menu and the requested creation-date ordering corresponds to “New”; stop after the selected label and reordered timestamps are observable.

skills.title: Compare Subscriber Counts Directly
skills.principle: Open the forum directory and inspect each forum card’s subscriber indicator, such as “N subscriber” or “No subscribers.” Track the largest numeric value and report the associated forum only after comparing all visible candidates; paginate if needed to cover the complete directory.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for forum-directory questions asking which community has the most subscribers, when subscriber counts are displayed on forum cards and the directory may span multiple pages.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Forum URLs
skills.principle: When a forum URL shows a 404 page, use the available return-home link or site navigation to locate the forum listing, then inspect subscriber counts across candidate forums and identify the maximum. Report unavailability only after verifying that the site provides no accessible route to the requested information.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a Reddit-like forum task opens an invalid or stale URL and the page visibly shows a 404 error with a homepage or navigation link available.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Reddit URLs
skills.principle: When an initial Reddit URL shows a 404 page, use the available “Go to home page” link rather than guessing a replacement URL. On the home page, locate and select the navigation link labeled “Forums.” Confirm completion from the “List of forums” page title or the `/forums` URL, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit/Postmill task starts on an invalid or deep-linked URL and the 404 page provides a home-page recovery link; verify the destination before reporting success.

skills.title: Recover From 404 Via Home Navigation
skills.principle:
1. If the requested page shows “404 Not Found,” use the visible “Go to home page” link rather than retrying the invalid location.
2. On the home page, locate the main navigation link labeled “Comments” and select it.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Recent comments” or the URL ends in “/comments,” then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill navigation request begins on a missing or invalid page and the accessibility tree exposes a home-page recovery link plus a main navigation entry for the requested destination.

skills.title: Find Tags Through Forums Navigation
skills.principle: From the Reddit/Postmill home page, open the “Forums” navigation entry. On the forums page, use the page-level navigation containing “Forums,” “Tags,” and “Alphabetical,” then select “Tags.” Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Tags” and the URL ends with “/tags,” even if the page reports no entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Tags and the home page lacks a direct Tags link. Requires access to the Reddit/Postmill home page and its Forums navigation.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Element References
skills.principle: After every navigation or click, inspect the latest accessibility tree and target an element using its current bid and role. Do not pass visible link text as a bid or reuse references from an earlier observation. If an action returns “element not found,” stop repeating it, re-read the tree, and choose a currently exposed control or navigate using its observed URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever BrowserGym reports a missing element, or the page contains repeated labels and dynamically refreshed accessibility trees. Prerequisite: obtain a fresh observation before each UI action.

skills.title: Advance One Forum Page
skills.principle: On the forum listing, use the bottom “More” navigation link to advance one page. After it loads, verify the URL or visible thread set has changed from the starting page and stop immediately once the requested page is reached; do not click “More” again.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific page in a paginated Postmill forum or submission list, with a visible bottom “More” link and the current page known.

skills.title: Open Forums Before Pagination
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the visible “Forums” entry rather than treating the home submissions feed as the forums list.
2. Inspect the refreshed accessibility tree for the forum-list pagination control, then activate it using its current accessible element reference.
3. Verify that the URL or displayed forum entries changed to page 2 before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to paginate a forum list but the current page shows submissions, comments, or another feed. First open the page labeled “Forums” and only use pagination controls present there.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Relevant Article
skills.principle: When a matching Reddit post is visible, open its linked article and inspect the resulting page for the requested information. Confirm the page loads and extract concrete details about the video before reporting completion; locating a relevant post alone is not sufficient.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit research tasks where the target post is identifiable in a feed and its title or link promises the requested information, especially when details must be gathered from an external article.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Target Article
skills.principle: When a forum listing matches the requested topic, activate its article link, wait for the destination page, and read the article’s visible content for the requested details. Confirm the page actually describes the target subject and video before reporting findings or completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the relevant post is visible in a Reddit-style listing and the task asks for more information rather than merely locating the post. Continue only after the article page loads and provides substantive details.

skills.title: Use Valid Final Response Actions
skills.principle: After locating the target post and reading the value adjacent to its “Upvote” control, send one concise user message using the exact supported action format. Avoid repeatedly wrapping or over-escaping the action inside JSON. If the response action errors, correct its syntax rather than repeating the same malformed payload, then terminate after successful submission.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/WebArena task asks for a visible post attribute and the answer is already identified, especially after a response action reports an empty or invalid action.

skills.title: Emit a Valid Final Action
skills.principle: After locating the requested value, send exactly one properly formatted `send_msg_to_user(...)` action through the browser tool. Do not place the action only inside explanatory text, nested JSON, or a raw-response field. Verify the tool accepts the action; once accepted, stop instead of repeating it.
skills.when_to_apply: When the answer is already visible in an accessibility tree and the task requires reporting a value, especially after a prior tool error indicating an empty or malformed action.

skills.title: Navigate Forums by Topic
skills.principle: From a general page, open the site’s “Forums” navigation entry. Scan the forum list for a title matching the requested topic, then open the most direct match. Confirm completion by checking the destination heading and visible posts are clearly relevant to the requested subject, then report the forum found.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to find a topic-specific forum on Reddit-like sites and the current page exposes a “Forums” link or equivalent navigation entry.

skills.title: Preserve Existing Downvotes
skills.principle: Find the target post by its title, then inspect its voting control. If it shows “Retract downvote” (and typically a negative score), the requested state already exists; report completion and stop. Do not click the control, because it would remove the downvote. If it shows “Downvote,” click it once and verify that it changes to “Retract downvote.”
skills.when_to_apply: When performing a Reddit/Postmill voting task and the target post is visible with its current score and vote-control label available.

skills.title: Respect Existing Vote State
skills.principle: When the target post shows “Retract downvote,” the requested downvote is already applied. Report completion and stop; do not retract and reapply it. If the control instead says “Downvote,” click it once, refresh the accessibility tree, and verify it changed to “Retract downvote” before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit voting tasks when the target post is identified and its vote control is visible. Treat “Retract downvote” as confirmed completion and act only on a currently observed “Downvote” control.

skills.title: Verify a Forum Moderation Log
skills.principle: From the target forum page, locate the Toolbox section and select the “Moderation log” link. Confirm the destination heading identifies the requested forum, then inspect the log content. Report whether entries are present; treat “There are no entries to display” as a valid completed result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore a specific forum’s moderation history and the forum page exposes a Toolbox with a “Moderation log” link.

skills.title: Use the Forum Toolbox Moderation Log
skills.principle: From a forum page, locate the sidebar's “Toolbox” section and select “Moderation log.” Confirm completion when the destination heading identifies the forum and the main content shows the moderation entries or an explicit empty-state message.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to review a specific forum’s moderation activity and the forum page is open with a visible Toolbox sidebar containing a Moderation log link.

skills.title: Upvote the Matching Reddit Post
skills.principle: Scan each post’s title and its nearby controls as one unit. When a title exactly matches the requested target, click that post’s “Upvote” button. Verify completion when the control changes to “Retract upvote” (and the score updates), then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit-like forum listing pages when a specific post must be voted on and multiple posts have similarly positioned upvote controls.

skills.title: Select Newest Forum Sort
skills.principle: Open the forum’s current sort control, choose the option labeled “New,” then verify completion by checking that the control displays “Sort by: New” and the page state reflects the newest-posts view. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a forum submission list whose current sort is not newest and the page provides a sort control with a “New” option.

skills.title: Open a Post’s Comment Thread
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target post by its distinctive title in the forum listing.
2. Activate that post’s comment-count link, rather than an external article link.
3. Confirm the destination shows the post title, a “Comments” heading, and visible threaded comments; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view comments for a specific Reddit/Postmill forum post and the forum listing shows both the post title and a comment-count link.

skills.title: Match Article Titles to Submission Timestamps
skills.principle: On a forum listing, scan each article’s heading for the requested title or distinctive keywords. Once matched, read the associated metadata, especially the nearby `time` element labeled with the submission timestamp. Report the exact date, time, and timezone shown, rather than relying on relative text such as “years ago.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit or Postmill tasks asking when a specific submission was posted, when the forum listing displays article headings alongside author and `time` metadata.

skills.title: Match Article Titles to Submitters
skills.principle: Scan the forum feed for the exact target title, then read the “Submitted by” metadata within the same article card. Verify the username belongs to that matching title before reporting it. Once confirmed, provide a concise answer and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked who submitted a specific Reddit/Postmill forum post and the feed displays multiple article cards with titles followed by “Submitted by” usernames.

skills.title: Match Article Titles to Submitters
skills.principle: On a forum listing, scan article headings for the requested title, allowing harmless trailing wording or punctuation differences. Within the same article card, read the adjacent “Submitted by” field and report the linked username. Verify that the submitter belongs to the matched card rather than a neighboring post.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when identifying who submitted a specific forum or Reddit-style post from a list of article cards containing headings and nearby “Submitted by” metadata.

skills.title: Use the Forum RSS Link
skills.principle: On a forum page, locate the sidebar link labeled “Subscribe via RSS” and activate it. Confirm the destination is the forum’s Atom/RSS feed by checking that the URL ends with the feed path and the page displays XML feed content. Provide the feed URL for adding to an RSS reader.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to subscribe to updates from a specific forum and its page contains a sidebar “Subscribe via RSS” link. The user must still add the resulting feed URL to an external RSS reader.

skills.title: Open a Forum’s Comments View
skills.principle: From a forum’s submissions page, select the navigation entry labeled “Comments.” Verify the destination heading identifies recent comments in the target forum and that comment entries are visible. If the task requires every available comment, follow the “More” link repeatedly until no further page is provided.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a forum currently showing submissions and the accessibility tree exposes a “Comments” navigation link; use pagination when a visible “More” control indicates additional comments.

skills.title: Open a Reddit User Profile
skills.principle:
1. On a Reddit/Postmill listing, identify a visible post or comment author link matching the requested user.
2. Activate the author link and verify the destination is a user page, such as a username heading or `/user/` URL.
3. Once the profile content loads, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a Reddit user profile and the target username appears as a clickable author link in the current listing or discussion.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL, page title, and visible content against the requested destination before acting. If they already match, report that the destination is open and stop; otherwise, use the visible navigation link matching the destination, then confirm the resulting page.
skills.when_to_apply: For navigation requests such as returning to forums, when the current accessibility tree exposes the page URL, title, or destination-specific content needed to determine whether navigation is already complete.

skills.title: Use Anchor Navigation for Skip Links
skills.principle: When a “Jump to main content” link is present but clicking it repeatedly fails because it is outside the viewport, use its observed destination fragment directly (for example, the page URL plus `#main`). Confirm the URL contains the main-content fragment and then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: On pages with accessibility skip links whose click action times out or reports the link is outside the viewport, provided the link exposes a same-page anchor such as `#main`.

skills.title: Submit Search And Verify Results
skills.principle: Use the site-wide searchbox for the requested term, then submit it with Enter when no explicit search button is available. Confirm completion by checking the resulting URL/query and a results heading showing the term and result count before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to search Reddit/Postmill content and a visible navigation searchbox is available. Fill the requested term, submit it, and verify that the search-results page displays matching results.

skills.title: Read the Target Post Directly
skills.principle: After opening the exact titled Reddit post, inspect its heading and visible body content first. Treat comments as supplementary discussion and external controls such as “View Poll” as separate linked content; follow them only when the task explicitly asks for poll details or linked material. Report the post’s visible content once read.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read a specific Reddit article or post and the title match opens a page containing the post body, comments, and possibly external links.

skills.title: Stop After Reading Target Article
skills.principle: Once the page heading matches the requested article and its visible content has been reviewed, report completion immediately and terminate. Do not pursue linked polls, comments, or related content unless the task explicitly requests them.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit reading tasks when the target submission is open and its title and content are visible. Treat reaching and reviewing the target page as completion unless additional navigation is explicitly required.

skills.title: Match Article Heading to Comment Link
skills.principle: Scan the forum submission list for the exact target article heading. Within the same article card, read the nearby link labeled with a comment count, then report that number. Stop once the heading and adjacent count clearly match.
