skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-style forum lists multiple submissions with separate comment-count links, especially when titles are similar and the count must be tied to one specific article.

skills.title: Use Search Result Comment Count
skills.principle: After searching the exact post title, verify the single result matches the target, then read the adjacent comments link directly. Treat its displayed count as the answer; do not open unrelated content or scroll through comments unless the count is absent. If navigating, confirm the destination heading still matches the target before extracting data.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill search returns a matching post with a visible “N comments” link, especially when element IDs may be stale or navigation could lead to another post.

skills.title: Open Target Author Profile
skills.principle: On a Reddit-style listing, locate an article submitted by the requested user and activate that article’s author link, not the article title or external source. Confirm the resulting page shows the target username in the page title, profile heading, or URL, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a Reddit user’s profile from a listing containing posts or comments, especially when the same username appears in multiple author links.

skills.title: Open Author Profile from Submission
skills.principle: On a Reddit-style submission list, locate the target article and activate the username link next to “Submitted by.” Confirm the resulting page identifies that user and shows profile navigation such as “Overview,” “Submissions,” or “Comments.” Once the profile is confirmed, stop unless the task explicitly requests a specific profile section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to the profile of a submission author and the current page displays author links associated with posts or articles.

skills.title: Open Target Article Comments
skills.principle: In a forum submission list, locate the article by matching its visible title, then activate the associated comments-count link within the same article entry. Confirm completion when the destination shows the matching article title and a visible “Comments” heading with comment content or a comment textbox.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to comments for a specific Reddit/Postmill article and the forum listing contains multiple similarly structured submissions.

skills.title: Submit Search and Verify Results
skills.principle: When the target post is not visible, use the site search deliberately: fill the search box, submit it (for example, press Enter), then inspect the resulting page for matching post titles. Open the exact matching post and confirm its title before using its “Comments” link or section. Do not treat merely filling the box or waiting on the unchanged page as a completed search.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a Reddit/Postmill post by title and the current page shows a different post or no matching target. The search field must be available, and completion requires a changed results view or an opened post with the requested title.

skills.title: Open the Target Post’s Comments
skills.principle: From a forum submission list, locate the target post by its exact title, then activate that post’s nearby comments-count link. Confirm success when the destination page shows the post title and a visible “Comments” heading, comment textbox, or existing comment list; report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to comments for a specific Reddit/Postmill submission and the forum list contains multiple similarly structured posts with distinct comments links.

skills.title: Inspect Matching Post Comments
skills.principle: On a Reddit-style forum, locate the submission whose heading exactly matches the requested title, open it, and inspect its body and visible comments. Extract the requested facts, compare repeated or quantified claims when available, then summarize the findings with appropriate attribution and uncertainty.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit or forum task asks for information about a specific post, poll, or article and the listing contains multiple similarly themed submissions.

skills.title: Send Complete Valid Messages
skills.principle: When reporting findings, construct one complete, syntactically valid message action. Properly escape quotation marks, close the message string and function call, then verify the action is nonempty before submitting. If the response is truncated or rejected, rebuild the entire message rather than repeatedly resending the malformed fragment.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply whenever a browser task is complete and the agent must call a message-sending function, especially when the summary contains quoted titles, apostrophes, or multiple findings.

skills.title: Match Post Title to Submitter
skills.principle: Scan the forum’s submission list for the post whose heading matches the requested topic. Within that same post card, read the username link immediately following “Submitted by,” then report it. Once the matching username is confirmed, stop instead of performing unrelated voting or navigation actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-style forum lists multiple posts and the task asks who submitted a specific post. Ensure the title match and adjacent “Submitted by” metadata are both visible before answering.

skills.title: Stop After Finding Submission Metadata
skills.principle: When the target post is visible, read the username next to its “Submitted by” label and report it immediately. Confirm the username belongs to the matching title, then terminate instead of clicking unrelated controls, voting, refreshing, or continuing to browse.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when searching Reddit or Postmill for a specific submission and the matching post’s title and “Submitted by” username are already visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Recover From Wiki Landing 404
skills.principle: When the Wiki navigation link opens a “Page not found” page, use its Wiki-specific navigation instead of retrying the same link. Open “All pages,” select an available page from the table, and verify the resulting page heading confirms Wiki content.
skills.when_to_apply: On Postmill, when clicking “Wiki” produces a “Page not found” message but the page still shows Wiki navigation links such as “All pages” or “Recent changes.”

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Stopping
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target article by its heading and inspect its nearby vote controls.
2. If the requested vote is already applied, leave it unchanged; otherwise click the appropriate “Upvote” or “Downvote” control once.
3. Recheck the updated label, such as “Retract upvote” or “Retract downvote,” and score.
4. Send a valid completion message only after confirmation, then terminate without toggling the vote again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill voting tasks when the target article is visible and vote controls show current state. Stop once the requested vote is confirmed, including when it was already applied.

skills.title: Stop Once Either Vote Is Set
skills.principle: For tasks allowing either upvote or downvote, inspect the target article’s current vote state first. If it already shows either active state, treat the task as complete. Otherwise click one vote control, verify the control changes to its corresponding “Retract” state, then terminate without toggling again or retrying unrelated completion messages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit/Postmill article lists when the instruction accepts either vote and the target’s vote controls visibly indicate an existing vote or a successful state change.

skills.title: Use Direct Profile Links After Click Errors
skills.principle: When a visible username control repeatedly produces malformed or empty click actions, use the observed profile link’s destination directly with navigation. Verify completion by checking that the page URL targets the user profile and the page heading or profile content names the requested user, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit/Postmill when a target username link is visible in the accessibility tree but clicking it fails or the control is a menu button rather than a navigable profile link.

skills.title: Select Top Sorting and Verify
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum’s current sort control, such as “Sort by: Hot.”
2. Select the “Top” option from the expanded menu.
3. Verify the page shows “Sort by: Top” or a corresponding top-sorted URL; report completion even if the selected time range contains no posts.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forum displays submissions with a sort menu and the task requests highest-rated or “Top” content. Verify the resulting sort state before stopping.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Browser Actions
skills.principle: When a valid control is visible but an action returns an empty-action error, verify the interaction syntax and resend a properly encoded role- or label-based click. Re-read the accessibility tree after each attempt; once the menu is expanded, choose the requested option and confirm the control label reflects the new setting. Do not switch to unsupported JavaScript or send a status message before completing the task.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a visible menu button, such as a post-sorting control, repeatedly produces an empty-action or parsing error despite remaining present and collapsed in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Broaden Time Range When Results Are Empty
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum’s sort menu and select “Most commented.”
2. Check the active time-range filter and visible results.
3. If the default range shows “There’s nothing here…”, open the time-range menu and choose a broader option, such as “All time.”
4. Confirm the sort and range labels update and posts appear ordered by descending comment counts.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on forum submission lists when asked to find the most discussed posts, especially when selecting the desired sort produces no results under the default time range.

skills.title: Verify Sort State Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting a sorting option, inspect the resulting page state. If the sort control displays the requested value and the page reflects the corresponding view, treat the task as complete and stop. Do not repeatedly reopen the menu or click the already-selected option.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a feed’s sort order through a menu, especially after navigation or a visible label/URL confirms the requested sort is active.

skills.title: Systematically Read All Matching Posts
skills.principle: On the forum listing, enumerate every post whose title or linked content matches the requested topic, including results on subsequent pages via “More.” Open each matching post, read its visible content and comments, and track completed items. Exclude incidental keyword matches when the topic is unrelated. Stop only after exhausting pagination and confirming no matching posts remain.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for broad “find and read all related posts” tasks on a forum listing, especially when relevant items are scattered across pages and keyword matches may include unrelated uses.

skills.title: Systematically Exhaust Related Forum Posts
skills.principle:
1. Scan each page for posts whose titles directly match the requested topic, recording their links and avoiding speculative matches.
2. Open every recorded post, read its content and comments as required, then return to the forum list.
3. Follow the forum’s “More” pagination control and repeat until no further pages remain.
4. Track visited posts and report completion only after all relevant pages and posts have been processed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find and read all topic-related posts in a forum list, especially when results span multiple pages and relevance must be judged from titles or post content.

skills.title: Open a User’s Submissions
skills.principle:
1. From a forum listing, select the target author’s profile link.
2. On the profile, choose the “Submissions” tab rather than “Overview” or “Comments.”
3. Confirm the page lists only that user’s posts and the URL indicates the user’s submissions view, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view all posts submitted by a specific user on Postmill/Reddit-style forums, especially when the profile initially opens on a mixed Overview page.

skills.title: Use the Author Profile for Submissions
skills.principle: For a task asking for all posts by a user, do not rely on the global search box, which searches entries rather than author ownership. Open the user’s profile via an observed author link or the site’s user-profile navigation, then select the profile’s submissions/posts view and follow pagination until complete. Treat “No results” from keyword search as inconclusive about authorship.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating all submissions from a specific Reddit/Postmill user, especially after global search returns no results or only content matches. Requires an observed username link or an available user-profile route.

skills.title: Use Search Results Directly
skills.principle: After submitting a forum search, verify the results page shows the query and total result count. Treat each result article’s heading and link as the posts to report; collect all visible matches and follow pagination if present. Do not open an individual result unless details are required, and stop once all result pages are covered.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find all forum posts matching a topic and the site provides a search page listing result articles with a total count or pagination.

skills.title: Summarize Relevant Release News
skills.principle: Scan the movie forum’s visible post titles for upcoming releases, premieres, announcements, or release-date changes. Open the most relevant article when details are needed, then report the matching headlines and key information to the user instead of only navigating or scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check out movie-release news on a Reddit-style forum and the page shows a list of submissions with titles and article links.

skills.title: Open and Summarize Relevant Movie News
skills.principle:
1. Open the movie forum’s “Sort by: New” menu to prioritize recent posts.
2. Scan titles for release, casting, production, or distribution updates about upcoming films.
3. Open a clearly relevant article and inspect its content or destination for concrete details.
4. Report the discovered movie news and release-related information only after the article page loads successfully.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check upcoming movie-release news on the Reddit-style movies forum, especially when the default feed is popularity-sorted or contains many unrelated discussions.

skills.title: Verify Search Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the site-wide search field for the target topic, submit the query, and inspect the resulting page. If it explicitly shows “No results” or “There are no entries to display,” report that the site lacks matching information and suggest an appropriate external source rather than claiming facts.
skills.when_to_apply: When researching a topic on a forum or content site and the search field is available, especially when the task requires information the site may not contain.

skills.title: Recover From Empty Site Search
skills.principle: When a site search returns no results, broaden or split the query into distinctive terms, then inspect the relevant forum’s visible posts and comments. If a navigation target shows “Page not found” or only generic content, abandon it and return to searchable discussions rather than repeatedly browsing unrelated pages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for information-retrieval tasks on Reddit-like sites when the initial multi-term search shows “No results,” especially before following generic Wiki or navigation links.

skills.title: Verify Moderation Log State
skills.principle: From the forum page, locate the Toolbox section and open “Moderation log.” Confirm the destination heading and inspect the main content. If it says “There are no entries to display,” report that no moderation actions are recorded and stop; open the global log only when the task explicitly requests site-wide actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view recent moderation actions for a Reddit-style forum and the page exposes a Toolbox sidebar with a “Moderation log” link.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Moderation Log
skills.principle: Click the forum’s “Moderation log” link and verify the resulting page heading and contents. If the log loads—even when it says “There are no entries to display”—the access task is complete; report the observed state and stop instead of exploring unrelated forums, Wiki pages, or Bans.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or view a Reddit/Postmill moderation log and the moderation-log page has loaded successfully, including an empty-log message.

skills.title: Open Notifications and Verify State
skills.principle: Select the top-navigation link labeled “Notifications,” then verify the notifications page has loaded. Completion is confirmed by the “Notifications” heading and either listed entries or an explicit empty-state message such as “There are no entries to display.” Report the observed state and stop once verified.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all notifications on Reddit/Postmill and the page exposes a top-navigation Notifications link. Open it and use the resulting page’s heading and entry or empty-state text as confirmation.

skills.title: Match Post Titles to Submission Times
skills.principle: Scan the visible post list for the entry whose heading matches the requested subject. Read the associated metadata paragraph and its time element, then report the complete displayed date, time, and timezone. Use the matching post’s timestamp rather than dates from linked external articles.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked when a Reddit/Postmill post was submitted and the feed displays multiple posts with headings, metadata, and time elements.

skills.title: Submit Search Through Its Actual Mechanism
skills.principle: After entering a target phrase in Postmill’s “Search query” field, submit it with the field’s supported action, such as Enter, rather than clicking the field again. Verify that the page or accessibility tree shows search results or navigation change before scrolling or changing submission sorting.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Postmill for a specific post or phrase and the query remains visible in the search field without any results, links, URL change, or other confirmed state transition.

skills.title: Count Submitters Across Forum Pages
skills.principle:
1. Review every article in the forum’s Submissions view and record the username following “Submitted by.”
2. Maintain a running frequency table, preserving counts while scrolling through all currently loaded posts.
3. If a “More” pagination control appears, open it and continue counting until no further submissions remain.
4. Report the user with the highest count and the verified total, checking that all articles were included.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for forum tasks asking which user submitted the most posts. Start from the forum’s Submissions page and ensure pagination or additional result pages are exhausted before declaring the winner.

skills.title: Use User Submissions Pages for Counting
skills.principle:
1. Open the forum’s “All” submissions view, ensuring the scope and time filter cover the complete dataset.
2. Group visible “Submitted by” usernames while paging through every result using “More” until no additional posts remain.
3. For leading candidates, open the user profile’s “Submissions” tab and verify its complete listing or pagination count.
4. Report the username with the highest verified submission count; do not infer it from “Top” ranking or a partial page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which Reddit/Postmill user submitted the most posts, especially when the forum feed has “Filter on: All” and user profiles provide a “Submissions” tab.

skills.title: Use Alphabetical Forums Navigation
skills.principle: From the forums listing, select the navigation entry labeled "Alphabetical" rather than changing the submission sort menu. Confirm completion when the resulting page is titled "All forums" and forum links are grouped under alphabetical letter headings.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view Reddit/Postmill forums alphabetically and the forums page exposes an "Alphabetical" navigation link alongside the default submission-sorted listing.

skills.title: Use Top Sorting for Time Filters
skills.principle: On a forum listing, open the sorting menu and select “Top” to reveal the time-period control. Open the control labeled “From: …”, choose the requested period such as “Past month,” then verify the label and resulting URL/state reflect that period. An empty-results message still confirms the filter applied.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering forum posts by a relative time period and the initial listing lacks a direct date filter. The sorting menu must offer “Top,” followed by a “From: …” period menu.

skills.title: Explore Sort Menus for Time Scopes
skills.principle: When no explicit date filter is visible, open the sorting menu and inspect each option’s resulting navigation or query parameters. Select a time-scoped option such as a day, week, or month when available, then verify the updated listing and timestamps before concluding the requested filtering is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Reddit/Postmill listing pages when the task requests a time period but the initial page shows only subscription and sorting controls. Do not report infeasibility until visible sort options and relevant listing pages are checked.

skills.title: Check Vote State Before Acting
skills.principle: Locate the target post and inspect its vote control. If it already shows the requested or acceptable state, report completion without clicking. Otherwise, click the appropriate vote control once, verify the label changes to its retraction state, then stop. Avoid toggling votes repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a Reddit/Postmill article where the task permits either upvote or downvote, especially when the target post may already have a recorded vote.

skills.title: Verify Target Vote State First
skills.principle: Locate the target article by its heading, then inspect only the vote controls within that article. If the requested state is already shown, such as “Retract upvote” with a positive score, stop because the task is complete. Otherwise click the appropriate “Upvote” or “Downvote” control once and confirm its label changes to the corresponding retract control.
skills.when_to_apply: When voting on a specific Reddit/Postmill list item, especially when multiple articles have identical vote controls and the page may already contain an existing vote.

skills.title: Inspect Matching Article Content
skills.principle: After locating the exact title in a forum list, open the matching article link, wait for the destination page, and read the article’s visible content before answering. Confirm the resulting page corresponds to the requested title rather than treating the listing itself as sufficient evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a search or forum listing visibly contains the requested article but the task asks to find information about it; the matching title link must be available to open.

skills.title: Read Beyond the Matching Post
skills.principle: After locating the exact title, open its article link and inspect the destination page for the requested information. Do not stop after confirming the title; extract relevant facts from the article, then report them with the source link.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit-style forum list contains the target article but the task asks for information about its contents, rather than merely locating or identifying the post.

skills.title: Use Direct Profile Navigation Fallback
skills.principle: Open the account menu and select “Profile” when visible. If the menu link becomes hidden or stale, navigate directly to the target user’s profile route instead of retrying the same element. Confirm completion when the page URL and heading identify the target profile, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a Reddit/Postmill user profile and the account menu’s “Profile” link is unavailable, hidden, or times out after the target username and profile route are known.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Navigation
skills.principle: When the page URL and heading confirm the requested user profile, report completion immediately and terminate. Do not browse additional profile tabs or repeat messages. Ensure the completion call is a valid, non-empty action; malformed or empty actions can prevent successful termination.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit profile-view tasks, once navigation reaches the target user URL and the accessibility tree shows the matching profile heading.

skills.title: Verify Requested Sort Then Stop
skills.principle: Open the forum’s “Sort by” menu, select the requested criterion, and verify the resulting button label or URL reflects that selection. For “Top” or “Controversial,” apply the requested time range using the separate “From” menu, then confirm its label. Once the requested sort state is confirmed, report completion and stop instead of exploring additional criteria.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting posts on a Postmill/Reddit-style forum, especially when the task names one or more criteria or time ranges and the page exposes separate sort and time-filter menus.

skills.title: Systematically Apply Requested Sorts
skills.principle: Use the forum’s “Sort by” menu to select each requested criterion, verifying the button label or resulting URL after every selection. Treat the separate time-range control as a filter, not a sorting criterion, and change it only when explicitly requested. After all requested sort criteria are applied and confirmed, stop rather than continuing exploratory clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forum task asks to sort posts by multiple criteria and the page exposes a “Sort by” menu plus optional time-range filters.

skills.title: Open a User Profile from a Post
skills.principle: On a forum listing, identify any visible post’s “Submitted by” username link and activate it. Confirm completion when the URL changes to the user page and the profile shows navigation such as Overview, Submissions, or Comments plus account/activity details.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a Reddit-style user profile and the current page is a forum or feed containing posts with clickable author usernames.

skills.title: Navigate Forums and Verify Posts
skills.principle:
1. From any forum page, open the global “Forums” navigation entry.
2. In the forum list, select the entry whose label matches the requested forum.
3. Confirm the destination heading and inspect the visible submissions; note the active sort control, such as “Sort by: Hot,” before summarizing results.
4. Once the requested forum and posts are confirmed, report the findings and terminate without extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check posts in a named forum and the current page is another forum or an unknown location. Requires access to the global Forums link and a visible forum listing.

skills.title: Use New Sort for Latest Posts
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the requested forum and inspect the current sort control.
2. If it shows “Hot” or another ranking, open it and select “New” or the chronological-latest option.
3. Verify the resulting list displays the newest submission times before summarizing or reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check the “latest” posts in a forum and the page defaults to a popularity-based sort such as “Hot”; the forum must be identified first.

skills.title: Verify Page State Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and page heading before acting. If they already indicate the requested view, confirm completion and stop. Otherwise, locate the navigation control by its current accessible label and role, then verify the resulting heading or URL after clicking.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task requires switching between forum views or tabs and the page may already be on the requested destination, especially after accessibility-tree updates that can invalidate element references.

skills.title: Respect Existing Subscription State
skills.principle: Inspect the forum control before acting. If it shows “Unsubscribe,” the account is already subscribed, so report completion and stop. If it shows “Subscribe,” click it once, then verify the control changes to “Unsubscribe” before terminating. Never unsubscribe and resubscribe merely to repeat the requested state.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a forum on Postmill or similar sites, especially when the forum page already displays a subscription toggle and the current account state is observable.

skills.title: Submit Search Queries Correctly
skills.principle: After filling the forum searchbox, submit the form with Enter or the explicitly labeled search-submit control; clicking the searchbox only focuses it and does not execute the query. Confirm completion by checking for a changed search URL or filtered results before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Reddit/Postmill forums and the searchbox contains the requested topic but the page still shows the original listing and URL.

skills.title: Submit Search Through Its Form
skills.principle: After filling the global search box, submit it using the field’s form mechanism, typically Enter, rather than clicking the unrelated navigation link labeled “Submit.” Verify that the page changes to search results and contains matching posts before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Postmill/Reddit-like pages with a global “Search query” box, especially when navigation also contains a separate “Submit” link for creating posts.

skills.title: Navigate Through the Forums List
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s “Forums” navigation entry when starting in another forum.
2. In the forum list, locate the target forum by its visible name and activate its forum link.
3. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the page heading, URL path, and visible submissions match the requested forum, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse a named forum from an existing forum page and the site provides a central “Forums” list with visible forum links.

skills.title: Submit Search With Enter
skills.principle: On Postmill, use the global “Search query” field for searches: fill the requested terms, then submit the field with Enter or its search-form control. Do not click the separate “Submit” navigation link, which opens “Create submission.” Verify the page changes to search results and contains matching posts before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Reddit/Postmill for posts from a forum page and the accessibility tree shows a global “Search query” searchbox alongside a separate “Submit” link.

skills.title: Submit and Verify Forum Searches
skills.principle: After entering the query in Postmill’s “Search query” field, submit the form with Enter or its actual submit control. Verify that the URL or page content changes and that search results are shown. If the page remains unchanged, correct the submission method instead of repeatedly scrolling or navigating the forum manually.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Postmill for posts matching a term, especially from a forum page, after the query is filled but the current page still shows the unchanged submission list.

skills.title: Use Wiki All Pages Listing
skills.principle: From any forum page, open the navigation entry labeled “Wiki.” If the landing route shows “Page not found,” inspect its Navigation sidebar and select “All pages.” Read the resulting table, using its Path and Page title columns to report every listed wiki page. Stop once the complete listing is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or enumerate all wiki pages on this Postmill-style Reddit site, especially when the top-level Wiki link opens a missing-page view with an “All pages” sidebar link.

skills.title: Enumerate Wiki Pages From the Table
skills.principle: Open the wiki’s “All pages” view and inspect every table row. Use the page-path link in each row, not the adjacent page-title cell, to open a page. After reading it, return to “All pages” and continue with each unvisited row. Treat the table’s actual row count as the completion boundary; stop when every listed page has been opened.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all wiki pages and the site provides an “All pages” table. Confirm each row’s link is distinct and stop after all listed rows are visited.

skills.title: Use Wiki Recent Changes Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's "Wiki" navigation entry.
2. If the wiki landing page shows "Page not found," use the sidebar "Recent changes" link instead.
3. Read the resulting table's Title, Author, and Date columns, then report the listed changes and stop once results are confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check recent wiki edits on this Postmill-style Reddit site, especially when the Wiki link opens a missing landing page but exposes sidebar navigation.

skills.title: Navigate to a Forum’s Recent Comments
skills.principle:
1. From the current forum or home page, open the target forum using its visible forum link, such as a subscribed-forum entry.
2. On the forum page, select the navigation link labeled “Comments.”
3. Confirm the page heading identifies recent comments in the target forum, then stop once the comment list is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view recent comments for a specific forum and the site exposes a forum page with separate “Submissions” and “Comments” navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Sort Change
skills.principle: Open the post sorting control, select any available option different from the current one, then verify the control label and resulting URL or post order reflect that selection. Once the new sort is confirmed, report completion and stop; do not reopen the menu or perform exploratory clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing Reddit/Postmill post sorting and the requested condition is simply a different available sort. After selecting an option, confirm the displayed sort label or resulting page state before terminating.

skills.title: Submit Search With Enter
skills.principle: Focus the forum's "Search query" field, enter the requested movie or topic, and press Enter when no visible submit control is available. Confirm completion by checking that the page changes to Search and displays a results heading such as the number of matches for the query.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on the Postmill/Reddit-style forum when the search field is visible and the task is to find a movie or topic. The query must be entered before pressing Enter.

skills.title: Select the Most Relevant Post
skills.principle: Scan the forum’s visible post headings and choose the item whose title most directly matches the requested topic. Open its title link, then verify the destination page heading matches the target before reporting completion. When multiple posts are related, prefer the one with the closest wording and specific subject requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-like forum lists several potentially matching submissions and the task asks you to view one specific post or topic. Ensure the destination heading confirms the correct post.

skills.title: Identify Release-Relevant Posts First
skills.principle: Review visible post titles and metadata to find posts explicitly announcing, scheduling, or previewing future movie releases. Open those relevant post links rather than selecting the first vaguely related result, and verify the resulting page contains release information before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a movie forum for upcoming releases and the page shows a mixed list of news, retrospectives, awards, and unrelated movie posts.

skills.title: Open Forum Post Links
skills.principle: When browsing Reddit-style forum posts, use each post’s comments or forum link to open the platform’s post page and inspect its content. Do not click the headline’s external source link unless the task requires reading the linked article. Continue through relevant release-related posts and confirm the forum page is being browsed.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a listing shows both an external headline/source link and a separate comments or forum link, especially when the task asks to browse posts rather than external articles.

skills.title: Search Directly and Verify Discussion
skills.principle: Use the forum’s search box instead of repeatedly paging through submissions. Enter distinctive words from the requested title, submit with Enter, select the matching result by its title or comments link, then verify the resulting page shows the discussion content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a requested Reddit/Postmill discussion is not visible in the current listing, especially when the page provides a search box and search results can identify the target post.

skills.title: Search Directly for Discussions
skills.principle:
1. When the target discussion is not visible, use the forum’s “Search query” field instead of repeatedly scrolling or guessing pagination controls.
2. Enter the distinctive title or keywords and press Enter to submit the search.
3. Confirm the results page shows the matching result, then open its discussion-title link to view the full thread and comments.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when searching a Reddit-like forum for a specific discussion whose title is absent from the current listing, especially when pagination links are difficult to identify or repeated browsing yields no match.

skills.title: Match Author and Date in Comment Lists
skills.principle: On a Reddit-style comments page, scan each comment’s author heading and timestamp together. When both match the requested author and date, extract the comment body and its associated post title from the nearby “Reply to” or “in” link. Report the text and context only after confirming these fields belong to the same comment card.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when locating a comment by author and calendar date in a chronological or paginated comment list, especially when many nearby comments have similar timestamps or unrelated post contexts.

skills.title: Use the User Comments Tab
skills.principle: For a Reddit comment lookup, navigate directly to the target user's profile and select the "Comments" tab, rather than inspecting the currently logged-in user's submissions. Review each comment's author, timestamp, parent post, and text; use "More" pagination when needed. Report only entries matching both the requested user and date.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks for comments by a specific Reddit user on a specific date, especially when the current page shows another user's profile or mostly submissions.

skills.title: Verify Vote State Before Clicking
skills.principle: Locate the target comment by matching its author within the article, then inspect that article’s voting control. If it says “Upvote,” click it; if it says “Retract upvote,” the comment is already upvoted, so report completion without clicking. Ensure the control belongs to the matched comment rather than a nearby article.
skills.when_to_apply: When upvoting a specific Reddit comment from a list containing many articles and voting controls, especially when the target may already have an existing vote.

skills.title: Verify Current Section Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current page title, URL, and primary heading before acting. If they already match the requested section, report that the goal is satisfied and stop. Otherwise, use the navigation link whose label matches the requested section, then verify the destination heading before completing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a user requests a named site section and the browser may already be there. Confirm the visible page state before clicking navigation controls or performing additional actions.

skills.title: Validate Navigation Actions and Stop
skills.principle: Use the visible link label or role to issue one valid click action, then inspect the resulting URL and page heading. If the target page is already displayed—such as a Wiki page titled “Information and Guides”—treat the task as complete and stop rather than repeating clicks or no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Reddit/Postmill page to a clearly labeled section, especially after an action error or when the accessibility tree already shows the requested destination.

skills.title: Use Account Menu for Profile Settings
skills.principle: Open the logged-in username menu and choose “My account” rather than only “Profile” or “Edit biography.” Confirm the resulting account page shows credential fields, email settings, save controls, and account-management options before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated Reddit/Postmill task asks for profile details and settings, especially when the username menu exposes separate “Profile,” “My account,” and “User settings” links.

skills.title: Verify and Submit a Reddit Comment Reply
skills.principle:
1. Identify the target comment by its author and surrounding post context, then activate that comment’s “Reply” control.
2. Fill the revealed “Comment” textbox with the intended response.
3. Click “Post” to submit the reply.
4. Confirm the new comment appears in the thread, then report completion and stop; avoid repeated completion messages or actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Postmill/Reddit comment-list or thread pages when replying to a specific author’s comment. Ensure the reply form is visible and verify the posted response appears before terminating.

skills.title: Use Sorted Lists to Identify Maximums
skills.principle: When a forum directory is sorted by the requested metric, compare the first entry with the following visible entries to confirm descending order. The first forum is then the maximum; report its name and displayed count immediately instead of paging through lower-ranked results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for ranking questions when the page shows a sort control or label matching the requested metric and the visible entries descend in value.

skills.title: Report Unavailable Aggregate Counts Honestly
skills.principle: On a forum page, inspect the heading, submission list, sidebar, and navigation for an explicit total. Do not infer a forum-wide count by counting visible posts or confuse subscriber counts with submissions. If no authoritative total is displayed, report that the count is unavailable through the current page and state that another source or method is required.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a forum’s total submissions and the target forum page shows posts, pagination, or subscriber metadata but no explicit aggregate submission count.

skills.title: Enumerate Forum Categories
skills.principle: Navigate to the platform’s “Forums” link from the main navigation. Read category names from the forum listing’s links or headings, then report them using the displayed labels. If pagination controls such as “Next” or additional page links are present, inspect those pages before claiming the inventory is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which forums, categories, or communities a Reddit-like platform offers and the current page is not already the forum directory.

skills.title: Use Pagination Before Repeated Scrolling
skills.principle: On a forum-list page, extract category names from the visible article headings and inspect pagination controls. If additional pages exist, open each page deliberately and deduplicate results; do not repeatedly scroll when the accessibility tree already exposes the list and page links. Once coverage is confirmed, provide the requested categories and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to enumerate forum categories and the forums page shows article headings plus Page or Next links, especially when scrolling leaves the accessibility tree unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Topic Forums From Forum List
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s “Forums” navigation entry rather than relying on comments or submissions pages.
2. Inspect the forum list for a heading or link matching the requested topic.
3. Open the matching forum and verify its page title and visible submissions are relevant.
4. Report availability once the matching forum and topic-focused content are confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked whether a topic-specific forum exists and the current page is unrelated, such as a comments or feed page. The site must expose a forum-list navigation entry.

skills.title: Verify Matching Forum Directly
skills.principle: On the forum list, inspect visible forum names for the requested topic. Open the matching forum link, then verify the destination heading identifies that topic. Once confirmed, report the forum as available and terminate instead of scrolling unrelated posts or repeatedly searching.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Reddit-style forums page visibly lists a forum matching the user’s topic and opening it shows a corresponding forum heading.

skills.title: Handle Existing Forum Names
skills.principle: Before creating a forum, check whether the requested name already appears in the forum list or after submission. If the form reports that the name already exists, do not silently rename it; locate and use the existing forum if appropriate, or report that creation cannot satisfy the exact request. Preserve the requested name and verify the resulting forum page or explicit success state.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a named forum in Postmill and the forums list or submission response may reveal an existing forum with the requested name.

skills.title: Resolve Tag Validation Before Submission
skills.principle: When a forum form displays tag validation errors, reduce the collection to at most five tags and use only letters, numbers, or underscores. Recheck the form state and confirm the validation warning disappears before clicking “Create forum”; then verify that the resulting page confirms creation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Postmill’s “Create new forum” form when the Tags field shows collection-size or character restrictions, especially after editing tags and before submission.

skills.title: Resolve Validation Errors Before Resubmitting
skills.principle: After submitting a forum form, inspect the returned page for validation messages. For collection fields such as Tags, satisfy every constraint: use no more than the stated maximum and only permitted characters. Correct the field, submit again, and verify that the page leaves the creation form or displays a success state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a forum on Postmill and the form remains visible after submission with inline validation guidance, especially for Tags fields imposing count or character restrictions.

skills.title: Operate Custom Forum Comboboxes
skills.principle: On Postmill’s Create submission page, treat the Forum control as a custom combobox, not a native select. Click the combobox, inspect the expanded listbox, then click the visible option using its current accessibility identifier. Verify the combobox value changed from “Choose one…” before clicking “Create submission.”
skills.when_to_apply: When submitting a Postmill Reddit post and the Forum control exposes role=combobox with a listbox after clicking, especially after select_option reports that the element is not a <select>.

skills.title: Use Anchor URLs for Skip Navigation
skills.principle: When a skip-navigation link repeatedly fails because it is outside the viewport, read its destination from the accessibility tree and navigate directly to the fragment URL. Confirm the page loads with the expected hash anchor, then report completion and stop rather than retrying the inaccessible click.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on forum pages when a labeled skip link such as “Jump to sidebar” is present but BrowserGym cannot click it due to viewport or visibility constraints.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: After activating a navigation or skip link, inspect the resulting page state. If the URL hash or focused target confirms the requested destination, report completion and terminate; do not navigate elsewhere or retry the completed action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for accessibility skip links and in-page navigation tasks when the post-action observation shows the requested destination, such as a matching URL fragment or visible target section.

skills.title: Pivot When Wiki Content Is Empty
skills.principle: When the Wiki page shows only a generic index and no formatting guidance, stop repeating clicks or scrolling. Use the site’s task-relevant route, such as opening a post’s comment interface, and look for a formatting-help control there. Verify that the resulting help content is visible before completing the task.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit/Postmill tasks asking about comment formatting when the Wiki or current page lacks a matching heading, link, or instructional content.

skills.title: Report Content Through User Messaging
skills.principle: On Postmill, when a comment has no visible Report control, open the author’s profile, choose “Send message” under “Toolbox,” and describe the offending content and policy concern clearly. Click “Send,” then verify the sent report appears in the message thread before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for inappropriate-comment reports on Postmill when the comment actions show Reply/Permalink but no Report option, and the author profile provides a “Send message” link.

skills.title: Save Existing Appearance Settings
skills.principle: On a preferences page, inspect the target appearance control. If it already shows the requested value, still activate the page’s save button to ensure the state is persisted, then verify the saved value or confirmation. If it differs, select the requested option before saving.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a user’s appearance settings and the accessibility tree already shows the desired option selected, especially when a visible save button indicates changes require explicit submission.

skills.title: Verify Mention Notifications Before Changing
skills.principle: Open the account menu, select the user settings entry (such as “Settings” or “Einstellungen”), and inspect the Notifications section. If “Notify on mentions” is already checked, leave it unchanged, do not save unnecessary changes, and report that notifications are already enabled. Otherwise, check it and save the changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing Reddit/Postmill account notification preferences and the settings page is accessible. Use this whenever the requested notification may already be enabled and its checkbox state is observable.

skills.title: Inspect Account Settings Before Declaring Infeasibility
skills.principle: For notification-preference tasks, distinguish the notifications inbox from account settings. Open the signed-in account menu, inspect its newly exposed options, and follow the settings/preferences entry to find mention controls. Use current accessible labels or element identifiers after each page change, verify the toggle’s resulting state, and only report infeasibility after confirming no settings control exists.
skills.when_to_apply: When a notifications page only shows existing notifications or an empty inbox, and the header contains a signed-in account button with a popup menu.

skills.title: Save Once, Then Terminate
skills.principle: On a user preferences page, inspect the target setting before acting. For disabling private messages, ensure the “Allow private messages” checkbox is unchecked; toggle it only if checked. Click “Änderungen speichern” once, verify the update confirmation alert and unchanged unchecked state, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Reddit/Postmill user’s privacy preferences and the target checkbox may already have the requested state. Requires access to the preferences page and a visible save control.

skills.title: Verify Filter State Before Changing
skills.principle: Read the current filter label and page state first, accounting for localized labels. If it already corresponds to the requested filter, leave it unchanged and report that it is already configured. Otherwise open the filter menu, select the matching option, then confirm the updated label or resulting route before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a Reddit/Postmill front-page filter and the current filter button or URL is visible, especially when UI labels may be translated.

skills.title: Verify Checkbox State Before Editing
skills.principle: On a user preferences page, locate the setting by its label and inspect the checkbox state before changing it. An unchecked checkbox means the feature is already disabled; report completion without toggling or saving unnecessary changes. If checked, uncheck it and confirm the resulting unchecked state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when disabling a preference represented by a checkbox, especially when the page may already reflect the requested state. Ensure the target user’s preferences page is open and the setting label is identifiable.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Desired State
skills.principle: When the target preference already matches the requested state, report completion and stop using a supported termination response. Do not repeatedly issue `noop`; it can be rejected as an empty action and prevent successful termination.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on preference pages when the target checkbox or control visibly already has the requested value, especially after confirming no change is needed.

skills.title: Save Appearance Settings After Verification
skills.principle: Open the account menu, choose the settings/preferences page, and locate the requested appearance option. If the option already shows the desired state, leave it unchanged; otherwise toggle it. Click the localized save-changes button, then verify the assertive confirmation alert indicating settings were updated before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill tasks that change a user’s display or appearance preference, when an authenticated account menu exposes settings and the preferences form includes the requested labeled control.

skills.title: Save Already-Enabled Preferences
skills.principle: On a preferences page, inspect the target checkbox. If it is already checked, preserve that state and activate the form’s save button to ensure the setting is persisted. Verify the page shows a saved state or confirmation, then terminate; do not repeatedly issue no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a requested preference is visibly enabled but the page provides an explicit save control, such as Reddit/Postmill account settings.

skills.title: Verify Preference State Before Editing
skills.principle: On a user preferences page, locate the setting by its semantic label and supporting description, then inspect its current checkbox state. If the requested state is already present, make no change; report that the goal is already satisfied and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a Boolean user preference, especially when the interface may be localized and the target label can be matched through translation or its explanatory text.

skills.title: Verify And Save Preference State
skills.principle: Use the checkbox’s accessible label and current checked state rather than guessing from the requested feature name. If the matching option is already unchecked, leave it unchanged; otherwise toggle it once. Click “Guardar cambios,” then verify the option remains unchecked or a success state appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a user preference and the requested setting may already match the target state, especially when labels are translated or differ from the task wording.

skills.title: Stop After Save Confirmation
skills.principle: Select the requested language in the preferences language combobox, click the localized save button once, and verify the success alert confirms the settings were updated. Once confirmation appears and the selected value remains correct, report completion and terminate instead of clicking save repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a Reddit/Postmill account preference through a form with a language combobox and save button. Prerequisite: the target language is visible and a success alert or equivalent confirmation can be observed.

skills.title: Stop After Save Confirmation
skills.principle: Select the requested value in the relevant preferences control, click “Guardar cambios” once, then inspect the resulting page. When an alert confirms that user options were updated, treat the task as complete and terminate instead of clicking the save button repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a Reddit/Postmill account preference. After saving, the page shows an update-confirmation alert and the requested preference remains selected.

skills.title: Verify Filter State Before Changing
skills.principle: Read the front-page filter button’s current label before acting. Treat localized “Todos” or “All” as the all-forums state. If it already matches the requested state, report completion and stop; otherwise open the filter menu, choose the target option, and verify the button updates accordingly.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a Reddit/Postmill front-page forum filter, especially with localized labels or a menu containing both subscribed and all-forums options.

skills.title: Stop After Save Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target setting shows the requested value and a success alert confirms the update, report completion and terminate. Do not repeat actions using stale accessibility-tree element IDs, since rerendered pages may assign different controls or make old elements invisible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a preference or filter produces a visible success confirmation and the resulting control state matches the requested value.

skills.title: Save and Verify Preference Changes
skills.principle:
1. In the relevant settings section, identify the labeled dropdown controlling the requested preference and select the target option.
2. Click “Save changes” to persist the selection.
3. Confirm the dropdown displays the target value and a success alert such as “User settings have been updated.”
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a Reddit/Postmill user preference through a settings form, especially when selecting a new value does not automatically persist it.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Sort Controls
skills.principle: Check the current sort label first; if it already shows the requested mode, stop and report completion. Otherwise, activate the sort button using its accessibility-tree bid, then choose the requested option and verify the label updates. Do not pass visible text, CSS selectors, or guessed DOM paths as BrowserGym element bids.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a feed’s sort order and the accessibility tree exposes a sort button, especially after an action reports that a text-based element cannot be found.

skills.title: Verify Settings Before Changing
skills.principle: Inspect the target preference’s current checkbox state before acting. If it is already checked, report that the option is enabled and stop; otherwise, check it, save changes, and confirm the saved state.
skills.when_to_apply: On a Reddit user-preferences page when asked to enable a boolean option, especially when the accessibility tree exposes the checkbox’s checked state and a save control.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Desired State
skills.principle: When a preference already matches the requested state, do not toggle it. Report that it is already enabled and terminate immediately instead of repeating no-op actions. If the state is not enabled, toggle the labeled checkbox, select “Guardar cambios,” verify the checkbox remains checked, then finish.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on account preference pages when the target checkbox is visible and its accessibility state clearly shows whether it is checked or unchecked.

skills.title: Save Preference Changes and Verify
skills.principle:
1. On the user preferences page, locate the target setting by its label and inspect its current checked state.
2. Toggle the setting only if its state differs from the requested state.
3. Click the form’s “Save changes” button to persist the update.
4. Confirm completion from the success alert and the setting’s resulting state before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Reddit/Postmill preference tasks when the target checkbox is visible in the settings form and changes require explicit submission through “Save changes.”

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Desired State
skills.principle: When the target preference already matches the requested state, do not issue a browser `noop` action. Report that the goal is already satisfied and terminate the trajectory; empty or unsupported actions can trigger execution errors.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on settings pages when the relevant checkbox or control visibly already has the requested value, especially when the browser environment does not support no-op actions.

skills.title: Use User Preferences for Notifications
skills.principle: Open the logged-in username menu and choose the explicit “Opciones de usuario”/preferences entry, not “Mi cuenta” or profile editing. On the preferences page, locate the setting for replies to your posts, disable it, save changes, and verify the control remains disabled after submission.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing Reddit/Postmill notification behavior and the username menu exposes separate account, profile, and user-preferences links. Use preferences for notification controls; account and biography pages do not provide them.

skills.title: Access Hidden Forums Through User Tools
skills.principle:
1. Open the account menu and choose “Opciones de usuario” rather than searching the general forum list.
2. In the user settings sidebar, under “Herramientas,” select “Foros ocultos.”
3. Verify the page heading and result text; “No hay entradas que mostrar” confirms the hidden-forum list is empty, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check a logged-in user’s hidden forums on Postmill and the account menu exposes user preferences with a “Herramientas” section.

skills.title: Report Empty Hidden Forums
skills.principle: Open the account’s “Hidden Forums” page from the profile tools. If the page shows “No entries to show,” treat the check as complete, report that no hidden forums are listed, and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check a user’s hidden forums and the account profile exposes a “Hidden Forums” link; completion is indicated by the page’s explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forum Listing
skills.principle: Navigate to the forums page, select the “Alfabético” navigation entry, and inspect the resulting “Todos los foros” page grouped by letter. Treat the ordered forum links as the browsing result; do not open each forum and repeatedly return unless the task explicitly requires visiting forum contents.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse forums alphabetically and the forums page exposes an “Alfabético” link. Completion is indicated by the alphabetical listing with letter headings and ordered forum links.

skills.title: Verify Sort and Pagination State
skills.principle: On a forums-list page, confirm the sort control shows submission-count ordering before navigating. Select the pagination link for the requested page, then verify the resulting URL or selected page indicator and that the sort control remains unchanged. Report completion only after both conditions are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to a specific page of a forum list under a requested ordering, especially after arriving from another page or when pagination links may preserve sorting state.

skills.title: Verify Canonical Pagination State
skills.principle: Use the forum list’s own pagination controls rather than guessing URL parameters. Select the link labeled “Página 2” or “Siguiente,” then verify that the resulting URL and pagination state identify page 2 with the requested sort order. Treat matching-looking content alone as insufficient when the page’s canonical link or active state disagrees.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a paginated, sorted forum list and multiple URL patterns or cursor-based links exist. Confirm the page control, canonical URL, and sort indicator before stopping.

skills.title: Navigate Paginated Forum Listings
skills.principle: Open the site’s forum listing and scan each visible forum entry for the requested name. If absent, use the pagination controls to advance. Select the matching forum link, then verify the destination by its heading and URL before reporting completion and stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a named forum and the initial page shows a sorted, paginated forum directory without the target immediately visible.

skills.title: Use Alphabetical Forum Navigation
skills.principle: From the forums page, select the “Alfabético” navigation entry to expose an ordered forum list. Locate the target forum by its visible name and open its forum link. Verify the resulting page identifies the requested forum; do not confuse general search results or post links with forum navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to visit a specific Reddit forum from a Postmill-style forum directory, especially when the initial list is sorted by popularity and scrolling does not reveal the target.

skills.title: Navigate Paginated Forum Listings
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s forum listing from the main navigation.
2. Scan the visible forum names; if the target is absent, use the pagination controls to inspect additional pages.
3. Click the forum link whose displayed name matches the target.
4. Confirm completion when the forum page heading and its posts are visible, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a requested Reddit/Postmill forum is not immediately visible in the forum index and the listing provides pagination. Ensure the target forum name is verified before opening it.

skills.title: Scan Current Page Before Paginating
skills.principle: When locating a named forum, inspect all visible article headings and links in the current accessibility tree before changing pages. If the target appears, click its forum link immediately and verify the destination page. Use pagination only after confirming it is absent from the current page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Reddit/Postmill forum lists when a target forum must be opened and the page contains multiple visible forum articles plus pagination controls.

skills.title: Read Counts From Forum Listings
skills.principle: Open the forum listing and locate the article whose heading matches the requested forum. Read the submission count displayed within that same article, then report it directly. If the target is not visible, use the listing’s pagination or sorting controls before extracting the count.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a forum’s submission count and the forums page presents each forum as an article containing its name and a submission-count paragraph.

skills.title: Use Verified Forum Navigation
skills.principle: When the target forum is not directly identified, open the site's Forums directory or search and select the exact forum by its displayed name. Use the forum page's actual navigation links, such as “Submissions,” rather than guessing a slug or appending URL paths. Verify the resulting page title and content before extracting the submission count.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving statistics for a named Reddit/Postmill forum and the current page shows only subscribed forums or a similarly named category, especially before navigating to a submissions listing.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to the Target Forum
skills.principle: Use the site’s forum directory or search rather than scanning the subscribed submissions feed. Open the forum matching the requested topic, then read its displayed submission count or forum statistics and verify the page identifies the correct forum before reporting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks for a forum’s submission count but the current page is a personalized or subscribed feed and the target forum is not visibly listed.

skills.title: Read Forum Counts From Listings
skills.principle: Open the forum listing and locate the target forum by its name. Read the submission count from the same forum entry, using the nearby text labeled “submissions.” Report that value directly once the target entry is identified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a forum’s submission count and the forums page exposes entries containing both forum names and submission totals; navigate to the listing first if starting elsewhere.

skills.title: Verify Forum Submission Totals
skills.principle: On a Postmill forum page, do not treat the currently loaded article list as the total. First inspect the forum header and sidebar for an explicit count. If none appears, use the “More” pagination control to enumerate additional submission pages and count distinct submission articles, stopping when no further page exists.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a forum’s total submissions and the forum page shows only a partial article feed without an explicit total count.

skills.title: Subscribe from the Forum List
skills.principle:
1. Open the site's forum list from the main navigation.
2. Locate the target forum by its displayed name, then use the subscribe control in that forum's list entry.
3. Confirm completion when the control changes from "Subscribe" to "Unsubscribe" and the subscriber count updates.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when subscribing to a forum on Reddit/Postmill and the forum list is accessible. Verify the target is currently unsubscribed before clicking, then stop after the control shows the subscribed state.

skills.title: Verify Subscription State After Clicking
skills.principle: On the forum list, identify the target forum’s article and activate its associated button labeled “Subscribe,” not a nearby submission-count element. Reinspect the page afterward and confirm that the same control changes to “Unsubscribe” (and subscriber status updates) before reporting completion. If unchanged, retry using the target article’s button.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a forum from a list containing repeated Subscribe buttons and nearby counts. Use the target forum’s visible name to associate the correct control, especially when accessibility references are close together.

skills.title: Verify Subscription State Before Toggling
skills.principle: On the forums listing, locate the target forum and inspect its subscription button. Click it only when it says “Subscribe.” If it says “Unsubscribe” or otherwise indicates an existing subscription, treat the goal as complete and report that state without clicking again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when subscribing to a forum from a list of forum cards, especially when the target may already be subscribed and the button label directly reflects current state.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Desired State
skills.principle: When the target forum’s control reads “Unsubscribe,” treat that as confirmed subscription. Report completion immediately and terminate the task; do not issue repeated no-op actions or click the control, which would reverse the subscription.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a Reddit/Postmill forum and the target forum entry visibly shows “Unsubscribe,” indicating the account is already subscribed.

skills.title: Report Existing Subscription Explicitly
skills.principle: When the target forum already appears under “Subscribed forums,” treat the goal as satisfied. Send a completion message containing explicit user-facing text, such as “The forum is already subscribed,” rather than submitting an empty or action-only message. Then terminate without further browser actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for forum-subscription tasks when the current page visibly lists the requested forum under “Subscribed forums” and no subscription change is needed.

skills.title: Verify Status From User Sidebar
skills.principle: On a user account or editing page, inspect the user-information sidebar for an explicit status label. Report the requested status only when the label directly matches the target state, such as “Whitelisted,” rather than inferring it from account fields or registration details.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when checking whether a Reddit/Postmill user has a platform status and the account page’s accessibility tree includes a user-information sidebar with explicit status text.

skills.title: Select Menu Destinations Directly
skills.principle: When an account menu is expanded, click the relevant destination link—such as “Profile” or “My account”—rather than repeatedly clicking the menu toggle. Verify that the URL or page content changes before inspecting the destination for the requested status.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task requires checking information beyond the current page and the accessibility tree shows an expanded username or account menu containing destination links.

skills.title: Verify Forum Description Across Views
skills.principle: Navigate to the forums list, open the target forum, and inspect its sidebar for description text. If absent, check the forum’s Comments view and sidebar as well. Treat only explicitly displayed descriptive text as the answer; distinguish it from metadata such as the forum name, ID, creation date, RSS link, or hide controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a Reddit/Postmill forum’s description and the initial forum page shows only posts and metadata, verify the corresponding Comments view before reporting that no description is visible.

skills.title: Verify Forum Description Visibility
skills.principle: On the forum page, inspect the sidebar accessibility tree for actual description text rather than assuming it exists. If the forum information section is collapsed, activate its disclosure control and recheck the tree. Only report completion after the description text is observable; otherwise continue locating the correct details control or acknowledge it is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a forum description and the forum page sidebar is visible, especially when the accessibility tree shows only the forum name, metadata, or a collapsed disclosure control without descriptive text.

skills.title: Stop After Subscription Confirmation
skills.principle: After clicking the target forum’s Subscribe control, re-read that forum’s row. Treat an updated “Unsubscribe” label and subscriber count as confirmation that subscription succeeded; stop immediately. Do not click the control again, because it toggles the subscription off.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a Reddit/Postmill forum from a forum list, after the target row’s control changes from “Subscribe” to “Unsubscribe” or otherwise shows an active subscription state.

skills.title: Sort Forums by Creation Date
skills.principle: On the forums listing, open the “Sort by” control and choose “Creation date.” Verify the control now reads “Sort by: Creation date” and the refreshed list shows recently created forums at the top, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forums page is open and the task requires newest forums first; the page must expose a sorting control with a “Creation date” option.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed UI Actions
skills.principle: Use a complete, valid action targeting the currently observed sort control. After any execution error, re-read the accessibility tree and retry with the correct syntax or a semantic locator; do not repeat the malformed payload or stale bid. Open the sort menu, choose the creation-date option, and verify the control label and forum order changed.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting Reddit/Postmill forum lists and a click or selection returns an action-format error, leaves the menu closed, or the accessibility tree shows unchanged state.

skills.title: Stop After Alphabetical View Loads
skills.principle: Navigate to the forums page and select the visible “Alphabetical” navigation entry. Confirm completion when the page heading indicates all forums and listings are grouped under alphabetical letter headings. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for forum-browsing tasks requesting alphabetical order when the forums navigation contains an “Alphabetical” option and the resulting page visibly groups forum links by letter.

skills.title: Use Pagination Links and Verify Page State
skills.principle: Navigate to the relevant list page, locate the pagination navigation, and select the link matching the requested page number. After navigation, verify completion using the URL and the pagination state showing that page as current, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests a specific page in a paginated list and the current page may be elsewhere. Prerequisite: the list exposes labeled pagination links or an equivalent next/previous control.

skills.title: Open Forums Before Paginating
skills.principle: For a request involving the forums list, first activate the top navigation entry labeled “Forums” rather than using the submission feed’s “More” control. Once the forums page loads, inspect its own pagination or next-page controls and verify the page indicator or resulting forum list before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a page of forums and the current view is the home or submissions feed, especially when a distinct “Forums” navigation link is visible.

skills.title: Open and Verify Account Menu
skills.principle: Identify the signed-in username control with a popup-menu attribute, then activate it if it is collapsed. Confirm completion by checking that its expanded state is true and the dropdown options are visible; report success without taking further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks you to access a Reddit/Postmill account menu and the accessibility tree shows a username button with popup-menu semantics and an expanded state.

skills.title: Stop After Menu Opens
skills.principle: When the account button shows `expanded=True` and its menu items are visible, the account menu has been accessed. Report completion and stop immediately; do not select a menu item or navigate elsewhere unless the task explicitly requests it.
