skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit account-menu tasks, after clicking the username control, verify the accessibility tree shows `hasPopup='menu'`, `expanded=True`, and visible entries such as Profile, My account, or User settings.

skills.title: Resolve Wiki URL Validation Errors
skills.principle: When saving a wiki page produces “This value is not valid,” inspect the form state and validation feedback before retrying. If the requested URL includes a leading slash, enter the equivalent page slug without the slash, resubmit, and confirm success by checking that the resulting page shows the requested title and body.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Postmill wiki creation forms when all required fields are filled but submission remains on the form with a URL validation error. Verify the destination page after correcting the slug.

skills.title: Resolve Wiki URL Validation Before Saving
skills.principle: When a wiki creation form reports “This value is not valid,” treat it as an unresolved input-format problem rather than repeatedly clicking Save. Inspect the field’s surrounding instructions or existing wiki URL conventions, enter the accepted path format, then resubmit once and verify that navigation leaves the creation form or displays the new page.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit/Postmill wiki page and Save leaves the form with a URL validation error. Confirm the required URL syntax before retrying, especially when the requested path includes a leading slash.

skills.title: Complete And Verify Wiki Creation
skills.principle: On a wiki creation form, fill every required field—URL, title, and body—using the field labels. Confirm the body preview renders correctly, select Save, then verify the resulting page displays the title and content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a new Reddit/Postmill wiki page and the accessibility tree shows required URL, Title, and Body fields plus a Save control.

skills.title: Resolve Validation Before Resubmitting
skills.principle: When saving a wiki page, fill URL, title, and content, then submit once. If validation reports “This value is invalid,” correct the URL using the page’s accepted wiki path/slug format rather than retrying unchanged data. Re-read the refreshed accessibility tree after validation, locate the current visible “Guardar” button, and submit again only after the error clears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Postmill wiki creation when submission stays on the form, displays a validation error, or the previously identified save control becomes invisible after rerendering.

skills.title: Verify Wiki Existence From Page Content
skills.principle: Use the site's “Wiki” navigation entry to open the wiki landing page rather than inferring status from a “Create new page” form. Confirm existence when the page loads with a title heading and substantive article content, then report the result and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked whether a wiki's main page exists and the current view may be a creation form or another wiki screen. The navigation must expose the relevant “Wiki” entry.

skills.title: Report After Confirming Page Existence
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested page and verify existence using its loaded URL, meaningful title, and substantive content. Once these signals confirm the page exists, immediately report the result and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when checking whether a Reddit/Postmill page exists and the browser already displays the target URL with a matching title and recognizable page content.

skills.title: Use Wiki Recent Changes Directly
skills.principle: If the wiki landing page is missing, inspect its error page for the Navigation sidebar. Open “Recent changes,” then read the table’s Title, Author, and Date columns and report the listed edits. Treat the resulting table as completion evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find recent wiki edits and the main Wiki link leads to a “Page not found” page that still exposes a “Recent changes” navigation link.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Recent Changes
skills.principle: When the wiki’s “Recent Changes” page is visible, verify its heading and edit table, then report the relevant changes and terminate. Do not repeat no-op actions after the goal is visibly complete.
skills.when_to_apply: For requests to inspect recent wiki edits, once navigation reaches the page labeled “Cambios recientes” or “Recent Changes” and its revision table is populated.

skills.title: Use a Relative Wiki Page URL
skills.principle: On Postmill’s “Create new page” form, enter a relative wiki slug/path in the required URL field, not the site’s full absolute URL. Fill the required Title and Body fields, click “Save,” and confirm the form leaves the page or displays the newly created wiki page without validation errors.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Postmill wiki page and the form shows required URL, Title, and Body fields. Use a unique relative page path and verify that saving does not produce “This value is not valid.”

skills.title: Resolve Wiki URL Validation Errors
skills.principle: On Postmill’s “Create new page” form, treat “This value is not valid” as a format or route-convention issue. Compare the URL field’s expected format with existing wiki links, replace the value using the accepted page identifier convention, then save and verify navigation to the newly created page instead of repeatedly submitting the same value.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Postmill wiki page, all required fields are filled but saving keeps the form open with a URL validation error.

skills.title: Verify Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current page and accessibility tree before taking navigation actions. If the requested destination is already open and its identifying heading or form is visible, treat the task as complete, report the confirmed state, and stop instead of navigating again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial browser state may already be the requested page; confirm a distinctive heading, URL, or required form controls before concluding.

skills.title: Use Semantic Targets and Verify Navigation
skills.principle: When a target link’s accessibility ID becomes unreliable, identify it by its visible label or observed destination URL rather than repeatedly clicking stale IDs. Navigate directly using the recorded href when appropriate, then verify the resulting URL and page heading match the requested destination. Once confirmed, stop without extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when navigation clicks time out, target IDs resolve to unrelated or hidden elements, or the destination link’s href is visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Create the Wiki Index Page
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s “Wiki” navigation entry rather than directly guessing a creation URL.
2. If the wiki shows “Page not found,” select “Create this page” to open the canonical index-page form.
3. Keep the prefilled, disabled URL, complete the required Title and Body fields, then click “Save.”
4. Confirm the resulting page state instead of assuming submission succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating the first wiki page on this Postmill-style site, especially when the Wiki entry reports “Page not found” and offers a “Create this page” link.

skills.title: Verify Submission After Server Errors
skills.principle: After submitting a wiki creation form, treat a 500 error as an ambiguous result. Navigate to the Wiki page or page listing and check whether the target page exists. If it appears, consider creation complete and stop; only retry with revised inputs when the page is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a wiki page produces a server error or unclear response after all required fields were submitted, especially when the site’s listing or navigation can confirm whether the page was created.

skills.title: Submit Search and Verify Results
skills.principle: Use the site-wide “Search query” searchbox from any page, including a missing wiki homepage. Fill the requested term, press Enter when no visible submit control is available, then verify navigation to the Search page and a results heading before reporting the count and result scope.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Reddit/Postmill wiki-related content and the current wiki page is missing or lacks a dedicated search form, provided the global navigation exposes a “Search query” searchbox.

skills.title: Stop After Profile Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the account menu’s “Perfil” link, verify the page heading or URL identifies the user profile. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate. Do not perform further clicks using element IDs from an earlier page; stale IDs can navigate away or trigger errors.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a Reddit/Postmill user profile, especially after a menu click causes the profile page to load. Confirm the destination state before taking any additional action.

skills.title: Check Reddit Block List
skills.principle: Open the authenticated user menu, select the clearly labeled “Block list” entry, and inspect the resulting page. Confirm completion from the page heading and its contents: “There are no entries to display” means no users are blocked; otherwise report the listed blocked users.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect a Reddit/Postmill account’s block list and the authenticated user menu is available. Navigate through the menu rather than guessing a URL, then verify the resulting page state.

skills.title: Check Reddit Block List Efficiently
skills.principle:
1. Open the logged-in username menu and select the localized block-list option, such as “Lista de bloqueos.”
2. Confirm the destination by its block-list heading and inspect the entries area.
3. If an empty-state message appears, report that no blocked users are listed; otherwise summarize the displayed entries.
4. Once verified, report completion and stop instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check the authenticated Reddit/Postmill account’s block list and the username menu is available. Use the page heading and entries or empty-state message as completion evidence.

skills.title: Toggle Theme Through User Menu
skills.principle:
1. Open the authenticated user menu and locate the theme button.
2. Click the button labeled with the opposite theme, such as “Dark mode” or “Light mode.”
3. Reopen the menu after it closes, then select the newly displayed opposite-theme button to complete the return toggle.
skills.when_to_apply: When Reddit/Postmill requests switching between dark and light mode and the theme control is not visible in the main page. Requires an accessible authenticated user-menu button.

skills.title: Save Preferences and Verify Confirmation
skills.principle:
1. Open the account menu and choose the clearly labeled “User settings” link.
2. On the preferences form, change the requested control to the requested value.
3. Click “Save changes” and verify the resulting success alert, such as “User settings have been updated.”
4. Report completion only after confirmation appears, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for authenticated Reddit/Postmill tasks requesting a user preference change, when the account menu exposes “User settings” and the preferences page provides the requested control and a save button.

skills.title: Save Changes on User Preferences
skills.principle: Open the logged-in user menu and choose the user-options/preferences entry. Adjust the requested setting, then activate “Guardar cambios” (Save changes). Verify a success message, persisted value, or refreshed settings state before reporting completion; changing a control alone does not save preferences.
skills.when_to_apply: When updating Reddit/Postmill account preferences and the settings page shows editable controls plus a separate “Guardar cambios” button. Requires an authenticated session and the requested preference to be identifiable.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL, page title, and main heading before navigating. If they already identify the requested destination, report that the goal is complete and stop; otherwise, use the navigation control whose label matches the requested page, then verify the resulting page state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the accessibility tree exposes current-page indicators and labeled navigation links, especially when the requested page may already be open.

skills.title: Confirm Navigation and Terminate
skills.principle: Click the navigation link matching the requested destination, then verify the resulting URL or page heading. Once the destination is visibly confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the target page is identified by a navigation label and completion can be confirmed through the URL, title, or heading.

skills.title: Use the Wiki All Pages View
skills.principle: From a wiki page, locate the navigation entry labeled “All pages” and activate it. Confirm completion when the destination shows an “All pages” heading and a table listing page paths and titles, then report the visible results and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view every wiki page from an existing wiki page, especially when the sidebar provides an “All pages” navigation link.

skills.title: Use the Wiki All Pages View
skills.principle: From the Wiki index, select the navigation link labeled “All pages” (or its localized equivalent). Confirm the destination shows a page-list table containing routes and titles. Once the table is visible, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view every Wiki page and the Wiki index provides an “All pages” navigation entry. Use this only after confirming the resulting page visibly lists the pages.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and visible page structure against the requested destination before taking navigation actions. If they already match, report that the goal is complete and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions or navigating unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a page and the browser may already be there; confirm the URL and recognizable page landmarks before acting.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Repeating
skills.principle: After a navigation action, inspect the updated URL and page landmarks. If the URL is the requested destination and its homepage content is visible, treat the task as complete, report success, and stop. Do not repeat clicks, scroll, or direct navigation merely because the page appears unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a known page, especially after clicking a navigation link, verify the resulting URL and recognizable page content before taking another action.

skills.title: Verify Target Forum Before Reporting
skills.principle: From an unrelated page, open the site’s “Forums” navigation, locate the requested forum by its visible name, and select it. Verify the destination heading and that the submissions list is displayed, noting its active sort (such as “Hot”) before summarizing the visible posts. Once the requested forum is confirmed, report completion and stop rather than retrying unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to inspect posts in a named forum and the current page is elsewhere. Confirm the forum heading and post-list state before reporting results.

skills.title: Select Newest Before Reviewing Posts
skills.principle: On a forum page, inspect the current sort control before browsing. If it shows a ranking such as “Hot” (“Caliente”), open it and select the newest/recent option. Verify the post list updates and use the first displayed entries as the latest posts; avoid repeated scrolling unless the requested results are not visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check the latest posts in a Reddit-style forum and the page visibly offers a sort control currently set to a ranking mode such as “Hot” or “Caliente”.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums View
skills.principle: From the forums listing, select the navigation link labeled “Alphabetical” rather than relying on sorting controls intended for submissions. Confirm completion when the page shows an all-forums listing grouped under letter headings with forum links ordered alphabetically.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view forums alphabetically on Postmill and the forums page exposes an “Alphabetical” navigation entry. If clicking a stale or hidden element fails, use the observed link destination or navigate directly to the alphabetical view.

skills.title: Validate Actions Before Declaring Infeasible
skills.principle: Use the exact accessible label or a correctly formed element reference for each click. After acting, verify that the URL or accessibility tree changed as expected. If the tool reports an empty or malformed action, resend a clean click rather than inferring the UI is unavailable. Only report infeasibility after inspecting the resulting menu or page and confirming the requested option is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Postmill forums or any accessibility-tree UI, especially after a click produces an empty-action or malformed-payload error and the observed page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Create a Forum from the Forums List
skills.principle:
1. If starting elsewhere, open the main “Forums” navigation entry rather than using an unrelated page form.
2. On “List of forums,” select “Create forum.”
3. Complete every required field: Name, Title, Description, and Sidebar; use the sidebar preview to confirm formatting when applicable.
4. Select “Create forum” and verify the resulting forum page shows the intended title and sidebar before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a new forum in the Reddit/Postmill interface, especially if the initial page is an unrelated wiki or content-creation form. A logged-in account with permission to create forums is required.

skills.title: Revalidate Stale Element Targets
skills.principle: After navigation, use the current accessibility tree to locate the intended control by role and label. Do not reuse an element ID from a previous page. After clicking, verify the URL, heading, and form state; if the result is unexpected, return to the relevant list page and locate the control again before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a multi-page task uses BrowserGym element IDs and navigation changes the page, especially after a click unexpectedly opens an unrelated item or the target control becomes invisible.

skills.title: Use the Forum Sort Menu
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the forum listing and inspect the current sort control.
2. Open the control labeled with the active criterion, such as “Sort by: Submissions.”
3. Select the “Title” option from the expanded menu.
4. Confirm completion when the control reads “Sort by: Title” and the listing is alphabetically ordered.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to sort forums by title on the forum listing page, especially when another criterion is currently active and a sort dropdown is available.

skills.title: Stop After Sorting Confirmation
skills.principle: After selecting the title sorting option, verify the page state once: the sort control should show “Título,” the URL or navigation should reflect title sorting, and the list should appear alphabetized. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeating no-op waits.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit forum list has been sorted and the updated sort control, navigation state, or ordered entries visibly confirm completion.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Repeating Navigation
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the semantically labeled Home link, rather than relying on stale element IDs. After clicking, verify the URL is the site root and the page shows normal home content. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and stop; do not repeat the navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a site's Home page from an error, wiki, or other page, especially after the accessibility tree changes element identifiers following navigation.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: After a navigation attempt, inspect the current URL and page landmarks. If the target page is already displayed, treat the task as complete and stop. If an interaction errors, issue one correctly formatted action using the observed link role or destination URL; do not repeat malformed clicks or identical navigation actions without new evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when returning to a known page from an error or intermediate state, especially when the accessibility tree already shows the target page’s URL, title, or navigation landmarks.

skills.title: Use Navigation Labels and Verify Destination
skills.principle: Select the navigation link whose accessible label matches the requested destination. After navigation, verify completion using the URL and a page-specific heading or content marker, then report success and stop without extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requires navigating from an error or unrelated page to a named destination and the accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation link.

skills.title: Use Valid Click Action Syntax
skills.principle: When a target link is clearly identified, issue one correctly formatted browser action using the observed element reference. If the tool reports an empty or malformed action, fix the serialization immediately rather than repeating the same payload. After navigation, verify the page title or URL matches the requested destination and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a BrowserGym click repeatedly returns an empty-action or formatting error despite the target link being visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to locate the navigation entry for the requested page and activate it. After navigation, verify the page title, URL or selected navigation state, and meaningful main-content text. Report the observed result only after confirming the destination, then stop once the task is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or check a specific page from an error or unrelated page, especially when navigation entries expose the destination and its content may be empty.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Completion
skills.principle: Once the requested page is reached and its state is observable, verify the relevant heading or status message, report the result, and terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions after completion is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation or checking tasks when the target page is visible and its accessibility tree shows the requested content or an explicit empty-state message.

skills.title: Stay on the Correct Page List
skills.principle: When asked to view all pages, use the page-index or “All pages” listing as the source of truth. Open each listed page link in order, verify the destination, then return to the listing before continuing. Do not follow unrelated global navigation links or stale element IDs from another page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for wiki or catalog tasks requiring every listed page, especially when the listing contains global links whose accessibility IDs can be confused with item links.

skills.title: Create a Wiki Page from an Error
skills.principle:
1. On a wiki “Page not found” screen, select the “Create this page” link to open the prefilled creation form.
2. Leave the generated URL unchanged, fill required Title and Body fields with the requested content.
3. Select “Save” only after all required fields are populated.
4. Confirm the resulting page displays the expected title and body before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a requested wiki URL shows “Page not found” and offers “Create this page”; requires permission to create pages and content for the title and body.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Page URL
skills.principle: When saving a wiki page produces “This value is not valid,” treat the URL format as the likely issue. Re-read the refreshed form and use the site’s expected page identifier or path format, guided by field examples or existing page URLs, rather than repeatedly trying arbitrary external URLs. Re-locate fields by their current labels after rerendering, then save and verify navigation to the created page.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a wiki page and submission remains on the form with a URL validation error. The form must retain valid title and body values, and the refreshed accessibility tree should be inspected before retrying.

skills.title: Locate a Topic-Specific Forum
skills.principle:
1. From an unexpected or broken page, use the site’s global “Forums” navigation entry.
2. Scan the forum list for the forum whose label matches the requested topic, then open its link.
3. Confirm completion when the destination heading names the target forum and its posts visibly cover the requested subject; report the forum and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a forum on Reddit-like sites and the current page lacks the requested content. Requires a visible global Forums link or an accessible forum listing.

skills.title: Stop After Finding the Target Forum
skills.principle: Once the forums list shows a matching technology-related forum, open it and verify the page heading identifies that forum. After this confirmation, report completion and terminate; do not scroll, reopen navigation, or search for additional forums unless the target is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit/Postmill tasks asking you to find a forum by topic, when a forum listing contains a clear topical match and its destination page visibly confirms the matching forum name.

skills.title: Use Pagination Links Precisely
skills.principle: From the forums listing, locate the pagination navigation and activate the link labeled with the requested page number. Confirm completion by checking that the URL or selected pagination state corresponds to that page and the listing has refreshed before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill forum or listing page contains numbered pagination controls and the task requests a specific page. Ensure the target page link is visible before selecting it.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Before Finishing
skills.principle: Open the relevant list page, inspect the accessibility tree for pagination, and activate the link matching the requested page. After navigation, verify the page indicator or URL reflects the target page, then stop without extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requests a specific page in a paginated Reddit/Postmill list and the initial view is not already confirmed as that page.

skills.title: Use the Submit Navigation Link
skills.principle: Check the current page first. If it is already the post-creation form, report that the destination is ready and stop. Otherwise, activate the navigation entry labeled “Submit,” then verify the resulting page shows the submission form before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a Reddit/Postmill page for creating a new post, especially when the current accessibility tree may already show “Create submission” and fields such as Title, Body, and Forum.

skills.title: Stop After Submit Page Opens
skills.principle: When the task is only to open the Submit page, click the navigation link and verify the resulting page shows the submission form, such as the “Create submission” heading. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not fill fields or submit a post unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks where the requested destination is the Reddit/Postmill Submit page and the resulting form is visibly loaded.

skills.title: Open Reddit Profile via User Menu
skills.principle:
1. Identify the authenticated username control in the Reddit navigation and open its menu.
2. Select the menu item labeled “Profile,” rather than account or settings options.
3. Confirm completion when the URL is the user profile route and the page shows profile navigation or the user’s submissions and comments.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to the current user’s Reddit profile from another page, especially when the username appears as a menu button rather than a direct profile link.

skills.title: Validate Actions Before Repeating
skills.principle: Use a valid, complete BrowserGym action targeting the user-menu control, then inspect the refreshed accessibility tree. Confirm the menu’s expanded state or new menu items before selecting the profile option. If the action errors or the state is unchanged, re-identify the control semantically rather than repeating the malformed action.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a Reddit/Postmill account menu or profile from a page and the accessibility tree shows a user button, especially after an action error or unchanged expanded state.

skills.title: Submit Searches Through Their Form
skills.principle: Use the search field’s own submission mechanism, such as pressing Enter or activating an adjacent search control, rather than clicking an unrelated global “Submit” navigation link. Verify that results appear or the page remains on the forums listing; if redirected to content creation, return to forums and retry.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching forums from a page containing both a searchbox and a separate global “Submit” link, especially when the search field has no clearly labeled button.

skills.title: Use the Alphabetical Forums View
skills.principle: On Reddit’s forums listing, identify the navigation option labeled “Alphabetical” rather than changing the submission sort control. Select it, then verify the resulting page shows an “All forums” view with forum names grouped under letter headings. Report completion once that state is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When the forums page currently shows a submission-based listing and the task requests alphabetical ordering. The forums navigation must expose an “Alphabetical” link or equivalent view control.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming View Change
skills.principle: Once the page visibly shows the requested view—here, an “All forums” page grouped alphabetically—treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately; do not repeat the same link or issue additional no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a sorting or view-change action has visibly produced the requested page state, especially after navigation succeeds and the accessibility tree confirms the new heading, grouping, or ordering.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Forums Page
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation link labeled “Forums” to open the forum directory. Confirm completion by checking that the page title or main heading indicates a forum list and that forum entries are displayed. Stop and report success once the directory is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse available forums from another Reddit/Postmill page, provided the navigation contains a visible “Forums” link.

skills.title: Terminate After Destination Verification
skills.principle: After navigating, verify the destination using the URL and a distinctive page heading such as “List of forums.” Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated noop actions or continue interacting with the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree clearly shows the requested destination, including its expected URL or distinctive heading, and no additional browsing action is explicitly required.

skills.title: Use All Pages When Wiki Index Is Missing
skills.principle: If the Wiki navigation link opens a “Page not found” index, use the sidebar’s “All pages” link instead. Verify the resulting table lists the available knowledge-base pages, then report completion and stop once the Wiki content is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When visiting a community Wiki leads to a missing or empty index page, provided the page exposes an “All pages” navigation link.

skills.title: Recover from Broken Wiki Landing
skills.principle: When the Wiki navigation link opens a “Page not found” page, use the Wiki sidebar’s “All pages” link to reach the knowledge-base index. Verify the destination by checking for an “All pages” heading and a table of wiki entries, then stop rather than repeatedly clicking the broken top-level Wiki link.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Postmill when the top-level “Wiki” link consistently shows “Page not found” but the error page exposes functional Wiki navigation such as “All pages” or “Recent changes”.

skills.title: Navigate to a Named Forum
skills.principle:
1. From the site navigation, open the forums listing.
2. Locate the forum whose displayed name matches the requested topic, using its semantic label rather than a fixed element ID.
3. Open that forum and verify the page heading and topic list match the requested subject.
4. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to visit a specific forum or community and the site starts elsewhere. The forums listing must be accessible, and completion is indicated by the target forum heading and relevant discussions.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Continuing
skills.principle: After each navigation, inspect the fresh accessibility tree and current URL before acting. If the target forum page is already open, confirm its heading or URL, report completion, and stop. Never reuse element IDs or assumptions from an earlier page state.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a forum list or similar dynamic page, especially after a click changes the URL or page heading. Stop once the target forum is visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Use a Unique Wiki Page URL
skills.principle: From the Wiki index, open “Create new page” rather than submitting a form prefilled with the default index URL. Enter a unique URL slug, the requested title, and body, then save and verify the resulting page appears instead of an error page.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a new Postmill wiki page and the initial form has a disabled or prefilled default URL such as “index,” especially after saving it produces a 500 error.

skills.title: Validate Form Input Before Saving
skills.principle: Use a short, plain-text body first to avoid malformed or truncated action payloads. After filling each required field, verify the accessibility tree shows the complete value and the preview renders correctly. Only then click Save; if submission returns a server error, stop and report the failure rather than taking unrelated navigation actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Reddit wiki page through a required Title/Body form, especially after fill actions have produced empty-action errors, truncated values, or malformed serialized content.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation entry, inspect the refreshed page state. Confirm the target URL, heading, or distinctive content matches the requested destination. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeating the click or performing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when a click may already have succeeded, especially if the accessibility tree shows the requested page heading or destination URL.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Navigation Actions
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation link’s semantic label or observed href, not a malformed or truncated element reference. If clicking produces an empty-action error, navigate directly to the link’s observed destination, then verify the page heading or URL. Once the target page is displayed, stop instead of repeating clicks or no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation click repeatedly returns an empty-action error, or the accessibility tree already shows the requested destination page and its identifying heading or URL.

skills.title: Create Wiki TOC with Markdown Headings
skills.principle:
1. On the wiki creation form, enter the requested page title.
2. In the Markdown-enabled body, use hierarchical headings: a main heading, second-level section headings, and third-level subsection headings.
3. Confirm the preview renders the heading hierarchy and generated navigation links, then select Save.
4. Verify the saved page displays the headings and table of contents before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a Reddit/Postmill wiki index or structured documentation page where the form supports Markdown and the preview shows rendered headings or navigation links.

skills.title: Verify Submission After Server Error
skills.principle: After submitting a wiki page, inspect the resulting page or navigate to the wiki index before retrying. A 500 response may occur after the page is created; confirm whether the target page and rendered headings already exist. If present, stop. Only reopen the form and resubmit when verification shows the page is absent, using freshly observed controls rather than stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a wiki page and submission returns a server error, blank state, or unexpected navigation. Verify the target page’s existence and rendered Markdown headings before attempting another submission.

skills.title: Edit Existing Wiki Pages After Creation Errors
skills.principle: If creating a wiki page returns a server error, revisit the Wiki section and check whether the target page already exists. When it does, use its “Edit page” control, replace or extend the body with the requested Markdown, verify the preview shows the intended headings and bullets, then click “Save” and confirm the rendered page contains the changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a wiki-page creation attempt fails or the target URL already displays an existing page, especially when the Wiki page exposes an “Edit page” control and the editor provides a rendered Preview.

skills.title: Verify Save Then Stop
skills.principle: After editing a wiki page, click the editor’s current “Save” button once. Confirm the resulting page shows the intended heading and bulleted list, then report completion and stop. Do not reuse stale element IDs or navigate elsewhere after the save has visibly succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: When a wiki edit returns to the page view and the updated content is visibly rendered, especially after element IDs may have changed between observations.

skills.title: Edit Existing Wiki Index
skills.principle:
1. Open the Wiki page and inspect whether the requested index already exists.
2. If it exists, use its “Edit page” control instead of creating a duplicate page.
3. Preserve existing content and append the requested section using Markdown fenced code blocks and supporting explanations.
4. Confirm the preview renders the heading and code block, then select “Save” and verify the published page displays the new section.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Reddit/Postmill Wiki task requests modifying an index or similarly named page and the Wiki page exposes that page with an “Edit page” control.

skills.title: Complete Required Wiki Fields
skills.principle: Before saving a Postmill wiki page, inspect every required control and fill each one, including the title; do not assume a field is populated. Click Save only after URL, title, and body contain valid values. If an alert says “Please fill out this field,” use the focused field or validation state to identify and complete it, then resubmit and verify navigation away from the creation form.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a Reddit/Postmill wiki page and the form shows required URL, Title, or Body fields, especially after Save triggers a browser validation alert.

skills.title: Reveal Wiki Markdown Formatting Help
skills.principle: On a wiki-page creation form, locate the collapsed “Formatting help +” control. If clicking the checkbox is blocked by adjacent text, click its associated label instead. Confirm expansion when it changes to “Formatting help −” and a formatting table appears, then extract the listed syntax examples and report them without saving changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which Markdown features a wiki editor supports and the creation form visibly offers a collapsed “Formatting help +” control with Markdown allowed.

skills.title: Read Expanded Formatting Help
skills.principle: After opening a wiki page’s “Formatting help” control, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree. When the control shows “−” and a formatting table is visible, extract the listed Markdown options directly and stop; do not toggle it closed or navigate elsewhere. If closed, activate the control once and verify the expanded state before reading.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which Markdown formats a wiki editor supports and the page contains a “Formatting help” checkbox or expandable section. Requires access to the editor’s refreshed page state or accessibility tree.

skills.title: Check Existing Wiki Documentation First
skills.principle: Before creating or editing a wiki page, inspect the current Wiki page and its rendered preview for the requested information. If a relevant section already documents the needed link syntax and examples render as clickable links, report those instructions directly instead of making unnecessary edits or saves.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to learn how to perform a wiki-related action and the site’s Wiki page or edit preview is already accessible, especially when existing documentation may satisfy the request.

skills.title: Validate Markdown Links in Preview
skills.principle: If the Formatting help control is obstructed, use the Body field directly: enter a Markdown link in `[label](destination)` form, then inspect the live Preview. A rendered link with the expected label and destination confirms the syntax; repeat with the relevant wiki, forum, or profile destination as needed.
skills.when_to_apply: When learning or composing links on a Markdown-enabled wiki page and the formatting-help toggle cannot be activated, provided the editor exposes a Body field and rendered Preview.

skills.title: Inspect Wiki Creation Requirements
skills.principle: Open the wiki’s “Create new page” control, then inspect the form’s accessibility labels and required markers. Treat fields explicitly marked “required” or with an asterisk as mandatory, and report their labels without submitting the form.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which fields are required to create a wiki page and the current view is a wiki page or landing page with a “Create new page” navigation entry.

skills.title: Verify Submission Before Reporting
skills.principle: Identify required inputs from labels marked with an asterisk, including disabled fields that are already populated. For an information-only task, report those fields without submitting the form. If submission is attempted, inspect the resulting page for confirmation; an error page such as “500 Internal Server Error” means creation was not verified, so report only the confirmed field requirements.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to determine form requirements, especially on wiki creation pages, and the accessibility tree visibly marks required fields. Do not claim successful creation unless post-submit state confirms it.

skills.title: Validate Actions and Stop on Success
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to identify the target navigation link, then issue a correctly formatted action with the element’s current identifier. If the tool reports an empty or malformed action, fix the payload format rather than repeating it unchanged. After navigation succeeds and the destination page heading or URL confirms completion, stop instead of clicking again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the target link is visible in the accessibility tree. Confirm the destination state after the action, especially when tool errors indicate the action payload was not executed.

skills.title: Report Wiki Changes After Opening List
skills.principle:
1. Open the Wiki and select the “Recent changes” navigation link.
2. Verify the resulting page is headed “Recent changes” and contains the revision table with title, author, and date columns.
3. Summarize the visible recent entries to the user, then terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check recent Wiki changes and the Wiki page exposes a “Recent changes” link plus a populated revisions table.

skills.title: Correct Malformed Click Actions
skills.principle: When a click produces an empty-action error, reissue it using the exact accessibility-tree target in valid action syntax, without extra escaping or parameters. Then verify navigation by checking the destination heading or URL; once the requested page is visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a visible navigation link is identified but the browser reports an empty action or malformed-action error, especially before repeating navigation attempts.

skills.title: Emit Valid Actions and Stop
skills.principle: Use the browser action syntax exactly as required, with a complete action such as `click("target")`; do not wrap it in malformed nested JSON. After an action succeeds, verify the resulting page state. If the requested content is already displayed, terminate instead of repeating clicks, scrolling, or other unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Reddit/Postmill pages using accessibility-tree targets, especially after an action-format error or once the requested list or page is visibly loaded.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Forum
skills.principle: Once the page URL and heading confirm the requested forum, treat browsing as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of clicking additional navigation links or exploring unrelated views.
skills.when_to_apply: When a forum-browsing task reaches a page whose URL and visible heading identify the requested community, such as `/f/<target>` and its matching forum name.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Forum Access
skills.principle: Once the target forum page is open and its heading plus visible submissions are present, treat exploration as complete. Inspect the displayed topics, then report completion and terminate. Only use the forum’s explicit “More” or pagination control when additional coverage is specifically required; do not repeat scrolling when the observation remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: For Reddit/Postmill exploration tasks, after navigating from “Forums” to the requested forum and confirming its heading and submission list are visible.

skills.title: Verify Product-Specific Compare Action
skills.principle: Identify the target product card by its visible name, then activate that card’s “Add to Compare” control rather than a neighboring action. Confirm completion from the resulting success alert naming the target product or from the comparison-list count increasing. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping product grids or showcase lists when adding one specific item to a comparison list and multiple product cards expose similarly labeled controls.

skills.title: Verify Comparison Addition Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting a product’s "Add to Compare" control, inspect the updated page for a confirmation alert stating it was added to the comparison list or a changed comparison count. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not retry stale element IDs or continue clicking, which can trigger unrelated controls such as "Add to Cart."
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product to a shopping comparison list, especially after asynchronous updates or accessibility-tree changes. Stop immediately once the page visibly confirms the comparison-list addition.

skills.title: Verify Submission After Timeout
skills.principle: After submitting a form, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree for a success alert before retrying. If confirmation text such as “Thank you for your subscription” appears, treat the task as complete, report success, and stop. Only retry when no success indicator exists, using newly observed controls rather than stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for newsletter, registration, or similar forms when a click reports a timeout or the page refreshes. The form must show a recognizable success message or otherwise provide updated state for verification.

skills.title: Re-fill Forms After Navigation
skills.principle: After a submission navigates or refreshes the page, re-read the current accessibility tree and locate the current form controls. Re-enter the required value into the newly rendered field, verify its value appears and validation errors clear, then activate the matching action button. Do not reuse stale element IDs or assume values persisted across pages.
skills.when_to_apply: When a form submission changes the URL or page state, especially if the next observation shows a new element ID, an empty field, or a required-field validation message.

skills.title: Use Advanced Search Description Field
skills.principle:
1. Open the shopping site's “Advanced Search” page.
2. Enter the requested product attribute or keyword in the “Description” field.
3. Click the form’s “Search” button.
4. Confirm completion when the results page displays the submitted criterion and a matching item count.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests finding products by a descriptive attribute or keyword and the site exposes an “Advanced Search” link with a “Description” textbox and “Search” button.

skills.title: Refresh Targets After Navigation
skills.principle: After every navigation or form submission, inspect the new accessibility tree before acting. Resolve controls by their current visible role and label rather than reusing stale element IDs. Verify the resulting page state matches the intended destination; if results are already displayed, stop or select a result deliberately instead of clicking an old “Search” target.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking links, submitting searches, or any action that changes the page, especially when accessibility-tree bids may be regenerated or when the observed page differs from the expected search form.

skills.title: Edit Cart Quantity Directly
skills.principle:
1. Open the cart using the cart link; if a mini-cart dialog appears, use its quantity controls or choose “View and Edit Cart.”
2. Identify the target item by its visible product name and associated “Qty” spinbutton.
3. Clear the existing quantity, enter the requested quantity, and verify the spinbutton displays the new value.
4. Report completion once the updated quantity is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping-cart quantity changes when the cart link and item-level “Qty” spinbuttons are available. Confirm the target item by visible name before editing, especially when multiple cart items are present.

skills.title: Save Cart Quantity Changes
skills.principle: In the cart mini-cart, adjust the target item’s quantity, then activate the newly displayed “Update” control. Verify the cart item count, quantity, and subtotal reflect the change. Once the updated cart state is visible, report completion and stop; do not open “Edit” or proceed to checkout unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing an item quantity in a shopping cart and the quantity field is followed by an “Update” control. Use the cart summary as the completion check before taking further actions.

skills.title: Use Product Search Directly
skills.principle: For a requested product, use the storefront’s Search field before manually browsing categories or showcase pages. Enter the full product name, submit the search, and inspect the resulting product titles and prices. If the results explicitly show no matches, report that the item was not found; otherwise open the matching listing and verify its displayed price.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site exposes a Search combobox or text field and the target product is not immediately visible on the current page.

skills.title: Report Unavailable When Product Is Absent
skills.principle: Check product listings for an exact name match and inspect available pagination before reporting a price. If no matching product appears, clearly report that it is unavailable on the current webpage rather than substituting a similar item or inventing a price.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping price lookups when the target product is not immediately visible and the page provides listings or pagination to inspect.

skills.title: Open Product Reviews Directly
skills.principle: From a product listing, select the target product’s review-count link to open its detail page at the reviews section. If reviews are not expanded, activate the product’s “Reviews (N)” tab. Read the customer review text, rating, and author, then report the requested findings and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read reviews for a specific product and the listing shows a review-count link or the product page provides a “Reviews (N)” tab.

skills.title: Activate the Reviews Tab
skills.principle: On a product page, clicking a review-count link may only set the URL anchor, not reveal review content. Activate the actual “Reviews” tab or its nested link, then verify the tab becomes expanded and review text appears. Scroll only after expansion; repeated scrolling cannot expose content that remains collapsed.
skills.when_to_apply: When the product page shows a “Reviews (N)” tab or review-count link but the accessibility tree contains no review text and the tab is marked expanded=false.

skills.title: Read Manufacturer From Product Details
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product in the shopping list or search results and open its product page.
2. Inspect the visible Details or Product Information section, especially the attribute table.
3. Find the row labeled “Manufacturer,” use its adjacent cell as the answer, then report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks for a product manufacturer and the product page exposes a Details or Product Information table. Verify the product title matches the requested item before reading the manufacturer row.

skills.title: Read Product Attribute Tables Directly
skills.principle: Inspect the product details accessibility tree before scrolling. When a table contains the requested row header, read the adjacent cell value immediately. Treat the visible label-value pair as completion evidence, report it, and stop instead of repeating scrolls or reopening an already expanded section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product pages when asked for manufacturer, brand, SKU, or another specification, especially when the Details panel or an attribute table is already visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Set Quantity Before Adding
skills.principle: On a product page, identify the labeled quantity field, replace its current value with the requested quantity, and confirm the field displays that value. Then activate “Add to Cart” and stop once the control changes to “Added” or an equivalent success state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requires adding a specific product quantity and the product page exposes a quantity input alongside an “Add to Cart” control.

skills.title: Stop After Cart Confirmation
skills.principle: Set the product quantity to the requested value, click “Add to Cart” once, then wait for the resulting confirmation. When an alert confirms the item was added or the button changes to “Added,” treat the task as complete and stop; do not click again, especially while the page shows loading or busy state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding a specified quantity from a product detail page, where the quantity control and “Add to Cart” button are visible and success is indicated by an addition alert, cart-count update, or “Added” button.

skills.title: Submit Product Reviews Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Open the target product page and choose “Add Your Review.”
2. Complete every required field, including nickname, summary, and review text.
3. For star ratings, click the visible rating label rather than a hidden radio input when clicks are intercepted; verify the selected state.
4. Click “Submit Review” and confirm an alert states the review was submitted for moderation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping product pages with a review form, especially when star-rating radio inputs are hidden, outside the viewport, or blocked by overlapping labels. Ensure the account is signed in and all required fields are populated.

skills.title: Verify Product Identity Before Reviewing
skills.principle: When search results contain related but nonmatching items, compare each result’s full title with the requested product before opening it. Use exact-title matching or refine the query; only then open the product page and its review form. Confirm the page heading identifies the requested item before entering review details.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping search returns approximate matches, related search terms, or many results and the task requires reviewing a specific product.

skills.title: Report the Extracted Product Attribute
skills.principle: When the target product page visibly contains the requested attribute, read the value from the labeled product-details row, provide it in the task response, and terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions after the answer is already supported by the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on product-detail pages when the requested field, such as Manufacturer, is visible in the details table and the product title matches the requested item.

skills.title: Locate Review Posting Date
skills.principle:
1. Identify the target product from the listing by matching its name and, when useful, its low rating or review count.
2. Open the product details page and select the Reviews tab.
3. Find the relevant negative review and read the date next to “Posted on.”
4. Report that date once it is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking when a particular product review was posted, when the product page exposes a Reviews tab and the review includes a visible “Posted on” date.

skills.title: Use Fresh Observed Product Controls
skills.principle: On search results, match the target by its exact product title rather than rating or review count. Use the currently observed product link or Reviews link, preserving its exact live bid; do not invent a prefixed or stale bid. After navigation, verify the product title, open Reviews, and identify the negative review’s displayed posting date.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search returns multiple similar products and the task requires inspecting a specific product review. Refresh or re-read the accessibility tree before acting, especially after any failed or stale-element error.

skills.title: Use Keyboard For Obstructed Star Ratings
skills.principle: When custom star controls are covered by overlapping labels, stop retrying pointer clicks. Focus the rating radio group, use keyboard navigation (Tab or arrow keys) and Space to select the requested stars, then verify the chosen radio is checked. Complete any required review fields and submit the form.
skills.when_to_apply: On a product review form where star radios or their labels report pointer-event interception, invisibility, or viewport errors, especially when the review section is already open and the rating group is accessible.

skills.title: Use Keyboard For Obstructed Star Ratings
skills.principle: When star-radio clicks time out because labels intercept pointer events, use keyboard interaction instead: focus the rating group, navigate with Tab or arrow keys to the requested star, and press Space. Verify the requested radio reports checked before completing required review fields and submitting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product review forms when star inputs are hidden, overlaid by neighboring labels, outside the viewport, or repeated pointer clicks produce interception or visibility timeouts.

skills.title: Verify Order After Submission Timeout
skills.principle: After selecting shipping and reaching “Review & Payments,” click “Place Order” once. If the action times out or a loading overlay appears, inspect the resulting page before retrying. A “Thank you for your purchase!” message, success-page URL, or order number confirms completion; report success and stop to avoid duplicate orders.
skills.when_to_apply: During shopping checkout when “Place Order” has been clicked and the browser reports a timeout, loading state, intercepted pointer, or uncertain navigation result.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Browser Actions
skills.principle: When an action returns an empty-action or parsing error, do not repeat the same malformed command or stale element reference. Re-read the current accessibility tree, target the visible control by its role and label, or navigate using its observed destination URL. Verify that the URL or page content changes before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task must open the cart or checkout and a click repeatedly produces an empty-action error, while the cart link and its destination remain visible in the current page state.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Editing
skills.principle: Open the cart and inspect its state before attempting item edits. If the page explicitly says the cart is empty, confirm that no target item exists, explain that editing requires adding the item first, and stop rather than searching for unavailable controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to modify a product already presumed to be in a shopping cart, especially after opening the cart or seeing an empty-cart message.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Full Cart
skills.principle: When selecting “My Cart,” distinguish the mini-cart dialog from the full cart page. Close the overlay or activate its “View Cart” control, then verify the page URL and cart contents. Only after the target item appears should you use its edit-options control; if the cart is genuinely empty, report that the requested edit cannot be completed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires editing an existing cart item and clicking “My Cart” produces an overlay instead of navigating to a cart page.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Shipping
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart and inspect its confirmed state. If it displays “You have no items in your shopping cart,” report that shipping cannot be calculated and ask the user to add items; otherwise continue to the shipping-cost controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check shipping for current cart items, especially from a product-list page. Confirm the cart page state before attempting shipping estimation.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Shipping
skills.principle: Open the cart and inspect its contents. If the page explicitly reports that the cart is empty, treat shipping-cost lookup as unavailable for the current cart and report that finding; do not add arbitrary products. If items are present, continue to the cart’s shipping estimator and verify the displayed cost.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check shipping for current cart items, after opening the cart or its mini-cart. This is especially important when the interface displays an explicit empty-cart message.

skills.title: Stop After Verified Cart Addition
skills.principle: Once an item from the requested category is added, verify the success alert or updated cart count. If the goal is satisfied, report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly opening products, returning to listings, or adding unnecessary items.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for broad shopping tasks requiring items from a category, especially after the page shows an “added to your shopping cart” alert or an increased cart item count.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category
skills.principle: After selecting the requested shopping category, verify the resulting page shows the category heading and product listings. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate unless the task explicitly requires a specific subcategory, product, or number of items. Avoid unnecessary pagination and exploratory clicks that can prevent clean task completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for broad shopping requests such as “explore [category]” when the category navigation succeeds and the resulting page visibly contains the requested category and products.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to a Department
skills.principle: From the storefront homepage, locate the navigation menu item matching the requested department and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the resulting page heading names the department and that its product listing or category contents are visible, then report completion without taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to browse or open a named shopping department and the homepage accessibility tree exposes that department as a navigation menu item.

skills.title: Use Exact Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When selecting a category from an accessibility tree, use the element’s exact current bid (for example, the menuitem bid), not its rendered label, icon text, or guessed ID. Emit one valid browser action with correct quoting, then inspect the updated URL or category heading to confirm navigation before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping category is visibly present in the accessibility tree but clicks return empty-action or element-not-found errors. Ensure the page state is current and the bid is copied exactly from that observation.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category Results
skills.principle: For broad exploration tasks, navigate to the requested category, then verify the page heading and visible product listings confirm the category loaded. Once products are displayed, report completion and terminate; do not keep drilling into subcategories or pagination without a specific additional requirement.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the user requests general product exploration and the category page visibly shows matching products, a result count, or listing controls confirming successful navigation.

skills.title: Navigate Directly Through Category Menus
skills.principle: Select the category menu item whose accessible name exactly matches the requested department. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the resulting URL, page heading, and visible item listing; once these identify the target category, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks you to find a department or category and the current page exposes a navigation menu with a matching accessible category label.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Once navigation reaches the requested category, verify the page heading or breadcrumb matches the target. Treat that observable state as completion; report success and stop instead of scrolling through products or taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks only to locate or open a category, and the resulting page visibly shows the requested category name in its heading, breadcrumb, or URL.

skills.title: Open Product Details from Listing
skills.principle: Locate the target product by its visible title in the product list and activate its title link, not an unrelated action such as “Add to Cart.” On the product page, verify the heading matches the target and the “Details” tab or details panel is selected and visible. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking to view a specific product’s details when the item appears in a product listing or search results and the page exposes a title link or details control.

skills.title: Verify Exact Product Before Opening
skills.principle: Search for the requested product, then compare result titles against the exact requested name and distinguishing attributes. Open a result only when it matches; otherwise inspect additional result pages or refine the query. Do not substitute a similar item. If no exact match is found, report that clearly instead of claiming success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search returns similar products but no exact title match. Use pagination or a refined query before opening details, and require the product page heading to match the requested item.

skills.title: Open and Verify Product Reviews
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product in the listing using its name or distinctive description.
2. Select the product’s review-count link to open its detail page and reviews anchor.
3. If the reviews tab is collapsed, expand it; verify it is selected and the review entries are visible.
4. Summarize the displayed review count, ratings, and recurring customer themes, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect reviews for a product and the shopping page shows a matching product card with a review-count link or product detail page with a Reviews tab.

skills.title: Report Reviews After Reading
skills.principle: When the product’s Reviews tab is expanded and customer review text is visible, extract the ratings and recurring sentiments, then immediately provide the requested summary to the user. Treat the visible review panel as completion evidence; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for another page change.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for product-review tasks when the target product details page is open and the Reviews link or tab has expanded to show customer ratings and comments.

skills.title: Read Price Directly From Product Page
skills.principle: On a product detail page, identify the requested item by its heading, then locate the nearby standalone price text. Report that displayed price directly; do not add cart or navigation actions when the answer is already visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for an item’s price when the product detail page is open and the item heading and price are both visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Recover Search After Navigation Changes
skills.principle:
1. After a search or navigation action, inspect the current accessibility tree before reusing any element reference.
2. Locate the visible search combobox by its current role or label, then fill the query and submit only when the current Search control is enabled.
3. If the page changed to Advanced Search or a category, use that page’s visible Product Name field and Search button instead of stale header references.
4. Confirm results by matching the target product title and displayed price.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching a shopping catalog and the page navigates, element IDs change, or a search control becomes disabled or invisible. Reinspect the current page and use controls belonging to that page.

skills.title: Report Unlisted Products Precisely
skills.principle: When a requested product is absent from the observed product list, inspect the displayed titles and page context, then report that it is not listed on the current page rather than inventing a rating. Suggest using the product name as a search query for broader lookup.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when answering a product-rating question and the target item is not present in the currently observed shopping page or product showcase.

skills.title: Interpret Star Ratings Correctly
skills.principle: When a product page shows star glyphs alongside a percentage, do not equate the number of rendered glyphs with the rating. Determine the filled-star proportion or accessible percentage: for example, 20% corresponds to 1 out of 5 stars. Report the rating value separately from the review count or rating distribution.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product-detail pages where the rating summary exposes stars plus a percentage, especially when accessibility text lists repeated star icons without indicating which are filled.

skills.title: Use Visible Product Details Directly
skills.principle: On a product page, inspect the accessibility tree for the title, price, SKU, stock status, and visible description or “Product Quick Look” content. If requested details are already exposed, extract and report them directly. Only interact with a details tab when information is actually hidden; use the observed element role or identifier rather than assuming a text label is a valid bid.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requesting product details when the product page is already open and its accessibility tree exposes pricing, identifiers, and description content.

skills.title: Search Exact Products First
skills.principle: Use the storefront’s Search combobox with the exact product name before manually scanning showcases or pagination. Submit the search, inspect the resulting product list or no-results message, and only report absence after confirming that state. Treat failed clicks or unchanged page content as uncompleted actions, not evidence that another page was checked.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for details about a specific product on a shopping site, especially when the initial showcase list does not contain it and pagination controls are present.

skills.title: Verify Stock Before Wishlisting
skills.principle: On a product page, inspect the availability status before attempting to wishlist. If it is out of stock, do not treat the visible “Add to Wish List” control as successful. If clicked, verify the resulting wishlist page or alert; report the stock-based failure when the page says the item cannot be added.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks that add a product to a wishlist, especially when the product page visibly indicates “OUT OF STOCK” or the wishlist operation returns an availability error.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirmed Completion
skills.principle: After performing the target action, verify the resulting page state or success alert. Once it confirms the requested item is present, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks when a confirmation alert, updated wishlist/cart count, or visible target item proves the requested change succeeded.

skills.title: Extract SKU From Product Details
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product in the shopping list and open its product-name link.
2. On the product page, find the labeled “SKU” field near the title and stock information.
3. Report the exact value shown next to “SKU,” confirming it matches the target product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a product SKU and the shopping site exposes product listings with links to detail pages. Ensure the opened page’s title matches the requested item before extracting the SKU.

skills.title: Verify Exact Product Before Extracting SKU
skills.principle: Use search results to locate candidates, but do not accept the first approximate match. Open the candidate, compare its title and distinguishing attributes with the requested product, and continue refining or paging if they differ. Extract the SKU only after the product identity is confirmed, then report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search returns similarly named products and the task requests a SKU or other product-specific identifier. Verify the product detail page matches the requested item before answering.

skills.title: Use Account Navigation Links
skills.principle: From an account-related page, locate the navigation entry whose accessible name matches the requested destination and activate it. Confirm completion by checking the resulting URL or page heading, then report success and stop without changing unrelated settings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the requested shopping-account destination appears as a labeled navigation link in the current accessibility tree, especially when the page heading or URL can confirm successful navigation.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target page is reached, verify completion using the current URL and a distinctive page heading or state. Report completion and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree and URL visibly confirm the requested destination, especially after a successful click or redirect.

skills.title: Verify Product Details Tab Selection
skills.principle: On a product page, locate the tab matching the requested information, then activate it if it is not selected. Confirm completion by checking that the tab shows selected=true or expanded=true and its associated panel visibly contains product details. Report completion only after this state is observed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a product’s details, specifications, description, or similar tab and the product page is already open or has been located.

skills.title: Verify Details Tab, Then Stop
skills.principle: On a product page, inspect the target tab’s state before acting. If the “Details” tab is already selected and its content panel is visible, report completion and terminate. Otherwise, click the Details tab once, verify it becomes selected and the panel appears, then stop without repeated clicks or no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view product details and the product page’s accessibility tree shows a Details tab and associated panel. Use the selected state and visible panel content as completion evidence.

skills.title: Check All Product Pages Before Concluding
skills.principle: When a requested product is absent from the current listing, inspect the full visible list and follow available pagination controls, such as “Page Next” or “Page 2.” Compare each product title with the exact requested item. Only report that it could not be found after the available listing pages are checked; do not add a merely similar product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring a specific product when the initial product listing does not contain an exact title and pagination is visible.

skills.title: Check Stock Before Wishlisting
skills.principle: On the exact target product page, verify both the title and stock status before acting. If the page shows “OUT OF STOCK” and the wishlist operation is rejected for unavailable stock, do not substitute a similar item; report that the requested product cannot currently be added.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific shopping item to a wishlist, especially after search results show similarly named products. Prerequisite: confirm the product title and availability on its detail page.

skills.title: Verify Product Before Comparing
skills.principle: Search for the requested product, then verify the result’s exact title before opening it; search relevance may place a different item first. On the product page, activate “Add to Compare” and confirm the success alert or updated “Compare Products” item count.
