skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific item to a Magento-style comparison list from search results, especially when multiple similarly named products appear and the compare header or confirmation alert is available.

skills.title: Verify Compare Addition and Stop
skills.principle: After selecting the product’s “Add to Compare” control, inspect the updated page for a success alert stating it was added to the comparison list or an increased compare-item count. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of clicking repeatedly or navigating unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product to a shopping site’s comparison list, especially after the page remains open and provides an alert, comparison-list link, or item count confirming the operation.

skills.title: Use Keyboard For Overlapping Ratings
skills.principle: When a rating radio or label is blocked by overlapping elements, stop retrying pointer clicks. Focus the rating group with keyboard navigation, select the requested option with arrow keys or Space, then verify its state is checked before submitting the completed review.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product review forms when rating controls remain unchecked and click errors report intercepted pointer events or viewport/visibility problems, despite the form being open and its required text fields available.

skills.title: Handle Obstructed Star Rating Controls
skills.principle: When rating radios are visually overlaid and clicks are intercepted, focus the rating group or a radio, then use keyboard navigation (ArrowRight or End) to select the requested star value. Verify the chosen radio is checked, confirm all required text fields contain values, then submit and check for a success message.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product review forms where star-rating clicks time out, labels intercept pointer events, or radios report being outside the viewport. Ensure the review form is expanded and the target product is identified.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to the Target Category
skills.principle: Use the main navigation menu to select the requested category by its visible label. After navigation, verify the page heading and item-range summary match that category, then report completion without taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to browse a named category and the current page exposes that category as a visible navigation menu item.

skills.title: Use Current Menuitem Bids
skills.principle: When navigating category menus, select the menuitem using its current accessibility-tree bid, not visible text, icon glyphs, or a stale bid from another page. After each navigation, re-read the tree, identify the target category’s current menuitem, activate it, and verify the resulting page heading matches the requested category before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping category pages when text-based element lookup fails, bids change after navigation, or the menu contains icon-prefixed labels and dynamically refreshed accessibility trees.

skills.title: Read Product Attributes Directly
skills.principle: On a product detail page, inspect the visible Details or Product Quick Look section before searching or interacting further. Match the requested attribute label, such as “Manufacturer,” to its adjacent value, verify it belongs to the target product, then report the value and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the target product page is already open and its accessibility tree exposes a Details, Product Quick Look, or specification table containing the requested attribute.

skills.title: Read Visible Product Details Directly
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree already exposes the requested product attribute, read the value directly beside its semantic label (for example, a table rowheader and cell). Report that value immediately; do not click static text or use fill on a nonexistent input. Stop once the label-value pair is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product-detail pages when the requested attribute, such as manufacturer, appears in the current accessibility tree under Details or a product-information table.

skills.title: Confirm Homepage Before Acting
skills.principle: When the current URL and visible content already satisfy a browsing request, treat the task as complete. Report that the user is already on the homepage with product listings, then terminate; do not issue repeated no-op actions, which can produce empty-action errors.
skills.when_to_apply: For shopping tasks requesting homepage browsing when the accessibility tree shows the store homepage URL and visible product listings or showcases.

skills.title: Use Pagination Deliberately
skills.principle: When browsing a paginated product catalog, inspect the item-count and pagination controls before repeated scrolling. Select the next-page control once, then verify the URL, visible product range, and current-page indicator. If navigation reports a timeout but the updated observation shows the next page loaded, continue from that state instead of retrying, reversing, or performing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a catalog shows multiple pages or an item range such as “1 to N of M total,” especially after a click reports a timeout but the subsequent accessibility tree reflects a changed page.

skills.title: Run And Verify Advanced Product Search
skills.principle:
1. Open the store’s “Advanced Search” link and identify fields matching the requested product criteria.
2. Enter the target term or constraints in the appropriate fields, then activate the form’s “Search” button.
3. Confirm completion on the results page by checking the displayed criteria, result count, product listings, and pagination; then report the outcome.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires advanced product filtering and the page exposes an “Advanced Search” link with labeled fields such as Product Name, SKU, description, or price.

skills.title: Use Real Search Criteria
skills.principle: Enter the actual product attributes supplied by the task, not placeholder text such as “desired product name here” or “desired SKU here.” Use one or more relevant fields, clear stale criteria before retrying, submit Search, and verify that the results page lists matching products. If no results appear, broaden or correct the query rather than adding arbitrary filters.
skills.when_to_apply: When using Magento Advanced Search or similar catalog forms and the task specifies products or attributes. Ensure the requested values are known before searching; if they are missing, obtain clarification instead of submitting invented criteria.

skills.title: Verify Sign-Out Completion
skills.principle:
1. Locate the account menu’s “Sign Out” control and activate it.
2. Confirm completion by checking for a “You are signed out” heading or equivalent signed-out confirmation, including replacement of “Sign Out” with “Sign In.”
3. Report completion and stop once the confirmation is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the shopping site shows an authenticated account and the task is to sign out. Do not perform further navigation after the logout-success page visibly confirms the session ended.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Sign-Out
skills.principle: Click the visible “Sign Out” control, then verify the resulting page shows “You are signed out” or changes the account control to “Sign In.” Once this confirmation appears, report completion and terminate; do not navigate elsewhere or attempt to sign in again.
skills.when_to_apply: For sign-out tasks when the page provides a “Sign Out” link and the post-action page visibly confirms logout.

skills.title: Open Popular Search Terms
skills.principle: On a shopping homepage, locate the footer link labeled “Search Terms” and open it. Confirm completion when the resulting page heading reads “Popular Search Terms” and a list of clickable search-term links is visible; stop there unless the user requests a specific term or product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view popular search terms, discover trending products, or browse common searches from a shopping site homepage. Requires the homepage to expose a footer or navigation link for search terms.

skills.title: Stop After Viewing Popular Terms
skills.principle: Once the page heading “Popular Search Terms” and its list of linked terms are visible, treat the discovery task as complete. Report completion and terminate. Do not click individual terms or continue browsing unless the task explicitly requests product details or further comparison.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view popular search terms or discover trending products, after navigating to the page displaying the “Popular Search Terms” heading and list.

skills.title: Verify Pagination State Before Reporting
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested category, locate the pagination control by its visible label, and select the target page. Confirm completion using the URL parameter and the item-range heading (for example, the target page’s displayed item range) before reporting success and stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for category-listing tasks requiring a specific page, especially when starting from another page type. The category page and pagination controls must be available, and completion should be verified from the resulting page state.

skills.title: Use Visible Category Navigation
skills.principle: Navigate to a product category through the visible category menu or its link, not an invented URL. Verify the resulting page shows the category heading, product listings, and pagination before selecting page 2. If navigation returns a 404, stop retrying the same address and recover using the store homepage or visible navigation controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a category’s product listing or a later pagination page, especially when the current page is a product detail page and category URLs are not confirmed.

skills.title: Navigate Account Pages by Visible Labels
skills.principle: From a signed-in shopping account page, locate the relevant entry in the visible “My Account” navigation and activate its text label, such as “Address Book.” Confirm completion by checking the page heading and URL or distinctive content. Once the target page is displayed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to visit an account-management page and the current observation shows a signed-in account navigation menu containing the requested destination.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once navigation reaches the requested page, verify its heading or distinctive content, then report completion and terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions after the goal is visibly satisfied, since unnecessary actions can prevent successful task completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree clearly shows the requested page title, URL, or distinctive content after navigation.

skills.title: Verify Target Page and Stop
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation item, inspect the updated accessibility tree and page title or URL. If the requested page is already displayed—such as a matching heading and relevant controls—treat the task as complete, report completion, and stop. Do not click repeated or non-interactive text elements merely because the label appears again elsewhere.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating account or shopping pages where the same destination label may appear as a link, heading, or static text, especially after a successful page transition.

skills.title: Use Recently Ordered Product Links
skills.principle: On an account dashboard, distinguish the “Recently Ordered” product list from the separate “Recent Orders” order table. Locate the target product by its visible title in “Recently Ordered” and open that product link directly; verify the product-detail page shows the matching title before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product from recently ordered items and the account page contains both “Recent Orders” and “Recently Ordered” sections.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After a click fails, re-read the latest accessibility tree and locate the target by its accessible name and role. Use the exact current bid as presented; do not add prefixes, reuse stale bids, or click surrounding containers. Confirm navigation by checking that the URL or page heading changes to the requested product details.
skills.when_to_apply: When selecting a product from a shopping page’s Recently Ordered list, especially after an element-not-found or empty-action error, and the latest accessibility tree still exposes the target product link.

skills.title: Verify Newsletter Subscription Status
skills.principle: Use the newsletter form’s email field and click “Subscribe.” Then inspect the resulting alert: if it says the address is already subscribed, treat the task as complete and report that status rather than retrying with another address.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to subscribe to a shopping-site newsletter and the page exposes a newsletter email field and “Subscribe” button. After submission, check for a success or already-subscribed alert.

skills.title: Reacquire Newsletter Form After Navigation
skills.principle: After any page change, reacquire the newsletter form from the current accessibility tree rather than reusing stale element IDs. Fill the required email textbox with the provided valid address, then activate the current “Subscribe” button. Verify a success confirmation; if the field shows “This is a required field,” refill it before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing through a footer newsletter form, especially after clicking causes navigation or rerendering. Requires a valid email address and a fresh accessibility-tree observation before submitting.

skills.title: Search Beyond the Current Wishlist
skills.principle: If the requested product is absent from the current wishlist, use the visible store search field with its name and submit the query. Inspect the results, open the matching product, and verify its title and details; request help only when an actual access or information barrier prevents continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view product details while a wishlist or other limited list lacks the target and store search is available.

skills.title: Search Beyond the Current Wishlist
skills.principle: When the requested product is absent from a wishlist, use the page’s visible Search combobox rather than stopping. Enter the product name, submit the search, inspect matching results, and open the matching product title or image. Confirm the product-detail page before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping task requests product details but the current wishlist or list view does not contain the target, and a Search field or navigation path is available.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Category Menus
skills.principle:
1. Identify the likely parent category from the visible navigation.
2. Hover the parent menu item to reveal its submenu.
3. Locate the target category by its accessible label and click it.
4. Confirm completion from the destination heading, breadcrumb, URL, or product listing before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests browsing a category that is absent from top-level navigation but may appear under a parent menu. Confirm the resulting category page is loaded before stopping.

skills.title: Verify Category Navigation Targets
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to locate the exact category label or category facet, rather than reusing an old element ID. Click the matching “Electronics” or relevant category control, then verify the page heading, breadcrumb, and URL reflect the requested section before continuing. If search results expose category facets, select the relevant facet directly.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping category is absent from the homepage or navigation changes after scrolling, searching, or page navigation. Reinspect the current accessibility tree before every click and confirm the resulting category page.

skills.title: Verify Cart Before Removing
skills.principle: Open the cart directly and inspect the complete “Shopping Cart Items” table for the target product. If its row is present, activate that row’s “Remove item” control and verify the row disappears or the cart total updates. If no matching row exists, report that the item is not currently in the cart instead of searching unrelated product listings.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to remove a specific product from a shopping cart and the current page is not already the cart. Ensure the cart table is fully loaded before concluding the item is absent.

skills.title: Verify Item Removal Before Continuing
skills.principle: In the cart, identify the target product row first, then activate that row’s own “Remove item” control. If a confirmation dialog appears, confirm it and wait for the cart to refresh. Verify the target is absent or the cart count changed before taking further actions; once removal is confirmed, stop instead of reusing stale element IDs or removing another row.
skills.when_to_apply: When removing a specific product from a shopping cart containing multiple similar rows, especially after a confirmation dialog or asynchronous cart refresh changes the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Clear Cart Through Sequential Removal
skills.principle: Open the full shopping cart, then repeatedly select each visible “Remove item” control. After every removal, re-read the updated page because item order and accessibility references may change. Continue until the cart count disappears or the page explicitly states, “You have no items in your shopping cart.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping cart lacks a single clear-all control and lists individual removal controls. Start from any page showing a cart indicator, and verify the empty-cart confirmation before reporting completion.

skills.title: Verify Cart Scope and State
skills.principle: Use the shopping cart page, not wishlist or comparison controls. Remove items through the cart’s "Remove item" links, then re-observe the updated page before selecting another item because accessibility IDs change. Treat a click timeout as inconclusive: verify the cart count and item table. Stop when the page states, "You have no items in your shopping cart."
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to empty a cart and the current page contains similarly labeled controls for wishlists, comparisons, or carts. First navigate to the cart and confirm its heading and item list before acting.

skills.title: Verify Cart Status Before Pricing
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the visible “My Cart” control. Check the resulting cart page or dialog for an explicit empty-cart message. If it states that no items are present, report that no total exists; otherwise, read and report the displayed cart total.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a shopping-cart total and the current page is another store page, especially when the cart control may show status in a dialog instead of navigating.

skills.title: Verify Element Identity Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s role and accessible name to target the actual cart link, not a nearby label or stale element ID. If a click reports pointer interception, inspect the resolved element and choose the link’s current locator or navigate using its observed href. Confirm the URL or cart heading changes before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a shopping cart from a product-listing page, especially after a click resolves to the search label, is intercepted by the search input, or leaves the page unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Cart State Before Editing
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the visible “My Cart” control. Check the resulting cart page or dialog for an explicit empty-cart message; if present, report that there are no items to view or edit and stop. Otherwise, proceed with the requested cart changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or edit cart details and the current page exposes a cart navigation control. This is especially useful when the cart may be empty and the interface displays status in a dialog or page message.

skills.title: Verify Cart State After Clicking
skills.principle: After selecting the shopping-cart control, inspect the resulting page or overlay rather than assuming navigation occurred. If it explicitly says the cart is empty, report that no details can be viewed or edited and stop. If items are listed, open the full cart view and edit the relevant quantities or options.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or edit cart contents, especially from another account page where the cart control may open a mini-cart overlay instead of navigating.

skills.title: Use Cart Popup Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the cart summary control, inspect the resulting popup. If it opens while the page remains unchanged, select its “View and Edit Cart” link to reach the full cart page, then verify the page heading or URL indicates the cart. Do not repeatedly click the same cart control.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site’s cart control opens a mini-cart dialog instead of navigating, and the dialog provides a “View and Edit Cart” option.

skills.title: Stop After Information Is Visible
skills.principle: When the requested account page is displayed and its fields are visibly populated, treat the task as complete. Do not click Save, focus fields, or repeat no-op actions unless the user requested an edit. Report that the information is visible and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: For account-information viewing tasks, after navigating from the account menu to a page headed “Account Information” or “Edit Account Information” with populated profile fields.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category Exploration
skills.principle: Once the requested category page is reached, verify its heading and visible product listings. For an “explore” request, this confirms completion; report success and terminate instead of drilling into subcategories, opening products, or continuing navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to explore or browse a broad shopping category and the page visibly shows the category name plus product listings. No specific product, filter, or purchase requirement should remain.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Category Exploration
skills.principle: For broad exploration tasks, open the requested category and verify the resulting page shows its title, product listings, and available navigation or filters. Once that state is observed, report completion and terminate rather than repeatedly switching subcategories, sorting, opening products, and returning to the category.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore a broad shopping category and the category page visibly contains products plus browsing controls. Treat the loaded listing as sufficient unless the task specifies a product, filter, or comparison.

skills.title: Open and Edit the Shopping Cart
skills.principle:
1. If the cart link is unavailable or not visible, navigate directly to the site’s shopping-cart page.
2. Confirm the page shows a “Shopping Cart” heading and a “Shopping Cart Items” table.
3. Identify editable “Qty” spinbuttons for the listed items; users can change quantities there.
4. Apply quantity changes by selecting “Update Shopping Cart,” then verify refreshed totals or quantities.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to view or edit the full cart, especially after the cart navigation link times out or is hidden, and the site exposes quantity fields and an update button.

skills.title: Reinspect Controls After Navigation
skills.principle: After each navigation, reread the current accessibility tree and locate controls by their visible role and label. On a product page, click that page’s current “Add to Cart” button, not a stale identifier from another page; verify the result indicates cart addition before opening “My Cart.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when moving between product listings, product pages, wish lists, and cart views where accessibility identifiers may change or similarly labeled controls are nearby.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Category Menus
skills.principle:
1. Identify the likely parent category from the task and hover its menu item to reveal nested options.
2. Re-read the accessibility tree after expansion, locate the submenu entry matching the requested product category by label, and click it.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, breadcrumb, URL, and visible product listings before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests browsing a product category that is nested under a visible navigation menu, especially when submenu items appear only after hovering.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category
skills.principle: Use the category hierarchy to reach the requested product category, then verify completion from the page state: the active category filter and product listing should visibly match the request. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of opening individual products or continuing exploratory actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to look at or browse a product category, especially after a parent category exposes a matching subcategory filter and the resulting page shows that category’s products.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category
skills.principle: Once the requested shopping category is selected, verify the page shows the category indicator (such as “Now Shopping by”) and a product listing. Treat that state as completion for a browse-only task, then report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly scrolling without a specific product or filter requirement.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for browse-only shopping tasks when the requested category is visible in the page state and products are listed, especially when no item, sort order, filter, or purchase action is specified.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Listing
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the visible cart navigation entry. Inspect the resulting cart page or dialog: if it explicitly states that no items are present, report the cart as empty; otherwise, enumerate each displayed item. Stop after the cart state is clearly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to list current shopping-cart items and the page exposes a cart link or control. Use the explicit empty-cart message or visible item list as the completion check.

skills.title: Verify Cart State Before Removing
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart and inspect its contents before taking removal actions. If the page explicitly says the cart is empty, treat the requested item as already absent, report that no removal is needed, and stop. Otherwise, locate the matching item and use its remove control, then verify it disappears.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to remove a specific product from a shopping cart, especially after navigating directly to the cart page. The cart contents or an explicit empty-cart message must be visible before deciding the task is complete.

skills.title: Terminate After Cart Verification
skills.principle: When the cart visibly states that it contains no items, treat the requested removal as complete, report completion, and terminate. Do not repeatedly issue noop actions or wait for another state change after the success condition is already observable.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to cart-removal tasks when the cart page clearly shows the target item is absent or explicitly displays an empty-cart message.

skills.title: Verify Wishlist Before Adding
skills.principle: Inspect visible account indicators and page sections before modifying a product. If the target item already appears under “My Wish List,” treat the task as complete, report that it is already saved, and stop. Otherwise, locate the product and use its “Add to Wish List” control, then verify the wishlist state.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to add or move a product to a wishlist, especially on shopping pages where account widgets or category pages may already expose the current wishlist contents.

skills.title: Stop After Wishlist Confirmation
skills.principle: Use the store search to locate the exact product, select its matching result card, and click “Add to Wish List.” Once the page shows a success alert or the wishlist lists the target item, report completion and terminate instead of performing additional waits or navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product to a logged-in shopping wishlist, especially after search results provide an exact title match and the interface confirms the item was added.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Checkout
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the visible “My Cart” control and inspect its resulting state. If the page or dialog says the cart has no items, report that checkout cannot proceed and request that items be added; do not attempt checkout actions without cart contents.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to proceed to checkout and the cart status is not yet known, especially on a shopping site showing a cart navigation control.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Clicks
skills.principle: When a control is identified in the accessibility tree, activate it using its current element bid or a supported role-based locator, not its visible label alone. After any action error, reread the updated tree and select a valid bid before retrying; do not repeat the same invalid locator or unrelated controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply whenever BrowserGym reports that an element cannot be found, especially when multiple elements share text or the tree exposes numeric bids alongside accessible names.

skills.title: Recognize an Empty Shopping Cart
skills.principle: On the shopping cart page, inspect the main content for an explicit empty-cart message such as “You have no items in your shopping cart.” If present, report that the cart is empty and no total cost exists; do not search for subtotal or checkout controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a cart total and the cart page is already open or accessible. Use this when the page visibly confirms that no items are present.

skills.title: Read Cart Subtotal From Mini-Cart
skills.principle: Click the cart control once, then inspect the resulting mini-cart dialog for “Cart Subtotal” and its currency value. If the dialog only provides navigation, select “View and Edit Cart” and read the cart summary there. Report the displayed amount and stop once the cost is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks for cart cost and the cart control opens a mini-cart overlay or cart page. Ensure the resulting UI is inspected for subtotal or total text before taking further actions.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Item Lookup
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart and inspect its current state before searching for the requested item. If the page explicitly indicates the cart is empty, report that the item cannot be viewed there and explain that it must be added first; do not claim to have opened item details.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view, edit, or inspect a specific product in a shopping cart, especially when the cart page is already open and its accessibility tree shows an empty-cart message.

skills.title: Verify the Target Cart Item First
skills.principle: In the cart, locate the row whose visible product name matches the requested item before selecting any control. Open that item’s product-name link or its associated Edit link, then confirm the resulting page heading matches the target. If the target is absent, do not inspect or edit an unrelated cart item; report the mismatch or search through the cart’s available pages.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view details for a specific cart item, especially when the cart contains different products. Use only element bids from the current accessibility tree, not raw URLs as click targets.

skills.title: Verify Cart Empty After Removal
skills.principle: In the shopping cart, identify the relevant item row and activate its “Remove item” control. Wait for the cart to refresh, then confirm the page displays “You have no items in your shopping cart.” Only after this observable confirmation report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when removing a requested cart item, especially when the cart contains a single item and the removal should leave the cart empty.

skills.title: Verify Cart Item Before Removing
skills.principle: In the shopping cart, locate the row whose product name matches the requested target, then activate that row’s “Remove item” control. If the target is absent, do not remove another product; recheck the cart or report that it is already absent. Confirm completion by verifying the target no longer appears in the cart.
skills.when_to_apply: When removing a specifically named product from a cart containing zero or more items, especially when the visible cart contents do not match the requested target.

skills.title: Search and Add Product to Wishlist
skills.principle:
1. Search for the requested product using the storefront search field and submit the query.
2. On results, match the product title or distinctive attributes before acting.
3. Click that product’s associated “Add to Wish List” control, not another result’s control.
4. Confirm completion from the success alert or the item appearing in “My Wish List,” then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping session must add a named product to a wishlist and the item is not visible on the current page. Requires a usable storefront search field and wishlist controls.

skills.title: Use the Storefront Search Control
skills.principle:
1. From the current storefront, use its visible Search combobox rather than repeated browser back navigation.
2. Enter the target product name and submit with the storefront Search control.
3. Open the matching product or use its associated Add to Wish List control.
4. Confirm completion through a success message or an increased wish-list item count.
skills.when_to_apply: When the target product is not in the cart and the storefront page exposes a Search combobox. Stay within the current site; do not navigate to invented external search URLs.

skills.title: Verify Order Success Before Repeating
skills.principle: After selecting shipping and payment details, click “Place Order” once and wait for the page to settle. Check for a success indicator such as “Thank you for your purchase!” and an order number. Once shown, report completion and terminate instead of clicking the stale button again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use during checkout after the final order-submission action, especially when the page may load asynchronously or the accessibility tree still shows a busy state.

skills.title: Respect the Current Cart Contents
skills.principle: Verify the cart before checkout. If it is empty, do not select an arbitrary product to satisfy a request about the current items; report that checkout cannot proceed until items are supplied. If items are present, open the cart, confirm them, choose “Proceed to Checkout,” and continue only after each checkout step visibly advances.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to proceed with existing shopping-cart items and the cart page visibly says it has no items, or when checkout controls are available only after confirming the current cart contents.

skills.title: Browse More Products via Pagination
skills.principle: From a category listing, use the visible category or subcategory links to enter the relevant product set, then activate the pagination control labeled “Page Next” or a specific page number. Confirm completion by checking the heading or item range shows a later page, such as items beyond the initial results, before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse additional products and a category listing displays products plus pagination controls. Ensure the requested category is active, and verify the resulting page range changes after navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category Browsing
skills.principle: Open the requested category from the main navigation, verify that its page displays product listings, and stop once additional products are visible. Do not continue paging or changing filters unless the task explicitly requests browsing a larger range or specific subset.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking to browse a category when the category page is accessible and already shows multiple products; completion is indicated by the category heading and visible product listing.

skills.title: Check Cart Prerequisites First
skills.principle: Verify that the shopping cart contains items before evaluating shipping eligibility. If the page explicitly reports an empty cart, explain that no order can be assessed and that items must be added before checkout displays shipping options and costs.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked whether an order qualifies for free shipping and the cart page is accessible. Apply when the page visibly indicates the cart is empty or contains no items.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Checkout
skills.principle: Inspect the shopping cart for an item list or an empty-cart message before attempting checkout. If the page states that no items are present, explain that checkout cannot proceed and that an item must be added first; do not search for or activate checkout controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to proceed to checkout from a cart page, especially when the accessibility tree visibly reports that the cart is empty.

skills.title: Navigate Category Pagination Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested product category from the site navigation.
2. Inspect the category page’s heading and pagination controls to determine the current page.
3. Select the numbered link matching the requested page, or use the relevant Next control.
4. Confirm completion from the URL, heading item range, or pagination text showing the requested page before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring a specific page within a product category, after the category listing has loaded and exposes pagination controls or page-state indicators.

skills.title: Apply Nested Category Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level shopping category.
2. In its Shopping Options or Category section, select the requested subcategory rather than relying only on the page heading.
3. Confirm completion by checking the applied-filter area names the target subcategory and the results count or products update accordingly.
4. Report completion and stop once the filtered category is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests browsing a specific subcategory nested under a broader category and the page exposes category links or shopping filters.

skills.title: Verify Home Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and visible page landmarks before acting. If the URL is the site root and the page shows the store heading or product showcases, treat the goal as complete and report completion. Otherwise, use the current page’s store-logo link or Home breadcrumb to navigate, then verify the resulting URL and content.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open an e-commerce site’s home page, especially from a product or other internal page, and the current accessibility tree exposes the URL and recognizable home-page landmarks.

skills.title: Verify Category Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current page title, URL meaning, and visible category heading before taking navigation actions. If they already identify the requested category, report completion immediately. Otherwise, use the navigation menu item matching the requested category, then verify the resulting page heading or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to return to a shopping category and the current accessibility tree exposes page title, URL, or category heading. Avoid redundant navigation when the requested category is already displayed.

skills.title: Use the Visible Account Link
skills.principle: When the page exposes a clearly labeled “My Account” link, activate that navigation entry rather than searching or using a hard-coded URL. After navigation, verify completion by checking that the page URL or main heading identifies “My Account,” then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping pages when the task is to reach the account dashboard and the accessibility tree contains a visible “My Account” navigation link.

skills.title: Navigate by Visible Category Label
skills.principle: Select the navigation menu item whose accessible label matches the requested product category. After navigation, verify completion by checking that the page heading names the target category and displays its product listing or item count, then report completion without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to browse a category and the current page exposes that category in the main navigation menu. Verify the destination heading before stopping.

skills.title: Navigate Categories Through Visible Menu
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the category menu item by its visible label and click it. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the page heading, URL meaning, or category contents. Once the requested category is visibly loaded, report completion and stop without additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a shopping category from another store page, especially when the category is exposed as a visible navigation menu item and completion can be verified from the resulting page state.

skills.title: Use Direct Cart Navigation
skills.principle: When the cart link cannot be clicked because another element intercepts pointer events, navigate directly to the cart URL or equivalent cart route. Confirm the cart page loaded, then inspect its state: report each item with quantity and price, or report that the cart is empty when the page explicitly says no items are present.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to list shopping-cart contents and the cart link is obstructed, unreliable, or difficult to activate. Requires access to the site’s cart route or the visible cart link URL.

skills.title: Report Empty Cart Once
skills.principle: When the cart page explicitly states that no items are present, send one concise user-facing response such as “Your shopping cart is empty,” then terminate. Do not repeat the same message or issue further browser actions after the state is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when viewing a shopping cart whose accessibility tree shows an explicit empty-cart message and no product rows, quantities, or prices.

skills.title: Advance Checkout Using Next
skills.principle: On the Shipping step, ensure a shipping method is available and selected, then activate the section’s “Next” button rather than clicking the future “Review & Payments” navigation label. Confirm completion when the URL or page state changes to payment and shows “Payment Information” or “Place Order.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when checkout is on Shipping, the desired destination is Review & Payments, and the shipping-method area may initially be loading or show no quotes.

skills.title: Validate Cart Before Checkout
skills.principle: Check the cart contents before attempting checkout. If the page states that the cart is empty, explain that an item must be added before checkout can proceed, then stop rather than repeatedly messaging, navigating, or attempting an inaccessible checkout step. Continue only after the cart visibly contains an item.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach a checkout stage and the current cart page visibly says there are no items. This prerequisite must be satisfied before shipping, review, or payment steps can load.

skills.title: Build Cart Before Changing Shipping
skills.principle:
1. On a product listing, select an available item and click its contextual “Add to Cart” control.
2. Verify the cart indicator or success message updates, then activate the observed “My Cart” link.
3. In the cart, choose “Proceed to Checkout” and change shipping only after checkout displays shipping options.
4. After each action, reacquire the accessibility tree and use current labels or bids.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change shipping on a shopping site while viewing a product listing, especially when the cart is empty and shipping controls are not yet visible.

skills.title: Verify Displayed Shipping Address
skills.principle: Open the cart and expand “Estimate Shipping and Tax” if needed, then choose “Proceed to Checkout.” On the checkout Shipping step, read the rendered “Shipping Address” block—including name, street, city, region, postal code, and country—rather than attempting to fill static text. Report the displayed address and stop once it matches the requested order.
skills.when_to_apply: When verifying an order’s shipping address on a logged-in shopping site, especially after checkout exposes a display-only “Shipping Address” section rather than editable form fields.

skills.title: Use Order History for Address Verification
skills.principle: If the cart is empty while the user asks to verify an order’s shipping address, do not add arbitrary products or pursue checkout. Open “My Account,” locate the relevant order in order history, and inspect its order details for the shipping address. If no order is available, report that the address cannot be verified from the current account state.
skills.when_to_apply: When verifying an existing order’s shipping address and the checkout/cart page visibly states that no items are in the cart. Requires an authenticated account with accessible order history.

skills.title: Report Unavailable Shipping Quotes
skills.principle: When the checkout Shipping Methods section explicitly states that no quotes are available, treat that message as the result. Report that shipping methods and costs cannot currently be provided, then stop without attempting unrelated checkout actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a checkout shipping page when the shipping-method area is loaded and visibly reports that no quotes are available for the order.

skills.title: Report Results After Verification
skills.principle: Once the order detail page visibly shows the requested shipping method and the “Shipping & Handling” amount, provide those values in the final response immediately. Do not issue repeated no-op actions after verification; report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking shipping details for an existing order and the order detail page displays both “Shipping Method” and “Shipping & Handling” fields.

skills.title: Verify Cart Before Applying Discounts
skills.principle: Check whether the shopping cart contains items before attempting discount-code entry. If the page states the cart is empty, explain that adding an item is required and direct the user to the available continue-shopping link; do not attempt coupon application without cart contents.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to apply a discount code and the shopping-cart page is visible, especially when its state message indicates no items are present.

skills.title: Apply the Actual Discount Code
skills.principle:
1. Advance checkout from Shipping to Review & Payments using the available Next control.
2. Expand the “Apply Discount Code” tab, enter the exact user-provided coupon, and select “Apply Discount.”
3. Verify success through a confirmation message or changed order summary; if an invalid-code alert appears, obtain or recheck the real code rather than submitting placeholders.
skills.when_to_apply: When checkout is on Shipping and no coupon field is visible, proceed to Review & Payments first. Use only a discount code supplied by the user or otherwise available in the task context.

skills.title: Verify Cart Before Shipping Changes
skills.principle: Check the cart or order page before attempting shipping changes. If the page explicitly states that the cart is empty, recognize that no shipping method can be selected; explain that items must be added and checkout initiated before shipping options become available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change a shipping method and the current shopping cart or checkout page is visible; prerequisite: verify whether an active cart or order with items exists.

skills.title: Verify Alternative Shipping Options
skills.principle: Inspect the complete “Shipping Methods” list and select a different radio option only when one is visibly available. Confirm the selected method changes in the order summary. If the list contains only the current method, recognize that the checkout cannot fulfill the requested change and stop rather than repeatedly advancing, going back, or refreshing.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a shipping method during checkout, after the shipping address is loaded and the Shipping Methods section displays its available radio options.

skills.title: Check Cart State Before Calculation
skills.principle: Before verifying an order total, inspect the cart or order-details page for the required subtotal and shipping values. If the page explicitly says the cart is empty or the order details are absent, report that verification cannot be performed and identify the missing prerequisite instead of inferring or fabricating amounts.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to validate a shopping total but the current page may lack an active cart, order, subtotal, or shipping information.

skills.title: Use Checkout Controls To Reveal Totals
skills.principle: When repeated scrolling leaves the accessibility tree unchanged, stop scrolling and use the page’s structural controls. Expand the “Item in Cart” order-summary tab or activate “Next” to reach the review step, then read the displayed subtotal, shipping, and total. Compare the target total with the sum of the relevant charges and report whether it matches.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on checkout pages when subtotal or total is not visible after scrolling, especially when the accessibility tree remains unchanged and controls such as an order-summary tab or “Next” button are available.

skills.title: Inspect Checkout Payment Methods
skills.principle: Open the cart, choose “Proceed to Checkout,” complete the shipping step with “Next,” then inspect the “Payment Information” section under “Review & Payments.” Report every payment method visibly listed; if only one appears and no other payment controls are present, report it as the sole available method without placing the order.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which payment methods are available for an existing cart purchase and the cart contains at least one item; requires reaching the checkout’s “Review & Payments” step.

skills.title: Use Current Checkout Controls
skills.principle: On a cart page, inspect the current accessibility tree before acting. Select the visible "Proceed to Checkout" control by its role and label, then verify the checkout page and inspect its payment section. Do not reuse element IDs from earlier pages or guess that shipping, navigation, or hidden menu elements represent payment methods.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking available payment methods from an existing cart, especially after navigation, scrolling, or a failed click changes the page state. A cart with items and a visible checkout control is required.

skills.title: Use Semantic Controls, Not Stale IDs
skills.principle: On checkout, identify the control by its accessible name and role, not nearby or stale numeric IDs. Select the actual button labeled “Place Order,” then verify navigation to an order-confirmation state or another explicit success indicator before stopping. If the checkout page remains unchanged, re-inspect the current accessibility tree and target the newly observed button rather than repeating an incorrect element ID.
skills.when_to_apply: When completing a purchase and the accessibility tree contains multiple nearby elements or changing IDs, especially after checkout transitions or asynchronous updates.

skills.title: Verify Shipping Options Directly
skills.principle: On checkout’s “Shipping Methods” section, inspect the complete accessible table and count selectable radio options. If only one method is listed and its radio is checked, conclude that no alternative is available at this stage. Report that result instead of repeatedly scrolling or advancing checkout.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked whether the current checkout shipping method can be changed and the shipping-method table is visible, especially after returning via a “Shipping Method” edit control.

skills.title: Verify All Cart Quantities Before Ordering
skills.principle: Use the expanded cart summary to inspect every listed item and its displayed quantity. Confirm the number of cart entries matches the requested count, check each quantity explicitly, and report the verification once all entries are visible. Do not place the order unless ordering is requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to review cart contents or quantities before checkout, provided the cart summary is visible or can be expanded and lists the relevant items with quantities.

skills.title: Trust Cart Count Before Troubleshooting
skills.principle:
1. Open “My Cart” and “View and Edit Cart,” then inspect the cart table’s item rows and each “Qty” field.
2. Compare the displayed item count and rows with the requested count; do not assume missing items are hidden.
3. If the cart visibly contains fewer items, report the discrepancy or add the required items through product pages before verifying.
4. Stop once every required item and quantity is visibly confirmed; do not use “Update Shopping Cart,” “Continue Shopping,” or checkout as speculative refreshes.
skills.when_to_apply: When verifying cart contents before checkout, especially if the cart badge, cart table, or checkout summary displays fewer items than the task requests.

skills.title: Use the Store Logo for Homepage Navigation
skills.principle: From checkout, identify the site-wide store logo link or an explicit “continue shopping” homepage link. Activate one, then verify the resulting page has the root homepage URL and recognizable homepage content such as the store heading or product showcases. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires leaving checkout for the store homepage and the accessibility tree exposes a store logo, homepage link, or “continue shopping” link.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Then Stop
skills.principle: After activating a navigation control, inspect the updated page state before taking another action. Confirm completion using the URL, page title, or distinctive homepage content. If the target homepage is displayed, report completion and terminate instead of repeating clicks or exploring unrelated links.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from checkout or another shopping page to the store homepage, especially after clicking the store logo or another direct homepage link.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL, page title, and distinctive heading against the requested destination. If they already match, report that the destination is open and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated no-op actions or unnecessary navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a website or page and the initial accessibility tree already shows the requested site identity, URL, and relevant page heading.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Homepage
skills.principle: When the observed page already matches the requested homepage, verify the page title, URL, and distinctive homepage content once. Then report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly issuing noop actions, which may be invalid or trigger empty-action errors.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree already shows the requested site's homepage, including its expected title, root URL, and homepage content.

skills.title: Verify Account Page Before Continuing
skills.principle: Check the current page title and URL first. If already on the account page, confirm visible account settings and order-history sections, report completion, and stop. Otherwise, activate the visible “My Account” navigation link, then verify the destination page before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a signed-in shopping account page from an arbitrary starting page, especially when the accessibility tree may already show “My Account” or its account and recent-orders sections.

skills.title: Stop After Account Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Click the account-navigation link, then verify the destination by its “My Account” heading and visible account information or recent orders. Once these elements confirm the requested page is open, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an authenticated shopping site to account settings or order history, especially after the accessibility tree shows the “My Account” heading and relevant account or order sections.

skills.title: Verify Page State Before Retrying
skills.principle: After a navigation click times out, inspect the current URL and page heading before retrying. If they already show the requested category and its product listing, report completion and stop; do not repeat the navigation action.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a shopping category and a click reports a timeout or uncertain completion, especially when the browser may have finished navigation despite the error.

skills.title: Use the Visible Advanced Search Link
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree exposes an "Advanced Search" link, activate that role-labeled link rather than manipulating search fields. After navigation, verify the page title, URL path, or heading says "Advanced Search" and confirm the advanced criteria form is present before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: For shopping tasks requiring navigation to advanced product search, when an "Advanced Search" link is visible in the header or footer and the destination can be verified by its heading or form.

skills.title: Stop Once Advanced Search Opens
skills.principle: Navigate from the current page to the store homepage if needed, then activate the visible “Advanced Search” link. Verify the page heading reads “Advanced Search” and stop immediately; do not fill fields or submit a search unless the task explicitly requests search execution.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks only to navigate to Advanced Search and the accessibility tree shows the Advanced Search heading after activating its navigation link.

skills.title: Verify Advanced Search Page
skills.principle: Use the visible role-labeled “Advanced Search” link from the shopping page, then verify navigation succeeded by checking the page heading or URL. Once the Advanced Search form and its filters are visible, report completion without performing an unnecessary search.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a shopping site's advanced product search and the current accessibility tree exposes an “Advanced Search” link or navigation entry.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When the requested navigation target is visible and the page heading confirms it, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate; do not invent search values or perform extra form actions unless the user explicitly requested a search.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only shopping tasks when the observed page title, heading, or URL confirms the requested destination has loaded.

skills.title: Verify Shipping Address Through Address Book
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in customer’s “My Account” page and locate “Default Shipping Address.”
2. Select its “Edit Address” control to inspect all populated fields, including name, phone, street, country, state, city, and postal code.
3. If the fields are correct, select “Save Address” and confirm the resulting “You saved the address” message and updated Address Book entry.
4. Report verification only after the confirmation appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for signed-in shopping accounts when asked to verify a customer’s shipping address and the account exposes “Default Shipping Address,” “Edit Address,” and a save confirmation.

skills.title: Validate Page Context Before Selecting Elements
skills.principle: After navigation, confirm the page heading, URL, and relevant controls match the intended task before interacting. If a 404 or unrelated listing appears, stop using stale accessibility IDs and selectors; recover through visible navigation such as My Account or the cart, then re-inspect the new accessibility tree. Only click elements whose role and label are actually present.
skills.when_to_apply: When verifying account or shipping details and navigation lands on an error page, unrelated page, or changed accessibility tree. Re-inspect before choosing selectors, especially after URL navigation or failed clicks.

skills.title: Read Empty Cart Status Directly
skills.principle: On the shopping cart or order-summary page, inspect visible status text before interacting with controls. If it states that there are no items, interpret this as a cart count of zero, report the count, and stop because the task is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for the cart’s item count and the current shopping-cart page visibly shows an empty-cart message such as “You have no items in your shopping cart.”

skills.title: Report Empty Cart as Zero
skills.principle: When the cart page explicitly says there are no items, interpret the count as 0 and report that directly. Do not claim the request is impossible or repeat failed message actions; send one valid completion message and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when checking cart quantity and the shopping-cart view visibly states that no items are present. Ensure the outbound response contains the actual user-facing message, not only an action name.

skills.title: Read Cart Subtotal
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the visible “My Cart” control. Read the amount paired with “Cart Subtotal” in the cart preview or cart page, then report that amount as the order’s total cost. Once the amount is confirmed, stop without additional navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the total cost of an existing order and the shopping page shows a cart control, especially with a nonempty item count. Verify the subtotal label and currency amount before responding.

skills.title: Target Cart Link Precisely
skills.principle: Use the element’s accessible role and name, not a nearby or stale element ID. Select the link labeled “My Cart” (the cart navigation link), dismissing any active search overlay first. After clicking, verify the URL or page heading changed to the cart page, then read the displayed grand total or order total.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking an order total from a product or category page, especially if the search field is focused or accessibility-tree IDs have shifted. Confirm the cart page loaded before extracting a monetary value.

skills.title: Check Cart Preconditions Before Applying Codes
skills.principle: Before applying a discount code, inspect the cart state. If the page explicitly says the cart has no items, do not search for checkout code controls; report that an item must be added first. If items are present, proceed to checkout and apply the code there.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for discount-code tasks when the current shopping-cart or checkout page is visible. First verify that at least one cart item exists, since an empty cart prevents code application.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Browser Actions
skills.principle: When a browser action returns an empty-action or parsing error, do not repeat the identical malformed command. Re-read the current accessibility tree, then issue a correctly serialized action targeting the visible control by role or label. After entering a discount code, activate “Apply Discount” and verify a success message or updated order summary.
skills.when_to_apply: Use during checkout when a visible discount-code textbox and apply button exist but the action repeatedly produces an empty-action or serialization error.

skills.title: Verify Payment Options Before Changing
skills.principle: On a checkout payment step, scroll until the complete Payment Information section is visible. Inspect the accessibility tree for selectable controls such as radio buttons, dropdowns, or change links. If only one payment method appears as a static label and no alternative control is exposed, report that the requested change is unavailable on this page and suggest returning to an earlier checkout step or contacting the store.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change payment method during checkout, especially after reaching the payment section and seeing one displayed method without visible alternative selectors.

skills.title: Handle Empty Payment Methods State
skills.principle: When “Stored Payment Methods” explicitly says no methods are stored and exposes no add, edit, or delete control, treat the page as non-actionable. Stop repeating no-op actions or revisiting it; return to the active cart or checkout payment step to select another option, if available. Otherwise report that the requested change cannot be completed from the accessible account settings.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a shopping payment method and the account’s stored-payment page shows an empty-state message without any actionable payment controls.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Item Details
skills.principle: Check the shopping cart page for the requested item before attempting to open details. If the page explicitly shows that the cart is empty, treat the request as unavailable and clearly report that no item details can be viewed; do not perform unrelated navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect a specific cart item and the cart page is already open or accessible. Use the empty-cart status message as the prerequisite check before searching for item controls.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Searching Further
skills.principle: Expand the cart summary and compare the target against every listed product name. Use the displayed item count and complete list as evidence; if the target is absent, stop searching, report that it is not in the current cart, and suggest checking cart or order history rather than repeatedly scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product’s cart details and the checkout order summary is available. First expand the item list and confirm the target appears before attempting to open its details.

skills.title: Set a Different Billing Address
skills.principle:
1. In checkout payment details, uncheck “My billing and shipping address are the same.”
2. Choose “New Address” in the Billing Address selector.
3. Fill every required billing field, including street, country, state/province, city, postal code, and phone.
4. Click “Update” and verify the saved billing address appears while the checkbox remains unchecked.
skills.when_to_apply: When checkout currently links billing to shipping and the task requires a separate billing address. Ensure the payment section is visible and the requested billing details are available.

skills.title: Verify Saved Address and Stop
skills.principle: After saving an account address, inspect the resulting Address Book page for a confirmation such as “You saved the address” and verify billing and shipping entries differ. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a shopping-account billing address and the save action returns to the address book or displays a success alert.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Editing
skills.principle: Before changing an item’s options, inspect the cart for the target item and confirm its current configuration. If the page explicitly says the cart is empty or the item is absent, do not attempt an edit; report the missing prerequisite and explain that the item must be added first.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping task requests modifying a cart item’s size, color, quantity, or other option and the cart page is already open or accessible.

skills.title: Verify Cart Item Before Editing
skills.principle: Inspect the expanded cart contents and confirm the target product is present before editing. If a different product appears, leave checkout and open the cart or product page to locate the target. Use the item’s product edit control for size changes; checkout address “Edit” only changes billing information. Verify the displayed size changes to the requested value before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a product variant from a checkout page, especially if the order summary is collapsed or shows an unexpected item. The cart must contain the intended product and expose a product-specific edit control.

skills.title: Verify Target Before Removing
skills.principle: Open the full shopping cart, inspect each item row by name, and use that row’s “Remove item” control only when it matches the requested product. If the target is absent, confirm the cart contents and current item count, then report that it is not present and stop; never remove a different item or reuse stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to remove a specific cart item, especially after starting on checkout or a mini-cart overlay. First reach the Shopping Cart page and wait for its current accessibility tree before acting.

skills.title: Use the Store Logo as Home Navigation
skills.principle: Locate the header link labeled “store logo” in the current accessibility tree and click that link, rather than relying on a remembered element ID. Confirm completion when the resulting URL is the site root or the page heading identifies the storefront homepage, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires returning to the store homepage from another page and the header exposes a logo link. Re-read the current accessibility tree because element IDs can change after navigation.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Then Stop
skills.principle: After clicking a navigation control, inspect the updated page state before acting again. If the URL is the site root and the homepage heading or content is visible, treat the task as complete, report completion, and terminate instead of repeating the click.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires navigating via a store logo or similar link, especially after the page updates and the accessibility tree shows the intended homepage.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Viewing Details
skills.principle: Open the cart and inspect its state before attempting item actions. If the page explicitly says the cart has no items, report that the requested details cannot be viewed and stop. If items are listed, select the requested item or its details control and confirm the resulting product-detail view.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage an item in a shopping cart, especially after arriving from a product listing. The cart page must first be checked for an empty-cart message or visible item entries.

skills.title: Use Stable Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When an accessibility-tree control is visible, use its numeric bid (for example, the bid attached to the “My Cart” link) rather than passing its name or icon text as a bid. Issue one valid click action, then verify navigation by checking the URL or cart-page heading before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a visible link or button repeatedly fails to activate because text or icon-based selectors are rejected, and the latest accessibility tree provides a numeric bid and destination URL.

skills.title: Open Cart Discount Section
skills.principle:
1. Ensure the cart contains an item, then open the cart from the cart link.
2. Locate and expand the “Apply Discount Code” tab in the cart summary.
3. Confirm the “Enter discount code” textbox and “Apply Discount” button are visible; stop once the section is open unless a code was requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a shopping site’s promotional-code area and the current page lacks that control. A nonempty cart is required if the discount section appears only in the cart.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Section
skills.principle: When the task asks only to navigate to a checkout section, locate and expand the relevant tab, verify its heading and controls are visible, then stop. Do not enter, submit, or test promotional codes unless explicitly requested; report completion once the section is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for checkout navigation tasks where the requested destination is an expandable section such as “Apply Discount Code,” and success is observable when its panel and input controls appear.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: After navigation, verify the page heading and relevant content match the requested destination. Once the goal is visibly achieved, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task reaches a page whose heading, URL, or content clearly confirms the requested destination, especially after an initial click succeeds.

skills.title: Stop At Checkout Confirmation
skills.principle: When the task asks to view the cart and proceed to checkout, click “My Cart,” verify its contents, then select “Proceed to Checkout.” Once the Checkout page appears, report completion and stop; do not select shipping, place an order, or continue shopping unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks whose endpoint is entering checkout. After selecting “Proceed to Checkout,” confirm the page heading or checkout URL is visible before terminating.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: After selecting the requested shopping category, verify the page heading, URL, and visible product listings confirm the category. Treat that state as successful browsing; stop rather than repeatedly scrolling. If more products are explicitly needed, use the page-size selector or pagination links and verify that the displayed item range changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks only to browse or navigate to a category and the accessibility tree shows the requested category heading with product listings. Use pagination or page-size controls only when additional items are required.

skills.title: Open Product Details from Listings
skills.principle: From an empty cart, use the “continue shopping” link to reach the storefront. Locate the target product by matching its visible name in the product list, then click its product-name link or image. Confirm navigation succeeded when the page title and main heading identify the requested product and its details are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a shopping product’s detail page and the current page is an empty cart or storefront listing. Use the visible product identity rather than a hard-coded element ID.

skills.title: Stop After Details Are Visible
skills.principle: Once the target product detail page is open and the relevant “Details” tab is expanded with product information visible, verify the page title and details content, then report completion and terminate. Do not continue scrolling or perform unrelated actions unless the requested information is not yet visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a product’s detail page or view more information, especially after search results lead to a page showing the target title and an expanded details section.

skills.title: Determine Cart Quantity From Visible Items
skills.principle: Inspect the cart’s item table for the requested product and read its associated quantity control or quantity text. If the product is absent, verify the cart contains only other items and report the requested quantity as zero. Use the cart item count as supporting evidence, not as a substitute for matching the product.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a product’s shopping-cart quantity and the shopping cart page is visible, especially when the requested product may be absent or the cart contains multiple items.

skills.title: Use Semantic Cart Navigation
skills.principle: When a recorded element ID resolves to the wrong control or click events are intercepted, stop retrying the stale ID. Locate the cart link by its accessible name and href, or navigate directly to the observed cart URL. On the cart page, inspect the item table for an exact product-name match and read that row’s quantity control before reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening a shopping cart from a page with ambiguous or stale accessibility IDs, especially after a click timeout or pointer-interception error; the cart URL or accessible cart link must be observable.

skills.title: Expand Discount Section Before Locating Fields
skills.principle: On the cart page, activate the accessible “Apply Discount Code” tab or accordion using its observed role and name. Verify that it expands, then inspect the updated accessibility tree for the discount-code textbox and apply button. Enter the provided code, submit it, and confirm a success message or updated discount and total. Do not construct selectors from accessibility-tree IDs or guessed child descriptions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a cart shows “Apply Discount Code” as collapsed or exposes no discount textbox. Expand the section first, then use freshly observed accessible names or roles to interact with its controls.

skills.title: Verify Cart State Before Editing
skills.principle:
1. Open the cart and distinguish a mini-cart dialog from the full cart page; navigate to the actual cart view if needed.
2. If the full cart shows the target item, use that row’s Remove control.
3. If it shows “You have no items,” treat the target as already absent; do not add it merely to remove it.
4. Confirm the target row is gone or the empty-cart message remains before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to remove a product from a shopping cart, especially when clicking “My Cart” opens an overlay instead of changing pages. Keep the cart unchanged if the target is already absent.

skills.title: Verify Cart Item Before Removing
skills.principle: Inspect the shopping cart’s item table and match the requested product by its displayed name before using its associated “Remove item” control. If no matching row exists, do not remove another product; clearly report that the requested item is absent and ask whether the user wants a different item removed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to remove a specific product from a shopping cart, especially when the cart may contain different items or the requested product may already be absent.

skills.title: Remove Items Directly From Cart
