skills.principle: Open the shopping cart first rather than searching the product catalog. Locate the exact requested item in the cart, activate its item-level “Remove” control, and verify the cart refreshes without that item before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for cart-removal tasks when the user identifies a product. Start from “My Cart” or the cart page; catalog search results do not establish whether an item is currently in the cart.

skills.title: Check Cart Before Shipping Methods
skills.principle: Verify that the shopping cart contains items before attempting to view shipping methods. If it is empty, explain that the user must add an item, proceed to checkout, and provide a shipping address before shipping options can be displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view order shipping methods and the cart page visibly states that there are no items in the cart.

skills.title: Verify Cart State Before Checkout
skills.principle: Inspect the current accessibility tree before acting. Confirm the cart contains items; if it is empty, add or restore the target order first. Then activate the actual checkout control by its current semantic label, not a stale element ID, and verify that the page changes to checkout before searching for shipping methods.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view shipping methods and the current page may be a product listing, cart, or checkout page. A non-empty cart and, where required, shipping-address information must be available.

skills.title: Use Exact UI Targets and Verify State
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s exact element identifier or navigate to the observed destination URL; do not substitute visible text for a bid. After navigation, verify the URL and page heading. For shipping changes, confirm the cart contains the relevant order before looking for shipping controls; if it is empty, report that the prerequisite is missing instead of repeating clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing shipping details from a shopping site, especially after a click fails or the cart page displays “You have no items in your shopping cart.”

skills.title: Verify Shipping From Cart Summary
skills.principle: Open the cart’s “Estimate Shipping and Tax” section and provide the destination if required. Inspect the resulting Summary table: a “Shipping” row with a nonzero charge means the order does not qualify for free shipping; a zero charge or explicit “Free Shipping” indicates qualification. Report the observed status and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking an existing order’s shipping eligibility from a shopping cart, especially when the cart exposes “Estimate Shipping and Tax” and a Summary table with shipping and order-total rows.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents First
skills.principle: Check the cart’s visible contents before attempting to open a product’s details. If the page explicitly states that the cart is empty, report that the requested item cannot be viewed and explain that it must first be added to the cart.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect an item supposedly in a shopping cart, especially when the cart page is already open and displays an empty-cart message.

skills.title: Open And Verify Cart Contents
skills.principle:
1. Click the cart control once and inspect the resulting state; a minicart may open without changing the URL.
2. If a minicart appears, activate “View and Edit Cart” to reach the full cart page.
3. Compare visible product names against the requested item, then click that item’s product link to view details.
4. If the requested item is absent, report that instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product already in a shopping cart, especially when clicking “My Cart” opens a minicart overlay rather than navigating to the full cart.

skills.title: Verify Navigation After Click Timeout
skills.principle: When a navigation click reports a timeout, inspect the refreshed page state before retrying. If the URL, page title, heading, or displayed content confirms the requested destination, treat the navigation as successful, report completion, and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking a category or navigation entry when the browser reports a timeout but may have completed navigation; verify destination indicators before taking another action.

skills.title: Use Visible Category Navigation
skills.principle: When the requested category is visible in the cart page’s navigation menu, activate that category menu item directly. An empty cart does not prevent navigation. If it has a submenu, expand it and select the requested category; verify the resulting page reflects that category before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when starting from a shopping cart or similar page where the requested category appears as a visible navigation menu item, regardless of whether the cart contains products.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Continuing
skills.principle: Use the shopping cart’s visible account-navigation link to open the requested account page. After navigation, verify completion by checking both the page heading and URL for the requested destination. If they already match, report success and stop rather than performing additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from a shopping cart or similar page to an account destination, especially when the current page may already be the requested destination.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the destination page is visibly confirmed—such as the expected page title and URL appearing—stop issuing browser actions. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of repeatedly calling noop or waiting for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after navigation tasks when the accessibility tree confirms the requested destination and no further interaction is required.

skills.title: Check Order Details for Delivery Estimates
skills.principle: Open the account’s order history, identify the target order, and select its “View Order” control. Inspect the order status and details for an explicit estimated delivery date. If no date appears—especially while status is “Pending”—report that the estimate is unavailable without inferring one, then stop after sending the response.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks for an order’s estimated delivery date and the user is logged in with access to account order history and individual order-detail pages.

skills.title: Use Existing Order History
skills.principle: For delivery-date questions, treat the cart as insufficient evidence. Open “My Account” → “My Orders,” identify the target order, and inspect its order or shipment details for an estimated delivery date. Do not place a new order merely to reveal delivery information; if no estimate appears, report that it is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks about an existing order but the current page is a cart or checkout page, especially before any order-confirmation or tracking estimate is visible.

skills.title: Open Advanced Search From Cart
skills.principle: From the shopping cart, activate the visible “Advanced Search” link rather than navigating through unrelated pages. Verify the Advanced Search heading and its search fields are visible. If the cart must remain open, use the cart control to open its dialog without leaving the advanced-search page, then confirm both states before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requires viewing advanced search options while the cart is open; the cart control and an “Advanced Search” link must be visible, and completion requires verifying the destination fields and cart dialog.

skills.title: Navigate From the Requested Context
skills.principle: Start from the page specified by the task, such as the shopping cart, rather than an equivalent link on another page. From the cart, locate and activate the relevant “Advanced Search” navigation entry, then verify the Advanced Search heading and search fields are displayed before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task specifies navigating from a particular page or workflow context and the same destination is also available elsewhere. First open the required source page, then use its navigation and verify the resulting page state.

skills.title: Use Continue Shopping To Return Home
skills.principle: From the shopping cart, activate the clearly labeled “Continue Shopping” link rather than unrelated checkout controls. Confirm completion when the resulting page’s URL is the site root and its content shows the store homepage or product showcases, then stop and report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires returning from the cart or checkout area to continue browsing, and the current accessibility tree exposes a “Continue Shopping” control linking to the store homepage.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Homepage
skills.principle: After navigating toward the homepage, inspect the updated page state. If the URL is the site root and the homepage heading or product content is visible, treat the goal as complete, report completion, and terminate instead of clicking the same homepage link again.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to return to a shopping site's homepage and the post-navigation observation already shows the site root URL and recognizable homepage content.

skills.title: Use Visible Account Navigation
skills.principle: Identify the visible navigation link labeled “My Account” and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading or URL indicates “My Account” and account sections such as contact information, addresses, or orders are visible; then report completion without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open an authenticated shopping site’s account page and the current accessibility tree shows a visible “My Account” link or equivalent account navigation entry.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Click Actions
skills.principle: When a visible link is correct but the tool reports an empty action, inspect the serialized command before retrying. Emit a complete, valid action; if repeated clicks fail, use the link’s observed destination URL directly. Verify navigation by checking the page heading, URL, or distinctive content before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a BrowserGym click repeatedly returns an empty-action or parsing error despite the target being present in the accessibility tree, especially when the link exposes a clear destination URL.

skills.title: Verify Wishlist State Before Reporting
skills.principle: Open the account’s “My Wish List” navigation entry, then inspect the page for its heading and item-status text. If it explicitly states that no items are present, report the wishlist as empty and stop; otherwise summarize the displayed wishlist contents.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a signed-in shopper’s wishlist and the page provides a “My Wish List” navigation link or equivalent account control.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target page is visibly confirmed—for example, the “My Wish List” heading and listed items appear—report completion and terminate immediately. Do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional observations after the requested view is already displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a browsing task asks only to view or open a page and the current accessibility tree already shows the requested page content and completion indicators.

skills.title: Open Cart Item Details
skills.principle: From the shopping cart, locate the target item by its product name or image link and activate it. Confirm completion when the product page shows the matching product heading and detail section; if the cart mini-dialog already exposes name, price, and quantity, use those visible details and report completion without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a product currently in the cart and the cart lists the target item or its cart mini-dialog is already open.

skills.title: Stop After Product Details Load
skills.principle: From the cart, activate the target item’s product-name link. When the resulting page shows the product heading and detail content such as price, stock, or description, the task is complete; report completion and terminate instead of navigating back to the cart or repeating clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view cart-item details and the product page has loaded with an identifiable product heading and detail section.

skills.title: Verify Category Navigation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Select the navigation entry matching the requested shopping category, then confirm the destination by checking the page heading, URL meaning, and visible product listings. Report completion only after these indicators show the requested category page is active.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse a store category and the initial page exposes category navigation. After selecting the category, verify the resulting page contains the category heading and product results.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the requested category page is open, verify the page heading or breadcrumb names the target category and the product listing is present. Treat that state as completion, report success, and stop instead of repeatedly scrolling when no specific product or detail was requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requesting only category browsing, especially when the page shows the target category heading, breadcrumb, and product listings after navigation.

skills.title: Update Cart Quantity Explicitly
skills.principle:
1. Open the cart and identify the target item’s quantity control.
2. Set the quantity to the requested value.
3. Click “Update Shopping Cart” to apply the change; editing the field alone may not persist it.
4. Verify the displayed quantity and subtotal reflect the requested update before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping-cart quantity changes when the target item is present. If the cart is empty, add the intended product first, then open the cart and continue.

skills.title: Clarify Cart Changes Before Checkout
skills.principle: For an ambiguous cart-update request, open the observed “My Cart” link and inspect item names, quantities, and available controls. Change only explicitly requested quantities or items, then click “Update Shopping Cart” and verify the resulting quantity, subtotal, or item list. If no concrete change is specified, ask for clarification instead of assuming checkout or navigating through shipping steps.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task says to update cart items but omits which item or quantity, especially when the cart page offers quantity fields, removal controls, and checkout links.

skills.title: Open Product Reviews and Report Findings
skills.principle:
1. Identify the exact target product in search results using its full title or distinguishing details.
2. Open the product page and select the “Reviews” link or tab, especially when it shows a review count.
3. Read the visible review text, rating, and relevant metadata, then report the findings accurately.
4. Once the review is confirmed and reported, stop without interacting with review-submission fields.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read reviews for a specific product on a shopping site, after locating the matching product page and confirming a Reviews control or review count.

skills.title: Use the Actual Review Link
skills.principle: On a search-results page, identify the target product by its visible title, then activate that product’s nearby review-count link (for example, “1 Review”), not the surrounding rating container or product-title identifier. After clicking, verify that the product page or reviews section appears before continuing. If the action errors, re-inspect the current accessibility tree and choose the currently exposed link by role and text instead of repeating the same selector.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read reviews from a product listing, especially when multiple products show similar ratings or review links and a previous click fails or leaves the page unchanged.

skills.title: Add the Correct Search Result
skills.principle: Identify the target product by its visible name within the search-results item container, then activate that item's associated “Add to Cart” button. Wait for the interface to update and confirm completion through a changed “Added” state, cart-count increase, or success alert. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search-results page shows the requested product alongside multiple similarly labeled “Add to Cart” buttons, and the product can be matched by its visible name.

skills.title: Use the Exact Search Input Bid
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree identifies a search combobox, use that input’s current bid—not its label, icon, or adjacent Advanced Search link. Fill the combobox with the target product, then submit using the enabled Search button or Enter. Confirm the results page contains the target item before selecting its Add to Cart control.
skills.when_to_apply: On shopping pages where the target product is not visible in the current listing and the accessibility tree exposes a labeled search combobox with a distinct input bid.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Product Categories
skills.principle: Select the navigation entry matching the requested category, then verify the resulting page using its URL and heading. Once the category page is confirmed, report the visible product count and available browsing controls, and stop rather than taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests opening a product category from search results or another catalog page, especially when the target category is already visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Category Navigation and Stop
skills.principle:
1. Click the requested category entry and verify the resulting heading, URL, or breadcrumb names the target category.
2. For exploration, inspect the displayed product range or use pagination deliberately; confirm the item range changes after navigation.
3. Once the requested category page is reached and additional exploration is satisfied, report completion and terminate instead of repeating no-ops or scrolling without new content.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open or explore a shopping category, especially after pagination or scrolling. Verify the visible category heading and item range before deciding whether further actions are necessary.

skills.title: Use Direct Category Navigation
skills.principle: If a category menu click repeatedly fails or produces an action error, navigate using the category link discovered in the page or its semantic URL. Verify completion by checking the address, page title, and category heading, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping category is visible but menu interaction fails, element identifiers are malformed or stale, and the target category URL can be reliably inferred from the observed navigation.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Continuing
skills.principle: Use the currently observed menu item for the requested category, then verify the page heading and URL show that category. If the target page is confirmed, stop and report completion. Do not repeat clicks, use stale element IDs, or manually guess a URL after success; if navigation fails, re-observe the current accessibility tree before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from search results or another catalog page to a named shopping category, especially after a click changes the URL or page heading.

skills.title: Use Inline Add-to-Cart Controls
skills.principle: On a shopping search-results page, locate the result whose accessible name matches the requested product, then activate that result’s adjacent “Add to Cart” button directly. Wait for the button to change to “Added” or for the cart indicator to update; once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When the exact requested product is visible in a search-results list and its result card exposes an inline “Add to Cart” control, especially when the cart may already contain other items.

skills.title: Stop After Cart Confirmation
skills.principle: After clicking the target product’s “Add to Cart,” wait for the button to show “Added” and verify the target item appears in the cart. Once the requested item is present, report completion and terminate; do not change its quantity, proceed to checkout, or interact with unrelated controls unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks that only require adding a specified product to the cart, especially when the cart already contains items or the add button changes to “Added.”

skills.title: Use Advanced Search Count
skills.principle: Open the shopping site's Advanced Search, enter the target term in the Product Name field, and submit Search. On the results page, use the explicit summary stating how many items were found, rather than counting visible products or pages. Report that total when the search criteria and item count are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the total number of products matching a term and the site provides Advanced Search with a Product Name field and a results-summary count.

skills.title: Read the Explicit Result Total
skills.principle: On a product search results page, use the explicit result summary such as “1–N of TOTAL” as the authoritative count. Do not multiply the visible page size by the number of pagination links, because only a subset of page links may be shown. Report TOTAL after confirming it belongs to the requested search or filter.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the total number of products matching a search or filter and the page displays an explicit result-range summary. Ensure the query or filter matches the user’s requested item set.

skills.title: Read Price Directly From Search Results
skills.principle: When the target product appears in a shopping search-results list, identify its exact product-name link and read the price displayed within the same product entry. Report that value directly without opening the product page or performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for price-check tasks when the search-results accessibility tree visibly contains the requested product and an adjacent price in its list item.

skills.title: Inspect Search Results Before Paging
skills.principle: After executing a product search, scan the current results list for an exact-name match before scrolling or changing pages. Read the price adjacent to that matching product, then report it and stop. Use the product name and control role from the latest accessibility tree rather than stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping price checks when search results are displayed. The target may already appear near the top, even if the agent initially assumes it is absent.

skills.title: Verify Catalog Results Before Concluding
skills.principle: Scan the current product listings for the requested item and sale indicators. If no match appears, inspect the accessibility tree for an actual pagination control before attempting navigation. If no usable next-page control exists, report that no matching sale item appears in the current results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when checking whether a specific product or attribute is available on a shopping catalog page, especially when the page shows a product showcase and pagination may be absent or stale.

skills.title: Verify Explicit Sale Indicators
skills.principle: Search for the target product, then inspect product cards for explicit sale evidence such as a sale label, crossed-out original price, discount percentage, or reduced-price display. Do not treat a merely low price as a sale. Check available result pages or relevant filters efficiently, then report the matching item(s) or that no explicit sale was shown.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked whether a product category or search result contains sale items, especially when results show prices but no obvious discount metadata.

skills.title: Use Observed Element Identifiers
skills.principle: When a semantic locator fails, inspect the current accessibility tree and use the displayed element identifier for the intended control. For product-price searches: focus the observed search combobox, replace its contents with the exact product name, activate the enabled Search button, then verify the results contain the exact product and its adjacent price.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping search pages when a guessed locator fails or the page has dynamic controls. Prerequisite: the accessibility tree exposes the search field, search control, and result listings.

skills.title: Search Product and Verify Listed Price
skills.principle:
1. Enter the complete target product name in the store’s Search field.
2. Submit the search and wait for the results page.
3. Identify the result whose title exactly matches the target product, then read the price displayed in that same product listing.
4. Report the price and stop once the matching listing and price are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product’s price when the storefront provides a Search field and results listings showing product titles with prices.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Native Sort Dropdowns
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the requested product category or apply its category filter.
2. Inspect the labeled “Sort By” combobox and open it if needed.
3. Use the select-option operation on the combobox rather than clicking an individual native option, which may be invisible.
4. Verify the selected value and refreshed URL or product ordering before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing sorting on a catalog or search-results page with a native HTML select, especially after directly clicking an option fails because the option is not visible.

skills.title: Filter Category Before Sorting
skills.principle: On a search-results page, first select the requested category (for example, via the sidebar category link) so the result set is scoped correctly. Then use the page’s “Sort By” combobox to choose “Price,” wait for reload, and verify the selected value is “Price” within the filtered category.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change sorting for a specific product category from a broad search-results page, especially when category links and a “Sort By” control are both visible.

skills.title: Use Advanced Search for Price Filtering
skills.principle:
1. Narrow results with the relevant category link, such as “Beauty & Personal Care,” rather than treating a broad search as the target set.
2. Open “Advanced Search” and enter the requested minimum and maximum prices in its price fields.
3. Submit the form and verify the results page reflects both the category and price constraints before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping results page lacks visible price facets but provides category links and an “Advanced Search” link. Use this before manually inspecting products or altering wishlist/cart contents.

skills.title: Search Then Verify Product Details
skills.principle:
1. Replace any stale search query with the exact target product name and submit it.
2. From the results, open the listing whose title exactly matches the target.
3. On the product page, read the prominently displayed SKU and the Manufacturer row in the details table.
4. Report both values only after confirming they belong to the matching product page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use shopping sites when the initial page has an unrelated query and the task asks for product metadata such as SKU and manufacturer. Ensure the exact product listing is available before extracting details.

skills.title: Use Current Search Input Bid
skills.principle: When searching a Magento catalog, target the visible search input’s current accessibility bid (for example, the element exposing role `combobox`), not the generic role name or its label. Fill the input, activate the enabled `Search` button, and verify the page heading and product results reflect the requested query before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on catalog search pages when generic role-based locators fail or a label click is intercepted by the input. Re-read the accessibility tree after navigation because bids can change between pages.

skills.title: Use Click for Category Links
skills.principle: When a category appears as a navigation menuitem backed by an anchor link, use click rather than select_option. After clicking, verify the page URL or heading names the requested category; if already confirmed, stop without repeating navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating a shopping site from a search or catalog page and the accessibility tree identifies the target category as a menuitem/link, not a native select element.

skills.title: Terminate After Verified Navigation
skills.principle: After clicking the target category, verify completion using the page title, heading, or URL. Once the target category is clearly displayed, provide the completion response and terminate the interaction; do not issue repeated no-op actions or continue polling the unchanged page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when a click has produced a page whose title, heading, or URL matches the requested category or destination.

skills.title: Use the Store Logo for Home
skills.principle: When starting from another shopping page, identify a visible link whose destination is the site root, such as the store logo or a labeled Home link. Activate it, then confirm the URL is the root and the page shows homepage content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping task requires navigating to the home page and the current accessibility tree exposes a store logo or Home link pointing to the site root.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Navigation Actions
skills.principle: Emit the browser action as a complete tool call, not as nested JSON or a truncated string. For navigation, use the observed Home link or store-logo destination. After execution, verify the URL or page heading changed to the home page. If the same action-format error recurs, stop retrying it and use the destination URL directly.
skills.when_to_apply: When a visible navigation link is available but the browser reports an empty-action or parsing error, especially when the submitted action appears truncated or double-encoded.

skills.title: Verify View State Before Switching
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the view controls and identify which option is highlighted or rendered as non-clickable.
2. If the requested view is already active, report completion without clicking or performing extra actions.
3. Otherwise, activate the clickable control for the requested view and confirm the page state, such as the selected label or updated URL parameter.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping search or category pages when asked to change Grid/List presentation and the current view controls are visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify View Mode Before Clicking
skills.principle: On a product-results page, distinguish the active mode from the switch control: the active mode appears as emphasized text, while the opposite mode is the clickable “View as …” link. Click the List link only when Grid is active, then verify List is emphasized or the page state includes list mode. Once confirmed, stop instead of toggling the view again.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing Grid/List display on shopping search or category results pages, especially after a page refresh or navigation where accessibility-tree element IDs may change.

skills.title: Search and Open the Matching Product
skills.principle:
1. Replace any unrelated existing query with the requested product name in the shopping site's Search field.
2. Submit using the enabled Search control and wait for results whose heading reflects the requested query.
3. Select a result whose product title explicitly matches the requested item, then confirm the product-page heading and details are visible.
4. Once the matching product page is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific product page and the current shopping page has an unrelated query or search-results list. Requires a visible Search field and product links in the resulting list.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Target Page
skills.principle: Once the page heading, URL, or other content clearly matches the requested product, treat navigation as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately; do not emit repeated no-op actions or wait for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigating to a requested product page when the accessibility tree visibly confirms the target item and its product details. This is especially important when the browser task has no further interaction requirement.

skills.title: Verify Results Before Repeating Actions
skills.principle:
1. Fill the advanced-search minimum and maximum price fields, then submit the form.
2. After any click timeout, inspect the current URL and page content before retrying.
3. Treat a results page showing the requested price criterion and matching item prices as completion evidence; report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping sites with advanced-search price-range fields, especially when form submission may navigate successfully despite a click or navigation timeout.

skills.title: Filter Products Directly From Listings
skills.principle: Read each listing item's displayed name and price, keep items whose prices fall within the requested inclusive range, and continue through every pagination control until all results are checked. Use the listing page rather than opening product details unless necessary. Report the qualifying products; do not add items to the cart unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find or list products matching a price range on a shopping category or showcase page, especially when prices are already visible and pagination indicates additional results.

skills.title: Use Advanced Search Field
skills.principle: On a catalog’s Advanced Search page, enter the requested keyword in the field matching the target attribute, such as Description, then activate Search. Confirm completion on the results page by checking the applied criterion and displayed result count before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks for products matching a specific catalog attribute and the accessibility tree exposes corresponding Advanced Search fields and a Search button.

skills.title: Stop After Search Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the search form is submitted, verify the results page shows the requested criterion and a result count. If confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not browse additional result pages unless the task explicitly requires inspecting or selecting a product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for product-search tasks when the results page visibly echoes the requested filter and reports matching items. Pagination is unnecessary unless the instruction asks for specific products or exhaustive review.

skills.title: Use Visible Footer Policy Links
skills.principle: When a requested informational page is not in the main navigation, inspect the page accessibility tree for matching footer links. Activate the link by its visible label or role, then verify the destination through the page heading, title, URL, and relevant content before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when navigating a shopping site to policies, terms, contact, or other informational pages and the current accessibility tree exposes the target as a footer link.

skills.title: Terminate After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Once navigation reaches the requested page, verify the page heading or URL matches the goal, report completion, and terminate the task immediately. Do not issue repeated no-op actions after the success state is already observable.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for direct navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree shows the requested page title or destination URL after a successful click or navigation.

skills.title: Use Advanced Search Price Ranges
skills.principle:
1. Open the shopping site's Advanced Search form and locate the two Price fields.
2. Enter the requested minimum and maximum values in the corresponding fields.
3. Activate the form's Search button.
4. Confirm completion when the results page states the matching price range and displays filtered products or a result count.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests products within a numeric price interval and the site exposes an Advanced Search form with separate lower and upper Price inputs.

skills.title: Fill Price Bounds Separately
skills.principle: On an advanced product search form, treat a price range as two numeric inputs: enter the minimum in the first Price field and maximum in the adjacent field. Click Search only after both contain valid numbers, then verify the validation error disappears and results or a no-results state is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the shopping search page shows separate lower- and upper-bound Price textboxes, especially after entering a hyphenated range produces a “Please enter a valid number” error.

skills.title: Submit Contact Form and Verify Confirmation
skills.principle:
1. Open the site’s “Contact Us” page and inspect the form.
2. Preserve prefilled name and email; fill every required field, especially the message field, with the user’s request.
3. Activate “Submit” using the currently observed control, not a stale element identifier.
4. Confirm the success alert indicating the message was received, then report completion and stop without resubmitting.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to contact customer service through a shopping site’s Contact Us page, after the page and its required form fields are visible.

skills.title: Verify Contact Us Navigation
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to activate the link whose role and name are exactly “Contact Us,” not its containing list or another footer link. Verify the resulting URL or page heading is the Contact Us page before acting further. If the task only requests reaching that page, stop there; submit a form only when the user provides a message and explicitly requests submission.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site exposes several similarly placed footer links and the task asks to contact customer service or reach the Contact Us page. Confirm the destination after clicking before filling fields or submitting.

skills.title: Verify Newsletter Status in Account
skills.principle: For a logged-in shopping account, open “My Account” rather than relying on the generic footer signup form. Read the “Newsletters” section and report the explicit subscription statement shown there. Once the status is reported, stop without additional navigation or actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked whether an account is subscribed to a store newsletter and the session is authenticated; use the account’s newsletter status section as the authoritative indicator.

skills.title: Check Newsletter Status Through Account Settings
skills.principle: Use the authenticated account area rather than inferring status from the homepage form. Open “My Account,” locate the account’s newsletter subscription or communication preferences section, and inspect the displayed subscription state. Report the state only after the account page visibly confirms it; do not submit the public “Subscribe” form, which could change the subscription.
skills.when_to_apply: When a signed-in shopping site shows a newsletter signup form but the task asks for the existing subscription status. Navigate through “My Account” first and verify account-specific preferences.

skills.title: Navigate Account Address Book
skills.principle: From any signed-in shopping page, open the account area via “My Account.” On the account dashboard, select “Address Book” or “Manage Addresses.” Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Address Book” and address-management controls such as “Change Billing Address,” “Change Shipping Address,” or “Add New Address” are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When the user asks to access or manage saved addresses and the shopping site shows a signed-in account entry. Stop after the Address Book page and its address controls are visibly loaded.

skills.title: Terminate After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate through the account area to the requested management page, then verify its heading and relevant controls are visible. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task asks to open an account-management page and the accessibility tree confirms the requested page heading and actionable controls are present.

skills.title: Verify Submission Before Retrying
skills.principle: After submitting a newsletter form, re-read the current accessibility tree before retrying. If a success alert such as “Thank you for your subscription” appears, stop and report completion. If confirmation is absent, locate the current email field and Subscribe button by their labels or roles, since element IDs may change after navigation or partial completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for newsletter signup tasks when a submit click times out, navigation occurs, or the page updates. The email must be entered first, and completion should be confirmed by the page’s success message.

skills.title: Verify Success After Timeout
skills.principle: After submitting a form, inspect the refreshed page even if the action reports a timeout. If a success alert or confirmation message appears, treat the task as complete, report completion, and stop. Only retry when confirmation is absent; re-identify the current input and button rather than reusing stale element references.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after newsletter signups or other form submissions where navigation may complete despite a timeout, especially when the page shows a refreshed accessibility tree or success alert.

skills.title: Verify Reorder Through Cart State
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in account area and locate the order-history or Recent Orders table.
2. Match the requested order by its visible order number and status, then activate that row’s Reorder control.
3. If navigation reaches Shopping Cart but the click reports a timeout, treat the action as potentially completed and inspect the cart contents.
4. Confirm the reordered items appear in the cart before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for signed-in shopping tasks that reorder a completed order, especially when the Reorder action navigates to Shopping Cart and browser automation reports a post-click timeout.

skills.title: Trust Post-Click Success State
skills.principle: After submitting a checkout action, inspect the resulting page even if the click reports a timeout. If it shows a purchase confirmation such as “Thank you for your purchase!” and an order number, treat the task as complete, report success, and stop instead of retrying or refreshing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking final actions like “Place Order,” especially when navigation may complete before the automation wait finishes or the click returns a timeout.

skills.title: Find an Order by Total
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in account and select “My Orders” or the orders “View All” link.
2. Scan the order-history table’s “Order Total” column across pages if necessary to locate the requested amount.
3. In the matching row, select “View Order,” then read the status displayed on the order-details page.
4. Confirm the page’s total matches the requested amount before reporting the status.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for signed-in shopping accounts when asked for an order’s status and the order is identified by its total rather than a known order number.

skills.title: Report Order Status After Verification
skills.principle: After opening the target order, verify that the displayed grand total matches the requested amount and read the visible status. Then immediately report the status in the task response and terminate; do not repeatedly issue no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an order-history task asks for the status of a specific order by amount, once its detail page visibly confirms the matching total and status.

skills.title: Use the Store Logo for Homepage Navigation
skills.principle: When the task is to reach a shopping site's homepage, activate the header link labeled or identified as the store logo. Confirm completion by checking that the resulting URL is the site's root homepage, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the browser is on a shopping-site page and the header exposes a store logo link pointing to the site's root URL.

skills.title: Stop After Homepage Confirmation
skills.principle: After selecting a homepage navigation control, verify the address and page identity. If the URL is the site root and the homepage content is visible, report completion and terminate; do not click the same link repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task asks for the homepage and the observed page already shows the site root URL plus recognizable homepage content such as the store title or product listings.

skills.title: Stop After Destination Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page heading and URL confirm the requested destination, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or waiting for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigation when the accessibility tree visibly shows the requested page title or heading and the current URL matches the destination; no further interaction is required.

skills.title: Navigate to and Verify Wishlist
skills.principle:
1. Locate the account navigation entry labeled “My Wish List” and activate it.
2. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and wishlist status message.
3. Report whether items are present; if the page states the list is empty, explain that products can be added from product pages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for authenticated shopping tasks asking to view a wishlist, especially when the account navigation exposes a “My Wish List” link. Verify the resulting page rather than assuming navigation succeeded.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: After a navigation click times out, inspect the current page title, URL, and visible heading before retrying. If they already identify the requested category or page, continue from that state and report the available products or controls. Use freshly observed element labels for any further action, not stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When a category-navigation click reports a timeout but the updated accessibility tree may already show the requested destination page.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When targeting a menu item, use its current numeric accessibility bid (for example, the bid attached to the menuitem labeled with the target category), not icon text, escaped labels, or guessed identifiers. After clicking, inspect the updated tree and select any revealed submenu item by its new bid. If the action errors, re-read the current observation before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a visible category or navigation control repeatedly fails with “empty action” or “element not found,” especially when its accessible name includes decorative icon characters or escape sequences.

skills.title: Verify Checkout State Before Retrying
skills.principle:
1. After submitting checkout, inspect the page for a loading indicator and wait until navigation settles.
2. If a click reports a timeout but the page has reached the success page, treat the order as completed rather than retrying.
3. Confirm completion using the success heading and order confirmation details, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When placing an order in a shopping checkout, especially after clicking “Place Order” or another submit control triggers loading, navigation, or a detached-element timeout.

skills.title: Target Checkout Controls by Role
skills.principle: On the payment step, identify the control by its accessible role and label, not nearby element IDs. Activate the button named “Place Order,” not an adjacent address or phone link. After clicking, verify navigation or an order-confirmation state; if the page is unchanged, re-inspect the tree and correct the target rather than repeating the same click.
skills.when_to_apply: When completing a shopping checkout and multiple links or controls appear near the final “Place Order” action, especially when accessibility-tree IDs may shift or be ambiguous.

skills.title: Verify Discount Panel State
skills.principle: On the shopping cart or checkout page, locate the tab labeled “Apply Discount Code.” If it is collapsed, activate it; if it already shows expanded/selected and exposes the discount-code field and “Apply Discount” button, stop and report completion without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a discount-code section and the cart or checkout page is visible. A cart item may be required before the panel appears.

skills.title: Verify Cart State Before Checkout
skills.principle: After selecting the cart link, inspect the resulting state rather than repeating the click. If a message indicates the cart is empty, add a product first; only then proceed to checkout and open the “Apply Discount Code” section. Confirm the checkout page and section are visible before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access a checkout-only control from another shopping page, especially when the cart link opens a modal or remains on the same page. A nonempty cart is required to reach checkout.

skills.title: Search, Open, and Summarize Products
skills.principle:
1. Enter the exact target product name in the storefront Search field and submit it.
2. In results, identify the matching product by its full title and distinguishing attributes, then open its product link.
3. Read the product page’s price and visible Details or Product Description content, including notable features and specifications.
4. Report only observed details to the user and stop once the requested information is covered.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requesting detailed information about a named product when the storefront provides a Search field and product-detail pages with visible descriptions.

skills.title: Inspect All Search Page Regions
skills.principle: After searching, inspect the entire accessibility tree—not just the main results grid. Check sidebar sections such as “Recently Ordered,” wish lists, and related links for an exact title match. Open the exact matching product link, then verify the product-page heading before collecting details; do not open merely similar results or reuse stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search returns many irrelevant or approximate matches, especially when the requested item may appear in account-specific sections such as Recently Ordered or a wish list.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation entry matching the requested page and activate it. After navigation, verify the page title, URL, or main heading matches the goal and report any relevant page state, such as an empty wishlist. Once confirmed, stop without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to open a specific account or shopping page and the current page may already contain a direct navigation link or may already be the requested destination.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: After navigating, verify the resulting page using its heading, URL, or distinctive content. Once the requested destination is visibly confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or waiting for further observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the page visibly matches the requested destination, such as a matching heading and URL. Stop immediately after confirmation, even if additional observations are provided.

skills.title: Modify And Verify Advanced Search
skills.principle:
1. From advanced-search results, select “Modify your search.”
2. Clear obsolete criteria and enter the new value in the requested field, preserving other constraints unless replacement is intended.
3. Submit with “Search.”
4. Confirm the results page summarizes the new field/value and displays refreshed results before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requires changing existing advanced-search criteria and the results page provides a “Modify your search” control. Verify the resulting summary after submission.

skills.title: Use the Advanced Search Form
skills.principle:
1. On search results, activate the explicit "Modify your search." link rather than editing summary text or sorting controls.
2. On the advanced-search form, inspect the accessibility tree and target actual input fields by their labels, not nearby result-page elements.
3. Fill the desired criteria and submit the form; confirm the results page reflects the updated criteria.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to modify shopping search criteria from an advanced-search results page, especially when displayed criteria are static text and the page offers a "Modify your search." link.

skills.title: Search, Compare, Then Verify
skills.principle:
1. Search for the exact product name and submit the query.
2. In results, identify the matching product by its title, then activate its adjacent “Add to Compare” control.
3. Confirm success through the confirmation alert, updated comparison-item count, or the product appearing in the comparison list.
4. Once verified, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding a specific product to a shopping site’s comparison list, especially when it is not visible in the current catalog view and search results provide product-level action controls.

skills.title: Target Controls by Current Semantics
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to identify the exact target product container, then activate its control labeled “Add to Compare.” Never reuse stale bids or infer a control from another section. After each navigation, re-read the tree and verify the target product and control are present; if the control is absent (for example, because the item is out of stock), use an appropriate listing or report that the operation cannot be completed rather than clicking unrelated elements.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific product to a shopping comparison list, especially after navigation, pagination, dynamic updates, or when product availability may change. Confirm the account remains signed in and the target control exists before acting.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Sorting
skills.principle: On product results pages, operate native sorting dropdowns with the select-option action rather than clicking individual option nodes. Select the requested field, then verify the combobox value, URL/state change, and direction control. For ascending order, ensure the control indicates descending is available, meaning the current direction is ascending.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping results page has a labeled native “Sort By” combobox and direct clicking an option is invisible or times out. Select the desired sort field and confirm the resulting order and direction.

skills.title: Use the Actual Sort Control
skills.principle: Locate the page’s explicit sorting control, such as a “Sort By” dropdown or price-order option, rather than clicking a product’s displayed price. Select ascending price, wait for the listing to refresh, then verify several visible prices are nondecreasing before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to sort products and the listing contains prices but no obvious table header; first inspect controls near the product list, and only finish after the displayed order matches ascending numeric prices.

skills.title: Compare Filtered Products Before Drilling Down
skills.principle: Scan every product card on the current page that matches the requested attribute, record each visible rating, and compare them before opening any item. Select the maximum and verify its name and rating on the product page only if needed. Once the result is confirmed, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for the highest-rated item matching a property within a specified page. Ensure the relevant page is loaded and compare only products visibly present on that page.

skills.title: Compare Ratings Across All Visible Products
skills.principle: Scan every product card on the requested page and read its displayed rating percentage or stars from the accessibility tree. Track each product name with its rating, compare all available values, and select the highest. Do not click product actions such as “Add to Cart” while collecting ratings; use product links or details only when rating data is unavailable in the list.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find the highest-rated item on a specific results page, especially when products are sorted by name or price and ratings are displayed inconsistently.

skills.title: Read the Search Results Total
skills.principle: On a product search or advanced-search results page, locate the summary text reporting how many items were found. Use that displayed total as the answer, rather than counting visible products or pages. Confirm the summary’s criteria match the requested query, then report the number exactly.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to count products matching a search and the results page visibly states an item total, with the requested query or filters shown in the summary.

skills.title: Verify Pagination After Navigation
skills.principle: When counting matching products, scan every result page and maintain a running count. After clicking a pagination control, verify completion by checking the URL, current-page indicator, and result range (for example, “Items … of … total”). Treat a click timeout as potentially successful if the page changed; inspect the new observation before retrying or navigating back.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring counts across paginated search results, especially when pagination clicks may report timeouts while navigation still completes.

skills.title: Verify Product Availability Systematically
skills.principle: For a product-details request, inspect the visible listings, follow available pagination, then use the site's labeled Search field with the exact product name. Open the matching product link when found; if all result pages and search show no match, report that the product is unavailable on this site.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping sites when the requested product is not immediately visible and the page provides product listings, pagination, and a site Search control.

skills.title: Stop After Product Details Load
skills.principle: Click the matching product title or image in the results. Verify the destination is the product page by checking its heading and visible details such as price or description. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to view a specific product and the product page is visibly loaded with its title and details.

skills.title: Refine Search With Category Facets
skills.principle: Search for the requested term, then use the results page’s Shopping Options category facet to constrain results to the target category. Verify completion by checking the “Now Shopping by” section names that category and the results heading shows the requested query and item count.
skills.when_to_apply: When a site-wide product search may return items across categories, especially after searching from a category page whose context might not persist.

skills.title: Filter Search Results by Category
skills.principle: After searching for the requested attribute, use the results page’s category facet to select the target category before browsing items. Confirm the heading or category count reflects that category, then inspect the displayed product names for matching options. Stop and report once relevant results are visible instead of paging through unrelated global results.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests products with a specific attribute within a named category, and site search returns results across multiple categories with a corresponding category filter.

skills.title: Verify View State Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the product view selector before clicking. If the requested view is already active—shown by its highlighted or non-clickable label, the alternate view remaining clickable, and matching URL or layout—report completion without changing it. Otherwise, select the requested view and confirm the selector and product layout update.
skills.when_to_apply: On shopping catalog or search-result pages when asked to switch between grid and list views, especially when the initial page may already use the requested view.

skills.title: Verify View Change Then Stop
skills.principle: On a product-results page, inspect the current “View as” control. If “List” is selectable, click it once. After the page refreshes, confirm list mode from the results layout, the active “List” indicator, or a list-mode URL parameter. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate without repeating the click or issuing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a shopping results page from grid to list view and the page exposes a “View as” control. Reinspect the refreshed accessibility tree before acting again.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Setting After Selection
skills.principle: On a product results page, use the labeled “Show” combobox to select the requested page size. After the page reloads, verify the combobox’s selected value and the results summary (for example, “Items 1–24”) or corresponding URL parameter. If the requested size is already selected, report completion without further changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing how many products appear per page on a shopping results or catalog page, especially after a selection triggers a reload and accessibility bids may change.

skills.title: Apply an Advanced Search Price Ceiling
skills.principle:
1. Open the existing search’s “Modify your search” control so current criteria are preserved.
2. Leave the minimum price blank and enter the requested limit in the maximum Price field.
3. Submit with “Search.”
4. Confirm the results page displays the original criterion and “Price: up to” the requested amount before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping results page already has a relevant search criterion and the task requires adding an upper price limit through an Advanced Search form.

skills.title: Use Structured Shopping Filters
skills.principle: For multi-constraint product searches, open the site's “Advanced Search” rather than entering natural-language constraints into the basic search box. Set the product keyword and explicit maximum-price field, submit, then verify the results heading, item count, and displayed prices before continuing. Use accessibility-tree labels or roles, not invented element IDs or DOM fields.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task combines keywords with a numeric constraint such as “vegan under $20,” especially when basic search returns an enormous, loosely matched result set or offers an “Advanced Search” link.

skills.title: Combine Advanced Search Criteria
skills.principle:
1. Open the advanced search form, using “Modify your search” when existing criteria need refinement.
2. Put the product keyword in “Product Name” and the qualifying attribute in “Description,” preserving any existing value.
3. Click “Search,” then verify the results page lists both criteria and reports matching items before confirming completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring products that satisfy multiple textual conditions, when the site provides separate advanced-search fields and the current form or results expose those controls.

skills.title: Use the Correct Advanced Search Controls
skills.principle: On the Advanced Search page, distinguish the header Search combobox from the form fields by their accessible labels. Enter the query in the relevant field, such as Product Name or Description, then activate the form’s Search button. Never use the header combobox as a product-type selector; verify results after submission.
skills.when_to_apply: When an advanced-search page contains both a global Search combobox and labeled criteria fields, especially when the task requires keyword filtering such as dietary terms and product categories.

skills.title: Use the Product Comparison Table
skills.principle: Search for the requested product category, then open the store’s “Compare Products” link when the target items are listed. Read each product name and displayed price from the comparison table, verify the items match the request, and summarize the price differences. Treat package size and quantity warnings in descriptions as relevant context.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring price comparison when target products are already in, or can be added to, the site’s comparison list and the comparison page exposes names and prices.

skills.title: Compare Products Directly From Results
skills.principle: On a shopping search-results page, identify products whose names match the requested category and use each item’s adjacent “Add to Compare” control. Confirm the comparison-list count or success alert increases, repeat for multiple distinct products, then open “Compare Products” and verify their names and prices appear together.
skills.when_to_apply: When comparing prices across several products and the results list already shows product names, prices, and per-item “Add to Compare” controls. Verify the clicked control belongs to the intended item before acting.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current page title, URL, and main heading before navigating. If they already identify the requested destination, report completion and stop. Otherwise, select the visible navigation link whose accessible label matches the destination, activate it, then confirm the resulting page state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree may already show the requested page or contains several similarly named links. Requires checking observable page identity before taking action.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once navigation succeeds, verify the URL or page heading matches the requested destination (for example, “My Account”). Report completion and terminate immediately; do not reuse stale accessibility bids or perform additional clicks, which can navigate elsewhere or sign the user out.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after any navigation action when the resulting observation shows the requested page title, heading, or URL. This is especially important when accessibility bids may change between page loads.

skills.title: Open And Verify Shopping Cart
skills.principle:
1. Locate the header cart control by its role and item-count label, then activate it.
2. If a mini-cart dialog appears, choose “View and Edit Cart” rather than checkout.
3. Confirm the resulting page is titled “Shopping Cart” and displays cart items, quantities, and totals; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a shopping cart from another shopping page, especially when the header cart control opens a preview dialog instead of the full cart page.

skills.title: Recover From Incorrect Element Targets
skills.principle: When a click times out or reports that another element intercepts pointer events, re inspect the accessibility tree instead of retrying the same bid. Locate the intended link by its accessible name and role, or navigate using its observed href. Verify the resulting page heading and URL before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a navigation control is visible but the selected accessibility bid resolves to a different element, is obscured, or repeatedly fails to click.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to the Requested Category
skills.principle: When the current page is unrelated, locate the navigation menu item matching the requested product category and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading names the category and that product listings are displayed; then report completion without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requesting browsing within a named category, especially when starting on search results or another unrelated catalog page and the navigation menu exposes the target category.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the requested category page loads, verify its heading and visible product listings. That state satisfies a browse request; report completion and stop instead of repeatedly paging through additional products unless the user explicitly requests more.
skills.when_to_apply: For simple shopping tasks asking to browse a named category, after navigation visibly shows the category title and product results.

skills.title: Verify Home Navigation and Stop
skills.principle: Click the breadcrumb’s explicit “Home” link, then verify the page URL is the site root and the main heading indicates the storefront home page. Once those observations confirm success, report completion and terminate instead of repeating clicks or opening unrelated account links.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests returning home via breadcrumbs and the page exposes an explicit “Home” breadcrumb link. After navigation, check the URL and page heading before taking further actions.

skills.title: Navigate to a Product Category
skills.principle: Select the navigation menu item matching the requested product category. Verify that the resulting page heading names the category and that product listings are visible, including the displayed item range or count. Then report that browsing is active and mention available category or price filters when shown.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse a shopping category and the page exposes a category navigation menu. The task is complete once the category page loads with recognizable product listings.

skills.title: Use the Requested Category Directly
skills.principle: Open the navigation entry matching the requested product category, such as “Health & Household,” rather than substituting a keyword search. Confirm the resulting page shows the category heading or category-specific product listing, then stop once browsing is established instead of repeatedly paging through unrelated search results.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks to browse a named shopping category and the page exposes that category in navigation. Use keyword search only when the user specifies search terms or the category entry is unavailable.

skills.title: Submit Search and Verify Results
skills.principle:
1. Locate the header Search combobox, enter the requested SKU or product identifier, and wait until the Search button becomes enabled.
2. Activate Search, then verify completion from the results page title, query value, and visible result-count summary.
3. Report the displayed result count and stop once the requested search is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for product searches when the page exposes a header Search combobox and Search control. The prerequisite is that the requested identifier can be entered as a searchable query.

skills.title: Use Visible Search Before Declaring Failure
skills.principle: When asked to find a product by SKU, use the visible Search combobox even if no SKU-specific filter is shown. Enter the exact identifier, submit via the enabled Search button or Enter, and inspect the resulting page for matching products. If needed, use Advanced Search and its available fields. Only report no match after completing an actual search and verifying the results state.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping pages displaying a Search combobox or Advanced Search link, especially when the requested identifier is absent from the currently visible product list.

skills.title: Verify Newsletter Status in Account
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in user's "My Account" page.
2. Locate the "Newsletters" section and read its status text.
3. Treat explicit wording such as "You aren't subscribed to our newsletter" as the authoritative result, report it, and stop without opening the editing form.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking whether the currently signed-in customer is subscribed to a store newsletter and the account page exposes a Newsletters status section.

skills.title: Trust Account Newsletter Status
skills.principle: When checking a logged-in customer’s newsletter status, open the account page and read the explicit “Newsletters” status message. Report that stated result once; after the answer is confirmed, terminate rather than repeating the message or taking additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for newsletter-subscription checks when the customer account is accessible and the account page contains a dedicated Newsletters section with an explicit subscribed or unsubscribed status.

skills.title: Use Recently Ordered Cart Selection
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in My Account page and locate the “Recently Ordered” section.
2. Identify the list entry whose product name matches the requested item, then select its adjacent “Add to Cart” checkbox.
3. Click the section’s “Add to Cart” button.
4. Confirm completion from the success alert stating the item was added and the updated cart count.
skills.when_to_apply: When a signed-in shopping task requests adding a previously purchased item specifically from “Recently Ordered,” provided the account page exposes that section and its selectable item list.

skills.title: Use the Recently Ordered Widget
skills.principle: On the account page, locate the heading "Recently Ordered" and inspect its item list directly. Match the target product by its visible name, then use that item’s checkbox or adjacent "Add to Cart" control. Confirm the cart count or success message changes. Do not substitute the full "Recent Orders" history, which lists orders rather than the widget’s product controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task explicitly requires adding an item from "Recently Ordered" and the signed-in account page exposes that heading with product-level Add to Cart controls.

skills.title: Identify Customer Service Contact Forms
skills.principle: Open the store’s “Contact Us” page and inspect the “Write Us” section. Report the available contact method, required fields such as name, email, and message, optional fields such as phone number, and any stated response expectation. Do not submit the form unless the user explicitly asks.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked how to contact a shopping site’s customer service and a Contact Us page or equivalent support form is available.

skills.title: Verify Submission After Timeout
skills.principle: After submitting a contact form, inspect the resulting page before retrying. A click timeout may occur while navigation is still completing; if the page shows a success alert such as “Thanks for contacting us,” treat the request as submitted, report completion, and stop. Retry only when no confirmation or validation error is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when submitting customer-service contact forms or similar actions where the browser reports a timeout during navigation. Check the updated accessibility tree for success alerts, confirmation text, or changed page state before taking further action.

skills.title: Expand Cart Item Details
skills.principle:
1. Open the cart using the visible cart control when starting elsewhere.
2. In the cart overlay, locate the requested item by its name rather than position.
3. Activate that item’s “See Details” tab.
4. Confirm the tab is expanded and read the resulting details panel before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks for attributes of a specific cart item and the cart overlay lists multiple products with per-item “See Details” controls.

skills.title: Stop After Product Details Appear
skills.principle: From the cart, identify the target item by its visible name and open its product link. Confirm the product page shows the matching title and details section or description. Once those details are visible, report completion and terminate; do not perform repeated no-op actions or unnecessary scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view an item’s details from a shopping cart and the cart contains a visible link matching the requested product.

skills.title: Find Billing Address in My Account
skills.principle: From any storefront page, open the authenticated “My Account” link. On the account overview, locate the section labeled “Default Billing Address” and read its displayed name, street, locality, region, postal code, country, and phone number. Report those values exactly, then stop once the section is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for authenticated shopping tasks asking for the default billing address when the current page offers “My Account” navigation or equivalent account access.

skills.title: Report Visible Account Information
skills.principle: Navigate to the signed-in account area and locate the section labeled "Default Billing Address." Extract the displayed name, address, and phone number, then provide them directly to the user. Once the requested information is visibly confirmed, send the final response and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for account-information tasks when the user is signed in and the requested details appear in a clearly labeled account section.

skills.title: Find an Order and Open Details
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in account area and choose “View All” or “My Orders” to access the complete order-history table.
2. Locate the row matching the requested order number, including paginating if necessary.
3. In that same row, select “View Order,” not “Reorder.”
4. Confirm the destination heading identifies the requested order and shows its details before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for authenticated shopping tasks requesting details for a specific order, especially when the account page shows only recent orders and the target may require the full order-history table.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Order Details
