skills.principle: Once the target order’s details page is visible, verify the heading matches the requested order and that order information is displayed. Then report completion immediately and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for another page change.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a specific order through an authenticated shopping account, after selecting its matching row and observing the order-details heading and information sections.

skills.title: Access Product Reviews Through Account
skills.principle:
1. From a signed-in shopping page, open the “My Account” area.
2. Select the account navigation entry labeled “My Product Reviews.”
3. Confirm the destination heading and read the review status message; report the displayed reviews or explicitly state when it says no reviews were submitted.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for signed-in shopping tasks asking to view a customer’s product reviews, when account navigation exposes “My Account” and “My Product Reviews” links.

skills.title: Treat Empty Review Lists as Completion
skills.principle: After opening the account’s explicit “My Product Reviews” page, verify the heading and displayed state. If it says there are no submitted reviews, treat that empty-state message as the successful result, report it, and stop instead of inspecting orders or taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping account contains a direct “My Product Reviews” navigation entry and the task is to view reviews, including cases where the resulting page may legitimately be empty.

skills.title: Use Account Newsletter Settings
skills.principle: From a logged-in shopping site, open “My Account” and locate the “Newsletters” section. Follow its “Edit” link, or use the sidebar’s “Newsletter Subscriptions” entry. Confirm the destination by checking for the newsletter subscription heading, subscription checkbox, and “Save” button before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to newsletter subscription or email-preference settings and the account page exposes a Newsletters section or Newsletter Subscriptions navigation entry.

skills.title: Verify Success After Save Timeout
skills.principle: After submitting an account change, inspect the resulting page before retrying. If it shows a confirmation alert or updated status, treat the operation as complete and stop; a click timeout may occur while navigation succeeds. Only retry when the post-action state still shows the old value and the save control remains available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when saving newsletter, profile, address, or similar settings triggers a click timeout but the page may have navigated or refreshed. Check for confirmation text or the updated account status first.

skills.title: Use Recently Ordered Directly
skills.principle: On account pages, inspect the “Recently Ordered” section before traversing the full order-history table. Match the requested product title, select its adjacent “Add to Cart” checkbox or button, then verify the cart count or confirmation. If the target is absent, use “View All” or order-history pagination and inspect each order’s details rather than repeatedly issuing no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to add a previously purchased item and the authenticated account page exposes “Recently Ordered,” “View All,” or paginated “My Orders” controls.

skills.title: Use Search Results Wishlist Controls
skills.principle:
1. Enter the exact target product name in the store’s Search combobox; filling it may submit automatically.
2. Check that the page changes to search results and identify the result whose title matches the requested item.
3. Click that result’s associated “Add to Wish List” control, not a neighboring product’s control.
4. Confirm the success alert or wishlist page shows the target item, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping session must add a specific product to a wishlist and search results expose per-item “Add to Wish List” controls. If a search-button click times out but results loaded, proceed from the results state.

skills.title: Add a Specific Product to Wishlist
skills.principle:
1. Search the exact product name using the storefront search field and submit the search.
2. Select the result whose displayed title matches the requested product, distinguishing it from similar items.
3. On the product detail page, activate “Add to Wish List.”
4. Confirm completion from the success alert or the item appearing in “My Wish List,” then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for logged-in shopping tasks that require adding one identified product to a wishlist, especially when search results contain similar products.

skills.title: Use Link URLs After Repeated Clicks Fail
skills.principle: When a visible navigation link does not change the page after a confirmed click, stop repeating the same element action. Read its observed destination URL and navigate directly to it, then verify the destination heading and relevant status text before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping navigation when the target link is visible in the accessibility tree, repeated activation leaves the URL and page unchanged, and the link exposes a destination URL.

skills.title: Open Full Cart From Mini-Cart
skills.principle: After selecting the cart control, inspect the resulting state. If a mini-cart dialog appears with items and a “View and Edit Cart” link, select that link to reach the full cart page. Verify the page heading or URL changes to the cart before stopping; do not repeatedly click the cart control while the dialog remains open.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site’s cart control opens an expandable mini-cart instead of navigating directly, and the task requires viewing the cart contents or full cart page.

skills.title: Verify Category Page Before Acting
skills.principle: After selecting a category, inspect the updated page rather than reusing earlier element IDs. Confirm the page title, breadcrumb, and visible product listing match the requested category. Once browsing is confirmed, report completion and stop; do not perform another navigation action.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse a shopping category and navigation may change accessibility-tree IDs or already lands on the target listing page.

skills.title: Stop After Category Loads
skills.principle: When asked to browse a product category, select the matching navigation entry and verify the resulting page shows the category heading and product listings. Once those products are visible, report completion and stop unless the task explicitly requests deeper browsing, filtering, or a specific item.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to simple category-browsing tasks when the category page loads successfully and its heading and product list are observable; do not paginate speculatively.

skills.title: Submit And Verify Product Search
skills.principle:
1. Locate the page’s Search combobox, enter the requested product term, and confirm the Search button becomes enabled.
2. Activate Search and wait for navigation or page refresh.
3. Verify the results page heading contains the submitted term and product listings or an item count are visible before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring a product search when a Search combobox and submission control are visible, including when starting from a non-catalog page.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Search Results
skills.principle: Enter the requested product query in the search combobox and submit it using the enabled Search button or Enter when appropriate. Confirm the results page shows a matching “Search results for” heading and product listings, then report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task only requires searching, after the query is entered and the results page visibly displays the matching heading and product listings.

skills.title: Open Reviews from Search Results
skills.principle:
1. Search for the requested product and inspect results for the exact product variant, not merely matching keywords.
2. Use that result’s “Reviews” link to open its product page and reviews anchor.
3. If reviews are not visible, activate the “Reviews (N)” tab.
4. Confirm completion when the tab is expanded and customer review entries with ratings and text are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view reviews for a product on an e-commerce site, especially when search results contain multiple variants or unrelated keyword matches.

skills.title: Stop Once Reviews Are Visible
skills.principle: After opening the target product’s reviews link, verify that the “Reviews” tab is expanded and the “Customer Reviews” panel with review entries is visible. This confirms the request to view reviews is complete; report completion and stop instead of repeatedly scrolling or trying to inspect every review.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product’s reviews and the product page already shows an expanded Reviews tab, Customer Reviews heading, and at least one review entry.

skills.title: Verify Cart State After Navigation
skills.principle: Click the visible “My Cart” link to open the cart or checkout page. Inspect the resulting accessibility tree for confirmation, especially an empty-cart message. Once the requested destination is reached, report the observed cart state and stop; do not attempt checkout when no items are present.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a shopping cart or checkout page and a visible “My Cart” navigation link is available. Verify whether the cart contains items before taking any checkout action.

skills.title: Verify Cart Navigation Completion
skills.principle: After selecting the cart control, inspect the resulting state. If a mini-cart dialog appears, choose “View and Edit Cart” to open the full cart page. Confirm the URL or page content reflects the cart page before reporting success; do not repeat the cart-control click or assume navigation occurred.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests the full cart or checkout page and selecting “My Cart” opens an overlay while the current URL and underlying page remain unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Wish List Contents
skills.principle: Open the account’s “My Wish List” link, then read the item count and each listed product’s name and price. Report the observed contents only after the wish-list page visibly confirms them, and stop once the requested check is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking what is in a signed-in customer’s wish list, when a “My Wish List” navigation link or equivalent account entry is visible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Wishlist Contents
skills.principle: Once the wishlist page is displayed, verify the heading and listed item details. Then provide a concise confirmation of the visible wishlist contents and terminate the interaction; do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional page updates.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to check wishlist items and the authenticated page visibly shows the wishlist heading, item count, and saved products.

skills.title: Read Price From Product Details
skills.principle: On a product-details page, confirm the heading identifies the requested item, then read the nearby price text in the main content area. Report that displayed amount directly without adding items to the cart or taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the requested product page is already open and its heading matches the target item; the price should be visible near rating, availability, or quantity controls.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Prices
skills.principle: When the target product page visibly shows a price, read and verify the amount, then provide it directly in the task response. Do not issue repeated no-op actions; terminate immediately after reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product price when the matching product page is open and the price is visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Stock on the Product Page
skills.principle: Read the target product page’s main content and locate the explicit stock-status text near the product heading. Report that status directly; do not infer availability from price, quantity controls, or an enabled purchase button.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking whether a specific shopping item is available and its product page is already open or has been located. Confirm the item identity before reporting the visible stock label.

skills.title: Report Stock Status and Stop
skills.principle: When the product details page identifies the requested item and visibly shows a stock label such as “IN STOCK” or “OUT OF STOCK,” treat the check as complete. Report the item’s stock status directly to the user, then terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for availability when the target product page is open and its stock-status text is clearly visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Read Product Rating Summary
skills.principle: On a product detail page, inspect the rating summary near the product title. Read the displayed percentage or star value and the adjacent review-count link, then report both directly. Convert a five-star percentage to stars only when the scale is clear (for example, 20% equals 1 out of 5).
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a product’s rating and review count and the product detail page or its accessibility tree exposes a rating summary and review-count link.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Ratings Immediately
skills.principle: When the product page visibly contains the requested rating and review count, extract both and respond immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions. Interpret the rating from its accessible numeric or percentage value when available, and use the nearby review link or label for the count. Then terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a product detail page where the target item is identified and rating metadata plus a review-count label or link are already present in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Systematically Review Product Gallery Images
skills.principle:
1. Open the product’s main image to enter the gallery or fullscreen viewer.
2. Identify every distinct thumbnail or image control shown, then select each one in turn.
3. Confirm the displayed image changes and stop only after all distinct images have been viewed.
4. Exit fullscreen if needed, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a product-detail page when asked to view all product images and the page exposes a main image plus gallery thumbnails or navigation controls.

skills.title: Use Gallery Thumbnails Directly
skills.principle: On the product detail page, inspect the gallery’s visible thumbnails and identify each distinct image. Select each thumbnail directly to display it; do not repeatedly click disabled navigation arrows or skip links. If fullscreen opens, use the visible thumbnails or “Exit fullscreen,” then verify every distinct thumbnail has been displayed before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all product images and the gallery shows thumbnails, disabled arrows, or a fullscreen overlay. Ensure the product detail page is loaded and use the gallery’s directly visible image controls.

skills.title: Open My Account and Verify Details
skills.principle: From any signed-in shopping page, select the visible “My Account” navigation link. Confirm the resulting page is titled “My Account” and visibly contains account information such as contact information and billing or shipping addresses. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the user asks to view account information and the page shows a signed-in session with a “My Account” link, such as in the site header.

skills.title: Set Product Quantity Directly
skills.principle: Identify the product page's labeled quantity spinbutton, replace its current value with the requested quantity, then inspect the updated accessibility state. Confirm completion when the control reports the requested value; no cart submission is needed unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to change quantity on an open product page and the accessibility tree exposes a labeled quantity input showing its current value.

skills.title: Persist Cart Quantity Changes
skills.principle: After editing an item's quantity in the mini-cart, open “View and Edit Cart” and use the cart's update/save control to persist the change. Verify the target item's quantity and recalculated cart totals after the cart refreshes; do not treat a changed input value alone as completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a product quantity through a shopping cart popup, especially when the popup shows no explicit update control or its subtotal remains unchanged.

skills.title: Use the Item-Scoped Wish List Control
skills.principle: Identify the target product by its visible name, then activate the “Add to Wish List” control within that product’s listing rather than a neighboring item’s control. Confirm completion from the resulting success alert and wishlist entry or item count. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping page lists the requested product and each listing provides its own “Add to Wish List” control. Verify the target listing before clicking and check the resulting wishlist confirmation.

skills.title: Use Semantic Wishlist Controls
skills.principle: Locate the target product card by its visible name, then activate that card’s actual “Add to Wish List” link—not a nearby container or guessed accessibility path. After activation, verify a success message, changed control state, wishlist count, or the item appearing on the wishlist page before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific product from a shopping listing, especially when accessibility-tree identifiers represent nodes rather than valid CSS selectors. Ensure the account is signed in and distinguish the product card’s wishlist link from its rating or cart controls.

skills.title: Check Product Details for Manufacturer
skills.principle: On a product page, open the “Details” tab and inspect its product-information table for the row labeled “Manufacturer.” Use the adjacent cell as the answer, then report it once the row is visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked who manufactures a specific product and the product page is already open, especially when the visible summary lacks manufacturer information but a “Details” tab is available.

skills.title: Read Product Details After Tab Switch
skills.principle: On a product page, open the tab labeled “Details” and re-scan the resulting accessibility tree. Locate the specifications table by its row header, such as “Manufacturer,” then read the adjacent cell. Treat the updated page state as authoritative; do not continue searching reviews, headings, or unrelated elements once the requested field is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks for a product attribute and the product page exposes tabbed content. After switching tabs, verify the new expanded state and inspect its associated panel for the labeled specification.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: After a category click, inspect the updated URL and page heading before retrying if the tool reports a timeout. If they already identify the requested category, treat navigation as complete, summarize the visible product listing and available filters, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating a shopping category succeeds visually but the browser action reports a timeout while waiting for navigation to finish.

skills.title: Stop After Category Loads
skills.principle: Select the category navigation entry using a correctly formatted click action. Verify completion by checking that the page heading and product list identify the requested category. Once those indicators appear, report completion and terminate instead of repeating the same click.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a shopping category, especially after navigation errors or delayed page updates. The skill requires a visible category heading or filtered product listing confirming that navigation succeeded.

skills.title: Use Pagination To Find More Products
skills.principle: Enter the requested product terms in the store search field and submit. Verify the results heading and item list, then use the visible “Page Next” or numbered pagination control to inspect additional results. Confirm the page indicator changed before reporting newly found alternatives, distinguishing actual kits from merely related items.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping search returns an existing product or too few alternatives and pagination controls are visible. Confirm the search results page and query before moving to another results page.

skills.title: Stop After Finding Relevant Alternatives
skills.principle: After submitting a product search, inspect the displayed results for distinct items matching the requested product type. Record or report the relevant alternatives, then stop once the request is satisfied. If results are noisy, refine the query or apply a relevant category instead of blindly paging through unrelated listings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking to find other or additional products when search results are visible, especially when broad queries produce many irrelevant items and pagination does not itself complete the task.

skills.title: Set Quantity Then Confirm Cart Addition
skills.principle: On a product page, identify the quantity spinner by its “Qty” label and fill it with the requested amount. Verify the spinner displays that value, then activate “Add to Cart.” Confirm completion when the control changes to “Added” or an equivalent success state, and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests a specific quantity for an item already displayed on its product page and the page exposes a labeled quantity spinbutton plus an add-to-cart control.

skills.title: Reinspect After Invalid Element Errors
skills.principle: When an action reports that an element bid cannot be found, stop repeating it. Reinspect the latest accessibility tree, identify the target control by its visible role and product name, then use the currently exposed bid. Confirm navigation changed before continuing to quantity or cart controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply whenever BrowserGym reports an invalid or missing bid, especially after page loads or rerenders. The latest accessibility tree must be available before selecting another product link or control.

skills.title: Check Gallery Boundary State
skills.principle: In a product image gallery, inspect the currently displayed image and the navigation controls. If the requested direction’s control is disabled, treat that as confirmation that the gallery is already at its boundary, report the situation, and stop. Otherwise, activate the directional control and verify the displayed image changed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a previous or next product image and the product page exposes gallery controls with enabled or disabled navigation state.

skills.title: Verify Gallery Changes Before Continuing
skills.principle: On a product page, identify the gallery’s enabled “Previous” control and click it once. Verify the main image changes, such as its source or thumbnail state, then stop because the requested image is displayed. Do not reinterpret “Next” or click again when “Previous” becomes disabled.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product’s previous image and the product page shows a carousel with navigation controls, thumbnails, or image-source changes. Check that the control is enabled before acting.

skills.title: Read SKU From Product Details
skills.principle: On a product page, identify the target product by its heading, then locate the visible “SKU” label in the product-information area and read the adjacent value. If the value is clearly present, report it immediately without navigating, clicking unrelated controls, or repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product SKU when the target product page is already open and the accessibility tree shows a “SKU” label with an adjacent identifier.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Identifiers
skills.principle: When the product page visibly shows the requested identifier beside its label, read and report that value immediately. Do not issue a no-op action; provide the answer as the final response and terminate once the requested information is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product-detail pages when the target item is identified and the requested SKU, model number, or similar identifier is already visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Destination
skills.principle: When the current URL and page content clearly match the requested destination, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of repeatedly issuing no-op actions or waiting for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to navigation tasks when the browser already displays the requested page, confirmed by its URL and recognizable page landmarks such as the site heading, logo, or homepage content.

skills.title: Complete Advanced Product Search
skills.principle:
1. Open the store’s “Advanced Search” link from the header or footer.
2. Enter the requested criterion in the matching labeled field, such as “Product Name,” and optionally add other filters.
3. Click the form’s “Search” button.
4. Confirm completion when the results page displays the applied criteria, item count, and product listings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring Advanced Search, when the store exposes an Advanced Search link and labeled filter fields. Stop after results visibly reflect the submitted criteria.

skills.title: Use Actual Advanced Search Criteria
skills.principle: On the Advanced Search page, fill one or more fields with the user’s requested product criteria rather than dummy text. Use the enabled Search button inside the Search Settings form, not the disabled sitewide search control. Submit once, then verify the results page reflects the entered criteria or shows a meaningful no-results message.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to search products through Advanced Search and the page presents labeled fields such as Product Name, SKU, Description, or Price, especially when a sitewide Search button is disabled.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Product Category
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation menu to select the requested product category. Verify completion by checking that the page heading/title matches the category and that category products or filtering options are displayed, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to browse a specific category and the current page exposes a navigation menu with a matching category label.

skills.title: Use Valid Actions After Interaction Errors
skills.principle: When an interaction repeatedly returns “Received an empty action,” correct the action serialization instead of retrying the same malformed payload. For a category menuitem with hasPopup, hover it to reveal submenu entries, then issue a syntactically complete click using the currently observed target. Verify the URL or visible category heading changes before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a shopping category and the accessibility tree shows a category menuitem with hasPopup, especially after browser actions fail with empty-action or unchanged-page errors.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to a Product Category
skills.principle: From any shopping page, locate the navigation entry matching the requested category and activate it. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading names the category and that category products are listed; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task is to browse a named shopping category and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching navigation menu item. No product selection or filtering is required unless requested.

skills.title: Confirm Category Load Before Scrolling
skills.principle: After selecting a category, inspect the resulting page state. If the heading names the requested category and a product listing is visible, browsing is complete; report completion and stop. Scroll only when the current observation shows that relevant listing content is not yet available or the task explicitly requires exploring additional items.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse a shopping category and navigation has just completed. Use the category heading, product count, and visible product cards as completion evidence before taking further actions.

skills.title: Navigate Using Footer Links
skills.principle: When a requested informational page is not visible in the main navigation, locate its semantically labeled footer link and activate it. Verify the resulting page by checking its heading or URL matches the requested destination, then report completion without unnecessary form interaction.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple page-view tasks when the target page has a labeled link in the storefront footer and the task does not request submitting or editing its form.

skills.title: Terminate After Destination Confirmation
skills.principle: When the target page is reached, verify its heading or URL matches the requested destination, then report completion and terminate immediately. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or continue interacting with the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks such as viewing a storefront information page, once the accessibility tree clearly shows the requested page heading or destination URL.

skills.title: Locate and Summarize Policy Sections
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to find the heading matching the user’s question, then extract the complete nearby paragraphs or list items. Summarize only the page-supported actions and rights, and stop once the relevant section is fully represented; do not keep scrolling when the content is already available.
skills.when_to_apply: When answering questions from a long privacy, cookie, terms, or help page and the accessibility tree already exposes the relevant heading and surrounding text.

skills.title: Verify Account Update Before Reporting
skills.principle: After saving account information, inspect the resulting page for a success confirmation or an error alert. If validation fails, correct the specified field and resubmit; report completion only when the page confirms the change. Never infer success merely from clicking Save.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing personal information in an authenticated shopping account, especially changes requiring current-password verification, and the page remains available after submitting the form.

skills.title: Stop After Anchor Navigation Succeeds
skills.principle: After activating a section link, verify the URL contains the expected anchor and the target heading or content appears in the accessibility tree. When both confirm success, report completion and terminate; do not continue scrolling or perform redundant actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for requests to navigate to a named section on a long page when an in-page link or anchor is available and the resulting observation exposes the target heading or content.

skills.title: Use Privacy Policy For Data Collection
skills.principle: For questions about a site’s collected personal information, open the footer’s “Privacy and Cookie Policy.” Locate the “What we collect” section, extract its listed categories, and summarize them faithfully. Distinguish personal-information categories from separate cookie details unless the task asks for both.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping sites when the task asks what personal information the website collects and a footer privacy-policy link is visible or accessible.

skills.title: Report Findings After Reading
skills.principle: Once the relevant policy section is visible, extract the requested facts and provide them directly in the final response. Do not repeatedly use noop after confirming the information; completion requires communicating the answer, not merely recognizing it internally.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for information-retrieval tasks when the page already displays the requested content, especially policy pages with clearly labeled sections such as “What we collect.”

skills.title: Sort Category Products by Lowest Price
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the requested product category and locate the labeled “Sort By” combobox.
2. Open the combobox and select the “Price” option.
3. Verify the page refreshes with “Price” selected and visible product prices increasing from the lowest displayed value.
4. Report completion once both the selected sort value and ascending prices confirm the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a shopping category or search-results page when the task requests products sorted by price ascending and a “Sort By” control includes a “Price” option.

skills.title: Use Observed Category Navigation
skills.principle: Navigate to product categories through visible, labeled menu controls rather than guessing URL paths. Activate the observed category entry, inspect the resulting page or submenu, and only then use its sort control. If navigation produces a 404, return and use the original category control or search field.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping page shows a category in its accessibility tree but its direct-looking URL is unknown, unsupported, or leads to a 404 page.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Category Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level department from site navigation.
2. On its listing page, inspect the Shopping Options or category filter area for the requested subcategory.
3. Select the subcategory by its visible label, then verify the listing reflects that category and shows relevant products.
4. Report completion only after confirming the filtered category and product results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping request names a nested category and the site starts elsewhere or at a broad department listing. The category filter must be visible before selecting the target subcategory.

skills.title: Use Current Accessible Labels
skills.principle: Before each interaction, re-read the current accessibility tree and select the element whose role and accessible name match the goal. Do not reuse stale bids or assume neighboring menu IDs represent subcategories. Submit a correctly formatted action, then verify the URL, heading, or product list reflects the intended category before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when browsing hierarchical shopping categories or recovering from an action error, especially after navigation changes the accessibility tree or when menu items have similar positions and dynamic bids.

skills.title: Use Facet Links for Price Filtering
skills.principle: On a category results page, inspect the Price facet’s element type before acting. If the range is represented by a link rather than a native select, click the link matching the requested range; do not use select_option. Verify the resulting URL, item count, or “Now Shopping by” summary confirms the price filter before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering products by price on a shopping category page, especially when accessibility data exposes price ranges as links and the requested range may be encoded differently in the destination URL.

skills.title: Verify Category and Exact Price Facet
skills.principle: Navigate using the visible category label, then verify the resulting page heading matches the requested category. In the “Shopping Options” panel, click the visible price facet link whose displayed bounds match the requested range exactly; do not use list-container IDs, dropdown actions on `<ol>` elements, or substitute a broader range. Confirm the URL, active filter, and result count afterward.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering products by category and price on a faceted shopping page, especially when category navigation may be mis-targeted or the requested price range may not exist among the visible facet links.

skills.title: Verify Cart Page Before Reporting
skills.principle: Select the header link labeled “My Cart,” then verify the resulting page is the cart page and inspect its cart-item list. Distinguish cart contents from “Compare Products” items or product-list entries. Report the visible item names only after confirming the cart page state.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all cart items and the current page contains several shopping lists, especially “My Cart,” “Compare Products,” or product-catalog entries.

skills.title: Verify Cart Page Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the cart control, verify that the URL or main heading shows the full cart page. If a mini-cart dialog opens instead, activate its “View and Edit Cart” link, then confirm the cart contents are displayed on the cart page before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all cart items and selecting “My Cart” opens an overlay or leaves the page URL and main content unchanged. Requires a visible full-cart navigation link or equivalent cart-page control.

skills.title: Use Category Filters to Reach Subcategories
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested top-level category from the site navigation.
2. In the category page’s “Shopping Options” or equivalent section, locate the exact requested subcategory by its visible label.
3. Select that subcategory, then verify the page reflects the selection through “Now Shopping by,” the item count, and relevant product listings.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing a named subcategory within a shopping site’s broader category, especially when navigation menus expose the parent category but the target appears as a sidebar category filter.

skills.title: Recover Directly From Blank Pages
skills.principle: When back navigation reaches `about:blank` or stops changing the page, stop repeating `go_back()`. Navigate directly to the storefront home page, or use the visible store logo/home link when available, then verify that the expected category navigation appears before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task starts on an irrelevant page or repeated back actions produce `about:blank` without progress. The storefront home URL or a visible home control must be available.

skills.title: Use the Account Dashboard’s Recently Ordered Section
skills.principle: Navigate from the current page to the signed-in user’s account using “My Account.” On the dashboard, identify the distinct “Recently Ordered” section rather than confusing it with the “Recent Orders” table, then read and report each listed product. Stop once the item names are visibly confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check recently ordered products on a shopping site and the user is already signed in, especially when the account dashboard exposes both “Recent Orders” and “Recently Ordered” sections.

skills.title: Stop When Recently Ordered Items Appear
skills.principle: On the signed-in account page, locate the section labeled “Recently Ordered” and read the listed products directly. Use its “View All” control only if the task requires more items. Do not open individual order details or confuse “Recent Orders” with “Recently Ordered.” Once the requested items are visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking recently ordered products on a shopping account page, especially when both “Recent Orders” and “Recently Ordered” sections are present.

skills.title: Verify View State Before Changing
skills.principle: Inspect the current page and relevant controls before acting. If the requested view is already active—or the page has no applicable grid/list control—avoid unnecessary interaction, report that no change is needed, and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change a shopping page’s display format, especially when the current observation may show a non-listing page or lacks grid/list toggle controls.

skills.title: Navigate Using Observed Element Targets
skills.principle: Start by verifying the current page is relevant to the task. Navigate to a product listing, then inspect the refreshed accessibility tree and activate the view-control element using its current observed role, name, or bid. Do not repeatedly click guessed text labels or controls copied from stale observations; confirm the page changed and the list layout is visible afterward.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing grid/list display or another catalog setting, especially after landing on a non-catalog page or receiving a missing-element error. First reach a product listing and use only controls present in its latest observation.

skills.title: Save Account Information Changes
skills.principle: From the signed-in shopping account, open “My Account,” choose the “Edit” control under “Account Information,” update fields if needed, and select “Save.” Treat the task as complete when the account page returns and displays a confirmation such as “You saved the account information.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to manage or update personal account information and the signed-in account page exposes an Account Information section with an Edit control.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Page
skills.principle: When the requested destination is visible, verify its heading or relevant account section matches the task, then report completion and terminate. Do not edit fields, save unchanged information, or navigate into unrelated account subsections unless the instruction explicitly requests those actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks, such as opening an account page, when the target page heading and relevant management options are already visible and no specific data change is requested.

skills.title: Use Description For Feature-Based Search
skills.principle:
1. Open the store’s “Advanced Search” feature.
2. Enter the requested product type and distinguishing features in the “Description” field, leaving unrelated filters blank.
3. Select “Search” and verify the results page shows matching criteria, result count, product names, and prices.
4. Report the matching results only after confirming the displayed result state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping request combines a product category with features or attributes, and the store exposes an Advanced Search form with a searchable “Description” field.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Form Controls
skills.principle: When a control is visible in the accessibility tree but semantic-label lookup fails, target its current accessibility bid rather than retrying or waiting. Fill the form field’s bid, then click the enabled Search button belonging to the form—not a duplicate disabled header Search control. Verify that the page changes to search results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on advanced-search pages when the tree shows labeled textboxes and multiple similarly named buttons, but label-based interaction returns “element not found” or a disabled-control timeout.

skills.title: Verify Product Claims on Details Page
skills.principle:
1. Search using the product’s distinctive name or model identifier.
2. From results, select the exact matching item, checking titles for distinguishing qualifiers such as included or missing accessories.
3. On the product page, verify the claim in the details or quick-look section.
4. Report the answer with the supporting wording when the page provides explicit confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping questions about whether a specific item includes an accessory or feature, especially when search results contain similar products or variants.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: After each navigation, re-read the current accessibility tree and act on the newly exposed role or label, not a stale icon string or bid. For product lookup, use the visible search control or the Advanced Search “Product Name” textbox, submit, and verify that results or the target product page appears before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When repeated clicks or focus actions report missing elements, or navigation changes the page. The latest accessibility tree must be treated as the source of valid targets and page state.

skills.title: Use Home Breadcrumb Navigation
skills.principle: When a shopping page is not the homepage, activate the explicitly labeled “Home” breadcrumb or store-logo link. Confirm completion by checking that the URL is the site root and the page shows the store’s main heading or product showcase, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when tasked with reaching an ecommerce homepage from an internal page and the accessibility tree exposes a Home breadcrumb, store logo link, or equivalent root navigation control.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Home
skills.principle: Click the store logo or equivalent home link once, then verify the page URL is the site root and the home-page heading or content is visible. When these signals confirm completion, report success and terminate instead of repeating the same click.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to a shopping site’s home page and the current page exposes a logo or home link. Stop after the observation shows the root URL and homepage content.

skills.title: Use Direct Navigation After Click Failure
skills.principle: When a visible navigation control is blocked or its accessibility identifier resolves to another element, stop repeating the same click. Read the control’s observed destination and navigate there directly, then verify the URL or page heading confirms completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping navigation when the cart link is visible but clicks time out, pointer events are intercepted, or the locator does not match the intended control.

skills.title: Verify Category Navigation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation entry matching the requested shopping category. After activation, confirm the page title or heading matches that category and that product listings are present. Then report completion, optionally mentioning visible filters or pagination; do not perform unnecessary additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse a named product category and the current page exposes a matching navigation menu item, especially from an unrelated page such as a policy or account page.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids, Not Visible Text
skills.principle: When an action repeatedly fails, stop guessing label strings. Re-read the current accessibility tree and target the actionable node's numeric bid (for example, the menuitem), not its nested StaticText or icon label. After acting, verify that the URL, page heading, or expanded menu changed before retrying or choosing another navigation path.
skills.when_to_apply: When BrowserGym reports an empty action or cannot find an element despite visible matching text, especially when the tree shows numeric bids on actionable menuitems, links, or buttons.

skills.title: Navigate By Semantic Category Labels
skills.principle: When a shopping task names a broad category, use the accessibility tree to locate the matching navigation label rather than relying on URLs or fixed element IDs. Select it, verify the resulting page heading and item count confirm the category, then summarize available filters and ask for the user’s specific product preference before adding anything.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the initial page is unrelated or a broad shopping category is requested, especially when the category menu and resulting listing provide recognizable headings, item counts, and filtering options.

skills.title: Stop After Cart Confirmation
skills.principle: After adding a suitable item, verify the cart indicator updates to show the item count. Once the requested shopping goal is satisfied and the cart state confirms success, report completion and terminate instead of continuing to browse or scroll.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for open-ended shopping tasks where adding at least one relevant category item satisfies the request, especially after the cart indicator visibly changes following an Add to Cart action.

skills.title: Verify Navigation After Timeout
skills.principle: After a navigation click reports a timeout, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree before retrying. Confirm the page title, URL, and relevant content match the requested destination; if the target category and products are visible, report completion instead of repeating the click.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking a category or navigation entry when the tool reports a timeout but may have completed navigation. Requires a new page observation with destination URL, title, or target content available.

skills.title: Use Valid Semantic Navigation Actions
skills.principle: Construct browser actions in the exact tool syntax, with a complete target reference and no stray quote or truncation. Prefer the observed element’s role and accessible label, such as the category menu item, over brittle copied IDs. After each action, inspect the updated URL or page heading; once the requested category listing appears, stop retrying and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an e-commerce category from a menu, especially after an action returns an empty-action or parsing error. Reinspect the current accessibility tree before retrying and confirm the category page loaded.

skills.title: Navigate Categories by Semantic Menu Labels
skills.principle: From the current page, locate the navigation menu entry whose accessible name matches the requested shopping category and activate it. Verify completion by checking the page heading, URL context, and visible product listing for that category. Once the category is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests browsing a named category and the current page exposes navigation entries with accessible labels, even if the starting page is unrelated.

skills.title: Explore Before Reporting Completion
skills.principle: For an exploration request, do not declare success immediately after opening the category. Browse meaningful results using available filters or pagination, verify each resulting heading or active-filter state, then provide one concise summary and stop. Avoid repeatedly retrying a reporting action after an execution error; resume exploration or submit the message once using the supported action format.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to explore a category and the category page is visible, especially when it offers product listings, filters, sorting, or pagination.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Category Access
skills.principle: Once the requested shopping category page loads and visibly lists products, treat exploration as complete unless the task specifies a deeper filter, product count, or comparison. Report that the category is available with representative visible items, then terminate instead of repeatedly opening products, changing subcategories, or paging indefinitely.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for open-ended shopping tasks such as “explore [category]” when the category heading, product listing, and relevant navigation state are visible. Do not stop early if the instruction requests specific products, filters, or exhaustive coverage.

skills.title: Reinspect Before Retrying UI Actions
skills.principle: When an element bid fails, re-read the latest accessibility tree and locate the intended control by its role and label rather than reusing the stale bid. Activate the newly observed control, then verify the resulting URL or page content matches the requested destination before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating shopping pages after a failed click or dynamic page update, especially when repeated accessibility-tree snapshots show changed element bids or a cart control opens an intermediate dialog.

skills.title: Search Products and Verify Price
skills.principle:
1. Open the store homepage when the current page lacks usable product-search controls.
2. Enter the target product name in the Search combobox and activate the Search button.
3. On the results page, match the exact product title and read its adjacent listed price.
4. Report the price only after confirming the result title and price correspond to the requested item.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product’s price when the item is not already visible. Requires access to the store homepage or another page exposing its Search combobox.

skills.title: Use Visible Product Links After Navigation Failure
skills.principle: When a guessed product or category URL fails, inspect the current page for a visible product link, such as a wishlist or listing entry. Open that link, verify the product title matches the requested item, then read the clearly displayed price from the product page and report it.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks when direct navigation returns an error, 404 page, or unexpected content, but the current page exposes a matching product link in a wishlist, search result, or product list.

skills.title: Trust Add-to-Cart Confirmation
skills.principle: After selecting the target product’s “Add to Cart” control, wait for the UI update. Treat a button changing to “Added” or a success alert confirming the item as completion. Do not click it again, since repeated clicks may increase quantity. If verification is needed, open the cart and confirm the target item appears there.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product from a shopping listing, especially when the page uses asynchronous updates and changes the button label or displays a cart confirmation alert.

skills.title: Use Direct Product Review Links
skills.principle: On a shopping homepage or product listing, locate the target item and activate its review-count link when it points to the reviews anchor. Verify completion by checking the product page URL contains the reviews anchor and the “Reviews” tab is selected with its review panel visible. If already there, stop and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the target product is visible in a listing or when its product page exposes a review-count link or “Reviews” tab. Reinspect the current accessibility tree before clicking to avoid stale element references.

skills.title: Terminate After Section Confirmation
skills.principle: On a product page, select the product’s review-count link or “Reviews” tab. Verify that the reviews tab is expanded and its “Customer Reviews” panel is visible. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not issue repeated noop actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to product reviews and the accessibility tree shows an expanded “Reviews” tab or visible “Customer Reviews” panel, indicating the destination has been reached.

skills.title: Navigate Category Pagination Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Select the requested category using its visible label, not a stale accessibility ID.
2. On the category listing, locate the pagination link matching the requested page.
3. After navigation, verify the heading, item range, URL, or “currently reading page” indicator confirms the target page before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When browsing to a numbered page in a shopping category, especially after the page changes and accessibility-tree element IDs may no longer match.

skills.title: Verify Category Before Paginating
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested category from the navigation menu before using pagination.
2. Confirm the page shows the category context or filtered product results.
3. Select the target page from that category’s pagination controls.
4. Verify the resulting page indicator and product range, then stop once the goal is satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse a specific product category and page, especially if the initial page is a general storefront whose pagination may apply to all products.

skills.title: Search and Select Exact Product
skills.principle:
1. Use the store’s search field when the target product is not visible.
2. Enter the product name and submit with the Search control.
3. In results, select the listing whose title matches the requested product, including distinguishing variants such as color.
4. Confirm the destination is the product details page by checking its heading and product information, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: For shopping tasks requiring a specific product page, especially when the item is absent from the current listing and search suggestions or results may contain multiple variants.

skills.title: Use Search Before Category Navigation
skills.principle: On a shopping site, use the visible Search combobox for a named product instead of guessing category-menu bids. Enter the exact product name, submit with the enabled Search control or Enter, then select the matching product-title link and verify the product details page heading.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task requests a specific product and the page shows a Search combobox. This avoids unreliable category-menu interactions, especially when accessibility-tree bids contain icon text or change between observations.

skills.title: Use Built-In Product Comparison
skills.principle: Search for each target product, identify the exact matching result by its full title, and activate that result’s “Add to Compare” control. After both products are selected, open the comparison view and verify that both appear in the comparison table before reporting differences.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks comparing two or more products when search-result cards expose an “Add to Compare” control and a comparison view is available.

skills.title: Use Built-In Product Comparison
skills.principle: For a comparison task, locate each exact product in search results and activate its associated “Add to Compare” control. After both are added, open the “Compare Products” section and verify both items appear before summarizing supported attributes such as price, design, and usage. Avoid relying on memory from separate result pages or continuing searches after a complete comparison is available.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site exposes “Add to Compare” controls and a “Compare Products” section. Confirm each intended product is selected and both appear in the comparison view before reporting results.

skills.title: Stop Repeated Back Navigation
skills.principle: When back navigation reaches the storefront or an empty `about:blank` page, stop using history. Navigate directly to a product listing or category page, then locate the pagination/display control and select the requested page size. Verify the listing summary or control reflects the new value before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing products-per-page settings and the current page is unrelated, especially after logout or when repeated `go_back()` actions produce the storefront or `about:blank`.

skills.title: Filter Search Results by Nested Category
skills.principle: Search for the requested product using the site-wide search, then use category facets to narrow broad results. Select the relevant parent category first; after the page refreshes, select the matching subcategory. Confirm completion from the active filter label, page heading, and product-count/results state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when direct navigation does not expose the requested subcategory, or when broad product-search results include category facets. Reinspect the accessibility tree after every navigation because element references may change.

skills.title: Use Stable Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When interacting with a BrowserGym accessibility tree, target the element's numeric bid (for example, the observed menuitem bid), not its accessible name or icon text. After each action, inspect the refreshed tree and use the newly observed bid; do not repeatedly reuse failed labels or stale identifiers.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a visible control has a numeric accessibility-tree bid and attempts using its name, icon, or copied text produce empty-action or element-not-found errors.

skills.title: Filter Products Before Reading Reviews
skills.principle:
1. Navigate from the broad department to the relevant subcategory using visible category filters, such as Makeup then Lips.
2. Compare listed products by rating and review count, prioritizing highly rated items with substantial review coverage.
3. Open each promising product and select the “Reviews (N)” tab; verify the expanded review panel displays customer entries.
4. Summarize recurring benefits and drawbacks, including notable safety concerns, then stop after covering the strongest candidates.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping category pages when asked to find top-rated products and read reviews. Begin with a broad department page, and continue only when product ratings, review counts, and a visible Reviews tab are available.

skills.title: Act on Loaded Page Evidence
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree already shows the target page and interactive controls, stop waiting and act on the observed state. Use the visible Search combobox or the relevant category filter, then select matching products and open their Reviews links. Confirm each resulting page before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when repeated waits leave the same populated accessibility tree, with usable search, category, product, or review controls already present.

skills.title: Verify Pagination While Tracking Maximum
skills.principle:
1. On each product-listing page, record every relevant item’s name and displayed price, updating a running maximum.
2. Use the visible “Page Next” or page-number control to advance, then verify the URL, page indicator, or item range changed.
3. Continue until the requested final page is visibly confirmed; report the recorded item and price only afterward.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when finding the highest- or lowest-priced item across multiple listing pages, especially when pagination controls or accessibility-tree element IDs may become stale.

skills.title: Use Current Pagination Element Identifiers
skills.principle: Before clicking pagination, inspect the latest accessibility tree and use the element’s current bid or a supported role-based selector, not only its visible label. After clicking, verify that the page indicator, item range, or URL changed. If the action fails, re-inspect and choose the newly observed pagination control rather than repeating the same selector.
skills.when_to_apply: When traversing multiple product-list pages, especially after scrolling or navigation errors, and the accessibility tree exposes pagination links or next-page controls with deployment-specific identifiers.

skills.title: Use the Wishlist Header Link
skills.principle: From a signed-in shopping page, locate the header link labeled “My Wish List” (often showing an item count) and activate it. Confirm completion when the destination shows the “My Wish List” heading and saved-item list, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open the user’s wishlist and the current page exposes a signed-in account header with a “My Wish List” link. Verify the resulting page heading or wishlist contents before finishing.

skills.title: Refresh Element References After Navigation
skills.principle: After every page transition, re-read the current accessibility tree and locate controls by their visible role or label before acting. Do not reuse element IDs from a previous page; if a click fails, inspect the updated tree, select the newly exposed matching element, and verify the destination heading or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when browsing shopping categories, filters, or product pages where accessibility-tree element IDs change after navigation, redirects, or filtering.

skills.title: Use Current Menuitem Bids
skills.principle: Read the latest accessibility tree before each navigation. Identify the target category by its visible name, then click that menuitem’s current bid—not a remembered bid, Unicode prefix, or reconstructed label. Verify the resulting page heading or URL matches the requested category before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating category menus with dynamically changing accessibility-tree bids, especially after page transitions or failed clicks. Ensure the target menuitem is visible in the latest observation before acting.

skills.title: Use Footer Links for Static Pages
skills.principle: When a requested informational page is not visible in the main navigation, inspect the page footer for a matching link. Activate the link, then verify the destination by checking the page heading and URL or selected footer state. Once the requested page is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping-site tasks requesting static pages such as Contact Us, policies, or search information, especially when the current page exposes footer navigation links.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Product Pagination
skills.principle: Select the pagination control labeled with the requested page, then verify the resulting page indicator, URL state, or product range matches the target. Once confirmed, report completion and stop; do not navigate backward and forward unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping product listing contains numbered pagination or Previous/Next controls and the requested destination page is available.

skills.title: Use Accessibility IDs for Links
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree exposes the needed link, use its current element identifier or navigate to its observed URL rather than passing visible text as a bid. For pagination, select the link labeled for the target page and verify the URL or page indicator changes before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping listing already shows pagination and actions fail with “Could not find element with bid” despite visible labels. Prefer the observed pagination link’s current ID or href, and re-inspect after each page update.

skills.title: Open Matching Product From Showcase
skills.principle: When the target product is visibly listed in a homepage showcase or results list, use its product-name link or image link to open the details page. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading matches the target and that product information such as price, stock, and description is visible before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring product details when the current page contains a matching product listing. Prefer semantic link text or the current observation’s element reference, and re-check the refreshed page before acting.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Product Details
skills.principle: Once the target product page shows its title and visible details panel, treat the request as complete. Do not repeatedly click the already-selected Details tab or issue noop actions; report completion and terminate immediately after confirming the observable success state.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view product details and the target product page is open with its title and details or description content visibly displayed.

skills.title: Use Visible Product Review Links
skills.principle: When the accessibility tree already shows the target product, select its product-name link or directly labeled review link instead of browsing categories. Verify the link’s associated product title, then activate the review link or open the product page and inspect the Reviews section. Avoid scrolling or clicking disabled controls when the target is already visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping pages where the target item and a nearby “Review” or “Reviews” link are present in the accessibility tree, especially after navigation lands on a product showcase or listing.

skills.title: Verify Product Price on Details Page
skills.principle:
1. Locate the exact target product name in the current listing and open its product link.
2. On the product page, confirm the heading matches the target item.
3. Read the displayed price near the product heading and report it only after this match is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for an item’s price when the target appears in a product listing or search results and a product-details page is available.

skills.title: Verify Search Field Roles Before Filling
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to distinguish the actual search textbox or combobox from nearby labels, legends, links, and buttons. Fill the element whose role is textbox/combobox and accessible name matches the intended field, then activate its Search control. Confirm the results page contains the target product before reading its displayed price.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching a shopping catalog and element identifiers are ambiguous or a fill action reports that the target is not an input. Inspect current roles and accessible names before retrying.

skills.title: Verify Product Identity Before Finishing
skills.principle: On a category or search results page, locate the listing whose visible title matches the requested product and open its title or image link. Confirm completion by checking the destination page heading and URL, then report success and stop. Include salient visible details such as price or stock only when useful.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open a specific shopping product page and the item appears in a visible listing. Prerequisite: the destination page must visibly confirm the requested product title.

skills.title: Inspect Search Results Before Scrolling
skills.principle: After submitting a product search, inspect the current results and accessibility tree for an exact or near-exact title before scrolling or declaring it unavailable. If the target appears, activate its product-name or image link immediately and verify the destination is the product page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping search-result pages whenever a target product may already be visible, especially after search submission and before pagination or scrolling.

skills.title: Verify Comparison Status First
skills.principle: Before adding a product to comparison, inspect the page’s “Compare Products” section or item count and match the target by name. If it is already listed, report that no addition was needed and terminate; otherwise, use the target product’s corresponding “Add to Compare” control, then confirm its presence.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to add a product to a shopping comparison list and the current page exposes comparison contents or an item count, especially when the target may already be present.

skills.title: Terminate After Success Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page confirms the requested product was added to the comparison list, treat the task as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or waiting for additional observations.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping action produces an explicit success alert, updated list count, or visible target entry confirming completion.

skills.title: Combine Category and Price Filters
skills.principle:
1. On the relevant shopping category page, select the most specific subcategory matching the requested product type.
2. Sort by Price when useful, then apply the price-range link whose displayed upper bound is below the budget.
3. Verify the active filters, result count, and visible item prices before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping page offers sidebar category and price facets, especially when the budget range is available only after selecting a specific subcategory.

skills.title: Combine Category and Price Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested department, then select the most specific relevant subcategory, such as “Sports,” rather than relying on the broad department alone.
2. Apply the exact visible price range matching the budget; avoid broader ranges that require manual filtering.
3. Verify product names and prices in the refreshed results, report qualifying items, and stop once the result is established.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests products from a department with both a semantic constraint and a price limit, especially when broad department results contain unrelated clothing or accessories.

skills.title: Verify Category Filter After Navigation
skills.principle:
1. On a category listing, locate the target subcategory under “Shopping Options” and activate its link.
2. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking “Now Shopping by” for the target category, the filtered item count, or URL parameters.
3. Once the target category is visibly confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating nested shopping categories from a product-listing page, especially when the target may already be active and the page exposes “Now Shopping by” or equivalent filter state.

skills.title: Use Current Element Bids
skills.principle: When interacting with an accessibility tree, distinguish the element’s current bid from its accessible name, Unicode icon text, or printed tree line. Select the live menuitem bid shown for the target category, click it, then inspect the refreshed tree for the expanded submenu and click the requested child category. After navigation, verify the URL or page heading reflects the target category.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this for category navigation or any BrowserGym interaction when clicks return empty-action or element-not-found errors, especially with icon-prefixed accessible names and nested popup menus.

skills.title: Verify Category Filter Before Reporting
skills.principle: On a category landing page, locate the target category under the relevant shopping-options section and select its link. After navigation, verify the page shows the target category in the active-filter or “Now Shopping by” area and displays representative products. Once both confirm the requested category, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse or check out a named shopping category, especially when the initial product listing is broad and the target appears as a sidebar category link.

skills.title: Verify Category Selection After Clicking
skills.principle: Use the category link whose accessible name exactly matches the requested category, then verify the resulting page state before browsing. Confirm the URL/filter state, heading, and any “Now Shopping by” label identify the target category. If they mismatch, return to the category list and select the correct link rather than scrolling or continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a shopping category page with several similarly placed filter links, especially before browsing products. Verify the resulting category state is visible and matches the task before taking further actions.

skills.title: Target the Wishlist Control Precisely
skills.principle: In a product listing, locate the target item by its name, then activate that item's specifically associated “Add to Wish List” control—not the product title, image, or another nearby action. After activation, verify a success message, wishlist-count change, or item presence in the wishlist before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific product from a shopping listing, especially when each product card contains several adjacent links and buttons. Verify the resulting page state before claiming success.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Product Sorting
skills.principle: On a product listing page, use the labeled “Sort By” combobox’s select operation to choose “Price” rather than clicking a native option directly. Wait for the page to refresh, then verify the combobox shows “Price” and visible product prices increase from top to bottom. Leave the direction unchanged when the control indicates ascending order.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting products by price on a listing page, especially when the accessibility tree exposes a native combobox whose individual options are not visibly clickable.

skills.title: Verify Sort Direction Before Toggling
skills.principle: On the target category page, select “Price” in the “Sort By” control. Read the direction control’s label: “Set Descending Direction” means prices are currently ascending, while “Set Ascending Direction” means descending. Click it only when the displayed direction is opposite the request, then verify the first two product prices and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting a category listing by price, especially when the page exposes a separate ascending/descending direction link. Confirm the selected sort field and visible price order before making another change.

skills.title: Verify Newsletter Subscription Status
skills.principle:
1. Locate the newsletter email field, enter the requested email address, and activate the adjacent “Subscribe” control.
2. Inspect the resulting alert or confirmation message.
3. If it says the address is already subscribed, report that status as completion; otherwise, report the displayed subscription confirmation or error.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing to a newsletter through a shopping site footer, with the requested email address available and a visible email field plus “Subscribe” control.

skills.title: Revalidate Newsletter Form After Navigation
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree after every navigation or submission. Locate the newsletter textbox and its adjacent “Subscribe” button by role, enter the user-provided email (not a placeholder), then submit. If the form reports “This is a required field,” refill the currently displayed textbox before retrying; confirm a success message before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When subscribing from a Magento-style footer newsletter form, especially after the page changes or an earlier element reference becomes invalid. Requires an actual user email address and a freshly observed form state.

skills.title: Verify Existing Category Filters First
skills.principle: Before clicking a category link, inspect the current results and sidebar for an active filter such as “Now Shopping by: Category.” If the requested category is already active and the item count reflects it, report completion without further navigation. Otherwise, select the matching category entry and verify the updated active-filter label and results count.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse a shopping subcategory and the current page may already be filtered; verify the active filter before relying on stale element references or performing navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page shows the requested category and its product count, treat browsing as complete and report success. If inspecting more products is necessary, use the visible “Show” control or pagination deliberately; stop when the displayed page state remains unchanged after scrolling.
