skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to browse a named category and the accessibility tree confirms that category is active with product listings, especially when repeated scrolling produces no new content.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Category
skills.principle: When a browsing task names a category, select the matching category link from the shopping options and verify the resulting page shows the requested category in its active filter or heading. Once confirmed, report completion and stop; do not enter unrelated subcategories or paginate unless the task explicitly requests deeper exploration.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for category-browsing tasks where the requested category is visible as a navigation or shopping-options link, and the post-navigation page confirms the active category.

skills.title: Stop After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Select the requested category from the shopping-options sidebar, then verify the resulting page shows the category in “Now Shopping by” and displays its product results. Once confirmed, report completion and stop; do not browse unrelated subcategories or paginate unless the task explicitly requires examining individual products.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore or open a specific shopping category and the category-filtered results page visibly confirms the requested label and product listing.

skills.title: Use the Labeled Category Navigation
skills.principle: On a shopping category page, identify the navigation menu item by its visible label and click the exact target category. Ignore unrelated controls such as Compare Products or Skip to Content. Confirm completion when the page heading, breadcrumb, or URL reflects the requested category, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a store section and the accessibility tree exposes that section as a labeled navigation menu item. Reinspect the current observation before acting, since element identifiers can change after navigation.

skills.title: Recover From Repeated Empty Actions
skills.principle: When a UI action repeatedly returns an empty-action error, stop retrying the same malformed command. Use an observable alternative, such as the target navigation URL exposed in the accessibility tree, then verify the destination by checking the page URL and heading match the requested section.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply during category-navigation tasks when clicking a visible menu item produces repeated empty-action errors, especially when the accessibility tree exposes a direct link or destination URL.

skills.title: Open the Matching Product Listing
skills.principle:
1. Scan the current category or search results for the exact product title.
2. Activate the product-name link, not an adjacent cart, wishlist, or comparison control.
3. Confirm the destination by checking that the product page heading matches the requested item and its details are visible.
4. Report completion and stop once the matching product page is open.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to look at a specific shopping product and the item appears in the current results list or category page. Verify the product heading after navigation.

skills.title: Use Direct Product Search
skills.principle: When the target product is not visible, use the search combobox directly rather than scrolling repeatedly or clicking its label. Fill the exact product name, wait for the search control to enable, submit it, then select the result whose title exactly matches the target and verify the product page loads.
skills.when_to_apply: On a shopping catalog page when the target item is absent from the visible product list, especially when the search label is obstructed or the search button is initially disabled.

skills.title: Verify Pagination State Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current page indicator and URL before navigating. If the requested page is already active, report completion without clicking. Otherwise, select the pagination link matching the requested page, then confirm the resulting page indicator or item range reflects that page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on category or search listing pages when asked to navigate to a specific page and the accessibility tree exposes pagination controls, a current-page indicator, URL parameters, or item ranges.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids Reliably
skills.principle: When an accessibility tree shows an element with a numeric bid, invoke browser actions using that bid rather than copying its displayed name, icon, or escaped Unicode label. After the category navigation succeeds, inspect the refreshed page and select the category-specific “Page 2” control.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a shopping category from an accessibility tree, especially if repeated name-based clicks produce empty-action or element-not-found errors. Confirm the category page loaded before using pagination.

skills.title: Navigate Departments via Visible Menu
skills.principle: Identify the requested department by its visible menu label, activate that menu item, then verify completion using the page title, URL meaning, or main heading. Once the destination department is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to open a department and the current page exposes department navigation in the accessibility tree. Prefer the visible semantic label over incidental element identifiers.

skills.title: Terminate After Category Confirmation
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested department. Verify completion using the resulting page heading, breadcrumb, or URL. Once the requested category is visibly confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task only requires opening a department or category and the post-click page visibly confirms the requested destination.

skills.title: Navigate Directly to Requested Category
skills.principle: From the current shopping page, locate the main navigation entry matching the requested product category and activate it. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the page heading, breadcrumb, or URL reflects that category and products are listed. If the request lacks platform or product-type details, report the category is open and ask what to narrow next.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests browsing a broad product category without specifying a particular item, platform, brand, or subtype, and the site exposes that category in its primary navigation.

skills.title: Complete Required Product Options
skills.principle: When an Add to Cart action opens a product page instead of confirming success, inspect the form for required options. Select valid values for every required field, click that page’s Add to Cart button, and verify a success message or increased cart count before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a listing’s Add to Cart control redirects to a product configuration page, especially when the page shows required radio buttons, dropdowns, or an error stating that required options were not entered.

skills.title: Use One Valid Terminal Response
skills.principle: When the requested product data is already visible, extract the review count and rating, then issue exactly one properly structured `send_msg_to_user` action. Do not embed the action as plain text, repeat failed submissions, or navigate unnecessarily. After the response is accepted, terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for product-listing or product-detail questions when the target item’s review count and rating are visible in the accessibility tree and no additional verification is required.

skills.title: Use Direct Valid Completion Actions
skills.principle: When the page visibly contains the requested product facts, answer immediately with one valid direct completion action. Do not wrap the action inside explanatory JSON or resend malformed payloads. After the response is accepted, stop rather than repeating the same message.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product-detail or listing pages when review count and rating are already visible in the accessibility tree and the task only requests those facts.

skills.title: Configure Required Options Before Adding
skills.principle:
1. If a listing’s quick-add action opens the product page with a required-options warning, inspect fields marked with asterisks.
2. Select one valid value for every required option, such as color and size.
3. Click the product-page “Add to Cart” button only after all required fields show selected.
4. Confirm completion when the button changes to “Added” or the cart status updates.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding a product whose listing-level “Add to Cart” action redirects to its detail page or displays a missing-options warning. Begin with the target product identified and its detail page loaded.

skills.title: Verify Cart Addition Before Retrying
skills.principle: After selecting all required product options, click “Add to Cart” once and wait for the request to finish. Confirm success through the “Added” button, success alert, or cart-count update; then stop and verify the cart if needed. Do not click again while loading or after success, because repeated clicks can increase quantity unintentionally.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a configurable product to a shopping cart, especially when the page shows a loading state, changes the button to “Added,” displays a success alert, or updates the cart count.

skills.title: Match Product Before Wishlist Action
skills.principle: On a product listing, locate the target by its exact displayed name, then activate the “Add to Wish List” control within that product’s own list item. After navigation or refresh, verify completion using the success alert and the item’s presence in “My Wish List”; once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for logged-in shopping tasks requiring a specific listed product to be added to a wishlist, especially when multiple nearby products have similarly labeled action buttons.

skills.title: Use the Product-Scoped Wishlist Button
skills.principle: Locate the target product’s list item, then activate the “Add to Wish List” button within that same item—not the product title link or a guessed Unicode selector. Use the button’s current accessibility bid from the latest tree. After clicking, verify a success message or updated wishlist state before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specific product from a shopping listing, especially when multiple “Add to Wish List” buttons share the same label and accessibility bids differ from nearby product-link bids.

skills.title: Add the Target Product to Compare
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product by its visible name within the product listing.
2. In that same product container, activate the labeled “Add to Compare” control.
3. Open “Compare Products” and confirm the target name appears in the comparison table.
4. Once present, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks to add a specific listed product to a compare list, especially when multiple products have identical action buttons. Verify the matching product name before clicking.

skills.title: Stop After Compare Confirmation
skills.principle: After clicking a product’s “Add to Compare” control, inspect the updated page state. If an alert says the product was added to the comparison list, treat the task as complete and stop. Do not retry the control, refresh, or edit the search field afterward, since unnecessary actions can corrupt the query or undermine a successful state.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product to a shopping comparison list and the page displays an explicit success alert or updated comparison-list entry after the action.

skills.title: Set And Verify Sort Direction
skills.principle: Select the requested field in the “Sort By” control, then inspect the direction link’s label. Click it only when it indicates the opposite of the required direction. Verify the selected field, direction state, URL or visible item order, and stop once correct; do not toggle repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting a product-listing page by a specified field and direction, especially where a direction link alternates between “Set Ascending Direction” and “Set Descending Direction”.

skills.title: Use Combobox Bids for Sorting
skills.principle: When a sorting control is exposed as a combobox, use the combobox’s current accessibility bid—not its visible label—as the selector. Select the requested option by its exact option value, then verify the combobox value and product ordering changed. Do not click individual native option elements, which may be hidden even when listed in the accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on category or search result pages where sorting appears as a native combobox with options such as Position, Product Name, or Price.

skills.title: Use Facet Links, Not Select Controls
skills.principle: On category listing pages, inspect the accessibility role before choosing a filter. If the category facet is exposed as a list, click the link matching the requested subcategory rather than using select_option. Confirm completion from the updated URL, active-filter summary, and changed item count or heading before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when filtering products through sidebar facets, especially after an attempted select action reports that the target is not a <select> element.

skills.title: Verify Applied Facet Before Stopping
skills.principle: After selecting a category facet, inspect the refreshed page before taking another action. Confirm the URL or results heading reflects the selected category, and verify the active-filter area names that category. Once confirmed, stop; do not click nearby controls such as “Remove This Item” or “Clear All.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product listing pages when filtering by category or another shopping facet. Apply the facet first, then wait for the results page and active-filter state to update before deciding whether any further action is needed.

skills.title: Apply and Verify Price Facets
skills.principle: On a category results page, locate the requested price range under “Shopping Options” and select its link. Verify completion by checking that “Now Shopping by” lists the requested price range and the results heading/count updates. Report completion and stop once both confirmations are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests filtering a specific category by a displayed price range and the page provides clickable price facets under “Shopping Options”.

skills.title: Apply Facets, Then Verify Results
skills.principle: When a category page shows a price range under “Shopping Options,” treat it as an available filter, not an applied filter. Select the link matching the requested range, wait for the page to reload, then verify the URL or active-filter summary and updated item count reflect that range. Only report completion after this confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping category pages where the requested category is open but the desired price facet appears as an unselected link in “Shopping Options.”

skills.title: Read Cart Count From Header
skills.principle: For a request asking how many cart items exist, inspect the shopping site's cart summary first. Read the numeric count shown beside “My Cart” or in the opened cart preview, and report that value directly. Use the preview's explicit “Items in Cart” count when available; do not count product rows or quantities manually.
skills.when_to_apply: When the shopping page is loaded and the header exposes a “My Cart” summary or cart-preview control, especially when the user requests only the current cart item count.

skills.title: Report Visible Cart Count
skills.principle: When the page header visibly shows a cart count beside “My Cart,” read that number as the current item count, state it directly in the task response, and terminate immediately. Do not use repeated no-op actions or navigate elsewhere unless the count is absent or ambiguous.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for the shopping-cart item count and the current accessibility tree contains a clearly labeled “My Cart” count, with no conflicting cart information visible.

skills.title: Read Price Filters Directly
skills.principle: On a category listing page, inspect the accessibility tree’s “Shopping Options” or filter sidebar. Locate the “Price” section and report each displayed range together with its item count; selecting a range is unnecessary when the task asks what ranges are available. Confirm the ranges belong to the currently selected category before responding.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for available price ranges in a shopping category and the category listing already displays a filter sidebar with a “Price” section.

skills.title: Enumerate All Price Filter Ranges
skills.principle: On a category page, inspect every entry under the “Price” shopping option rather than treating the first range as exhaustive. Read each range label and item count, including “and above” entries, then report the complete set. Do not infer missing ranges from the visible product list or the selected filter state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for available price ranges in a shopping category and the page exposes a “Price” section with multiple filter links or entries.

skills.title: Read Category Facets Accurately
skills.principle: On a category listing page, inspect the “Shopping Options” section and read every entry under the “Category” heading, including displayed item counts. Also check “Now Shopping by” to distinguish available subcategories from an already-applied filter, then report both clearly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which categories are available within a shopping department and the page exposes category facets, especially when an active category filter may hide or contextualize the listing.

skills.title: Use Numeric Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When interacting with BrowserGym accessibility trees, use the numeric bid shown in brackets for the target element, not its rendered label, icon text, or Unicode glyph string. Re-read the current tree after each page change, perform the action on the matching numeric bid, and verify that the menu expands or navigation state changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a visible menu item or control repeatedly returns “could not find element” or “empty action” despite its label appearing in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Full Cart Before Checkout
skills.principle:
1. Select the header’s “My Cart” control and inspect the mini-cart contents.
2. Choose “View and Edit Cart” when the task requires viewing the full cart.
3. Confirm the “Shopping Cart” page shows the items, quantities, and summary, then select “Proceed to Checkout.”
4. Stop and report completion when the checkout shipping step is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: For shopping tasks requesting cart review followed by checkout, especially when “My Cart” opens a mini-cart dialog instead of navigating directly to the full cart page.

skills.title: Recover From Empty Click Actions
skills.principle: When a visible link’s click repeatedly produces an empty-action error, stop retrying the malformed click payload. Use the link’s observed destination URL with direct navigation, then verify the page heading or URL changed. Once the requested cart page is confirmed, use its “Proceed to Checkout” control and stop unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping navigation link is visible with a valid href, but BrowserGym click attempts return “Received an empty action” and the page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Pagination State After Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Locate the category pagination control labeled with the requested page number or “Page Next.”
2. Activate it only when the current page indicator does not already show the requested page.
3. Confirm completion using the URL parameter, current-page indicator, and displayed item range; then report the resulting page.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating paginated product-category listings, especially when the requested page may already be open. Ensure pagination controls and a current-page or item-range indicator are visible.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting the requested pagination link, verify the resulting URL or page heading shows the target page and item range. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not continue clicking other pagination links or oscillate between pages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests opening a specific product-list page and the page provides numbered pagination or Previous/Next controls.

skills.title: Navigate to a Nested Category
skills.principle:
1. On the parent category page, locate the Shopping Options or Category section.
2. Select the link whose label matches the requested subcategory.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page’s active category indicator and that the product listing reflects the selected subcategory.
4. Report completion once both indicators match the request.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific subcategory within an already open shopping category and the page exposes subcategory links or filters.

skills.title: Follow the Exact Category Hierarchy
skills.principle:
1. Hover the requested parent category and inspect its expanded submenu.
2. Select only a child whose label belongs to that parent; do not click a similarly named top-level sibling.
3. If the target is absent, inspect nested submenu items or reassess the hierarchy rather than using unrelated sidebar filters.
4. Confirm the resulting heading, breadcrumb, or active category reflects the requested parent-child path.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating shopping menus with similarly named categories, especially when the target subcategory may be nested or absent from the first expanded submenu.

skills.title: Verify Category Filter Completion
skills.principle: From a parent category listing, locate the requested subcategory under “Shopping Options” and activate its link. After navigation, verify completion using observable state: the page’s “Now Shopping by” area names the requested subcategory and the product listing reflects that filtered category. Then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests opening a named subcategory from an already loaded parent-category page and the page exposes subcategory links plus a filter-status area.

skills.title: Use the Visible Category Filter
skills.principle: On a category listing page, inspect the accessibility tree for the target subcategory under “Shopping Options” → “Category.” Activate that category link directly, rather than guessing navigation-menu or dropdown controls. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the URL, page heading, or item count reflects the target subcategory.
skills.when_to_apply: When the requested subsection is already exposed as a labeled category link in the current page’s accessibility tree, especially after guessed menu bids fail.

skills.title: Open Matching Product From Listing
skills.principle: Scan the current product listing for the target item's accessible name, then activate its product-name link rather than a nearby action button. Confirm completion when the destination page heading matches the target and shows product details and purchase controls such as price, options, and Add to Cart.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a specific product page from a shopping category or search-results listing, especially when the target is already visible among similarly structured product cards.

skills.title: Terminate After Product Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the target product detail page is displayed, verify its heading matches the requested item and that details or purchase options are visible. Then report completion and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for additional prompts.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a specific shopping product page and the accessibility tree shows the matching product heading, detail content, and purchase controls such as options, quantity, or “Add to Cart”.

skills.title: Browse Category Using Visible Controls
skills.principle:
1. From the current category page, select the navigation entry matching the requested category.
2. Verify the page heading and product count confirm the destination.
3. Use labeled subcategory or price filters only when they support browsing; verify the active filter in “Now Shopping by.”
4. Navigate with the visible “Page Next” control and confirm the item range changes before reporting findings.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to browse a shopping category and related products, especially when the page offers navigation menus, “Shop By” filters, and pagination. Verify each navigation or filter action before continuing.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids Reliably
skills.principle: When a target menu item appears in the accessibility tree, use its current numeric bid (for example, the menuitem’s listed ID), not its displayed text or decorative icon. After clicking, verify the URL, page heading, and product list changed to the requested category. If the action fails, re-inspect the refreshed tree rather than repeating the same selector; never treat a 404 page as success.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an e-commerce category from an accessibility-tree menu, especially after a click or hover reports an empty action or missing element. Confirm the target bid exists in the latest tree before acting.

skills.title: Complete Advanced Product Search
skills.principle:
1. Open the shopping site's “Advanced Search” page.
2. Fill the relevant product criterion and both minimum and maximum price fields, leaving unrelated fields blank.
3. Click the form’s “Search” button.
4. Confirm the results page summarizes the requested criteria and displays a matching item count before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requires products matching a name or other field plus a price range, and the site exposes an “Advanced Search” form with separate lower and upper price inputs.

skills.title: Use Numeric Price Range Fields
skills.principle: On Magento Advanced Search, treat both Price inputs as numeric bounds: enter the minimum and, only if needed, a numeric maximum. Do not enter the adjacent currency label (such as “USD”) into the maximum field. Submit Search, then verify that validation errors disappear and a results page or product list appears.
skills.when_to_apply: When using a shopping site's Advanced Search form with a Price range showing two textboxes separated by a dash and a currency label nearby.

skills.title: Read Price From Product Page
skills.principle: On a product-detail page, locate the target item's title and inspect the nearby price text. Report the displayed price directly, without selecting configurable options or adding the item to the cart unless the task explicitly requires it.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for a product's price and the product-detail page is open, showing the matching title and a visible price.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Price Immediately
skills.principle: When the target product page visibly shows the requested price, read the value associated with the product heading and report it directly. Do not select required options, add the item to cart, or repeat no-op actions. After sending the answer, terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product’s displayed price when the target product page is already open and the price is clearly present in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Search Before Declaring Product Unavailable
skills.principle: When the target product is not visible in the current listing, use the page’s Search field with the exact product name and submit it. Inspect search results and pagination before concluding it is unavailable; open the matching product and select its Reviews link or section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring reviews or details when the target item is absent from the currently displayed product list and a Search field or additional result pages are available.

skills.title: Use Review Pagination Efficiently
skills.principle: After opening the product’s Reviews section, read the visible review entries and inspect pagination controls. Select “Page 2” or “Page Next” when additional reviews exist instead of repeatedly scrolling. After each action, verify that the review content or page indicator changes; once the requested reviews are visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a product page expands a reviews tab and shows a review list with pagination links, especially when repeated scrolling leaves the accessibility tree unchanged.

skills.title: Read All Visible Product Variants
skills.principle: When a product page directly exposes a required variant group, inspect the complete group of labeled controls, count each distinct option, and report the labels exactly as displayed. Do not select an option or proceed to purchase when the task only asks to view available choices.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product-detail pages when the requested options are already visible as labeled controls, such as radio buttons under a Color, Size, or Style section.

skills.title: Inspect All Listed Product Options
skills.principle: When asked to view all options, inspect the complete labeled option group first and record every visible choice. Do not click each radio button unless selection changes hidden content or is explicitly required. Verify the list is complete, including the final option, then report the collected options.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product pages where options such as Color appear together as labeled radio buttons or swatches and the task asks to view or identify all available choices.

skills.title: Enumerate Product Option Labels Once
skills.principle: Locate the requested product attribute by its visible field label, then enumerate every associated option label (such as radio buttons) from the accessibility tree. Send one concise, correctly formatted response listing those options. Once the response is accepted or the goal is otherwise complete, stop instead of retrying or issuing additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping product page exposes the requested variants or attributes as labeled controls in the accessibility tree, especially radio-button groups or selectable option lists.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Options
skills.principle: When the requested product attribute is already visible, read every option associated with that attribute, distinguish it from neighboring attributes, and immediately provide the complete list in the task response. Do not click options unless selection is requested. After reporting the list, terminate rather than repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product detail pages when the requested attribute’s controls or labels are visible in the accessibility tree, especially when the task asks which options are available rather than asking you to select or purchase one.

skills.title: Read Product Rating Directly
skills.principle: On a product detail page, locate the rating summary near the product title or price. Read the displayed percentage or score and review count, then report the value exactly as shown. Do not interact with purchase options when the rating is already visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked for an item's overall rating and the product detail page is open or accessible. Confirm the rating summary and review count are visibly associated with the target item.

skills.title: Report the Displayed Rating
skills.principle: When the product page already shows a rating, read the explicit numeric value near “Rating:” (such as a percentage or score), rather than inferring from decorative or duplicated star icons. Return that value to the user immediately, then terminate without repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a product-details page where the target item is identified and a visible “Rating:” field includes an explicit numeric score or percentage.

skills.title: Use Direct Cart Navigation When Needed
skills.principle: If the cart header link is present but its clickable target is hidden or unstable, navigate directly to the cart page using its observed destination. Verify the resulting page heading and cart contents. If it states the cart is empty, report that checkout cannot proceed until items are added, then stop instead of probing an unsupported checkout URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests cart review or checkout, especially if the cart control times out or the cart page visibly reports no items.

skills.title: Select Required Product Options
skills.principle: Before adding a configurable product, inspect the form for required fields. Select one valid option in every required group, such as Color and Material Type, then click “Add to Cart.” Verify the cart contains the item before proceeding to checkout; if validation errors remain, resolve them instead of repeatedly retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When an ecommerce product page shows required option groups or “This is a required field” validation after clicking “Add to Cart,” especially when the cart remains empty.

skills.title: Use My Account for Profile and Orders
skills.principle: Select the authenticated site's “My Account” navigation link. Confirm the destination by checking for account information such as contact details and a “Recent Orders” table or “My Orders” link. Once both profile and order-history access are visible, report completion without opening unnecessary order details.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping site starts on another page and the user asks to view their profile and order history; the page must expose a “My Account” or equivalent account-navigation entry.

skills.title: Terminate After Account Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page heading shows “My Account” and profile details plus recent orders or a “View All” orders link are visible, treat the task as complete. Report that the account page has been opened, then terminate the browser interaction instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For requests to view an authenticated shopping account’s profile and order history, after navigating through “My Account” and confirming the expected account and order sections are displayed.

skills.title: Use Pagination for Exact Product Matching
skills.principle: When a category page contains many products, compare full product titles rather than settling for similar items. If the target is absent from the visible listings, use the page’s explicit “Page Next” or numbered pagination control, then rescan the new page. Open the listing whose title exactly matches the requested product and verify the product detail page shows the matching heading and details.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring a specific product in a paginated category listing, especially when visible results contain similar but non-identical products.

skills.title: Validate Browser Actions Before Repeating
skills.principle: When an action returns an empty-action or parsing error, inspect the emitted tool payload rather than repeating the same intent. Send one complete, syntactically valid action with all arguments (for example, fill the search field with the target query), then verify the field contains text and the Search control becomes enabled before submitting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use during product searches or other multi-step shopping tasks when the accessibility tree remains unchanged, the intended action reports an empty or malformed payload, or a control stays disabled.

skills.title: Disambiguate Duplicate Product Controls
skills.principle: On a product page, locate the control by its accessible name and role, not a stale numeric ID. Distinguish the product action link labeled “Add to Wish List” from nearby gallery controls, then click the matching action and verify a success message or updated wish-list state before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When a product page contains repeated links, dynamic accessibility IDs, or image-gallery overlays, especially after navigation changes the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Product Availability Before Concluding
skills.principle: Use the store’s Search field with the exact product name before declaring an item unavailable. If browsing category results, inspect pagination and confirm each newly loaded page; when the exact product appears, open its product link and select its “Reviews” link. Only report unavailability after search and all relevant result pages show no exact match.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to read reviews or details for a specific product and it is not visible in the current category results, especially when pagination or a site-wide search field is available.

skills.title: Inspect Search Results Before Scrolling
skills.principle: After submitting a product search, inspect the accessibility tree and result list for the exact or clearly matching product title. If present, open its product link or Reviews link immediately and verify the review section. Do not infer absence from viewport position or begin pagination while matching results are already available.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping search-results pages when the requested product may be present in the rendered accessibility tree, even if it is not visually obvious in the current viewport.

skills.title: Search Exact Product Names
skills.principle: Use the store’s search field with the full product name or model identifier, submit the search, then inspect the results list. Match the requested item by its visible title and read the price shown in the same product entry, avoiding similarly named products.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks for a product’s price and the storefront provides a search field. Ensure the results page visibly contains the requested product before reporting its listed price.

skills.title: Report Visible Price and Stop
skills.principle: When the target product page clearly shows the product identity and price, extract the displayed price, provide it directly to the user, and terminate. Do not continue issuing no-op actions after the requested fact has been verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product price when the matching product page or listing visibly contains the target item and an associated price.

skills.title: Search Before Declaring a Product Missing
skills.principle: Use the store’s Search field with the exact product name first. If search is unavailable or returns no match, inspect every available pagination link, such as “Page 2” or “Page Next,” before concluding the product is absent. Only report unavailability after exhausting the listed results and confirming no matching product details or rating.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a product attribute on a shopping site and the current product listing does not contain the target. Requires a visible search control or pagination that can be checked.

skills.title: Report Retrieved Information and Terminate
skills.principle: Once the target product’s rating is visible and correctly associated with its product title, provide the requested rating in the final response. Do not repeat no-op actions; completing an observation is not the same as submitting the answer.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for product-information tasks when the listing or details page visibly shows the target item and its customer rating, with no further navigation required.

skills.title: Compare Matching Product Prices
skills.principle: Review all visible product listings, select items whose names or descriptions match the requested feature, record each displayed price, and sort the resulting products from lowest to highest. Include the price range and distinguish clearly relevant variants from unrelated products.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on category or search pages when asked to compare prices for products sharing a feature, especially when multiple matching items appear among unrelated listings.

skills.title: Read Listing Prices Directly
skills.principle: For a price-comparison request, inspect the current product listing and pair each relevant product title with its adjacent displayed price. Use semantic product names and visible text, not accessibility IDs or product-title links. If needed, switch to list view, adjust items per page, sort by price, or paginate; then report the collected prices without opening product pages or using the compare feature.
skills.when_to_apply: When the requested products and prices are already visible in a shopping-category listing, especially when the page contains multiple irrelevant products and navigation controls.

skills.title: Verify Review Count on Product Page
skills.principle:
1. Search for the requested product using the storefront search field and submit the search.
2. From results, choose the matching product title, not merely a related item.
3. On the product page, read the review count from the rating summary or the Reviews tab/link.
4. Report the count only after the product identity and displayed count correspond.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product’s review count when search results may contain multiple related products and the product page exposes a Reviews count.

skills.title: Read Review Counts From Search Results
skills.principle: Search for the requested product, then inspect result cards for the matching product title or model. Read the number in the adjacent “Reviews” link directly; open the product page only if the count is absent. Once the matching count is visible, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search returns multiple similar products and the task asks only for a review count. Verify the result title matches the requested item before using its adjacent Reviews count.

skills.title: Verify Product Absence Across Pages
skills.principle: When a requested product is not visible, inspect the full current listing and follow the available pagination control. Confirm the next page loads and review its product names; only after all listed pages are checked, report that the item is unavailable rather than adding a different product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping requests on storefronts with paginated product listings, when the target item is absent from the initially visible products and pagination controls expose additional results.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After each page update, inspect the fresh accessibility tree and use the element’s current bid (often numeric) for actions. Match the bid to the intended role and nearby label, rather than passing the visible label as an identifier. If an action fails, re-read the tree and select the updated bid before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When a BrowserGym action reports that an element cannot be found, especially for search fields or form controls whose visible labels differ from their accessibility bids.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree and current URL to identify the requested destination. If a clearly labeled navigation link exists, activate it, then verify the resulting page heading, URL, or distinctive controls. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and stop instead of performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to navigation tasks when the page exposes a labeled link or other route to the requested destination, and completion can be confirmed through the resulting URL, heading, or page-specific controls.

skills.title: Open Cart Preview Then Full Cart
skills.principle:
1. Identify the header control labeled “My Cart” and activate it.
2. If it opens a cart preview dialog, verify that cart items are shown, then select “View and Edit Cart” to open the full cart page.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading “Shopping Cart” and visible item table before reporting the result.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to or inspect a shopping cart and the storefront’s “My Cart” control opens a preview dialog instead of directly navigating to the full cart page.

skills.title: Verify Navigation and Use Direct Fallback
skills.principle: After activating a cart link, verify the URL or page heading changed to the cart and that cart items are visible. If the page remains unchanged, use the link’s observed destination URL directly rather than repeatedly clicking a stale element ID. Once “Shopping Cart” and its item table appear, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to a shopping cart from a product or category page, especially if clicks appear ineffective, the URL remains unchanged, or accessibility-element IDs become stale after navigation.

skills.title: Add the Correct Product to Wishlist
skills.principle: Identify the target product by its visible name within the product list, then activate that product row’s “Add to Wish List” control rather than relying on position alone. Confirm completion from the resulting success alert, wishlist count, or visible wishlist entry, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping page lists the requested product and each product row provides an “Add to Wish List” control. Verify the target name and resulting wishlist state before finishing.

skills.title: Sort Products by Price Descending
skills.principle:
1. In the product-list toolbar, set the “Sort By” control to “Price.”
2. Activate the direction control labeled “Set Descending Direction.”
3. Confirm completion when the control changes to “Set Ascending Direction,” the URL indicates descending price order, and visible prices decrease from top to bottom.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping category page must be ordered from highest to lowest price and it provides a “Sort By” selector plus an ascending/descending direction control.

skills.title: Reinspect Accessibility Targets After Errors
skills.principle: After a locator error, re-read the current accessibility tree and identify the control by its role and nearby label, then use its current target identifier. For product sorting, select the “Price” option in the “Sort By” combobox, activate “Set Descending Direction,” and verify the combobox state and product prices are reordered highest first before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping listing exposes sorting controls but an interaction reports a missing element or stale locator. Reinspect the latest page state before retrying, especially after navigation or UI updates.

skills.title: Verify Existing Category Filters
skills.principle: Check the shopping page’s “Now Shopping by” section before changing filters. If it explicitly shows the requested category, verify the displayed products are consistent, report that the filter is already applied, and stop without redundant navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to filter a product listing and the page is already open; use this when “Now Shopping by” visibly lists the requested category.

skills.title: Confirm Active Filter and Finish
skills.principle: When the product listing already shows the requested category in the active-filter or “Now Shopping by” section, treat the filter as applied. Verify the listing state once, then report completion and terminate rather than issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping category pages when the requested category is visibly listed among active filters, such as “Now Shopping by,” and the page has loaded successfully.

skills.title: Inspect and Summarize Cart Contents
skills.principle: Click the header’s “My Cart” control to open the cart summary dialog. Read each line item and its quantity, distinguish total units from unique products, aggregate repeated products, and report the subtotal when shown. Stop once the dialog provides complete cart contents.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked what is currently in a shopping cart and the page exposes a “My Cart” link or item-count indicator. Ensure the cart summary dialog is open before reporting.

skills.title: Reconcile Cart Count Before Reporting
skills.principle: Open the cart and verify both the displayed total quantity and each line item’s quantity. Distinguish total units from distinct products or line items. If the observed count differs from the requested count, explicitly report the discrepancy and provide the cart contents actually shown rather than treating the request’s count as fact.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect a shopping cart with a specified item count, especially when a cart preview or page displays totals, quantities, and duplicate product lines.

skills.title: Use Simple Completion Messages
skills.principle: After confirming the search result, send one concise, properly quoted completion message stating the outcome and any useful next step. Avoid nested quotes, unnecessary escaping, or repeated malformed attempts. Once the message is accepted, stop interacting.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping search has completed and the page visibly reports results or no matches, especially before using send-message actions that require correctly formatted string arguments.

skills.title: Confirm Search Results Before Finishing
skills.principle: After submitting Advanced Search, inspect the new results page rather than waiting unnecessarily. Confirm it shows the expected search criteria and a results count or matching products, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an e-commerce Advanced Search form has been submitted and the page visibly changes to search results showing the applied criteria or matching-item count.

skills.title: Open Product Details From Listings
skills.principle: On a shopping category page, locate the listing whose accessible name matches the requested product and activate its product-title link or image. Confirm navigation by checking that the product detail page shows the matching title and product information. Once the details page is visible, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific product’s details and the current page is a category, search-results, or product-listing page containing the requested item.

skills.title: Open Complete Order History
skills.principle: From the signed-in account dashboard, distinguish the limited “Recent Orders” table from its “View All” link. Activate the link labeled “View All” near that section, then verify the resulting page shows the complete order-history list rather than only the dashboard summary.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping account dashboard displays a “Recent Orders” summary and the task asks to view all past or recently ordered items. Requires an authenticated account and a visible order-history navigation link.

skills.title: Use Account Dashboard Order Sections
skills.principle: From the shopping homepage, open the authenticated “My Account” link. On the account dashboard, locate the “Recent Orders” table to view currently listed orders and items. If the task requires the complete order history rather than the dashboard subset, use its adjacent “View All” or “My Orders” link. Confirm the relevant order list is visible before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping task asks for recently ordered items or order history and the current page is not already the account dashboard.

skills.title: Use Advanced Search Form Correctly
skills.principle: When the site opens Advanced Search, use the dedicated form rather than the header search: fill the textbox labeled “Product Name” with the target product, then click the form’s “Search” button. Verify that results appear, select the matching product title, and confirm the product-detail page has loaded.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping-site search link leads to an Advanced Search page, especially when the header search control is disabled or behaves differently from the page’s dedicated search form.

skills.title: Inspect Cart Preview Before Navigating
skills.principle: When the header’s cart control displays an item count, activate it and inspect the resulting cart dialog or preview. Extract each visible product name, quantity if shown, price, and subtotal. If the preview contains the requested information, report it immediately without opening the full cart page or taking additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking what is currently in the cart, when a visible cart control shows an item count and activating it produces a dialog or preview with cart contents.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Element Identifiers
skills.principle: When a visible control repeatedly fails to click, stop retrying its displayed accessible name. Re-read the latest accessibility tree, identify the control’s current numeric bid, and click that bid. For a link whose observed href is unambiguous, navigate directly to that href instead. Confirm the URL or page heading changed before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping page shows a cart or other navigation link, but clicks using its visible label or icon text return element-not-found or empty-action errors.

skills.title: Filter Search Results by Category
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested product query in the store’s search field and activate Search.
2. On the results page, locate the category facet matching the requested category and select it.
3. Confirm completion when the results show the query, the selected category under “Now Shopping by,” and the filtered item count.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring a keyword search constrained to a specific category, when the results page exposes category facets with item counts.

skills.title: Use Accessibility IDs for Search
skills.principle: Inspect the current accessibility tree and target controls by their observed bid and role, not visible label text. For a product search, fill the search combobox, verify the Search button becomes enabled, activate it, and confirm the results page reflects the query. If the desired category is absent, use the site’s search control rather than repeatedly clicking nonexistent filters.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping page exposes controls in the accessibility tree but text-based bids fail, especially when filters do not list the requested product category.

skills.title: Verify Existing Filters Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the active-filter area and current results before changing a shopping category. If the requested price range is already listed as active, use the displayed result count or URL state as confirmation, report completion, and stop. Otherwise, select the matching price link under Shopping Options, then verify the active filter and updated results count.
skills.when_to_apply: On a category or search-results page where the task requests a price range and the page may already contain that filter. Verify active filters or URL state before clicking, and confirm results after applying changes.

skills.title: Verify Filter State Before Repeating
skills.principle: After selecting a price facet, verify completion using the URL, the “Now Shopping by” summary, and the result count. If they show the requested range, treat the filter as applied and stop. Do not clear or reapply it merely because product names or counts differ from expectations; use the visible facet label rather than stale element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering a category listing by price or another sidebar facet, especially after navigation changes the accessibility-tree element IDs or the filtered result set looks unfamiliar.

skills.title: Use Category Navigation and Verify Page
skills.principle:
1. Locate the navigation entry matching the requested product category by its visible label or role.
2. Select it and wait for the page state to update.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading and product listings identify the requested category, then report that the products are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to look at products in a named shopping category and the current page shows a different category. Requires a visible category navigation menu and a resulting product-list page.

skills.title: Use Valid, Current Element References
skills.principle: After each observation, target the currently visible element by its accessible role or label rather than a stale bid. Emit a complete, correctly formatted browser action, then verify the page changed. If a menu item is hidden, open its parent menu or use the visible search control; do not repeatedly retry an invisible or malformed action.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigation or form actions return empty-action, parsing, or visibility errors, especially after the page refreshes and accessibility-tree element identifiers or visibility states may have changed.

skills.title: Open Full Shopping Cart Details
skills.principle: Select the header cart control, then use the cart overlay’s “View and Edit Cart” link rather than “Proceed to Checkout.” Confirm completion when the page title is “Shopping Cart” and the cart-items table displays item names, quantities, prices, and totals.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or inspect cart contents and the site’s cart control opens a summary dialog. Requires a visible cart control and, for full details, a “View and Edit Cart” link.

skills.title: Stop After Cart Contents Appear
skills.principle: Once the cart page is reached and the shopping-cart item table or item list is visible, the viewing task is complete. Report completion and terminate instead of opening item editors, retrying stale controls, or performing unrelated cart actions.
skills.when_to_apply: For requests to view cart contents, after selecting the cart entry and observing a Shopping Cart heading with listed items. Do not continue into item details unless the user explicitly requests editing or inspection.

skills.title: Verify Wishlist Page State
skills.principle:
1. From an authenticated shopping page, select the navigation link labeled “My Wish List.”
2. Confirm the destination heading identifies the wishlist and inspect its status message.
3. Report whether saved items are present; if the page states there are none, report the empty wishlist and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a customer’s saved shopping items and the account navigation exposes “My Wish List.” Authentication must already be active.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Wishlist Page
skills.principle: Use the current URL and page heading to distinguish a wishlist preview from the actual wishlist page. Click the visible “My Wish List” or “Go to Wish List” link, then verify navigation by checking the URL or page heading and confirming the saved-item list is displayed before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping page shows a “My Wish List” item preview or count but the current URL and page heading still identify another page, especially for authenticated users.

skills.title: Navigate Categories by Visible Labels
skills.principle: From any product-category page, locate the navigation menu item matching the requested category and activate it. Verify the destination by checking the page heading and visible product listing, then summarize representative items and available subcategory filters. Once the requested category is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to browse a broad shopping category and the current page exposes category navigation plus a product listing or category heading.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Requested Category
skills.principle: Navigate to the requested shopping category, then verify the page heading or breadcrumb matches it. For a broad browsing request without a specific product, treat that state as complete and stop instead of opening arbitrary subcategories, paging through listings, or inspecting products.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks only to browse or access a named category and provides no product, price, or filtering criteria. Confirm the category label is visible before terminating.

skills.title: Execute And Verify Product Search
skills.principle:
1. Locate the page’s search combobox and focus it.
2. Enter the requested product keyword; wait for the Search control to become enabled.
3. Activate Search, then verify the results page heading or URL contains the submitted keyword and product listings are displayed.
4. Report completion only after this state is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks requiring keyword-based product discovery when a search field and submit control are visible. Verify navigation to search results before reporting success.

skills.title: Re-locate Search Controls After Navigation
skills.principle: After submitting a search, inspect the new accessibility tree before further interaction. Re-identify the current search combobox and Search button by their roles and labels; do not reuse stale element IDs from the previous page. Enter the requested product keyword, submit, and verify the heading reflects that keyword or results appear.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching products across page navigations or search-results refreshes, especially when element IDs change or the tree shows stale, hidden, or non-input elements.

skills.title: Use Footer Policy Links
skills.principle: When a task asks to view a site policy, inspect the accessibility tree for the footer (contentinfo) and activate the link matching the requested policy. Verify completion by checking the destination heading or page title, then summarize the relevant visible sections and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping sites when the requested privacy, cookie, terms, or similar informational page is not immediately open and the accessibility tree exposes footer navigation links.

skills.title: Terminate After Reaching Requested Page
skills.principle: Once the page matching the user’s request is visible, verify its heading or content, report completion, and terminate the task. Do not repeatedly issue no-op actions while waiting for the user to read an already displayed page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for information-viewing tasks when navigation has reached the requested page and its relevant heading or content is visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Search Control Roles
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s role and accessible name to identify controls before acting. Fill the actual search combobox, then activate the enabled Search button; use the Advanced Search link only when needed. After submission, inspect the results or explicit no-results state before concluding the product is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching a shopping site and multiple nearby elements have similar labels or stale element identifiers, especially after an interaction error. Confirm the current control roles and enabled state before retrying.

skills.title: Report Price Once Confirmed
skills.principle: When the matching product page visibly shows the requested price, treat the task as complete: provide the product name and displayed price in the final response, then terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for another page state after the evidence is already present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product price when the page title matches the requested item and a visible price is present.

skills.title: Open a Specific Order
skills.principle:
1. From any shopping page, open “My Account” and locate the “Recent Orders” table or “My Orders” page.
2. Match the requested order number exactly within the order-number column.
3. In that same row, select “View Order,” not “Reorder.”
4. Confirm the destination displays the requested order number in the page heading before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for authenticated shopping tasks requesting order details, especially when multiple orders appear in a table and each row provides separate “View Order” and “Reorder” actions.

skills.title: Use Observed URLs When Bids Fail
skills.principle: When a visible link repeatedly fails by accessibility bid, use its observed destination URL with direct navigation instead of retrying stale identifiers. After navigation, verify the page heading and target record, then activate the record’s detail link or navigate to its observed detail URL. Never submit an empty action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on account/order pages when the target link is visible but bid-based clicks return “element not found,” especially after navigation or accessibility-tree changes.

skills.title: Retrieve Order Status and Details
skills.principle:
1. Open the signed-in account area and locate the order-history or Recent Orders table.
2. Match the requested order number exactly, then select its associated “View Order” control.
3. Verify the order page heading and status, then read requested details from labeled sections such as Items Ordered and Order Information.
4. Report the verified status and relevant details, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for signed-in shopping tasks requesting a specific order’s status or details, when the account page exposes order history or a Recent Orders table with per-order “View Order” controls.

skills.title: Use Semantic Order-Row Matching
skills.principle: On the account page, inspect the current order table and match the requested order number in its row before acting. Activate that row’s “View Order” link, not the surrounding table or a stale element reference. If absent, activate the actual “View All” navigation link or “My Orders,” then inspect the resulting order-history page and pagination. Confirm the destination displays the requested order number and status.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a specific order from a shopping account, especially when it is not listed in Recent Orders or repeated clicks leave the page unchanged. Requires an authenticated account and a current accessibility tree.

skills.title: Read Default Billing Address
skills.principle: Open the signed-in user's “My Account” page, then locate the “Default Billing Address” section and transcribe its complete name, address, country, and phone. If the displayed name differs slightly from the requested name, verify identity using other account evidence such as the email or recent orders before reporting the address.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a signed-in customer's default billing address and the storefront shows a “My Account” link or account dashboard with address information.

skills.title: Verify Customer Identity Before Reporting
skills.principle: Confirm the signed-in customer matches the requested person before using account details. If names differ, do not report the displayed customer’s billing address as the target’s. Search the account page for a supported account switch or a matching customer record; if none exists, clearly report that the target’s address is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an account page displays a different customer name than the requested person, especially when billing or shipping details are customer-specific.

skills.title: Edit and Verify Saved Address
skills.principle:
1. Open the account’s Address Book and locate the relevant default or additional address entry.
2. Select its “Change” or edit control to open the editable address form.
3. Fill the field labeled “Street Address: Line 1” with the requested value, then click “Save Address.”
4. Confirm completion by checking the success alert and the displayed address value.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when updating a signed-in shopper’s saved billing or shipping address, especially when the Address Book initially shows only summarized address text rather than editable fields.

skills.title: Verify Saved Changes Then Stop
skills.principle: After submitting an account change, inspect the resulting page for a success message and the updated value. Once both confirm completion, report success and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a shopping account or address form, after clicking its save or submit control and the page returns to a confirmation or summary view.

skills.title: Update Address Country and Region
skills.principle:
1. Open the account’s address book and choose the relevant billing or shipping address edit control.
2. Select the requested country; when the country changes, inspect the refreshed State/Province field and choose a valid region if required.
3. Save the address, then verify the confirmation message and displayed country/region before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a customer’s address country in a shopping account, especially when country selection dynamically replaces the region options or makes the region field required.

skills.title: Verify and Stop After Saving
skills.principle: After opening the relevant address editor, inspect the current country value. If it already matches the requested country, click “Save Address” once. Confirm completion using the success alert and the address listing showing the target country, then terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or reopen the editor after the save succeeds.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for account address-country updates when the address editor or address book is visible, especially when the target country may already be selected. Requires an authenticated account and a recognizable save confirmation.

skills.title: Verify Search Control Before Filling
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to confirm the search element’s role before acting. Fill the element identified as a combobox with the product name, then activate the Search button and inspect results. Do not treat an unrelated link, stale element ID, or a few category pages as evidence that the product is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating a named product on a shopping site, especially when multiple nearby controls have similar labels or element references and the search field is exposed as a combobox.

skills.title: Report Rating After Verification
skills.principle: Search for the target product, confirm the exact product title, and read the percentage adjacent to its “Rating:” label. Once the percentage is visible in the results or product page, immediately report it to the user and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions or continue browsing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product’s rating percentage, after a search result or product page visibly identifies the requested item and displays its rating.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Pagination
skills.principle: Select the requested category first, then use the current accessibility tree to identify the pagination link’s numeric bid. Click that bid and re-check the updated URL or active-page indicator before continuing. Do not repeatedly invoke clicks using visible link text when the browser tool requires bids.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating category listings with BrowserGym and a text-based click fails or the page remains unchanged. Re-observe the accessibility tree, confirm the target listing context, and use the newly provided pagination bid.

skills.title: Use Exact Search Suggestions
skills.principle: After entering a product name, inspect the autocomplete list. If an exact product suggestion appears, select it or submit the search, then open the matching product and use its “Add to Cart” control. Do not browse unrelated categories while an exact search suggestion remains unprocessed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site’s search field displays an autocomplete option matching the requested product name, especially before pagination or category browsing.

skills.title: Use Valid Search Actions
skills.principle: When locating a product, issue a complete, correctly formatted action targeting the observed search combobox: click or focus it, fill the query, then press Enter or activate Search. After each action, verify the field value or resulting results page before retrying; do not repeat malformed actions that produce empty-action errors.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on shopping pages when the target product is not visible in the current listing and the accessibility tree exposes a search combobox or Search control.

skills.title: Add a Product to Compare
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product card by its displayed name, keeping its controls associated with that card.
2. Click that card’s “Add to Compare” button.
3. Confirm the success alert, comparison-list entry, or increased “Compare Products” count, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping category or search-results page visibly lists the requested product and provides an “Add to Compare” control; verify the resulting success state before taking further actions.

skills.title: Verify Compare Addition In Context
skills.principle: After clicking the target product’s “Add to Compare” control, inspect the resulting page for an assertive confirmation stating it was added to the comparison list and check the compare-item count or listed product. If either confirms success, stop; do not retry or misinterpret an existing compare-list entry as failure.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product to a shopping site’s compare list, especially when the page provides an asynchronous confirmation alert or a persistent compare-item count.

skills.title: Verify Cart Contents Before Reporting
skills.principle: Open the shopping cart using the cart control. If a preview dialog appears, select “View and Edit Cart” to inspect the complete item table. Verify the displayed item count and listed products, then report the actual cart state rather than assuming the requested count; do not modify items unless explicitly instructed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view shopping-cart contents and the cart indicator conflicts with the requested item count, especially when a complete itemized view is needed.

skills.title: Use the Cart Link Destination Directly
skills.principle: When a visible cart control is obstructed or its accessibility identifier resolves to another element, stop retrying the same click. Read the cart link’s destination from the current observation and navigate directly to it. Confirm completion by checking for the “Shopping Cart” heading and the cart-items table.
skills.when_to_apply: When an online store shows a cart-count link but clicking it repeatedly times out, especially when the reported element identifier maps to a search label or another intercepting control.

skills.title: Interpret Sort Direction Controls Correctly
skills.principle: On a product listing, select the desired sort field, then interpret the direction link as the action it will perform—not the current state. If it says “Set Descending Direction,” prices are currently ascending; leave it unchanged. If it says “Set Ascending Direction,” click it once, then verify the first and last visible prices or URL state before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When sorting products by price on a paginated shopping category, especially after selecting “Price.” Use the displayed direction label and resulting price order to confirm ascending or descending state before taking another action.

skills.title: Add Multiple Target Products Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Locate each requested product by its visible name within the product list, then activate that product’s adjacent “Add to Cart” control.
2. Wait for the update and verify the control changes to “Added” or a matching cart alert appears before continuing.
3. Repeat for every remaining target, then report completion only after each target shows successful addition.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requires adding several distinct products from a listing page, especially when the cart already contains unrelated items and the header count alone cannot confirm the requested additions.

skills.title: Use Cart Controls for Cart Tasks
skills.principle: When the task says add products to the cart, use each matching product’s “Add to Cart” control, not “Add to Compare.” After each addition, verify a cart confirmation or updated cart item count, then confirm all requested products appear in “My Cart” before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on shopping product listings or detail pages whenever the requested destination is the cart. Distinguish similarly labeled controls such as “Add to Cart,” “Add to Compare,” and “Add to Wish List” before acting.

skills.title: Navigate Cart Through Checkout Review
skills.principle:
1. Select the header cart control and, if a mini-cart dialog opens, choose “View and Edit Cart” to reach the full Shopping Cart page.
2. Verify the cart contents, then select “Proceed to Checkout.”
3. On Shipping, confirm an address and selected shipping method, then choose “Next.”
4. Stop at “Review & Payments” once the order summary and “Place Order” control are visible; do not place the order unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view cart items and proceed to checkout, with an existing cart and usable shipping address or checkout profile. Completion is the Review & Payments page.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Order Success
skills.principle: After submitting an order, inspect the resulting page state before acting again. If it shows a success page with a purchase confirmation and order number, report completion and terminate immediately. Do not retry the payment action or continue waiting based on stale checkout observations, even if the previous click returned a timeout.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking “Place Order” when the interface may show a loading overlay or delayed navigation. Verify the current page contains explicit purchase-success text and an order confirmation before stopping.

skills.title: Use the My Account Entry
skills.principle: Identify the account-navigation link by its visible role or label, such as “My Account,” and activate it. Confirm completion when the resulting page has an account heading and management sections such as contact information, addresses, or recent orders; then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to an account page from another shopping-site page, especially while signed in and a visible “My Account” link appears in the header or banner.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Click Actions
skills.principle: When an interaction returns an empty-action or parsing error, stop repeating the same malformed command. Reconstruct a valid action using the current accessibility-tree target, or navigate directly to the target link’s observed destination. Confirm success by checking that the URL or page content changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a visible account or navigation link remains unchanged after an attempted click and the tool reports an empty action, malformed payload, or parsing error.

skills.title: Verify Wishlist Page Before Acting
skills.principle: Check the current page and accessibility tree first.
