If it already shows the wishlist heading and saved-item controls, treat the navigation goal as complete; otherwise activate the visible “My Wish List” or “Go to Wish List” link. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and item listing, then report completion without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open or view a signed-in shopping wishlist, especially when the current page may already contain a wishlist sidebar or direct wishlist navigation link.

skills.title: Recover From Empty Click Actions
skills.principle: When a visible navigation link is present but a click returns an empty-action error, submit a clean, minimal action using the current observation’s semantic target, without malformed escaping, extra modifiers, or unnecessary parameters. If clicking still fails, navigate using the link’s observed destination URL. Verify the URL or page heading changes before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for BrowserGym navigation when an accessibility-tree link clearly matches the requested destination but the action payload repeatedly produces an empty-action or formatting error.

skills.title: Navigate Categories by Visible Label
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to find the navigation entry whose visible label matches the requested category, then activate that entry. Verify completion by checking that the page heading, breadcrumb, URL context, or displayed item listing reflects the target category. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task requests navigation to a product category and the current page exposes category navigation entries in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Validate Actions and Stop on Confirmation
skills.principle: Use a valid, complete action payload with a semantic target such as the visible category label, rather than repeatedly submitting malformed or truncated selectors. After clicking, verify the URL, page title, or main heading matches the requested category. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating ecommerce category menus, especially after an action returns an empty-action error or the page state changes. Reinspect the accessibility tree and stop immediately when the requested category is visibly loaded.

skills.title: Navigate to Advanced Search
skills.principle: Use the visible “Advanced Search” link in the site header or footer. After activation, verify the page heading and URL indicate “Advanced Search”; report completion when the detailed fields, such as Product Name, SKU, Description, and Price, are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a shopping site’s advanced product-search page and the current accessibility tree exposes an “Advanced Search” link.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Page
skills.principle: When the task asks only for navigation, click the relevant navigation link, then verify the destination using the page heading or URL. Once the requested page is visibly loaded, report completion and terminate instead of filling forms or performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the target page is confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive controls. Do not proceed into optional workflows unless the instruction explicitly requests them.

skills.title: Verify Homepage Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and visible page content first. If the root store URL and homepage elements such as product showcases are already present, report completion and stop. Otherwise, activate the semantic store-logo or Home link, then verify the URL and homepage content before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open an e-commerce store’s homepage, especially from an arbitrary category or product page. Use the observed URL and homepage landmarks to confirm completion before taking further actions.

skills.title: Verify Homepage Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting the store logo or navigating directly, inspect the resulting page state. If the URL is the site root and the main-store heading or homepage content is visible, treat navigation as complete, report success, and terminate instead of repeating clicks, refreshes, or navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open an online store’s homepage from another page, after a navigation action produces a site-root URL and recognizable homepage content.

skills.title: Verify Category Navigation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Click the navigation entry matching the requested category, then verify the resulting page by checking its URL, page heading, and visible category contents. Once these observations confirm the requested category is active, report completion and stop without additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks you to navigate to a category and the page provides labeled navigation entries plus a category heading or URL that can confirm successful navigation.

skills.title: Validate Category Navigation Actions
skills.principle: Use the category’s visible menu item or an observed destination link with valid browser-action syntax. After acting, verify that the URL, page heading, or breadcrumb reflects the requested category. If the page remains unchanged or an action is rejected, inspect the updated accessibility tree and retry with a supported control rather than inventing URL fragments or declaring success.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating between shopping categories, especially from a menuitem with a popup, and the initial click produces no page change, an empty-action error, or unchanged heading/breadcrumb.

skills.title: Navigate Categories via Visible Menu
skills.principle: Select the requested category directly from the visible navigation menu, then verify navigation succeeded by checking the page URL and main heading for the category name. Once the heading and product listing confirm the destination, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping task asks you to open a product category and the current page displays a navigation menu containing the requested category.

skills.title: Read Price Directly From Product Page
skills.principle: Locate the target product’s main content and identify the standalone currency amount near its title, availability, SKU, or purchase controls. Verify it belongs to the requested item, then report the displayed price immediately without adding items or navigating elsewhere.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping product page is already open and the accessibility tree exposes the requested item title and a nearby currency-formatted price.

skills.title: Report Visible Product Prices Immediately
skills.principle: When the product page visibly shows the requested price, extract the displayed amount and return it in the task response. Do not issue repeated no-op actions; once the answer is verified, report completion and terminate the browsing trajectory.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking for a product price when the matching product page is loaded and an observable price is displayed near the product title or purchase controls.

skills.title: Verify Product Availability Before Reporting
skills.principle: When a requested product is absent from the visible listing, inspect the complete available inventory: check the current page, use visible pagination to open subsequent pages, and compare product names. Only after all relevant pages are checked should you report that the product is unavailable and suggest a direct search.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task targets a specific product that is not visible in the initial listing and pagination or other inventory-navigation controls are available.

skills.title: Expand and Verify Product Reviews
skills.principle: On a product page, use the visible “Reviews (N)” tab or review-count link to expand the reviews panel. Confirm completion when the panel exposes “Customer Reviews” and individual review text, rather than repeatedly scrolling. Once reviews are visible, report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a product’s reviews and the product page shows a review count or collapsed “Reviews (N)” tab, especially when scrolling does not reveal review content.

skills.title: Verify the Requested Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current page title, URL, and main heading before acting. If they already identify the requested destination, confirm any relevant state shown there and stop. Otherwise, use the clearly labeled navigation link, then verify the destination heading or URL before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial accessibility tree may already show the requested account, wishlist, cart, or other destination page.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate using the relevant account or header link, then verify the destination through its page heading or URL. Once the requested page is visibly confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for simple navigation tasks when the current page or newly loaded page clearly shows the requested destination heading, label, or URL.

skills.title: Use Product Review Anchor
skills.principle: On a product page, locate the labeled “Add Your Review” link near the rating and review count, then activate it. Confirm completion when the Reviews area expands and the review form is visible with rating, nickname, summary, and review fields. Report completion without submitting the form.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a product’s review-entry section and the product page exposes an “Add Your Review” link or equivalent anchor near its rating information.

skills.title: Complete All Required Review Fields
skills.principle: Before submitting a product review, inspect every required control. Select one rating option, then fill the nickname, summary, and review fields. Click “Submit Review” only after all required fields are populated; if validation appears, follow its message and correct the missing field.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping product’s “Add Your Review” form is open and includes required rating controls plus text fields. This is especially important before submitting, since an unselected rating can block submission.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the navigation entry matching the requested destination and activate it. After navigation, verify completion using the page title, URL, heading, or task-specific controls. Once the destination is clearly confirmed, report completion and stop without extra actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task asks you to open a named page and the current accessibility tree exposes a matching link or navigation control.

skills.title: Stop After Page Confirmation
skills.principle: After navigating to the requested page, verify the accessibility tree shows the expected page title or heading and its distinctive controls. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current observation already shows the requested destination, such as an “Advanced Search” heading and search form.

skills.title: Use Add-to-Cart as Stock Evidence
skills.principle: After searching, inspect every visible result title for the requested product or a clear product-name variant. If the matching result has an enabled “Add to Cart” control, treat it as in stock and report availability. Do not infer absence from scrolling or related-search sections when the item already appears in the accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks asking whether a specific product is in stock, especially when search results include title variants and product cards expose an enabled “Add to Cart” button.

skills.title: Report Stock Status and Terminate
skills.principle: When the product page visibly shows a definitive availability label such as “IN STOCK” or “OUT OF STOCK,” use that observation as the answer. Report the target item’s status immediately, then terminate the task rather than repeatedly issuing no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a product-detail page when the target item is identified and its availability status is explicitly visible in the accessibility tree or page content.

skills.title: Use Product Descriptions for Specifications
skills.principle: Read the product title and visible description first for the requested specification. Prefer the detailed description when it distinguishes related values, such as fixed optical magnification versus adjustable digital zoom. Report the exact attributes together once the page provides sufficient evidence; avoid unnecessary navigation or interaction.
skills.when_to_apply: When answering a product-specification question and the target product page is already open with a visible title, description, or quick-look section containing the requested attribute.

skills.title: Inspect Search Results Before Concluding
skills.principle: When searching for a product specification, inspect the returned product titles and snippets for the exact target before reporting failure. If the target appears, extract the requested attribute directly when stated (such as magnification in the title); otherwise open the matching product listing and check its details.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after a shopping-site search returns results, especially when the exact product name appears in a listing title or related search suggestion.

skills.title: Stop After Add Confirmation
skills.principle: Set the product quantity to the requested value, click “Add to Cart” once, then wait for the page to finish processing. When an “Added” state, success alert, or cart update confirms completion, stop immediately; repeated clicks add duplicate quantities.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a specified quantity from a product page, especially when the page shows a loading or busy state after submission. Verify the requested quantity before the first click and use the success feedback as the completion condition.

skills.title: Use Review Labels, Then Verify
skills.principle: On a product page, activate the control labeled “Reviews” or “Reviews (count),” not an unlabeled or unrelated element ID. After activation, verify that the reviews tab is expanded and its panel contains “Customer Reviews” and review entries. Once the entries are visible, report completion and stop; do not repeatedly scroll, refresh, or click without checking the updated accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all reviews for a product and the page exposes a review-count link or tab alongside other product-detail elements. Use the current accessible label and confirm the review panel is populated.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Full Cart
skills.principle:
1. Select the header’s cart control when it exposes the cart item count.
2. If a cart preview dialog appears, select “View and Edit Cart” to reach the full cart page.
3. Confirm completion using the “Shopping Cart” page title, cart item table, and displayed total before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to or inspect a shopping cart, especially when the header cart control opens a preview instead of directly loading the full cart page.

skills.title: Open the Full Cart Page
skills.principle: After selecting the cart control, distinguish a mini-cart dialog from the full cart page. If the dialog appears, choose “View and Edit Cart” to navigate to the cart page. Confirm completion by checking for the cart page URL or full cart contents, then stop instead of repeatedly clicking or waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping site’s cart control opens an overlay containing items and a “View and Edit Cart” option, rather than navigating immediately to the full cart page.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Wishlist
skills.principle: When the task is to view saved items, click the clearly labeled “My Wish List” navigation link, then verify the page heading and displayed wishlist state. An empty-list message is still a valid result; do not add products or browse elsewhere. Once the wishlist page is confirmed, report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an authenticated shopping site shows a “My Wish List” link and the task only asks to navigate to or view the wishlist, regardless of whether it contains items.

skills.title: Activate Hidden Star Ratings by Keyboard
skills.principle: When a star radio is obscured by visual labels, focus the intended rating control and press Space to select it. Verify its accessibility state changes to checked, then complete the required review fields and submit. If submission reports a timeout after the click, inspect the page for a confirmation alert before retrying; an alert stating the review was submitted for moderation confirms completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on product review forms where star radio inputs are hidden or pointer clicks are intercepted, and after submission when navigation waits time out but the page may already display a success confirmation.

skills.title: Read Product Specification Tables
skills.principle: On a product page, inspect the visible product details or specification table for the requested attribute. Match the attribute label, such as “Material,” to its adjacent value, then report that value directly. Stop once the requested field is located and verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the target product page is already open and its accessibility tree exposes a Details section or specification table containing the requested attribute.

skills.title: Use Observed Product Links Directly
skills.principle: When the target product appears in the accessibility tree—such as Compare Products, Recently Ordered, or a wishlist—open its product-name link directly. Prefer verified observed links over guessing category URLs, slugs, or navigation paths; then inspect the product page for the requested attribute.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when a target item is already listed anywhere on the current shopping page, especially after a 404 or failed category navigation. Verify the link’s accessible name matches the requested product before opening it.

skills.title: Open Wishlist From Account Header
skills.principle: Click the account-header link labeled "My Wish List" or equivalent saved-items entry. Confirm navigation by checking that the page heading identifies the wishlist and that saved product entries are visible. Once the saved items are displayed, report completion and stop without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an authenticated shopping page shows a wishlist or saved-items link in the account header, and the task is to view saved products rather than modify them.

skills.title: Terminate After Goal Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the page visibly confirms the requested destination and content, report completion and terminate the task. Do not repeat no-op actions or wait for additional observations after the goal is already satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task reaches a page whose heading, URL, or visible content clearly confirms the requested destination, such as a wishlist page displaying saved items.

skills.title: Use Footer Policy Links
skills.principle: When a shopping task asks to view a policy page, inspect the page footer for a link matching the requested policy name, activate it, then verify the destination by checking the page heading, URL, and substantive policy content. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on storefront pages when the requested informational page is not directly visible and the footer contains navigation links such as Privacy, Cookie, Terms, or Contact.

skills.title: Explore Category Through Subcategories
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested top-level category and verify its heading and item count.
2. Inspect visible product listings, then open representative products through their title links.
3. Return using the breadcrumb category link and explore relevant subcategories, confirming the updated heading and filters.
4. After viewing representative product details across subcategories, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for broad shopping tasks asking to explore a product category, especially when the page provides category filters, product listings, breadcrumbs, and product detail pages.

skills.title: Use Pagination for Product Exploration
skills.principle: On a category listing, inspect the heading, visible product list, and pagination controls before scrolling. Increase the “Show” count when useful, then review the loaded products and use “Page Next” or a numbered page link for additional results. Stop scrolling when the product list and page range remain unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to explore products in a category listing with many results, especially when the accessibility tree already exposes product items, a “Show” selector, and pagination links.

skills.title: Navigate Hierarchical Shopping Categories
skills.principle: Use the visible category hierarchy rather than scanning unrelated products: open the relevant top-level department, select the target category in the “Shop By” sidebar, then choose the most relevant subcategory for the requested product type. Confirm completion by checking the active category label, result count, and product listings before summarizing findings.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping request names a product category or use case and the current page is unrelated or broad. Apply when the sidebar exposes category and subcategory links.

skills.title: Use the Search Input Directly
skills.principle: When the search control is a combobox, target the input by its role, placeholder, or accessible name—not its decorative icon or parent label. Fill the query directly, verify the field contains it and the Search button becomes enabled, then submit with Enter or the enabled button. If a click succeeds, proceed to filling instead of repeating clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this on storefront pages when search icons or labels resolve incorrectly, while the accessibility tree exposes a focused combobox input and possibly a disabled Search button.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Shopping Categories
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level department from the navigation menu.
2. On its category page, inspect the “Shopping Options” category list rather than relying only on visible products.
3. Select the target subcategory by its semantic label.
4. Confirm completion from the filtered-page state, including the category heading, active filter, and relevant product listings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping request asks you to explore a specific subcategory and the initial page is unrelated or only shows a broad department.

skills.title: Re-ground Before Each UI Action
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to identify elements by role and visible name, not copied icon-text strings or stale identifiers. After each action, verify that the page state, URL, or expanded menu changed. If it did not, re-ground and retry with the observed combobox or menuitem rather than repeating malformed actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating category menus or searching products and an action returns an empty-action, missing-element, or unchanged-page result. Reinspect the latest accessibility tree before continuing.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Before Completion
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested product category from the site navigation.
2. Locate pagination by its semantic labels, such as “Page 2” or “Page Next,” rather than relying on fixed element identifiers.
3. Select the requested page, then verify the URL, active-page indicator, and item range confirm the destination.
4. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for category-listing tasks requiring a specific page. First ensure the target category is open and pagination is visible; complete only after the page indicator or item range verifies the requested page.

skills.title: Paginate Within the Correct Category
skills.principle:
1. Open the requested product category before using pagination; do not assume homepage showcases belong to that category.
2. In the category listing, select the requested page link or “Page Next.”
3. Verify both the category context and the pagination state show the requested page, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping task requests a specific page of a category and the initial page may be a homepage, mixed showcase, or otherwise lack category context.

skills.title: Use Listing Sort Controls Directly
skills.principle: From a product detail or homepage, navigate to the relevant category or product-listing page rather than repeatedly using browser history. Locate the listing’s sort control, choose “Price: Low to High” (or equivalent), and verify the displayed products are ordered ascending by price before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to sort products and the current page is a product detail page or homepage without a visible sort control. Use category navigation or another listing entry point; avoid repeated back navigation when it risks leaving the store.

skills.title: Submit Product Searches Before Browsing Results
skills.principle: After entering a product name in the store search field, activate the matching autocomplete option or click the enabled “Search” button. Inspect the resulting search-results page, open the exact product listing, select “Add to Cart,” and verify the cart confirmation or updated item count before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When the target product is absent from the current showcase or category page and the search field shows an autocomplete match or enabled Search control.

skills.title: Stop After Add-To-Cart Confirmation
skills.principle: After clicking the target item's "Add to Cart" control, verify the success alert stating it was added to the shopping cart or the cart count increased. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not repeatedly click "My Cart" or perform unnecessary navigation that can leave an overlay open.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for shopping tasks when the add-to-cart action produces a visible success alert, updated cart count, or cart preview containing the target item.

skills.title: Read Existing Dashboard Tables Directly
skills.principle: When the requested information is already visible, use the relevant dashboard table instead of navigating or filtering. Identify its column headers, read each displayed row, preserve the requested fields and units, then report the values accurately and stop once complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin dashboard tasks asking for summary data already present in an accessible table, such as recent orders, customers, totals, or item counts.

skills.title: Read Visible Order Tables Directly
skills.principle: When the requested order data is already present in an accessibility tree, identify the table by its heading and headers, then transcribe each relevant row directly. Do not click table containers, headers, or cells unless interaction is required; clicking a linked row may navigate away and lose the overview context. Report the requested fields and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin dashboards where a “Last Orders” or similar table visibly contains the requested customer, item-count, and total columns in the current observation.

skills.title: Read Dashboard Search Terms
skills.principle: When the Magento Admin dashboard already contains a “Top Search Terms” table, use it directly rather than navigating elsewhere. Read each row’s Search Term, Results, and Uses columns, preserve the table’s ranking order, and report the requested fields accurately.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when asked for top search terms and the dashboard observation visibly includes a “Top Search Terms” table with populated rows and the relevant columns.

skills.title: Read Existing Table Data Directly
skills.principle: Inspect the current accessibility tree before navigating. If the requested information already appears in a table, read the relevant column headers and row cells directly, preserving their order, and report the values. Do not click rows or use fill, focus, or press on read-only table cells; those actions are for interactive controls, not extraction.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin retrieval tasks when the current page visibly contains the requested records, especially tables whose values are exposed as accessible cell text.

skills.title: Read Visible Dashboard Metrics
skills.principle: Inspect the current dashboard accessibility tree before navigating or refreshing. Locate the metric labels requested, read their adjacent displayed values, and report them directly. Treat the visible page state as sufficient completion when all requested metrics are present.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for dashboard tasks asking for current metrics when the relevant summary values are already visible in the initial page observation.

skills.title: Report Visible Dashboard Metrics
skills.principle: When requested metrics are already visible, read the labeled values and provide them in the final response. Do not repeatedly issue a no-op: the environment may treat it as an empty action and fail. Once the requested information is confirmed, report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on dashboard-viewing tasks when the accessibility tree already shows the requested metric labels and values, such as Revenue, Tax, and Shipping, without requiring filters or navigation.

skills.title: Verify Order Export Completion
skills.principle: Open Sales > Orders, apply the requested filters, and choose Export with CSV selected. Confirm the browser reports a successful download or exposes the exported file before reporting completion; if only the click is observable, report that export was requested and its result remains unverified.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting an order grid to CSV from Magento Admin and the desired grid filters are already applied.

skills.title: Use Observed Admin Navigation Links
skills.principle: When a guessed admin URL returns a 404, stop retrying it. Reopen the relevant navigation menu and follow the exact observed link for the target page, such as the visible “Orders” entry. Confirm the destination loads the intended list before searching for export controls.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when navigating Magento Admin or similar back-office pages, especially after a direct URL produces a 404 or the accessibility tree exposes a concrete navigation link.

skills.title: Verify Product Fields Before Saving
skills.principle: On Magento’s New Product form, fill the required Product Name, SKU, and Price, plus inventory Quantity when needed. After each fill, inspect the field value; if text was appended rather than replaced, clear the field and re-enter the intended value. Click Save only after all values are correct, then verify the resulting success state or product listing.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product through Catalog > Products > Add Product, especially when form filling may append to preexisting or autofilled values.

skills.title: Verify Form Values Before Saving
skills.principle: After filling each Magento product field, inspect its displayed value before continuing. If text was appended or entered into the wrong field, clear the field and re-enter the intended value. Confirm required fields—especially Product Name, SKU, and Price—are correct, then click Save and verify the resulting success state.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a Magento product, particularly after sequential fill actions where the form may retain focus or append text unexpectedly.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales To Orders
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the current page before acting; if the Orders heading and order table are already visible, report completion immediately.
2. Otherwise, open the SALES navigation entry and select the visible Orders submenu item.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading is Orders and the orders table or record count is displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when asked to view all customer orders, especially from another admin page. Prerequisite: the SALES navigation entry and its Orders submenu are available.

skills.title: Use Exact Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When a navigation click repeatedly returns an empty-action or lookup error, stop reusing escaped icon text, labels, or guessed XPath. Read the current accessibility tree and invoke the exact bid assigned to the navigation element by role and meaning. After SALES opens, inspect the refreshed tree and select Orders, confirming the page heading or order grid appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin or similar menus when a visible navigation label is represented by an icon-font link and repeated text-based clicks fail.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Admin Menus
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level navigation menu, such as Sales, to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu entry matching the requested management section, such as Invoices.
3. Verify completion from the destination heading, URL meaning, and visible records or controls; report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requests a specific section hidden under a collapsed navigation menu and the destination can be confirmed through its heading and management table.

skills.title: Use Observed Menu Targets
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, interact only with elements currently exposed in the accessibility tree. Click the observed SALES navigation entry, verify that its submenu appears, then click the observed Invoices link by its current role, label, or bid. After each action, confirm the page or menu changed before continuing; never fabricate submenu labels or reuse malformed bids.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from the Magento Admin dashboard to a nested Sales destination such as Invoices, especially when navigation entries initially expose only placeholder URLs or collapsed menus.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus
skills.principle:
1. From the Magento Admin Dashboard, open the SALES navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the Transactions link by its visible label and role, not a hard-coded element ID.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading and URL indicate Transactions, then report any table state such as record count or an empty-results message.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access payment transactions in Magento Admin and the dashboard navigation is visible. Verify the Transactions page itself before reporting completion, including whether records are present.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Transactions
skills.principle: Once the Sales submenu reveals the “Transactions” link, open it and verify the page heading is “Transactions.” If the task only asks to access the section, report completion immediately; do not click Search, change filters, or investigate empty results unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking only to access the Transactions section. After navigation, confirm the Transactions heading or page URL is visible before terminating.

skills.title: Expand Catalog to Reach Products
skills.principle:
1. From the Magento Admin dashboard, activate the top-level “CATALOG” navigation entry.
2. When its submenu appears, select the “Products” link.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Products” and product-management controls such as “Add Product” are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open Magento’s product-management area from the admin dashboard, and the accessibility tree shows a collapsed “CATALOG” navigation entry.

skills.title: Use Exact Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When a navigation element appears in the accessibility tree, use its current numeric bid exactly (for example, the Catalog link’s bid), without icon text, guessed labels, extra escaping, or unnecessary modifiers. After clicking, inspect the refreshed tree for the expanded submenu and then select Products using its newly reported bid. If the page does not change, re-read the tree before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this on BrowserGym admin pages when clicks fail with empty-action or element-not-found errors, especially when visible labels include icon glyphs or menu items are revealed only after expansion.

skills.title: Verify Navigation After Clicks
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation menu item, inspect the refreshed page state before retrying. If the URL, heading, and expected content already confirm the destination, treat the task as complete and report success rather than repeating a stale element click.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating admin interfaces where a click may trigger navigation before the automation reports completion, especially after a timeout occurring during scheduled-navigation waiting.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Node Bids Precisely
skills.principle: When an accessibility tree exposes numeric element identifiers, use the element’s current bid (for example, the catalog link’s node identifier) rather than its visible label or icon text. After clicking, inspect the updated tree, expand the catalog menu if needed, then select Categories. If an action fails repeatedly, change the targeting method instead of retrying identical invalid clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Magento Admin page whose accessibility tree shows navigation links with numeric node identifiers, especially when text-based clicks produce empty-action or element-not-found errors.

skills.title: Resolve Product URL Key Conflicts
skills.principle: When Magento rejects a product because its URL Key already exists, make the product name sufficiently unique to generate a distinct URL key, then click Save again. Confirm completion by checking for the “You saved the product.” success message and the resulting product edit page.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento catalog product, the Save action displays a URL Key conflict and the product remains on the New Product form.

skills.title: Verify Product Save Completion
skills.principle:
1. Complete all fields marked required, especially Product Name, SKU, and Price; clear any prefilled value before entering replacement text.
2. Click the Magento Admin “Save” button.
3. Inspect the resulting page for a success confirmation, product identifier, or return to the product list; if validation errors remain, correct them and save again.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a product in Magento Admin and the form contains required fields or possible prefilled values. Apply after saving to confirm the product was actually created rather than assuming the click succeeded.

skills.title: Edit and Verify Magento Category
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s CATALOG menu and select Categories.
2. Select the target category from the visible category tree, then edit its Category Name field.
3. Click Save and wait for the page to refresh.
4. Confirm the updated name and the success message “You saved the category.” before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing an existing Magento product category and the Categories page displays a navigable category tree, editable Category Name field, and Save button.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Category Save
skills.principle: After editing the category and clicking Save, verify the success message and updated category name. Before changing any additional setting, compare its current state with the requested state; leave already-correct toggles unchanged. Once the save is confirmed, report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing an existing Magento category, especially after the page shows “You saved the category” and the updated name or values are visible.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Viewing Inventory
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to Catalog, then Products.
2. Inspect the listing for active filters, especially keyword filters inherited from prior state.
3. Select “Clear all” when filters are present.
4. Confirm completion when the grid shows the full record count and pagination across multiple pages, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all products in a Magento Admin inventory and the Products grid may retain filters from an earlier search. Requires access to Catalog > Products and a visible listing state.

skills.title: Verify Online Customer Status
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Customers navigation and expand it if needed.
2. Select “Now Online” and wait for the customer grid to load.
3. Report the displayed count; treat “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records” as confirmation that no customers are currently online.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check currently online customers in the Magento admin, with access to the Customers navigation and its “Now Online” page.

skills.title: Verify Admin Sections Before Navigating
skills.principle: Use visible navigation and page labels to locate the requested admin section rather than guessing a URL from a dashboard tab. After navigation, verify the heading and content match the requested function. If the page shows a 404 or the feature is absent, report that availability depends on permissions or configuration instead of treating an unrelated page as evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests a dashboard section such as “Now Online,” especially when the current dashboard lacks that section or exposes only similarly named customer tabs.

skills.title: Find Customer Impersonation Logs
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers navigation menu rather than System or generic Action Logs.
2. Select “Login as Customer Log.”
3. Confirm completion from the page heading and grid; report the displayed record count, including “0 records found” when the table is empty.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing administrator customer-impersonation history in Magento Admin, starting from any admin page with the Customers navigation available.

skills.title: Use Visible Labels, Not Icon Glyphs
skills.principle: Target navigation entries by their visible accessible names, such as “CUSTOMERS,” rather than copying decorative icon glyphs or stale element bids. Submit a correctly formed browser action, then verify the URL or page heading changed. If repeated attempts leave the page unchanged or return an empty-action error, reacquire the current accessibility tree and choose a valid element instead of retrying the same malformed command.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar menus where links expose both decorative icon text and visible labels, especially after an action error or unchanged page state.

skills.title: Avoid Speculative Admin Changes
skills.principle: For an underspecified management request, navigate to the requested section and inspect the existing records before modifying anything. Do not invent a new record or choose an arbitrary edit target. If creating an item, first check whether the intended name already exists; edit the existing item instead of submitting a duplicate. After reaching the correct section, stop or request clarification unless a concrete change is specified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in admin list-management tasks when the request names a section but does not specify which record or operation, especially before creating customer groups or editing existing system-defined records.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Requested Section
skills.principle: When the task only specifies managing a named admin section without a concrete create, edit, or delete request, navigate to that section, verify its heading and available controls, then report completion. Do not invent a new record or modify existing data. If an exploratory save produces a duplicate or validation error, return to the listing and stop unless the task specifies a corrective change.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for underspecified Magento Admin tasks that name a section, such as Customer Groups, but provide no target record or requested mutation.

skills.title: Create Customers Through Magento Admin
skills.principle:
1. Open CUSTOMERS, select All Customers, then choose Add New Customer.
2. Keep valid defaults for website and group unless the task specifies alternatives.
3. Fill every required field marked with an asterisk, especially First Name, Last Name, and Email.
4. Select Save Customer and stop only after the listing page shows “You saved the customer.”
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer in Magento Admin, after reaching the dashboard and having the required identity and email details available.

skills.title: Use Observed Customer Navigation
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open CUSTOMERS, select the observed “All Customers” menu entry, and wait for the Customers list. Click the visible “Add New Customer” button, then verify the “New Customer” form appears before entering details. Use accessibility-tree labels and links instead of guessing admin URLs, especially after a 404.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer from Magento Admin and the dashboard lacks a direct creation control. Prerequisite: the CUSTOMERS menu is available; confirm each navigation result before proceeding.

skills.title: Open Magento Content Navigation
skills.principle: Click the Magento Admin navigation entry labeled “CONTENT.” Confirm completion when its menu expands and shows content-related options such as Pages, Blocks, Widgets, Media Gallery, and Design configuration. Once the menu is visibly expanded, report completion without selecting a submenu.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task is to reach Magento Admin’s Content section from the dashboard and the top navigation contains a visible “CONTENT” entry.

skills.title: Use Exact Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When a navigation control is visible, use its exact current accessibility bid, not its icon glyph, visible text, or AX-tree index formatted as a string. After clicking, inspect the updated tree; if the control points to a placeholder or menu, hover or expand it and select the revealed destination. Avoid repeating malformed actions after the same error.
skills.when_to_apply: When BrowserGym reports an empty action or cannot find an element while navigating an admin menu, especially when labels are accompanied by icon glyphs and placeholder URLs.

skills.title: Expand Customers and Select All Customers
skills.principle:
1. Click the main “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select “All Customers” rather than another customer-related option.
3. Confirm completion from the page heading “Customers,” the customer grid, and the customer-list URL or equivalent page state.
4. Report completion and stop once the Customers page is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping-admin dashboard task asks to open the Customers section and the main navigation shows a collapsible “CUSTOMERS” entry with an “All Customers” submenu option.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Repeating Clicks
skills.principle: Expand the relevant navigation section, then click its visible destination link once. Confirm completion from the resulting URL or page heading; if already on the requested page, stop instead of clicking hidden or repeated menu elements.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating admin dashboards with expandable menus, especially after a click leaves the target page already loaded or a submenu item becomes hidden.

skills.title: Navigate to Catalog Price Rules
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin MARKETING menu and locate the Promotions section.
2. Select the "Catalog Price Rule" navigation entry.
3. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and visible "Add New Rule" and "Apply Rules" controls, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to reach Magento’s catalog discount-rule management page, starting from an admin page where the MARKETING navigation is available.

skills.title: Use Marketing Promotions for Catalog Rules
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the MARKETING navigation entry and inspect its expanded submenu. Under Promotions, select the visible “Catalog Price Rule” link rather than searching under Catalog or Sales. Use the accessibility tree’s current label and role to identify the link, then verify navigation reaches the catalog price-rule page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or configure product discounts in Magento Admin and the dashboard navigation is visible. Expand MARKETING and use Promotions when Catalog Price Rule is not present under Catalog or Sales.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Blocks
skills.principle:
1. From the Magento Admin dashboard, expand the CONTENT navigation entry.
2. Under Elements, select the Blocks link.
3. Confirm completion when the Blocks page appears with its management table and controls such as Add New Block, search, filters, or Actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open Magento’s reusable content block management page from the Admin dashboard. The CONTENT menu must be available; expand it before selecting Blocks.

skills.title: Use Accessible Names, Not Icon Text
skills.principle: When a browser action reports an empty action or missing bid, stop retrying the same selector. Re-read the accessibility tree and target the navigation entry by its accessible name, such as “CONTENT,” or by the currently observed valid element reference. After clicking, verify that the menu expands or the page state changes before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating an admin sidebar or menubar from an accessibility tree, especially when labels include decorative icon glyphs and repeated clicks produce selector or empty-action errors.

skills.title: Use the Explicit Design Schedule Link
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open CONTENT and expand the Design submenu. Select the explicitly labeled “Schedule” entry rather than Configuration, Themes, or unrelated controls. Verify the resulting page heading and schedule records before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view planned theme changes from the Magento dashboard and the CONTENT menu is available, especially when its Design submenu exposes a direct “Schedule” link.

skills.title: Explore Admin Navigation Before Reporting Failure
skills.principle: When the dashboard lacks the requested record, actively inspect the relevant top-level menus and their expanded submenu labels, then use the admin search field with task-specific terms. Navigate to candidate pages and verify the resulting heading or table before reporting inability. Avoid repeating speculative messages without taking a browser action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks where the initial dashboard does not show the requested schedule, configuration, or record and navigation menus or global search are available.

skills.title: Open Order Details From Search
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, search for the target order ID and confirm the results contain the matching record. Use that row’s “View” action, then verify the destination heading identifies the target order and its information panel is visible. Once the details page is confirmed, report completion without taking unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for requests to view a specific order when the Orders grid is available and supports keyword search. Prerequisite: the search result must visibly match the requested order before selecting its row-level “View” action.

skills.title: Filter Orders by Exact ID
skills.principle:
1. Open the Sales orders grid instead of relying on the dashboard’s limited “Last Orders” list.
2. Apply an exact filter for the requested order ID and submit it.
3. Open the matching result, then verify the order-view heading and “Order & Account Information” show the same ID before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task requests a specific order ID and the dashboard list omits that order or does not visibly identify rows by ID.

skills.title: Use Grid Reset for Active Filters
skills.principle: When asked to clear a keyword filter, stay on the relevant listing grid and use its filter reset or clear-filters control. Do not open a search-term record and blank its required Search Query field; that edits the record and triggers validation. Confirm the keyword field is cleared and the unfiltered grid reloads.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Magento Admin listing pages when a keyword filter is active. First locate the grid’s filter controls; use Reset/clear filters there, especially when the underlying Search Query field is required.

skills.title: Verify Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL, page heading, and visible content before taking navigation actions. If the requested page is already open and displays the target information, report completion immediately; otherwise select the matching navigation entry and verify the destination loaded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin-console tasks requesting navigation to a named page, especially when the initial page may already be the requested destination.

skills.title: Confirm Dashboard and Stop
skills.principle: When the observed URL and page heading already match the requested dashboard, verify that the relevant performance metrics are visible, then report completion and terminate. Do not repeatedly issue no-op actions; the dashboard state itself is the completion evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current accessibility tree already shows the requested admin page and its target content, such as a dashboard heading and performance metric panels.

skills.title: Recognize When Already in Target Section
skills.principle: Verify the current URL, page heading, and visible management content before navigating. If they identify the requested admin section and its relevant interface, report that the goal is already satisfied and stop without redundant navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open an administrative section and the initial observation already shows the section’s navigation label, matching page heading, and task-relevant management interface.

skills.title: Verify Success After Timeout
skills.principle: When a confirmation action times out after the click completes, inspect the resulting page before retrying. If a success message such as “You sent the shipment.” is visible, treat the operation as complete and stop; retry only when the confirmation or success state is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after confirming Magento actions in dialogs, especially when the browser reports a timeout while waiting for navigation or scheduled events. Check the refreshed page for a success notice before performing the action again.

skills.title: Open Magento Product Catalog
skills.principle:
1. From another Magento Admin section, activate the top navigation entry labeled "CATALOG".
2. Select the revealed "Products" submenu item.
3. Confirm the Products page displays catalog controls such as "Add Product," filters, search, and the product-record table; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage product listings in Magento Admin and the current page is outside the Catalog Products section.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Customer Management
skills.principle:
1. From the Magento Admin navigation, select the top-level “CUSTOMERS” entry to expand its submenu.
2. Choose “All Customers” to open the customer management grid.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading is “Customers” and customer-management controls or records are visible; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to visit or manage customer accounts in Magento Admin and the current page is another admin section with the main navigation visible.

skills.title: Inspect Magento Promotion Rules
skills.principle:
1. Expand the MARKETING navigation and locate the Promotions subsection.
2. Open both Catalog Price Rule and Cart Price Rules, unless the task names only one.
3. Read each table’s record count, rule names, dates, status, coupon codes, and website scope.
4. Report only observed promotional details, then stop once the requested section is checked.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking to check marketing promotions, when the MARKETING menu and Promotions links are available and the relevant rule tables can be inspected.

skills.title: Use Visible Marketing Navigation
skills.principle: When checking promotional activities, expand the visible “MARKETING” menu and select its actual promotional submenu entry by label. Do not guess administrative URLs or reuse an element ID from another menu. Confirm completion by verifying a promotions heading or activity list; if the selected entry produces a 404, return to the menu and inspect available entries before reporting unavailability.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply in Magento Admin when the task asks to inspect marketing promotions and the dashboard exposes expandable navigation menus. Verify the menu’s current accessibility tree before clicking, especially after navigation changes.

skills.title: Use Data-Aligned Report Date Ranges
skills.principle: When generating a Magento sales report, choose a date range that covers known order activity rather than an arbitrary recent period. Fill both required From and To fields, click “Show Report,” and inspect the result. If it shows zero records, broaden or reposition the range around observed order dates, and refresh statistics when the page indicates they may be stale.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Reports pages with required date filters, especially when order records or their dates are visible elsewhere and an initial report returns “0 records found.”

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Report Generation
skills.principle: Navigate Reports → Sales → the requested report, fill both required date fields, and click “Show Report.” Verify the resulting report page and record count, including “0 records found” as a valid completed result. Once generation is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of exploring unrelated reports or exporting unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to explore or generate a sales report and the report page shows the selected filters and a refreshed result state after “Show Report.”

skills.title: Verify Navigation Targets Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to locate the navigation link by its visible label, such as “FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS,” rather than reusing an earlier element ID. Click the currently exposed target, then verify the destination heading and page content match the request. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Magento Admin page or similar dynamic interface, especially after a page transition or when previously recorded element IDs may be stale.

skills.title: Use Observed URLs After Selector Failures
skills.principle: When a visible navigation link repeatedly fails to resolve by text, Unicode label, or XPath, stop retrying selectors. Read its destination URL directly from the accessibility tree, navigate there with the browser’s URL action, and verify the page URL or heading changed to the requested destination.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the target link is visible with a destination URL, but multiple accessibility-bid or selector-based clicks produce empty-action or element-not-found errors.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog Products
skills.principle:
1. Open the top navigation item labeled “CATALOG.”
2. Select “Products” from its expanded menu rather than stopping at the menu state.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Products” and product-management controls such as “Add Product,” search, or filters are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Magento Admin’s Catalog area for product management, especially from another section such as Orders. Verify the Products page is loaded before reporting completion.

skills.title: Use Semantic Navigation Links
skills.principle: Select the admin navigation entry whose label directly matches the requested destination, such as “FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS.” After activation, verify the URL and page headings/content show the intended destination. Once confirmed, report completion and stop rather than taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Magento Admin task from another section and the accessibility tree exposes a clearly labeled destination link. Verify the resulting page before declaring success.

skills.title: Stop After Marketplace Page Loads
skills.principle: After selecting “FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS,” verify the page heading is “Magento Marketplace” and that partner and marketplace sections are visible. This confirms the requested navigation; report completion and terminate instead of opening external directory or marketplace links unless specific listings are requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to navigate to the Marketplace or find partners and extensions, and the loaded page visibly contains “Partner search” and “Magento Marketplace” sections.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching New Order
skills.principle: When the task is only to navigate to order creation, click “Create New Order” and verify the resulting page heading or URL shows the new-order interface. Once that state is visible, report completion and terminate instead of selecting customers, stores, products, or submitting an order.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a shopping-admin task asks only to navigate to new-order creation and the page visibly changes to a “New Order” or equivalent order-creation screen.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching New Order
skills.principle: When the task is to navigate to order creation, click the visible “Create New Order” control from the Orders page. Once the page heading indicates “New Order” or the order-creation form is displayed, confirm the destination is reached and terminate; do not select a customer, store, products, or fill fields unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the requested goal is only to open the new-order workflow and the resulting page shows a New Order heading or order-creation form.

skills.title: Verify Exact Inventory Boundaries
skills.principle: Use the product grid’s Quantity filter to narrow the catalog, apply the range, then inspect every returned row’s stock value. For a strict condition such as “less than” a threshold, exclude or manually reject values exactly equal to the threshold before reporting results.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Magento Admin products by stock quantity and the requested comparison is strict, especially when the filter’s upper bound may be inclusive.

skills.title: Search Products Before Editing
skills.principle:
1. Open Catalog and select Products.
2. Enter the target product name in “Search by keyword” and activate “Search.”
3. Confirm the filtered results identify the intended product, then choose its row’s “Edit” link.
4. Verify the product edit page is loaded by checking its heading and editable fields before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when navigating to a specific product’s edit page, especially when the product list contains many records or the displayed name may have changed.

skills.title: Verify Exact Product Identity
skills.principle: After searching the Magento product catalog, confirm the result’s exact product name or another matching identifier before opening its edit link. If the result differs from the requested product, refine the search or inspect identifiers rather than treating the closest name match as correct. Open the edit link only after identity is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from a Magento product list to an item’s edit page, especially when search results contain renamed, similar, or partial-name matches.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Before Acting
skills.principle: After navigation, inspect the page heading, URL meaning, and key form controls. If they confirm the requested destination—such as a “New Product” page with product-entry fields—report completion and stop instead of performing unrelated edits or additional navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the observed page may already be the requested destination, especially after clicking a clearly labeled control such as “Add Product.”

skills.title: Use Observed Element Bids
skills.principle: When an action reports that a label-based identifier cannot be found, re-read the latest accessibility tree and use the element’s current observed bid for the matching role and label. Do not retry the failed identifier or confuse accessible names with bids. After acting, verify the field value or focus state before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on admin forms when the accessibility tree exposes a labeled control with a numeric bid, but fill or focus actions using the label text return a missing-element error.

skills.title: Disable a Magento Product Variant
skills.principle:
1. Search broadly when an exact product-name filter returns no records, then identify the requested variant by its full displayed name or SKU.
2. Select only that row using its checkbox and open the Actions menu.
3. Choose Change status, then Disable.
4. Confirm completion from the banner stating that the expected number of records has been updated, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin’s Products grid when disabling one specific product or variant. Ensure the target row is visibly matched and selected before using Actions; completion requires an update-confirmation banner.

skills.title: Verify State After Timeout
skills.principle: After a bulk status action times out, inspect the refreshed page before retrying. Treat a success banner such as “record(s) have been updated” and the target row showing “Disabled” as completion evidence; then stop. Only reopen the action menu and retry if the target remains enabled and the current accessibility tree exposes a fresh “Disable” option.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a product’s status in Magento Admin or similar grids, especially after a click reports a timeout or navigation delay. Verify the refreshed row and confirmation message before taking another action.

skills.title: Use Catalog Grid Keyword Search
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, stay on the Catalog > Products grid and use its “Search by keyword” field for the requested name term. Submit with “Search,” then verify the active Keyword filter, record count, and every visible result; inspect pagination if multiple pages exist. Do not open an individual product or guess a separate catalog-search URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find products by text in their names and the Products grid provides “Search by keyword,” especially when an existing filter may be stale or overly specific.

skills.title: Use Customers Menu Subsections
skills.principle: Expand the Customers navigation entry, then choose the subsection matching the task: select “All Customers” for customer accounts or “Customer Groups” for group management. Verify the resulting page heading and URL indicate the intended subsection before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin customer-management tasks and the Customers menu is visible. Choose the specific submenu rather than treating the top-level menu or All Customers page as covering group management.

skills.title: Assign Groups from Customer Grid
skills.principle:
1. Filter the customer grid to the target account and select its row checkbox.
2. Open Actions and choose "Assign a Customer Group."
3. Click the desired group name in the expanded list; treat these entries as clickable list items, not a native select control.
4. Verify the customer’s Group column reflects the chosen group.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing customer groups in Magento Admin’s Customers grid, after the target customer is visible and before using the bulk Actions menu.

skills.title: Verify Expanded Review Results
skills.principle: Open the target product’s “Product Reviews” section, then inspect the refreshed review table and its “records found” count before reporting. If the section initially appears empty or the action errors, re-check the current accessibility tree; report only the latest confirmed records and details.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing reviews for a product in Magento Admin and the review section is collapsible, dynamically refreshed, or may show conflicting counts after expansion.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Browser Actions
skills.principle: When an interaction repeatedly returns an empty-action or parsing error, stop repeating the same command. Re-read the current accessibility tree, identify the visible control by its role and label, issue a correctly formed action using the current reference, then verify that the menu or page state changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in admin navigation when clicking or hovering a visible section such as Stores produces an empty-action error or leaves the accessibility tree unchanged.

skills.title: Expand System Navigation Menu
skills.principle: Click the main navigation entry labeled “SYSTEM.” Verify that its expanded menu appears with system-management categories such as Data Transfer, Extensions, Tools, Permissions, and Other Settings. Treat the task as complete once these submenu options are visible; do not open a specific submenu unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks you to navigate to the System section and the main navigation visibly contains a SYSTEM entry. Completion requires observing the expanded System submenu.

skills.title: Open Magento Add Product Page
skills.principle: On Magento’s Products page, locate and activate the “Add Product” control. Confirm navigation succeeded when the page heading changes to “New Product” and product creation fields such as Product Name, SKU, and Price are visible, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task is only to navigate to product creation, the Magento Products page is displayed, and the “Add Product” control is available.

skills.title: Stop Once Target Page Is Reached
skills.principle: When the requested destination is visible and confirmed by the page heading or URL, treat navigation as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of clicking Save, editing fields, or performing unrelated configuration actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the target page, such as Magento’s “New Product” form, is visibly loaded and no creation or data-entry action was requested.

skills.title: Align Report Dates With Target Data
skills.principle: When a sales report initially shows no records, set both date fields to a range covering the target item's actual availability and current reporting period. Do not assume an outdated “today” date. Click “Refresh,” then verify the target item appears in the Product column before concluding it has no sales.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this on Magento Ordered Products or similar sales reports when the target item’s catalog record is newer than the assumed report end date, or when filtered results omit the item.

skills.title: Validate Report Filters Before Scanning
skills.principle: In Magento’s Ordered Products Report, set both date fields to a valid, task-relevant range, then click Refresh. Verify the resulting table contains the target product and its ordered quantity. If it does not, adjust the range or choose the appropriate product-sales report instead of repeatedly scrolling a large unrelated result set.
skills.when_to_apply: When a product-sales report initially shows no records or results without the target product, especially before relying on manually chosen dates or scanning a long table.

skills.title: Open Catalog View Settings
skills.principle:
1. On the product catalog page, open the saved-view control labeled “Default View” to expose view options.
2. Open “Columns” to display the column-selection checkboxes.
3. Confirm completion when the Columns menu is open and its visible/hidden column options are shown.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to product catalog display or view settings in Magento Admin, with the catalog page already loaded and the “Default View” and “Columns” controls visible.

skills.title: Use Default View for Catalog Settings
skills.principle: On the Magento Products grid, distinguish the saved-view control from the column chooser. Open “Default View” to access view-management settings; use “Columns” only for showing or hiding individual grid attributes. Confirm the opened menu’s labels before changing any checkboxes, then verify the resulting view state.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change catalog product display or view settings and the Products grid shows both “Default View” and “Columns” controls.

skills.title: Expand Magento Marketing Navigation
skills.principle: Click the visible “MARKETING” navigation entry in the Magento Admin menubar. Confirm completion when its expanded menu displays marketing categories such as Promotions, Communications, SEO & Search, and User Content; then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to navigate to Marketing and the main navigation menubar is visible with a “MARKETING” entry.

skills.title: Use Main Navigation and Verify Destination
skills.principle: From the current admin page, identify the main navigation link matching the requested destination and activate it. Confirm completion by checking the resulting page heading and URL or equivalent page-state indicator; once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requires moving between Magento Admin sections and the current accessibility tree exposes a labeled destination link in the primary navigation.

skills.title: Calculate Relative Dates Before Scheduling
skills.principle: For a scheduled sale, determine the current date from the page or environment, then calculate the requested relative date (such as next week) from it. Enter that date in “Special Price From” using the displayed format, optionally set only a user-requested end date, click “Done,” save the product, and verify the save confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: When scheduling Magento product pricing with relative timing such as “next week,” especially if an existing date is shown. Do not replace it with an invented fixed date or assume an unspecified sale duration.

skills.title: Enable Magento Product Backorders
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, search for and open the target product. Open Advanced Inventory, uncheck the Backorders field’s “Use Config Settings” checkbox, then choose an allowed-backorders option. Click “Done,” click the product-page “Save” button, and verify the “You saved the product” confirmation before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring backorders for a Magento product and the Backorders control is disabled because it inherits global configuration. Access to the product edit page and permission to save changes are required.

skills.title: Verify And Save Inventory Changes
skills.principle:
1. Open Advanced Inventory and inspect the Backorders value; select an option that permits backorders if needed.
2. Click Done once, then verify the dialog disappears before continuing.
3. Click the product-level Save button and wait for a success confirmation or updated page state.
4. If the dialog remains open, re-observe and target its visible Done control rather than repeatedly clicking the underlying inventory button.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product’s inventory settings, especially after interacting with the Advanced Inventory dialog. Confirm each UI transition and save the product after closing the dialog.

skills.title: Export Magento Products as CSV
skills.principle:
1. Open System > Data Transfer > Export.
2. Set Entity Type to Products and verify Export File Format is CSV.
3. Click Continue; if the page reports the export is queued, wait for a generated product CSV to appear.
4. Open the newest file’s Select menu and choose Download; confirm the download action before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin product-catalog exports when the Export page is accessible and the user requests a CSV. Ensure Products is selected, and wait for queued exports to finish before downloading.

skills.title: Complete Magento Catalog Export
skills.principle:
1. Open System > Data Transfer > Export rather than the product-grid Actions menu.
2. Set Entity Type to Products and verify Export File Format is CSV.
3. Scroll to and select Continue; this queues the export asynchronously.
4. Wait, refresh, and download the file once it appears in the export table; if it remains empty, verify the cron job is running.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a Magento product catalog as CSV, especially when Continue reports that the file was queued and the export table initially shows no records.

skills.title: Check Pending Reviews in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “MARKETING” navigation menu.
2. Under “User Content,” select “Pending Reviews.”
3. Confirm the page heading and inspect the grid’s “records found” count or empty-state message.
4. Report the observed pending-review count and stop once verified.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check pending reviews in Magento Admin and the navigation menu is available. Use the visible “MARKETING” menu, not “CONTENT,” because “User Content” contains the review links there.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Templates
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin CONTENT navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Under the Elements section, select the Templates link.
3. Confirm the Templates page by its heading and URL; an empty table or “We couldn't find any records” still verifies successful access.
4. Report the observed state and stop once the requested page is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Templates in Magento Admin Content Elements, starting from another admin page with the main navigation visible.

skills.title: Open Magento Sales Navigation
skills.principle: Click the top-navigation "SALES" entry rather than a submenu item. Confirm completion when its vertical dropdown appears with sales options such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, and Credit Memos; then stop and report success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin tasks requesting navigation to the Sales section, when the top horizontal navigation visibly contains a "SALES" entry and the goal is to open its menu rather than visit a specific sales subsection.

skills.title: Validate Menu Expansion After Clicking
skills.principle: Use a syntactically valid click action targeting the visible navigation entry by role or accessible text. After clicking, inspect the next accessibility tree: completion is indicated when the section is focused or expanded and its submenu links appear.
