Do not repeat identical malformed actions; if the menu is expanded, stop and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin’s top-level sections, especially when the entry URL is a placeholder and navigation occurs through an expanded inline menu.

skills.title: Open Magento Customers List
skills.principle:
1. In Magento Admin, activate the top-level “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select “All Customers” rather than stopping at the expanded menu.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Customers” and a customer table is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Magento’s Customers section from another admin page, especially when “CUSTOMERS” initially expands a submenu instead of navigating directly.

skills.title: Distinguish Navigation From Dashboard Widgets
skills.principle: Use the top navigation entry matching the requested section, not a similarly named dashboard widget or tab. Activate the navigation entry with a complete, valid click action; inspect the expanded menu and select the destination item. Verify the resulting heading, URL, or content reflects the requested section before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin dashboard contains both a top-level section label and a dashboard tab/widget with the same name, especially when navigation links initially point to a placeholder or hash.

skills.title: Verify Menu Expansion Before Reporting
skills.principle: Use the visible navigation label matching the requested section, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. Confirm the section is active or focused and its expected submenu options are visible before reporting completion. Once confirmed, stop without selecting a deeper submenu unless the task explicitly requests one.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks to navigate to a top-level admin section and clicking that navigation entry may open an in-page dropdown rather than change the URL.

skills.title: Verify Menu Expansion Before Waiting
skills.principle: Click the top-level “CONTENT” navigation entry, then inspect the refreshed accessibility tree. Treat the expanded “Content” menu and its submenu entries as confirmation that the section is open; report completion and stop. If the task names a specific content area, click the corresponding submenu item instead of repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin’s top navigation and clicking a section expands an in-place menu without changing the URL. Inspect the resulting tree immediately to confirm expansion or choose the requested submenu.

skills.title: Expand the Requested Admin Menu
skills.principle: Click the top-level navigation entry matching the requested admin section. Confirm completion when its submenu becomes visible and shows relevant subsection headings; do not select a deeper submenu unless the task explicitly requests a specific page.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks you to navigate to a top-level section, and the accessibility tree shows that section as a navigation link or menu entry.

skills.title: Verify Navigation State Before Repeating
skills.principle: Click the navigation category once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree and URL. If its submenu expands and shows the requested section, treat navigation as complete; otherwise select the relevant submenu entry. Do not repeat clicks or waits when the page state remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin console with expandable menu categories, especially when the category link retains the current URL and reveals submenu items instead of loading a new page.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Before Continuing
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to locate the navigation entry by its visible label, rather than reusing stale element IDs. After navigation, verify the URL, page heading, and distinctive content match the requested destination. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar interfaces, especially after a click timeout or page transition, and the current accessibility tree may contain refreshed element identifiers.

skills.title: Verify Page Semantics Before Retrying
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation entry, verify success using the current URL, page heading, and distinctive content. If these match the requested destination—even when the URL remains unchanged because it is already the target route—report completion and stop. Do not repeat clicks or refresh merely because the address did not change.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin interface where a menu link may point to the current route or reload the same page. Apply after the first navigation action, using visible headings and destination-specific content as completion evidence.

skills.title: Save Complete Category SEO Updates
skills.principle:
1. Open the category’s “Search Engine Optimization” section.
2. Fill Meta Title, Meta Keywords, and Meta Description with category-relevant, compelling content; preserve an existing URL Key unless instructed otherwise.
3. Click the page’s current “Save” button, using its present accessibility label rather than a stale element ID.
4. Confirm the observable “You saved the category.” message before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento category and improving its search visibility, after the correct category edit page is open and the SEO section is available.

skills.title: Expand SEO Section Before Editing
skills.principle: On Magento category edit pages, section headers such as “Search Engine Optimization” are accordion controls and may hide their fields. Click the SEO section header to expand it, then edit the visible Meta Title, Meta Description, and Meta Keywords fields. Click “Save” and verify a success notification or persisted values instead of repeatedly scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When the category form shows “Search Engine Optimization” but no SEO inputs in the accessibility tree. Confirm the target category is open and the form is editable before expanding and saving.

skills.title: Stop Once Subcategories Are Visible
skills.principle: In Magento’s category tree, inspect the target category’s child list first. If the subcategories are already displayed, report them once and terminate. Use “Expand All” only when children or nested items are collapsed; do not click the category name itself, since it navigates to the edit page rather than merely expanding the tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a category’s subcategories and the accessibility tree already shows child links beneath the target category. Confirm the list is visible before taking further actions.

skills.title: Use Valid Actions and Stop After Completion
skills.principle: When the target category is already expanded, read its indented child entries and report them once. Emit the browser action directly in the action field with valid syntax; do not place a JSON snippet or prose there. After the message is accepted, stop instead of retrying or repeating the same action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for category-tree tasks when the target node and its child list are already visible. Confirm the children are indented beneath the target, then send one properly formatted completion message and terminate.

skills.title: Expand Schedule Design Update
skills.principle: On the target Magento category’s edit page, locate and expand the “Schedule Design Update” section. Inspect the “Schedule Update From” and “To” fields; report their displayed dates, or state that no update is scheduled when both fields are empty.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view scheduled design changes for a category and the category edit page is already open or can be selected from the category tree.

skills.title: Target the Semantic Category Link
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s element role and accessible name to identify the target category link, not nearby list items or image IDs. Invoke a complete, valid click action on that link, then verify the category details page opened before searching for “Schedule Design Update.” If the page does not change, re-inspect the current tree and select the link again rather than repeating an invalid selector.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin category trees or similar lists, especially when multiple nested list, image, and link elements surround the named target and an action error leaves the page unchanged.

skills.title: Save Menu Inclusion After Verification
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Catalog → Categories and select the target category. Verify that Enable Category and Include in Menu are checked. If Include in Menu is already enabled, do not toggle it; click Save. Confirm the “You saved the category.” message and the checkbox remains checked before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento category must appear in storefront navigation and its category edit page is available. This is especially useful when a styled checkbox’s underlying input is blocked by pointer-event interception.

skills.title: Edit Existing Category Menu Visibility
skills.principle:
1. In Magento Catalog > Categories, locate the target category in the tree before creating a new one.
2. Select it, set “Include in Menu” to “Yes” using the visible toggle label when the hidden checkbox intercepts clicks.
3. Click “Save” and verify the category remains enabled and appears in the category tree or storefront navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When a requested category already appears in the Magento category tree and must be added to navigation; ensure the category is enabled and save changes before verifying.

skills.title: Update Category URL Key Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Open the target category’s edit page and expand “Search Engine Optimization.”
2. Locate the “URL Key” field by its label, then enter a lowercase, hyphen-separated slug based on the category name.
3. Click the current “Save” button identified from the latest accessibility tree.
4. Confirm the field retains the new value and a “You saved the category” message appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento category’s SEO URL key. Re-read the accessibility tree after navigation or saving because element identifiers and positions can change.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation Before Direct URLs
skills.principle:
1. From the Magento dashboard, expand the visible CATALOG navigation and choose the category-management entry rather than guessing an administrative URL.
2. Confirm the resulting page shows category controls or a category tree before proceeding.
3. If a 404 appears, return to the dashboard and navigate through the visible menu; do not infer infeasibility from an unverified route.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento category or similar admin record and the dashboard is available, especially after a guessed direct URL produces a 404 page.

skills.title: Enable Category URL Redirect
skills.principle:
1. Open the target category’s edit page and expand “Search Engine Optimization.”
2. Check “Create Permanent Redirect for old URL.”
3. Click “Save.”
4. Confirm completion by verifying the “You saved the category.” success message before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a permanent redirect for a Magento category’s previous URL, with the target category edit form accessible and its SEO section available.

skills.title: Verify Navigation After Timeout
skills.principle: After a click reports a timeout, inspect the current URL, heading, and accessibility tree before retrying. If the target edit page is already loaded, continue from that state: expand the relevant Search Engine Optimization section, configure the permanent redirect, save, and verify the resulting success state. Do not waste actions scrolling, refreshing, or repeating a completed navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after clicking a category or other list item causes a timeout while the observation may already show the target edit form, matching heading, or changed URL.

skills.title: Resolve Category URL Key Conflicts
skills.principle: When saving a Magento category triggers a duplicate URL Key error, expand “Search Engine Optimization,” edit the “URL Key” field to a unique slug, then click “Save” again. Confirm completion by checking for “You saved the category” and the new category appearing under the intended parent in the category tree.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating or editing a Magento category and saving produces an error stating that the URL Key would generate an existing URL.

skills.title: Set URL Key in SEO Section
skills.principle: When Magento reports a duplicate URL Key, expand the "Search Engine Optimization" section and edit its actual "URL Key" field—not the admin search box. Enter a genuinely unused URL key, click "Save," and verify that the error disappears and the category list or success notification confirms creation.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a Magento category or subcategory, especially after saving produces a duplicate URL Key error. Ensure the category name is filled and locate the SEO section before editing the URL key.

skills.title: Update Magento Category Product Position
skills.principle:
1. Open the category’s “Products in Category” section and locate the target product by name.
2. Edit that row’s “Position” textbox with the requested numeric value.
3. Click “Save” and wait for the page response.
4. Confirm completion from the “You saved the category.” message; if the value remains unchanged after saving, refill it and save again.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when repositioning a product within a Magento Admin category and the category edit page provides a “Products in Category” grid with editable Position fields and a Save button.

skills.title: Expand Product Positioning Controls
skills.principle: In Magento category editing, do not report reordering as infeasible while “Products in Category” is collapsed. First select the exact target category by its visible name, expand that section, locate the target product’s position control, set the requested order, click “Save,” and verify the product list or position reflects the change.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a product’s order within a Magento category and the category tree is visible but product controls are hidden in a collapsed “Products in Category” section.

skills.title: Filter Category Products by SKU
skills.principle:
1. Open the selected category’s “Products in Category” section.
2. Locate the filter-row textbox under the “SKU” column and enter the requested SKU.
3. Click “Search” to apply the filter.
4. Confirm completion when the results count updates and displayed rows contain the requested SKU, including relevant variants.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when searching products associated with a specific category and the category editor exposes a “Products in Category” grid with SKU filters and a “Search” button.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After each observation, select the current element bid matching the intended navigation role or label. Do not pass visible icon text, escaped glyphs, or stale identifiers as bids. If an action fails, re inspect the latest accessibility tree and choose a newly observed control before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin interface and a visible menu item repeatedly raises a missing-element error, especially when labels include icons or escaped characters.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and page heading against the requested destination. If both identify the target page, take no navigation action and report that the goal is already satisfied; otherwise, use the admin navigation entry for that destination, then verify the resulting URL and heading.
skills.when_to_apply: For admin-panel navigation tasks, when the initial accessibility tree includes a page heading and URL that may already match the requested destination.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Completion
skills.principle: When the requested page is already displayed, verify the URL and heading match the target, then report completion and terminate the task. Do not repeatedly issue a no-op action; in this environment, it can be rejected as an empty action and prevent successful completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the accessibility tree already shows the requested destination, including a matching page heading and URL. After confirmation, stop rather than sending further browser actions.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Management
skills.principle:
1. Open the top navigation menu labeled “CONTENT.”
2. Wait for its submenu and choose the relevant content area, such as “Pages,” “Blocks,” or a “Design” entry.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, URL, and management table match the selected area.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting from another Magento Admin section and asked to manage CMS pages, blocks, widgets, media, themes, or design settings. The CONTENT navigation must be visible.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When an accessibility-tree element is visible, invoke the browser action with its current numeric bid or a supported role/name locator—not the displayed icon text or copied escaped label. After acting, inspect the refreshed tree and confirm the target section or submenu appeared before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when navigating admin menus or any page where actions repeatedly report an empty action or missing element despite the target being visible in the latest accessibility tree.

skills.title: Search Orders Before Transactions
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin Orders page, not Transactions, when retrieving an order.
2. Enter the target order number in “Search by keyword” and activate “Search.”
3. Confirm the matching row, then select its “View” link.
4. Read the selected “Information” tab and report the requested fields; stop once details are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requesting details for a known order ID, especially when the Transactions page shows no records or lacks a direct order-number search.

skills.title: Report Order Details After Verification
skills.principle: Once the order detail page is open, verify its heading or order number matches the requested target. Extract the requested fields from the visible Information panel, then immediately provide the details to the user and terminate the task.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin order search returns a matching row and its View link opens a detail page. The task is incomplete until the extracted information is reported, not merely displayed in the browser.

skills.title: Export Orders as CSV
skills.principle:
1. Open the Sales navigation and choose Orders rather than Transactions.
2. On the Orders grid, activate Export.
3. In the export dialog, confirm CSV is selected, then click Export to initiate the download.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting order records from Magento Admin and the current page is another Sales subsection, such as Transactions. Ensure the Orders grid is loaded before using its Export control.

skills.title: Verify Export Dialog Completion
skills.principle: After opening the grid’s Export menu, select CSV and activate its dialog Export control. Confirm a download or success indication; if the dialog remains unchanged, treat the export as incomplete, inspect for validation or filter issues, and retry the export action rather than repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting order-grid data and the CSV export dialog remains visible after submission, with no observable download or success confirmation.

skills.title: Filter Customers by ZIP
skills.principle:
1. Open Customers and select All Customers.
2. Click Filters, enter the requested value in the ZIP field, then choose Apply Filters.
3. Verify the active filter shows the requested ZIP and the table’s record count; report each matching customer from the filtered rows.
4. After reporting the verified results, terminate without additional actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer-list tasks requiring all customers matching a ZIP code, when the Customers menu and All Customers grid are accessible.

skills.title: Navigate to the Customer Grid
skills.principle:
1. Distinguish the dashboard’s Customers widget from the admin customer-management page; the widget only shows summary rows.
2. Expand the main navigation entry labeled “CUSTOMERS,” then select its customer-list submenu rather than clicking unrelated navigation items.
3. On the customer grid, locate the ZIP/postcode filter, enter the requested value, apply filters, and verify the resulting rows before reporting them.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin opens on the dashboard and the task requires listing or filtering customers by address data such as ZIP code. Use the full Customers navigation menu, not dashboard customer widgets or an individual customer record.

skills.title: Verify Export Completion Before Retrying
skills.principle: On the customer list, open “Export,” confirm “CSV” is selected, and click the modal’s “Export” once. Then check for a download or success state. If the dialog remains unchanged, inspect filters or page feedback rather than repeatedly clicking; report completion only after confirming the file transfer.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting customer data from Magento Admin and the CSV export dialog remains visible after submission, especially when repeated clicks produce no observable page change.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Reports by Visible Labels
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin "REPORTS" navigation entry to reveal its categorized submenu.
2. Under the relevant category, select the report whose visible label matches the requested report.
3. Confirm the destination heading and inspect the record count or empty-state message.
4. Report the displayed result; export only when the task explicitly requires a downloadable file.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when retrieving a named Magento Admin report from another admin page. The navigation menu must be available, and completion is indicated by the matching report heading plus its records-found count or empty-state message.

skills.title: Navigate Reports Instead of Transactions
skills.principle: When a requested report is absent from the current Transactions grid, use the admin navigation: open REPORTS, locate the report matching the requested name, and select it. Verify the destination heading and report controls or results before reporting completion; do not conclude unavailable merely because it is absent from the current page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin report requests when the current page is a different Sales or Operations grid and the accessibility tree exposes a REPORTS navigation entry.

skills.title: Navigate Reports Through Visible Menus
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level admin section and inspect its expanded submenu rather than guessing direct destinations.
2. Choose the report link matching the requested entity, such as “Newsletter Problem Reports,” under the appropriate category.
3. Verify the destination heading and result message; report the empty-state text when it confirms no records.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requesting a specific report when the dashboard exposes expandable navigation menus. Confirm the final report page and its records-found or empty-state message before responding.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility References
skills.principle: Act on the current accessibility tree’s concrete element references, such as numeric IDs, rather than copied icon text, Unicode labels, or guessed names. After each action, inspect the refreshed tree and select the newly exposed menu item by its observed role and label. If navigation fails, verify the resulting URL and page heading before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin navigation controls display icon-prefixed labels or repeated links, especially after a failed click or page transition. Requires a fresh accessibility-tree observation before each interaction.

skills.title: Submit Required Report Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open Reports, expand the Sales category, and select the Orders report.
2. Inspect required filter fields before submitting; fill both From and To with the requested date range.
3. Click Show Report and verify the Orders Report page displays results or an explicit empty-records message before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin Orders sales reports when the report page has required From and To date fields. Completion requires submitting the filters and confirming the resulting report state, including zero-record results.

skills.title: Stop Once Report Page Appears
skills.principle: When the requested report page is visible, verify its heading and report controls, then treat navigation as complete and stop. Do not alter date filters or other fields unless the task explicitly requests filtering or report results. If filtering is required, use the field’s displayed date format and verify values after submission.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task asks to view a named report and the page heading, filter controls, or report table confirms the requested report has loaded.

skills.title: Locate and Verify an Admin Order
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin Sales menu and select Orders, rather than Transactions.
2. Inspect the orders table for the exact target order number; use the table’s search field when it is not visible.
3. Select the matching row’s View control.
4. Confirm the detail page heading contains the target number and read the status, customer, items, and total before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to find an order in Magento Admin and the current page is another Sales subsection or an orders list. Verify the order-detail page before responding.

skills.title: Use Validated Accessibility Selectors
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to target elements by their exact observed role and accessible name or bid. Submit a syntactically complete action, then verify the page state changed. If an action errors, reread the updated tree and select a currently exposed element instead of repeatedly modifying escaped selectors or inventing nested labels.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar interfaces, especially after a selector error or unchanged page. The current accessibility tree must expose the target navigation control before acting.

skills.title: Use the Orders Grid for Customer Searches
skills.principle: On Magento Admin, search customer orders from the Sales > Orders grid, not the Transactions grid. Identify the filter whose meaning is customer name, enter the target customer, click Search, and verify the results count and order rows before reporting them. Do not use date fields or the global header search for customer matching.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find orders belonging to a customer and the current page is labeled Transactions or shows payment and transaction columns rather than customer/order columns.

skills.title: Use Order Details for Grand Totals
skills.principle: For a requested order total, navigate to the Magento Sales > Orders list rather than Transactions. Search using the visible Order ID filter, submit Search, open the matching order, and read the Grand Total in its order summary. After navigation or filtering, inspect the fresh accessibility tree before selecting controls; do not reuse stale element bids.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin opens on Transactions or another sales subsection and the task asks for an order’s grand total. The Orders page and its current accessibility tree must be available before interacting.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Sales Management
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the “SALES” navigation and verify that the management links “Orders,” “Invoices,” and “Shipments” are visible. Once those links are displayed, the Sales section is reached; report completion and terminate instead of opening an arbitrary order or repeatedly exploring empty tabs and action menus.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only asks to navigate to Magento’s Sales section for managing orders, invoices, and shipments, and the expanded Sales menu visibly contains those navigation entries.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Management
skills.principle:
1. Select the top-level "CONTENT" navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Choose the relevant content-management link, such as "Pages," "Blocks," or a Design option.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, URL, and visible management controls match the selected area.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requests access to pages, blocks, media, or design tools and the current page is elsewhere or the Content submenu is collapsed.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Content Menu
skills.principle: When the task is to access Magento’s Content section, click “CONTENT” and verify that its submenu shows relevant entries such as Pages, Blocks, Widgets, or Design. Once this menu is visibly expanded, report completion and stop; do not open a specific item, create a page, modify settings, or navigate elsewhere unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the instruction only asks to go to or access Magento Admin’s Content section, and the expanded Content menu visibly exposes the requested management categories.

skills.title: Find a Customer’s Latest Order
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s Sales > Orders page.
2. Enter the customer’s name in “Search by keyword” and click “Search”; confirm the active filter and result count update.
3. Identify the matching row with the newest “Purchase Date,” then click its row-level “View” link.
4. Verify the order details page shows the customer name, order number, date, and status before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when locating a customer’s most recent order in Magento Admin. Requires access to Sales > Orders and a visible customer-name search field; verify sorting and matching row data before opening details.

skills.title: Clear Unintended Catalog Filters
skills.principle: On the Magento Products grid, inspect the “Active filters” area before judging results. If an inherited keyword or SKU filter is unrelated to the task, click “Clear all” and confirm the grid refreshes. Use the resulting record count and product rows to determine whether the catalog loaded successfully.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening Magento Catalog > Products and the grid shows zero records or an unexpected empty state, especially when “Active filters” displays a prefilled keyword or SKU value.

skills.title: Search Orders and Inspect Shipping Details
skills.principle:
1. On the Magento Admin Orders page, enter the requested order identifier in the “Search by keyword” field and activate “Search.”
2. Confirm the results count and matching order ID, then select its row’s “View” link.
3. In “Address Information,” read the “Shipping Address” block and report the displayed recipient, street, locality, country, and phone number.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an order identifier is known and the Orders table is large, empty, or filtered. Ensure the search results show the exact requested order before opening its “View” link.

skills.title: Recover From Failed Navigation Actions
skills.principle: After a navigation action returns an error or leaves the page unchanged, stop repeating it. Reinspect the current accessibility tree, target the visible control by its semantic label or current reference, and use valid action syntax. Confirm success through a changed URL, heading, or displayed section before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin navigation control produces an empty-action/error response or repeated clicks do not change the page state.

skills.title: Open and Verify Marketing Navigation
skills.principle: Click the top-level “MARKETING” navigation entry from another Magento Admin section. Confirm the menu expands and visibly lists categories such as Promotions, Communications, SEO & Search, and User Content before reporting that the Marketing section is available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Magento Admin’s Marketing area from another section, and the accessibility tree shows a top-level “MARKETING” navigation entry.

skills.title: Verify Menu State Before Selecting Items
skills.principle: After opening a Magento Admin top-level menu, use the refreshed accessibility tree to identify the expanded submenu and click its actual destination links. Do not click presentation-only group headings or stale element references. If a submenu interaction fails, use the visible link's role and label, or its observed destination, and verify that the page heading and URL changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Magento Admin menus such as Marketing, especially after a menu click changes the accessibility tree or when group headings intercept clicks and the intended destination links are visible.

skills.title: Verify Bulk Action Availability
skills.principle: On the Magento Orders page, select the requested orders and confirm the selected count. Open Actions and inspect its actual options; do not assume a status-update command exists. If the target operation is absent, close the menu using its toggle or Escape, then locate another status-editing control while verifying the page title and URL before clicking. Avoid arbitrary page clicks that may trigger actions such as “Create New Order.”
skills.when_to_apply: When updating multiple Magento orders and the Actions menu is open, especially when the desired status is not listed or a click fails because an overlay intercepts pointer events.

skills.title: Use Order Detail Status Control
skills.principle: When bulk Actions lacks a status-update option, open each target order’s View page. Use the order detail Status combobox to select “Processing,” then submit the change through the available form control (such as “Submit Comment”). Return to Orders and repeat for every target, verifying each row shows the requested status.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin Orders when selected orders cannot be status-updated from the Actions menu, but an order detail page exposes a Status combobox and submission control.

skills.title: Open Admin Account Settings
skills.principle:
1. On any Magento Admin page, activate the logged-in administrator’s username link in the header.
2. Select the revealed “Account Setting” entry rather than unrelated options.
3. Confirm navigation by checking for the “My Account” heading and account-information form, then report completion without changing fields.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to access Magento administrator profile settings. The header must show the logged-in username, and completion is confirmed by the “My Account” page with user, password, locale, and identity-verification fields.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Target Page
skills.principle: Once navigation produces the requested page, verify its heading and relevant controls, then report completion and terminate. Do not issue repeated no-op actions, since they add no progress and can prevent the trajectory from being recognized as complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current observation clearly shows the requested destination, such as the expected page heading, URL, or task-specific form controls.

skills.title: Open Magento Product Views Report
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the REPORTS navigation menu, locate the Products section, and select “Views.” Confirm completion by checking that the page heading reads “Product Views Report”; the report may legitimately show no records for its default date range.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view most-viewed products in Magento Admin and the Reports navigation is available. Use the displayed report heading to verify successful navigation before reporting completion.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility References
skills.principle: After each page observation, act only on element references present in that observation. If a click fails because a bid is missing, re-inspect the current accessibility tree, locate the target navigation entry by its visible role or label, and retry with its current reference rather than repeating the stale bid. Confirm the resulting page before declaring the task infeasible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating admin menus or multi-page interfaces where accessibility bids can change, disappear, or differ from identifiers inferred in prior observations.

skills.title: Confirm Empty Filtered Results
skills.principle: For an admin record search, verify the requested date range is shown as an active filter, click Search, and inspect the grid’s result count and empty-state message. If the grid reports zero records, communicate that no matching records were found and stop; do not repeat searches or export an empty result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when searching an administrative grid for records matching a date range or other criteria, especially when the page already displays the requested filter and an explicit zero-records or empty-state result.

skills.title: Use Date Filters, Not Keyword Search
skills.principle: On the Credit Memos grid, open the “Filters” control and set the “Created” date range to the requested period. Apply the filter, then verify the active filter label and resulting record count. Do not enter a date range into “Search by keyword,” because that searches text rather than dates.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Magento Admin credit memos or similar grids by creation date, especially when a keyword field and a separate Filters control are both visible.

skills.title: Expand Sales and Verify Destination
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, activate the top-level “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu, then select “Orders” (or the requested sales subsection). Confirm completion by checking the page heading and URL show the selected subsection, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Magento Admin’s Sales section and the current page may already be within Sales but its submenu is collapsed.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Section
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation section, verify the active label and visible submenu or section content. Once the target section is clearly active, report completion and terminate; do not repeat clicks or issue repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the requested admin section is already open or becomes active after one click, evidenced by its highlighted label and visible related navigation options.

skills.title: Export Empty Grids Without Assumptions
skills.principle: Check the current filters and record count before exporting. If the requested grid is empty, distinguish an empty result from a disabled export: use the available export control and inspect its response, reporting a header-only or empty file only when the resulting download is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting an administrative grid that shows zero records or an empty-results message.

skills.title: Verify Export Completion Directly
skills.principle: On the Magento Credit Memos grid, open Export, keep CSV selected, and click the dialog’s Export button. Verify completion through a download event or downloaded file, not merely unchanged page content or repeated waiting. If the export dialog remains open, inspect and retry the dialog action rather than assuming success.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a Magento admin grid to CSV and the page remains unchanged after clicking Export; prerequisites are access to the target grid and an enabled Export control.

skills.title: Open Matching Credit Memo Details
skills.principle: In the credit-memo list, locate the row whose Order # matches the requested order, then activate that row’s “View” action. Verify the destination by checking the details page heading and Order # link before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific order’s credit memo in Magento Admin and the credit-memo list contains an Order # column with row-level “View” actions.

skills.title: Stop After Details Are Displayed
skills.principle: When the target record’s details page is visible, verify its heading and identifying information match the requested item. Then report completion and terminate immediately; do not issue repeated no-op actions or remain idle on the page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for administrative tasks requesting a record’s details when the page visibly shows the expected detail heading and matching order, memo, or record identifier.

skills.title: Export Magento Grid Data as CSV
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant Magento Admin sales grid, such as Credit Memos.
2. Click the grid’s “Export” control and choose “CSV” in the export dialog; leave it selected if already defaulted.
3. Click the dialog’s final “Export” button to initiate the download.
4. Report completion after the final export action; do not repeat unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when exporting records from a Magento Admin grid and the page provides an “Export” control with CSV and Excel format options.

skills.title: Confirm Export Completion State
skills.principle:
1. Click the grid’s “Export” control to open export options.
2. Verify the “CSV” radio option is selected, then click the dialog’s “Export” button once.
3. Check for a browser download or visible success/error indication; do not repeatedly click or wait without new evidence.
4. If no completion signal appears, investigate downloads or page errors before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a Magento Admin grid such as credit memos, with the target records and the grid-level “Export” control visible. Use only after confirming the desired filters and format.

skills.title: Export Data in Excel XML Format
skills.principle:
1. On the relevant Magento admin listing, click the main “Export” control to reveal format options.
2. Select the “Excel XML” radio option, confirming it becomes checked instead of the default format.
3. Click the dialog’s “Export” button to initiate the download, then report completion without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when exporting records from a Magento admin grid and the requested output is Excel XML. The listing must expose an Export control and the format-selection dialog must include “Excel XML”.

skills.title: Complete Export With Verification
skills.principle: On the Magento Credit Memos grid, open Export, select Excel XML, then activate the dialog’s Export button. Verify that a download or browser download-state change occurs; once confirmed, stop immediately rather than repeatedly clicking Export.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting credit memo records from Magento Admin and the Export dialog offers CSV and Excel XML choices. Ensure the intended format is selected before submitting, then verify the download through available browser state.

skills.title: Open Matching Credit Memo Details
skills.principle: From the Credit Memos list, identify the row matching the requested memo identifier and customer, then activate its row-level “View” link. Confirm the detail page shows the matching customer and memo context before reporting completion; do not perform unrelated edits or actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a specific Magento Admin credit memo and the list contains identifiable memo, customer, and “View” action fields.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Details
skills.principle: After opening the target record, verify the page heading and identifying fields match the requested item. Once the details are visibly displayed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for record-view tasks when the target details page has loaded and its heading plus identifying information visibly match the requested record.

skills.title: Expand Sales and Verify Destination
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level navigation menu, such as “SALES,” to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu entry matching the requested destination, such as “Billing Agreements.”
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading or title matches the destination, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Magento Admin from another page to a destination hidden inside a collapsible top-level menu. Verify the resulting heading before concluding.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Once the target page is visible and its heading or URL confirms successful navigation, report completion immediately and terminate the interaction. Do not issue repeated no-op actions or wait for additional observations after the goal is already satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: Use navigation tasks when the requested destination is visibly confirmed by the page heading, selected menu item, or URL, especially when no edits or further page interaction are required.

skills.title: Apply and Verify Status Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the list's Filters panel.
2. Set the relevant Status dropdown to the requested value.
3. Click Apply Filters to submit the selection.
4. Confirm completion by checking Active filters shows the requested status and the table rows reflect it, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin list pages when filtering records by status. The Filters control and an Apply Filters button must be available; verify the resulting active filter and displayed records before finishing.

skills.title: Verify Filters Then Stop
skills.principle:
1. Open the list’s Filters panel and set the requested field to the target value.
2. Click “Apply Filters.”
3. Confirm the active-filter summary shows the requested criterion and inspect the result count and rows for matching values.
4. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not repeat no-op waits or invent counts.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering an admin list and the page shows filter controls, an active-filter summary, and a result table after applying criteria.

skills.title: Apply Created-Date Range Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the list’s Filters control.
2. In the Created date group, enter the requested start date in from and end date in to, using the page’s expected format.
3. Select Apply Filters.
4. Confirm the Active filters section shows the intended range and inspect the resulting records count or rows.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin list pages when the task requires restricting records by creation date. Ensure the Filters panel is available and distinguish Created dates from similarly labeled date fields such as Order Date.

skills.title: Clear Stale Filters Before Applying
skills.principle: On an admin grid, inspect the active-filter summary before filtering. Remove unrelated existing filters with “Clear all” or individual remove controls, open “Filters,” set the requested field and date range, then click “Apply Filters.” Confirm the active-filter summary and result count reflect the intended criteria before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin listing already shows active filters, especially when the task requests only a new date or field constraint and stale filters could silently narrow the results.

skills.title: Filter Credit Memos by Customer
skills.principle:
1. On the Credit Memos page, open “Filters” and locate the “Bill-to Name” field.
2. Enter the requested customer name and select “Apply Filters.”
3. Confirm the active filter, record count, and matching customer row before reporting the memo’s relevant details and stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when searching Magento Admin credit memos by customer name and the Credit Memos page exposes “Filters,” “Bill-to Name,” and “Apply Filters” controls.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Search Results
skills.principle: When the requested record type and search criterion are already visible, verify the result count and matching row, then report completion. Do not open customer or record details unless the task explicitly requests details; unnecessary navigation can lose the valid filtered state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin list-search tasks when the page already shows the requested filter and at least one matching result, especially when the instruction asks only to search rather than inspect or modify a record.

skills.title: Recover Orders Through Stale Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales > Orders rather than another sales record type.
2. If inherited filters produce no records, use “Clear all,” then confirm the order list repopulates.
3. Identify the target row using its order number or other supplied attributes, and select that row’s “View” action.
4. Verify the detail page heading and key order fields before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin’s Orders page opens with unexpected search filters, zero results, or a stale customer/keyword filter, and the task requires viewing a particular order’s details.

skills.title: Verify Existing Filters Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current Credit Memos page for active filters and result rows before changing anything. If the customer filter is already applied and the results show the requested status, confirm the matching count and key details, then report completion without reapplying filters or taking unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping-admin list page may open with filters already applied. Confirm the active filter labels, result count, and relevant status column before performing additional filtering.

skills.title: Apply Filters Through Visible Controls
skills.principle: Open the Filters panel before editing filter values. Set each required field using its visible label, such as customer name and status “Refunded,” then click “Apply Filters.” Verify the active-filter summary and records-found count before stopping; do not repeatedly click Search when the page state is unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin grid pages when filters are hidden or active-filter chips are already shown, especially when direct interaction with previously used filter element references reports that the control is not visible.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the CATALOG menu and select Categories. After clicking, verify the resulting URL, page title, and category tree. If these indicate the Categories management page loaded, report completion immediately; do not retry the click merely because navigation timed out.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin from another page to Catalog > Categories, especially if the click reports a timeout after scheduled navigation may already have completed.

skills.title: Use Valid Navigation Targets
skills.principle: When navigating an admin menu, target the actual visible navigation link by its role and readable label, not the parent menubar or a copied Unicode-heavy bid. Ensure the emitted action is complete and nonempty. After an element or selector error, re-inspect the current accessibility tree and choose a new valid target rather than repeatedly retrying the same malformed selector.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when an admin page exposes section navigation such as CATALOG and browser actions return empty-action or element-not-found errors, especially when accessibility labels contain icon glyphs.

skills.title: Verify Search Results Before Reporting
skills.principle:
1. Enter the target record identifier in the page's keyword search box.
2. Activate the labeled Search control.
3. Confirm execution by checking the identifier appears as an active Keyword filter, the result count is shown, and the matching record appears in the table.
4. Report completion and stop once these indicators confirm the search succeeded.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin list pages when asked to search for a specific sales record and the page provides a keyword search box, Search control, active filters, and result table.

skills.title: Verify Search Results and Stop
skills.principle: After submitting a list search, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree for the active keyword filter, matching row, and result count. When the target appears and the count confirms results, report completion and terminate immediately rather than clicking Search again or issuing repeated waits.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin grid searches when the search field and Search button are available, especially when the page already shows an active filter and a matching record.

skills.title: Open and Verify the Sales Menu
skills.principle: Click the admin navigation entry labeled “SALES” to expand its submenu. Confirm completion by checking that the submenu is visibly open and exposes sales-related options such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, and Credit Memos, then report success without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to an admin panel’s Sales section and the page already displays the main navigation bar. Use the visible submenu contents as the completion signal.

skills.title: Stop After Expanding Sales
skills.principle: Click the top-level “SALES” navigation entry once. Confirm the Sales submenu or “Sales” section label is visible; this indicates navigation is complete. Do not open Orders, Invoices, Shipments, or other child pages unless explicitly requested. Report completion and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only asks to navigate to the admin panel’s Sales section and the top-level “SALES” entry is visible in the navigation menu.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog Products
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation entry labeled “CATALOG” to reveal its submenu.
2. Select “Products” rather than stopping at the expanded menu.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Products” and product-management controls such as “Add Product,” filters, and the product table are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires reaching the product-management area from another admin page, and the navigation shows a collapsible “CATALOG” entry with a “Products” submenu item.

skills.title: Navigate Marketing Promotions
skills.principle:
1. Open the main navigation's “MARKETING” section to reveal its submenu.
2. Under “Promotions,” select “Cart Price Rules” for promotion management.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Cart Price Rules” and controls such as “Add New Rule,” search, and filters are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Magento Admin’s Marketing area to manage promotions, starting from another admin page with the main navigation visible.

skills.title: Use the Visible Toggle Control
skills.principle:
1. When a styled checkbox reports pointer interception, target its visible switch label or Yes/No control instead of the hidden input.
2. Activate the control and inspect the accessibility tree for the updated checked state or visible “Yes” label.
3. Continue only after confirming the toggle changed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento admin forms where a checkbox is implemented as a styled switch and clicking the underlying input times out because its label or switch text intercepts pointer events.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Management
skills.principle:
1. Identify the top-level “CONTENT” navigation entry in the accessibility tree and activate it.
2. Select “Pages” under the expanded “Elements” submenu to open the CMS page-management area.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Pages” and the CMS pages list is visible, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Magento Admin’s Content management area and the navigation menu exposes “CONTENT”; select “Pages” when a concrete CMS management destination is required.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Content Section
skills.principle: When the requested destination is a navigation section, click the matching menu entry once, then verify its submenu or heading appears. Once the Content menu and its Elements options are visible, report completion and terminate; do not enter Pages, create records, or perform unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only Magento Admin tasks requesting the Content section, when clicking CONTENT reveals the Content menu with options such as Pages, Blocks, Widgets, or Media Gallery.

skills.title: Confirm Visible Filter State
skills.principle: When the requested search term is already shown in the page’s keyword textbox and active-filter summary, verify the displayed value and result status. Report the value directly, noting zero results if shown, then terminate without repeating no-op actions or reopening the search.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin list pages when the requested search/filter information is already visible and the page state clearly shows the active keyword and resulting record count.

skills.title: Navigate to the Requested Admin Feature
skills.principle: Do not interpret a grid’s existing “Search by keyword” value as the requested Search Terms page. Use the visible admin navigation to open the section containing Search Terms, select that navigation entry, and verify the destination by its page heading or content. If the requested feature is not present on the current page, navigate rather than repeatedly issuing no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task names a report, configuration page, or feature that is absent from the current page, especially when a similarly named search field or filter is already populated.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog Management
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation’s “CATALOG” menu.
2. Select “Products” to enter the catalog management area.
3. Confirm completion when the page shows the “Products” heading and product-management controls such as “Add Product,” search, or filters.
4. Report completion and stop once the destination is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Magento’s Catalog area from another admin page, provided the top navigation contains a visible “CATALOG” entry and its submenu exposes “Products” or another relevant catalog destination.

skills.title: Expand Reports Navigation
skills.principle: Click the visible Reports navigation entry in the admin menu. Confirm the menu expands and exposes categorized report links, such as Sales, Products, Customers, Marketing, Statistics, or other performance reports; this expanded menu state completes navigation when no specific report was requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks to navigate to the Reports section generally, and the accessibility tree shows a visible Reports navigation entry. Do not open an individual report unless the task names one.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Page Templates
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin CONTENT navigation entry.
2. Under Elements, select the Templates link.
3. Confirm the destination by checking the Templates heading and inspect the records count or empty-state message before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Page Templates in Magento Admin and the CONTENT navigation menu is available. Use the Templates entry under Elements, then verify the resulting page state.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate through the relevant admin section, then verify the destination by its heading, URL, or distinctive page controls. Once the requested page is visibly loaded, treat access as complete and terminate; do not search for creation controls or perform repeated no-op actions unless the task explicitly requires further changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the accessibility tree shows the requested destination page loaded, even if its list is empty or no additional action is visible.

skills.title: Expand Navigation Before Declaring Infeasibility
skills.principle: When the requested Magento Admin page is not visible, inspect the relevant top-level navigation instead of concluding it is unavailable. Expand CONTENT, locate the Design submenu, and select Configuration. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the page heading or resulting URL before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a requested admin page is absent from the current content view but a matching top-level navigation entry, such as CONTENT, is visible and expandable.

skills.title: Follow Related Order Links
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, use the record’s action link to open its details, then follow the embedded “Order #” link to reach the full order page. Confirm completion when the page heading shows the target order number and the Information panel displays order, customer, items, and totals.
skills.when_to_apply: When a target order is represented indirectly in a Credit Memos or similar sales list, and its details view exposes an “Order #” link to the full order record.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Admin Reports
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation section matching the report category, such as “REPORTS.”
2. Read the expanded submenu and select the exact report label, such as “Newsletter Problem Reports.”
3. Confirm the destination heading and table result; report the explicit empty-state message when no records exist.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requesting a specific report when the report is nested under a top-level navigation menu. Verify the destination page and its records or empty-state text before responding.

skills.title: Stop After Target Page Confirmation
skills.principle: Navigate through Reports, open the Marketing subsection, and select “Newsletter Problem Reports.” Once the page heading and report table confirm the requested destination, report completion and terminate. Do not reset filters, change pagination, inspect unrelated system messages, or navigate away unless the task explicitly requests further investigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks to view a specific report and the accessibility tree shows the matching page heading, report columns, and current results state.

skills.title: Read Shipping Address From Credit Memo
skills.principle: On a Magento credit memo view, locate the “Address Information” section and distinguish “Shipping Address” from “Billing Address.” Read the complete shipping address block, including recipient, street, locality, country, and phone, then report it without confusing it with the billing address.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a credit memo page is already open and the task asks for its shipping address. Confirm the address comes from the labeled “Shipping Address” block under “Address Information.”

skills.title: Report Findings After Verification
skills.principle: Once the target credit memo’s detail page is open, read the value under “Shipping Address,” provide that address in the task response, and terminate. Do not repeat noop actions after the information is verified; page inspection alone does not complete a read-only task.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin credit memo detail page visibly shows the requested Shipping Address and the task asks you to check or report it.

skills.title: Add and Verify Credit Memo Comments
skills.principle:
1. On the target credit memo page, locate the textbox labeled "Comment Text" and enter the requested comment.
2. Leave notification and storefront visibility options unchanged unless explicitly requested, then click "Submit Comment".
3. Confirm completion by checking that the exact comment appears as the newest entry in "Credit Memo History", then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requires adding a comment to an existing Magento credit memo and the credit memo view is available. Verify the target order or memo before submitting.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When semantic locators fail, use the numeric bid shown for the intended control in the latest accessibility tree. Fill the comment textbox, click the current “Submit Comment” button bid, then verify the new comment appears in the history before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento credit memo pages when label-based or description-based textbox locators return “Could not find element.” Reinspect the latest accessibility tree because bids can change after submission.

skills.title: Confirm Email Success After Dialog
skills.principle: On the relevant order or credit memo page, select the "Send Email" action. When the confirmation dialog appears, activate "OK". If the click reports a timeout but the dialog disappears, inspect the refreshed page before retrying; a visible "You sent the message" notice confirms completion. Stop and report success once that notice appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when sending an order-related email in Magento Admin and a confirmation dialog precedes the action. The relevant order or credit memo page must expose a "Send Email" control.

skills.title: Verify Email Success Before Retrying
skills.principle: After selecting Send Email and confirming the modal with OK, inspect the resulting page state. Treat messages such as “You sent the order email” or “order confirmation email was sent” as completion, even if the click reports a navigation timeout. Stop immediately once success is visible; do not click Send Email again.
skills.when_to_apply: When sending an order email from a Magento order-details page, especially after a confirmation click returns a timeout while the page may already display a success notification.

skills.title: Use the Partners Directory Link
skills.principle: From an unrelated Magento Admin page, select the navigation entry labeled "FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS." On the marketplace page, locate the requested partner under the relevant partner tier, read its heading and description, then report the partner classification and stated capabilities. Stop once the matching partner information is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to retrieve information about a Magento partner and the current Admin page exposes the "FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS" navigation entry. Verify the requested partner appears in the resulting partner listing before responding.

skills.title: Use Visible Partner Details Directly
skills.principle: On the Magento Marketplace page, inspect the Featured Platinum Partners section and match the requested partner by its accessible name. Read the adjacent description first; use its “Read More” or “Partner Page” link only if additional detail is required. Report the observed information once the partner and description are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving information about a named Magento partner and the Marketplace page shows Featured Platinum Partners with accessible headings, descriptions, and partner-specific links.

skills.title: Use Visible Partner Details First
skills.principle: When the target partner is listed, extract the displayed heading and description as the answer. Report the relevant facts immediately once they satisfy the request; open “Read More” or “Partner Page” only when the visible information is insufficient, and verify the resulting page before taking further action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin’s “FIND PARTNERS & EXTENSIONS” page when the requested partner appears in the Featured Partners list with an accessible description.

skills.title: Use Visible Partner Details First
skills.principle: On the Magento Marketplace partner page, locate the target partner card and extract its heading and descriptive paragraph directly. Report those visible details as the answer; only open “Read More” or “Partner Page” if the request explicitly requires information not shown in the card.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to retrieve information about a named Magento partner and the partner card is already visible with a heading and description.

skills.title: Read Credit Memo Refund Items
skills.principle: On a Magento credit memo page, locate the “Items Refunded” table and read the Product cell. Report the product name and any displayed identifying options, such as SKU, size, and color. Once the requested refund item is confirmed, report it and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which product was refunded for an order and a corresponding Magento credit memo or refund-details page is already open.

skills.title: Verify Refunded Order Items
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s Sales menu and select Orders.
2. Search the order list using the requested order number, then open the matching order.
3. In Items Ordered, identify rows whose Item Status is “Refunded” and report the product name and refund amount.
4. Confirm the result from the item row’s refund status and amount before responding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking which product was refunded in a specific order, provided you can access Sales > Orders and the order appears in search results.

skills.title: Use Visible Partner Details Directly
skills.principle: When the target partner appears in the current Marketplace accessibility tree, extract and report its heading and descriptive paragraph immediately. Treat associated “Read More” or “Partner Page” links as optional only when additional detail is explicitly required; do not navigate away before capturing the visible answer.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Marketplace pages when the requested partner is listed with readable descriptive text and the task asks to retrieve information rather than open a separate partner profile.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales to Invoices
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento admin Sales navigation entry from the current page.
2. Select the visible Invoices submenu item.
3. Confirm the Invoices page is loaded and verify its record count and invoice table before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all invoices in Magento Admin, especially when starting on another Sales-related page and the Sales menu is available in the navigation.

skills.title: Distinguish Subscriber Search From Creation
skills.principle: On Magento's Newsletter Subscribers grid, treat the email field and Search button as filters only; they cannot create records. First look for an explicit add/create control. If none exists, use the supported subscription workflow instead of entering a new email into the filter or expecting zero results to offer creation.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a newsletter subscriber from the Magento admin and the page shows a subscriber grid with filter fields, Search, and management actions such as Unsubscribe or Delete but no explicit creation control.

skills.title: Pivot From Subscriber List Management
skills.principle: When the Magento Newsletter Subscribers page shows only filters, Search, Export, and actions such as Unsubscribe or Delete, treat it as an existing-record management view. Do not enter a new email into a filter. Navigate to Customers > All Customers, create or edit the target customer, enable newsletter subscription, save, and verify the subscriber appears in the list.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding a subscriber is requested but the Newsletter Subscribers page has no Add New control and its actions only manage existing records.

skills.title: Verify Invoice List Completeness
skills.principle: Open Sales, select Invoices, and verify the grid’s “records found” count, per-page setting, and pagination state. If all records fit on one page and navigation controls are disabled, the complete invoice list is already visible; report completion without opening each invoice or performing extra scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all invoices in Magento Admin and the Invoices grid is accessible. Use the record count and pagination controls to confirm completeness before considering individual invoice details.

skills.title: Review Every Credit Memo Once
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales, select Credit Memos, and inspect the table’s record count, active filters, and pagination.
2. Clear unintended filters before reviewing all available records.
3. Open each memo’s View action, examine its details, then use Back to return to the list.
4. Stop only when every listed record and page has been reviewed, then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring review of all credit memos, especially when the list may be filtered or paginated. Verify the displayed count and active filters before concluding.

skills.title: Verify List Scope Before Reviewing Records
skills.principle:
1. On the Credit Memos list, inspect active filters and clear any inherited keyword or order filter.
2. Confirm the displayed record count and pagination before opening records; do not assume unseen memo numbers exist.
3. Open each visible memo using its current row action, then return to the memo list through the current Sales > Credit Memos navigation.
4. Recheck the list state after every return and stop when all pages and rows are reviewed.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing all records in an admin grid, especially after arriving from a filtered detail or order page. Prerequisite: verify filters, record count, and pagination before iterating.

skills.title: Save and Verify Newsletter Edits
skills.principle: On the pending newsletter’s Edit Queue form, make a targeted change to the required subject or message field rather than submitting an oversized payload. Click “Save Newsletter,” then verify the resulting confirmation or updated queue state before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a newsletter has been queued and the “Edit Queue” form is open with editable Subject or Message fields and a visible “Save Newsletter” control.

skills.title: Verify Queue Availability Before Editing
skills.principle: Navigate through Marketing to Communications, then open Newsletter Queue. Inspect the result count and table contents before attempting edits. If the page shows zero records or “We couldn't find any records,” report that no editable queued item exists and request creation or queueing of a newsletter first.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a pending newsletter in Magento Admin, after opening Marketing > Communications > Newsletter Queue and before selecting or modifying any queue entry.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL, page heading, and navigation labels before acting. If they already identify the requested admin section, report completion and stop. Otherwise, activate the navigation entry matching the requested section, then verify the resulting heading or URL before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin-panel navigation tasks when the initial page may already be the requested section and the accessibility tree exposes URLs, headings, or navigation labels.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Target State
skills.principle: When the current page already matches the requested destination, verify it using the URL, page heading, or selected navigation label. Then report completion and terminate with the environment’s valid completion mechanism; do not emit a no-op action, which may be rejected as an empty action.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to navigation tasks when the accessibility tree already shows the requested section and the browser is at its corresponding page. Use a supported termination or completion action rather than repeatedly submitting noop.

skills.title: Verify Online Customer Results
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Customers navigation and select “Now Online.”
2. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and results area.
3. Report the displayed count; treat “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records” as no customers online.
4. If navigation reports a timeout but the destination page is already loaded, use its observed results instead of retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking current customer presence in Magento Admin, after the Customers menu exposes “Now Online.” Use the page heading and records count as completion evidence, including an empty-results state.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming No Online Customers
skills.principle: Navigate to Customers > Now Online and inspect the result count and table. If the page explicitly shows “0 records found” and “We couldn't find any records,” report that no customers are currently online. Do not alter pagination, apply empty filters, revisit the page, or inspect unrelated account activity unless the task specifically requires troubleshooting.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking Magento customer presence and the Now Online page loads successfully with an explicit zero-record count and empty-results message.

skills.title: Open Magento Content Navigation
skills.principle: In the Magento Admin navigation bar, locate the top-level “CONTENT” entry and activate it. Confirm completion when its expanded dropdown is visible, showing grouped options such as Elements, Media, and Design; stop there unless the task names a specific submenu destination.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to Magento Admin’s CONTENT section without opening a particular content-management page. The navigation bar must be visible and the CONTENT entry identifiable.

skills.title: Verify Expandable Navigation Menus
skills.principle: Treat a top-level admin label with a `#` or unchanged URL as an expandable menu, not a destination page. Click it once, inspect the newly revealed submenu, then select the required child link such as Pages, Blocks, or Media Gallery. Confirm completion by checking that the submenu is visible or the destination URL/page content changes; do not repeat the same click indefinitely.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin navigation label remains on the same URL after clicking and reveals child entries, especially when the task requests access to a section containing specific content-management pages.

skills.title: Open Admin Navigation Sections
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to locate the requested top-level admin navigation entry by its visible label and role. Activate it once, then verify completion from the updated page state: the entry is focused or expanded and its submenu options are visible. Report completion immediately when this state matches the request.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin-panel task asks to navigate to a top-level section and the accessibility tree exposes that section as a labeled navigation link or menu entry.

skills.title: Select Stores Submenu Destination
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, clicking the top-level “STORES” entry only expands its menu. After expansion, choose the submenu item matching the task, such as “All Stores,” and verify navigation by checking that the page content or URL changes. Do not repeat the parent-menu click when the submenu is already visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests the Stores section and the accessibility tree shows “STORES” expanded with submenu entries such as “All Stores” or “Configuration”.

skills.title: Expand Magento System Menu
