skills.principle: In the Magento Admin navigation, locate the top-level link labeled "SYSTEM" and click it. Confirm completion when the System menu expands and its submenu categories, such as Data Transfer, Tools, or Permissions, become visible; then stop without performing unrelated actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task is to navigate to Magento Admin’s SYSTEM section and the accessibility tree shows the top-level "SYSTEM" navigation link.

skills.title: Use Current Navigation Element Bids
skills.principle: When a navigation label includes an icon and its displayed link URL is only a placeholder, activate the navigation element using its current accessibility-tree bid or a properly resolved locator—not copied icon text. Then inspect the updated tree for an expanded submenu or active state. Treat an unchanged page, title, or hash fragment as unverified rather than successful.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this in admin panels when a section such as SYSTEM appears in the accessibility tree but text-based or icon-inclusive clicks fail, especially when the link href points to a dashboard placeholder.

skills.title: Search Orders and Verify Status
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales, then select Orders.
2. Use the current textbox labeled “Search by keyword” to enter the target order number; rely on the current accessibility tree rather than stale element identifiers.
3. Activate Search and confirm exactly one matching row.
4. Open its View link and read the “Order Status” field on the details page before reporting it.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving an order’s status in Magento Admin, with access to the Sales > Orders page and a target order number.

skills.title: Report Status After Verification
skills.principle: When the order details page shows the target order and an explicit “Order Status” value, read that value, report it as the task result, and terminate. Do not repeatedly issue no-op actions after verification; the observable status row is sufficient completion evidence.
skills.when_to_apply: For Magento Admin tasks asking for an order’s status, after opening the matching order details page and locating the “Order Status” row.

skills.title: Recognize Already-Loaded Memo History
skills.principle: When the current Magento credit memo page already shows the target order and the “Credit Memo History” heading with its entries, use the visible list as completion evidence. Avoid unnecessary navigation or repeated scrolling, and report that the history is available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view credit memo history and the loaded admin page identifies the target order and visibly contains the “Credit Memo History” section and entries.

skills.title: Verify Navigation State Before Continuing
skills.principle: Use the visible accessibility tree to drive navigation. Expand the Sales menu, then select the explicitly labeled Orders or Credit Memos entry. After each click, confirm the URL, heading, or newly exposed menu items changed. If the state is unchanged, stop repeating the same target and inspect the current tree for the correct control before acting.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin from the dashboard to order-related records, especially when a menu click leaves the page unchanged or the intended submenu is not yet visible.

skills.title: Verify Save and Stop
skills.principle: After completing all required newsletter fields, click “Save Template” and confirm the list page shows a success message such as “The newsletter template has been saved” and the new record. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of performing unnecessary follow-up actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento newsletter template and the save action returns to the template list, especially when a visible success confirmation and newly increased record count establish that creation succeeded.

skills.title: Report Visible Order Address Immediately
skills.principle: When an order or credit-memo page already displays the requested shipping address, read the values under the explicitly labeled “Shipping Address” section, distinguish them from “Billing Address,” report the complete address and phone number, then stop. Do not navigate to unrelated admin features after the requested information is found.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento order-information tasks when the current page is associated with the target order and its Address Information section visibly contains a Shipping Address block.

skills.title: Report Address After Verification
skills.principle: Once the target order’s details page shows a clearly labeled “Shipping Address” section, read the displayed name, street, locality, region, postal code, country, and phone number. Use the visible address directly for a check-only task; open “Edit” only if full field-level inspection is necessary. Report the address immediately after verification and terminate instead of repeating no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check an order’s shipping address and the order view or address form visibly contains the requested fields. No save action is needed unless the task explicitly requests changing the address.

skills.title: Verify URL Rewrite Saves
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, identify product rewrites by a `Target Path` beginning with `catalog/product/view`, open the row’s `Select` menu, choose `Edit`, change only the `Request Path`, and click `Save`. Confirm “The URL Rewrite has been saved” and verify the updated request path appears in the table before editing another record or finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing product URL rewrites in Marketing → SEO & Search → URL Rewrites, especially after changing a request path and before claiming completion.

skills.title: Edit the Requested Rewrite Precisely
skills.principle: In Magento Marketing > SEO & Search > URL Rewrites, identify the target product by its product target path and store view rather than choosing an arbitrary row. Open Select > Edit, change only the requested Request Path, leave the disabled Target Path unchanged, click Save, and verify the confirmation message and updated table entry before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing Magento product URL rewrites, especially with many duplicate store-view records. Use the task’s specified product, store scope, and desired path; do not invent SEO values or modify unrelated rewrites.

skills.title: Summarize Visible Credit Memo Details
skills.principle: When the correct credit memo page is already open, read the refunded-items table and credit memo totals directly. Report the target product’s identifying attributes, quantity, item-level amounts, shipping, grand total, and relevant history. Send one properly formatted completion message, then stop; do not repeat submissions, emit nested JSON, or use unnecessary no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking about a refunded product when the credit memo view is already visible and contains the Items Refunded, Credit Memo Totals, and history sections.

skills.title: Use Credit Memos for Refunded Products
skills.principle: For a refunded product in Magento Admin, open SALES and choose Credit Memos rather than relying on the Orders keyword search. Search or inspect credit-memo records, open the relevant memo, and verify the refunded item in its details or linked order. Treat “no records” and absent status options as signals to switch to the refund-specific section.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks for details about a refunded product and the Orders grid returns no matches, especially when the grid’s Status options do not include “Refunded.”

skills.title: Use Direct Dashboard Navigation
skills.principle: From an admin detail page, choose the persistent top-navigation link labeled “DASHBOARD” rather than a generic Back button when the goal names the dashboard. After navigation, verify completion through the page heading, title, or URL showing “Dashboard,” then stop and report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When working in Magento Admin or a similar backend and asked to return to the dashboard from a detail or transaction page with a persistent dashboard navigation link visible.

skills.title: Submit Credit Memo Comments
skills.principle:
1. Open the target credit memo and locate the “Comment Text” field in the “Credit Memo History” section.
2. Enter a concise comment describing the requested issue, preserving relevant order context when needed.
3. Leave “Notify Customer by Email” and “Visible on Storefront” unchanged unless explicitly requested, then click “Submit Comment.”
4. Verify the new comment appears at the top of the history list before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding an administrative note to an existing Magento credit memo. Confirm the correct order or memo is open and the comment field, submission control, and history list are accessible.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Editing
skills.principle: Use the visible link’s role and label to open the target record, then verify the URL or page heading changed before editing. Only fill a textbox or textarea explicitly labeled for comments; never fill a table cell or action container. If navigation fails, retry with a valid locator and re-inspect the updated accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin list contains a target record with a View or Edit action and the next step requires fields on a detail page. Confirm navigation succeeded before locating form controls.

skills.title: Expand Catalog and Open Products
skills.principle: From a Magento Admin page, select the main navigation entry labeled “CATALOG” to reveal its submenu. Choose “Products,” then verify completion using the Products heading and the catalog products page state or URL. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting from another Magento Admin section, such as a credit memo, and the task requests navigation to the Catalog section without specifying Categories or another catalog subsection.

skills.title: Use Expanded Catalog Submenu
skills.principle:
1. Click the Catalog navigation entry once to expand its submenu.
2. Select the specific destination, such as Products or Categories, from the revealed submenu rather than clicking Catalog repeatedly.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the URL, heading, or main content reflects the selected Catalog page.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin from another section and Catalog expands in-place, especially when its parent link retains the current URL and only submenu links lead to destination pages.

skills.title: Expand Customers, Then Select All Customers
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the top-level “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry to reveal its submenu, then select “All Customers.” Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Customers” and the customer-management controls, such as “Add New Customer,” search, and filters, are visible; then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting on another Magento Admin page and asked to reach customer account management or the Customers section. The Customers submenu must be expanded before selecting “All Customers.”

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: Expand the relevant Magento Admin navigation entry, select the destination submenu such as “All Customers,” then verify the page heading or URL shows the requested section. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not repeat clicks on already-active navigation links.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating from an admin record view to another section, especially after the destination page heading and URL are visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Navigate Through Magento Sales Menu
skills.principle: From a Magento Admin sales subsection, open the top-level “SALES” navigation to reveal its submenu, then select “Billing Agreements.” Confirm completion by checking that the page heading reads “Billing Agreements” before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting on a sales-related detail or listing page where the target administrative page is available under the expandable “SALES” menu, but no direct page link is visible.

skills.title: Recover From Invalid Element Bids
skills.principle: When an interaction returns an empty-action or missing-element error, stop repeating the same locator. Re-read the current accessibility tree, identify the element’s actual bid or accessible name (for example, the navigation link’s recorded bid rather than its icon glyph), perform one valid action, and verify that the URL or visible menu state changes before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply whenever a BrowserGym action fails with an invalid, empty, or not-found locator, especially after the page state remains unchanged.

skills.title: Follow Associated Order Link
skills.principle: On a credit memo detail page, locate the linked order identifier in the Order & Account Information section and activate it. Confirm the destination is the order details page by its order heading or order-view page state, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a Magento Admin credit memo and the task requires returning to its associated order details page; the memo must display a clickable order identifier link.

skills.title: Navigate Through Sales Context
skills.principle: When the current page is the Magento Admin dashboard instead of a credit memo, use the visible SALES navigation to reach the relevant credit memo or order list. Open the target credit memo, then follow its associated order link and verify the order details page loaded; do not rely on scrolling the dashboard.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a task requires navigation from a credit memo but the accessibility tree shows Dashboard content without credit memo controls or an associated-order link.

skills.title: Use Orders as Sales Landing View
skills.principle: From a Magento Admin record page, activate the top-level “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu. Select “Orders,” the default/main Sales view, rather than repeatedly toggling the section or selecting the current record type. Confirm completion when the page heading is “Orders” and the URL represents the Sales orders listing.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate from a Sales-related detail page, such as a credit memo, to the general Sales section in Magento Admin and the Sales submenu contains “Orders.”

skills.title: Complete Two-Level Sales Navigation
skills.principle: Click the top-level “SALES” navigation entry to expand its menu, then select the requested Sales subsection (such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, or Credit Memos). Confirm the submenu selection changes the page or URL before reporting completion; an expanded menu alone is not navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin page shows a top-level “SALES” menu whose link preserves the current URL and reveals submenu entries instead of loading a new page.

skills.title: Navigate From Dashboard Menu
skills.principle:
1. If the task specifies navigation from Dashboard, first open the Dashboard link when not already on that page.
2. Re-read the accessibility tree after navigation and locate the main-menu entry by its visible label.
3. Click the target section and verify its dropdown or section-specific options appear.
4. Report completion and stop once the requested menu is visibly open.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring navigation from Dashboard to a top-level section, especially when starting on another admin page and menu links initially have different accessibility identifiers.

skills.title: Select the Shipping Address Edit Link
skills.principle: On a credit memo view, locate the Address Information section and distinguish Billing Address from Shipping Address. Click the Edit link associated with Shipping Address, then verify the destination shows an address-edit form with shipping details and a Save Order Address control. Once this form is displayed, report completion without making unnecessary changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate from a Magento Admin credit memo or order-related view to edit the shipping address, provided both billing and shipping address sections are visible.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Edit Form
skills.principle: When the requested navigation succeeds, verify the destination by its heading, URL, or visible form fields. Once the shipping-address edit form is displayed, report completion and terminate; do not save unchanged data, navigate back, or reuse element IDs from earlier pages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a task asks only to navigate to an admin edit page and the current observation already shows the corresponding edit form, such as “Order Address Information” with address fields and a save button.

skills.title: Expand Content Navigation Menu
skills.principle: Click the visible “CONTENT” navigation entry in the Magento Admin menubar. Confirm completion when the menu expands and its grouped options, such as “Elements,” “Media,” and “Design,” become visible; stop without selecting a deeper submenu unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to navigate to the Content section from another admin page, and the top navigation exposes a visible “CONTENT” entry.

skills.title: Navigate Menus Using Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree’s numeric bid for the top-level menu control, not its visible label or icon text. After the menu expands, select the specific submenu link matching the destination, then verify the page heading or URL changed. Treat a parent link with a “#” URL as a menu toggle rather than the final destination, and stop retrying unchanged actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin navigation label repeatedly fails as a text selector or its link points to “#”. Prerequisite: inspect the latest accessibility tree and identify the current numeric bid and visible submenu options.

skills.title: Open Magento All Stores
skills.principle:
1. From any Magento Admin page, open the top-level “STORES” navigation entry.
2. In its expanded menu, select “All Stores” under “Settings.”
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Stores” and the website, store, and store-view table is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requires reaching store hierarchy settings from another page, especially when the Stores menu is collapsed and the destination must be verified.

skills.title: Use Exact Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: In BrowserGym, invoke actions with the element’s current numeric accessibility bid, not its visible label, icon text, XPath, or stale identifier. For a navigation link, use the bid shown beside that link, then verify the URL or page heading changed to the requested section before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When an accessibility tree exposes navigation links with numeric bids and attempts using labels, icon strings, or XPath produce empty-action or element-not-found errors.

skills.title: Open the System Navigation Menu
skills.principle: From the current Magento Admin page, locate the top navigation entry labeled “SYSTEM” and click it. Confirm completion when the System entry is focused or expanded and its dropdown displays system categories such as Data Transfer, Extensions, Tools, Permissions, or Other Settings.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task asks to reach the System section from another Magento Admin page and the horizontal navigation bar is visible.

skills.title: Recognize Expanded Admin Menus
skills.principle: Activate the relevant top-level admin menu once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. If its submenu appears with a “System” heading and links such as Import or Cache Management, the System section is open; stop rather than repeatedly clicking the parent, which can collapse the menu.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin navigation item has a placeholder link or URL ending in “#” and activation reveals nested menu entries instead of changing the page URL.

skills.title: Read Last Orders Directly
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the Magento Admin Dashboard using the visible “DASHBOARD” navigation entry.
2. Locate the “Last Orders” section and read its table columns, including customer, item count, and total.
3. Report the visible order details; opening individual order links is unnecessary unless the task requests deeper information.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to check Last Orders details in Magento Admin and the Dashboard is not currently displayed. Confirm completion when the Last Orders table and its requested fields are visible.

skills.title: Recover From Duplicate Customer Email
skills.principle: When saving a new customer produces a duplicate-email error, replace the email with a unique address while preserving the other completed fields, then select “Save Customer” again. Confirm completion only after the customer list appears with a success message such as “You saved the customer.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use while creating customers in Magento Admin when the save attempt reports that the email already exists for an associated website.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Form Interaction
skills.principle: After navigating in Magento Admin, inspect the accessibility tree and confirm the expected customer-list or creation form is present. If the page shows “404 Error” or lacks the form, return to a valid observed navigation entry and retry using its current label or URL. Only interact with element identifiers present in the latest observation; never guess bids or field selectors.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a customer or opening any Magento Admin form, especially after direct navigation or a failed menu action. Verify the destination before filling fields or submitting data.

skills.title: Export Current Customer Data
skills.principle:
1. On the Customers grid, activate the visible “Export” control.
2. In the export options, keep the default “CSV” format unless another format is requested.
3. Click the confirmation “Export” button to initiate the download, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task requests exporting the currently displayed customer dataset and the Customers grid provides an “Export” control with format options.

skills.title: Verify Search Results Before Reporting
skills.principle: Enter the requested keyword in the page's search field and activate Search. Confirm the refreshed results state by checking the record count and empty-state message; if it shows zero records and indicates no records were found, report that outcome directly and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin list pages when searching for a customer or other record, after the keyword is entered and the page exposes a Search control and result-count or empty-state feedback.

skills.title: Search Magento Customers by Keyword
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers menu and select “All Customers.”
2. Enter the requested customer keyword in “Search by keyword,” then click “Search.”
3. Verify the result state: inspect matching customer rows, or report no matches when the grid shows “We couldn't find any records” and zero records found.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Magento Admin for customer details and the Customers list is accessible. Use the displayed result count and grid message to distinguish matching records from a confirmed empty search.

skills.title: Confirm Requested Customer Changes
skills.principle: Before editing a customer, identify the exact field and new value required by the task. If the instruction only says to edit details without specifying a change, do not invent a value or modify a field; request clarification. After saving a specified change, verify the success message and updated record, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento customer edit tasks when the target customer is identifiable but the requested field or replacement value is missing or ambiguous.

skills.title: Stop After Save Confirmation
skills.principle: After saving a customer, verify the success message (for example, “You saved the customer.”). Once confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately; do not reopen the record or make additional speculative edits.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento customer edit returns to the customer list with a visible save-success confirmation. This is the completion state, even if other editable fields or tabs remain available.

skills.title: Inspect Visible Customer Rows First
skills.principle: On a customer-list page, inspect the currently rendered table before using filters or search. Match the requested name against the Name column, verify identifying fields such as ID, email, group, or location, then report the matching record. If no visible match exists, use the keyword search or relevant filters.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to find a customer in an admin customer list and the table is already loaded with records. Verify the row before reporting, especially when names may have middle names or duplicates.

skills.title: Navigate to the Customer Grid
skills.principle:
1. Use the main “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry, not the dashboard’s “Customers” report tab or “Last Orders” widget.
2. Select the customer-list submenu, then verify the page heading and customer-grid controls appear.
3. Apply the name filter for the requested customer and confirm the resulting row before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find a customer in Magento Admin from the dashboard, especially when the name appears in a dashboard report but the full customer list is not open.

skills.title: Find a Customer’s Group
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s CUSTOMERS menu and select “All Customers.”
2. Search the customer’s name using “Search by keyword,” then apply the search.
3. Locate the matching record and read its “Group” column; confirm the result count and identity match.
4. Report the displayed group and stop once verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking which customer group a named customer belongs to, when the Customers area and its searchable customer grid are accessible.

skills.title: Read Customer Since Directly
skills.principle: When the Customers table is already filtered to the target customer, identify the matching row and read its “Customer Since” column. Report that exact date and time, then stop once the requested account-creation information is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer account-date tasks when the customer list or search results visibly contain the target customer and a “Customer Since” column.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed UI Actions
skills.principle: After an action returns an empty-action or serialization error, do not repeat the same payload or accessibility bid. Re-read the current accessibility tree, target the visible control by its role and label (such as the “Customers” link), issue a correctly formatted action, and verify that the URL or page content changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar dashboards, especially after a click produces an empty-action error or leaves the page unchanged. Reinspect the latest accessibility tree before retrying.

skills.title: Read Location Fields From Customer Results
skills.principle: Search the Customers grid for the requested person, verify the result matches the target, then read the values under the visible “Country” and “State/Province” columns. Report both values directly once the matching row is confirmed; opening the edit page is unnecessary when the grid already exposes these fields.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer lookups when the Customers grid is available and includes Country and State/Province columns. Confirm the search returns the intended customer before reporting location details.

skills.title: Use Partial Customer Matching
skills.principle: In Magento’s Customers grid, search using a distinctive partial name or inspect existing matching rows before concluding a customer is absent. Account for middle initials or name variations. Read the Country and State/Province columns directly; do not open “Add New Customer” merely because an exact full-name search returns no records.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating an existing customer whose displayed name may include a middle initial, suffix, or formatting variation, especially when the customer already appears in order or dashboard records.

skills.title: Open Magento Sales Navigation
skills.principle: Click the visible “SALES” navigation entry in the Magento Admin menu. Confirm completion when it is focused or expanded and the submenu displays sales options such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, or Credit Memos; then report completion without selecting a submenu item.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to open Magento Admin’s Sales section and the accessibility tree shows a top-level “SALES” navigation entry.

skills.title: Navigate to Customer Groups
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the top-level “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry, then select the revealed “Customer Groups” link. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading or browser title reads “Customer Groups” before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Magento’s Customer Groups page from another admin page, especially when the customer-related submenu is initially collapsed.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Viewing All Orders
skills.principle: On the Orders page, inspect the search state before declaring completion. If an active keyword or other filter is present, select “Clear all” (or remove each filter), then verify the order table refreshes and shows the unfiltered record count. Only report success when no unintended filters remain.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view all orders and the Orders page shows an active filter, a populated search box, or a suspiciously small record count. Requires the Orders list to be loaded and filter controls accessible.

skills.title: Expand Magento System Navigation
skills.principle: Click the admin navigation entry labeled “SYSTEM.” Confirm completion by checking that its expanded menu displays system subsections such as Data Transfer, Extensions, Tools, Permissions, or Other Settings. Once visible, report that the System section is ready and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks to reach the System section from another admin page, and the main navigation visibly contains a SYSTEM entry.

skills.title: Expand Marketing Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Inspect the admin navigation for the top-level “MARKETING” entry.
2. Activate that entry and verify the accessibility tree shows its expanded state and marketing subsections such as Promotions, Communications, SEO & Search, or User Content.
3. Once expanded, report completion and stop without opening an unrelated subsection.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks you to access the Marketing section and the navigation menu is visible. This applies when merely expanding the section satisfies the task, rather than entering a specific marketing subsection.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Inspect the current page heading, URL, and visible controls before navigating. If the requested destination is already displayed, confirm the relevant form or controls are present, report completion, and stop. Otherwise, use the visible navigation control whose label matches the requested destination, then verify the resulting page state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the browser may already be on the requested page or a nearby list page, especially in admin interfaces with destination-specific headings and action buttons.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Reports Menu
skills.principle:
1. From any Magento Admin page, select the top navigation entry labeled "REPORTS" to expand its categorized submenu.
2. Choose the report link matching the user’s requested report type, such as "Orders" under Sales.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading identifies the selected report and its filter controls are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a Magento Admin report and the Reports navigation entry is available. Use the report category and link labels shown in the expanded menu rather than relying on fixed element IDs.

skills.title: Navigate Magento System Integrations
skills.principle:
1. Open the main navigation's “SYSTEM” menu.
2. Under “Extensions,” select “Integrations.”
3. Confirm completion when the page heading is “Integrations” and integration controls such as “Add New Integration” and the integrations table are visible; then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires reaching System technical settings or integration management from another admin section, with the main navigation visible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Destination
skills.principle: Use the visible System menu to reveal its submenu, choose the requested technical-settings destination such as Integrations, then verify the resulting page heading or URL. Once the requested section is visibly open, report completion and terminate instead of exploring controls, adding records, or issuing no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks only to navigate to a system, settings, or integrations section and the destination page is confirmed by its heading, URL, or visible controls.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Orders Efficiently
skills.principle:
1. From any Magento Admin page, open the “SALES” navigation menu and select “Orders.”
2. Locate the target order using the order list or “Search by keyword,” then select its row’s “View” action.
3. Confirm the order detail page by checking the order number, status, customer, and available tabs such as Information, Invoices, Shipments, and Comments History.
4. Report the verified result and stop unless the user requests a specific management action.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage an order in Magento Admin, starting from another admin section and having a target order identifier or other distinguishing information.

skills.title: Navigate Orders Using Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: On Magento Admin, expand the visible “SALES” navigation entry, then click the revealed “Orders” link using its current accessibility bid. Confirm the destination by checking for the “Orders” heading and orders table. For a broad “view and manage Orders” request, stop at the orders list or selected order details unless a specific edit is requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting on the Magento dashboard for an order-management task, especially when navigation links share placeholder URLs. Use current accessibility-tree bids and verify the resulting page before taking further actions.

skills.title: Create and Verify Magento URL Rewrites
skills.principle:
1. Open Marketing, expand the SEO & Search section, and select URL Rewrites.
2. Click Add URL Rewrite, keep Create URL Rewrite as Custom, choose the applicable Store View, and fill Request Path and Target Path.
3. Select Permanent (301) when the SEO mapping is permanent, optionally document it, then click Save.
4. Confirm the listing shows “The URL Rewrite has been saved” and the new row has the intended paths and redirect type.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring a Magento Admin SEO rewrite and the target internal path, request path, and applicable store view are known; verify the saved row before reporting completion.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Select the target navigation control from the latest accessibility tree, using its current bid and role/name (for example, the visible CONTENT link). Do not infer bids from position, prior observations, icons, or unrelated controls. After clicking, verify the URL, heading, or expanded submenu changed before continuing; if unchanged, re-inspect the refreshed tree and choose the newly observed target.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin menus or any dynamic BrowserGym page where bids change after navigation, expansion, or rerendering, especially after an element lookup or click fails.

skills.title: Read Visible Product Details
skills.principle: When the requested product edit page is already open, inspect the accessibility tree and report the currently visible fields directly. Include key identity, pricing, inventory, tax, visibility, and manufacturing values; mention expandable sections only as additional context. Do not modify fields or save when the task is view-only.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to Magento Admin product-detail tasks when the target product page is already open and the requested current information is exposed in visible form controls or labels.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Product Details
skills.principle: Once the target product’s edit page is visible and its current fields are accessible, treat the viewing task as complete. Report completion or the requested details immediately, then terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a shopping-admin product search has produced the target item and its edit/details page visibly shows the current product fields.

skills.title: Verify Save Button and Confirmation
skills.principle: On an admin product-edit page, identify the button whose accessible name is exactly “Save” from the current accessibility tree, rather than relying on stale element IDs. Click it, then verify the page displays a success confirmation such as “You saved the product.” Report completion and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When saving edits in a Magento-style product form, especially after the page updates or a prior element reference may be stale. Ensure the current page exposes a Save button and check for an explicit success message afterward.

skills.title: Bypass Blocked Menus Directly
skills.principle: When a navigation overlay intercepts clicks, stop retrying the same menu control. Navigate directly to the relevant catalog list, filter by the target product name, open its row’s Edit link, then use the product page’s Save control. Verify a success notice or persisted product page state before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when the Catalog menu is visible but an overlay blocks pointer events, especially when the target product must be located by name before saving its details.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Subsections
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the requested subsection by its visible label, such as “Credit Memos.”
3. Confirm completion from the destination page heading and listing content, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests visiting a Sales subsection and the current page is elsewhere, use the visible navigation labels and verify the destination heading before terminating.

skills.title: Use Sales Submenu for Credit Memos
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the top-level “SALES” navigation entry, inspect its visible submenu, and select “Credit Memos” directly. Verify completion by checking that the page heading reads “Credit Memos” or the URL represents the credit-memo listing, then stop without repeating menu clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting from another Magento Admin page and asked to visit Credit Memos. The Sales submenu must be expanded so its child links, including “Credit Memos,” are visible.

skills.title: Verify Existing Tax Class Before Editing
skills.principle: On a product edit page, locate the Tax Class combobox and inspect its current selected value. If it already matches the required assignment, leave it unchanged and report completion; only choose another option when the observed value differs from the task requirement.
skills.when_to_apply: When assigning a tax class in Magento Admin and the product edit form is already open with a visible Tax Class combobox and selected value.

skills.title: Verify and Apply Tax Class
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, inspect the Tax Class combobox against the requested classification. If it differs, select the requested option; do not assume the existing value is correct. Click Save once, then stop after confirming the “You saved the product.” message.
skills.when_to_apply: When assigning a tax class to a product and the edit form already displays a tax-class value. The requested classification must be known before changing or preserving the selection.

skills.title: Verify Before Changing Product Visibility
skills.principle: Inspect the product editor’s Visibility combobox and compare its selected value with the requested option. If it already matches, do not alter or save unnecessarily; report completion. Otherwise, select the requested visibility option and verify the combobox reflects the new selection before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a product in Magento Admin and asked to set Visibility, especially when the current accessibility-tree selection may already satisfy the request.

skills.title: Use Valid Current UI Actions
skills.principle: Act only on elements present in the latest accessibility tree, using valid action syntax and the element’s semantic role. For Magento product visibility, open the product’s Visibility combobox, choose the requested option, click Save, and verify the field or success state reflects the change. Do not guess product identity, reuse stale element IDs, or continue after malformed-action errors without re-reading the page.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product from the catalog and the accessibility tree exposes the target product and its Visibility combobox. Re-observe the page after navigation or any action error before proceeding.

skills.title: Save and Verify Product Details
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, click the primary “Save” button, then inspect the refreshed page for the confirmation message “You saved the product.” Once that message appears, report completion and stop instead of taking further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when product information is already entered on a Magento Admin product edit form and the task is to save it. Confirm success through the visible save-success notification before finishing.

skills.title: Validate Required Product Fields Before Saving
skills.principle: On Magento’s New Product form, fill every required field—especially Product Name, SKU, and Price—before selecting Save. After saving, inspect the form for validation messages such as “This is a required field.” Correct all errors and save again. Confirm completion only when a success notification appears or the product list shows the new record.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a Magento product and the form remains open after Save, particularly when required fields are marked with an asterisk or validation messages appear.

skills.title: Read SKU From Product Edit Form
skills.principle: On a product edit page, identify the target product from the page heading or Product Name field, then read the value in the labeled “SKU” textbox, noting its scope if shown. Report that value directly once the product and field match; do not modify or save the form.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked for a product SKU and the admin product edit page is already open with the target product identifiable and a visible “SKU” field.

skills.title: Open Products Before Searching
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin "CATALOG" menu and click its "Products" entry; opening the menu alone does not navigate away from the dashboard.
2. Confirm the page heading or URL changes to the product grid before attempting search, filtering, scrolling, or opening an item.
3. In the product grid, locate the target product, open its details, and read the SKU field.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving a product attribute in Magento Admin and the Catalog menu expands while the dashboard remains visible. Click "Products" and verify the product-grid state before continuing.

skills.title: Read Current Inventory Status Directly
skills.principle: On a product edit page, locate the field labeled “Stock Status” and read its currently selected value; use “Quantity” as corroborating evidence when visible. Do not change the status merely to verify availability. If an element identifier fails, refresh the accessibility tree and target the newly observed semantic control or visible value.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking whether a catalog product is in stock in an admin inventory form, especially when accessibility-element identifiers are stale or interaction is unnecessary.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: When a navigation action fails, re-read the current accessibility tree and target the element’s current role, name, or observation-specific bid. Do not reuse malformed labels or assume scrolling will fix an identification error. After clicking, verify that the URL, menu, heading, or page content changed; otherwise choose an alternate observed navigation control.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when an admin-page navigation control is visible in the accessibility tree but clicks return empty-action or element-not-found errors, especially when the navigation is fixed and unaffected by scrolling.

skills.title: Open Product Reviews in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Open CATALOG, choose Products, and search by the target product name.
2. Open the matching product’s edit page and scroll to the Product Reviews accordion.
3. Expand Product Reviews and inspect the records count or empty-state message.
4. Report the displayed review result, treating “We couldn't find any records” as no reviews.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect reviews for a specific product in Magento Admin, with access to the CATALOG > Products list and the product’s edit page.

skills.title: Verify Section Labels Before Clicking
skills.principle: On product edit pages, distinguish the section’s visible label from neighboring controls and changing accessibility bids. Click the control whose accessible text is exactly “Product Reviews,” not the adjacent “Images And Videos” element. After clicking, verify that Product Reviews expands and its content appears before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating collapsible sections in Magento product editing pages and nearby sections have similar structure or accessibility-tree bids may shift after each expansion.

skills.title: Expand Product SEO Settings
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, locate the collapsed “Search Engine Optimization” section and activate its section header. Confirm completion when the section expands and SEO fields such as URL Key, Meta Title, Meta Keywords, and Meta Description become visible, then report success without making unrelated changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to access SEO settings for a specific product already open in Magento Admin, and the “Search Engine Optimization” header is visible but its fields are hidden.

skills.title: Stop After Opening Requested Settings
skills.principle: When the requested product settings section is expanded and its relevant fields are visible, treat the access task as complete. Verify the section heading and fields, then report completion and terminate; do not edit, save, or perform unnecessary review actions unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento product-navigation tasks asking only to access or view a settings section, once the target product is open and the named section is visibly expanded.

skills.title: Verify Before Editing Product Attributes
skills.principle: On the Magento product edit page, locate the requested attribute by its label and inspect its current selected value. If it already matches the requested value, make no changes; report that the setting is already correct and terminate. Otherwise, select the requested value, save the product, and verify the saved state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when updating a product attribute in Magento and the product edit page is available, especially when the requested value may already be set.

skills.title: Verify Product Edit Navigation
skills.principle: Use the product row’s actual “Edit” link, not the “Action” column header or another nearby element. After clicking, verify the page heading or URL changes to the product edit form before searching for attributes. If the products grid remains visible, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree and retry the correct row-level control.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product from the Products grid, especially when multiple nearby table elements have similar roles or accessibility references.

skills.title: Use Existing Attribute Options Exactly
skills.principle: When creating an attribute reports that its code already exists, stop creating it. Close every open attribute dialog, return to the product form, and expand the Attributes section. Inspect the existing attribute’s options; if the requested value is absent, add it through the attribute’s option-management interface rather than selecting a near match. Select the exact requested value, save the product, and verify the field displays that value.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and a requested attribute may already exist, especially after a duplicate-code error or when the attribute’s dropdown lacks the exact requested value.

skills.title: Check Existing Attributes First
skills.principle: In Magento product editing, use “Add Attribute” to inspect the existing-attribute list before creating anything. Search or paginate through all records for the requested label. If it exists, select it with “Add Selected,” then edit its value on the product. Only use “Create New Attribute” when no matching attribute exists, avoiding duplicate-code errors.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a named product attribute in Magento and the product edit page provides “Add Attribute”; verify the full paginated list before opening the creation form.

skills.title: Add and Save Related Products
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” on the product edit page.
2. Click “Add Related Products,” use “Filters” or the product table to locate the intended item, and select its checkbox.
3. Click “Add Selected Products,” then click the page-level “Save” button.
4. Verify the item appears under Related Products and the page confirms “You saved the product.”
skills.when_to_apply: When managing product associations in Magento Admin and the target product edit page is open. Use this for adding a related item, not an up-sell or cross-sell.

skills.title: Expand the Related Products Section
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree to identify the accordion heading "Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells". Click the heading or its expansion control instead of repeatedly scrolling. Once expanded, use the revealed related-products controls to search for and select the target product, then click Save and verify the selection remains visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the relevant relationship section appears as a collapsed accordion heading in the accessibility tree, especially when scrolling does not reveal its controls.

skills.title: Use Requested Promotion Parameters
skills.principle: In Magento product editing, open Advanced Pricing and enter the requested Special Price and any specified Special Price From/To dates. Do not invent discount amounts or dates when the instruction omits them; preserve unspecified fields. Click Done, then Save, and verify the saved product reflects the promotion.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring a product promotion in Magento and the task provides exact price or date-range requirements, or leaves some promotion fields unspecified.

skills.title: Complete and Save Special Pricing
skills.principle:
1. Open Advanced Pricing and verify the dialog is present before interacting further.
2. Enter or confirm the requested Special Price, Special Price From, and To values; do not assume existing values satisfy the task.
3. Click the dialog’s Done button and verify the dialog closes.
4. Click the product page’s Save button and verify a success confirmation or updated saved state.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring a Magento product promotion from the product edit page, especially after Advanced Pricing opens or existing pricing values are displayed. Ensure the product is saved after closing the dialog.

skills.title: Verify Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Inspect the current URL, page title, and main heading before taking navigation actions. If they already identify the requested destination, report completion and terminate. Otherwise, use the visible navigation entry matching the destination, then confirm the resulting URL or heading.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial page may already be the requested admin destination and the accessibility tree exposes URL, title, heading, or navigation labels.

skills.title: Terminate After Confirming Navigation
skills.principle: After navigating, verify the URL and page heading match the requested destination. Once the destination is confirmed, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the browser observation already shows the requested page, including its expected URL or heading. Stop after one confirmation, even if additional observations repeat the same state.

skills.title: Open Magento Sales Menu
skills.principle: Click the visible “SALES” entry in Magento’s main navigation. Confirm completion when its expanded vertical submenu appears with sales options such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, or Credit Memos; then stop without selecting a submenu item.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento admin task asks you to navigate to the Sales section and the main navigation visibly contains the “SALES” entry.

skills.title: Use Expanded Sales Submenu
skills.principle: Click the top-level “SALES” navigation entry once to expand its menu. Then select the relevant submenu link, such as “Orders,” instead of clicking the parent repeatedly. Confirm completion by checking that the submenu destination loads and the URL or page heading changes from the dashboard.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento’s top-level Sales entry points to a dashboard hash and expands a vertical submenu rather than navigating directly. Use this after the submenu links become visible.

skills.title: Expand Magento Customers Navigation
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, click the top-level “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry to expand its submenu, then select “All Customers” to open the customer management interface. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Customers” and the customer grid is visible, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting elsewhere in Magento Admin and the task is to reach customer management. The “CUSTOMERS” menu must be available; select “All Customers” rather than relying only on submenu expansion.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Section
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the relevant top navigation entry, select the requested subsection, and verify the destination heading or URL. Once the Customers page is visibly loaded, report completion and terminate; do not inspect unrelated controls or click actions such as “Add New Customer.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the requested admin section is confirmed by its page heading, URL, or distinctive controls. Stop immediately after that confirmation.

skills.title: Open Magento Content Navigation
skills.principle: Click the Magento admin navigation entry labeled “CONTENT.” Confirm completion when its dropdown opens and visibly lists content subsections such as Elements, Media, and Design. Stop once the menu is open; do not select a subsection unless the task requests one.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to navigate to Magento’s Content section from any admin page and the top navigation bar contains the CONTENT entry.

skills.title: Validate Action Syntax Before Retrying
skills.principle: When an interaction returns an empty-action or parsing error, inspect and correct the action payload before retrying. Use the current accessibility label or freshly observed target, ensure the click command is complete, and verify the page changes after execution. Do not repeatedly reuse malformed payloads or substitute another menu item's identifier.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin interface produces repeated empty-action errors and the page remains unchanged. Re-check the current accessibility tree and action syntax before attempting the target menu item again.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Retrying
skills.principle: After activating a navigation control, inspect the updated URL, page heading, and content before repeating the action. If the target page is not loaded but its destination URL is visible, navigate directly to that URL. Once the target heading and expected content appear, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating an admin interface through a header icon or menu link, especially when the control remains focused and the page appears unchanged after activation.

skills.title: Use “See All” for Notifications
skills.principle: When the notification badge opens a dropdown, treat it as a preview rather than navigation. Select the “See All” link to open the notifications page, then verify the URL or page content changed before proceeding. Avoid repeated no-op actions while the interface remains unchanged.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin notification badge expands an inline list and the current page URL remains unchanged; the dropdown contains a “See All” link.

skills.title: Resolve Duplicate Product URL Keys
skills.principle:
1. Save the product after completing required fields and inspect the resulting page for a duplicate URL Key error.
2. If reported, expand “Search Engine Optimization” and replace the URL Key with a unique slug, incorporating a stable product identifier when appropriate.
3. Save again and verify the page shows “You saved the product” before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a product in Magento Admin and saving triggers an error stating that the URL Key or generated URL already exists; required product fields should already be populated.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When an interaction reports that an element cannot be found, re-read the current accessibility tree and target the element’s actual bid, not its accessible name or label text. For example, identify the Product Name textbox by role and label, then use its current numeric bid before filling it. Do not repeat the same invalid selector or rely on scrolling to fix a selector mismatch.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Magento Admin forms or any BrowserGym page when a visible control is listed in the accessibility tree but actions using its label fail with “element not found.”

skills.title: Upload Product Images Through Expanded Section
skills.principle: On a Magento product form, expand “Images And Videos” to reveal “Choose Files,” then use the file-upload action with an existing local image path. Verify the control shows the selected filename or a thumbnail; clicking the chooser alone does not upload an image.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding an image to a new or existing Magento product and the “Images And Videos” section is collapsed. A valid accessible image file must exist before invoking file upload.

skills.title: Expand Image Section Before Uploading
skills.principle: On a Magento new-product form, first activate the collapsed “Images And Videos” accordion to reveal its upload controls. Then inspect the updated accessibility tree and use the actual file-input or upload-button reference; never invent a bid from an assumed element. Confirm that an image thumbnail or filename appears before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding product media and the accessibility tree shows “Images And Videos” only as a collapsed section without file controls. Expand it first, then re-read the page before uploading.

skills.title: Resolve Required Fields Before Saving
skills.principle: On a Magento product form, complete all required fields marked with an asterisk before saving. If Save keeps the form open, inspect validation messages, fill the missing field, then click Save again. Confirm completion by checking for the product edit page and the message “You saved the product.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating or editing a product and Save does not navigate away, especially when the form displays a required-field validation message.

skills.title: Target the Categories Control Precisely
skills.principle: On Magento's new-product form, distinguish the Categories control from nearby attribute fields such as Weight. Activate the control labeled "Categories" and "Select...", choose the requested category from the revealed category tree or list, and verify the category appears as selected before saving. Use the current accessibility tree to identify the control; do not reuse an unrelated selector or assume an option that is not exposed.
skills.when_to_apply: When assigning a category during Magento product creation, especially when Categories is rendered as a custom selector rather than a native combobox and nearby fields have similar accessibility identifiers.

skills.title: Set Magento Product New-Date Range
skills.principle:
1. On the Magento product form, locate the “Set Product as New From” and “To” textboxes.
2. Fill the start field with today’s date in the displayed format, then calculate and enter the corresponding one-month-later date in “To”.
3. Verify both fields show the intended dates and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento product form exposes paired “Set Product as New From” and “To” date fields and the requested interval is relative to today.

skills.title: Use the Correct Product Description Editor
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Content section and distinguish Short Description from the main Description field.
2. For the main Description, use its Page Builder workflow: add a Row, then add a text/content element inside that row.
3. Do not use the Short Description editor or unrelated controls as a substitute.
4. Close any Apply Template modal before interacting with fields, then verify entered content and save.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product’s detailed description and the Content section exposes both a TinyMCE Short Description editor and a Page Builder Description field. Ensure no modal is blocking pointer events.

skills.title: Target Newly Exposed Description Editor
skills.principle: After expanding Content, identify the main Description control by its visible label. If using Page Builder, add the required row, column, and Text element, then wait for the canvas to expose its editor. Target that newly exposed text area by role or label, enter the description, confirm the text appears, and click Save. Do not reuse a stale or inaccessible iframe reference from an earlier accessibility tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product description through the Content section, especially after switching to Page Builder or after the accessibility tree changes and previously observed editor references fail.

skills.title: Use Observed Bids for Date Fields
skills.principle: On Magento product edit pages, use the numeric accessibility bid shown beside each textbox, not the label text as a locator. Fill the observed “Set Product as New From” and “To” fields with the current date and calculated one-month-later date, then click “Save” and verify the saved values or success notice.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product’s new-item date range and the accessibility tree exposes date textboxes with numeric bids, especially after a label-based locator fails.

skills.title: Open Sales Orders Page
skills.principle:
1. Activate the admin navigation entry labeled “SALES” to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the “Orders” submenu item.
3. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking the page heading “Orders,” the sales-order route, and an orders table or record count; then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Magento Admin sales order management from another admin page, especially when SALES is a collapsed top-level navigation entry.

skills.title: Use Valid Semantic Navigation Actions
skills.principle: Target the visible navigation entry by its accessible label, using valid BrowserGym action syntax. After activating a menu such as “SALES,” inspect the resulting submenu and select the intended destination. Confirm the page heading or URL changes before proceeding; do not infer a destination from a placeholder “#” href or repeatedly submit malformed clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin navigation item is visible but its accessibility-tree href is “#,” especially after an action error or when the page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Add an Existing Product Attribute
skills.principle:
1. In the Magento Admin product form, click “Add Attribute.”
2. In the “Add Attribute” dialog, locate the row by its attribute label and select its checkbox.
3. Click “Add Selected,” expand the “Attributes” section, and verify the attribute field appears with its available values.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a product form needs an existing catalog attribute added. The “Add Attribute” control and target attribute must be available; confirm completion by checking the expanded Attributes section.

skills.title: Reuse Existing Product Attributes
skills.principle: In Magento’s product attribute picker, first search the attribute list for the requested label. If it already exists, select its row checkbox and click “Add Selected” rather than creating a duplicate. Use “Create New Attribute” only when no matching attribute exists, then complete required properties and save it.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding an attribute from a Magento product form and the “Add Attribute” dialog displays existing attribute rows, especially when the requested label may already be available.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Native Dropdowns
skills.principle: When a product attribute is a native combobox, open or focus the field and use the select-option operation with the target label rather than clicking an invisible <option> element. Verify the combobox value and selected option reflect the requested setting before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this in Magento Admin product forms when the accessibility tree exposes a native combobox whose options appear in the tree but direct option clicks fail visibility or timeout.

skills.title: Use Current Combobox Bid
skills.principle: When a semantic or generated bid fails, re-read the latest accessibility tree and use the current numeric bid for the labeled control. For a native select, apply `select_option` to the combobox itself—not to its option—and verify its displayed value changed before saving.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this on Magento product forms when a dropdown action reports that a generated bid cannot be found, especially after the control has been focused or expanded and the accessibility tree exposes a current numeric bid.

skills.title: Identify Required Magento Fields
skills.principle: On a Magento product-creation form, inspect each field label and treat only labels explicitly marked with an asterisk (*) as required. Report those fields separately from visible optional fields, rather than inferring requirement from field presence or default values.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which fields are required on a Magento new-product form and the accessibility tree exposes field labels, values, and asterisk markers.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Choose the numeric bid from the latest accessibility tree for the intended control, rather than copying rendered icon text or stale identifiers. After clicking, verify the page changed. If navigation returns a visible “404 Error” or “Page not found,” stop treating it as the target form, return to a known page, and resume using freshly observed controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento navigation actions repeatedly report missing elements, especially menu labels containing icon glyphs, or when a guessed product-creation URL displays a 404 page.

skills.title: Verify Catalog Menu Expansion
skills.principle: Click the top-level “CATALOG” navigation entry and inspect the updated accessibility tree. Treat the task as complete when the Catalog menu is expanded and role-specific options such as “Products” and “Categories” are visible; do not open a submenu unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Magento Admin’s CATALOG section and the top navigation contains a visible “CATALOG” entry. Confirm completion from the expanded menu rather than assuming navigation occurred.

skills.title: Stop After Catalog Activation
skills.principle: Click the top-level “CATALOG” navigation entry and verify that its submenu expands, showing options such as “Products” and “Categories.” Treat the expanded Catalog menu as completion for a navigation-only request; do not open a submenu unless the task explicitly requests a specific catalog page.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked only to navigate to Magento Admin’s CATALOG section and the top-level entry expands a visible Catalog submenu, even if the URL remains unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Files Before Uploading
skills.principle: Expand the product form’s “Images And Videos” section, locate “Choose Files,” and upload only a user-provided file path that exists locally. After selection, confirm the control no longer shows “No file chosen” and that images appear in the product gallery.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding product images in a Magento-style product creation form, after the image section is expanded and before invoking the file-upload action; a valid local image path is required.

skills.title: Use Current Bids and Verify State
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s current bid for the intended section, not a nearby or stale element. Submit a correctly formatted browser action, then inspect the updated tree to confirm the section expanded and its upload controls appeared. If the state is unchanged, re-identify the target element and try once with its current role or label rather than repeating the same bid.
skills.when_to_apply: When administering a product form with collapsible sections such as Magento’s “Images And Videos,” especially after an action error, unchanged page state, or shifting accessibility-tree bids.

skills.title: Complete Required Fields Before Saving
skills.principle: On a new Magento product form, fill all required core fields—Product Name, SKU, and Price—before saving SEO attributes. After clicking Save, verify required-field errors are absent and the SEO section no longer indicates unsaved changes; only then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing SEO attributes on a new Magento product, especially if the form still shows blank required core fields or Save may trigger validation errors.

skills.title: Place Page Builder Text Blocks Correctly
skills.principle: In Magento’s Description Page Builder, add a Row, then drag the Text element into the row’s canvas rather than merely clicking it. Wait for the text editor to appear, enter the full description and dimensions, then verify the content is visible before saving.
skills.when_to_apply: When a product Description uses Page Builder and the accessibility tree shows “Drag Row, Columns, Tabs, Block, Dynamic Block or HTML Code here” but no editable text field after selecting a Text element.

skills.title: Populate Magento Page Builder Content
skills.principle: After opening “Edit with Page Builder,” create a content-bearing element rather than only selecting a Row. Expand “Add Content,” choose an available text or HTML element, place it inside the row, and enter the detailed description. Verify the text appears in the builder, then save the product.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento product’s main “Description” uses Page Builder and the editor shows an empty canvas with “Drag Row... here.” A row alone is only a container and cannot hold the requested description.

skills.title: Expand SEO Before Editing Fields
skills.principle: In Magento’s product editor, treat “Search Engine Optimization” as an accordion header, not an input. Click the section header to expand it, then inspect the refreshed accessibility tree for editable fields such as Meta Title, Meta Description, and Meta Keywords before filling them. Save only after confirming those fields contain the intended values.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the accessibility tree shows “Search Engine Optimization” only as a strong/header element without visible textboxes or textareas.

skills.title: Verify Quantity Field Before Reporting
skills.principle: On a new-product form, locate the textbox labeled “Quantity,” enter the requested stock amount, then inspect the updated accessibility state. Report completion once the field visibly contains the requested value; do not perform unrelated actions unless saving is explicitly required.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to set inventory quantity on a new product and the product form visibly exposes a labeled Quantity textbox. Completion is indicated by that field showing the requested value.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Form Fields
skills.principle: When an accessibility tree shows a target field, interact using its numeric element bid, not the field’s accessible name or a guessed CSS/XPath selector. For this form, use the observed Quantity textbox bid, enter the requested value, then save and verify the resulting state.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when BrowserGym reports “Could not find element” despite the desired control appearing in the accessibility tree. Reinspect the latest tree and use the bracketed bid associated with the target control.

skills.title: Update Product Design Settings
skills.principle: Expand the product form’s “Design” section, set the requested Layout and Display Product Options In values, and leave Custom Layout Update unchanged unless instructed. Click “Save,” then verify the selected values and confirm no unsaved-changes indicator remains. If required-field validation appears, complete those fields and retry saving before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing product design settings in a Magento admin product form, especially when the Design section is collapsed or saving may trigger validation for other required product fields.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After expanding a form control, re-read the latest accessibility tree and interact using the control’s current element bid, not a stale or semantic identifier. If direct selection fails, click the visible combobox bid, then choose the requested option by its displayed label and verify the value changed.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing Magento product fields or any dynamic form where element identifiers may change or direct select actions report that a combobox cannot be found.

skills.title: Enable Product Gift Messages
skills.principle:
1. Expand the product’s “Gift Options” section.
2. If “Allow Gift Message” is disabled, uncheck “Use Config Settings” to enable product-level control.
3. Activate “Allow Gift Message,” preferably by clicking its visible label if the input is intercepted.
4. Click “Save” and verify no required-field errors remain and the setting persists as enabled.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and asked to enable gift options. The product form must have required fields completed before saving can persist the gift-message setting.

skills.title: Use Visible Section Controls Directly
skills.principle: When a target section label is already present in the accessibility tree, activate that section control instead of repeatedly scrolling. Expand “Gift Options,” inspect its fields, set the requested option, then click “Save” and verify the saved state or confirmation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento product create or edit pages when the accessibility tree already exposes the target accordion section, such as “Gift Options,” even if its contents are collapsed or off-screen.

skills.title: Populate Magento SEO Metadata
skills.principle:
1. Expand the “Search Engine Optimization” section on the product form.
2. Fill “Meta Title” with a concise, keyword-relevant product title.
3. Fill “Meta Description” with factual product benefits, following the displayed character guidance, ideally 150–160 characters and below the maximum.
4. Confirm both fields visibly contain the intended values before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing or creating a Magento product and the task requests SEO metadata, especially when the “Search Engine Optimization” section is collapsed and its fields are not yet visible.

skills.title: Clear Stale Catalog Filters First
skills.principle: Before searching Magento’s Products grid, inspect the “Active filters” area and remove any stale keyword or field filters with “Clear all.” Then enter the target product name or SKU in “Search by keyword,” click “Search,” and verify that matching records appear before opening the product edit page.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Products grid shows an unexpected active keyword filter, zero records, or a failed search; the target product must be identifiable by its name or SKU.

skills.title: Expand Relevant Product Relationship Section
skills.principle: On a Magento product form, locate and expand the collapsed “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” section. Read the revealed subsections and their labeled controls: “Add Related Products,” “Add Up-Sell Products,” and “Add Cross-Sell Products.” Use the accompanying descriptions to distinguish their purposes, then report the available configuration options without modifying the product.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect available related-product or upsell configuration options on a Magento product page, especially when the relevant accordion section is initially collapsed.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: When a menu action fails, inspect the latest accessibility tree and target the current element’s role and accessibility identifier (for example, the navigation link’s bid), rather than guessing from visible text or icon glyphs. Retry only after verifying the target exists; if it remains unavailable, use an observed alternative navigation element instead of repeating the same action.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply in BrowserGym admin pages when a navigation control is visible in the accessibility tree but text-based or icon-based clicks return empty-action or missing-element errors.

skills.title: Inspect Dropdown Options Semantically
skills.principle: In Magento’s product form, expand “Customizable Options,” click “Add Option,” then inspect the accessibility tree for the actual focused option-type control and its list items.
