Target the combobox or visible option text, not the associated label or nearby “Required” checkbox. Treat the revealed list as authoritative and report all displayed types.
skills.when_to_apply: When catalog tasks ask which customizable product options are available and the product form exposes a collapsed “Customizable Options” section with an “Add Option” control.

skills.title: Open Customizable Options Directly
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, locate and expand the accordion labeled “Customizable Options.” Inspect its contents for existing options or an option-creation control. Do not use “Add Attribute,” because that opens the product-attribute selector rather than customizable product options. Report the observed options or controls once the section is expanded.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking which customizable options are available for a product in Magento Admin, after opening the target product’s edit page and seeing the collapsed “Customizable Options” accordion.

skills.title: Use Page Builder Canvas Drops
skills.principle: In Magento Page Builder, palette clicks only expand or select components; they do not place content. Drag Row into the actual visible canvas drop zone, then drag Text and Media components into the created row. After each drop, verify the canvas shows the new structure before continuing or saving.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product Description with Page Builder, after required product fields are filled and the Content section is expanded. Use the visible canvas/drop target rather than a sidebar control or guessed element.

skills.title: Drag Page Builder Elements
skills.principle: In Magento Page Builder, drag layout and content elements from the sidebar onto the canvas rather than clicking them. Build the row/column structure, then drag a Text element and media element into target columns. Verify each element appears on the canvas before editing its content or inserting images.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a product Description with Page Builder and the canvas still displays “Drag ... here” after selecting a sidebar element; required product fields should already be completed.

skills.title: Use Valid Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Select the navigation element by its current accessibility-tree bid, such as the numeric bid for the link labeled “CUSTOMERS,” rather than copying icon text or malformed escaped strings. Issue a syntactically complete click action, then verify the URL or page heading changed before continuing. Treat placeholder “#” hrefs as non-destination indicators and rely on the rendered control’s role and observed state.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin interface from an accessibility tree and actions return empty-action or element-not-found errors, especially when labels include icon glyphs or links show placeholder URLs.

skills.title: Open New Cart Price Rule Form
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation entry labeled “MARKETING” and wait for its submenu.
2. Under “Promotions,” select “Cart Price Rules.”
3. On the “Cart Price Rules” page, select “Add New Rule.”
4. Confirm the resulting heading is “New Cart Price Rule” before reporting the form is ready.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access Magento Marketing to set up a promotion, especially from an unrelated admin page. The navigation menu must be visible, and completion is indicated by the “New Cart Price Rule” form.

skills.title: Complete And Save Promotion Setup
skills.principle: On Magento’s Cart Price Rules page, open “Add New Rule,” fill the required rule information, select at least one website and customer group, and configure coupon details only when needed. Expand and complete Conditions and Actions, then click “Save.” Verify the rule is persisted by the success message or its appearance in the rules list.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task requires creating a Magento promotion and the new-rule form is open. Apply before reporting completion; reaching the form or filling basic fields does not create the promotion.

skills.title: Inspect Product Design Options
skills.principle: On a Magento product form, expand the “Design” section and then “Schedule Design Update.” Read the revealed controls and option values, including layout, product-option placement, custom layout, date range, theme, and scheduled layout fields. Summarize only options visibly present after expansion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked what product display or design customization options are available and the Magento product form shows collapsed “Design” or “Schedule Design Update” sections.

skills.title: Inspect And Report Product Customization Options
skills.principle:
1. Expand the section matching the request, then inspect the newly rendered controls rather than waiting repeatedly.
2. Distinguish design settings from customer-selectable options: record labels, available choices, and current values.
3. Report the observed options once the relevant section is visibly populated; do not modify fields unless explicitly asked.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to discover available product design or customization settings in Magento Admin, especially after expanding Design or Customizable Options on a product form.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog Subsections
skills.principle:
1. Open the top navigation's “CATALOG” menu and wait for its submenu to appear.
2. Choose “Products” or “Categories” according to the requested management area.
3. Verify completion from the page heading, URL, and visible product grid or category tree before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when starting from another admin page and the task requires access to Catalog product or category management.

skills.title: Verify Attribute Save Completion
skills.principle: After configuring the product attribute, click “Save Attribute,” then inspect the resulting page for a success confirmation or return to the Product Attributes list showing the new attribute. Treat the task as incomplete until one of these observable states confirms persistence.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a Magento product attribute, especially after saving a form where the terminal page or success notification is not automatically available.

skills.title: Verify Attribute Creation After Saving
skills.principle: After configuring the new product attribute and clicking “Save Attribute,” wait for the page response. Confirm a success message, redirect to the Product Attributes list, or the new label appearing in the table before reporting completion. If validation errors remain, correct the highlighted fields and save again.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento product attribute through Stores > Attributes > Product, especially after adding dropdown options and submitting the form.

skills.title: Open Marketing Navigation Menu
skills.principle: Click the top-level “MARKETING” navigation entry once, then verify its submenu appears with categories such as Promotions, Communications, and SEO & Search. Treat the visible submenu as confirmation that the Marketing section is open; report completion without selecting a deeper tool unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when asked to reach the Marketing section generally, especially from another admin page, and the top navigation visibly includes a “MARKETING” entry.

skills.title: Explore Magento Reports by Category
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation’s REPORTS menu and inspect its categorized options.
2. Select representative report links under Sales, Products, and Customers, such as Orders, Bestsellers, and Order Total.
3. Confirm each destination by its page heading and report controls; use date filters, refresh/show-report controls, or export options when needed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate Magento Admin reports and view multiple store-statistics categories, with access to the admin navigation and REPORTS menu.

skills.title: Verify Reports Navigation Before Continuing
skills.principle: Open the admin “REPORTS” menu, select a report entry by its category (such as Sales, Products, or Customers), and verify the resulting page heading and URL. If the report page has required filters, complete them and click “Show Report.” Once the requested Reports section or report is visibly reached, stop instead of repeatedly hovering or opening unrelated top-level menus.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task asks you to access reports and the navigation uses expandable top-level menus. Confirm the destination page before taking further actions, especially when report pages require date filters.

skills.title: Expand Customizable Options Section
skills.principle: Locate the product form’s “Customizable Options” section by its visible label, activate its collapsible header, and verify expansion by checking that “Add Option” and “Import Options” controls appear. Once visible, report that the section is ready for configuration.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing customization choices in a Magento Admin product form and the “Customizable Options” section is collapsed or its option-management controls are not yet visible.

skills.title: Navigate to System User Management
skills.principle:
1. Select the top-level “SYSTEM” navigation entry to open its dropdown.
2. Under “Permissions,” choose “All Users.”
3. Confirm completion when the page shows the “Users” heading and user-management controls such as “Add New User” and the users table.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests the System section for user accounts or permissions, starting from another admin page with the main navigation visible.

skills.title: Stop After System Section Opens
skills.principle: For a navigation-only request, click the top-level “SYSTEM” entry and verify that its expanded menu or System heading is visible. Once the requested section is clearly reached, report completion and stop; do not open “All Users,” account settings, or other submenu items unless explicitly requested.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks only to navigate to a Magento Admin top-level section and the accessibility tree shows that section expanded with its menu options.

skills.title: Configure Product SEO Fields
skills.principle:
1. Expand the “Search Engine Optimization” section on the product form.
2. Fill the URL Key, Meta Title, Meta Keywords, and Meta Description fields with product-relevant content.
3. Keep the meta description within the displayed limit, preferably the recommended 150–160 characters.
4. Verify each field visibly contains the intended value before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring SEO for a Magento product and the Search Engine Optimization accordion is visible but collapsed, with its URL Key and metadata fields available after expansion.

skills.title: Validate Menu Targets Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to identify the navigation item by its visible label and role, then issue a syntactically complete click targeting that item. Verify the action payload is nonempty and the page or menu changes. If an element lookup fails, refresh the tree and reselect the correct target rather than repeatedly retrying a stale bid or clicking an unrelated menu item.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin menus or any dynamic sidebar, especially after an element lookup error, unchanged page state, malformed action, or confusing accessibility-tree identifiers.

skills.title: Save Magento Special Pricing Changes
skills.principle:
1. On the product edit page, open Advanced Pricing.
2. Enter the requested value in the Special Price field.
3. Select Done to close the pricing dialog, then select Save on the product form.
4. Confirm completion by checking for the “You saved the product.” message before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the task requires a special price. The product edit form must expose Advanced Pricing and a Save control; verify the save confirmation after submitting.

skills.title: Use Observed Labels, Not Guessed IDs
skills.principle:
1. Select controls by their current accessible label or role; do not invent element IDs or field names.
2. On Magento product editing pages, activate the visible “Advanced Pricing” button, whose state or newly exposed content confirms expansion.
3. Re-inspect the accessibility tree, locate the textbox labeled “Special Price,” enter the requested value, then click “Save.”
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento catalog product and the needed pricing field is hidden behind “Advanced Pricing,” especially after an element lookup fails or the accessibility tree shows no state change.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level “SALES” navigation entry from the current Magento Admin page.
2. Inspect the expanded submenu and select the link matching the requested destination, such as “Billing Agreements.”
3. Verify navigation by checking the page heading or URL and report any visible record state, such as an empty results table.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires reaching a Sales operations page from another admin section, especially when the destination is hidden inside the collapsed SALES submenu.

skills.title: Stop After Destination Confirmation
skills.principle: Use the admin navigation hierarchy: open the relevant top-level section, select the destination entry, then verify the resulting page heading matches the requested destination. Once the heading and page state confirm arrival, report completion and terminate instead of attempting unrelated searches or filters.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task requests opening a specific Magento Admin page and the destination heading is visible after selecting its menu entry.

skills.title: Use Catalog Menu to Reach Products
skills.principle: From a Magento product-edit page, open the top navigation's “CATALOG” menu, select the “Products” entry, then verify completion by checking that the page heading is “Products” and the product-management table is visible. Report completion once this state is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open Magento’s product catalog while starting elsewhere in the admin, especially on a product-edit page where the Products destination is nested under the CATALOG menu.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Products Page
skills.principle: Navigate through CATALOG to Products, then verify the page heading is “Products” and the product-list controls are visible. Once this state matches the navigation goal, report completion and terminate; do not add, edit, save, or otherwise manipulate catalog items unless explicitly requested. Use observed accessible labels rather than invented element IDs.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only requests opening Magento Admin’s Products page and the accessibility tree shows the “Products” heading with catalog controls or the product grid.

skills.title: Navigate Catalog Menus Reliably
skills.principle:
1. Open the relevant top-level menu, such as “CATALOG,” to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the destination by its visible meaning, such as “Categories,” rather than relying on fixed element IDs.
3. Confirm completion from the resulting URL, page title, and distinctive content like the category tree, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requires reaching a nested management page from another section and the navigation menu is visible in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Categories
skills.principle: Once the Catalog submenu exposes the “Categories” link, select it and verify the page heading or URL indicates the Categories page. When that state is confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not create, edit, or save categories unless the task explicitly requests those changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the task only asks to navigate to Magento’s Categories page and the Categories management view is visibly loaded after selecting Catalog > Categories.

skills.title: Verify Product Reviews In Magento
skills.principle:
1. On the target product’s edit page, locate and expand the “Product Reviews” accordion section.
2. Read the reviews grid and its record count; treat “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records.” as confirmation that no reviews exist.
3. Report the observed review status and stop once confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking reviews for a product in Magento Admin, with the product edit page already open and the “Product Reviews” accordion visible or reachable by scrolling.

skills.title: Open Product Reviews Directly
skills.principle: After opening the target product, inspect the current accessibility tree for the exact “Product Reviews” accordion heading. If it is already present, click that section to expand it and verify its review content; do not keep scrolling when the target control is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking reviews in Magento Admin after locating and opening a product, especially when the Product Reviews section appears in the accessibility tree but is collapsed or its contents are not yet shown.

skills.title: Edit Magento Rich Text Fields
skills.principle:
1. On a Magento product edit page, expand the collapsed “Content” section to reveal “Short Description.”
2. For the rich text editor, target the editable paragraph inside the “Rich Text Area” iframe, not the iframe element itself.
3. Fill the paragraph with a concise feature-focused description, click “Save,” and confirm the “You saved the product.” message.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product’s short description and the field is hidden under “Content” or implemented as a TinyMCE-style rich text iframe. Requires access to the product edit form and its Save control.

skills.title: Expand Content Before Editing Description
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, locate the collapsed “Content” section rather than repeatedly scrolling. Expand it, identify the “Short Description” editor, enter the requested feature-focused text, click “Save,” and verify the page reports a successful save or retains the updated value.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the product form shows a collapsed “Content” section but no visible description fields. Expand the relevant section before searching or entering text.

skills.title: Configure Magento Cross-Sell Products
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells,” then choose “Add Cross-Sell Products.”
2. In the selection dialog, open “Filters” if the product table is empty, search or inspect the catalog, and select the target product checkbox.
3. Click “Add Selected Products” and verify the product appears in the Cross-Sell Products table.
4. Click “Save” and confirm the “You saved the product” success message.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento catalog product and asked to configure cross-sells, especially when the add-product dialog initially shows no records and requires expanding filters before products can be selected.

skills.title: Use the Modal’s Product Filters
skills.principle: In the “Add Cross-Sell Products” dialog, do not fill a table row. Click “Filters” to reveal editable filter fields, identify the field by its accessible label, enter the target product name or SKU, and apply the filter. Select the matching product checkbox, click “Add Selected Products,” then click “Save” and verify the product appears under “Cross-Sell Products.”
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento’s product-association dialog initially shows a grid or “no records found” without a visible search textbox, especially after an attempted fill targets a table row instead of an editable control.

skills.title: Expand the Sales Navigation Menu
skills.principle: Click the top-level "SALES" navigation entry rather than assuming it opens a separate page. Confirm completion when the Sales menu expands and its sales-related options, such as Orders and Invoices, become visible. For a request to access the section, stop after this expanded-menu state is observed.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks to go to or access the Sales section and the accessibility tree shows a top-level "SALES" navigation link.】【。

skills.title: Use Sales Submenu Navigation
skills.principle: When a top-level admin navigation item points to a placeholder such as “#”, click it to expand the submenu, then select the relevant destination such as “Orders.” Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL belong to the Sales section; do not repeatedly click the already-expanded parent.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin page shows the “SALES” navigation link with a placeholder URL and its submenu is not yet visible. Select a visible Sales destination and verify the resulting page state.

skills.title: Open Magento Search Terms Report
skills.principle:
1. From Magento Admin, open the REPORTS navigation menu.
2. Under the Marketing section, select “Search Terms.”
3. Verify the “Search Terms Report” heading and read the table’s Search Query, Results, and Hits columns.
4. Summarize the displayed records, distinguishing search frequency (Hits) from returned products (Results).
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect search-term performance in Magento Admin and the Reports navigation is available. Confirm completion when the Search Terms Report table and its records are visible.

skills.title: Use Visible Dashboard Search Metrics
skills.principle: When the dashboard already contains a “Top Search Terms” section, inspect its visible table directly. Read the Search Term, Results, and Uses columns, and report those values. Do not navigate elsewhere unless the requested section is genuinely absent from the current page.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking for Top Search Terms or similar dashboard metrics when the accessibility tree visibly includes the named section and its table.

skills.title: Search Orders from the Sales Grid
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, use Sales > Orders rather than the dashboard’s limited “Last Orders” list. Locate the “Search by keyword” textbox by its accessible role, enter the target order number, and click “Search.” Verify the active Keyword filter and matching ID, then click that row’s “View” link. Confirm completion when the order-view page heading shows the requested order number.
skills.when_to_apply: When an order is absent from the dashboard’s recent-orders list and the Magento Admin Orders grid is available. Prefer semantic labels and roles over stale element IDs, and verify the filtered row before opening details.

skills.title: Export the Complete Orders List
skills.principle: Before exporting, inspect the orders grid for active filters. Clear any incidental search or filter so the displayed record count represents the requested list. Open Export, keep CSV selected, click the modal’s Export button, and verify a download or success indication before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting all orders from a Magento Admin orders grid, especially when the page shows an active keyword filter or unexpectedly low record count.

skills.title: Verify Store Selection State
skills.principle: After choosing a customer, select a store-view radio option and re-check the accessibility tree. Continue only when the chosen radio reports checked=true and the “Please select a store” message disappears. If it remains unchecked, activate the associated label or radio control again and verify before searching for order controls.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin’s new-order page displays customer-specific store-view radio options and still shows “Please select a store” after an attempted selection.

skills.title: Verify Order Search Results
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Sales, choose Orders, and inspect the existing keyword search before changing it. If the requested keyword is already present, confirm the active filter, record count, and matching order row. Report completion once the result is visible; do not perform unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to search Magento orders by keyword and the Orders page may already contain a populated search field or active filter.

skills.title: Use the Orders Grid for Searches
skills.principle: From Magento Admin, open Sales and then the Orders list rather than opening a single order from the dashboard’s Last Orders table. Enter the requested keyword in the appropriate order-grid filter or search field, apply filters, and verify the results contain the target order before opening its details. If no rows appear, report that the search returned no matching order.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find an order by number or keyword from the Magento dashboard, especially when the dashboard only exposes individual recent-order links and no comprehensive search control.

skills.title: Check Order Status Before Cancellation
skills.principle: On the Magento Admin Orders page, locate the target order and inspect its Status before acting. If it is cancellable, select its checkbox, open Actions, and choose Cancel. If the status is Closed, do not attempt cancellation; report that the system prevents it and explain the order lifecycle is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when canceling a selected Magento order, after locating it in Sales > Orders and before selecting the bulk Actions > Cancel operation.

skills.title: Hold an Order from Its Details
skills.principle:
1. Open the target order’s details page from the sales order list or another order reference.
2. Check the current status and available actions; if the status is already “On Hold,” report completion without changing it.
3. Otherwise, select the “Hold” button.
4. Confirm completion by checking for an “On Hold” status, an “Unhold” button, or a success message.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin order-hold tasks when the target order can be identified and its details page exposes the “Hold” action or already shows “On Hold”.

skills.title: Verify Order Status Before Unholding
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales > Orders and locate the target order using its identifier or search.
2. Inspect the order's visible Status before attempting any action.
3. Use the unhold action only when status is "On Hold"; otherwise report that unholding is unavailable because the current status does not satisfy the prerequisite.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to unhold an order in Magento Admin, after locating the target order and before selecting bulk or detail actions.

skills.title: Verify Order Status Before Editing
skills.principle: On the order details page, inspect the displayed status and all available actions before changing anything. Use the explicit hold/unhold action when present; do not substitute an unrelated status such as Complete. If the order is canceled or the dropdown offers only its current status, re-check the selected order and stop rather than repeatedly retrying unavailable options.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing a Magento order whose requested state change depends on its current status, especially when the details page shows a status different from the task description or the status control has no alternative options.

skills.title: Print Invoices from Filtered Orders
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales and select Orders.
2. Filter the order list using the target order identifier, then verify the matching row and select its checkbox.
3. Open Actions and choose Print Invoices.
4. After selecting the print action, report completion and terminate when the print dialog or generated PDF is expected.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when printing invoices for a known order and the Orders page supports keyword search, row selection, and an Actions menu containing Print Invoices.

skills.title: Recover Navigation and Print an Invoice
skills.principle:
1. If repeated menu clicks produce empty-action or missing-element errors, stop reusing stale bids and navigate directly to the admin invoice-list route.
2. Confirm the page heading is “Invoices” and identify the target row using its order or invoice information.
3. Select that row’s checkbox, open “Actions,” and choose the available print operation.
4. Verify the resulting print view or download before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin navigation controls fail or accessibility bids become stale, but the invoice-list route is known or inferable and the page contains the target invoice row and selection controls.

skills.title: Recover From Stale Navigation Targets
skills.principle: After a click fails because its bid cannot be found, re-inspect the latest accessibility tree and target the currently exposed element by its visible role and label. Do not repeat the same escaped or stale bid, and do not spend turns on repeated delays. If the navigation remains unavailable, use another visible route to the relevant order-management page, then verify the page heading before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin navigation control is visible in an observation but BrowserGym reports that its bid cannot be found, especially after the page remains unchanged following a short wait.

skills.title: Print All Available Order Documents
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales > Orders, locate the target order, and open its details.
2. Inspect document tabs such as Invoices, Credit Memos, and Shipments; treat empty results as unavailable documents.
3. For every available document, open its row’s details and click the page’s “Print” button.
4. After all available documents are printed, report completion and note any unavailable document types.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when asked to print all documents for a selected order and the order details page exposes separate tabs for invoices, credit memos, or shipments.

skills.title: Use Orders Bulk Print Action
skills.principle: On Magento Admin, select the target order using its row checkbox on Sales > Orders, open the bulk Actions menu, and choose the print-documents operation. Verify the resulting confirmation or print/download state. Do not infer that documents are absent merely because the order’s Invoices, Credit Memos, or Shipments tabs show no records.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to print all documents for a selected Magento order and the Orders grid exposes row checkboxes plus an Actions menu. The target order must first be located or filtered in the grid.

skills.title: Select Shipment Records Before PDF Export
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the target order’s Shipments tab and verify that shipment records exist. Select the relevant shipment row(s) before opening Actions and choosing “PDF Shipments.” If the tab shows zero records or the order is canceled, acknowledge that no label can be generated and stop instead of retrying the export.
skills.when_to_apply: When printing shipping labels from an order’s Shipments tab, especially when Actions offers “PDF Shipments”; selection is required and the order must have at least one shipment record.

skills.title: Filter Customers by Keyword
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Customers menu and select “All Customers.”
2. Enter the requested location or attribute in “Search by keyword,” then click “Search.”
3. Confirm the table shows the active keyword filter and a matching “records found” count; report completion only after results are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring all customers matching a location or other searchable attribute, when the Customers menu and All Customers grid are available.

skills.title: Sort Customer Registrations Newest First
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers section and choose “All Customers,” not “Now Online.”
2. Locate the “Customer Since” column and click its header until the newest-first sort indicator appears.
3. Read the first row’s registration timestamp and associated customer details; the first row is the most recent record.
skills.when_to_apply: When finding the latest customer registration in a Magento Admin customer list, provided the “Customer Since” column is available and sortable.

skills.title: Navigate From Online Customers View
skills.principle: When the current Customers page is a specialized subsection such as “Customers Now Online” and lacks the requested field, use the main “CUSTOMERS” navigation entry to open the customer grid. Locate the registration-date column and sort descending, then verify the first customer record is the most recent.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a Magento Admin customer task starts on an online-customer or similarly filtered view showing no records or no registration dates, but the main customer navigation is available.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Records
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin “SALES” navigation entry.
2. Select the requested record type, such as “Credit Memos,” from the revealed submenu.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading and visible records table, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task asks you to access a sales-related record list and the current page shows the collapsible SALES navigation entry.

skills.title: Stop When Credit Memos Opens
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the SALES navigation and select the visible “Credit Memos” entry. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Credit Memos” and its grid is displayed, then report completion and stop; do not open records, search, or perform extra navigation unless requested.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task only asks to access Credit Memos and the Magento Admin SALES menu is available. The Credit Memos heading and listing grid are sufficient completion evidence.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “SALES” navigation entry from the current page.
2. Select the submenu item matching the requested management area, such as “Billing Agreements.”
3. Verify the destination heading and table contents; if it shows zero records, report that no matching entities currently exist rather than attempting unnecessary changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests managing a Sales-related entity and the current page is elsewhere. The Sales menu must be expanded before its submenu options become accessible.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Labels
skills.principle: When navigating an admin menu, select controls by their exact current accessible name or role, not copied icon strings or guessed bids. After each click, verify the accessibility tree changed before continuing. If an action returns an empty-action or element-not-found error, correct the selector syntax and re-read the current page rather than repeatedly escalating malformed clicks.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an admin task begins on an unrelated page and menu navigation is required, especially when accessibility-tree labels contain icons, escaped characters, or links whose URLs do not reveal their submenu.

skills.title: Navigate Reports by Semantic Submenu
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation section matching the task, such as “REPORTS.”
2. Inspect the expanded submenu and choose the entry whose label and category match the requested report, such as Reviews → By Customers.
3. Confirm completion from the destination heading and visible report content before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task requests a specific report and the current page exposes hierarchical navigation. The relevant top-level menu must be available, and completion should be verified from the resulting page heading or report table.

skills.title: Stop After Report Access
skills.principle: Once the requested report page is reached, verify its heading or distinctive controls, report completion, and terminate. Do not open individual records, edit entries, save changes, navigate back, or scroll unless the task explicitly requests those additional operations.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks only to access or open an admin report and the page visibly shows the requested report title, report controls, or results table.

skills.title: Navigate Reports by Semantic Submenu
skills.principle: Open the admin navigation's "REPORTS" menu, then choose the review report organized "By Products" rather than "By Customers." Confirm completion by checking that the page heading says "Product Reviews Report" and that a product review-statistics table is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view a Magento admin product reviews report and the current page is elsewhere in the admin panel, with the main navigation and Reports submenu available.

skills.title: Expand Reports Menu Before Navigating
skills.principle: When a Magento Admin navigation link points to `#`, treat it as a menu trigger rather than a destination. Activate the visible REPORTS entry, inspect the expanded submenu, and choose the review report by its label (such as Product Reviews). Verify the resulting page heading or report grid before stopping; do not substitute Advanced Reporting or dashboard search.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requesting a specific report when the top navigation shows the relevant section but its link URL is `#` and no submenu items are initially exposed.

skills.title: Run Magento Shipping Reports Correctly
skills.principle:
1. Open Reports, expand the Sales section, and select Shipping.
2. Fill both required From and To date fields using the requested range before selecting Show Report.
3. Verify the refreshed report state, including the displayed date values and record count or empty-results message, then report the result.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin shipping-report tasks when the Shipping page requires a date range; the report cannot generate valid results until both required date fields are populated.

skills.title: Stop After Opening Shipping Reports
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open REPORTS, expand the Sales category, and select Shipping. Confirm the page heading is “Shipping Report” and the report controls are visible. If the task only asks to check shipping reports, report completion immediately; do not add arbitrary date filters or submit unnecessary queries.
skills.when_to_apply: When the requested task is simply to check or open Magento shipping reports and the Shipping Report page is visibly loaded. Use additional filters only when the task specifies a date range or other criteria.

skills.title: Navigate and Verify Low Stock Reports
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Reports navigation and locate the Products subsection.
2. Select the Low Stock report using its visible label.
3. Confirm the report page and read the record count or empty-table message.
4. Report the observed stock status, then stop once completion is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to monitor inventory in Magento Admin and the Reports navigation is available. Use the report’s displayed count and table state as the completion evidence.

skills.title: Use Reports for Low-Stock Monitoring
skills.principle: Open the admin REPORTS navigation and locate the inventory or product report labeled “Low Stock.” Use that report as the monitoring destination, then verify that its page displays low-stock items or report controls before finishing; do not substitute the dashboard’s Advanced Reporting link without confirming it contains the requested report.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to monitor low-stock inventory from the Magento Admin dashboard, especially when the visible dashboard offers an Advanced Reporting link but no low-stock report content.

skills.title: Resolve Duplicate Customer Email
skills.principle:
1. Fill the required customer fields and select “Save Customer.”
2. If the form reports that the email already exists, replace it with a unique valid email while preserving the other details.
3. Save again and confirm completion by observing the customer listing and a success message such as “You saved the customer.”
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer in the Magento Admin form, especially when the requested email may already belong to a customer in the associated website.

skills.title: Refresh Locators After Form Rerender
skills.principle: When saving reveals a validation error and the form rerenders, re-read the current accessibility tree before editing. Locate the live textbox by its label or role, then fill the replacement value directly and click the current “Save Customer” control. Do not reuse stale element IDs from the previous page state; confirm success through the resulting confirmation or navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on dynamic admin forms after submission errors, validation messages, or page updates change accessibility-tree element identifiers. Requires the form to remain available and the current observation to expose the relevant labeled fields and save control.

skills.title: Verify Website Options Before Associating
skills.principle: Open the “Associate to Website” dropdown and inspect all exposed options, using keyboard navigation only if necessary. If the current website is the sole available option, do not claim an association change; report that the requested operation requires another configured website first.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento customer and asked to associate them with a different website, especially when the dropdown shows one selected option and no alternatives in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Edit Customer Website Association
skills.principle:
1. Select the intended customer and open the row’s “Edit” action, rather than guessing an unavailable mass-action option.
2. On the customer edit form, locate the field labeled “Associate to Website” and choose the requested website.
3. Save, then verify the customer’s website association or success confirmation before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento’s customer-grid Actions menu does not visibly contain “Associate to Website,” especially after selecting a customer. Use the customer edit form and save the actual labeled website field.

skills.title: Use Side Link and Verify Focus
skills.principle: When the target section is represented by a side-navigation link, click that link rather than interacting with similarly named content in the main pane. Confirm completion by checking that the link is focused or the target section and its fields are visible, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin pages with section-based side navigation, especially when the target heading already appears in the main content and could be confused with the navigational link.

skills.title: Verify Target State Before Repeating Actions
skills.principle: Check whether the requested section is already displayed by its heading or visible content. If it is, report completion and stop. Otherwise, activate the relevant navigation link once, then verify that the page state or URL changed before taking another action.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating within an admin form or page with anchor-style side links, especially when the target heading and fields may already be visible and repeated clicks produce no observable change.

skills.title: Create Customers Through Required Fields
skills.principle:
1. On the Magento Admin “New Customer” form, identify required fields marked with an asterisk.
2. Fill the customer’s first name, last name, and email using the requested values; leave optional fields unchanged unless required.
3. Click “Save Customer.”
4. Confirm completion when the Customers page displays “You saved the customer.”
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer in Magento Admin and the “New Customer” form is available with the requested name and email details.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Form Fields
skills.principle: When semantic labels fail, use the exact numeric bid shown for the target control in the latest accessibility tree. Fill required fields by their observed bids, then click the form’s save action and verify the resulting success message or page state. Do not repeatedly retry an unresolved label or guess another field.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on BrowserGym forms when a visible label or role-based locator raises “Could not find element,” especially when the accessibility tree exposes numeric bids for the intended textbox and save button.

skills.title: Use Unique Email Before Saving
skills.principle: When creating a customer, provide an email address unique to the selected website. If saving displays a duplicate-email error, replace the email with a genuinely unique address, click “Save Customer” again, and verify a success message or return to the customer list before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Magento Admin customer-creation forms whenever the initial save reports that the email already exists, or whenever email uniqueness has not been established.

skills.title: Verify Unique Email Before Saving
skills.principle: When creating a customer, use an email address known to be unique for the selected website. After clicking “Save Customer,” inspect the resulting page: if a duplicate-email warning remains, generate a genuinely unused address, replace the Email field, and retry. Report completion only after a success confirmation or clear post-save state appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when adding customers in Magento Admin or similar systems where email uniqueness is enforced per website, especially after a save attempt shows a duplicate-email validation warning.

skills.title: Create and Verify Customer Group Assignment
skills.principle:
1. On Magento’s New Customer form, select the requested customer group from the Group dropdown.
2. Fill every required field marked with an asterisk, including first name, last name, and a valid email address.
3. Click “Save Customer” only after verifying the group and required values.
4. Confirm completion by checking for the “You saved the customer.” success message before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a Magento Admin customer and assigning a specific group. The New Customer form must expose the Group selector, required account fields, and the “Save Customer” control.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After an interaction fails with “Could not find element,” re-read the latest accessibility tree and target the element’s current numeric bid, not its visible label or generated name. For a dropdown, use the current combobox bid, select the requested option by its visible text, and verify the combobox value changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on BrowserGym forms when labels or generated accessibility names do not resolve to elements, especially after the page reports a missing bid or repeated interaction failure.

skills.title: Register Customers with Unique Emails
skills.principle:
1. Complete the Magento customer form’s required fields and enter the requested Tax/VAT Number.
2. Select “Save Customer”; if the page reports that the email already exists, replace it with a unique valid email and submit again.
3. Confirm completion by checking for the “You saved the customer.” message before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento Admin customer with business tax information, especially when email uniqueness is enforced and the save result must be verified.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Customer Save
skills.principle: After submitting the customer form, verify the resulting page shows a success message such as “You saved the customer” and returns to the customer list. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not click “Add New Customer” or modify another form.
skills.when_to_apply: When registering a customer in Magento Admin and the save action produces a visible success confirmation or customer-list redirect. This confirmation is sufficient evidence that the requested record was created.

skills.title: Filter Customers by Registration Date
skills.principle:
1. Open the customer listing rather than the new-customer form.
2. Use Filters and populate the Customer Since “from” and “to” fields with the requested date range.
3. Select Apply Filters, then verify the active filter and records-found count.
4. Report matching customers, or report no results only when the page shows zero records and an empty-results message.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer searches requiring a registration-date range, after reaching the Customers listing page and confirming the date fields and Apply Filters control are available.

skills.title: Clear Restrictive Filters Before Searching
skills.principle:
1. On the customer grid, enter the target location or keyword in “Search by keyword” and click “Search.”
2. If results show zero records while an unrelated active filter remains, remove that filter using its adjacent remove control.
3. Confirm the updated record count and visible matching rows before reporting results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when searching Magento customer records and the grid contains pre-existing filters, especially when a keyword search unexpectedly returns no records.

skills.title: Open the Customer Grid Before Filtering
skills.principle: From the Magento dashboard, use the top navigation’s “CUSTOMERS” entry to open the customer management grid, not the dashboard’s “Customers” report tab. Verify the page heading and grid show customer columns plus filter controls, then apply the State/address filter and search. If a click leaves the URL and page unchanged, stop repeating it and choose the navigation control instead.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find customers by state or address from a Magento Admin dashboard, especially when a dashboard report tab labeled “Customers” is visible but lacks customer-grid filters.

skills.title: Verify Filters Before Reporting Results
skills.principle: On an admin listing page, inspect the visible “Active filters” summary before changing anything. Confirm each filter matches the requested attributes, then read the result count and empty-state message. If the filters match and the page reports zero records, report that no matching records were found; otherwise, adjust filters before concluding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a customer or record listing already displays active filters and a task asks for filtered results. The filter summary and result count must be visible.

skills.title: Expose Attributes Before Filtering
skills.principle: In the Magento customer grid, first clear stale active filters. Open Columns and enable the relevant attributes, such as Gender and Date of Birth; then reopen Filters and use the newly exposed, accessibility-labeled fields. Set Gender to Female and use the Date of Birth range spanning the target month, apply filters, and verify the result count and rows reflect both criteria.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento customer-list task requires filtering by attributes absent from the current grid or filter panel, especially Gender or Date of Birth, and the accessibility tree shows those columns unchecked.

skills.title: Clear Existing Filters Before Searching
skills.principle:
1. Open the customer listing rather than relying on a creation form.
2. Inspect active filters and clear unrelated constraints before searching globally.
3. Open Filters, enter a wildcard in the Tax VAT Number field, and select Apply Filters.
4. Confirm completion from the active filter and resulting record count; report zero records only when the results explicitly show none.
skills.when_to_apply: When searching Magento Admin customer records for any populated Tax/VAT field, especially when the listing already shows an active geographic or other restrictive filter.

skills.title: Expose VAT Data Through Grid Columns
skills.principle: On Magento’s Customers grid, do not repeatedly search the Filters panel when Tax/VAT Number is absent. Use Columns to enable the Tax/VAT Number column, then inspect the resulting rows across every page (or export the grid) and retain customers whose value is non-empty. Verify the full record count and pagination before reporting all matches.
skills.when_to_apply: When the Customers grid has a Columns control but its Filters panel exposes only fields such as date, name, email, and phone, and the task requires finding records by another customer attribute.

skills.title: Use Field-Specific Customer Filters
skills.principle: On Magento’s customer list, open “Filters” rather than relying on the global keyword search for structured criteria. Set the Phone filter to match the requested area-code prefix and Country to the requested country, then apply the filters. Confirm the resulting record count and inspect the Phone and Country columns before reporting matches or none.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating customers by multiple structured attributes such as country and phone prefix, especially after a global keyword search returns zero records despite visible matching table rows.

skills.title: Use Structured Customer Filters
skills.principle: On Magento’s Customers list, use the Filters control to constrain the relevant phone field and country/address field separately. Apply the filters, verify the active-filter summary and result count, then inspect every remaining row or customer details when country is not shown in the grid. Traverse all result pages before reporting matches.
skills.when_to_apply: When identifying customers by both phone pattern and country, especially when the grid lacks country and keyword search returns unrelated phone values or an unexpectedly large result set.

skills.title: Bulk Unsubscribe Filtered Customers
skills.principle:
1. Open the customer list and apply the requested attribute filter; verify the active filter and record count.
2. Select all filtered records through the header checkbox or its Options menu’s “Select All” command.
3. Open “Actions,” choose “Unsubscribe from Newsletter,” and confirm “OK” in the dialog.
4. Stop only after the page reports that the expected number of records was updated.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer-list tasks requiring a newsletter change across a filtered population, especially when the header checkbox is obstructed and “Options” provides “Select All.”

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Filtering
skills.principle: After expanding the Customers navigation, select the visible "All Customers" entry rather than the parent menu link. Confirm the page heading or URL changes to the customer grid before searching. If the view remains the dashboard, take a concrete navigation action instead of repeatedly waiting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin menu expands but the parent control does not navigate, especially before applying customer filters or bulk newsletter actions.

skills.title: Confirm Bulk Customer Group Assignment
skills.principle: On the Magento Customers grid, select exactly the requested records and verify the selected count. Open Actions, choose Assign a Customer Group, select the requested group, then click OK in the confirmation dialog showing the matching record count. Verify the resulting success message or updated Group column before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin bulk customer-group tasks when the Customers grid is available, the target records can be selected, and the Actions menu includes Assign a Customer Group.

skills.title: Verify Bulk Group Assignment
skills.principle: After selecting the target records and choosing the destination group, confirm the assignment dialog with “OK.” Wait for the page update, then verify a success notification and that the selected records’ Group values now show the destination group before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer-list bulk group changes whenever a confirmation dialog appears after choosing “Actions” → “Assign a Customer Group” → the destination group.

skills.title: Customize Admin Table Columns
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the relevant listing page, not a create or edit form.
2. Open the listing's “Columns” control and inspect which column checkboxes are currently selected.
3. Leave only the requested columns checked; uncheck every other optional column.
4. Close the selector, then verify the table headers show exactly the requested columns, allowing unavoidable system columns such as selection options.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin listing pages with a “Columns” selector when a task requests a specific visible-column set. Ensure the listing page is open and verify the resulting table after closing the selector.

skills.title: Hide a Customer List Column
skills.principle:
1. Navigate to the customer list, using Back if starting on a customer form.
2. Open the Columns control and locate the checkbox matching the target column label.
3. Uncheck the target column; verify its visible count decreases and the table header disappears.
4. Close the column menu if needed, then report completion only after confirming the column is absent.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when customizing visible columns in a Magento Admin customer list, especially when the current page is a customer form and the target column is available in the Columns menu.

skills.title: Reset Admin Grid Columns
skills.principle: On the relevant Magento admin listing, open Columns rather than the view selector. Click Reset in the column configuration, then close the panel with Cancel. Confirm the grid returns to its standard column set and the configuration panel is no longer open.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin table’s column layout must be restored and the page exposes both a view selector and a Columns configuration control.

skills.title: Use the Customer Grid View Controls
skills.principle: Navigate to the Customers listing and confirm the customer table is visible before changing settings. Use the grid’s column configuration or view control to restore defaults; do not use a similarly labeled form Reset button. Verify the table columns visibly return to the default arrangement before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When restoring default columns in a Magento Admin customer table, especially if the current page is a New Customer form rather than the customer listing grid.

skills.title: Use Stable Navigation Targets
skills.principle: When an accessibility tree shows a named link, distinguish its visible label from its actionable bid. Activate the element using the current numeric bid or navigate through its observed href; do not pass icon text or escaped label text as the bid. After acting, verify the URL or page heading changed to the requested destination before retrying.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin navigation link is visible but clicking its copied label produces an empty-action or “element not found” error. Verify the current tree before choosing a stable target.

skills.title: Verify Expanded Navigation Menus
skills.principle: After activating a top-level Magento Admin navigation entry, inspect the updated accessibility tree. Treat the section as reached when its heading and submenu items appear; do not repeatedly click, scroll, or wait. If a specific destination is requested, select the relevant visible submenu item next.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin from the dashboard and a top-level section uses an expandable menu, especially after the page remains on the dashboard URL.

skills.title: Use Expanded Menu Destinations
skills.principle: When a Magento Admin navigation label only expands an inline menu, treat the expansion as intermediate rather than completion. Inspect the revealed Marketing categories, select the specific relevant child link, and verify the URL or page heading changes. If the task only requires opening the section, confirm the expanded menu visibly contains its Marketing options before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when clicking a top-level Magento Admin section leaves the current page unchanged but reveals submenu headings and links, indicating the parent is an expandable navigation control rather than a destination page.

skills.title: Use Expanded Navigation Menus Correctly
skills.principle: Click the Magento Admin navigation category once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. When its submenu expands, select the relevant child entry or confirm the expanded category is the requested destination. Do not repeatedly click the parent: repeated clicks can collapse the menu and leave the URL unchanged. Verify completion through the destination heading, submenu state, or changed URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin sections such as Content from another page, especially when the category link keeps the same URL and reveals child entries only after expansion.

skills.title: Expand Reports Navigation Menu
skills.principle: Click the admin navigation entry labeled “Reports.” Confirm completion when the Reports entry is highlighted or expanded and its report categories, such as Sales, Customers, Products, or Statistics, are visible. Then stop and report completion without opening an individual report.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to navigate to the Reports section of a Magento Admin panel and the main navigation menu is visible. The goal is the expanded section, not a specific report page.

skills.title: Select a Reports Submenu Entry
skills.principle:
1. Click the top-level “REPORTS” navigation entry to expand its menu.
2. Choose the relevant report link inside the expanded submenu, such as a Sales, Products, Customers, or Marketing report.
3. Verify navigation succeeded by checking that the URL or page heading changes from the dashboard; do not repeatedly click the parent menu or wait indefinitely.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin’s “REPORTS” control uses a hash URL and only expands an overlay menu. The task requires entering the Reports area, so a visible submenu entry must be selected and the resulting page state verified.

skills.title: Verify Notification Page Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting the admin notification indicator, inspect the updated page state rather than assuming navigation succeeded. If the notification dropdown remains open or the URL and page heading are unchanged, select its “See All” link to open the full Notifications page. Confirm the destination through the page heading, URL, or notification list before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin notification icon opens an in-page dropdown instead of directly navigating, especially when the accessibility tree still shows the original page and offers a “See All” link.

skills.title: Verify Notification Page Navigation
skills.principle:
1. Select the notification indicator only to open its menu, then inspect the resulting accessibility tree and URL.
2. If the page remains unchanged and a “See All” link appears, activate that link to open the full Notifications page.
3. Confirm completion by checking the URL or page heading indicates the notifications index before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating to Magento Admin notifications from a bell or unread-count control, especially when clicking it opens a dropdown instead of changing pages.

skills.title: Use Footer Link for Account Activity
skills.principle: On a Magento Admin page, locate the footer link labeled “Account Activity” and activate it. Confirm navigation succeeded by checking that the page heading is “Account Activity” and that concurrent session or security-event information is displayed, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to open Magento Admin’s Account Activity page from another admin page, especially when the footer contains a directly labeled “Account Activity” link.

skills.title: Read Product Identity Fields
skills.principle: From a Magento product list, open the target product’s details or edit page. Read the values displayed in the “Product Name” and “SKU” fields without modifying them. Report both values, then stop once the fields are visibly populated and correspond to the target product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to extract a Magento product’s name and SKU and the product is accessible through a catalog list or product edit page.

skills.title: Select Products From Catalog Menu
skills.principle: After opening Magento’s CATALOG menu, click the visible “Products” entry rather than assuming the catalog click navigated. Verify the page heading or URL changes to the product grid, then inspect product rows or open the target product to read its Name and SKU. If the observation remains the dashboard, take the missing navigation action instead of repeatedly waiting or scrolling.
skills.when_to_apply: When extracting product fields in Magento Admin and CATALOG expands a submenu while the page remains the dashboard. Requires a visible “Products” navigation entry or equivalent product-grid control.

skills.title: Read Product Fields Directly
skills.principle: On a product edit page, identify the target product from the heading, then read the values associated with the labeled “Price” and “Stock Status” fields. Report both values, including currency and the exact selected stock option. Do not modify fields or navigate elsewhere once both are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin product-information tasks when the target product edit page is already open and the labeled Price textbox and Stock Status combobox are present.

skills.title: Read Product Status Without Editing
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, extract the displayed Price, Quantity, and Stock Status values directly. For stock status, target the visible combobox labeled “Stock Status,” not an individual hidden option. Do not fill fields or select options when the task only requests information; report the current displayed value and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to retrieve product price or inventory status from Magento Admin and the product edit page visibly shows labeled fields such as Price, Quantity, and Stock Status.

skills.title: Complete and Save Product Associations
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” and process each category separately.
2. In each “Add … Products” dialog, use meaningful filters and select suitable products; click “Add Selected Products.”
3. Confirm each category’s table contains the intended items, then click “Save.”
4. Verify the saved page still shows all three association lists before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring Magento product recommendations and the page contains separate Related Products, Up-Sell Products, and Cross-Sell Products controls. Ensure every requested category is populated and saved, not merely opened or partially configured.

skills.title: Target Product Row Checkboxes Precisely
skills.principle: In Magento product-link dialogs, distinguish the header selection control from each product row’s checkbox. Re-read the current accessibility tree after opening or filtering, locate the target product by its visible name and row, then click that row’s checkbox. Confirm the selected count increases before clicking “Add Selected Products.”
skills.when_to_apply: When adding related, up-sell, or cross-sell products in a Magento product-edit dialog, especially after filtering or rerendering changes element identifiers and the header “Options” control may intercept clicks.

skills.title: Expand Magento Sales Navigation
skills.principle: In the Magento Admin top navigation, locate and activate the top-level “SALES” entry. Confirm completion when its expanded submenu visibly lists sales options such as Orders, Invoices, Shipments, or Transactions; then report completion and stop without selecting a submenu item.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task asks only to navigate to or expose Magento’s SALES section and the top navigation is visible. Do not open a specific sales submenu unless the task explicitly requests it.

skills.title: Save Already-Set Product Attributes
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, inspect the target attribute before changing it. If its displayed value already matches the requested value, click the page-level “Save” button anyway to persist or confirm the state. Verify the “You saved the product.” confirmation and the attribute’s displayed value, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when modifying a product attribute in Magento and the target product page already shows the requested value, especially when persistence must be confirmed through the page-level Save action.

skills.title: Persist Already-Correct Product Values
skills.principle:
1. Locate the target product attribute and compare its current value with the requested value.
2. If it already matches, click the page’s “Save” control to persist or confirm the state rather than repeatedly using no-op actions.
3. Verify the resulting success or saved-state indication, then terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin product-edit pages when the requested attribute already displays the desired value and a Save control is available.

skills.title: Filter and Open Credit Memo Details
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin Sales menu and choose Credit Memos.
2. Enter the requested memo identifier in “Search by keyword” and select “Search.”
3. Confirm the results show the target memo, then use its row’s “View” link.
4. Treat the “View Memo” page as complete when order, customer, refunded items, history, and totals are displayed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for retrieving a specific credit memo in Magento Admin when the Sales navigation and Credit Memos list are available.

skills.title: Retrieve a Magento Credit Memo
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin SALES menu and select Credit Memos.
2. Enter the target memo number in Search by keyword and activate Search.
3. Confirm the results contain the matching memo, then select its associated View link.
4. Treat the View Memo page, with order, customer, refunded items, history, and totals visible, as completion; report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving a specific credit memo in Magento Admin, starting from the dashboard and requiring its detailed record rather than changing any data.

skills.title: Confirm Price Before Editing
skills.principle:
1. Open the target product’s edit page and click the visible “Advanced Pricing” control.
2. Locate the “Special Price” field; do not substitute the regular “Price” field.
3. If the requested replacement value is unspecified, ask for clarification instead of inventing a price.
4. Enter the confirmed value, click “Save,” and verify the saved state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento product-price tasks when the product is identified but the requested special-price value is missing or ambiguous, especially when both Price and Advanced Pricing controls are visible.

skills.title: Read the Product Price Field
skills.principle: When the relevant product edit page is already open, identify the product heading, then read the value in the field labeled "Price" and its adjacent currency. Report that displayed value directly without editing or saving the product.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin product-price lookups when the target product edit page is open and the accessibility tree exposes the product heading and a labeled Price field.

skills.title: Report Visible Values Directly
skills.principle: When the requested product attribute is already visible, read its labeled field and provide the value in the final response. Do not emit a browser `noop` as the completion mechanism; it can be treated as an empty action and cause repeated failures. After reporting the value and unit or currency, terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on an admin product-edit page when the target product is identified and the requested attribute, such as Price, is already displayed in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Search Products Directly for SKU
skills.principle:
1. Open Catalog > Products rather than repeatedly scrolling the dashboard.
2. Enter the target product name in the “Search by keyword” field and activate “Search.”
3. Verify the filtered row matches the product, then read its SKU column or open its edit page.
4. Report the SKU once the matching result is visibly confirmed and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when locating a product attribute such as SKU. The Products grid must be accessible, with its keyword search and result columns visible.

skills.title: Inspect Magento Product Up-Sells
skills.principle:
1. Open the product’s “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” accordion.
2. Locate the “Up-Sell Products” subsection and inspect its listing area.
3. Report the displayed products; if the area is empty and only “Add Up-Sell Products” is available, report that no up-sells are configured.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a Magento Admin product edit page and asked to inspect existing up-sell products. Ensure the product relationship accordion is expanded before judging whether the up-sell list is empty.

skills.title: Emit Valid Browser Actions
skills.principle: Use the browser tool’s exact action schema, sending a complete executable click with the observed element reference and button argument—not a nested JSON object or truncated `raw_response`. After execution, inspect the updated accessibility tree; if unchanged or errored, correct the payload or target once rather than repeating the same malformed action.
skills.when_to_apply: When an intended control is visible but browser actions return an empty-action or parsing error, especially while expanding Magento product sections such as “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells”.

skills.title: Inspect Existing Cross-Sell Listings
skills.principle: Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells,” then inspect the existing “Cross-Sell Products” table and report its listed items. For a view-only request, do not click “Add Cross-Sell Products”; that opens a selection dialog for modifying associations rather than simply displaying the current list.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing cross-sells for a product in Magento Admin and the relationship section is collapsed. Use this after confirming the target product page and recognizing that the task asks to view, not add or edit.

skills.title: Save and Verify Inventory Changes
skills.principle:
1. On the product edit page, locate the Quantity field by its label and replace its current value with the requested quantity.
2. Click the page’s Save button.
3. Confirm completion from the visible “You saved the product.” message and verify the Quantity field shows the requested value before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When modifying inventory for an existing product in Magento Admin, provided the product edit page is open and the requested quantity is known.

skills.title: Open Products Before Searching
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin “CATALOG” menu and click its “Products” entry; do not search or scroll the dashboard.
2. Confirm the page heading is “Products” and use “Search by keyword” with the target product name, then click “Search.”
3. Open the matching “Edit” link, update inventory quantity, save, and verify the saved value or success message.
skills.when_to_apply: When modifying a Magento product from the dashboard, especially when the catalog menu is expanded but the product grid is not yet visible.

skills.title: Save and Verify Product Field Updates
skills.principle:
1. On the product edit page, locate the requested attribute by its accessible label and scope, such as the global Price field.
2. Clear the existing value and enter the requested replacement.
3. Click the labeled Save button to persist the change.
4. Confirm the new value and a success message such as “You saved the product.” Then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When updating a product attribute in Magento Admin and the product edit form, labeled target field, Save button, and post-save confirmation are available.

skills.title: Verify Product Grid Navigation
skills.principle: After opening Magento’s CATALOG menu, activate the explicitly labeled “Products” link, not the surrounding menu container. Verify that the URL or page heading shows the product grid before attempting searches, filters, or scrolling. If the page instead shows category fields or a category tree, return to Catalog and correct navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a product in Magento Admin and the Catalog menu is expanded, especially when multiple nested menu elements appear in the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Media-Specific Delete Controls
skills.principle: In Magento’s “Images And Videos” section, distinguish media types before acting. For each product image, use its image deletion control (such as “Delete image in all store views”), not a nearby “Delete video” button. Refresh the accessibility tree after each deletion because element bids can change. Confirm no image elements remain, click “Save,” verify “You saved the product,” then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product with existing media and the task targets images specifically. Expand “Images And Videos” first, and rely on current labels and observations rather than stale accessibility bids.

skills.title: Verify Product Images Before Editing
skills.principle: In Magento’s product editor, expand “Images And Videos” and inspect the rendered gallery, not just the accessibility tree. If thumbnails exist, use each thumbnail’s delete control, then click “Save” and verify the gallery is empty. If only “Browse to find or drag image here” appears, confirm that empty state before reporting no images.
skills.when_to_apply: When removing images from a Magento product and the accessibility tree shows only the uploader or omits thumbnail controls; visual gallery inspection is required before concluding that no images exist.

skills.title: Expand the Requested Product Section
skills.principle: On a product edit page, locate the accordion section matching the requested label and activate its header. Confirm completion by checking that the header is focused or marked expanded and that section-specific controls are visible, such as upload or add-media buttons. Once those controls appear, report completion without performing unrelated edits.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a shopping-admin task asks to navigate to a specific section of an already-open product page and the accessibility tree shows that section as a collapsible header.

skills.title: Open a Product’s Images And Videos Section
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s CATALOG menu and select Products.
2. Enter the target product name in “Search by keyword,” select Search, and confirm the matching product row.
3. Open its “Edit” link, then expand “Images And Videos.”
4. Verify the section is expanded by checking for controls such as “Add Video” and “Choose Files.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requires reaching media management for a specific product and the Products grid is available. Search and verify the matching product before opening its edit page.

skills.title: Verify Upload Files Before Retrying
skills.principle: For admin image uploads, expand “Images And Videos,” choose “Choose Files,” and upload only a verified, accessible image path.
