If upload_file returns ENOENT, do not guess alternate filenames or retry repeatedly; identify a valid provided asset or report the limitation and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: When an upload control is available but the required local asset is not explicitly provided or an upload attempt reports a missing file path.

skills.title: Verify Image File Before Uploading
skills.principle: In Magento’s product editor, expand “Images And Videos” and use “Choose Files” only with an image file that actually exists in the accessible filesystem. After selecting it, confirm the filename or thumbnail appears, then save the product. Do not retry invented filenames; if no accessible image exists, report the upload prerequisite clearly.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product image through Magento Admin and the upload control is available, but file-upload actions require a local filesystem path or available asset.

skills.title: Add Related Products in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Open the product’s “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” section.
2. Select “Add Related Products” and inspect the dialog’s selection count, even if the grid reports zero records.
3. If products are already selected, click “Add Selected Products.”
4. Confirm completion when the Related Products table lists the added items, then report success.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the related-products section is collapsed. This applies when the selection dialog shows a nonzero selected count, including cases where its grid displays no records.

skills.title: Complete Magento Related Product Assignment
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” and click the actual “Add Related Products” button, not the section header or table row.
2. In the product picker, select the target product using its selection control, then use the picker’s confirmation/add control.
3. Verify the target appears in the Related Products table, then click “Save” and confirm the unsaved-changes indicator disappears.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and adding a related product. The related-products section must be expanded, the target must be available in the picker, and changes must be saved after the table updates.

skills.title: Remove Up-Sells and Verify Save
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” and inspect the “Up-Sell Products” table.
2. Click “Remove” for the requested up-sell, re-read the table after each removal because rows and controls can reflow.
3. If the task requires clearing existing up-sells, continue until the up-sell table has no product rows.
4. Click “Save” and confirm the success message, such as “You saved the product.”
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a product in Magento Admin and removing one or more existing up-sell associations. The product edit page must be open, and changes must be saved after the table reflects the intended result.

skills.title: Expand the Product Association Section
skills.principle: Use the visible accordion heading “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” directly instead of repeatedly scrolling. Activate the heading to expand its controls, select the Up-Sells subtab or list, remove the existing association using its row control, click Save, and verify the association no longer appears after the section reloads.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento product and the target association section is visible as a collapsed accordion heading in the accessibility tree. Expand it before searching for or modifying related, up-sell, or cross-sell products.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Native Dropdowns
skills.principle: On an admin product edit page, locate the field by its label and inspect its current value. For a native HTML combobox, use the dropdown-selection action with the target option text rather than clicking an option element directly, which may be invisible. Verify the target value is selected, click the page’s “Save” button, and confirm a success message such as “You saved the product.”
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a product attribute in Magento Admin or another form using a native combobox, especially after direct clicking an expanded option fails or reports that the option is not visible.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: After an interaction fails, re-read the latest accessibility tree and identify the element’s actual role, accessible name, and current bid. Do not repeatedly click guessed text, icon-prefixed labels, XPath, or stale identifiers. If the target is absent, expand the relevant menu or use an observed navigation link, then verify the URL or page heading changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating an admin interface from a dashboard, especially after a click reports that an element or bid cannot be found.

skills.title: Expand the Product Content Section
skills.principle: On a product edit page, locate the collapsed section heading labeled "Content" and activate it. Confirm completion when the heading indicates expansion and content fields such as "Short Description" and "Description" become visible. Then stop and report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to product content in Magento Admin and the product edit page is already open with a visible, collapsed "Content" section heading.

skills.title: Distinguish Navigation From Product Sections
skills.principle: On a Magento product edit page, do not repeatedly click the global “CONTENT” navigation entry when the task names a product section. Identify the matching accordion heading inside the product form, such as “Content,” and activate that control. Confirm completion by checking that its fields or expanded panel become visible; if the page does not change, reassess the target control.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open a section of a product’s edit page and the accessibility tree contains both a global navigation item and an in-form accordion with the same label.

skills.title: Expand and Verify Product Reviews
skills.principle: On a product edit page, locate the collapsed “Product Reviews” accordion and expand it. Confirm navigation by checking the revealed reviews grid and its record count; “0 records found” or an empty-record message is a valid result. Report the observed state once, then terminate without repeating successful actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to inspect a specific product’s reviews in Magento Admin and the product edit page is already open or reachable.

skills.title: Open the Matched Product Record
skills.principle: After applying a product-name filter, verify the results count and inspect the visible row. When the target product row and its “Edit” link are present, open that product record immediately; do not repeat menu clicks or scroll unnecessarily. Continue from the product editor to locate the requested reviews section.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when Catalog > Products is filtered and the target product row is visibly listed with an Edit control.

skills.title: Match Labels to Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Use the accessibility tree’s visible label-to-element mapping, not nearby or remembered bids. Locate the exact “Search Engine Optimization” text and activate its associated control. After clicking, verify that SEO fields appear or the section’s expanded state changes; if not, re-read the refreshed tree and select the newly reported control rather than repeating the same bid.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating collapsible sections in Magento product editing pages, especially after the tree changes or similar headings are adjacent. Confirm the target label and its current associated element before acting.

skills.title: Activate Catalog Menu and Verify Submenu
skills.principle: Click the main navigation entry labeled “CATALOG,” then inspect the updated accessibility tree. Confirm completion when the entry is focused or active and its submenu, such as “Products” and “Categories,” is visible. Once confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin navigation tasks requesting a top-level section. Start from any admin page where the horizontal main menu is visible, and verify the section expands before terminating.

skills.title: Stop After Catalog Menu Expands
skills.principle: Click the main-menu “CATALOG” entry once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. When its Catalog submenu appears (for example, “Products” and “Categories”), the navigation goal is complete; report completion and terminate instead of issuing further clicks, keyboard actions, or guessed URLs.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked only to navigate to a Magento Admin main-menu section and the section expands in place, evidenced by visible submenu entries or expanded menu state.

skills.title: Add Related Products in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” on the product edit page.
2. Click “Add Related Products,” open “Filters,” and filter or inspect the product grid by name or other relevant attributes.
3. Select each target product checkbox, then click “Add Selected Products.” Repeat if needed.
4. Confirm all targets appear under “Related Products,” click “Save,” and verify “You saved the product.”
skills.when_to_apply: Use when editing a Magento product and adding one or more related products. Ensure the product grid is loaded, select products by visible names rather than row position, and save only after all targets appear in the related-products table.

skills.title: Expand Visible Product Relations Section
skills.principle: When the product editor’s accessibility tree already shows “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells,” treat it as a collapsed accordion. Click that section heading to expand it, then configure the requested cross-sell items and use Save; do not keep scrolling when the target section is already present.
skills.when_to_apply: In Magento product editing, when the target relations section appears in the current accessibility tree but its fields are absent, indicating the accordion is collapsed.

skills.title: Configure Product Cross-Sells in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Expand “Related Products, Up-Sells, and Cross-Sells” on the target product.
2. In “Cross-Sell Products,” click “Add Cross-Sell Products”; use “Filters” if the dialog initially shows no records.
3. Select appropriate complementary products, click “Add Selected Products,” then click “Save.”
4. Confirm the page displays “You saved the product” and the selected items appear in the Cross-Sell Products table.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing cross-sell associations for a Magento product and the product edit page is available. Use complementary, enabled catalog items and verify the save confirmation before reporting completion.

skills.title: Open Magento Catalog Products
skills.principle:
1. Activate the main navigation entry labeled “CATALOG” to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the “Products” submenu link for the catalog’s product-management page.
3. Confirm completion from the page heading, URL path, or visible product grid before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Magento Admin’s Catalog section, especially from another admin page. The authenticated admin session must be active and the CATALOG navigation entry visible.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Repeating Navigation
skills.principle: After selecting a navigation menu entry, verify the resulting page using its URL, page title, heading, or visible content. If the target section is already displayed, report completion and stop. Do not repeatedly click stale element IDs; reopen the menu and re-inspect the current accessibility tree only when the destination is not confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar menus, especially after a submenu click changes the page and accessibility-tree element IDs.

skills.title: Verify Menu Expansion Before Reclicking
skills.principle: Click the target top-level navigation entry once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. If its submenu appears with the section heading and child links, navigation is complete; stop or select the requested child item. Do not repeat the same click merely because the URL remains unchanged or focus persists.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in admin interfaces where top-level navigation opens an in-page dropdown or flyout instead of changing the URL, especially when the updated tree exposes submenu headings or links.

skills.title: Open Magento Reports Menu
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, locate the top navigation entry labeled “REPORTS” and activate it. Confirm completion when its expanded menu displays report categories such as Marketing, Reviews, Sales, Customers, Products, Statistics, or Business Intelligence. Once the menu is visibly open, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task is to navigate to Magento Admin’s Reports section and the top navigation bar is visible, even if the current page URL does not change after opening the menu.

skills.title: Verify Menu Expansion, Then Stop
skills.principle: After selecting a Magento Admin navigation category, inspect the updated accessibility tree. If the category expands and shows its submenu, treat that visible state as completion for a section-navigation request and terminate. If a specific report is requested, click the matching submenu link instead of repeating no-op actions; confirm the resulting page or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin top-level item such as REPORTS uses an in-page dropdown or hash link and the accessibility tree shows submenu entries without changing the URL.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once the required admin page is visibly confirmed by its heading and relevant URL, treat navigation as complete. Report completion and terminate; do not inspect records, open an invoice, or perform extra actions unless the task explicitly requests them.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the target page is loaded and its identifying heading or content is visible, such as Magento’s Invoices page.

skills.title: Check Catalog Availability First
skills.principle: Navigate to the relevant catalog listing and inspect its result state before selecting an item. If the table explicitly shows zero records or no matching records, report that the requested item cannot be viewed or edited and identify the available creation control, such as “Add Product,” as the prerequisite.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or edit an existing catalog item, especially after arriving from an edit page or when the listing may be empty. Confirm the table’s record count before attempting item selection.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Catalog Items
skills.principle: When navigating a Magento catalog list, select the target product using the accessibility tree’s current element bid, preferably the product-name cell or containing row. Do not pass the product URL as a click target. After activation, verify the page heading or URL identifies the product edit page, then stop once the requested view is reached.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this when a catalog list exposes product rows and accessibility bids. First locate the target by its visible name, activate its associated row or link, and confirm the resulting product edit page.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog to Products
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation's “CATALOG” menu.
2. Select the visible “Products” entry from the expanded submenu.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “Products” and product-management controls such as “Add Product,” filters, and the catalog table are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting from another Magento Admin page and asked to reach the Products page for managing products or inventory; use the observed menu labels rather than fixed element IDs.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: Once the requested Products page is visibly confirmed by its heading and product-management controls, report completion and terminate. Do not add products or alter inventory merely because filtered results show zero records; active filters may explain the empty list.
skills.when_to_apply: For navigation-only admin tasks, after selecting Catalog > Products and observing the Products heading, product controls, and the expected page URL or equivalent page state.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Catalog Categories
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin CATALOG navigation entry from the current page.
2. Select the visible “Categories” submenu link.
3. Confirm completion when the Categories page shows its category tree and controls such as “Add Root Category” or “Add Subcategory,” then report completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requires reaching catalog category management from another admin page, especially when the category tree and management controls must be visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: When the requested admin page is open and its heading, URL, or controls confirm the destination, treat navigation as complete. Report completion and terminate instead of creating or modifying catalog data unless the task explicitly requests those changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks such as opening Magento’s Categories page, when the destination page is visibly loaded and no specific edit, creation, or deletion is requested.

skills.title: Navigate Magento to Themes
skills.principle:
1. Open the CONTENT menu in Magento Admin.
2. Under the Design section, select the Themes link.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading says “Themes” and a theme table is visible; then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to access or manage store design themes from a Magento Admin page, especially when the current page is elsewhere in the admin interface.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Themes Page
skills.principle: Navigate through CONTENT → Design → Themes, using the visible “Themes” submenu link directly if expanding the Design heading is blocked. Once the page shows the “Themes” heading and theme list, recognize the task as complete and stop; do not open individual theme “View” links or perform unrelated verification.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked only to access Magento’s Themes page and the page visibly displays the “Themes” heading with a theme list.

skills.title: Filter Customer Order Total Reports
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s REPORTS menu and select Customers → Order Total.
2. Enter the requested From and To dates, then click Refresh.
3. If Refresh times out, inspect the page: use the report table and Total row only if the requested range and populated results are visibly confirmed.
4. Compare customer Total values and report the highest-value customers with the aggregate order count and value.
skills.when_to_apply: When identifying high-value customers in Magento’s Customer Order Total report, especially when the initial table is empty or a refresh action times out but filtered results may already be loaded.

skills.title: Navigate to the Ordered Products Report
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin "REPORTS" navigation entry to expand its menu.
2. Under the "Products" section, select the "Ordered" link.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading reads "Ordered Products Report"; report filters include "From:", "To:", "Show By:", and "Refresh".
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to access product sales or ordered-product reporting and you are starting from another admin page. Stop after the report heading and controls are visibly confirmed.

skills.title: Choose the Correct Ordered Report
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open REPORTS and select the “Ordered” link under the “Products” section, not “Orders” under “Sales.” Verify the destination heading and report context before entering filters; “Orders Report” is a different report.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access the Ordered Products report from Magento’s Reports menu, especially when both “Orders” and “Ordered” links are visible.

skills.title: Broaden Empty Sales Report Ranges
skills.principle:
1. Open Reports, then choose Sales > Orders.
2. Set the required From and To dates and select Show Report.
3. If the result shows zero records, broaden the date range and run the report again.
4. Confirm completion from the records count and populated table, then summarize the displayed metrics or available export options.
skills.when_to_apply: When analyzing Magento Sales Orders and the initial report has required filters but displays “0 records found.” Broaden the date range before concluding that no orders exist.

skills.title: Verify Report Date Formatting
skills.principle: Enter dates using the report’s displayed locale format or calendar picker, then verify both fields retain the intended dates before clicking “Show Report.” If the page reformats them unexpectedly, correct the format first; do not interpret zero results until the submitted date range is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering Magento Sales Orders reports with required From and To fields, especially after entering dates programmatically and the UI displays a transformed or implausible date.

skills.title: Preserve Requirements After Duplicate Errors
skills.principle: When creation reports a duplicate name, preserve the requested name and inspect the existing record before proceeding. Recheck fields reset by validation, including website exclusions; update an existing record only when authorized, and use a different name only when the user permits it.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento customer-group save reports an existing name, especially if selected exclusions reset after the failed save.

skills.title: Verify Tax Class Before Editing
skills.principle: On the customer-group edit form, inspect the current “Tax Class” value first. If it already matches the requested class, make no changes and report completion. Otherwise, change only that field, click “Save Customer Group,” and confirm the success message before stopping.
skills.when_to_apply: When administering a Magento customer group and the requested tax class may already be configured. The group’s edit form must expose the “Tax Class” field and a save control.

skills.title: Open and Edit the Target Group
skills.principle: On the customer-groups listing, first clear any active filters or search for the requested group. Use that row’s “Select” action to open its edit form, change the Tax Class field to the requested value, save, and verify the confirmation or persisted field value. Do not report infeasibility merely because the listing itself lacks the setting.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin customer-group task starts on the group listing, especially when an active filter hides the requested group or the tax-class control is not visible in the table.

skills.title: Recover From Duplicate Group Names
skills.principle: When saving a new customer group triggers a duplicate-name error, replace the name with a unique value. Recheck the excluded-website list after validation, because the selection may reset; select the target website again, save, and confirm the success message and return to the groups list.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when creating a Magento customer group with website exclusions and saving displays a duplicate-name error or rerenders the form, especially when the previously selected website is no longer marked selected.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Finding Groups
skills.principle: On the Customer Groups page, inspect the active filters before searching. If a filter excludes the requested group, use “Clear all” or adjust the filter, then verify the unfiltered results count and table rows. Search or filter by the target group name rather than repeatedly scrolling a filtered list.
skills.when_to_apply: When a requested customer group is absent from the visible Magento table, especially when “Active filters” shows a restrictive Group filter and pagination indicates only a subset of records.

skills.title: Read the Grid Record Count
skills.principle: On the relevant admin listing page, use the visible “records found” count as the total available items. Verify that the listing is unfiltered or account for any active filters before reporting the number. Once the count is confirmed, report it directly and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin tasks asking how many records exist when the corresponding listing page is already open and visibly shows a records-found count; check active filters first.

skills.title: Count Distinct Group Rows
skills.principle: On the Customer Groups page, use the displayed record count and inspect each table row’s Group value. Count distinct group names, not merely repeated-looking entries or the active filter label; report the resulting total and names only after reconciling all visible rows.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking how many customer groups exist in an admin list, especially when the page shows active filters or multiple records with similar names.

skills.title: Verify Destination After Navigation Timeout
skills.principle: After a navigation click reports a timeout, inspect the current URL, page title, and visible page content before retrying. If they identify the requested section and its management interface is visible, treat the task as complete, report success, and stop rather than repeating the click.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin-menu navigation action times out while the browser may already have completed navigation, especially when the current accessibility tree shows the target section and its expected controls.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Then Stop
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree after each menu interaction. Open “CATALOG,” click the currently observed “Categories” link, and verify the destination through the page URL or Categories page content. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op actions or using stale element references.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin or similar nested menus, especially after a menu click changes the accessibility tree. Prerequisite: the target menu entry must be visible in the latest observation.

skills.title: Change Admin List Page Size
skills.principle: On an admin listing page, locate the textbox labeled “per page,” replace its current value with the requested record count, and verify the field displays the new value. Once the displayed value confirms the change, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to change how many records an admin grid displays per page and the accessibility tree exposes a “per page” textbox or equivalent page-size control.

skills.title: Use Expanded Navigation Submenus
skills.principle: When a top-level admin menu expands, inspect its submenu instead of repeatedly clicking the parent. Select the exact entry matching the task, such as “Customer Groups,” then verify the destination page and its grid controls before concluding the setting is unavailable.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a dashboard navigation item reveals a vertical submenu containing the requested entity or management page, especially before attempting direct URLs or reporting failure.

skills.title: Audit Catalog Price Rule Groups
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Marketing > Promotions > Catalog Price Rule. Inspect every listed rule, open each rule’s details, and record the customer groups marked selected in the “Customer Groups” listbox. Consolidate the rule-to-group mapping, report it once, then terminate without resending or performing unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked which customer groups receive special pricing and the Customer Groups page lacks pricing indicators. Ensure all catalog price rules shown in the listing are reviewed before reporting.

skills.title: Validate Message Action Formatting
skills.principle: After gathering the results, send one concise `send_msg_to_user` action using valid quoting and escaped newlines. Avoid nested JSON, unescaped apostrophes, or excessive backslashes. Confirm the action payload is nonempty and syntactically complete before submitting; once accepted, stop rather than retrying unnecessarily.
skills.when_to_apply: When a BrowserGym task is complete and the final response must be sent through `send_msg_to_user`, especially after an earlier attempt returns an empty-action or formatting error.

skills.title: Export Customer Data as CSV
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers section and choose All Customers.
2. Click the page’s Export control to reveal format options.
3. Confirm CSV is selected, then click the dialog’s Export button to initiate the download.
4. Report completion after the export action is submitted.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task requires exporting customer records from Magento’s Customers page and the Export control is available. Check the requested format before submitting the export dialog.

skills.title: Navigate to Pending Product Reviews
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the Marketing menu, locate the User Content subsection, and select Pending Reviews. Confirm the destination using the page heading and inspect the results count and empty-state message. Report whether reviews exist, then stop once the result is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to review pending product reviews in Magento Admin and the Marketing navigation is available. The task is complete after the Pending Reviews page visibly reports its records or an empty state.

skills.title: Act on Unchanged Navigation Evidence
skills.principle: When a menu expansion leaves the page and accessibility tree unchanged, treat it as evidence that the current section is not the target. Stop repeating no-op observations; inspect other task-relevant navigation sections, especially those whose submenu semantics match the requested content, and click the specific review-management entry. Confirm the destination heading or records list before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requires locating a specific management page and expanding a navigation section reveals unrelated submenu items while repeated observations show no new target controls.

skills.title: Navigate to Magento URL Rewrites
skills.principle: Expand the Marketing navigation menu, locate the SEO & Search subsection, and select URL Rewrites. Confirm completion when the page heading reads “URL Rewrites” and controls such as “Add URL Rewrite,” “Filters,” and the rewrites table are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests URL rewrite management and the current page is elsewhere in the admin panel. Use the observed navigation labels rather than hard-coded element identifiers.

skills.title: Use Valid Semantic Navigation Targets
skills.principle: Navigate using the visible accessible label and role, such as the “CONTENT” link, rather than an icon’s internal glyph or guessed identifier. After issuing the action, verify that the page URL or menu state changes. If the action payload is empty or errors, immediately choose a different semantic locator or keyboard navigation strategy instead of repeatedly waiting on an unchanged page.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin dashboard exposes navigation entries by accessible names but clicking an icon-based or guessed selector produces an empty-action error and the page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Edit and Verify Magento Search Terms
skills.principle:
1. Open Marketing and expand the SEO & Search section, then select Search Terms.
2. Identify the target search-term row by its visible query and open its Edit control.
3. Change the requested field, such as Number of results, while preserving other values.
4. Select Save Search and confirm completion by checking the success message and updated listing value.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring viewing and editing an existing search term, when the Marketing navigation and target record are accessible and the form exposes the requested field.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids, Not URLs
skills.principle: When clicking an observed link, use its accessibility-tree bid or locate it by visible label; do not pass the link’s href as the click target. After an interaction error, re-inspect the current tree and choose a valid element bid before retrying or navigating through the relevant admin menu.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever BrowserGym reports that an element cannot be found despite showing an href in the accessibility tree, especially when opening Magento admin records or configuration sections.

skills.title: Create and Verify an Email Template
skills.principle:
1. Open Marketing, expand Communications, and select Email Templates.
2. Choose Add New Template, then complete the required Template Name, Template Subject, and Template Content fields.
3. Select Save Template.
4. Confirm the success message and verify the new template appears in the email-template grid.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer-communication email template in Magento Admin, after reaching the Marketing navigation and having the intended name, subject, and message content ready.

skills.title: Stop After Save Confirmation
skills.principle: After saving a Magento email template, verify the success state by checking for the confirmation message “You saved the email template.” and the returned template list containing the new entry. Once both indicate completion, report success and terminate without clicking Save again or performing unnecessary waits.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating an email template and the Save Template action returns to the Email Templates list with a visible success confirmation and the new template appears in the records.

skills.title: Handle Duplicate Customer Emails
skills.principle: When creating a customer, select the required customer group, fill all mandatory fields, and use an email address known or generated to be unique for the associated website. If saving shows a duplicate-email validation error, replace the email with another unique address, click “Save Customer” again, and verify the success state before finishing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this on Magento Admin’s New Customer form when creating an account, especially if the initial save displays “A customer with the same email address already exists in an associated website.”

skills.title: Navigate to Magento Widgets
skills.principle:
1. Open the CONTENT navigation entry to reveal its menu.
2. Under Elements, select the Widgets link.
3. Verify the destination by checking for the “Widgets” heading, widget-instance list, and management controls such as “Add Widget”.
4. Once verified, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Magento Admin’s Widgets area from another admin page, especially when the CONTENT menu is collapsed and the destination must be confirmed from the accessibility tree.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Navigation
skills.principle: Target navigation controls using the current accessibility-tree bid, not visible text or icon content. For example, select the CONTENT link’s observed bid, then inspect the updated tree for the expanded submenu and choose Widgets. If an action errors or the tree is unchanged, re-inspect and use the newly reported bid instead of repeating the failed selector.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating a Magento Admin menu from the dashboard, especially when visible labels cannot be resolved as BrowserGym element bids or repeated clicks leave the page unchanged.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Media Gallery
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin CONTENT navigation entry.
2. Under the Media section, select “Media Gallery.”
3. Confirm the “Manage Gallery” page appears, with media actions and a directory tree; report the currently selected directory and whether records are present.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or manage website images and media files in Magento Admin, starting from another admin page with the top navigation available.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Media Gallery
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open CONTENT, select Media Gallery, and verify the Manage Gallery page is displayed. If the task only requests access, report completion immediately; do not invent an upload, folder, or file-management action without explicit requirements and a valid local file.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access or open the Media Gallery and the page heading “Manage Gallery” is visible. Stop unless the task explicitly requests a subsequent media operation.

skills.title: Verify Customer Email Registration
skills.principle:
1. Open Customers > All Customers in the admin panel.
2. Enter the target email in the “Search by keyword” field and activate “Search.”
3. Confirm completion from the filtered state: a matching customer row means registered; “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records” means not registered.
4. Report the result and stop once the filtered result is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when checking whether an email exists in the Magento customer database and the Customers > All Customers page provides its keyword search field and Search control.

skills.title: Verify Page Builder Insertions
skills.principle: After opening Magento’s Page Builder, place elements using the supported drag-and-drop interaction rather than merely clicking their palette entries. Confirm the canvas no longer shows “Drag Row, Columns, Tabs, Block, Dynamic Block or HTML Code here” before adding nested content or saving.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating or editing a Magento CMS block with Page Builder, especially after adding layout or content elements and whenever the canvas still displays its empty-state instruction.

skills.title: Save and Verify New CMS Blocks
skills.principle:
1. In Magento Content > Blocks, open “Add New Block” and fill the required title, unique identifier, store view, and intended content.
2. If using Page Builder, drag elements onto the visible content canvas/drop zone, not a nearby sidebar textbox; confirm the element appears in the canvas.
3. Click “Save” and verify the block-list page or success notification shows the newly created block.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento CMS block and the form is populated or Page Builder content has been added. The task is incomplete until “Save” is pressed and the resulting block or success confirmation is observed.

skills.title: Create and Verify Magento Category
skills.principle:
1. Open Magento Admin’s Catalog menu and select Categories.
2. Choose the appropriate parent in the category tree, then click “Add Subcategory” or “Add Root Category.”
3. Enter the required “Category Name”; retain or adjust “Enable Category” and “Include in Menu” as needed, then click “Save.”
4. Confirm the resulting category edit page shows “You saved the category” and the new category in the tree.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a product category in Magento Admin, with access to the Catalog > Categories page and a known parent category or root-category requirement.

skills.title: Review CMS Pages From Content Menu
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin’s “CONTENT” navigation and select “Pages” under “Elements”.
2. Read the CMS pages table, using the record count and each row’s Title, URL Key, Store View, Layout, and Status columns.
3. Summarize totals and distinguish enabled from disabled pages, including notable configuration patterns.
4. Report the findings once the complete table is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when reviewing existing CMS pages in Magento Admin and the Content navigation is available. Confirm the Pages table has loaded and shows the full record count before reporting.

skills.title: Read CMS Status From Listing
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Content > Elements > Pages and inspect the existing grid directly. The table’s Status column reports each page’s content status (for example, Enabled or Disabled); use Search by keyword or Filters only when needed. Do not open Add New Page or select row checkboxes when the task is review-only.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing existing Magento CMS pages and the Pages grid is visible with Title, URL Key, Store View, and Status columns. Read and report the displayed statuses without modifying records.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When a navigation item is visible in the accessibility tree, activate it using its current numeric bid (for example, the CONTENT link’s bid), not its displayed name, icon text, or URL. If activation fails, obtain a fresh tree and select the newly assigned bid before retrying; verify that the menu expands or the destination page appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this in BrowserGym admin navigation when a visible link repeatedly raises “Could not find element” despite matching text or URL, especially when labels include icon glyphs or dynamic accessibility text.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Payment Transactions
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin SALES navigation entry to reveal sales-related destinations.
2. Select the Transactions link.
3. Confirm the page heading is “Transactions”; report the displayed records, including an explicit empty-state message when no records are found.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view payment transactions in Magento Admin and starting from another admin page. Use the SALES menu and verify the destination heading and record count before reporting completion.

skills.title: Target the Actual Date Input
skills.principle: On Magento Transactions, distinguish the editable date textbox from its adjacent calendar button. Use the textbox labeled “To” for direct date entry; use the calendar button only to open the picker, then select the required month, year, and day. After both dates are set, click “Search” and verify the records-found result.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering Magento Admin transaction records by date and the accessibility tree exposes separate “From”/“To” textboxes alongside calendar buttons. Re inspect element roles after any locator error instead of retrying the same target.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Template Save
skills.principle: After editing the required email template fields, click “Save Template” and verify the success message, such as “You saved the email template.” Once the requested customization is confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of creating additional templates or taking unrequested actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento email-template edit shows a successful save confirmation and the requested template customization is complete; do not expand the task unless the user explicitly requests multiple templates.

skills.title: Verify Template Edits Before Saving
skills.principle: After filling an email template field, confirm the accessibility tree shows the intended value. If the action errors or the content remains unchanged, retry with valid, simpler input before saving. Only claim customization after the saved page displays a success confirmation and reflects the intended changes.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing Magento Marketing > Communications > Email Templates, especially after inserting long HTML or variable syntax that may be rejected or malformed.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Marketing Communications
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin MARKETING menu.
2. Under Communications, select the clearly labeled Newsletter Subscribers entry.
3. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and visible subscriber grid before reporting completion or choosing a specific management action.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage newsletter subscribers in Magento Admin and the current page is elsewhere. Requires access to the MARKETING navigation and its expanded Communications submenu.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility IDs Exactly
skills.principle: After each observation, use the exact current accessibility-tree bid in the action, not a string-concatenation expression or stale identifier. If an action reports that an element cannot be found, re-read the latest tree, locate the intended control by its visible role or label, and try that current bid once. Avoid repeated scrolling or unrelated controls without evidence they support the task.
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever BrowserGym actions fail with an element-not-found error, especially after navigation or scrolling, and the latest accessibility tree still exposes the relevant control.

skills.title: Open the Products in Cart Report
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Reports navigation and expand its menu.
2. Under Marketing, select “Products in Cart.”
3. Verify the page heading and report result; “0 records found” or “We couldn’t find any records” confirms an empty cart report.
4. Report the observed result and stop once the report is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view products currently in customer carts in Magento Admin, provided the Reports navigation and Marketing report menu are accessible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Empty Report
skills.principle: Once the relevant report page is open, verify its heading and inspect the record count. If it clearly shows zero records and an empty-results message, treat that as the current result, report that no matching records were found, and stop. Do not change pagination or export format, repeatedly search, or click controls that are absent or invisible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin report such as “Products in Carts” loads successfully and visibly shows zero records with an empty table message.

skills.title: Review Abandoned Cart Reports
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Reports navigation and expand its submenu.
2. Under Marketing, select “Abandoned Carts.”
3. Verify the report heading and inspect the record count or empty-state message.
4. Report the observed cart count and relevant available columns; stop once the report state is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to review abandoned carts in a Magento admin environment and the Reports navigation is available. Use the visible record count or “We couldn't find any records” message as completion evidence.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching the Requested Report
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open REPORTS, expand Marketing, and select Abandoned Carts. Once the report page is displayed, inspect its record count and table. If it shows “0 records found,” report that result and stop; apply date filters only when the task specifies a date range.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to review a named Magento report and the report page is accessible. Treat the displayed count and table state as the result unless filtering criteria are explicitly requested.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Reports by Semantic Category
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level “REPORTS” navigation entry and inspect its expanded categories.
2. Under the “Customers” category, select the report whose label matches the requested metric, such as “Order Count.”
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading and report controls; report an empty-result message accurately without treating it as navigation failure.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests a customer, sales, or product report and the current page is elsewhere. The Reports menu must be accessible, and the target report should be selected by visible category and label.

skills.title: Validate Action Serialization Before Retrying
skills.principle: When a browser action returns an empty-action or parsing error, inspect the emitted tool payload before retrying. Ensure the action is passed as a complete, valid command with the intended target, then execute it once and verify that the page URL or visible content changes. Repeating the same malformed payload cannot advance the task.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply after any browser action reports an empty action, parsing failure, or unchanged page. Prerequisite: the intended control is still visible and identifiable in the current accessibility tree.

skills.title: Customize Currency Symbols in Magento
skills.principle:
1. Open Stores and expand its menu.
2. Select Currency Symbols under the Currency section.
3. Replace the target currency’s symbol field, leaving “Use Standard” unchecked for a custom value.
4. Click “Save Currency Symbols” and verify the success message and updated field value before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring a currency symbol change, when the Stores navigation and Currency Symbols page are available and the target currency field can be edited.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Form Fields
skills.principle: Use the textbox’s accessibility-tree bid, not its visible label, when invoking BrowserGym actions. On the Currency Symbols page, identify the bid associated with the target currency field, fill it with the desired symbol, click “Save Currency Symbols,” and verify the saved value or success indication.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento admin form field is visible but actions using its label repeatedly return “Could not find element,” re inspect the current accessibility tree and target the field’s numeric bid before retrying.

skills.title: Verify Required Options Before Saving
skills.principle: When a required dropdown value is not visible, inspect the control’s actual available options or use supported keyboard navigation, then verify the selected value changed. Do not infer absence from a truncated accessibility tree. If the value remains unavailable, investigate the relevant configuration or report the blocker instead of saving a partially compliant record.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when completing an admin form with mandatory fields and a requested value is missing from the accessibility tree or selection attempt times out, especially before clicking a save button.

skills.title: Verify Dropdown Selection Before Saving
skills.principle: When changing a required dropdown, inspect its available options and select the requested value using a supported control method. After selection, confirm the field visibly reports the requested value. If it remains unchanged or the option is unavailable, investigate rather than guessing with repeated arrow keys; only save after every required field is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin forms with dropdowns or comboboxes, especially when option selection errors occur or the accessibility tree still shows the original value. Verify the target value before submitting.

skills.title: Verify Existing Order Filters First
skills.principle:
1. Navigate through Sales to Orders in the Magento Admin panel.
2. Inspect the Active filters area before changing anything.
3. If Purchase Date already spans the requested period, verify the visible order dates and record count match.
4. Report completion without reapplying or altering correct filters.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to filter Magento orders by a date range and the Orders page may already contain saved or preapplied filters.

skills.title: Search and Verify Magento Orders
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales > Orders from the admin navigation.
2. Enter the exact order identifier in “Search by keyword” and click “Search.”
3. Verify the filtered row matches both the target order ID and customer, then select its “View” link.
4. Confirm the order details page shows the matching order number and customer before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a specific order in Magento Admin, especially when the order list is large and the request includes both an order identifier and customer name.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility IDs for Search
skills.principle: After navigation, re-read the current accessibility tree and target the search textbox by its current role, label, or bid. Do not reuse an ID from a previous page or confuse the global admin search with the Orders grid's “Search by keyword” field. Clear the active filter, enter the target order identifier, select Search, then open the matching order row and verify its details.
skills.when_to_apply: When locating an order in Magento Admin’s Sales > Orders grid, especially when the page has preexisting filters or navigation has changed the accessibility-tree element IDs.

skills.title: Find and Open a Magento Order
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin SALES menu and select Orders.
2. Enter the target order identifier in “Search by keyword” and activate Search.
3. Confirm the filtered row matches the requested order and customer, then select its “View” action.
4. Verify the order detail page shows the matching order number and customer information before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring order details when the target order identifier and, ideally, customer name are known. The Orders grid must be accessible and support keyword filtering.

skills.title: Validate Actions Before Retrying
skills.principle: When a browser action returns an empty-action or element-not-found error, stop repeating the same malformed command. Re-read the current accessibility tree, construct a complete action using the current element’s accessible role or label, and verify the payload is syntactically complete. For order searches, clear existing filters such as stale keywords or invalid dates before entering the target identifier or customer and submitting Search.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin list pages when navigation or filtering actions fail, especially after accessibility-tree bids, escaping, or stale filter state causes empty results or command errors.

skills.title: Verify Order Row Before Opening
skills.principle:
1. In Magento Admin, open Sales > Orders and inspect the table for the target order ID.
2. Confirm the same row shows the requested customer; clear active filters or search by keyword if the order is not visible.
3. Click that row’s “View” action, then verify the detail page heading and customer information match before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to view a specific Magento order and the Orders grid may contain active date filters, multiple pages, or several orders for the same customer.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Order Details
skills.principle: Once the order view page visibly shows the requested order number and matching customer, treat the task as complete. Report completion immediately and terminate; do not issue repeated noop actions or continue interacting with the unchanged page.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing an order in Magento Admin, after filtering Orders and opening the result whose order number and customer match the request.

skills.title: Clear Unintended Filters Before Searching
skills.principle: On an admin list page, inspect the “Active filters” section before adding the requested filter. Remove any unrelated filters, such as Gender, then open “Filters,” set the target field (for example, Country), and click “Apply Filters.” Confirm the active-filter summary and record count match the unscoped request before reporting results.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a list already contains active filters and the task asks for all records matching one new criterion. Verify unrelated filters are removed before concluding the displayed records are complete.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Customer Search
skills.principle:
1. Open Customers > All Customers and inspect active filters.
2. If stale keyword, country, or state filters exist, select “Clear all” before searching.
3. Enter the target customer’s identifying name or email in “Search by keyword,” then select “Search.”
4. Verify the matching row’s name and identifying details, and open its “Edit” link; completion is confirmed when the account details page appears.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when the customer list shows unexpected filters, zero results, or many records. Ensure the target’s name or email is known before searching.

skills.title: Use Visible Customer Navigation
skills.principle: Navigate through the observed Customers menu rather than guessing admin URLs. Select the visible “All Customers” link, verify the resulting page is a customer grid rather than a 404, then inspect its filter controls for the requested attribute and apply the gender filter. If navigation fails, return to the last valid page and use its rendered links.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering customer records in Magento Admin and the current page exposes a Customers menu or “All Customers” link. Verify each navigation result before attempting filters or repeating menu interactions.

skills.title: Verify All Customer Pages Before Reporting
skills.principle:
1. Open the customer list and locate the “Confirmed email” column.
2. Inspect every result page using pagination; do not infer the full result from the first page.
3. Treat “Confirmation Not Required” as distinct from explicit confirmation, and collect only records showing confirmed status.
4. If no explicit confirmations appear after all pages, report that none are present and explain the configuration implication.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when generating a customer list filtered by email-confirmation status in Magento Admin, especially when the grid shows multiple pages or indicates that confirmation is not required.

skills.title: Verify Every Result Page
skills.principle: Clear unrelated active filters, then inspect the full customer grid rather than only the first page. Use the displayed record count and pagination controls to review every page, checking the “Confirmed email” status on each row. Report an empty result only after all pages contain no confirmed entries.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin listing has pre-existing filters, multiple pages, or a requested status is represented by a table column rather than a visible filter.

skills.title: Read Creation Method From Customer Results
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Customers → All Customers, preserve or apply the identifying customer filter, and inspect the matching row’s “Account Created in” column. Use the displayed value as the creation store or method, verify the record count, then report the result. If no dedicated filter exists for that column, do not infer one; read the column directly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when identifying how a known customer was created and the Customers grid already supports filtering by an identifier such as tax number, email, or name.

skills.title: Verify Customer Creation Before Reporting
skills.principle: Complete the customer form and select “Save Customer.” If Magento reports that the email already exists, do not substitute a different address or claim success. Preserve the requested details, report the duplicate-email conflict, and ask whether an alternative address is authorized. Only report creation after the page shows a successful save confirmation or the new customer appears in the customer list.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a Magento customer and saving produces a duplicate-email error or the page remains on “New Customer.”

skills.title: Respect Exact Email Constraints
skills.principle: When creating a customer, enter the requested name and email, then select “Save Customer.” If Magento reports that the email already exists, preserve the requested email, recognize that creating a duplicate account is impossible, and report the constraint instead of substituting an unrequested address. Confirm success only after the page shows a post-save result or success notification.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin’s New Customer form when the requested email may already belong to an account, especially after a save attempt displays a duplicate-email error.

skills.title: Create Accounts from All Customers
skills.principle: For a customer-account task, do not create a customer group first. Navigate to Customers → All Customers → Add New Customer, then select the required group, fill all mandatory identity fields, enter the Tax/VAT Number, and click “Save Customer.” Verify the resulting success message or customer record shows the saved account and VAT value.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task requests a new customer account, especially with a tax/VAT number, and the current Magento Admin page is Customer Groups or another non-account form.

skills.title: Create Customers Directly
skills.principle: For a customer-account task, use Customers > All Customers and start the customer creation flow. Fill the requested identity, contact, customer-group, and tax/VAT fields in the account form. Create a new customer group only when explicitly required or when no suitable existing group is available; verify the saved account and VAT value afterward.
skills.when_to_apply: When the Magento Admin opens on Customer Groups or another unrelated page while the task requests a customer account with tax/VAT data, navigate to Customers > All Customers before editing configuration.

skills.title: Read Customer Groups From Listing
skills.principle: From a customer-group creation form, use the “Back” control to return to the Customer Groups listing. Read the table rows and record each displayed group, using the visible record count to verify completeness. Report the listed groups as the options available for new customer creation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which customer groups can be selected for a new customer and the current page is a group-creation form or another detail view. Ensure the listing table and record count are visible before reporting.

skills.title: Verify Customer Groups Before Reporting
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers navigation menu and select the visible “Customer Groups” entry, using its label rather than dashboard tab IDs.
2. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading “Customer Groups” and the groups table.
3. Read the listed group names, report them to the user, and terminate once the list is verified.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked which customer groups are available for creating customers in Magento Admin, starting from the dashboard or another Customers page.

skills.title: Navigate to All Customers
skills.principle: Open the admin navigation entry labeled “CUSTOMERS,” then select “All Customers” from its expanded menu. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Customers” and a customer table with management controls, such as “Add New Customer” or “Actions,” is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting from another Magento Admin page and the task requires viewing or managing the complete customer account list.

skills.title: Use Valid Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When a click fails, re-read the current accessibility tree and use the exact element bid format exposed by the browser tool. Do not reconstruct bids from visible text, icons, indices, or guessed concatenations. If repeated attempts fail, use a visible navigation control or a confirmed route only when supported by the observation, then verify the destination heading or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when navigating an admin page after an action reports an empty action, missing element, or invalid locator, especially when visible labels include decorative icon text.

skills.title: Return From New Group Form
skills.principle: When the target is the customer-group listing, distinguish the creation form from the listing page. Use the form’s “Back” control to return, then verify the page heading, group table, and management controls are visible before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a Magento Admin task requests the Customer Groups page but the current accessibility tree shows “New Customer Group” with form fields such as Group Name and Tax Class.

skills.title: Terminate After Verifying Target Page
skills.principle: After navigation, verify the page heading and URL match the requested destination. Once the target page is visibly loaded, report completion and terminate; do not repeat no-op actions or perform unrelated management actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the requested destination is confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive controls, such as Magento’s Customer Groups page.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus
skills.principle: Expand the Magento Admin "SALES" navigation entry, then select the visible "Invoices" submenu item. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is "Invoices" and the invoice table or record count is displayed before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires opening invoices and the current page is elsewhere. Use the observed navigation labels and verify the destination heading and invoice records after navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Invoices
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open SALES, select the Invoices entry, and verify the page heading is “Invoices” with the invoice grid visible. Once this destination is confirmed, report completion and terminate unless the task explicitly requests filtering, viewing, or modifying a specific invoice.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task only asks to navigate to the Invoices page and the accessibility tree shows the “Invoices” heading and invoice table.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Subpages
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the task-relevant submenu item, such as “Shipments.”
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL correspond to the requested destination, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requests a Sales-related page and the current observation shows the top navigation with a collapsible “SALES” entry.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Transactions
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “SALES” navigation to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the “Transactions” entry.
3. Verify the destination by checking the page heading “Transactions” and the transaction table or record count.
4. Report completion, including an empty-state count when shown, and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to reach Magento Admin payment transactions from another admin page, provided the top navigation includes “SALES” and the destination can be verified by its heading.

skills.title: Stop After Destination Confirmation
skills.principle: Once the requested admin page is reached, verify the page heading or URL matches the task, report completion, and terminate. Do not apply unrelated filters, search empty tables, or perform additional actions when the task only requires navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the target page is visibly confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive controls; no further data retrieval or modification is requested.

skills.title: Verify Available Select Options
skills.principle: When a select control shows only one option and direct selection fails, do not guess with repeated keyboard presses. Inspect the control’s actual available options and values, then select an option only if it exists. Verify the displayed value changes before saving or continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin forms when a required dropdown’s requested value is absent from the accessibility tree or a selection action reports that the option cannot be found.

skills.title: Verify Dropdown Options Before Selecting
skills.principle: Inspect the combobox’s currently available options and their labels before attempting selection. Select the requested option only when it is actually present, then verify the field value changed. If repeated attempts report that the option is missing and the displayed value remains unchanged, treat this as a configuration or prerequisite issue rather than repeatedly guessing with clicks or arrow keys.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin form requires selecting a named value from a dropdown, especially after select_option fails or the accessibility tree shows only the current option.

skills.title: Select Exclusion and Save
skills.principle:
1. In the customer-group form, locate the “Excluded Website(s)” multiselect listbox.
2. Select the target website option and confirm its accessibility state changes to selected.
3. Click “Save Customer Group.”
4. If validation reveals missing required fields, complete them before saving again; otherwise report completion only after the save action succeeds.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento customer group to exclude a website, provided the form’s required fields are populated or can be completed and the target option appears in the exclusion listbox.

skills.title: Interpret Excluded Website Selection Correctly
skills.principle: In Magento’s customer-group form, the “Excluded Website(s)” multiselect lists websites to exclude, so the target website must be selected. Select it only when its observed state is unselected, then click “Save Customer Group” and verify the saved state or confirmation. Do not toggle a correctly selected option or assume selection means inclusion.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento customer group and the target website appears in the “Excluded Website(s)” multiselect. Check its current selected state before acting, and save after making the required change.

skills.title: Retrieve Magento Order Details
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales and select Orders.
2. Search or locate the target order using its ID and customer name, then verify the matching row.
3. Select that row’s View action and read the order information page, including account, addresses, payment, shipping, items, taxes, status, and totals.
4. Report the requested details only after the order number and customer identity match.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requesting details of a specific order, when authenticated access is available and the Sales > Orders navigation and order list are accessible.

skills.title: Reinspect Before Retrying Actions
skills.principle: After any empty-action, missing-element, or 404 error, re-inspect the current accessibility tree before acting. Confirm the page is the intended section, then target a currently exposed control by its role or label. Do not reuse stale element IDs, malformed escaped selectors, or guessed URLs; verify navigation success from the resulting heading and content.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating an admin interface or searching records after an action fails, the page remains unchanged, or the resulting page shows an unexpected state such as 404.

skills.title: Navigate to Magento Order Creation
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the “SALES” navigation entry, choose “Orders,” then activate “Create New Order.” Confirm completion when the page heading indicates “New Order” or the customer-selection order-creation screen appears; stop immediately because the initiation goal is complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to initiate a new sales order from an arbitrary Magento Admin page and the “Create New Order” control is not currently visible.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Task Completion
skills.principle: Once the requested control has been clicked and the resulting page confirms the intended state, report completion and terminate. Do not repeat the action using a stale accessibility ID; after navigation, re-observe the current page before any further interaction.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for UI tasks where a click causes navigation or state change. Apply when the new page or heading visibly confirms the requested action succeeded, especially before attempting additional clicks with previously captured element IDs.

skills.title: Inspect Dropdown Options Directly
skills.principle: Open the relevant combobox and inspect every option exposed in the accessibility tree. If the expanded control shows only one option, optionally close and reopen it to confirm; then report the observed set without changing the selection.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for administrative tasks asking which values are available in a dropdown, when the form and target combobox are visible and its expanded accessibility state exposes option entries.

skills.title: Locate and Verify Customer Impersonation Logs
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers navigation menu and select “Login as Customer Log,” rather than unrelated system or account-activity pages.
2. Verify the destination heading and inspect the records count, table, and empty-state message.
3. Report the displayed activity accurately; an explicit zero-records state confirms no impersonation activity is currently logged.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing customer impersonation activity in Magento Admin, especially from an unrelated starting page. Requires access to the Customers navigation and the Login as Customer Log entry.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: Before acting, select an element from the current accessibility tree using its exact accessible name or valid bid. Do not reuse guessed icon strings, concatenate labels, or send empty actions. After each click, verify the URL or page content changed; if not, reopen the relevant navigation section and choose the specifically labeled log entry instead of repeatedly retrying malformed selectors.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin menus or any accessibility-tree interface, especially after an action returns an empty-action, missing-element, or unchanged-page error.

skills.title: Respect Exact Names on Duplicate Errors
skills.principle: When creating a uniquely named admin entity, enter the requested name and save. If the interface reports that the name already exists, do not append dates, numbers, or other text; verify the existing entity and its relevant attributes, then report that the requested entity already exists or cannot be newly created. Only claim success after observing a clear save confirmation or updated listing.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin creation form requires an exact name and saving produces a duplicate-name error, especially when changing the requested name would alter the task’s required outcome.

skills.title: Handle Duplicate Customer Group Names
skills.principle:
1. Enter the requested group name and verify the required tax class before saving.
2. After selecting “Save Customer Group,” inspect the resulting page for a success confirmation or an error such as “Customer Group already exists.”
3. If duplication is reported, do not claim creation; report that the name is unavailable and request a different name or user direction.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a customer group in Magento Admin, especially when the requested name may already exist. Apply after saving, using the displayed confirmation or validation message to determine completion.

skills.title: Use Reset to Clear Admin Forms
skills.principle: On an administrative creation or edit form, locate the visible “Reset” button and activate it rather than manually clearing each field. Treat the form as complete when its inputs return to their default or empty state, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When the task requests clearing entered information from a currently open admin form and a clearly labeled “Reset” control is present.

skills.title: Verify Form Reset Before Stopping
skills.principle: Click the form’s “Reset” control once, then inspect every editable field, selector, and multiselect. Confirm text fields are blank and choices are cleared or restored to their documented defaults. Only after this observable check report completion and terminate; do not repeatedly issue no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to clear an admin creation or edit form and a visible “Reset” control is available, especially when the initial form state or reset effect is not otherwise confirmed.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Subsections
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu link matching the requested record type, such as “Invoices.”
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, URL context, and displayed records before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating Magento Admin from an unrelated page to a Sales subsection. The top navigation must expose “SALES,” and completion is indicated by the requested subsection heading and its record-management table.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Target Page
skills.principle: After navigating to the requested admin section, verify the page heading or URL matches the target, then report completion and stop. Do not open unrelated menus or bulk actions unless the task explicitly requests an operation beyond navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the target page is visibly confirmed, such as Magento Admin showing the requested section heading and corresponding page URL.

skills.title: Stop After Verified Review
skills.principle: Navigate to the relevant admin list, inspect each available record through its details control, and verify the list count before reporting. Once all records are reviewed and the result is confirmed, send one final summary and terminate; do not perform unnecessary navigation or duplicate messages.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin tasks that require reviewing all records, especially when the list shows a definitive record count and each row provides a details or View control.

skills.title: Use Observed Navigation Targets
skills.principle: For Magento navigation, use the current accessibility tree to identify the exact visible Sales control and submit a valid, non-empty click action. After clicking, inspect the refreshed tree for the expanded submenu and select the visible Credit Memos entry. If an action errors or the page shows 404, stop repeating it, re-observe the page, and avoid guessing URLs.
skills.when_to_apply: When opening Credit Memos or another admin subsection from a Magento dashboard, especially after malformed click errors, unchanged page state, or a 404 response.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level “SALES” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu item matching the requested sales record type, such as “Transactions.”
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL correspond to the requested destination, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requests a sales-related page and the current view is elsewhere. The top-level “SALES” entry must be available and expandable in the navigation.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Page
skills.principle: Navigate through the relevant admin menu, then verify the destination by its page heading and URL. Once the requested page is visibly loaded, report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation-only tasks when the destination page is confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive content and no filtering, editing, or data extraction is requested.

skills.title: Navigate Magento to Categories
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin’s CATALOG navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu item labeled “Categories.”
