3. Confirm completion when the page heading or accessibility tree shows the Categories section and the category hierarchy is visible; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting elsewhere in Magento Admin and the task requires managing or organizing the product catalog’s category structure.

skills.title: Use Accessibility Bids for Navigation
skills.principle: When a navigation label is visible but text-based lookup fails, use the element’s current accessibility-tree bid (for example, the numeric bid on the CATALOG link). Activate it, inspect the refreshed tree for the expanded menu, then select Categories and verify the page or heading changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this in admin dashboards when a menu entry appears in the accessibility tree but clicking by its displayed label or icon returns an element-not-found error.

skills.title: Save and Verify Product Forms
skills.principle: After reaching the new-product form, fill every required field using the current accessibility-tree controls, confirm each value is correct, then click “Save.” Wait for a success message, redirect, or persisted product record before reporting completion. If a click times out but the page already changed, inspect the current state and continue rather than retrying navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When adding a product in Magento Admin or completing any multi-field catalog form, especially after a navigation timeout or when required fields are populated but the record is not yet visibly saved.

skills.title: Verify Replacement Before Saving
skills.principle: When filling product forms, verify each field’s displayed value immediately afterward. If text was appended instead of replaced, clear the field completely and re-enter the intended value, especially for unique fields such as SKU. Confirm all required values are correct, then click Save and verify the resulting success state.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento product creation or similar forms when entering multiple fields, particularly after a fill action leaves unexpected combined text or before saving a new catalog item.

skills.title: Open Magento Email Templates
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin “MARKETING” navigation entry.
2. Under “Communications,” select “Email Templates.”
3. Confirm the destination by checking the “Email Templates” heading and template table.
4. Use “Add New Template,” a template row, “Preview,” or the table filters according to the requested management operation.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing customer communication email templates in Magento Admin and the current page is elsewhere. The Marketing navigation must be available; verify the Email Templates heading before acting on templates.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Template Save
skills.principle: When managing Magento email templates, navigate through Marketing > Communications > Email Templates, perform the requested change, and verify the success message and resulting record. Once the task is confirmed complete, report completion and terminate instead of inventing additional templates, previews, or edits.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when the requested email-template operation has produced a visible confirmation such as “You saved the email template” and the updated template appears in the list.

skills.title: Use Select Option for Native Dropdowns
skills.principle: When a required native select is expanded but its option is not visibly clickable, use the select control’s option-selection operation with the option’s value or label. Then verify the control displays the chosen store or value before saving the form.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply on Magento Admin forms such as New Search when a required Store combobox exposes options in the accessibility tree but direct clicking an option fails because the option is hidden or not visible.

skills.title: Verify Search-Term Saves Before Continuing
skills.principle: Edit only the target search term, then click “Save Search” and wait for the confirmation message or updated list value. If changing a native dropdown, use option selection rather than clicking an invisible option. After the requested change is visibly persisted, stop instead of opening additional records or making speculative improvements.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing Magento Marketing > SEO & Search > Search Terms, especially after editing fields such as result count, redirect URL, or suggested-term visibility.

skills.title: Verify Current Page Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL and visible page heading against the requested destination. If they already match, report that the goal is complete and terminate with a user message; do not issue an empty or unnecessary browser action.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to a page and the initial accessibility tree already shows the requested page heading and matching destination URL.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales Submenus
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level “SALES” navigation entry from the current Magento Admin page.
2. Select the visible “Shipments” submenu item rather than relying on fixed element IDs.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading is “Shipments” and shipment records are displayed, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires reaching Shipments from another admin page and the top navigation shows a “SALES” entry. Verify the destination heading and table before concluding.

skills.title: Recover From Malformed Browser Actions
skills.principle: When a browser action repeatedly returns an empty-action error, inspect the exact emitted payload rather than retrying the same intent. Ensure the action string is syntactically complete, targets an element present in the latest accessibility tree, and uses the correct tool format. After execution, verify that the menu expanded or the page changed before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply during admin navigation when actions fail without changing the accessibility tree, especially after repeated clicks use truncated selectors, mismatched quotes, or otherwise malformed payloads.

skills.title: Verify Empty Billing Agreements State
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open SALES, select Billing Agreements, and inspect the records table. If it shows “0 records found” and “We couldn't find any records,” reset filters once to rule out filtering; if the empty state remains, report that no agreements are available and stop without attempting unsupported creation actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage Billing Agreements and the Magento Admin page is initially elsewhere or the Billing Agreements table appears empty.

skills.title: Expand Sales Menu Before Navigating
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the visible “Sales” navigation entry and inspect the updated accessibility tree. Select the “Billing Agreements” submenu link once it appears, rather than repeatedly guessing dashboard anchors or switching sections. Confirm the destination page loads before taking further action.
skills.when_to_apply: When Billing Agreements are requested from the Magento dashboard and the initial tree shows only top-level navigation entries without submenu items.

skills.title: Open Magento All Customers
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Customers navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu item labeled “All Customers.”
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading identifies the customer list and the table or customer-management controls are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When starting from another Magento Admin page and asked to view or manage customer accounts. The Customers navigation entry must be available, and completion requires the customer-list page to load.

skills.title: Verify Target Page Then Stop
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the Customers navigation, select the visible “All Customers” entry, and verify the page heading, customer grid, or URL indicates the destination loaded. Once confirmed, report completion and terminate instead of repeating clicks or no-op actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When a navigation task asks for Magento’s All Customers page and the accessibility tree shows the Customers submenu or the customer grid already loaded.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Newsletter Queue
skills.principle:
1. Open the Marketing navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Under Communications, select “Newsletter Queue.”
3. Verify the page heading and inspect the record count and table state; report whether scheduled newsletters exist, using filters when needed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage scheduled newsletters in Magento Admin, especially from an unrelated starting page. Requires access to the Marketing navigation and its Communications submenu.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Queue State
skills.principle: Navigate through Marketing → Communications → Newsletter Queue, then inspect the page heading, record count, and table state. If the queue displays the requested management page and explicitly shows zero records, treat that as the complete observable result, report it, and terminate. Do not switch to Newsletter Templates or create unrelated content unless the task explicitly requests creation.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or manage a newsletter queue and the queue page is reached, especially when its table explicitly reports no records.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Marketing Submenus
skills.principle:
1. Open the top-level "MARKETING" navigation entry from the current Magento Admin page.
2. In the expanded menu, locate "URL Rewrites" under "SEO & Search" and select it.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading is "URL Rewrites" and its rewrite table or "Add URL Rewrite" control is visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reach Magento Admin's URL Rewrites management page from another admin screen, provided the top navigation includes MARKETING and its submenu can be expanded.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When navigation actions fail, use the element’s current accessibility-tree bid rather than visible text, icon text, or guessed labels. Re-read the tree, target the observed navigation link, and verify that the URL or menu state changes before continuing. If the same action fails repeatedly, stop retrying and choose a different evidence-based route.
skills.when_to_apply: Use this in BrowserGym admin navigation when a visible menu item is present but text-based clicks produce empty-action or element-not-found errors, or when the page remains unchanged after repeated attempts.

skills.title: Verify Pending Reviews Before Acting
skills.principle: Open the admin area's Marketing menu, select User Content → Pending Reviews, and inspect the results table. If it displays zero records or “We couldn't find any records,” report that no approvals are currently needed and stop; otherwise, manage the listed reviews.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to approve or manage pending customer reviews in Magento Admin, especially from an unrelated starting page. Confirm the Pending Reviews page and its record count before taking review actions.

skills.title: Handle Empty Pending Review Lists
skills.principle: Open Marketing > User Content > Pending Reviews and verify the page heading and record count. Reset filters once; if the table still shows zero records, report that no reviews require approval and stop. Use bulk status actions only when review rows are present and selected.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing Magento product reviews and the Pending Reviews page displays “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records,” especially after resetting filters.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Widgets
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin navigation’s “CONTENT” section.
2. Under “Elements,” select “Widgets.”
3. Confirm the destination by checking the “Widgets” heading, widget list, and “Add Widget” button; stop once these are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task requires accessing widgets or adding dynamic store content, and the admin navigation is available.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Widgets
skills.principle: When the requested admin page is visible, verify its heading or URL matches the goal, then report completion and terminate. Do not infer that “access” requires creating or editing a widget unless the task explicitly requests a new widget or configuration.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks such as accessing Magento Content > Elements > Widgets, when the Widgets page heading and widget list are already visible.

skills.title: Disambiguate Customers by Group
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Customers → All Customers and search for the target name. If multiple matching rows appear, select the row whose Group matches the requested customer group, then read the Phone and ZIP columns directly from that row. Report both values only after confirming the group and identity match.
skills.when_to_apply: When retrieving contact or address fields for a named customer and duplicate names may exist. Requires access to Magento Admin’s customer grid and a requested customer group.

skills.title: Follow Semantic Navigation Targets
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree to select the element whose label and role match the task, not a nearby or stale identifier. For Magento customer lookup, expand CUSTOMERS, activate the observed “Customer Groups” link, then confirm the page or URL changes before continuing. If the state remains unchanged, re-inspect the tree and correct the target rather than repeating the same click.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating nested admin menus and the intended page does not open, especially when nearby menu items have different labels or accessibility identifiers.

skills.title: Verify Existing Scope Before Changing
skills.principle: Read the current scope control value first. If it already matches the requested scope, report that the setting is satisfied and stop. Otherwise, open the scope menu, select the requested option, and verify the control displays the new value before completing.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a dashboard or admin-page scope, store view, or similar selector, especially when the observed control may already show the requested value.

skills.title: Reload Dashboard Data
skills.principle: From any Magento Admin page, use the navigation entry labeled “DASHBOARD” to open the dashboard. Locate and click the “Reload Data” button, then confirm completion when a success notification such as “We updated lifetime statistic.” appears. Report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to refresh or reload Magento Admin Dashboard data and the current page is elsewhere in the admin panel. Requires access to the dashboard navigation and its “Reload Data” control.

skills.title: Verify Reload Completion Once
skills.principle: On the Magento Admin Dashboard, click the “Reload Data” button once. Wait for the dashboard response and confirm the success notification “We updated lifetime statistic.” Once this confirmation appears, report completion and stop; do not repeatedly click an unchanged button.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to reload Magento dashboard data and the dashboard visibly contains the “Reload Data” control. Use the success notification as the completion signal before terminating.

skills.title: Open the System Navigation Menu
skills.principle: From the Customers admin page, activate the top-level “SYSTEM” navigation entry. Confirm completion when its expanded menu appears with system categories such as Data Transfer, Extensions, Tools, or Permissions, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the task asks to enter or open the System section from a Magento Admin Customers page, and the top navigation visibly contains the “SYSTEM” entry.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Menu Expansion
skills.principle: Click the relevant top-level section once, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. If its submenu appears, treat the section as entered and stop; do not repeatedly click the focused or highlighted label. If a specific destination is required, select the appropriate visible submenu item and verify the resulting page.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin sidebar where top-level labels expand menus instead of directly changing the URL, especially when the clicked section becomes focused or highlighted.

skills.title: Find Account Creation Date
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open Customers > All Customers, search the target customer, and inspect the matching row’s “Customer Since” column. If multiple names match, distinguish the correct account using email or other identifying fields before reporting the displayed date and time.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked when a customer account was created and the Customers grid is available, especially when search results may contain multiple customers with the same name.

skills.title: Open Magento Customer Email List
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin “CUSTOMERS” navigation.
2. Select “All Customers.”
3. Verify the customer grid contains an “Email” column and visible email values; use pagination if needed to inspect additional records.
4. Once the list is displayed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view customer email addresses in Magento Admin and the navigation menu exposes “CUSTOMERS” with an “All Customers” entry.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Reviewing All Customers
skills.principle: On the Magento Admin Customers page, inspect the “Active filters” area before collecting a complete customer list. Click “Clear all” (or remove each filter), then verify the table count and pagination represent the full customer set. Read the Email column across every page, and only report completion after confirming no restrictive filters remain.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view or collect data for all customers and the Customers grid shows active keyword or attribute filters, a limited record count, or pagination.

skills.title: Find Customers by Group
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Customers list rather than relying on the customer-group edit page, which only shows group properties.
2. Clear any pre-existing keyword or active filters before searching.
3. Filter the customer table by the requested group, or inspect its Group column across every page.
4. Collect each matching customer’s name, ID, and email, verifying the result count and pagination before reporting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking which customers belong to a named customer group, especially when the group edit page lacks a member list and the Customers table provides Group, ID, Name, and Email columns.

skills.title: Use the Actual Group Filter Control
skills.principle: On Magento’s Customers grid, distinguish the “Filters” button from the adjacent active-filters container and the “Search” button by accessible role and label. Click the actual Filters button, set the Group field to the requested group, apply the filter, then read customer names from resulting rows and verify the displayed group and record count.
skills.when_to_apply: When identifying customers in a specific group from the Magento Customers grid, especially when nearby accessibility-tree elements have similar positions or unlabeled layout containers.

skills.title: Filter Customers by Group
skills.principle:
1. Open the Customers list from the Customers navigation section.
2. Open Filters, set the Group dropdown to the requested customer group, and select Apply Filters.
3. Confirm the active-filter indicator names that group, the record count updates, and every visible row shows the matching group; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requires viewing customers belonging to a specific group and the Customers list provides a Filters control with a Group dropdown and Apply Filters button.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Targets
skills.principle: When an element lookup fails, do not repeatedly wait while the accessibility tree remains unchanged. Reinspect the latest tree and target the element by its current semantic label or role, avoiding copied icon text and stale identifiers. If navigation controls remain nonfunctional, use an available direct navigation route or alternate relevant control, then verify the destination page.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when a visible Magento Admin navigation item appears in the accessibility tree but clicking a copied label or icon string raises an element-not-found error and subsequent observations remain unchanged.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Bulk Update
skills.principle: After choosing the intended bulk action, verify the success banner and updated-record count. Once the requested change is confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not reopen Actions or perform further clicks, since selection may reset and trigger a misleading “no items selected” dialog.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on admin list pages after a bulk operation. Apply when a success notification explicitly reports that records were updated and the requested state change is complete.

skills.title: Stop After Confirmed Bulk Update
skills.principle: After applying a customer bulk action, inspect the refreshed page for a success confirmation such as “record(s) were updated.” If the requested operation and intended selection are confirmed, report completion and terminate; do not select additional rows or reuse element references from the previous page state.
skills.when_to_apply: When managing customers through an admin grid and a bulk action produces a success message or refreshed result page confirming the requested newsletter subscription.

skills.title: Verify Before Editing Customer Records
skills.principle: Open the customer listing, locate the target by name and distinguishing details, and inspect the relevant field in its row. If the current value already matches the requested value, report that no update is needed and stop; otherwise open that record’s Edit control, change the field, save, and verify the result.
skills.when_to_apply: When updating a customer attribute in Magento Admin and the Customers table exposes the target record and relevant field, especially when duplicate names may require checking additional identifying details.

skills.title: Verify Shared Address Updates Before Editing
skills.principle: In Magento customer addresses, update and save the relevant address, then inspect both Default Billing Address and Default Shipping Address. If both display the requested phone number, treat the task as complete and stop; do not open another address dialog or make unnecessary edits. If one remains outdated, edit only that address, save it, and verify again.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing a customer phone number in Magento and billing and shipping addresses may be linked or shared. Apply after saving the first address, using the displayed phone values as the completion check.

skills.title: Validate Actions Before Repeating
skills.principle: After an action returns an empty-action or parsing error, inspect the emitted command for truncated quotes or malformed syntax and resend one complete, valid action. Verify the page state changed before retrying. For customer-grid configuration, navigate to the actual Customers management grid rather than repeatedly targeting a dashboard widget.
skills.when_to_apply: When BrowserGym reports an empty action, parsing error, or unchanged page after interacting with a dashboard control, especially when the task requires editing a management grid rather than viewing dashboard data.

skills.title: Verify Customer CSV Export
skills.principle: Open Customers > All Customers, apply the requested filters, and select Export with CSV chosen. Confirm a successful download or an accessible exported file before reporting completion; when download status is unavailable, state that export was initiated without claiming a verified file.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting customer records from the Magento Admin grid and the requested filters are already applied.

skills.title: Clear Filters Before Customer Export
skills.principle: On the Magento Customers grid, inspect “Active filters” before exporting. For a complete customer list, click “Clear all,” confirm the grid shows the unfiltered record set, then click “Export,” keep “CSV” selected, and click the modal’s “Export” button. Confirm the download through an observable browser download or changed UI state before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting all customers from a Magento customer grid, especially when the page shows an active keyword or other filter. Clear filters first unless the task explicitly requests a filtered subset.

skills.title: Review Magento Credit Memos
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales and select Credit Memos.
2. Check the records-found count and read each row’s order, date, customer, status, and refunded amount.
3. Open each row’s View action to verify order details, refunded items, totals, and memo history.
4. Report the verified findings and stop once all records are reviewed.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing refunded orders in Magento Admin and the Sales navigation exposes Credit Memos. Use the listing count to determine whether all records have been covered.

skills.title: Use the Direct Credit Memos Link
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the SALES navigation and select the visible “Credit Memos” entry directly. Confirm navigation by checking that the page heading and URL represent the credit-memo grid, then review its records. Do not route through Orders or infer refunds from unrelated order statuses such as “Canceled” when the dedicated credit-memo page is available.
skills.when_to_apply: When reviewing refunded orders in Magento Admin and the expanded SALES menu visibly contains “Credit Memos,” especially if the current page is unrelated to sales records.

skills.title: Verify Billing Agreements Status
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Sales menu and select “Billing Agreements.”
2. Confirm the page shows the billing-agreements table and inspect its record count and empty-state message.
3. Report whether agreements exist, using the displayed count; when it shows zero records and no records found, state that none are configured.
4. After reporting the verified result, terminate without unnecessary actions.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check payment-processor billing agreements in Magento Admin, especially from an unrelated starting page. Requires access to the Sales navigation and the Billing Agreements listing.

skills.title: Use Visible Navigation and Filter Controls
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the visible SALES menu and choose the explicitly labeled “Billing Agreements” entry. On the resulting grid, interact with the visible status combobox itself, not its hidden option nodes; select a status, click “Search,” and verify the record count or empty-state message before concluding.
skills.when_to_apply: When checking payment processor billing agreements in Magento Admin, especially after a menu navigation changes the page and accessibility-tree element IDs or option visibility are unstable.

skills.title: Save Inventory Status Changes
skills.principle: On a product edit page, update the Quantity field, set Stock Status to the appropriate value (such as “In Stock”), then click “Save.” Confirm completion by checking that the edited values persist and a success message such as “You saved the product” appears before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when managing a product’s inventory and the edit page exposes Quantity, Stock Status, and Save controls. Verify the saved state rather than assuming field edits were committed.

skills.title: Navigate to the Section Landing Page
skills.principle: When asked to navigate to an admin section, distinguish being inside a subsection from reaching the section entry point. Open the section navigation (for example, CUSTOMERS), choose its relevant landing or list entry, and verify the resulting heading or URL. Do not repeatedly use noop or guess with unrelated controls such as view-management buttons.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when the current page shows a subsection such as customer-group editing while the task requests the broader Customers area. A section label or breadcrumb alone does not confirm that the landing page has been reached.

skills.title: Expand Content Navigation
skills.principle: Click the admin navigation entry labeled “CONTENT,” then verify its submenu expands and exposes the relevant management links, such as Pages, Blocks, Widgets, and Design Configuration. Once these options are visibly available, report navigation complete rather than opening an individual subsection.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task asks to reach the Content area and the navigation tree shows a collapsed “CONTENT” entry. Completion requires observing the expanded submenu with the requested management options.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Requested Section
skills.principle: When the task asks only to navigate, expand the relevant navigation section, verify its submenu or destination is visible, and stop. Do not open creation forms or modify records unless the instruction explicitly requests those changes.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply to admin-navigation tasks where the requested destination is already available in the current menu, especially when expanding a section reveals management links such as Pages, Blocks, Widgets, or Design.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Reports Categories
skills.principle: Click the Magento Admin left-navigation “REPORTS” entry to expand its categorized submenu. Select the report matching the requested analytics area, such as “Orders” under Sales or a report under Products, Customers, or Marketing. Confirm completion when the page heading and URL identify the selected report.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requires opening Magento sales, product, customer, or marketing analytics and the Reports navigation entry is visible.

skills.title: Use Valid Accessibility Target IDs
skills.principle: When a click returns an empty-action error, do not retry stale or mismatched element IDs. Re-read the current accessibility tree, identify the target by its visible label and current ID, then click that target and verify the URL or page heading changed. If the labeled navigation item is only a placeholder, use the observed functional link instead.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin from the dashboard and a Reports or Advanced Reporting control is visible, especially after a click fails or the page remains unchanged.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Select the navigation link using its current accessibility-tree bid or accessible name, not the icon glyph shown inside its label. After clicking the Stores navigation entry, inspect the updated tree for its submenu or destination and continue from the newly exposed controls. If the action fails, re-read the current tree before retrying rather than repeating a stale selector.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin sections and the visible link includes an icon plus text, especially after an action error or page refresh that may invalidate element bids.

skills.title: Open Magento Product Filters
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Catalog navigation and select Products.
2. On the Products grid, activate the Filters control.
3. Confirm the filter panel is visible, including fields such as Name, SKU, ID, Price, Status, and Visibility; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access product filters in Magento Admin, starting from another admin page and requiring the filter form to be opened rather than search criteria applied.

skills.title: Open Products Before Searching
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand the CATALOG navigation entry, then select its Products submenu item rather than repeatedly clicking the parent. Verify the product-grid page appears, including product-listing controls or a changed Products URL, before looking for filters. If the page remains unchanged, reassess the navigation state and choose the visible submenu link.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to access product filters from an arbitrary Magento Admin page and expanding CATALOG reveals Products and Categories submenu links.

skills.title: Stop After Reaching Target Details
skills.principle: Once the requested item’s details page is open and its editable fields are visible, verify the page heading and relevant form contents, report successful access, and terminate. Do not begin unrelated administrative actions after the task goal is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to an admin list item’s view/edit page and the accessibility tree shows the target heading, editable fields, and the relevant save control.

skills.title: Verify Search Term Row Before Editing
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, expand Marketing and select Search Terms. Identify the target row by its visible Search Query, then activate that row’s associated Edit link. On the edit page, verify the heading and Search Query match the target before changing fields or saving; afterward confirm the success message and updated list entry.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a specific search term from the Search Terms table, especially when multiple rows have identical Edit links and accessibility IDs may shift between observations.

skills.title: Open and Verify Dashboard Tab
skills.principle: Locate the dashboard tab matching the requested view by its visible label, click its associated tab/link, and wait for the panel to load. Confirm completion when the tab is selected or expanded and its expected content, such as a data table, is visible; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin dashboard task requests viewing a specific dashboard widget or tab, and the accessibility tree exposes labeled tabs or links with dynamically loaded panels.

skills.title: Verify File Availability Before Uploading
skills.principle:
1. Navigate through Content to Media Gallery and activate “Upload Image.”
2. Use `upload_file` only with a real, accessible image path supplied by the environment or user.
3. If the path returns ENOENT, do not retry guessed filenames; obtain a valid path or explain that manual file selection is required.
4. Confirm the new image appears in the gallery before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When uploading an image through Magento Media Gallery or another file chooser, especially when the agent lacks direct access to the user’s local files.

skills.title: Use an Existing File Path
skills.principle: Before selecting an upload control, ensure a real image file path is available. Open the Media Gallery’s “Upload Image” control, then use `upload_file` with that exact existing path—not a guessed filename. After submission, verify that the image appears or a success confirmation is shown; if no valid path is available, request one instead of retrying placeholders.
skills.when_to_apply: When uploading an image through Magento Admin’s Media Gallery or another file chooser, especially when the required local file path has not been supplied or verified.

skills.title: Verify Dropdown Selection Before Saving
skills.principle: On an admin edit form, inspect the tax-class combobox’s actual available options before choosing. Select the requested label only if it exists; otherwise investigate the option list or correct target group rather than guessing with repeated arrow presses. Confirm the field value visibly changed to the requested class, then click “Save Customer Group” and verify the success message.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a customer group or similar record and the requested dropdown option is missing from the accessibility tree, selection times out, or keyboard navigation leaves the displayed value unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Dropdown Options Before Selecting
skills.principle: Use the control according to its element type: native `<select>` fields require `select_option`, not text filling. Before retrying, inspect the currently exposed options and confirm the requested value exists. If absent, resolve the missing prerequisite through the relevant configuration page or report that it cannot be selected; do not repeat unsuccessful guesses. After selecting an available value, click the form’s save button and verify the persisted value.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing an admin form with a dropdown whose requested value is not visible or selection attempts time out. Confirm the option exists before acting, especially when the task may require prior configuration.

skills.title: Verify Existing Exclusion Before Editing
skills.principle: Inspect the customer group’s “Excluded Website(s)” multiselect before changing it. If the target website appears selected, treat the exclusion as already satisfied, avoid redundant edits or saving, and report the confirmed current state.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing a Magento customer group and the requested website exclusion may already exist; first verify the target option’s selected state in the “Excluded Website(s)” listbox.

skills.title: Edit Multiselect Exclusions and Save
skills.principle: On the correct customer-group edit page, locate the excluded-websites multiselect and click the selected target website to deselect it. Then click “Save Customer Group.” Confirm completion from the resulting success message, such as “You saved the customer group,” before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when changing a website exclusion for an existing Magento customer group and the target website appears selected in the “Excluded Website(s)” multiselect. Ensure the group identity is verified before editing.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Orders by Visible ID
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin SALES menu and select Orders.
2. Locate the target order by matching its ID in the orders table, rather than relying on row position.
3. Activate that row’s View link.
4. Confirm the order detail page heading and information panel show the requested order ID before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks asking to view a specific order when starting from another admin page and the SALES navigation is available. Verify the detail page heading matches the requested ID.

skills.title: Verify Order ID Before Viewing Details
skills.principle:
1. Open Sales > Orders rather than selecting a dashboard table container.
2. Use the orders grid’s Order ID filter or search field to locate the requested order.
3. Open the matching order row and verify the page heading and “Order #” exactly match the requested ID before reviewing details.
4. If they differ, return to the grid and continue searching instead of scrolling the wrong order page.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin opens on the dashboard and the task requests a specific order ID, especially when “Last Orders” shows no order-ID column or only recent orders.

skills.title: Search and Open an Order
skills.principle:
1. Open the admin Sales navigation and choose Orders.
2. Enter the target order identifier in “Search by keyword” and submit Search.
3. Confirm the results show the matching order, then select its row’s “View” link.
4. Verify the order detail page heading or information panel contains the requested identifier before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when asked to view a specific order and the order identifier is available. The Orders grid must provide keyword search and a row-level “View” action.

skills.title: Simplify Messages After Action Errors
skills.principle: When sending a completion message repeatedly returns an empty-action or formatting error, retry with a concise plain-text message. Remove escaped newlines, nested quotes, and unnecessary punctuation while preserving the verified target and key details. Stop once the message is accepted.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after the page already displays the requested record and the messaging action fails with an empty-action or similar formatting error.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: Read the current accessibility tree and act on its numeric element bid, not an icon glyph, serialized label, or guessed text. From a customer-group edit page, use the visible “Back” control to return to the groups list, then locate the target group and open its details. Reinspect the tree after each navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: When Magento Admin navigation actions fail with empty-action or missing-element errors despite a visible menu item, especially on customer-group edit pages. Prerequisite: the latest accessibility tree exposes numeric bids for actionable controls.

skills.title: Verify the Target Group Before Inspecting
skills.principle: First compare the page heading and Group Name field with the requested customer group. If they differ, return to the customer-group list and open the matching group. Only then inspect the “Excluded Website(s)” multi-select, using its exposed option labels and selected states rather than repeatedly clicking or waiting for expansion.
skills.when_to_apply: When answering an admin question about a specific customer group and the current edit page may belong to a different group. Confirm the target identity before reading or changing fields.

skills.title: Verify Saved Rename Before Stopping
skills.principle: Edit the target customer group’s Group Name field, replace the old name with the requested name, and click “Save Customer Group.” Confirm completion from the success message and the updated name in the resulting list or page title, then report completion and stop without further navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin customer-group renaming when the edit form is available. After saving, verify both a save confirmation and the requested name before taking any additional action.

skills.title: Use Fresh Locators After Navigation
skills.principle: After any navigation or save, re-read the current accessibility tree and locate controls by their visible role or label. If the target value already matches, verify the list and completion message, then stop. Otherwise edit the field, activate the current “Save Customer Group” control, and confirm the success message and updated row before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing Magento customer groups or similar admin records, especially after navigation, redirects, or stale-element errors make previously observed element references unreliable.

skills.title: Verify Target and Saved Field Value
skills.principle:
1. Locate the customer group by exact name; do not substitute a merely similar row.
2. Open Tax Class and choose a visibly different option from the current value.
3. Confirm the combobox value changed before clicking “Save Customer Group.”
4. After saving, verify the success message and reopen the target if necessary to confirm the persisted tax class.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when editing a Magento customer group or similar admin record where names may be similar and keyboard selection may leave the original value unchanged.

skills.title: Verify Dropdown Selection Before Saving
skills.principle: After opening a form dropdown, choose a visibly available option and confirm the field’s displayed value changes from its original value. If keyboard navigation leaves the value unchanged, inspect or reopen the option list and select explicitly; only then click the save button and verify the success message.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when editing an admin record with a dropdown whose options are missing or dynamically rendered in the accessibility tree, especially when the requested target record must be distinguished from similarly named records.

skills.title: Deselect Multiselect Options Correctly
skills.principle: In a multiselect listbox, do not use a selection action to remove an already-selected option; it selects or preserves that option. Use the UI’s deselection interaction (such as modifier-clicking the selected option), then verify its state is no longer selected before saving. Reopen the record after saving and confirm the option remains deselected.
skills.when_to_apply: When editing an admin form with a multiselect field, especially when removing an existing exclusion. Apply only after confirming the exact target record and observing that the option is currently selected.

skills.title: Save and Verify Customer Group Changes
skills.principle: On the customer group edit page, locate the role-labeled "Save Customer Group" button and activate it. After navigation or refresh, verify the visible success notification stating that the customer group was saved; once present, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When changes are pending on a Magento Admin customer group edit form and the save control is visible. Use the success notification as the completion prerequisite before taking no further actions.

skills.title: Verify Target Before Saving
skills.principle:
1. Confirm the page is the edit form for the requested customer group by matching its name and editable fields.
2. If on the groups list, locate the target row by name and activate that row’s “Edit” link.
3. Click the visible “Save Customer Group” button on the edit form, not a stale element ID or success message.
4. Confirm navigation back to the list and the “You saved the customer group.” notification before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When saving changes to a Magento customer group and the current page may be a list, stale edit form, or post-save state. Verify the target group first and require the save confirmation before claiming success.

skills.title: Use Current Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After each navigation attempt, inspect the refreshed accessibility tree before acting again. Target the element’s current accessibility bid, not its displayed label or icon text. If navigation succeeds, stop retrying the previous action and locate the requested submenu or page from the new observation, verifying the heading or URL before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin menus or any BrowserGym page where clicks report missing elements, especially after the URL or page heading changes.

skills.title: Open and Verify Customer Login Log
skills.principle:
1. Expand the Magento Admin CUSTOMERS menu and select “Login as Customer Log.”
2. If an unexpected or invalid date filter is active, use “Clear all” to remove it.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, record count, and table empty-state or login-history rows.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to view Magento’s admin-as-customer login history from an arbitrary Admin page, especially when the log opens with an invalid or unintended filter.

skills.title: Navigate Nested Admin Menus
skills.principle:
1. Identify the relevant top-level navigation entry from the accessibility tree and activate it to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the submenu item matching the requested management page.
3. Confirm completion by checking the page heading, URL meaning, and presence of the expected list or management controls; then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task starts on a detail or edit page and requires reaching a broader management list through nested navigation menus.

skills.title: Use Valid Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: When navigating from an admin detail form, prefer the visible role-specific control already present, such as the “Back” button, to return to the list. If using navigation, target the element’s numeric accessibility bid from the current tree (for example, the Customers link), not icon text, labels, or guessed indices. Verify the URL or page heading changes before continuing.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an admin task starts on an individual record form and requests the encompassing list page, especially after locator errors or when navigation labels include decorative Unicode icons.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Sales to Orders
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin SALES navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Select the Orders link.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading is “Orders” and the orders grid is visible, then report completion without further actions.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when starting elsewhere in Magento Admin and asked to view customer orders. Ensure the SALES menu is available; completion is indicated by the Orders heading and visible order table.

skills.title: Clear Active Filters Before Concluding Empty
skills.principle: When an admin grid shows no records, inspect the “Active filters” area before concluding the dataset is empty. Remove restrictive filters with “Clear all” (or reset individual filter chips), then verify the refreshed record count and table rows. Only report that nothing exists after checking the unfiltered view.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin list pages such as Invoices when “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records” appears, especially when a status or keyword filter is visibly active.

skills.title: Verify Menu State Before Clicking
skills.principle: Use the current accessibility tree after every navigation action. If the target submenu link is visible, click that link directly. If only the parent section is visible, activate the parent and wait for the submenu to appear, then re-read the tree and select the target by its current role or label. Do not reuse stale element identifiers across pages; confirm completion by checking the destination heading or URL.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating hierarchical admin menus, especially after a page transition or failed click, and the target submenu may be hidden or represented by different accessibility identifiers.

skills.title: Verify Empty Transaction Results
skills.principle:
1. Expand the admin Sales menu and select the Transactions entry.
2. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and transaction-table columns.
3. Report the displayed record count; if it shows “0 records found” or “We couldn't find any records,” state that no transactions are currently available.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check transaction history in a Magento admin panel, after reaching the Sales navigation and opening Transactions; use the table count and empty-state message as completion evidence.

skills.title: Refresh Element References After Filtering
skills.principle: After changing a grid filter, reread the current accessibility tree before clicking or filling anything else. Use the newly observed control reference for Search or Reset Filter, because filtering can rerender the grid and invalidate earlier element identifiers. Confirm the resulting record count or table state after submitting.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on Magento Admin transaction-history grids or similar dynamic tables when applying filters causes controls or grid elements to receive new accessibility references.

skills.title: Recognize When Already On Target Page
skills.principle: Check the current URL and page heading before navigating. If they already identify the requested destination, report that the goal is complete and stop; do not perform redundant navigation.
skills.when_to_apply: For navigation tasks when the initial accessibility tree includes the requested page’s distinctive heading, URL, or other reliable destination indicator.

skills.title: Use Current Catalog Menu Targets
skills.principle: Open the visible “CATALOG” menu, then select the currently displayed “Products” or “Categories” link by its role and text. Do not reuse accessibility IDs after navigation, because IDs can refer to different menu items or become stale. Confirm the destination heading or URL before continuing; once the requested Catalog section is open, stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating Magento Admin’s Catalog menu, especially after using back navigation or switching pages, when accessibility IDs may have been reassigned and the task only requires reaching Products or Categories.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Content Pages
skills.principle:
1. Open the Magento Admin “CONTENT” navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Under “Elements,” select “Pages” rather than a neighboring design option.
3. Confirm completion when the page heading is “Pages” and the interface shows page-management controls such as “Add New Page” and the pages table.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when asked to reach Magento’s Content area for website page management, starting from another Admin section and requiring confirmation that the Pages interface is open.

skills.title: Stop at the Requested Content Section
skills.principle: When the task asks only to navigate to Content, click CONTENT, verify its submenu appears, and stop once the relevant section is visible. Select a subsection such as Pages only when explicitly requested; do not add, edit, or save content as an assumed next step.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin navigation tasks whose goal is reaching the Content section or exposing its Elements, Media, or Design submenu, without a separate content-creation instruction.

skills.title: Select a Concrete System Destination
skills.principle: When a top-level “SYSTEM” navigation control expands a flyout but keeps the dashboard URL, treat it as a menu toggle, not completed navigation. Choose the relevant concrete submenu link—such as Cache Management, Index Management, Import, or User Roles—then verify the destination URL or page heading changed before proceeding.
skills.when_to_apply: Use in Magento Admin when clicking a top-level section expands submenu options while the current page remains the dashboard. A specific system tool or settings destination must be selected to complete navigation.

skills.title: Use Notification Dropdown’s See All
skills.principle:
1. Locate the admin notification indicator, typically a bell or count link, and activate it.
2. If a notification dropdown appears, select its “See All” link rather than treating the dropdown as the full page.
3. Confirm the destination by checking the page heading and notification table, then summarize the visible alerts and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to check system alerts in a Magento Admin interface and the notification indicator opens a preview dropdown instead of immediately showing the dedicated Notifications page.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Acting Further
skills.principle: After activating a navigation control, inspect the updated page title, URL, heading, and relevant content. If they confirm the requested destination and its data is visible, report completion and stop. Do not click notification details or other links unless the task explicitly requires inspecting a specific alert.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when navigating an admin interface to a requested page, especially when the initial click already produces a page whose heading and URL match the task.

skills.title: Open the Matching Shipment Record
skills.principle:
1. In the shipments table, locate the row whose Shipment value exactly matches the requested identifier.
2. Activate that row’s associated “View” link, not a neighboring row’s control.
3. Confirm completion when the destination page heading displays the requested shipment identifier and its detail sections are visible.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin shipments list is open and the requested shipment may be among several similarly formatted rows. Verify the identifier before selecting the row’s “View” control.

skills.title: Terminate After Detail Page Loads
skills.principle: After selecting the target record’s “View” action, verify the destination page shows the record identifier and detail sections. Once those elements are visible, treat the task as complete, report completion, and terminate instead of issuing repeated no-op waits.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin-list task asks you to open a record’s details and the resulting page visibly contains the requested identifier and relevant detail content.

skills.title: Confirm Export Format and Download
skills.principle:
1. On the relevant administrative list page, click the primary “Export” control to reveal format options.
2. Preserve the requested or default format when it matches the task, such as CSV.
3. Click the dialog’s secondary “Export” confirmation button to initiate the download, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when exporting a complete administrative table and an Export control opens a format-selection dialog. Ensure the displayed default format satisfies the requested output before confirming.

skills.title: Verify Two-Stage Export Completion
skills.principle:
1. Click the list’s “Export” control to open format options.
2. Keep the requested format selected, then activate the dialog’s separate “Export” button.
3. Confirm the dialog closes or a download/notification appears; if it remains open, re-target and activate the dialog button rather than waiting repeatedly.
4. Stop only after observable completion.
skills.when_to_apply: When exporting a table from an admin list where “Export” first opens a format dialog and a second “Export” control performs the download.

skills.title: Verify Current Location Before Navigating
skills.principle: Check the current URL, page heading, and relevant navigation link before clicking. If they already identify the requested destination, avoid redundant navigation, report that the goal is complete, and terminate.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial accessibility tree or page state may already show the requested section, such as a matching URL and heading.

skills.title: Stop After Verifying Navigation
skills.principle: Click the requested navigation link once, then inspect the resulting page. If the URL or page heading confirms the target section, report completion and terminate; do not click the same already-selected link repeatedly.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a navigation task reaches a page whose URL, heading, or main content clearly matches the requested destination, especially when the link remains visible in a persistent admin navigation bar.

skills.title: Verify Expanded Navigation Menus
skills.principle: Click the requested navigation entry, then inspect the updated accessibility tree. Confirm completion by checking that the entry is focused or active and its submenu options are visible. Report the visible categories or links and stop once the requested section is confirmed open.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for admin navigation tasks where clicking a top-level menu may expand an inline submenu rather than change the page URL. The updated tree must show the requested menu and its child entries.

skills.title: Recognize Expanded Navigation Menus
skills.principle: Click the section’s navigation control using its current accessibility-tree bid, then inspect the updated tree. If the section expands and reveals its submenu categories, treat that as successful exploration; do not repeatedly click the parent or assume a URL change is required.
skills.when_to_apply: When a task asks to explore an admin navigation section and clicking its visible heading leaves the page URL unchanged but exposes submenu content such as Promotions, Communications, or SEO & Search.

skills.title: Refresh UI State Before Applying Filters
skills.principle: After opening the shipment-list Filters panel, re-read the current accessibility tree and target controls by their labels or roles, not stale element IDs. Enter the requested criteria, then click “Apply Filters” only while that button is visible. Confirm completion by checking that the panel closes and the list or record count reflects the applied filters.
skills.when_to_apply: When filtering a Magento shipment or similar admin grid, especially after a click changes visibility or causes a timeout, stale locator error, or refreshed accessibility tree.

skills.title: Verify Shipment Records Before Ranking
skills.principle: Open the relevant order’s Shipments tab and inspect the results grid. If shipment rows exist, compare their Total Quantity values and identify the largest. If the grid states “We couldn't find any records,” report that no shipments exist instead of inventing a maximum.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to find the shipment with the highest quantity in Magento Admin and an order detail page provides a Shipments tab. Confirm the tab’s selected state and resulting grid before answering.

skills.title: Use Live Table Evidence
skills.principle: Compare every value in the target column, then identify the corresponding row and activate its current semantic control, such as the row’s “View” link. After navigation, verify the detail page heading or matching record identifier and report it. Never reuse stale accessibility bids or keep scrolling once the target is confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: When finding a maximum or minimum record in an admin table, especially when opening its details. First ensure all relevant rows are loaded and use the current accessibility tree to locate the matching row control.

skills.title: Inspect Shipment Details Directly
skills.principle:
1. In the shipments table, identify the row whose Order # matches the requested order.
2. Activate that row’s View link, then locate the “Shipping and Tracking Information” section on the shipment details page.
3. Read and report the shipping method and Total Shipping Charges exactly as displayed; stop once both values are confirmed.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin shipment inquiries when the shipments list is available and the target order can be matched by its Order #.

skills.title: Inspect and Report Shipment Details
skills.principle: After opening the target shipment, read the accessibility tree directly. Extract the visible shipping method, charges, shipping address, shipped items, and any tracking row values. Distinguish table headers and empty tracking-entry fields from existing data. Once the requested details are confirmed or absent, report the result and stop; do not repeat scrolling or focusing.
skills.when_to_apply: When viewing a Magento Admin shipment page and the target order or shipment details are already loaded in the accessibility tree, especially when tracking fields may be empty.

skills.title: Verify Sales Page Before Opening Records
skills.principle:
1. Expand SALES and activate the link whose accessible name is exactly “Shipments,” not a neighboring menu item.
2. Confirm the page heading and URL identify Shipments before interacting with the table.
3. Locate the target shipment row by its displayed number, then activate that row’s “View” link—not its checkbox or surrounding cell.
4. Confirm the resulting heading and shipment-specific details before reporting completion.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin tasks requiring a specific order, invoice, shipment, or credit memo. After each navigation, the page heading and accessible labels must match the requested record type before selecting table controls.

skills.title: Read Shipment Shipping Address
skills.principle:
1. In the Shipments table, locate the row matching the requested shipment identifier and open its details using the row’s View control.
2. On the shipment details page, find the “Shipping Address” section and read the displayed recipient, street, locality, region, postal code, country, and phone.
3. Report those values to the user; do not open the address “Edit” page when merely checking information.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for Magento Admin shipment lookup tasks when the shipment list is visible and the goal is to inspect, not modify, the shipping address.

skills.title: Use Observed Accessibility Bids
skills.principle: After each page update, select controls using the current accessibility-tree bid or a verified role/name locator. Do not pass visible text as a bid. For Magento order details, open the target order, then activate the observed “Shipments” tab/link and verify the resulting shipment details before reporting the address.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento admin control is visible in the accessibility tree but clicks fail with “Could not find element” errors, especially while navigating from an order view to shipment information.

skills.title: Apply Grid Column Changes Correctly
skills.principle: Open the grid’s “Columns” menu and select each requested unchecked column. Close the menu by toggling “Columns” or clicking outside, not “Cancel,” which discards pending selections. Verify completion by checking that the requested labels appear as table headers and their cells are populated.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring visible columns in a Magento Admin data grid, after the requested column options are available in the open “Columns” menu.

skills.title: Verify Column Changes Before Closing
skills.principle: On an admin grid’s Columns menu, toggle the requested column checkboxes and inspect the grid or visible-column count for immediate application. Do not treat “Cancel” as Save: clicking it can discard the changes. After confirming the target columns appear in the grid, close the menu without reverting them.
skills.when_to_apply: When configuring columns in a Magento-style admin grid where checkbox changes may apply immediately and the menu offers “Reset” and “Cancel” but no explicit Save button.

skills.title: Batch Print Selected Shipments
skills.principle:
1. In the shipments table, check the box for each shipment requiring a packing slip.
2. Confirm the selection count reflects all intended shipments.
3. Open the Actions menu and choose “PDF Shipments” to generate the combined packing-slip PDF.
4. Treat the action as complete once the PDF generation is triggered, then report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use on a Magento Admin Shipments list when multiple packing slips are requested and the table provides row checkboxes plus an Actions menu containing “PDF Shipments”.

skills.title: Execute Shipment PDF Action Once
skills.principle: On the Shipments grid, select the required shipment rows, open Actions, and choose the visible “PDF Shipments” menu item once. After the menu closes or a download/navigation begins, verify the resulting state instead of clicking the stale menu item again; report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When printing multiple packing slips in Magento Admin and the Actions menu shows “PDF Shipments” after shipment checkboxes are selected.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Before Changing
skills.principle: Open the relevant Magento Admin grid through Sales, then Shipments. Inspect the visible “per page” control before editing it; if it already shows the requested value, make no change and report that the setting is already satisfied.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to change how many records a Magento Admin list displays per page, especially from a dashboard where the target grid is not immediately visible.

skills.title: Verify Pagination Before Changing It
skills.principle: On the relevant admin grid, inspect the current “per page” value first. If it already matches the requested count, treat the task as complete and stop. Otherwise open the per-page selector, choose the requested option once, then verify the control reflects that value before reporting completion. Do not repeatedly reopen the selector or use no-op waits as refreshes.
skills.when_to_apply: When changing the number of records shown in a Magento-style admin grid, especially when the pagination control may already display the requested value.

skills.title: Open Magento System Menu
skills.principle: Click the top navigation entry labeled “SYSTEM.” Confirm completion when its expanded menu appears with system categories such as Data Transfer, Extensions, Tools, Permissions, or Other Settings.
skills.when_to_apply: When a Magento Admin task asks you to navigate to the System section and the top navigation bar is visible. Stop once the System dropdown is visibly expanded.

skills.title: Use Observed Navigation Targets
skills.principle: When a menu link is visible, target its observed accessible label or current element identifier, not an icon glyph or guessed text encoding. After an action error, refresh the accessibility tree and select the new target. For navigation, verify the resulting heading or URL before trying alternatives; do not invent a route unless the interface exposes it.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating an admin interface and the desired section is visibly listed but clicks fail, especially when icon glyphs appear in accessible names or guessed direct URLs may not correspond to real routes.

skills.title: Verify Destination Before Acting
skills.principle: Check the current URL, navigation label, and page headings before navigating. If they already identify the requested destination, report completion immediately. Otherwise, select the navigation entry whose accessible name matches the target, then confirm the resulting URL and content before terminating.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the initial accessibility tree may already show the requested page or when a navigation link directly names the destination.

skills.title: Verify Navigation Before Repeating Actions
skills.principle: After activating a navigation entry, inspect the resulting URL, page title, heading, and relevant content. If they match the requested destination, treat the task as complete and stop. Do not repeatedly click a link whose destination is already displayed; only retry when the page state shows navigation failed.
skills.when_to_apply: When navigating within an admin interface, especially when the target link may point to the current page. Confirm completion from observable page state before taking another action.

skills.title: Navigate Hierarchical Admin Menus
skills.principle:
1. Identify the top-level navigation category matching the target page’s domain.
2. Activate that category to reveal its submenu, then locate the submenu entry by its visible label.
3. Select the matching entry and verify completion using the resulting page heading, URL, or distinctive content.
4. Once the target page is confirmed, report completion and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when an admin task requests navigation to a page accessible through nested navigation menus and the current accessibility tree shows the relevant top-level category.

skills.title: Stop After Confirming Destination
skills.principle: Once the target page is visibly confirmed by its heading, URL, or distinctive content, report completion and terminate immediately. Do not repeat noop actions or click navigation controls again, because continued interaction can prevent the task from being recognized as complete.
skills.when_to_apply: Use for navigation tasks when the current observation already shows the requested page and its identifying heading or URL.

skills.title: Navigate Magento Newsletter Subscribers
skills.principle:
1. Open the MARKETING navigation entry to reveal its submenu.
2. Under Communications, select the “Newsletter Subscribers” link.
3. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading and URL identify Newsletter Subscribers, then report success and stop.
skills.when_to_apply: Use when a Magento Admin task requests the Newsletter Subscribers page and the current view is elsewhere in the admin panel. Verify the destination after navigation before ending.

skills.title: Terminate After Verifying Target Page
skills.principle: Once the page heading and URL confirm the requested destination, treat navigation as complete. Report completion and terminate immediately instead of issuing repeated noop actions or waiting for another observation.
skills.when_to_apply: Use after navigating to an admin page when the accessibility tree visibly shows the requested page title or heading and the current URL matches the destination.

skills.title: Use the Verified Sitemap Route
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, when the Site Map menu entry is not visible, navigate to the admin sitemap route rather than repeatedly reopening unrelated menus. If the first route shows “404 Error,” remove the dashboard segment and retry the standard sitemap path. Confirm completion by checking the page heading “Site Map” and sitemap table before reporting success.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to open Magento Admin’s Site Map and menu inspection does not expose a matching link, especially after a candidate sitemap URL produces a visible 404 page.

skills.title: Distinguish Navigation From Record Search
skills.principle: Use the admin navigation to locate destination pages, not a list’s keyword search. A search box inside CMS Pages searches page records only; a zero-record result does not mean the admin feature is absent. If the opened submenu lacks the target, return to navigation and inspect another relevant top-level section.
skills.when_to_apply: When an admin task requests a built-in page or feature and the current screen is a record-management grid with a keyword search, especially after that search returns no records.

skills.title: Locate Pending Reviews in Marketing
skills.principle: In Magento Admin, open the Marketing navigation and inspect its User Content section. Select the visible “Pending Reviews” entry, then verify completion by checking that the page heading reads “Pending Reviews” and the review grid has loaded. Report the displayed record count if useful, then stop.
skills.when_to_apply: When asked to navigate to Pending Reviews from another Magento Admin page and the main navigation is visible. Use the Marketing menu, especially its User Content subsection, rather than Catalog.

skills.title: Use Section Navigation for Admin Pages
skills.principle: When the current admin grid or detail page lacks the requested destination, use the top-level section navigation—such as SALES or the relevant Operations entry—to open its submenu and select the target page. Do not treat row Actions, filters, scrolling, or detail controls as site-wide navigation. Confirm completion by checking that the page heading matches the requested destination.
skills.when_to_apply: Apply when an admin task requests a page not represented by the current list, Actions menu, filters, or detail view, especially when the top navigation exposes relevant Sales or Operations sections.

skills.title: Select Styled Radios Through Their Labels
skills.principle: When a styled radio times out and the error identifies its associated label as intercepting the click, click that label using its current observed identifier. Confirm the requested radio becomes checked before submitting the form. On GitLab group creation forms, apply this to visibility and audience choices, then confirm the creation message and resulting group page.
skills.when_to_apply: When selecting group visibility or audience in GitLab and a click error identifies the corresponding label as covering the radio input.

skills.title: Open the Creation Form Before Filling Fields
skills.principle: On GitLab’s New Group chooser, select the Create group entry to open the creation form. Locate the Group name textbox in the updated observation and use its current identifier before entering the requested name. When scrolling leaves the chooser unchanged, return to its creation entry rather than guessing a field identifier.
skills.when_to_apply: When creating a GitLab group and the page shows Create group and Import group choices but no Group name textbox, or an attempted fill reports an unknown element.
